Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Scores (ASPECTS) from RapidAI and neuroradiologists were compared to follow-up magnetic resonance (MR) or CT imaging using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). A linear mixed-effect model was adjusted for age and sex. Subgroup analyses examined infarct burden and infarct location (cortical vs deep).
RESULTS: In total, 481 patients (49% female; median age: 74 years) were included. Neuroradiologists had higher agreement with the reference standard than RapidAI (ICC: 0.627 vs 0.546). RapidAI had a smaller adjusted difference (β = -0.10; P = 0.198) than neuroradiologists (β = 0.74; P < .001). Although agreement was poor across both groups, RapidAI showed higher agreement in extensive ischaemia (ASPECTS: 0-4: 0.194 vs 0.115; ASPECTS: 0-2: 0.083 vs 0.059), whereas neuroradiologists had higher agreement in threshold, ASPECTS: 5-7 cases (0.141 vs 0.068). Neuroradiologists showed superior agreement in deep infarcts (ICC: 0.612 vs 0.452).
CONCLUSION: Neuroradiologists maintain higher overall agreement in mid-range ASPECTS cases and deep infarcts, but RapidAI exhibited higher agreement in lower ASPECTS cases. RapidAI demonstrates context-dependent accuracy, serving as an adjunct requiring cautious use alongside neuroradiologist interpretation for clinical judgement.
title: RapidAI compared to RapidAI-assisted neuroradiologist interpretation in evaluating acute ischaemic stroke: A local experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral embolic protection (CEP) devices have been developed to reduce postoperative neurological outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI); however, their effectiveness remains controversial.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of CEP use during TAVI on the occurrence in clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Databases were used to search for randomized clinical trials. The occurrence of all strokes, of disabling strokes specifically, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), all-cause mortality, and vascular complications were analyzed. Conventional meta-analysis was conducted using fixed-effects modeling and trial sequential analysis (TSA: type I error of 5%, power of 90%). The systematic review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420251081075).
RESULTS: In total, eight clinical trials were included, gathering 11,589 patients randomized between those who used the devices (5,943) and those who did not (5,646). The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between CEP use and reduced odds of all-cause stroke (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, p = 0.46) and disabling stroke (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, p = 0.20). The sequential analysis identified a lack of evidence for all strokes (required sample size [rSS] = 38,626; 10.53%), disabling strokes (rSS = 59,732; 17.05%). In terms of mortality, there was no significance in the use of devices (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, p = 0.69), reaching evidence for support (rSS = 7,053; 42.25%).
CONCLUSION: The data on the use of CEP is insufficient to support meta-analytic conclusions regarding cerebrovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, TSA demonstrated evidence supporting futility regarding mortality reduction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials with trial sequential analysis, eight trials, 11,589 patients randomised (5,943 with devices, 5,646 without); PROSPERO CRD420251081075.
appraisal.main_limitation: Fixed-effects pooling of heterogeneous device trials, published in a non-cardiology journal, and no individual patient data.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of eight randomised trials of cerebral embolic protection during TAVI finding no association with stroke, with trial sequential analysis showing the evidence base is insufficient for stroke but suggests futility for mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause stroke OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, p = 0.46; disabling stroke OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, p = 0.20; all-cause mortality OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, p = 0.69.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports the view that routine cerebral embolic protection in TAVI is not justified by current trial evidence, while showing that stroke remains underpowered.

title: Safety and efficacy of cerebral embolic protection devices during TAVI: a meta-analysis and sequence analysis of trials.

abstract: Plasma ceramide levels are elevated in cardiovascular disease and predict recurrent adverse events and mortality after myocardial infarction (MI). However, mechanisms driving post-MI ceramide accumulation and pharmacologically actionable targets to counteract ceramide-driven myocardial damage are still lacking. Here, we identify FK506-binding protein 5 (FKBP5) as a druggable immunometabolic regulator of ceramide metabolism in cardiac macrophages, linking FKBP5 suppression to interrupted pathological crosstalk among sphingolipid remodeling, mitochondrial impairment and post-MI inflammatory injury. Using murine MI models and FKBP5-deficient cells, we examined FKBP5 inhibition or deficiency reduced infarct size and fibrosis, improved cardiac function, and protected against adverse remodeling. Mechanistically, FKBP5 was associated with the sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (Smpd3) promoter region and contributed to the regulation of its transcriptional activity after MI, thereby promoting ceramide accumulation. Specifically, FKBP5-mediated ceramide 24:1 (Cer24:1) upregulation impaired mitochondrial redox homeostasis by disrupting electron transport chain integrity, thereby reinforcing M1 polarization and exacerbating myocardial injury. Elevated Cer24:1 directly bound the mitochondrial TU translation elongation factor (TUFM), disrupting electron transport chain integrity and mitochondrial respiration, providing a defined link between ceramide species and mitochondrial dysfunction. Notably, in vivo treatment with Cer24:1 attenuated the cardioprotective effects of FKBP5 inhibition after MI. Collectively, we describe a previously unrecognized FKBP5-Smpd3-Cer24:1-TUFM signaling axis in cardiac macrophages. FKBP5-governed ceramide metabolism drives macrophage immunometabolic reprogramming, marking FKBP5 as a promising pharmacological target for ischemic heart disease. Our findings support the role of the FKBP5-ceramide axis in mediating post-infarct myocardial dysfunction and highlight pharmacological FKBP5 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy against post-MI cardiac injury.
title: Targeting the FKBP5-ceramide axis driven mitochondrial reprogramming in cardiac macrophages attenuates post-infarct cardiac injury.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cardiovascular disease are frequently treated with regimens incorporating non-PEGylated liposomal anthracycline to mitigate cardiotoxicity while preserving antitumor efficacy. However, considering their unique pharmacokinetics, validation of a cardiovascular risk stratification tool for these patients is much needed.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, non-PEGylated liposomal doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-COMP) between 2014 and 2025. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular history and medications, echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were recorded. Patients were stratified into risk categories according to the Heart Failure Association International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) score. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS) and incidence of cardiovascular events defined as asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, new-onset or worsening heart failure and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 265 patients [median age 73 years (69-77); 51% males]; 41% were classified as moderate risk, 55% as high risk, and 4% as very high risk. During a median follow-up of 29 months, 38 patients (14%) died. OS and cardiovascular events occurrence significantly differed across the three HFA-ICOS risk categories; in particular, very high-risk patients exhibited substantially higher hazards of mortality (HR 5.8) and cardiovascular events (HR 40.4). Cardioprotective therapy at baseline appears not influence cardiovascular outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: The HFA-ICOS score effectively stratifies mortality and risk of cardiovascular events among patients treated with R-COMP. Despite the limited number of very-high risk patients and the heterogenous, non-randomized cardioprotective strategies at baseline, our findings may provide evidence supporting its integration into practice.
title: Cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing liposomal anthracycline: Association with cardiovascular outcomes and overall survival.
Antiplatelet pretreatment in acute coronary syndromes: Bridging the gap between guideline recommendations and clinical practice.
Secondary mitral regurgitation in HFrEF: Predicting reversibility on medical therapy before intervention.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries up to a 15% risk of complete heart block (CHB) within 30 days, but the mechanisms driving recurrent heart block after the apparent initial conduction system recovery post-TAVR remain incompletely understood. Phase 4 atrioventricular block, a pause-dependent phenomenon occurring when supraventricular or ventricular impulses encounter diseased His-Purkinje fibers during diastolic depolarization, may contribute to post-TAVR conduction disturbances. We present an instructive case of a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic valve stenosis who developed CHB in the setting of phase 4 atrioventricular block following TAVR. Despite recovering sinus rhythm with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction within 12 hours post-procedure, she experienced recurrent ventricular standstill upon temporary pacemaker removal, ultimately requiring permanent pacemaker implantation. This case illustrates the multiple mechanisms and temporal patterns of post-TAVR conduction system disorders, the potential unreliability of early apparent conduction recovery as a predictor of durable atrioventricular conduction, and the necessity for careful and more prolonged patient monitoring before and after temporary pacemaker removal.
title: Phase 4 Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Unmasking Latent Conduction Disease.
Association of pre-existing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy with outcomes in cardiogenic shock: a multicentre cohort study.

abstract: The study aimed to evaluate whether a half-dose heparin flush strategy during intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support improves safety compared with the standard-dose strategy in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 128 CS patients who received IABP support between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. Sixty-eight patients received a standard-dose heparin flush, and 60 received a half-dose flush. The primary endpoints were clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 2, 3, or 5) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100 × 109/L). Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, adjusting for dual antiplatelet therapy and renal dysfunction. The incidence of clinically significant bleeding events and thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the half-dose group than in the standard-dose group (P < .05). Compared with the standard-dose group, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was significantly associated with a lower risk of clinically significant bleeding (odds ratio = 0.15; 95% confidence interval = 0.03-0.68). Among the secondary outcomes, the half-dose group had a significantly lower transfusion requirement than the standard-dose group (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in activated partial thromboplastin time, activated clotting time, in-hospital mortality, or catheter-related occlusion events. In patients with CS receiving IABP support, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was associated with lower incidences of thrombocytopenia, clinical bleeding, and transfusion requirements. No device-related thrombotic events were observed in either group, suggesting that the half-dose heparin flush strategy may contribute to optimizing anticoagulation management during the peri-support period.
title: Comparison of anticoagulation efficacy and safety of different heparin dosages in cardiogenic shock patients supported by intra-aortic balloon pump: A retrospective cohort study.

abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that inflammatory mechanisms may play a key role in linking psychological disorders to cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to explore the association between anxiety and depression levels and two inflammatory markers, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 1498 patients with ACS who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) in Rasht, Iran, between January 2022 and June 2023. SII and SIRI were calculated for all patients. Patients' psychological status regarding anxiety and depression was evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). All data analyses were conducted using SPSS version 22. The mean age of the patients was 58.49 ± 11.14 years, with males comprising 57.5% of the sample. Male participants exhibited significantly higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to females (P < .05). Individuals with comorbidities showed significantly lower anxiety scores (P < .05). Anxiety levels varied significantly based on CAG findings (P = .004). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression analyses, neither SII nor SIRI was significantly associated with depression severity (SII: OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.70-1.49; SIRI: OR = 1.012, 95% CI: 0.86-1.03) or anxiety severity (SII: OR = 0.906, 95% CI: 0.63-1.29; SIRI: OR = 1.005, 95% CI: 0.98-1.03). Systemic inflammation indices (SII and SIRI) did not show significant associations with anxiety or depression severity in cardiac patients, highlighting their limited utility as psychological predictors.
title: Association of SII and SIRI with anxiety and depression severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated the prognostic role of pathological Q waves and T-wave inversions (TWI) in patients with anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
METHOD: Prospective cohort study of 658 anterior STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was conducted. Participants were divided into four categories based on the presence of pathological Q waves and TWI presence on initial ECGs: Q + TWI+ (n = 34), Q + TWI- (n = 132), Q-TWI+ (n = 81), and Q-TWI- (n = 411). The primary endpoint was a composite outcome, which includes cardiovascular death, newly developed or aggravated New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV heart failure, recurrent myocardial infarction, and cardiogenic shock. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the total study period was one year. Survival differences and hazard ratios among groups were assessed using log-rank tests and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Patients had significant baseline differences in age, gender, and clinical parameters. Survival analysis revealed significantly higher mortality risks in Q + TWI+ (aHR: 7.2, 95% CI: 1.80-28.83), Q + TWI- (aHR: 2.46, 95% CI: 1.1-5.5), and Q-TWI+ (aHR: 4.28, 95% CI: 1.31-13.89). In isolated analyses, both T-wave inversion (aHR: 3.08, 95% CI: 1.15-8.21) and Q waves (aHR: 1.99, 95% CI: 1-3.96) were independently associated with increased mortality. For secondary outcomes, only Q-TWI+ showed significantly elevated risk (aHR: 3.73, 95% CI: 1.01-13.77).
CONCLUSION: In anterior STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, Q waves predicted short-term risk, while TWI strongly associated with long-term risk; their combination conferred the highest risk. Unadjusted for door-to-PCI time, these hypothesis-generating findings may reflect ischemic duration. Ultimately, they validate prior reports in a Middle Eastern cohort and support dynamic risk stratification.
title: Investigating predictive value of Q-waves and inverted T-waves in anterior STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI: a prospective cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for pure aortic regurgitation (AR) remains challenging, especially in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) anatomy, which has been excluded from pivotal trials of dedicated AR devices. Whether cusp-engaging devices can be used in type 1 BAV with raphe is unknown.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report two East Asian male patients (aged 72 and 62 years) with severe pure AR and type 1 bicuspid aortic valve, confirmed by transthoracic echocardiography. Pre-procedural multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) demonstrated a raphe between the left and right coronary cusps in both patients, with relatively symmetric cusp sizes and minimal calcification. Self-expanding Taurus-Trio valves (27 mm and 25 mm, respectively) were successfully implanted under monitored anaesthesia care (MAC) with TTE guidance. Post-procedural TTE showed only trivial paravalvular leak (PVL). At 6-month follow-up, MDCT confirmed favourable valve performance, with all three locators appropriately engaged within the corresponding cusps, preserved leaflet morphology and motion, and no evidence of hypo-attenuated leaflet thickening (HALT). Neither patient developed new conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation.
CONCLUSIONS: This case report demonstrates the feasibility of using a dedicated cusp-engaging transcatheter valve in carefully selected patients with type 1 BAV-AR, favourable cusp symmetry, and minimal calcification. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation; they should not be generalised to all BAV subtypes or to patients with significant calcification.
title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation in bicuspid aortic valve regurgitation: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical importance of acute brain injury (ABI) during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the mechanism of ECMO-associated ABI remains poorly understood, partly because conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is incompatible with ECMO devices. Ultra-low-field portable MRI (ULF-pMRI) enables high-quality bedside neuroimaging during ECMO. We aimed to characterize imaging phenotypes of ABI and explore mechanisms underlying lesion distribution across ECMO configurations.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, adults receiving ECMO who underwent bedside ULF-pMRI at Johns Hopkins University and University of Texas-Houston from December 2021 to May 2026 were included. ABI was defined as ischemic stroke (IS), intraparenchymal hemorrhage (IPH), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or subdural hematoma (SDH). Lesions were characterized according to vascular territory, cortical/subcortical lesion versus deep white matter (WM)/basal ganglia (BG) involvement, laterality, lesion burden, and cerebral small-vessel disease (SVD) using Fazekas scale. Associations between ECMO configuration (central venoarterial [VA], peripheral VA, and venovenous [VV]), echocardiographic findings, and ECMO parameters were examined.
RESULTS: Among 70 patients analyzed (55.9 ± 16.2 years; 54.3% male), 29 (41.4%) had ABI. IS was the predominant type of ABI (82.8%), with most strokes affecting the frontal lobe (48.3%). All the central VA-ECMO patients with ABI demonstrated predominantly cortical/subcortical lesions, whereas deep WM/BG involvement was more frequent in peripheral VA-ECMO (53.8%). Peripheral VA-ECMO demonstrated left hemispheric predominance (85% vs. 15% right-sided, P =0.002), and deep WM/BG lesions in peripheral were associated with higher ECMO pump flow and lower pulse pressure. Among VV-ECMO patients, bilateral lesions were more common (62.5%), with a high prevalence of deep WM/BG involvement (62.5%) and SVD (75%).
CONCLUSIONS: ULF-pMRI revealed distinct radiological phenotypes of ABI across ECMO configurations; cortical/subcortical lesions in central VA-ECMO, left-sided predominance in peripheral VA-ECMO and frequent deep WM/BG in VV-ECMO. These findings generate mechanistic hypotheses regarding configuration-specific pathways of ABI and may inform future strategies for risk stratification, prevention and monitoring.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Radiological Phenotypes of Acute Brain Injury During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation on Ultra-Low-Field Portable MRI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tobacco smoking is the largest modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet population-level surveillance still relies on self-reported and retail data, which are subject to measuring bias and lag. Urinary and salivary cotinine quantify individual tobacco exposure, but no analogous, objective metric exists at the community level. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has transformed surveillance of infectious diseases and illicit drug use; whether the same approach can yield a community-level signal of CVD risk is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to track community-level wastewater nicotine biomarkers and evaluate potential correlations with relative CVD burden in El Paso, Texas.
METHODS: We integrated wastewater nicotine biomarker surveillance with electronic health record (EHR) data across four sewersheds in El Paso, Texas. Twenty-four-hour composite influent samples were collected monthly (June 2024-May 2025; n=48) and quantified by liquid-chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for five nicotine metabolites. Cotinine, nornicotine, and trans-3'-hydroxycotinine (3HC) were detected in 91.6-100% of samples, whereas tobacco-specific nitrosamines were below limit of detection. CVD cases (January 2021-December 2024) were obtained from the Paso del Norte Health Information Exchange and mapped to sewersheds by residential ZIP code using ArcGIS. At the sewershed level, population-normalized nicotine mass loads tracked the proportional burden of atherosclerosis/ischemia/infarction and heart failure. Across the sewersheds, monthly 3HC mass load and the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR) were strongly and specifically associated with incident ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) (3HC vs. STEMI: ρ = 0.893, p = 0.012), without parallel associations for non-ST-elevation or old myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that integrating wastewater nicotine surveillance with EHR data can reveal community-level 3HC and NMR as specific indicators of incident STEMI. Our findings indicate wastewater surveillance as a novel, objective tool to inform cessation policy and CVD prevention.Lay Words: This study investigated using wastewater to measure population-level nicotine consumption and to see if it was related to local cardiovascular disease.The study took place in El Paso, Texas, USA across 4 different wastewater treatment collection points over the course of one year.Three metabolites of human nicotine consumption were detected in wastewater samples. The increased nicotine mass loads were proportional with community-level heart failure and atherosclerosis.Wastewater can be a helpful tool to inform cardiovascular disease prevention efforts and smoking cessation practices.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Community-Level Wastewater Surveillance of Nicotine Biomarkers Tracks Cardiovascular Disease Burden and Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) mechanical function predicts outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Recovering these parameters from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) could enable point-of-care risk assessment wherever an ECG is acquired.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanics predict all-cause mortality after AMI and myocardial infarction (MI)-specific mortality in the general population and add information beyond the GRACE score and ejection fraction.
METHODS: Synthetic peak systolic (s') and early diastolic (e') mitral annular velocities and mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) were derived from the 12-lead ECG by a previously validated generative adversarial network, applied without retraining and blinded to outcome. Associations were assessed in an AMI cohort (n=1,065) by Cox regression and a population cohort (n=219,564) by Fine-Gray models. Incremental value was tested against GRACE, three AI-ECG reduced ejection fraction (EF) models, and measured LVEF.
RESULTS: In the AMI cohort (109 deaths; median follow-up 1.44 years), all three parameters predicted all-cause mortality (each P<0.001). Synthetic e' was the sole independent predictor after adjustment for clinical covariates (HR=0.90 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.84-0.98) and for GRACE (HR=0.90; 0.83-0.97; P=0.006). In the post-discharge cohort (n=1,017; 61 deaths), synthetic e' improved discrimination beyond GRACE (C-index 0.67 to 0.70; HR=0.84 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.76-0.93; P=0.001) and remained independent of AI-ECG-predicted and measured LVEF (HR 0.84-0.86 per 1 cm/s; all P≤0.004), contributing 28-46% of each model's prognostic information. In the population cohort (817 MI deaths; median follow-up 3.42 years), all three predicted MI-specific mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and ECG abnormalities, MAPSE showing the largest effect (sHR=0.49; 95% CI 0.37-0.65), with s' (sHR=0.78; 0.72-0.84) and e' (sHR=0.87; 0.82-0.93) also predictive (each P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanical parameters predict all-cause mortality after AMI and fatal MI in the general population, adding information beyond the GRACE score and LVEF.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
keywords: electrocardiogram; tissue Doppler imaging; generative adversarial network; myocardial infarction; mortality prediction; risk stratification.
title: ECG-Derived Synthetic Left Ventricular Mechanics Predict Mortality After Acute Myocardial Infarction and Fatal Myocardial Infarction in the General Population.

abstract: Artificial intelligence models may improve emergency department (ED) screening for acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but such models often rely on International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes as training labels, whose accuracy in contemporary ED populations is uncertain. In this 10-year retrospective study of 619,599 adult ED encounters, we compared ICD-coded ACS against a chart-reviewed reference standard defined as the treating team's documented diagnosis. Sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value were 94.4%, 99.7%, and 72.4%, respectively. Disagreement occurred in 0.31% of encounters. Among false positives (n=1,647), the leading reason was ACS suspected but later ruled out (80.3%); among false negatives (n=257), coder omission of documented ACS (86.0%). ACS ICD codes are suitable training labels for screening models where missing ACS is more consequential than over-identification, and the observed error patterns are systematic and interpretable rather than random.
title: Validating Acute Coronary Syndrome ICD Codes as Training Labels for Clinical AI.

abstract: Cardiogenic shock still carries a 30-day mortality of approximately 40%-50% despite reperfusion, vasoactive support and modern intensive care. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can rapidly restore systemic perfusion, but recent randomised evidence has reframed its role. In infarct-related shock, randomised trials have not shown a clear survival benefit from routine early VA-ECMO; ECLS-SHOCK and pooled analyses also found more bleeding and vascular complications. In the same period, DanGer Shock showed that a primary microaxial-pump (Impella CP) strategy improved survival in a carefully selected population with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock, although it was tested against standard care rather than head-to-head against VA-ECMO and does not isolate unloading as the causal mechanism. Read together, these data motivate the central argument of this review: peripheral VA-ECMO is usefully managed not only as a problem of circulatory flow, but also as a dynamic problem of ventricular loading. We advance this as an organising framework rather than as a demonstrated mechanism, since differences in patient selection between these trials offer a competing and equally tenable explanation. Retrograde aortic return increases effective LV afterload, while venous drainage reduces preload; the clinical result depends on the interaction between circuit flow, native contractility and biventricular loading conditions. This narrative, non-systematic review synthesises contemporary trial evidence, the physiology and treatment of LV loading, and approaches to serial assessment of the supported heart, from haemodynamics and bedside echocardiography to emerging deformation and advanced imaging tools. VA-ECMO should therefore be viewed as a time-limited bridge whose net benefit depends on reversible disease, early recognition of clinically relevant ventricular overload and repeated assessment of recovery, escalation options and futility.

register_verdicts.note: Narrative review of VA-ECMO loading physiology with no new trial data.

title: Beyond flow: a ventricular-load framework for VA-ECMO in cardiogenic shock.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect (pMI-VSD) remains a catastrophic mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction despite advances in surgical management. We evaluated early and long-term outcomes after surgical repair of pMI-VSD at a tertiary referral center.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 80 consecutive patients who underwent surgical repair of pMI-VSD between January 1995 and November 2025. Early outcomes, postoperative complications including residual shunting, and long-term all-cause mortality were analyzed. Long-term survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and a parsimonious Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: The mean age was 70.4±9.1 years, and 47.5% were male. The 30-day mortality rate was 7.5%. Residual shunts were detected in 35 patients (43.8%), of whom five (6.3% of the overall cohort) underwent reoperation. During a median observed follow-up of 58.5 months, 38 patients (47.5%) died. Estimated survival was 81.0% [95% confidence interval (CI): 72.8-90.1%] at 1 year, 70.5% (95% CI: 60.8-81.8%) at 5 years. In multivariable analysis, age and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD) were associated with all-cause mortality. Survival differed between patients operated on in ≤2015 and >2015 (log-rank P=0.03), although this unadjusted comparison may reflect concurrent changes in patient characteristics and management.
CONCLUSIONS: Favorable early and long-term outcomes were observed among selected patients who underwent surgical repair of pMI-VSD at an experienced center. Residual shunt status was not associated with a statistically detectable difference in long-term survival, although quantitative hemodynamic assessment was not uniformly available. Survival was better in the more recent era, although the contributions of changes in patient selection, surgical technique, and perioperative management cannot be distinguished in this observational cohort. However, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature of the study.
title: Surgical outcomes and long-term survival after repair of post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect: a 30-year single-center experience.
Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation versus off-pump lung transplantation: a long-standing debate.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), patients remain at risk for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The apelin-12/white blood cell ratio (AWR), a ratio has never been studied before, may reflect the balance between cardioprotective apelin signaling and systemic inflammation. We examined the prognostic value of admission AWR for long-term MACEs in STEMI patients after primary PCI.
METHODS: This secondary analysis included 464 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at The First People's Hospital of Taizhou (Zhejiang, China) between January 2010 and October 2014. Blood samples were collected on admission, immediately before primary PCI, for apelin-12 measurement. Patients were followed for 30 months. MACE was defined as the composite of cardiac death, cardiogenic shock, congestive heart failure, recurrent target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target-lesion revascularization. AWR was analyzed as a continuous variable and by pre-specified tertiles (cut-points 6.48 and 10.49). Cox proportional-hazards (PH) regression with a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-derived minimal adjustment set (age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, serum creatinine, and Killip class) was used to estimate associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), C-index, bootstrap optimism correction, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI).
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.0 months, 118 patients (25.4%) experienced MACEs. Patients in the highest AWR tertile were older and less likely to be male than those in the lowest tertile. Higher AWR was independently associated with lower MACE risk [per 1-standard deviation (1-SD) increase: hazard ratio (HR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.40-0.68, P<0.001; highest vs. lowest tertile: HR 0.40, 95% CI: 0.24-0.65, P<0.001]. The protective association strengthened after the first month. Adding AWR to the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) 2.0 and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) scores significantly improved reclassification (IDI and NRI both P<0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: A lower admission AWR is associated with an increased risk of long-term MACEs in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, supporting its potential as a prognostic biomarker.
title: Prognostic value of the apelin-12-to-white blood cell ratio for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG.
METHODS: In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards.
RESULTS: A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89-4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57-6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76-2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14-4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22-1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13-8.31; P=0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.
title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study.

abstract: Background and aim Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) frequently undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using either radial or femoral arterial access. Prior studies have shown potential benefits of radial access; however, data are limited regarding these approaches in patients from Puerto Rico. This study aimed to compare bleeding, vascular complications, and 30-day all-cause mortality between radial and femoral access for PCI in patients with STEMI in southern Puerto Rico. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional review of medical records of patients aged 21-90 years admitted with STEMI at Centro Médico Episcopal San Lucas in southern Puerto Rico from 2021 to 2023. We excluded patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction or unstable angina. A total of 311 patients were identified and included in the study. Patients were stratified according to radial or femoral access on the first attempt. Outcomes included 30-day all-cause mortality, pseudoaneurysm, hematoma, and bleeding after thrombolysis in myocardial infarction. All statistical analyses were conducted using RStudio (Boston, MA: Posit, PBC). Results Among the study subjects, 90 patients had first-attempt radial access, while 221 patients had first-attempt femoral access. There were no major bleeding events in any of the groups. Minor bleeding events were reported for one out of 90 patients in the radial group compared to 21 patients out of 221 in the femoral group. This difference was statistically significant (p=0.01791). Pseudoaneurysm did not occur in the radial group, while seven occurred in the femoral group; however, this difference was not statistically significant. No hematoma was seen in any patient in the first-attempt radial access group, compared with 33 patients with hematoma in the femoral access group (p=0.001). Mortality within 30 days from all causes occurred in one of 90 patients in the radial group compared with 26 of 221 patients in the femoral group. The 30-day survival rate was 98.9% in the radial group and 88.2% in the femoral group, representing a statistically significant difference (p=0.0012). Conclusion Among patients with STEMI undergoing PCI in southern Puerto Rico, first-attempt radial access was associated with lower rates of minor bleeding, hematoma, and 30-day all-cause mortality compared with first-attempt femoral access. The results suggest potential clinical advantages of radial access when clinically appropriate. However, since the current study is of an observational design, it is not reasonable to claim a cause-and-effect relationship. Larger studies that control for clinical factors are needed.
title: Clinical Outcomes of Radial Versus Femoral Access for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Study From Southern Puerto Rico.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report a case of post-detachment Woven EndoBridge (WEB) displacement successfully managed through microcatheter manipulation alone, avoiding unplanned stenting, which necessitates long-term dual antiplatelet therapy.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 42-year-old male presented with an unruptured middle cerebral artery bifurcation aneurysm. Device sizing was planned using high-resolution 3D DSA and volumetric analysis on a Siemens ARTIS icono biplane (ARTIS icono VE20 software; Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany). A WEB SL 5 × 3 mm device (Terumo Neuro, Tustin, CA, USA) was deployed and detached. However, the subsequent withdrawal of an adjunctive microcatheter from a branch vessel caused vascular recoil, leading the detached WEB to rotate and protrude toward the branch orifice, compromising distal flow. Instead of rescue stenting, we performed a "pushing technique" using a Leonis Mova microcatheter (SB-Kawasumi Laboratories, Kanagawa, Japan). The device was successfully reseated within the aneurysm sac, albeit with a 90° rotation. Final angiography confirmed stable seating and excellent branch patency. The patient was discharged without neurological deficits on single antiplatelet therapy.
CONCLUSION: Post-detachment WEB displacement can occur due to dynamic vascular shifts even with precise volumetric sizing. Microcatheter manipulation is a feasible alternative bailout option that preserves the low-profile advantages of the WEB device and avoids the risks associated with rescue stenting.
title: Post-Detachment Displacement of a Woven EndoBridge (WEB) Device Managed via Microcatheter Manipulation: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrical storm (ES) during mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in the setting of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) represents a life-threatening condition driven by sympathetic hyperactivation and repolarization abnormalities. While stellate ganglion block is recognized as an effective autonomic modulation strategy for drug-refractory ventricular arrhythmias, its use may raise concerns regarding bleeding complications in patients receiving systemic anticoagulation. Stellate ganglion phototherapy (SGP) is a non-invasive alternative, but its clinical utility for ES under MCS remains unclear.
CASE SUMMARY: This case series describes two patients with drug-refractory ES complicating ACS during MCS management. Patient 1, a 78-year-old woman with cardiogenic shock, developed recurrent ventricular fibrillation (VF) with QT prolongation while on veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Overdrive pacing caused haemodynamic deterioration, and conventional antiarrhythmic drugs failed. Following SGP initiation, no further VF requiring electrical shocks occurred. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was subsequently withdrawn. Patient 2, a 77-year-old man, developed recurrent torsades de pointes/VF with QT prolongation after left main revascularization under Impella support. Following SGP initiation, no further episodes requiring electrical shocks occurred. Impella was subsequently removed.
DISCUSSION: Stellate ganglion phototherapy may represent a non-invasive autonomic modulation strategy for drug-refractory ES in ACS patients requiring MCS. Although concomitant therapies and gradual recovery from myocardial ischaemia may have contributed to arrhythmia suppression, the temporal association suggests a potential contribution of SGP. Stellate ganglion phototherapy may serve as a bridge to recovery when invasive approaches pose additional challenges.
title: Stellate ganglion phototherapy for electrical storm during mechanical circulatory support in acute coronary syndrome: a case series.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-leaflet device attachment (SLDA) is a rare but serious complication of mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (MTEER). When SLDA occurs after full device release, management options are limited. In contrast, intra-procedural SLDA recognized before full implant release may allow a specific bailout strategy.
CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with severe degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) underwent MTEER using the PASCAL Ace system because of high surgical risk. Initial device implantation reduced MR from severe to mild. However, after removal of both clasp lines during the release process, SLDA occurred at the posterior leaflet, resulting in recurrent severe MR. Although standard retrieval was no longer feasible, the implant remained connected to the steerable catheter. Under fluoroscopic and transoesophageal echocardiographic guidance, a guide sheath was advanced coaxially towards the implant. Controlled insertion of the guide sheath between the clasp and paddle, followed by gradual paddle opening, enabled leaflet disengagement and successful device retrieval without leaflet injury. A second implantation achieved a sufficient reduction in mitral regurgitation.
DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates a novel bailout technique for intra-procedural SLDA. Successful retrieval requires precise coaxial device alignment, careful catheter manipulation, continuous monitoring of leaflet tension, and meticulous guidance using fluoroscopy and transoesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Importantly, prompt recognition of SLDA by TEE is a prerequisite for this technique. In conclusion, the guide-sheath-assisted retrieval technique can represent a potential bailout strategy for intra-procedural SLDA before full implant release during MTEER.
title: Guide-sheath-assisted bailout technique for intra-procedural single-leaflet device attachment using the PASCAL system: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the acceleration of global population ageing and the increasing burden of chronic diseases, the number of older adults with coronary heart disease is steadily increasing. Medication literacy is an important foundation for safe medication use and is closely associated with medication management and secondary prevention among older adults with CHD after percutaneous coronary intervention. However, research on medication literacy in this population remains relatively limited, and factors associated with medication literacy have not been sufficiently investigated. Therefore, further research is needed to examine the factors associated with medication literacy among older adults with CHD after PCI, which may help inform future targeted intervention studies and the development of appropriate clinical interventions.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the status of medication literacy among older adults with coronary heart disease after PCI, examine the association between health empowerment and medication literacy, and further assess the indirect association of self-efficacy for appropriate medication use in this relationship.
METHODS: This study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. Using convenience sampling, 483 older adults with coronary heart disease after PCI were recruited from two Grade A tertiary hospitals in Sichuan Province, China, from March to October 2025. On-site questionnaire surveys were conducted. The research instruments included the demographic characteristics, patient perceptions of empowerment scale, self-efficacy for appropriate medication use scale, and medication literacy scale for patients after PCI. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0 and its PROCESS macro program.
RESULTS: Among the 483 older adults with coronary heart disease after PCI in this study, the score of health empowerment was 36.69 ± 6.19, the score of self-efficacy for appropriate medication use was 28.25 ± 4.73, and the score of medication literacy was 70.62 ± 17.82. Pearson correlation analysis showed that medication literacy was positively correlated with health empowerment (r = 0.810, p < 0.01) and self-efficacy for appropriate medication use (r = 0.821, p < 0.01), while health empowerment was positively correlated with self-efficacy for appropriate medication use (r = 0.811, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis showed a statistically significant indirect association between health empowerment and medication literacy through self-efficacy for appropriate medication use, with an indirect effect of 0.346. This indirect effect accounted for 47.92% of the total effect (95% CI: [0.287, 0.410]). In addition, the total effect was 0.722 (95% CI: [0.666, 0.777]), and the direct effect was 0.376 (95% CI: [0.299, 0.452]).
CONCLUSION: Medication literacy among older adults with coronary heart disease after PCI was at a moderate level. Health empowerment, self-efficacy for appropriate medication use, and medication literacy were significantly and positively associated with one another, and a statistically significant indirect association between health empowerment and medication literacy through self-efficacy for appropriate medication use was observed. These findings suggest that healthcare professionals should consider health empowerment and self-efficacy for appropriate medication use when developing strategies to improve medication literacy among older adults after PCI, which may provide a reference for future intervention studies.
title: Association between health empowerment and medication literacy among older adults with coronary heart disease after PCI: the mediating role of self-efficacy for appropriate medication use.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) may cause anemia, hypovolemia, and hemodynamic compromise, potentially contributing to myocardial injury during the acute illness. Troponin elevation in this setting requires careful interpretation because an isolated measurement cannot reliably distinguish acute injury from elevation without qualifying change or establish myocardial infarction. The frequency, temporal evolution, and clinical significance of acute myocardial injury in patients with UGIB remain incompletely characterized. This prospective multicenter study evaluated its prevalence, associated admission factors, serial troponin dynamics, and relationship with in-hospital outcomes, including subsequent mortality among patients surviving the first 24 hours.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter observational cohort study enrolled 1,000 adults at tertiary care hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan, between January 2025 and August 2026. Cardiac troponin I measurements were scheduled at presentation, 3-6 hours, and 20-24 hours. Acute injury required a concentration above the applicable 99th-percentile reference limit and a serial maximum-minimum range of ≥10 ng/L and ≥20% of the earliest observed concentration, using at least two measurements spanning ≥3 hours. Prevalence was estimated with Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression examined admission factors associated with injury. A 24-hour landmark analysis evaluated subsequent mortality among patients alive and still hospitalized with classifiable injury status.
RESULTS: Injury status was classifiable in 960 patients; 104 had acute injury, giving a prevalence of 10.8% (95% CI: 9.0-13.0%). A further 131 patients (13.6% of classifiable assessments) had troponin elevation without qualifying change, while 40 assessments were indeterminate. Older age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per decade: 1.40; 95% CI: 1.21-1.63), coronary artery disease (aOR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.10), and lower hemoglobin (aOR per 1 g/dL decrease: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.06-1.51) were associated with acute injury. Fourteen acute-injury cases (13.5%) first met the classification criterion at the late measurement. Among 810 landmark patients with known outcomes, 34 died. Subsequent mortality was 15.2% with acute injury versus 2.8% without acute injury (aOR: 3.47; 95% CI: 1.58-7.62; p=0.002). An adverse differential assignment of unresolved mortality outcomes attenuated this association (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 0.94-3.69).
CONCLUSIONS: Acute myocardial injury affected approximately one in 10 classifiable patients with UGIB and was associated with older age, coronary artery disease, lower hemoglobin, and higher subsequent in-hospital mortality. Serial measurements distinguished acute changes from elevation without qualifying change. The mortality association requires cautious interpretation because of limited events, residual confounding, and incomplete follow-up.
title: Acute Myocardial Injury in Patients Presenting With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Prevalence, Predictors, Troponin Dynamics, and In-Hospital Outcomes.

abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) vasculitis (IgAV), formerly known as Henoch-Schönlein purpura, is a systemic small-vessel vasculitis caused by IgA immune-complex deposition; cardiac involvement is exceedingly rare and incompletely characterized. We describe a 41-year-old woman with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy who presented with progressive dyspnea, hemoptysis, and a painful purpuric rash and was found to have severe multisystem IgAV with simultaneous cardiac, pulmonary, renal, and cutaneous involvement. High-sensitivity troponin T peaked at 20,208 ng/L and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 49,428 pg/mL. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25%, diffuse mid-wall and epicardial late gadolinium enhancement with abnormal T1 and T2 values, and a 25 × 15 mm apical thrombus. Skin biopsy confirmed leukocytoclastic vasculitis and bronchoscopy confirmed diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, while multimodality imaging and a negative serologic work-up excluded cardiac sarcoidosis, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis, and anti-glomerular basement membrane disease. The patient was treated with pulse methylprednisolone, plasma exchange, rituximab, and cautious anticoagulation, with resolution of alveolar hemorrhage, a progressive decline in cardiac biomarkers, resolution of the left ventricular thrombus, and partial recovery of left ventricular systolic function. This case expands the recognized spectrum of cardiovascular involvement in adult IgAV and highlights the value of multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary management in establishing the diagnosis and guiding therapy.
title: Pulmonary-Cardiac Involvement in a Patient with IgA Vasculitis.

abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare radiation dose and image quality of coronary artery reconstructions obtained from non-coronary-dedicated transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) planning CT scans using ultra-high-pitch photon-counting CT (PCCT) and ultra-high-pitch energy-integrating detector dual-source CT (EID-DSCT; hereafter referred to as DSCT), including assessment of the feasibility of coronary artery evaluation according to the Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study on consecutive patients with aortic valve stenosis (AS) undergoing contrast-enhanced TAVI planning CT, either PCCT or DSCT between August 2021 and June 2023. CT dose index (CTDI) and dose length product (DLP) were used to calculate the effective radiation dose (eRD). Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were calculated using standardized region-of-interest (ROI) analysis. Coronary arteries were evaluated by three independent radiologists using 5-point Likert scales followed by a classification according to the CAD-RADS system.
RESULTS: 187 patients (83 female, median age 82, IQR: 76-84) underwent 190 CT-examinations, 103 PCCT (54.2%) and 87 (45.8%) DSCT. Three patients underwent both PCCT and DSCT for clinical reasons. Mean CTDI and DLP were significantly lower in PCCT compared to DSCT (21.9 vs. 52.8 and 607.9 vs. 906.8, respectively; both p < 0.001), with a correspondingly lower mean effective radiation dose (eRD) in PCCT compared to DSCT (10.3 ± 5.4 mSv vs. 15.4 ± 5.6 mSv, p < 0.001). While both SNR and CNR were lower in PCCT than in DSCT (SNR: 35.28 ± 11.63 in PCCT vs. 45.6 ± 16.3 in DSCT, p < 0.001; CNR: 49.25 ± 13.31 in PCCT vs. 57.42 v ± 22.55 in DSCT, p = 0.004), PCCT outperformed DSCT in every one of the eleven visual image categories. Overall image quality was rated as good or excellent in 71.8% (74/103) of PCCT vs. 19.5% (17/87) of DSCT scans. Coronary reconstructions were rated as good or excellent in 72.8% (75/103) of PCCT vs. 20.7% of DSCT datasets. CAD-RADS [1-5] rating was possible in 68.9% (71/103) of PCCT vs. 39.1% (34/87) of DSCT datasets.
CONCLUSION: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) allows for significantly improved assessability of the coronary arteries in TAVI planning CT compared with dual-source CT (DSCT), while achieving a substantially lower radiation dose.
title: Ultra-high-pitch photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) versus ultra-high-pitch dual-source computed tomography (DSCT) for coronary artery disease evaluation in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) patients.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) patients exhibit heterogeneous left heart remodeling, with unclear impacts on postoperative prognosis. This study aimed to classify left heart remodeling subtypes using the left atrial (LA) to left ventricular (LV) volume ratio, analyze subtype differences, and validate the ratio's predictive value for 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 350 RMS patients who underwent mitral valve surgery between February 2021 and October 2024. Preoperative LA end-systolic volume (LAESV) and LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) were measured by three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography to calculate the LA/LV volume ratio. The optimal cutoff value was determined by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Patients were divided into predominantly LV remodeling (PLVR) and predominantly LA remodeling (PLAR) groups. Clinical data, echocardiographic parameters, and 1-year adverse outcomes [a composite of heart failure (HF) rehospitalization and all-cause mortality] were compared. Risk factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: The LA/LV volume ratio yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.723 (P<0.001) for predicting 1-year adverse outcomes, with an optimal cutoff of 0.61. PLAR patients (LA/LV >0.61, n=168) were older, more frequently female, had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), more severe mitral stenosis, and larger right atrial volume (all P<0.001). PLVR patients (LA/LV ≤0.61, n=182) had a higher rate of ischemic heart disease, lower LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and a higher proportion of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (all P<0.001). The 1-year composite adverse event rate was 20.6% overall, significantly higher in the PLAR group than in the PLVR group (34.3% vs. 15.1%, P<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression identified PLAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.72, P=0.008], preoperative N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >3,000 pg/mL (HR =1.91, P=0.002), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV (HR =2.15, P=0.002), moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (HR =1.58, P=0.036), and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR =1.63, P=0.029) as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: The LA/LV volume ratio (optimal cutoff 0.61) effectively classifies RMS left heart remodeling subtypes. PLAR is associated with increased 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes, and integrating mitral/tricuspid regurgitation assessment and extended echocardiographic parameters enhances prognostic accuracy. This provides a robust tool for preoperative risk stratification and individualized treatment in RMS patients.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
keywords: left atrial/left ventricular volume ratio (LA/LV volume ratio)
title: Value of left atrial to left ventricular volume ratio in left heart remodeling classification and postoperative prognosis assessment in patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis.

abstract: Hypersensitivity myocarditis caused by NSAIDs can mimic acute STEMI, yet nimesulide as the trigger of primary myocardial injury has rarely been documented. This article reports a 57-year-old male who developed rash and persistent chest pain after taking nimesulide for fever due to respiratory syncytial virus infection. Electrocardiogram revealed ST-segment elevation in leads V2-V3, and the patient was admitted with acute heart failure and shock. Norepinephrine was administered to maintain circulation. Suspected nimesulide-associated hypersensitivity myocarditis was considered based on elevated eosinophil count, medication history and rash. Following methylprednisolone therapy and hemodynamic stabilization, coronary angiography showed no vascular lesions. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated myocardial edema and mid-wall injury of the interventricular septum. Continued glucocorticoid treatment resulted in marked improvement in the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, with SCAI shock stage improving from stage C on admission to stage A at discharge.Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance at 3-month after onset showed complete resolution of myocardial injury without fibrosis. Clinicians should be alert to this rare cardiac adverse reaction of nimesulide.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention
journal_abbrev: Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev
title: Suspected nimesulide-associated hypersensitivity myocarditis presenting as ST-elevation myocardial infarction: A case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a first-line non-invasive imaging modality for CAD evaluation, but conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) is often limited by blooming artifacts, noise, and partial-volume effects. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) provides superior spatial resolution, reduced blooming, and multi-energy spectral data, yet its ultra-high-resolution (UHR) datasets frequently suffer from increased noise and complex spectral information that require advanced processing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to fully exploit PCD-CT's advantages. This narrative review aims to synthesize the current evidence on AI applications in PCD-CT for CAD imaging, evaluate their technical performance and clinical potential, identify limitations, and propose future directions.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. Original English-language studies applying AI techniques to PCD-CT data for CAD imaging were included, and categorized using a 5-level translational framework.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Thirty single-center studies were identified and grouped into three main categories. In image quality improvement, denoising models achieved 60-96% noise reduction while preserving spatial and spectral fidelity. Radiomics studies (the largest group) identified specific texture features in myocardium, plaques, pericoronary, and epicardial adipose tissue associated with coronary artery calcium severity, hypercholesterolemia, aging, and CAD presence, although feature reproducibility was only moderate. Automated detection/quantification/segmentation tools demonstrated high reproducibility, improved stenosis quantification, substantial workflow benefits, and promising CT-fractional flow reserve (FFR) performance with strong intra-individual agreement to EID-CT.
CONCLUSIONS: AI has shown promising technical advancements when applied to PCD-CT for CAD imaging. However, the evidence base remains limited by small sample sizes, single-center and single-scanner designs, lack of external validation, and absence of outcome-driven studies. Future research should focus on multicenter prospective validation, standardized protocols, human-in-the-loop systems, and clinical impact assessment to support the safe and effective translation of AI-enhanced PCD-CT into routine clinical practice.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Artificial intelligence applications in photon-counting detector CT for coronary artery disease imaging: a narrative review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, the incidence and mortality rates of coronary artery disease (CAD) have been rising annually. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of the coronary artery tree description and lesion evaluation (CatLet) angiographic scoring system to stratify risk and to elucidate its independent prognostic value in "all-comers" patients with CAD.
METHODS: A total of 373 consecutive CAD patients were enrolled at The First People's Hospital of Hefei following coronary angiography. The residual CatLet (rCatLet) score was calculated based on the residual lesions after completion of required revascularization at physicians' discretion during this hospitalization for all enrolled patients, who subsequently underwent follow-ups. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Secondary endpoints included all-cause death and cardiac death. Survival rates were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic factors, while the prognostic value of the rCatLet score was evaluated by the time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC).
RESULTS: This was a single-center cohort study of 279 patients, including 56 (20.07%) with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and 223 (79.93%) with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed progressively worse prognosis across higher rCatLet score tertiles for all endpoints (all log-rank P<0.001). Cox regression revealed that, compared with the low tertile, the highest rCatLet tertile was associated with a significantly increased risk of MACCEs [hazard ratio (HR) =4.96; 95% confidence interval (CI): 3.03-8.12], and the medium tertile showed a non-significant trend toward higher risk (HR =1.39; 95% CI: 0.79-2.43). Time-dependent ROC analysis showed that the rCatLet model predicted 1-, 3-, and 6-year MACCEs with AUCs (95% CIs) of 0.85 (0.77-0.92), 0.73 (0.64-0.81), and 0.71 (0.64-0.77). The multivariable-adjusted models performed better, and their AUCs (95% CIs) at the three time points were 0.87 (0.83-0.92), 0.78 (0.72-0.86), and 0.78 (0.73-0.84), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Our exploratory findings suggest that the rCatLet score has predictive value for the short- and long-term clinical prognosis in "all-comers" patients with CAD. Furthermore, the rCatLet score adjusted for clinical variables showed improved prognostic predictive values. These findings require further validation in future studies.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
keywords: Residual coronary artery tree description and lesion evaluation score (rCatLet score)
“all-comers” patients with coronary artery disease (“all-comers” patients with CAD)
title: Residual CatLet score predicts the long-term prognosis in "all-comers" patients with coronary artery disease: a survival analysis study based on time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=-0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=-0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=-0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=-0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=-0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=-0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=-0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain.
CONCLUSIONS: MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
keywords: cardiac magnetic resonance feature tracking (CMR feature tracking)
title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) myocardial strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature tracking enables sensitive detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, factors associated with early post-infarction LV myocardial function following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain incompletely understood, particularly in the context of inflammation-related myocardial injury. The platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) which combines two routinely measured blood cell counts and may reflect the dynamic interplay between platelet recovery and inflammatory dynamics, has emerged as a potential biomarker of systemic inflammatory status. This study investigated the association between PWR and LV myocardial strain in patients with STEMI after PCI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 222 patients with STEMI who underwent CMR imaging within 1 week after PCI. Demographic information, laboratory test results, and CMR parameters were collected. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup, sensitivity and nonlinear analyses were performed to investigate the association between post-PCI PWR and CMR-derived LV myocardial strain.
RESULTS: Patients in the highest PWR quartile had significantly higher LV ejection fraction (LVEF) (53.4% vs. 45.0%, P<0.001) and a smaller median infarct size (IS) (11.9% vs. 18.8%, P=0.006) than those in the lowest quartile (Q1). In the fully adjusted logistic model, higher PWR was independently associated with lower odds of impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS) [odds ratio (OR) 0.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.05-0.30, P<0.001] and impaired global circumferential strain (GCS) (OR 0.18; 95% CI: 0.06-0.49; P=0.001), and with higher odds of preserved global radial strain (GRS) (OR 5.57; 95% CI: 2.06-15.06; P=0.001). RCS analysis showed a linear association between PWR and the odds of LV myocardial strain impairment. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses yielded similar associations.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher post-PCI PWR was independently associated with more favorable LV myocardial strain after PCI in patients with STEMI. As a routinely available ratio, PWR may complement the early description of myocardial strain impairment.
