title: Correlation between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and left ventricular myocardial strain in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a cardiac magnetic resonance feature-tracking study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) at high bleeding risk (HBR) are also at increased risk of ischemic events, making the optimal antiplatelet therapy challenging. Whether HBR identifies patients who may benefit from upfront aspirin omission at the time of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: In this study, we sought to evaluate whether HBR modifies the effect of aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI.
METHODS: The PREMIUM trial randomized patients with STEMI before primary PCI to low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin plus prasugrel. In the DAPT group, patients meeting Academic Research Consortium (ARC) for HBR criteria were permitted to discontinue aspirin at 3 months, whereas non-HBR patients were intended to continue DAPT for 12 months. This post hoc analysis assessed the primary outcome of a 12-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, or myocardial infarction and the major secondary outcome of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5 bleeding according to HBR status.
RESULTS: Among 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) met ARC-HBR criteria. HBR patients had higher rates of the primary outcome (16.2% vs 6.2%; HR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.05-3.52) and the major secondary outcome (10.9% vs 4.9%; HR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.65-3.14). The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy vs DAPT in 18.0% vs 14.5% of HBR patients (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.91-1.82) and 7.4% vs 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.01-2.37; P for interaction = 0.51). The major secondary outcome occurred in 9.2% vs 12.5% of HBR patients (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.46-1.11) and 3.8% vs 6.1% of non-HBR patients (HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.38-1.00; P for interaction = 0.67).
CONCLUSIONS: ARC-HBR identified patients with a substantially higher overall risk after primary PCI for STEMI, but did not identify a subgroup with a more favorable treatment effect of upfront aspirin omission. Clinically meaningful treatment-effect modification cannot be excluded, owing to limited precision. These findings do not support using HBR status alone to guide upfront aspirin omission and should be interpreted in the context of the low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan. (Prasugrel Monotherapy Following Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction [PREMIUM; NCT05709626]).

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial; 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) meeting ARC-HBR criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc and underpowered for interaction; low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan limits transportability.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc PREMIUM analysis found that ARC-HBR status did not identify patients in whom upfront aspirin omission worked differently after primary PCI for STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy vs DAPT in 18.0% vs 14.5% of HBR patients (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.91-1.82) and 7.4% vs 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.01-2.37; P for interaction = 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests whether HBR status can be used to select patients for aspirin-free strategies in STEMI, a live question for antithrombotic de-escalation.

journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
title: High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial.

abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis.
METHODS: We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression.
RESULTS: We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older.
CONCLUSION: Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.
title: Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention with balloon angioplasty and stent implantation is standard therapy for coronary artery disease, but accurate prediction of patient-specific procedural outcomes remains challenging.
CASE SUMMARY: Patient-derived imaging data were used to reconstruct three-dimensional coronary models, which were further translated into a three-dimensional-printed physical phantom and a finite element digital twin. The identical stent and balloon were deployed in the phantom; stent deployment was computationally simulated, and both were compared with the clinical optical coherence tomography.
DISCUSSION: Both platforms reproduced key procedural features. The phantom moderately underestimated, and the finite element model overestimated, the clinically observed lumen gain. These proof-of-concept findings support the technical feasibility of building patient-specific artificial twins, but quantitative accuracy will require further model refinement and validation before clinical use.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patient-specific models offer a means to visualize procedural characteristics and test alternative stent designs or deployment strategies outside the patient.
title: Patient-Specific Physical and Computational Models for Replicating Coronary Stent Deployment.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution.
CASE SUMMARY: An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium.
DISCUSSION: Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.
title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial bridge (MB) is largely considered a benign condition, though it may lead to myocardial ischemia because of coronary vessel compression. It is a known cause of sudden cardiac arrest/death in young athletes.
CASE SUMMARY: A 16-year-old boy athlete with asthma presented with exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and tachycardia following 3-mile races. Echocardiography showed a small atrial septal defect and normal coronary artery origins. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a left anterior descending MB. Stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging showed no inducible perfusion defects. Cardiac catheterization for intracoronary flow assessment demonstrated compromised coronary flow distal to the MB, with compression on intravascular ultrasound. Surgical unroofing of the MB allowed a safe return to competition.
DISCUSSION: Exhaustive workup and invasive assessment of intracoronary flow are invaluable to determine significant compression of a MB causing ischemia in athletes with exertional symptoms.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Exertional symptoms in athletes should be considered for advanced imaging to exclude significant lesions that compromise coronary flow.
title: Myocardial Bridge in High School Athlete With Exertional Symptoms: Innocent Bystander or Major Player?

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis.
RESULTS: Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897).
CONCLUSIONS: MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms.
KEY POINTS: Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.
title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Long-Term Outcomes in Stable Coronary Artery Disease: Extended Follow-Up of the COURAGE Randomized Trial.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle.
INTERVENTION: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time.
RESULTS: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of the randomised ISCHEMIA trial; 5179 participants, 1071 deaths, randomised at 320 sites in 37 countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Excludes left main disease, unacceptable angina and recent acute coronary syndrome, and the invasive strategy was not limited to symptomatic benefit; follow-up beyond the active trial phase relied on vital status ascertainment.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of ISCHEMIA to a median of 9 years found no significant long-term all-cause mortality difference between routine invasive and initial conservative management of chronic coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It settles the question of long-term survival for routine invasive management of stable high-risk chronic coronary disease and bears directly on guideline recommendations for revascularisation in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with a history of lymphoma may develop significant coronary artery disease (CAD), which may be treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet long term outcomes are not well characterized.
METHODS: We reviewed patients with a history of lymphoma undergoing PCI from our institutional PCI database and compared characteristics and outcomes to a cohort without cancer. Long-term mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE) (cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), target vessel revascularization (TVR)) were assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 11,953 patients identified, 83 (0.7%) had past or current lymphoma. Most had Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (n=23; 28.8%) or Hodgkin's Lymphoma (HL) (n=22; 27.%), and 31 (37.3%) presented with acute coronary syndrome. Lymphoma patients, as compared to non-lymphoma patients, were similar with respect to age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior MI, and prior PCI (all p=ns). The 1, 3, and 5-year survival rates were 90.5%, 69.5 %, and 52.5% in lymphoma patients as compared to 88.0%, 77.1%, and 66.7% in propensity matched non-lymphoma controls. Lymphoma was an independent predictor of mortality (OR 1.59; 95% CI 1.07-2.36, p=0.02) after multivariable adjustment. In propensity matched analysis over a median follow up of 4.2 years (IQR 1.28, 7.73), lymphoma was not independently associated with worse survival or MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with CAD undergoing PCI, <1% had previous or active lymphoma. Although lymphoma may appear predictive of mortality in regression models with multivariable adjustment, mortality and MACE rates are similar to propensity matched controls.
title: Long Term Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Lymphoma: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
Can Intravenous Cangrelor Protect the Myocardium in Infarction-related Cardiogenic Shock?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question.
METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered.
RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month.
CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified, not separately powered imaging substudy of a randomised trial; echocardiography in 208 enrolled and CMR in 93 enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small evaluable numbers (MVO evaluable in 60 patients), loss of imaging over follow-up and a hypothesis-generating design.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified imaging substudy of DAPT-SHOCK-AMI reporting lower acute microvascular obstruction and better functional recovery with cangrelor than crushed ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers a mechanistic signal that may inform the design of larger trials of intravenous P2Y12 inhibition in cardiogenic shock.

title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies.
METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina.
RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified second randomisation of a randomised trial at 17 centres in South Korea; 3048 patients (1525 combination, 1523 monotherapy).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a single country with a composite endpoint including soft components such as revascularisation and unstable angina hospitalisation.
appraisal.one_line: Second randomisation of Ez-PAVE found no difference in 3-year cardiovascular events between initial statin-ezetimibe combination and statin monotherapy within LDL-C targeting strategies.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs initial lipid-lowering regimen choice in secondary prevention, including patients after PCI.

title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Qiliqiangxin Capsule (QLQX) is a guideline-recommended adjunctive therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, but mechanisms underlying post-myocardial infarction heart failure (post-MI HF) remain incompletely defined, particularly gut-heart microbial metabolism.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize the gut microbial and fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) alterations associated with the cardioprotective effects of QLQX and to determine whether gut-associated factors contribute functionally to its therapeutic effects in post-MI HF.
METHODS: A rat model of post-MI HF was established by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. Cardiac function, ventricular remodeling, histopathological injury, and inflammatory indices were evaluated after QLQX treatment. An integrated analytical strategy comprising fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, targeted fecal SCFA quantification, untargeted fecal and myocardial metabolomics, myocardial transcriptomics, and targeted protein analyses was used to characterize gut and cardiac responses. A publicly available human ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction transcriptomic dataset was included for exploratory pathway-level comparison. Spearman correlation analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was performed to examine associations among microbial taxa, SCFAs, inflammatory markers, and cardiac functional indices. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to assess the structural plausibility of selected candidate interactions, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was performed to experimentally evaluate the predicted interaction between isobutyrate and JNK1. Antibiotic treatment and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) were further performed to evaluate the functional contribution and transferability of gut-associated fecal factors.
RESULTS: QLQX improved cardiac dysfunction, adverse ventricular remodeling, myocardial injury, and inflammatory responses in post-MI HF rats. Treatment reshaped the fecal microbial community and altered the fecal SCFA profile, including restoration of butyrate and isobutyrate. Selected SCFAs and bacterial taxa were associated with inflammatory markers and cardiac functional indices. Integrated omics and protein analyses further showed that these gut-associated alterations were accompanied by coordinated changes in myocardial cAMP, nuclear HDAC3 abundance, histone H3 acetylation, AMPK/mTOR signaling, and JNK/TGF-β related molecular indices. SPR analysis further demonstrated concentration-dependent binding of isobutyrate to JNK1, with an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of 5.89 × 10⁻⁵ M. Antibiotic treatment attenuated the therapeutic response to QLQX, whereas FMT from QLQX-treated donors partially transferred the protective phenotype, supporting a functional contribution of fecally transferable gut-associated factors.
CONCLUSION: QLQX ameliorated post-MI HF in association with remodeling of the gut microbial ecosystem, alterations in fecal SCFA profiles, and coordinated myocardial metabolic, epigenetic, and stress-signaling responses. The antibiotic and FMT experiments suggest that gut-associated factors partly contribute to the cardioprotective effects of QLQX. Butyrate and isobutyrate emerged as prioritized candidate metabolites, with SPR providing direct binding evidence for the isobutyrate-JNK1 interaction, although their broader causal roles and myocardial exposure require further validation.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
title: Qiliqiangxin Capsule ameliorates post-myocardial infarction heart failure: associations with gut microbiota remodeling, altered fecal short-chain fatty acid profiles, and myocardial HDAC3-associated histone acetylation and JNK/TGF-β-related signaling.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS.
METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.
INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.
FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised trial at 29 hospitals in five European countries; 605 patients randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307).
appraisal.main_limitation: The laboratory endpoint was analysed in only 56 (19%) and 68 (22%) patients, and the non-inferiority margin of 1 percentage point was narrow relative to the observed event rates.
appraisal.one_line: First randomised trial of P2Y12 strategies in AMI-CS: cangrelor gave better platelet inhibition than crushed ticagrelor but non-inferiority for the 30-day clinical endpoint was not shown.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary laboratory endpoint was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It provides the first randomised evidence on antiplatelet strategy in cardiogenic shock after MI, a setting where oral absorption is impaired, and defines the effect size for future trials.

title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal extended antiplatelet strategy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in patients with heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: In OPT-BIRISK, patients at high ischemic and bleeding risk who completed 9-12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) were randomized to clopidogrel plus placebo or aspirin for 9 months. This analysis compared treatments by recorded HF history. The primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding; the key secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebral events (MACCE).
RESULTS: Of 7,758 patients, 653 (8.4%) had HF history. Without HF, bleeding occurred in 83/3,565 (2.3%) monotherapy recipients and 118/3,540 (3.3%) DAPT recipients (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53-0.92). With HF, bleeding occurred in 12/308 (3.9%) and 9/345 (2.6%), respectively (HR 1.49, 95% CI 0.63-3.53). MACCE occurred in 90/3,565 (2.5%) versus 120/3,540 (3.4%) patients without HF (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.98) and 11/308 (3.6%) versus 16/345 (4.6%) patients with HF (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.36-1.66). Interaction P values were 0.1021 for bleeding and 0.9345 for MACCE.
CONCLUSIONS: Extended clopidogrel monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding in patients without a history of HF after PCI for ACS. No statistically significant treatment-by-HF interaction was observed for bleeding or MACCE, although HF-specific treatment effects remain inconclusive because of limited events.

abstract: Management of left ventricular (LV) thrombus in patients with high bleeding risk presents a therapeutic challenge. Warfarin has been the traditional anticoagulant used for left ventricular thrombus; direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives. We decided to study whether DOAC offered any advantage over Warfarin in this high-risk group of patients. Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we identified adult patients with LV thrombus and high bleeding-risk conditions (such as prior bleeds, CKD stages 3-5, Peptic ulcer disease) between 2013 and 2023. Patients were stratified into two cohorts: DOAC (n=3,762, matched n=2,208) and Warfarin (n=2,542, matched n=2,208). Outcomes assessed over one year included stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), cerebral infarction, mortality, acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding, systemic arterial embolism, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), major bleeding, embolic events, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); p-value <0.05 was considered significant. The mean age was 66.8 ± 14.4 for patients on DOAC and 63.9 ± 15.0 for those on warfarin. After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. At one year, DOAC use was associated with significantly lower risks of mortality (24.9% vs 29.3%, HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.75-0.94, p=0.003), systemic arterial embolism (1.9% vs 3.1%, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.88, p=0.008), intracranial hemorrhage (1.3% vs 2.3%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.90, p=0.016) and all-cause hospitalization was slightly lower with DOACs (72.0% vs 75.5%, HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p=0.001). No significant differences were observed for Stroke/TIA, cerebral infarction, or major bleeding. In conclusion, in this large propensity-matched cohort of patients with LV thrombus and high bleeding risk, use of DOACs demonstrated superior safety and effectiveness compared to warfarin, with reduced mortality, major bleeding, and thromboembolic complications. These findings support the use of DOACs in this high-risk population, though prospective randomized trials are warranted.

No significant differences were observed for Stroke/TIA, cerebral infarction, or major bleeding.

abstract: Enterococci are emerging as important pathogens in an era of an aging population with high healthcare and antibiotic exposure, along with an increasing utilization of prosthetic valves, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). Contemporary cohorts place enterococci among the three leading causes of infective endocarditis, with highest risk after TAVR, where enterococci account for 15% to 30% of cases in several registries. Enterococci cause a smaller proportion of CIED infections, but present late with lead or valve involvement. Enterococcus faecalis currently causes majority of enterococcal endocarditis. Its endovascular tropism, adhesion to damaged tissue and prosthetic surfaces, biofilm tolerance, and association with occult infective endocarditis during bacteremia make it the principal cardiac species of concern. Enterococcus faecium represents a distinct future threat. Hospital-adapted lineages combine prolonged intestinal colonization, environmental persistence, mobile resistance elements, ampicillin resistance, frequent vancomycin resistance, and biofilm capacity. Absolute burden may rise because the population-at risk-living with cardiac foreign devices is expanding. Future monitoring therefore requires linked, species-level surveillance that connects bacteremia, imaging, recurrence, resistance, and genomic data.
title: Enterococci as Emerging Pathogens in Infective Endocarditis and Cardiac Device Infections: Future Implications.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Right radial access is increasingly used as the sole secondary arterial access during minimalist transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, unfavorable right subclavian-aortic arch angulation or marked supra-aortic tortuosity may prevent spontaneous advancement of a radial pigtail catheter into the descending aorta.
TECHNIQUE: We describe the CAST (Capture-Assisted Safari Tracking) technique, a simple and reproducible maneuver for repositioning a radial pigtail catheter into the descending aorta using the Safari XS guidewire already in place during TAVI. The technique consists of four sequential steps: encounter, capture, pull-down, and release. The Safari XS guidewire acts as a traction rail, allowing the pigtail loop to be captured and guided in a controlled manner toward the descending aorta.
RESULT: This maneuver enables successful repositioning of the pigtail catheter into the descending aorta despite unfavorable supra-aortic anatomy, without requiring additional arterial access or dedicated equipment.
CONCLUSION: The CAST technique is a simple, reproducible, and equipment-free maneuver that can overcome selected difficulties encountered with radial access during minimalist TAVI. It may reduce repeated catheter and guidewire manipulation and avoid the need for additional femoral access.
title: The CAST technique: A novel capture-assisted Safari tracking maneuver for radial pigtail repositioning after TAVI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced renal function is linked to coronary calcification, which can limit stent expansion, and to contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CI-AKI). We examined renal function, optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined calcification and OCT measures of stent optimization in a Vietnamese provincial hospital.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, cross-sectional study included consecutive patients undergoing OCT-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (December 2023 to January 2026). eGFR was calculated with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation and CI-AKI defined by KDIGO creatinine criteria. Lesion-level associations were estimated by logistic or linear regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors, before and after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, smoking and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 300 patients, 309 procedures and 356 lesions. Mean eGFR was 79.7 ± 20.7 mL/min/1.73 m2 and 60 procedures (19.4%) had eGFR <60. Calcification was present in 235 lesions (66.0%). Each 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 lower eGFR was associated with calcification in unadjusted analysis (OR 1.19; 95% CI 1.03-1.38), but not after adjustment including age (OR 1.04; 0.88-1.22), whereas age remained associated (OR 1.46 per 10 years; 1.09-1.95). Mean minimum stent area was 5.75 ± 2.26 mm2 and was not correlated with eGFR (ρ=0.05; P=0.36); stent expansion ≥80% (87.4%) and procedural success (88.7%) were not associated with eGFR in crude or adjusted models. CI-AKI occurred in 8 of 206 procedures with paired creatinine (3.9%). Subgroups with eGFR <45 (22 lesions) and <30 (7 lesions) were small, and these analyses were exploratory.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cross-sectional study, the crude association between lower eGFR and OCT-defined calcification was largely explained by age. Under OCT guidance, renal function was not associated with stent optimization, and CI-AKI was infrequent. Prospective studies with larger advanced-CKD populations and a comparator arm are needed to establish whether OCT guidance offsets renal-related procedural disadvantage.
title: Renal Function, OCT-Defined Coronary Calcification and Stent Optimization in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract: Background Women with acute myocardial infarction are treated less invasively than men and die in hospital more often. Whether expanding acute coronary care narrows these differences is unknown. Methods We conducted a nationwide time-series study of the Brazilian public health system from 2008 through 2024. Outcomes were hospitalization with acute myocardial infarction (ICD-10 I21-I23) as the principal diagnosis, death with infarction as the underlying cause, and admission for infarction with coronary angioplasty. Rates were standardized by age and sex to the 2022 Census. Trends were estimated by Prais-Winsten regression, and change in the sex disparity was tested as a sex-by-year interaction. Results We analyzed 1,927,152 admissions, 1,513,299 deaths, and 543,290 angioplasty admissions. From 2008 to 2024 the age-standardized hospitalization rate rose from 59.8 to 111.7 per 100,000 in men and from 33.8 to 60.0 per 100,000 in women (annual percent change, +3.69% and +3.34%); mortality fell from 69.0 to 54.4 per 100,000 in men and from 46.8 to 34.1 per 100,000 in women (-1.44% and -1.92%, respectively); and angioplasty rose from 11.1 to 41.8 per 100,000 in men and from 5.0 to 20.1 per 100,000 in women (+8.22% and +8.17%, respectively). The men-to-women rate ratio stayed within narrow bands (hospitalization, 1.76 to 1.87; mortality, 1.47 to 1.60; angioplasty, 2.08 to 2.22), and no sex-by-year interaction was significant (p=0.20, p=0.10 and p=0.24). Among admitted patients, standardized in-hospital case fatality fell from 12.9% to 7.0% in men and from 16.1% to 8.3% in women. Women had higher case fatality in every year and every age group from 40 years onward; the adjusted relative risk of in-hospital death for men as compared with women was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.83 to 0.85) and did not change over time (p=0.89). Conclusions Brazil's public system expanded admission and angioplasty for myocardial infarction; outcomes improved in both sexes, but the gap between them did not close.
title: Sex Disparities in Acute Myocardial Infarction Hospitalization, Mortality, and Coronary Angioplasty in the Brazilian Public Health System: A Nationwide Time-Series Study From 2008 to 2024.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with a low socio-economic status (SES) exhibit high cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) and a high burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but they are under-recognized in clinical practice. In this study, we explored CVRFs and CVD in low-SES patients, and estimated the guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) prevalence for each CVD.
METHODS: Consecutive individuals with low-SES who attended the primary care and cardiology clinics within a single charitable medical center between 2024 and 2025 were retrospectively recruited. Data on SES, symptoms, CVRFs, CVDs, and treatment strategies were collected and analyzed descriptively. GDMT comprised class I medications reported by patients and documented in their medical records at the time of data collection for each CVD.
RESULTS: Among the 2374 patients, the mean age was 58.7 ± 6 years (57.2% females). Common CVRFs included hypertension (39.5%), diabetes (28.6%), and hyperlipidemia (27.4%). Common CVDs included coronary artery disease (CAD) (12.4%), heart failure (HF) (6%), and atrial fibrillation (AF) (1.7%) (mean ages: 55.79, 63.12, and 62.4 years, respectively). CAD patients had a high prevalence of acute coronary syndrome (74.2%), with most managed noninvasively (87%), but 38.5% received GDMT. HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) exceeded HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) (63.6% vs. 32.8%). Prevalent HF causes included CAD, hypertension, and valvular disease (33.6%, 27.3%, and 26.6%, respectively). GDMT rates for HFrEF and HFpEF were 18.7% and 34%, respectively. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 3.5 for AF patients, with 42.8% on GDMT (78% on warfarin).
CONCLUSIONS: Low-SES patients had a high prevalence of CVRF, where CAD, HF, and AF were most common. The patients were relatively young and managed conservatively, but GDMT rates were low. These findings may guide policymakers to improve cardiovascular care in low-SES individuals.

title: Cardiovascular diseases and guideline-directed medical therapy in low socio-economic status patients: A single center experience.

abstract: The European Resuscitation Council published its updated Guidelines for Resuscitation in 2025. The revised guidelines highlight advanced life support and post-resuscitation care, as well as post-resuscitation rehabilitation, as the third and fourth links in the updated Chain of Survival. In this review, we summarize the key updates and principal messages of the new guideline on advanced life support and post-resuscitation care. Although the Advanced Life Support guidelines do not represent a paradigm shift, they place a stronger emphasis on delivering high-quality, timely resuscitation. High-quality chest compressions remain the cornerstone of resuscitation, complemented by early, safe, and correctly performed defibrillation with minimal interruptions, appropriate drug administration, and prompt identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The updated guidelines also address emerging topics, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation-induced consciousness, the specific considerations for cardiac arrest occurring in closely monitored patients, and the introduction of physiology-guided resuscitation. Similarly, the post-resuscitation care guidelines introduce no major changes compared with previous recommendations. Instead, they reinforce the importance of delivering high-quality post-resuscitation care, with particular emphasis on neuroprotection. The key components of the stabilization, diagnostic, and optimization phases include an ABCDE approach to patient assessment, optimization of oxygenation, ventilation, and hemodynamic status, seizure management, prevention of fever during the first 72 hours after return of spontaneous circulation, and identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The indications for immediate coronary angiography following successful cardiopulmonary resuscitation have been further refined, and the guidelines also clarify the diagnostic approach when a non-cardiac cause of cardiac arrest is suspected. Greater emphasis is placed on multimodal neuroprognosis and post-resuscitation rehabilitation. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1810-1824.
title: [The novelties of adult advanced life support and post-resuscitation therapy according to the 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines].

abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL.
CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention.
REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.
authors: FRENCHIE-Lp(a) Investigators and the French Alliance for Cardiovascular Trials (FACT) investigators network
title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.

abstract:
AIM: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-coated balloon (DCB) is a coronary revascularization strategy; however, the prognostic impact of achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels after intervention remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to understand the association between LDL-C and the clinical outcomes in patients undergoing PCI with DCB.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent PCI with DCB (April 2019-March 2023) and had available 6-month LDL-C data. The clinical outcomes were assessed using a 6-month landmark approach. Patients were stratified by LDL-C level (＜70, 70-＜100, and ≥ 100 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and target lesion revascularization (TLR).
RESULTS: Among 320 patients, 47.8% had LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL, 31.6% had 70-＜100 mg/dL, and 20.6% had LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL. The cumulative incidence of MACE and TLR was significantly higher with increasing LDL-C levels (log-rank P = 0.006 and P = 0.023, respectively), whereas all-cause mortality and myocardial infarction did not differ significantly. In a multivariate Cox regression analysis, LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL independently predicted TLR (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.31; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-4.61; P = 0.02). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower achieved LDL-C levels and reduced rates of MACE and TLR.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI with DCB, higher achieved LDL-C levels, particularly LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL, were independently associated with an increased TLR risk, which primarily drove the observed difference in MACE. These findings highlight the importance of optimal LDL-C management following PCI with DCB.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) should target the saphenous vein graft (SVG) or the native coronary vessel in patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) who present with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is uncertain. We compared outcomes after culprit-lesion PCI of the SVG versus the native vessel in this population.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective analysis of a PCI database (January 2003-July 2025), we included patients with prior CABG presenting with NSTEMI whose culprit-lesion PCI was in an SVG or in a native vessel supplied by an SVG. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality at discharge and at 5 years.
RESULTS: Of 631 patients, 283 (44.8%) underwent native vessel PCI and 348 (55.2%) SVG PCI. SVG PCI patients had older grafts (13.5 vs 10.8 years, p < 0.001), more left main disease (29.9% vs 17.8%, p < 0.001), and more laser atherectomy (9.2% vs 1.8%, p < 0.001) and thrombectomy (10.4% vs 3.6%, p = 0.001); native vessel PCI more often involved bifurcation lesions (6.4% vs 0.6%, p < 0.001) and chronic total occlusions (3.6% vs 0%, p < 0.001). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between SVG and native vessel PCI at discharge (6.9% vs 3.5%, p = 0.063) or at 5 years (47.5% [95% CI 40.3-54.3] vs 45.0% [95% CI 37.5-52.2]; log-rank p = 0.236), nor did in-hospital complications.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, in-hospital and long-term mortality did not differ significantly between SVG and native vessel PCI. Because target-vessel selection was not randomized and its rationale was not captured, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not alone guide target-vessel choice.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Clinical outcomes of native vessel versus saphenous vein graft percutaneous coronary intervention in coronary artery bypass graft patients presenting with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: While Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) is a recognized driver of cardiovascular disease, its specific prognostic impact on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) in young adults presenting with Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) remains poorly defined. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association and clinical consequences of MetS on primary outcomes, including MACE, in this increasingly affected demographic.
METHODS: Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261423823), a systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and CENTRAL (initiation to June 2026) identified observational studies on young adults (younger than 45 or 50 years) with ACS and MetS defined by validated criteria. Data on baseline characteristics and primary outcomes-including MACE, recurrent myocardial infarction (re-MI), and stroke-were extracted. Pooled Risk Ratios (RR) were estimated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Four high-quality studies encompassing 3,691,728 participants were included. MetS was associated with an approximate two-fold increase in MACE risk (RR: 1.93; 95% CI: 1.83-2.03). Elevated risks were also observed for re-MI (RR: 2.08; 95% CI: 1.17-3.68) and stroke (RR: 2.33; 95% CI: 1.38-3.91). Subgroup analysis successfully explained initial heterogeneity in stroke (I2 = 0% in medium-term follow-up) and re-MI through follow-up duration and diagnostic criteria. The overall certainty of evidence was graded as Moderate for all primary outcomes under the GRADE framework.
CONCLUSIONS: MetS is a significant independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in young ACS survivors. These findings underscore the necessity for early risk stratification and aggressive metabolic management to mitigate the nearly two-fold increase in clinical risk.
title: The impact of metabolic syndrome on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in young adults with acute coronary syndrome: a GRADED systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the diagnostic value of the Residual Cholesterol Inflammatory Index (RCII) for assessing coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to provide evidence for clinical risk stratification and individualized treatment.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on 351 patients diagnosed with PCAD who underwent PCI at Nantong First People's Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were divided into four groups (low, medium, high, and extremely high RCII) based on RCII quartiles. Baseline characteristics, laboratory parameters, and coronary angiography data were collected. Coronary lesion severity was evaluated using the Gensini score. Associations between RCII and coronary lesion severity were analyzed using the Kruskal‑Wallis H test, χ² test, multiple linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.
RESULTS: With the increase in RCII levels, the Gensini score, the rate of three-vessel coronary artery disease, and the incidence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in PCAD patients undergoing PCI increased significantly (all P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression analysis, after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors, showed that RCII exhibited a significant non-linear (inverted U-shaped) association with Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with a positive linear relationship predominantly observed in the low-to-moderate RCII range (≤ 40, accounting for 94% of the population) (unstandardized regression coefficient B = 0.52, 95% confidence interval 0.338-0.701, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis revealed a significant inverted U-shaped nonlinear association between RCII and Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with an inflection point threshold of approximately 40. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of RCII for assessing severe coronary artery disease (Gensini score ≥ 60) was 0.698, for three-vessel coronary artery disease was 0.723, and for AMI was 0.598, all of which were significantly higher than those of residual cholesterol (RC) alone (all P < 0.05 for DeLong test).
CONCLUSION: RCII demonstrates moderate predictive ability for coronary lesion severity in PCAD patients undergoing PCI, serving as an independently associated indicator for severe coronary lesions. Its predictive performance is superior to RC alone, making it a potential auxiliary biomarker for risk assessment. While its clinical application value still needs to be further verified in large-sample, multi-center, prospective cohort studies.
title: The diagnostic value of residual cholesterol inflammatory index for coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) requires rapid identification in the emergency department (ED). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation systems have shown strong diagnostic accuracy, no multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) has evaluated their clinical impact. This protocol describes a RCT for assessing whether real-time AI-ECG can be safely integrated into routine emergency care for undifferentiated chest pain.
METHODS: ROMIAE-2 is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication conducted at 12 academic tertiary EDs in South Korea. A total of 4,670 adults with acute chest pain will be randomized 1:1 to AI-ECG-guided or standard care. In the intervention arm, a deep learning algorithm (AiTiAMI Ver 2.00.00) will analyze the initial 12- lead ECG and generate an AMI probability score, which is combined with the HEART score to classify patients into four integrated risk categories for clinical decision-making. The primary outcome is 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), assessed using a noninferiority framework with a 3.0% margin. The trial will be powered at 80% with a onesided significance level of 0.025. Secondary outcomes include missed AMI at the index visit, ED length of stay, early discharge, 7-day ED revisit, hospital admission, hospital length of stay, AI-ECG diagnostic performance, additional testing, and direct medical costs. Clinical endpoints, including MACE and AMI, will be adjudicated by two emergency medicine specialists blinded to the group allocation.
DISCUSSION: ROMIAE-2 will provide randomized evidence on whether integrating AI-ECG into routine emergency care can preserve patient safety while improving efficiency in patients with undifferentiated chest pain.
title: Study protocol for Rule-Out Acute Myocardial Infarction Using Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram 2 (ROMIAE-2) in patients with chest pain: a multicenter randomized noninferiority trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with increased mortality. Despite substantial advances in the management of both conditions, the population-level mortality burden involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate national trends and disparities in mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025 using CDC WONDER data, forecasts were generated through 2030, with exploratory projections extending through 2040, stratified by DM type, age, sex, and race and ethnicity.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of U.S. national mortality data from 1999 to 2025 was conducted to identify deaths among adults aged ≥ 25 years in which AMI; ICD-10 code I21 was the underlying cause and DM; ICD-10 codes E10-E14 was a contributing cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and crude mortality rates (CMRs) were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Time-series methods were used to forecast mortality through 2030, with exploratory projections through 2040 .
RESULTS: Trend analyses were conducted using observed mortality data from 1999 to 2025, whereas projections extended from 2026 to 2040. A total of 762,802 deaths were attributed to AMI, with DM documented as a contributing cause, among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025. Overall mortality significantly declined (AAMR: 18.9 to 9.16; AAPC: -3.05; 95% CI: -3.3 to -2.9; P < 0.001). Males showed higher AAMRs (23.32 in 1999 to 12.72 in 2025) when compared to females (15.74 to 6.2). Older adults aged ≥ 65 years carried the greatest mortality burden, with CMR decreasing from 72.9 in 1999 to 32.4 in 2025. NH Blacks had the highest AAMR (29.95 to 12.68). Forecasts projected a decline in overall AAMR from 8.17 in 2026 to 6.72 in 2030. Exploratory projections suggested a further decline to 3.08 by 2040, although substantial uncertainty surrounded these long-term estimates. The AAMR for deaths involving AMI as the underlying cause and T2DM as a contributing cause increased from 3.34 in 1999 to 4.15 in 2025, whereas the corresponding AAMR for T1DM decreased from 1.90 to 0.23.
CONCLUSION: Mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause has significantly declined and is projected to continue declining through 2040. Disparities among males, NH Blacks and older adults require refined strategies to improve outcomes.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02124-x.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
title: Trends in acute myocardial infarction mortality with diabetes mellitus as a contributing cause of death in the United States, 1999-2025, with forecasts through 2030 and exploratory projections for 2031-2040.

abstract: As the number of patients supported with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) continues to rise, vascular surgeons are challenged to adopt alternative endovascular access strategies to manage life-threatening ischemic or hemorrhagic complications. We present the case of a pediatric patient maintained on central venoarterial ECMO who developed a left hemothorax in impending cardiorespiratory collapse. A 11F Y-connector was fashioned into a Berlin arterial cannula (Berlin Heart GmbH) for endovascular access to the mid-ascending aorta and was used to treat proximal subclavian artery extravasation. This approach demonstrates the utility of maintaining arterial outlet pressures while simultaneously providing endovascular access to urgently treat patients on ECMO.
journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
journal_abbrev: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
title: Repair of iatrogenic subclavian injury through paracorporeal endovascular access.

abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old man with prior endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of the abdominal aorta complicated by type Ia endoleak requiring two proximal aortic cuffs. Ten years later, he underwent transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for severe aortic stenosis. During the delivery of the transcatheter aortic valve replacement device, one of the aortic cuffs was displaced into the distal thoracic aorta. This case report describes a rare complication of delayed device displacement during TAVR and demonstrates a novel strategy for endovascular salvage. It highlights the opportunity for endovascular repair during TAVR planning in patients with prior aortic stent grafts. In addition, close multidisciplinary collaboration is valuable for managing unexpected device interactions.
journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
journal_abbrev: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
title: Novel endovascular management of a displaced aortic endograft component during transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

abstract: Iatrogenic popliteal artery injury is a rare but severe complication of knee arthroplasty. A 75-year-old woman developed massive bleeding and acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. Angiography showed severe popliteal flow impairment with thrombus and absent distal runoff. Because bleeding was controlled and guidewire crossing appeared feasible, an endovascular-first strategy was chosen. After successful crossing, an intravascular ultrasound scan confirmed severe arterial wall disruption and an adequate distal landing zone. VIABAHN stent grafts excluded the injured segment, and tibial thrombus aspiration restored distal perfusion. The patient was discharged without gait impairment. Endovascular-first treatment may be effective in selected patients.
journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
journal_abbrev: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
title: Endovascular repair of iatrogenic popliteal artery injury with acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.

abstract: Takayasu arteritis is a rare large-vessel vasculitis that predominantly affects the aorta and its major branches. Although stenotic lesions and fibrotic wall thickening are common, extensive aortic calcification with mesenteric involvement is exceedingly rare. Diffuse calcification of the aorta poses significant challenges for both open and endovascular treatment. We report the case of Takayasu arteritis with near-circumferential calcification of the entire aorta and most visceral branches, successfully managed with intravascular lithotripsy.
journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
journal_abbrev: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
title: Intravascular lithotripsy for calcific stenosis of the abdominal aorta in a patient with Takayasu arteritis.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transient ischaemic attack after patent foramen ovale closure presents diagnostic challenges.
PATIENT INFORMATION: A 17-year-old male with homozygous MTHFR polymorphism underwent successful patent foramen ovale closure under nitrous oxide anaesthesia.
CLINICAL FINDINGS: Post-procedure, he experienced neurological deterioration and loss of consciousness with elevated homocysteine levels (43 mmol/L).
CONCLUSION: Nitrous oxide-induced methionine synthase inhibition may precipitate transient ischaemic events in genetically susceptible patients.
title: Transient neurological deterioration after patent foramen ovale closure associated with nitrous oxide exposure in an adolescent with homozygous MTHFR polymorphism.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mehran 2 score was developed to predict contrast-associated acute kidney injury after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Its prognostic value beyond renal complications remains uncertain. We evaluated the association of preprocedural (model 1) and postprocedural (model 2) Mehran 2 scores with renal outcomes and 1-year mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 1025 patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Both scores were calculated and categorized into four risk groups. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality, while secondary outcomes included contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) and dialysis requirement. Prognostic performance was assessed using multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.
RESULTS: CIN occurred in 105 patients (10.2%), dialysis was required in 21 (2.0%), and 102 (10.0%) died within 1 year. All outcomes increased progressively across Mehran 2 risk categories (P < 0.001). Both scores were independently associated with 1-year mortality [model 1: adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.59, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.37-1.84; model 2: adjusted OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.41-1.83; both P < 0.001]. The area under the curves (AUCs) for mortality were 0.794 and 0.806, respectively, with a modest improvement for model 2 (ΔAUC: 0.012; P = 0.049). Higher scores were associated with significantly lower 365-day survival (log-rank P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Both Mehran 2 models were associated with renal complications and 1-year mortality in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. The preprocedural model may facilitate early cardiorenal risk stratification, whereas the postprocedural model provides only modest incremental discrimination. Further validation against established mortality risk scores is needed.
title: Prognostic impact of the Mehran 2 risk score on 1-year mortality after acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited.
METHODS: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide, nonrandomized study in the Netherlands; 144 patients in the intervention group and 87 in the conventional group (NCT04620070).
appraisal.main_limitation: Nonrandomised allocation by HEMS capability, so residual confounding and selection are likely, and the sample is small.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide Dutch non-randomised comparison of prehospital ECPR delivered by physician-staffed helicopter services versus conventional care in young adults with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, reporting higher survival to discharge with ECPR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the main non-randomised signal for prehospital ECPR in the NEJM, relevant to systems-of-care design for refractory arrest alongside the randomised ECPR trials.

journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).
journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
