RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).
journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe mechanical hemolysis following the use of a paravalvular leak occluder plug is a challenging complication, particularly for patients with multiple comorbidities who face prohibitive risks with repeat surgery.
CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old multimorbid man with end-stage renal disease presented with severe microangiopathic hemolytic anemia after transcatheter paravalvular leak closure. Ten months earlier, he had undergone aortic and mitral valve replacements and coronary bypass, complicated by a difficult recovery requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support with an Impella. Now, to minimize the operative risk and avoid the difficult postoperative course experienced after the previous surgery requiring mechanical circulatory support, a modified, infrequent surgical strategy was used: On-pump, beating-heart redo mitral valve replacement with extraction of the occluder plug. It successfully circumvented global myocardial ischemia and simplified complex redo surgery. Postoperatively, the hematologic parameters normalized within days.
DISCUSSION: This personalized, risk-adapted surgical strategy mitigates operative risk in a high-risk patient, achieving rapid, definitive resolution of hemolytic anemia.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Eliminating the source of mechanical hemolysis results in rapid normalization of laboratory parameters within days. On-pump beating-heart surgery is a valuable strategy to simplify complex redo procedures while minimizing high perioperative risk.
title: On-Pump Beating-Heart Redo Mitral Valve Surgery: A Personalized, Risk-Adapted Surgical Strategy for Plug-Induced Hemolysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is widely used as temporary mechanical circulatory support in patients with refractory heart failure complicated by cardiogenic shock. However, its use is generally limited to short-term therapy because of device-related complications.
CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy receiving guideline-directed medical therapy and cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation developed cardiogenic shock refractory to inotropic therapy, requiring IABP implantation. Mechanical circulatory support was maintained for 293 days, including 291 days as a bridge to heart transplantation and 2 days after transplantation.
DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that prolonged IABP support is feasible when combined with transition to a left subclavian approach, serial device replacement, and meticulous multidisciplinary management.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In carefully selected patients, prolonged IABP support, combined with individualized device management and multidisciplinary care, may provide sustained clinical stabilization and serve as an effective bridge to heart transplantation.
title: 293-Day Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support as a Bridge to Transplantation in Refractory Heart Failure.

abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine whether visual or quantitative mitral annular calcification (MAC) burden on routine non-contrast, non-ECG-gated chest computed tomography (CT) is associated with permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation for advanced atrioventricular (AV) block. MAC has been linked to conduction disturbances after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Whether MAC visible on routine chest CT is associated with significant AV conduction disease in non-TAVI patients remains uncertain. In this retrospective single-center case-control study, 39 consecutive patients who underwent PPM implantation for symptomatic advanced AV block and had non-contrast chest CT were compared with 39 age- and sex-matched controls without AV block or prior PPM. MAC was graded visually by annular circumference involvement and quantified using an Agatston-based score. Visual MAC was more prevalent in the PPM (+) group than in the PPM (-) group (22 of 39 [56%] vs. 12 of 39 [31%]; P = 0.039). The prevalence of PPM implantation increased across visual MAC categories, from 39% with no MAC and 48% with MAC involving < 1/3 of the annular circumference to 80% with MAC involving 1/3 to 1/2 and 100% with MAC involving > 1/2 of the annular circumference (P = 0.007). Quantitative MAC categories also differed (44%, 33%, and 78% PPM implantation for MAC scores of 0, 1 to 400, and > 400, respectively; P = 0.022). In multivariable analysis, MAC score > 400 remained independently associated with PPM implantation (odds ratio: 24.6; 95% confidence interval: 1.63 to 370.96; P = 0.02).Visual and quantitative MAC burden on routine non-contrast chest CT were associated with PPM implantation for advanced AV block. Structured assessment and reporting of marked MAC may provide a clinically useful marker in patients with suspected AV conduction disease.
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
title: Mitral annular calcification on routine Non-ECG Gated Chest CT Is associated with advanced atrioventricular block requiring permanent pacing: A case-control study.

abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications.
RECENT FINDINGS: Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.
title: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The electrocardiogram reflects the vectorial summation of myocardial injury, yet the mechanisms underlying some myocardial infarction (MI) patterns remain uncertain. We hypothesized that the precordial swirl pattern, traditionally attributed to LAD occlusion proximal to the first septal (S1) branch, may instead reflect an interaction between transmural and subendocardial injury.
METHODS: We analyzed 105 prospectively enrolled patients with first anterior ST-elevation MI treated with successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) 3-7 days later. The precordial swirl phenotype was defined as ST elevation in V1-V2 with ST depression in V5 and/or V6. Segmental late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) transmurality, edema, LAD occlusion relative to S1, and continuous lateral ST deviation were analyzed.
RESULTS: Twenty-two patients (21.0%) had the phenotype. Median patient-level mean LGE transmurality was lower (33.3% [30.8-40.6] vs 39.6% [33.3-46.9]; P = 0.008), and the proportion of involved segments with <50% transmural LGE was higher (71.4% [55.6-87.5] vs 55.6% [40.0-66.7]; P = 0.003). Proximal-to-S1 occlusion was similar (36.4% vs 36.6%; P = 1.000). More negative V5-V6 ST deviation correlated with lower LGE transmurality (ρ = 0.310; P = 0.002) but not basal-mid septal LGE burden (ρ = 0.096; P = 0.341). After adjustment for infarct size, sex, and hypertension, the association with the fraction of segments exhibiting ≥50% transmural LGE persisted (β = -10.89 percentage points; P = 0.039).
CONCLUSIONS: Precordial swirl was associated with less transmural LGE, without detectable enrichment for proximal-to-S1 occlusion or greater septal injury, although moderate anatomical differences cannot be excluded. These findings are compatible with a contribution from heterogeneous transmural injury to the surface ST field.
title: Swirling vectors: The myocardial substrate of the precordial swirl pattern in anterior myocardial infarction.

abstract: Triple-rule-out computed tomography angiography (TRO-CTA) was introduced to evaluate acute coronary syndrome (ACS), pulmonary embolism (PE), and acute aortic syndrome (AAS) in a single emergency department (ED) examination. Early single-pass protocols were limited by compromise bolus timing, retrospective gating over a long z-axis, high radiation and iodine burden, and inconsistent coronary image quality, and routine use appropriately declined as dedicated coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and high-sensitivity troponin algorithms matured. A subset of patients nevertheless remains difficult to triage: older or multimorbid patients with overlapping symptoms, nonspecific troponin or D-dimer elevation, or limited access to subspecialty interpretation. Wide-detector and high-pitch acquisition, low-tube-voltage imaging, iterative and deep-learning reconstruction, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based motion correction have reduced the penalties that constrained early protocols, and sequential multiphase acquisition images each territory within its own enhancement window from one coordinated injection. This review reappraises TRO-CTA from a contemporary cardiovascular CT perspective. Dedicated coronary, pulmonary, or aortic CTA remains preferred when one diagnosis is dominant, and selective TRO-CTA is confined to stable patients with persistent diagnostic ambiguity after first-tier evaluation. For contemporary sequential multiphase TRO-CTA, evidence remains largely limited to single-center feasibility and image-quality studies; robust prospective comparative data on diagnostic timeliness, missed diagnoses, downstream testing, and clinical outcomes remain lacking. Value is additionally context-dependent, varying with ED case-mix, scanner platform, availability of expert interpretation, local disease prevalence, and access to staged reassessment. Contemporary TRO-CTA is therefore a selective, institution-calibrated option requiring explicit activation criteria, demonstrated coronary image quality, and prospective multicenter evaluation.
title: Triple-rule-out computed tomography (CT) angiography revisited: selective contemporary use enabled by sequential acquisition and modern cardiovascular computed tomography (CT).

Associations of clinical frailty and the triglyceride-glucose index with major adverse cardiovascular events in older adults with acute coronary syndrome in southern Vietnam: a prospective multicentre cohort study.
Transradial access in patients with Raynaud's phenomenon: when 'radial-first' requires nuance.

abstract: The role of revascularization and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with acute coronary syndrome is well established. However, the incremental value of revascularization over guideline-directed medical therapy is controversial. Currently available data supports the use of PCI to improve angina and quality of life for chronic coronary disease and heart failure (HF). However, there is insufficient data to support revascularization with PCI to improve mortality, reduce cardiovascular events, or improve ejection fraction over medical therapy alone. Additional trials are necessary to identify HF patients who may benefit from revascularization, and the optimal revascularization strategy for this population.
title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Heart Failure due to Coronary Artery Disease.

abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading etiology of heart failure (HF) and serves as a significant therapeutic target to ameliorate HF-associated morbidity and mortality. Key management considerations include pharmacologic treatment, electrophysiological devices, and coronary revascularization, aimed toward preventing CAD progression, left ventricular remodeling, sudden death, and reinfarction. The optimal revascularization strategy for patients with CAD and HF who are surgical candidates requires careful assessment of each patients' unique risk/benefit profile and individual preferences. Several novel pharmacologic agents are in development with hopes of adding to the armamentarium of treatment of CAD and HF.
title: Coronary Artery Disease and Heart Failure: Medical Management and Future Direction.

abstract: The review discusses angiographic and hemodynamic features of invasive and computed tomography coronary angiography, which inform diagnosis, prognosis, and coronary revascularization in patients with systolic heart failure.
title: Coronary Angiography in the Evaluation of Systolic Heart Failure.

abstract: Patients with concomitant severe aortic stenosis and significant coronary artery disease present a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in clinical practice. There are no clear-cut guidelines as to the timing of revascularization in these patients who are referred for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This article aims to show that in patients without high-grade proximal coronary artery disease, revascularization after TAVR is safe, feasible, and practical. Additionally, the use of preoperative TAVR computed tomographic angiography might be used in both intermediate and high-risk patients rather than invasive coronary angiography to assess for significant proximal coronary artery disease to help guide the timing of revascularization.
title: Coronary Artery Revascularization in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: Coronary artery obstruction is a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This risk increases in TAVR-valve-in-valve procedure. Several anatomic risk factors were described in many studies to identify the predictive elements of coronary artery occlusion on computed tomography cardiac scan. Rescue percutaneous coronary intervention was the first approach described to treat this complication with a high mortality rate. Later on, preventive chimney stenting technique was evaluated and results showed that is a safe and effective strategy but it leads to a difficult coronary access later. New preventive techniques are being evaluated recently (Basilica and Shorctut).
title: Coronary Risk in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement, Overview of Data, Challenges, and Best Practices.

abstract: Valvular heart disease is an uncommon but high-risk cause of cardiogenic shock requiring rapid, multidisciplinary management aimed at bridging patients to definitive surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Early comprehensive Doppler echocardiography is essential, as clinical signs may be subtle. Distinguishing decompensated chronic valvular disease from acute unstable lesions guides urgency and treatment strategy. Medical stabilization and mechanical circulatory support vary markedly between stenotic and regurgitant lesions, and standard shock therapies may be harmful in specific contexts. Transcatheter approaches are preferred when feasible, though their expanding use introduces added complexity in cardiac intensive care.
title: Valvular Shock in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Perioperative Care for Transcatheter Valve Interventions.
The PORTICO IDE Trial: A New Kid on the Block.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.
METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).
title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Staging Cardiac Damage in Aortic Stenosis: A Better Map, But Not Yet a Compass.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline).
RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121).
CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.
title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch After TAVR: The Durability of Clinical Benefit.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.
METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.
authors: EARLY TAVR Trial Executive Committee and Study Investigators
title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
Tailoring Early Interventional Approach in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis: When Might Early AVR Be Too Late?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.
METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.
title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
Paravalvular Regurgitation After TAVR in Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: How Much Is Too Much?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.
METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs).
RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of the CMS MedPAR database (2017-2023); 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative claims data in patients aged 65 years or older with residual confounding by anatomy and valve type, and no echocardiographic detail.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare propensity-matched comparison of off-label TAVR versus SAVR for isolated native aortic regurgitation, with early advantages and later repeat-replacement signal for TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years, TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31).
appraisal.why_it_matters: TAVR for pure aortic regurgitation is off-label and unsupported by randomised data, so a large comparative analysis informs a decision that currently lacks trial evidence.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.
title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis: Is it Time to Refine Our Classification Before We Randomize?
Sutureless Surgical Valve-in-Frame After SURPLUS for Failed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Mavacamten for Refractory Dynamic Intraventricular Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
TEE Artifact Reduction With Positional and Ventilatory Modification During M-TEER.
Prosthesis Infolding During Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement.
Left atrial appendage closure, direct oral anticoagulants or warfarin in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.

abstract: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is a chronic, progressive, and degenerative process characterized by calcium deposition along the mitral annulus. This leads to stiffening and distortion of normal mitral annular architecture and ultimately MAC-related valvular dysfunction, which can manifest as mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, or mixed valvular disease. Due to its anatomic complexity, transcatheter and surgical interventions for MAC carry significant procedural challenges. As such, multi-modality imaging and multi-disciplinary heart team discussions are critical in MAC evaluation and procedural planning. This review summarizes the epidemiology and pathophysiology of MAC, highlights the critical role of multimodality imaging in the evaluation and procedural planning of MAC, and reviews established transcatheter mitral valve procedures and surgical options for managing MAC, MAC-related valvular dysfunction, and potential complications.
title: Mitral annular calcification.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To derive and internally validate a mortality score (ECMO-PoCS) for use at venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) implantation for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS), hypothesizing that a few implantation-time variables would discriminate in-hospital mortality better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), or pre-ECMO lactate.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 149 consecutive adults receiving VA-ECMO for PCS (2007-2024), excluding 7 bridged directly to transplantation.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hospital mortality was 65.8% and 1-year survival 33.4%. A 4-variable logistic model (age, pre-ECMO lactate, peripheral artery disease [PAD], and any preoperative right ventricular [RV] dysfunction) was fitted in 133 complete cases; PAD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 4.58; p = 0.022) and RV dysfunction (adjusted OR = 3.16; p = 0.020) were independently associated with mortality. In 130 patients with all comparators, ECMO-PoCS (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.715) discriminated better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) (0.583; DeLong p = 0.043) and lactate alone (0.601; p = 0.030) but not significantly better than APACHE II (0.610; p = 0.13); adding these variables to APACHE II increased its AUC to 0.727 (likelihood ratio p = 0.002). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.687 and the shrinkage factor 0.82. A 0- to 5-point score defined low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (mortality 23.1%, 63.6%, and 86.0%, respectively; trend p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-PoCS, based on 4 variables available at implantation, discriminated in-hospital mortality better than EuroSCORE II and lactate alone and added information to APACHE II. Internally validated only, it is intended for risk description, research stratification, and benchmarking, not for decisions to initiate or withdraw support, pending external validation.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
title: The ECMO-PoCS Score: Derivation and Internal Validation of an Implantation-Time Model for In-Hospital Mortality in Postcardiotomy Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for refractory cardiocirculatory failure but carries a high bleeding risk, partly due to acquired von Willebrand syndrome (aVWS). With limited evidence-based treatments, von Willebrand factor (VWF) is often used off-label. This study examines nationwide use of VWF in VA-ECMO patients with aVWS in Germany and compares bleeding, thromboembolic events, and survival between treated and untreated patients.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study based on reimbursement data (2019-2023).
SETTING: Multi-institutional analysis of adult VA-ECMO cases treated in German hospitals.
PARTICIPANTS: 530 adult patients supported with VA-ECMO and diagnosed with aVWS.
INTERVENTIONS: Administration of any dose of VWF during VA-ECMO support versus no VWF treatment.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 530 patients, 389 (73%) received VWF across 35 of 71 centers contributing patients. Intracranial hemorrhage occurred less frequently in the VWF group (8% v 15%, p = 0.0238). However, haemothorax (37% v 20%, p = 0.0028) was more common with VWF. Thromboembolic events did not differ between groups. ICU LOS was shorter in VWF-treated patients (14 v 18 days, p = 0.0168). The 90-day survival was numerically higher in the VWF group but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.188).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of VA-ECMO patients with aVWS, VWF was frequently used and associated with lower ICH rates and shorter intensive care unit length of stay, there was no evidence of increased thromboembolic events, but higher rates of other bleeding complications. Prospective randomized trials are warranted to clarify the impact of VWF on clinical outcomes.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
title: Use of von Willebrand Factor in VA-ECMO‒Associated Acquired von Willebrand Syndrome: A Nationwide Retrospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted PCI (R-PCI) reduces measured radiation exposure to the primary operator, but procedural and patient-radiation benefits over manual PCI (M-PCI) remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To compare procedural/PCI time, fluoroscopy time, contrast volume, air kerma, and dose-area product between R-PCI and M-PCI after incorporation of randomized evidence.
METHODS: Randomized and nonrandomized comparative studies of adults undergoing PCI were included. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Mean differences (MDs) were calculated as M-PCI minus R-PCI. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I; certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Twelve studies, including 2 randomized trials, contributed data. No primary pooled outcome differed significantly: procedural/PCI time, MD -3.90 min (95% CI: -16.15 to 8.35); fluoroscopy time, 0.17 min (95% CI: -2.61 to 2.95); contrast volume, 7.79 mL (95% CI: -3.08 to 18.66); air kerma, 232.01 mGy (95% CI: -145.67 to 609.70); and dose-area product, 31.31 dGy·cm2 (95% CI: -49.45 to 112.07). Heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 72%-93%). A direct-report-only analysis favored R-PCI for contrast volume (MD: 17.76 mL; 95% CI: 4.62-30.90), but other sensitivity analyses did not materially change interpretation. Certainty was very low for all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: R-PCI has not shown consistent patient procedural or radiation benefit. Operator protection is supported descriptively but was not pooled; contrast reduction appeared only in sensitivity analysis. Future trials should assess patient benefit and team-wide occupational exposure.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Robotic-assisted versus manual percutaneous coronary intervention after contemporary randomized evidence: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of patient-level procedural and radiation outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women are underrepresented in cardiovascular clinical trials and evidence regarding sex-specific long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between patient sex and duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with the 10-year prognosis of patients enrolled in the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ISAR-SAFE trial.
METHODS: This post-hoc analysis included 1,871 patients from centers that participated in the ISAR-SAFE trial and agreed to collect 10-year follow-up data. In the ISAR-SAFE trial, a 6-month DAPT duration was compared with a 12-month DAPT regimen in patients treated with drug-eluting stents (DES). The primary endpoint of the present study was all-cause death at 10 years.
RESULTS: Compared to men, women were older (69.0 ± 9.7 vs. 64.8 ± 10.4 years, P < 0.001), had lower body weight (72.1 ± 14.2 vs. 84.8 ± 13.5 Kg, P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (93.2% vs. 89.3%, P = 0.031) and dyslipidemia (85.1% vs. 77.9%, P = 0.003). The 10-year mortality was 11.9% in women and 9.3% in men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.28 [95% confidence interval 0.91-1.81], P = 0.156). The 10-year mortality was 10.1% in the 6-month DAPT arm and 9.6% in the 12-month DAPT arm (HR 1.06 [0.79-1.42], P = 0.685). There was no significant interaction between sex and DAPT duration with respect to mortality. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR per 1 year increase 1.08 [1.06-1.09]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI with DES implantation, neither patient sex nor duration of DAPT regimen were independently associated with 10-year all-cause mortality after adjustment for relevant clinical covariates.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post-hoc analysis of the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled ISAR-SAFE trial; 1,871 patients with 10-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post-hoc analysis restricted to participating centres, with limited power for sex-by-treatment interaction.
appraisal.one_line: Post-hoc ISAR-SAFE analysis finding no association of sex or 6-month versus 12-month DAPT duration with 10-year all-cause mortality after DES implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 10-year mortality was 11.9% in women and 9.3% in men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.28 [95% confidence interval 0.91-1.81], P = 0.156). The 10-year mortality was 10.1% in the 6-month DAPT arm and 9.6% in the 12-month DAPT arm (HR 1.06 [0.79-1.42], P = 0.685).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It provides rare 10-year randomised-cohort follow-up on short versus standard DAPT duration and on sex differences after PCI.

journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Impact of patient sex and dual antiplatelet therapy duration on 10-year mortality following percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents: A post-hoc analysis of the ISAR-SAFE trial.

abstract: To investigate whether pre-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical metrics are associated with post-TAVR pulmonary hypertension (PH) with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). In this post-hoc analysis of a prospective single-center registry (Invasive PPM Registry; UMIN-CTR: 000054628), 97 patients undergoing TAVR with complete CT, echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamics were evaluated. Prespecified CT metrics included main, left and right pulmonary artery diameters, right ventricle/left ventricle ratio (RV/LV), right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness, septal deviation, and the pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio (P​A:​AA). The primary endpoint was post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR (mean pulmonary artery pressure > 20 mmHg and PVR > 2 Wood units). Incremental value beyond right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) was assessed. PH with elevated PVR occurred in 21 (21.6%) patients. Diastolic PA:​AA showed the best discrimination, although this was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.526-0.798), other metrics performed less well (AUCs 0.46-0.60). At the Youden-optimal threshold of ≥ 0.90, sensitivity was 61.9%, specificity 72.4%, positive predictive value 38.2% and negative predictive value 87.3%. RVSP discriminated poorly (AUC 0.558); adding PA:​AA(d) improved discrimination (AUC 0.710; ΔAUC 0.152), model fit (p = 0.015), risk separation (IDI 0.066; p = 0.020) and reclassification (category-free NRI 0.690; p = 0.024). PA:​AA(d) correlated modestly with post-procedural mPAP (Spearman ρ = 0.247; p = 0.015). In this exploratory analysis, a larger pre-TAVR diastolic PA:AA ratio was associated with post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR and improved discrimination when combined with echocardiographic RV​SP.Trial registration: This study was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry and accepted by the International Committee of Medical Journal ​Editors (UMIN ID: 000054628).
title: Pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio on pre-procedural computed tomography and pulmonary hypertension after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Provisional stenting is the conventional method for coronary bifurcation lesions; however, the optimal side branch (SB) optimization strategy is still a topic of debate. In a unified mechanical and hemodynamic framework, no prior computational study has directly compared distal proximal optimization technique (POT), proximal POT, kissing balloon inflation (KBI), and ostial optimization technique (OOT). The objective of this investigation was to evaluate the hemodynamic and mechanical consequences of these strategies in a computational model of coronary bifurcation stenting.
METHODS: A sequential finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) framework was applied to a Medina 1,1,1 bifurcation using a three-layer hyperelastic vessel wall, hyperelastic-plastic plaque, folded balloons, and a cobalt-chromium stent. Each SB optimization strategy was followed by rePOT. Transient non-Newtonian (Carreau) CFD was performed on the post-deployment geometries during a cardiac cycle. Outcomes included stent stress, wall stress, malapposition, neo-carina length, time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT), Q-criterion, helicity, and local normalized helicity (LNH).
RESULTS: In the modelled anatomy, distal SB access was associated with more favorable hemodynamic metrics. TAWSS < 0.4 Pa, OSI > 0.1, and RRT > 20 was observed in 46.6, 6.2, and 11.0% within the bifurcation core, respectively, compared to 52.3, 12.5, and 18.0% with proximal access resulting in adverse outcomes. Intermediate hemodynamic profiles were observed in KBI and OOT. Proximal access was associated with greater vortex disruption, whereas distal access preserved more coherent helical structures. Mechanically, OOT exhibited the lowest malapposition (13.6%), wall stress (219 kPa), and neo-carina length (0.00 mm). The largest residual neo-carina (0.57 mm) was observed in proximal access.
CONCLUSION: In this single idealized Medina 1,1,1 computational model, distal SB access was associated with more favorable simulated hemodynamic characteristics, while OOT achieved favorable mechanical outcomes. These results establish a mechanistic foundation for additional research on the potential impact of SB optimization strategies on the mechanics and flow of the local stent-vessel system. However, the relative performance of these strategies may depend on bifurcation anatomy, plaque distribution, device characteristics, and procedural conditions. Consequently, the current findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require validation across a range of anatomies, devices, and boundary conditions before clinical implications can be established.
title: In Silico Comparative Analysis of Optimization Techniques for Coronary Bifurcation Provisional Stenting: A Coupled FEA-CFD Procedure.

abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare the real-world effectiveness and safety of prasugrel versus ticagrelor among patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the United States.
DESIGN: Retrospective new-user cohort study.
DATA SOURCE: MarketScan Research Databases, 2017-2023.
PATIENTS: Patients aged 18 years or older with ACS and PCI initiated on either prasugrel or ticagrelor were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) diagnosis codes and prescription records. The prescription fill date was assigned as the index date. Patients were required to have continuous enrollment in their health care plan for 1 year prior to and including the index date.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Stabilized inverse probability treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Cox proportional hazards models with adherence adjustment were used to estimate 1 year risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of myocardial infarction [MI], ischemic stroke, or stent thrombosis), bleeding events, and individual MACE components. The study included 6662 prasugrel-treated and 25,452 ticagrelor-treated patients. Prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of MACE (3.83 vs. 5.61 events per 100 person-years; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-0.92) and MI (3.43 vs. 4.73 events per 100 person-years; aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.97) compared with ticagrelor, respectively. Bleeding risk did not differ between prasugrel versus ticagrelor (2.85 vs. 3.89 events per 100 person-years, respectively; aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.13). Sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with high medication adherence and without contraindications to prasugrel showed similar results.
CONCLUSION: Among commercially insured US patients with ACS undergoing PCI, prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of ischemic cardiovascular events compared with ticagrelor, without an increase in bleeding risk, including in patients with high medication adherence. These findings provide contemporary real-world evidence supporting the preferential use of prasugrel over ticagrelor following ACS and PCI in appropriately selected patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective new-user cohort (MarketScan) with inverse probability weighting; 6662 prasugrel and 25,452 ticagrelor patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational claims data with residual confounding and channelling, and no death outcome in the MACE composite.
appraisal.one_line: In a US claims cohort of patients with ACS treated with PCI, prasugrel was associated with lower MACE and MI than ticagrelor, with no difference in bleeding.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds large real-world evidence to the prasugrel versus ticagrelor debate after ACS and PCI.

title: Real-World Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor After Acute Coronary Syndrome and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis is associated with reduced survival in ambulatory cardiology populations, but its prognostic significance when identified during an intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis is unknown. We examined its association with 90-day mortality in this setting.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and its echocardiogram-matched subset (MIMIC-IV-ECHO). We included each adult's first intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis with an interpretable baseline transthoracic echocardiogram recording peak aortic jet velocity. Stenosis was graded from the peak velocity (no stenosis < 2.0, sclerosis or mild 2.0-2.9, moderate 3.0-3.9, severe ≥ 4.0 m/s). The echocardiogram defined time zero; the primary outcome was all-cause mortality within a fixed 90-day window. Associations were estimated with multivariable Cox models adjusted for acute-illness severity and comorbidity, with propensity-score matching, velocity-gradient concordance grading, pre-specified ejection-fraction subgroups, and an E-value.
RESULTS: Of 12,878 patients (10,511 no stenosis, 1,797 sclerosis, 411 moderate, 159 severe), 3,605 died within 90 days. Crude 90-day mortality rose across grades (26.1%, 34.4%, 40.4%, 46.5%). After adjustment, the hazard increased monotonically: sclerosis 1.17 (95% CI 1.07-1.28), moderate 1.33 (1.13-1.56), severe 1.61 (1.27-2.03). The moderate-stenosis association was modest but consistent, attenuating slightly in the most conservative specifications (propensity-score matched 1.20 [1.02-1.40]; parsimonious 1.22 [1.05-1.43]); the E-value was 1.73 (lower limit 1.41). It was numerically concentrated in the first two weeks (1.58 [1.30-1.93], days 0-14) and numerically larger with reduced (1.47 [1.10-1.97]) than preserved ejection fraction (1.10 [0.87-1.39]); neither the proportional-hazards nor the grade-by-ejection-fraction interaction test was significant (interaction P = 0.21), and both are exploratory numerical patterns, not demonstrated effect modification.
CONCLUSIONS: In non-cardiac critical illness, velocity-defined moderate aortic stenosis identified during the intensive care admission was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality, with exploratory numerical patterns of greater early risk and of greater risk with reduced ejection fraction. These data identify a higher-risk phenotype; they do not establish a causal adverse effect of moderate valvular obstruction itself. It is best regarded as a prognostic marker warranting closer surveillance rather than, on current evidence, a target for valve intervention.
title: Moderate aortic stenosis identified during intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis and 90-day mortality: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV echocardiography database.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. Whether the magnitude of this benefit differs according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status remains uncertain.
METHODS: This pre-specified subgroup analysis of the multicenter randomized DAPA-TAVI trial conducted at 39 centers in Spain, which enrolled 1222 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR with prior HF and at least one high-risk condition. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of DM. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or worsening HF at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of the primary endpoint, cardiovascular death, and safety outcomes. Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, coronary artery disease, baseline ejection fraction and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to estimate treatment effects.
RESULTS: Among 1222 patients, 537 (43.9%) had DM. In patients with DM, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the primary endpoint compared with standard care (15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866; p = 0.008; number needed to treat [NNT] = 11), driven primarily by fewer worsening HF events. In patients without DM, the reduction was numerically lower and non-significant (15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183; p = 0.280; NNT = 32). Genital infections were more frequent with dapagliflozin in patients with DM, whereas symptomatic hypotension was more common in those without DM. No significant differences in serious adverse events were observed in either subgroup. No statistically significant interactions between DM status and treatment effect were observed for the primary or secondary endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: In this pre-specified subanalysis of the DAPA-TAVI trial, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of death or worsening HF in patients with DM undergoing TAVR, with a favorable benefit-risk profile, whereas a more modest and non-significant effect was observed in non-DM patients. Although no statistically significant interaction according to diabetes status was observed, the apparently greater benefit among patients with DM warrants further investigation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified subgroup analysis of a multicentre randomised trial at 39 centres; 1222 patients, 537 with diabetes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis without a significant interaction test, open-label design and a single-country population.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified subgroup analysis of DAPA-TAVI showing dapagliflozin reduced death or worsening heart failure after TAVI in patients with diabetes, with a smaller non-significant effect without diabetes and no significant interaction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: With diabetes: 15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866. Without diabetes: 15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183. No statistically significant interaction by diabetes status.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports applying the DAPA-TAVI result irrespective of diabetes status and informs cardiometabolic therapy questions after TAVI.

title: Influence of diabetes mellitus on dapagliflozin response after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR): insights from the DAPA-TAVI trial.

abstract: Wire-impenetrable chronic total occlusion (CTO) proximal caps cannot be penetrated with conventional guidewire escalation. They are often associated with severe calcification and proximal cap ambiguity. Wire-impenetrable proximal caps can be approached using a "go through" or a "go around" strategy. "Go through" involves using penetrative guidewires or other plaque-modifying equipment, such as laser and electrocautery-assisted re-entry (e-CART). The "go around" approach involves getting into the extraplaque space, through which the CTO is traversed in either the antegrade or the retrograde direction, followed by re-entry into the true lumen. Strong guide-catheter support is required for both the "go through" and "go around" approaches. We discuss the approach to wire-impenetrable CTO proximal caps, propose a step-by-step treatment algorithm, and address potential challenges and their troubleshooting.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Step-by-Step Approach to the Wire-Impenetrable Chronic Total Occlusion Proximal Cap.

abstract: Angiographic narrowing of a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) bypass graft does not always reflect atherosclerotic progression. Chronic or spontaneous LIMA graft dissection may be identified using optical coherence tomography (OCT). A patient with severe multivessel coronary disease and a history of coronary stenting and triple coronary artery bypass grafting presented with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated critical left main-left circumflex disease, extensive left anterior descending artery in-stent restenosis, an occluded venous graft, and eccentric mid-LIMA narrowing. Urgent native-vessel revascularization restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow and relieved the patient's symptoms. During staged LIMA assessment 6 days later, OCT was performed using a Dragonfly OpStar imaging catheter. OCT identified the entry of a longitudinal intimal flap separating the true and false lumens over a long segment, without significant atherosclerosis in the imaged segment. The operators interpreted this "double-barrel" configuration as a nonobstructive dissection of presumed chronicity. Preserved LIMA flow and clinical stability supported stent deferral; the patient remained asymptomatic and with preserved ejection fraction at the 2-month follow-up visit. This report offers important lessons for interventionalists: intravascular imaging can distinguish dissection from apparent atherosclerotic stenosis and significantly drive further management. Inadvertent false-lumen stenting could expand the false channel, compress the true lumen, and compromise graft perfusion. OCT clearly elucidated lesion morphology and supported clinical restraint; however, it did not independently establish dissection age or an exact mechanism of dissection.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Internal Mammary Artery Bypass Graft Dissection Mimicking Atherosclerotic Stenosis: Optical Coherence Tomography to Guide Stent Deferral.

abstract: We report a rare case of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) catheter entrapment in which extensive twisting of the catheter shaft prevented retrieval. In this phenomenon, termed "catheter suicide," the mechanical IVUS catheter twisted within the left main coronary artery (LMCA) and formed complex loops. Initial removal attempts were unsuccessful, and, during these bailout attempts, the imaging core of the IVUS catheter was found to be severed in its proximal portion. Subsequent imaging of another vessel confirmed extensive twisting, with associated iatrogenic dissection, as the cause of entrapment. Ex vivo experiments reproduced this rotational torque-driven complication. The twist was eventually released incidentally when the IVUS catheter was advanced further, and a larger guiding catheter was used, thereby facilitating safe retrieval. Subsequently, a stent was placed to treat the LMCA dissection, achieving thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow, and the patient was discharged without complications. This case illustrates a severe complication specific to mechanical IVUS systems and emphasizes the importance of prevention and early surgical consultation.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Intravascular Ultrasound Catheter Entrapment Caused by Extensive Twisting in the Left Main Coronary Artery: A Challenging Retrieval.
Creating space for a third valve: bioprosthetic valve fracture facilitating TAVI-in-TAV-in-SAV.

abstract: Myocardial bridging (MB) is usually managed medically, and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is generally avoided for isolated bridging. In clinical practice, however, stent extension into a bridged segment may be difficult to avoid when proximal left anterior descending (LAD) disease reaches the bridge entrance, LAD chronic total occlusion obscures distal bridge involvement, diffuse disease leaves no bridge-free landing region, or bailout coverage is required for edge dissection or procedural instability. Once implanted within the bridge, a stent is exposed to repetitive extrinsic compression, caliber mismatch, dynamic deformation, and abnormal local shear, creating a substrate for restenosis, deformation, fracture, perforation, and target lesion failure. This focused review addresses unavoidable bridged-segment stenting as a distinct PCI scenario rather than as a general review of myocardial bridging. We summarize lesion-bridge patterns, anatomic and physiologic mechanisms, the role of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)/optical coherence tomography (OCT), and invasive physiology in procedural planning, and practical strategies to minimize metal burden and optimize stent-edge placement. We also examine drug-coated balloons, surgical unroofing, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in selected anatomy, and emerging bioadaptor technology, while explicitly distinguishing established clinical evidence from limited observational data and hypothesis-generating concepts.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Unavoidable Stent Extension Into the Bridged Segment During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Bridging: A Focused Review of Mechanisms, Pitfalls, and Treatment Strategies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United Kingdom-British Cardiovascular Intervention Society complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary intervention (UK-BCIS CHIP) score was developed to identify patient- and procedural factors to predict short-term adverse outcomes in patients undergoing high risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in a patient population treated with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) for severe coronary calcification remains unknown.
AIMS: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI for severe coronary calcification, and to assess procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes across CHIP score categories.
METHODS: This international, multicenter, prospective study included consecutive patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI between May 2019 and December 2025 from the BENELUX-IVL registry. Patients were stratified according to UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5). The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality, procedural outcomes, and periprocedural complications. Discrimination of the UK-BCIS CHIP score was assessed using the AUC for in-hospital events and the Harrell's C-index for 1-year outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 911 patients were included. Higher UK-BCIS CHIP scores were associated with increased clinical comorbidity, lesion complexity, and procedural intensity. Procedural, device, and technical success rates were comparable across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (85.1%, 94.4%, and 85.7% overall; p = 0.850, p = 0.813, and p = 0.781, respectively). Complications requiring intervention occurred in 5.5% of patients and did not differ significantly across CHIP score categories (p = 0.347). The 1-year cumulative incidence of MACE, accounting for all-cause death as a competing risk, did not differ significantly across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (Gray's test p = 0.53).
CONCLUSION: In IVL-assisted PCI, the UK-BCIS CHIP score effectively identifies patients with increased clinical and procedural complexity but shows limited discrimination for mid-term ischemic outcomes. IVL-assisted PCI is safe and effective across the full spectrum of CHIP risk, while long-term prognosis appears primarily driven by underlying comorbidity burden.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: External Validation of the UK-BCIS CHIP Score to Predict 1-Year Outcomes in Patients Undergoing IVL-Assisted PCI: Insights From the International BENELUX-IVL Registry.

abstract: Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre-syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve-in-valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon-expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post-implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve-in-valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high-risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post-implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Using Balloon-Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) measures angiography-derived coronary physiology, whereas radial wall strain (RWS) characterizes cyclic lumen deformation. We investigated their complementary long-term prognostic information in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.
AIMS: We investigated the complementary long-term prognostic information of QFR and RWS in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses, and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 236 patients with 236 untreated index vessels and 50%-90% diameter stenosis. QFR and maximum RWS (RWSmax) were calculated offline and were unavailable to treating clinicians. Target vessel failure (TVF) comprised cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization (TVR). Prespecified Cox models used multiple imputation, and four nested models underwent 1000-bootstrap validation with repeat imputation and fitting. Fixed 3-year analyses, calibration, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Over a median potential follow-up of 66.8 months, 55 patients experienced TVF, including 40 TVR events. TVF occurred in 37/108 patients (34.3%) with RWSmax > 12% and 18/128 (14.1%) with RWSmax ≤12%. In the primary model, the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.06-1.23; p = 0.001) per 1% increase in RWSmax and 1.34 (95% CI: 1.08-1.67; p = 0.010) per 0.05 decrease in QFR. The combined model had an apparent C-index of 0.733 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.704, compared with 0.597 for the clinical model. Its corrected 3-year AUC was 0.733, and its corrected calibration slope was 0.90.
CONCLUSIONS: Joint assessment of coronary physiology and wall strain provided incremental long-term prognostic information beyond clinical and angiographic characteristics in untreated intermediate lesions. Lower QFR and higher RWSmax were independently associated with TVF, and each added prognostic information beyond the other. The signal predominantly concerned subsequent revascularization. External validation is needed before clinical application.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Angiography-Derived Quantitative Flow Ratio and Radial Wall Strain in Untreated Intermediate Coronary Stenoses: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract: The jailed balloon technique (JBT) is an effective strategy for side branch (SB) protection during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary bifurcation lesions; however, jailed balloon entrapment is a rare but serious complication. We report the case of a man in his 70s who was successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation and underwent emergency PCI for a right coronary artery bifurcation lesion. A drug-eluting stent was deployed from the mid right coronary artery to the posterior descending branch using JBT. The jailed SB balloon became entrapped and could not be retrieved despite repeated inflation and deflation, traction, and rotational torque. Further traction resulted in deep engagement of the guiding catheter and an accordion phenomenon of the right coronary artery, raising concern about vascular injury. A balloon was therefore inflated within the stented main vessel, and forward pressure was applied to its shaft to provide counterforce against traction on the entrapped SB balloon. Using this technique, which we termed the "reverse balloon anchoring technique," the entrapped balloon was successfully retrieved without apparent device damage. Final angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved SB flow and adequate stent apposition. The reverse balloon anchoring technique may represent a useful bailout option for jailed balloon entrapment when conventional retrieval maneuvers fail.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Reverse Balloon Anchoring for Retrieval of an Entrapped Side-Branch Balloon During the Jailed Balloon Technique.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) expose patients and operators to ionizing radiation, posing risks of deterministic effects such as skin injury and stochastic effects including malignancy. Although real-time dosimetry and dose alerts have been associated with radiation-dose reductions in prior reports, the level of patient radiation reduction associated with implementing a formal, multifaceted radiation reduction program has not previously been reported in a high-volume catheterization laboratory.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a substantial radiation dose level (SRDL) protocol on patient radiation exposure during PCI.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 19,249 PCI procedures at a tertiary center from July 2012 to December 2021. Patients were stratified into a pre-protocol cohort (Phase 1: 17,332 procedures) and a post-protocol cohort (Phase 2: 1917 procedures following implementation in November 2019). The SRDL protocol included real-time radiation monitoring, alert thresholds at 5 Gy air kerma, and structured follow-up for high-dose cases. Study outcomes included air kerma (Ka,r) dose-area product (DAP), contrast volume, and fluoroscopy time.
RESULTS: The study cohort (mean age 66.3 years; 28.5% female) demonstrated significant reductions in radiation exposure after implementing the protocol. Median air kerma declined from 2.6 to 2.0 Gy (23% reduction; p < 0.0001), and median DAP decreased from 158 to 125 Gy·cm2 (20.8% reduction; p < 0.0001). Contrast volume was reduced by 15 mL (11.1% reduction; p < 0.0001), while fluoroscopy time remained unchanged (18.1 vs. 18.3 min; p = 0.094). Despite increased procedural complexity in Phase 2 (multivessel PCI: 69.5% vs. 65.2%; p < 0.001), radiation reduction remained significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of an SRDL protocol was associated with significant reductions in patient radiation exposure during PCI without increasing procedure time, supporting its use as a safety intervention in high-volume catheterization laboratories.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Reducing Patient Radiation Skin Dose in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using a Dedicated Protocol: A Single-Center Experience.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.
title: When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) adaptation to increased pulmonary afterload is a major determinant of prognosis in pulmonary hypertension (PH), yet comprehensive validation of simple noninvasive markers against invasive hemodynamic parameters remains limited. We investigated whether the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure (TAPSE/sPAP) ratio reflects the clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic spectrum of PH.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 209 consecutive patients with right heart catheterization-confirmed PH who underwent comprehensive clinical assessment, transthoracic echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamic evaluation between 2016 and 2024. Patients were stratified into quartiles according to the TAPSE/sPAP ratio, and clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic characteristics were compared.
RESULTS: The mean age was 58.8 ± 16.5 years, and 61% of patients were female. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios were associated with older age, higher NT-proBNP and serum uric acid levels, and lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (all p < 0.05). Decreasing TAPSE/sPAP ratios were also associated with larger right atrial and right ventricular dimensions, lower TAPSE, and higher tricuspid regurgitation velocity and estimated sPAP (all p < 0.001).
