Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated progressively higher right ventricular systolic pressure, mean pulmonary artery pressure, and pulmonary vascular resistance (all p < 0.001), whereas mixed venous oxygen saturation increased across quartiles (p = 0.036).
CONCLUSIONS: The TAPSE/sPAP ratio is a practical, noninvasive marker that closely reflects right ventricular remodeling and invasive hemodynamic impairment in pulmonary hypertension. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios identify patients with more advanced RV-pulmonary arterial uncoupling and may improve bedside hemodynamic risk stratification.
title: Clinical and Invasive Hemodynamic Correlates of the TAPSE/sPAP Ratio in Pulmonary Hypertension.

abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Diagnosing acute myocardial injury remains a significant challenge in contemporary cardiovascular and critical care medicine. Myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) frequently present with overlapping features, chest pain, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and electrocardiographic abnormalities, yet require divergent management, making rapid and accurate etiological diagnosis essential for optimal patient outcomes.
METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiology and biomarker signatures of myocarditis, ACS, and SICM, and examines how these signatures can be integrated into a practical diagnostic approach for the emergency department and intensive care unit.
RESULTS: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) remains the central biomarker of acute myocardial injury, but its kinetics differ across the three conditions. A steep rise and fall in ACS, a sustained moderate elevation in myocarditis, and a gradual, severity-parallel course in sepsis. Among complementary biomarkers, C-reactive protein lacks specificity, whereas procalcitonin supports the recognition of bacterial sepsis in SICM, and natriuretic peptides reflect myocardial wall stress, disproportionately elevated relative to troponin in SICM. Emerging molecular biomarkers, circulating microRNAs (like miR-4763-3p and miR-155) and extracellular matrix remodeling markers, show promise for distinguishing inflammatory from ischemic myocardial injury, but remain investigational owing to the lack of standardized assays and practical constraints on acute bedside use. Therefore diagnosis rests on an integrated, multimodal assessment.
CONCLUSION: The differential diagnosis of acute myocardial injury requires a systematic, biomarker-centered multimodal approach. Future research should prioritize the prospective validation of multi-biomarker panels and the development of rapid non-invasive tools to reduce reliance on emergency coronary angiography.
title: Biomarkers for differential diagnosis of myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome, and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) aneurysm most commonly follows transmural myocardial infarction and is rarely described in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). When DCM and ischemic injury coexist, the presentation may be atypical and progression can be rapid.
CASE SUMMARY: A 52-year-old man developed chest tightness and dyspnea after an upper respiratory tract infection. Echocardiography showed LV dilatation with reduced systolic function (LVEF 36%). Coronary angiography on hospital day 4 demonstrated severe stenoses of the left circumflex/obtuse marginal branch and a moderate right coronary artery lesion, and a drug-eluting stent was implanted in the left circumflex artery. One month later, he was readmitted with recurrent dyspnea, BNP 2,627 ng/L, complete left bundle branch block, marked LV dilatation (end-diastolic diameter 113 mm), severe functional mitral regurgitation, and a large inferolateral apical LV aneurysm (74 mm × 50 mm) with paradoxical motion. Despite intensified heart failure therapy, he progressed to end-stage heart failure and underwent heart transplantation. Histopathology of tissue adjacent to the aneurysm was consistent with myocardial infarction with chronic inflammatory cell infiltration, and the sampled left circumflex artery showed atherosclerotic stenosis.
CONCLUSION: In DCM with new regional wall motion abnormalities or rapid structural deterioration, concomitant ischemic injury should be considered even when symptoms are non-specific. Electrical and mechanical dyssynchrony may increase regional wall stress and contribute to aneurysm formation, accelerating clinical decline.
title: Heart transplantation for rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy complicated by an inferolateral left ventricular aneurysm: a case report.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a minimally invasive treatment for aortic stenosis. Although significant advancements in the TAVI technique have been made, the risk of requiring a permanent pacemaker remains clinically relevant.
AIM: The aim of the study was to analyze the relationship between peri-procedural blood count parameters and the risk of pacemaker implantation after TAVI.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The retrospective study analyzed 115 patients (median (Q1-Q3) age of 76.7 (73.5-81.9) years). Demographic and clinical data were collected. The counts of leukocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets were assessed before the procedure, on the day of the procedure (8 hours after the procedure), 24, 48, and 72 hours after the procedure, and at hospital discharge. Pre-procedural and post-procedural heart rhythm disturbances have been recorded.
RESULTS: The analysis showed a predominant increase in neutrophil and monocyte counts after the procedure, without differences between subgroups. Moreover, a decrease in lymphocyte counts was observed after TAVI; however, it was less pronounced in patients who required pacemaker implantation. Patients without heart rhythm disturbances experienced a greater decrease in their lymphocyte count. In the multivariable analysis, an increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was an independent factor for pacemaker implantation (OR = 5.2, 95% CI: 1.6-16.3, p = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: After TAVI, increases in neutrophil and monocyte counts and decreases in lymphocyte counts are observed; however, the lymphocyte count decrease is less pronounced in patients with heart rhythm disturbances requiring pacemaker implantation. An increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was independently associated with pacemaker implantation.
journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
title: Peri-procedural immune blood cell count changes and pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory study.

abstract: Gemella haemolysans is an uncommon cause of infective endocarditis, yet infection involving a prosthetic valve may be accompanied by extensive extracardiac disease. A 79-year-old man with a history of transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with fever, rigors, dyspnea, severe low back pain, and inability to walk after a fall. Two sets of blood cultures grew G. haemolysans. Echocardiography demonstrated a 0.6 × 0.6 cm vegetation at the aortic valve annulus. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging identified discitis and vertebral osteomyelitis at L4-L5 and L5-S1, an anterior epidural abscess, and moderate-to-severe spinal canal stenosis. Abdominal imaging revealed a right psoas abscess and a 6.2-cm splenic infarction. Antimicrobial therapy was narrowed to intravenous ceftriaxone according to susceptibility testing. Fever resolved and inflammatory markers declined during hospitalization; a 6-week course was arranged at discharge without valve surgery. This case highlights the association between endocarditis and vertebral infection, the limitations of vegetation size as a measure of extracardiac disease, and the complexity of treatment decisions following transcatheter valve replacement.
first_author_country: Los Robles Regional Medical Center Thousand Oaks California USA
last_author_country: Los Robles Regional Medical Center Thousand Oaks California USA
title: From Valve to Spine and Spleen: Multisystem Complications of Gemella haemolysans Prosthetic-Valve Endocarditis.

abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognized non-atherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome and an important mechanism of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), particularly in younger women without traditional cardiovascular risk factors. SCAD results from separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall, with formation of a false lumen and impaired myocardial perfusion. Conventional coronary angiography, although the first-line diagnostic tool, may not adequately identify intramural disease; therefore, intracoronary imaging with optical coherence tomography or intravascular ultrasound, and cardiac magnetic resonance in selected MINOCA patients, are used to refine diagnosis and identify the underlying mechanism. Treatment is usually conservative, as most dissections heal spontaneously. Observational data suggest that b-blockers may reduce recurrence, especially in patients with hypertension or left ventricular dysfunction. Revascularization with stenting or coronary artery bypass grafting is reserved for patients with ongoing ischemia or hemodynamic instability. Despite a favorable overall prognosis, recurrence - particularly in the presence of fibromuscular dysplasia and uncontrolled hypertension - remains a concern.
journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
keywords: myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) as a cause of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) de-escalation strategies including early switching from a potent P2Y12 inhibitor to clopidogrel become attractive for patients with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI). It is unclear whether DAPT de-escalation after optical coherence tomography (OCT)- or angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves neointimal coverage in STEMI patients who have completed 1-month DAPT with aspirin plus ticagrelor.
METHODS: This report describes the design of a randomized study evaluating the neointimal coverage in STEMI patients after guiding de-escalation of DAPT from aspirin plus ticagrelor to aspirin plus clopidogrel at 1 month after PCI with drug eluting stent implantation by OCT or angiography and 1-month DAPT with aspirin plus ticagrelor. Eighty patients who meet the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 fashion to the OCT- or angiography-guided group (first randomization). All patients will receive open label ticagrelor plus aspirin for 1 month after the index PCI. At 30 ± 7 days after the index PCI, patients with no major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) or major bleeding (⩾Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] 3a) will be randomized in a 1:1 fashion to either the ticagrelor plus aspirin group or clopidogrel plus aspirin group for an additional 11 months (second randomization). The primary endpoint is the stent-strut neointimal thickness by OCT assessment at 12-month follow up.
DISCUSSION: The data obtained from DAPT-OCT study will explore the neointimal coverage after guiding de-escalation of antiplatelet treatment in STEMI patients undergoing PCI by OCT.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06339021.
title: Evaluation of Neointimal Coverage After Guiding De-escalation of Antiplatelet Treatment in Patients with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention by Optical Coherence Tomography or Angiography: Rationale and Design of the DAPT-OCT Study.

abstract: Background and objective Cardiac catheterization laboratories (Cath Labs) increasingly perform fluoroscopy-guided diagnostic and interventional procedures, making systematic monitoring of radiation exposure important. Structured archiving can support radiation surveillance, quality assurance, and procedural evaluation. This study aimed to examine dose-area product/kerma-area product (DAP/KAP), cumulative air kerma (CAK/Ka,r), and fluoroscopy time, with particular attention to variation by procedure type and the influence of BMI. Methods A hospital-based retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory of Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. A total of 190 archived patient records were analyzed. Demographic variables, procedure category, fluoroscopy time, DAP/KAP, and CAK were evaluated. The association between BMI and radiation exposure was also examined. Results The mean age of the cohort was 55.88 ± 11.04 years and mean BMI was 26.78 ± 3.87 kg/m². Coronary angiography (CAG) + percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) was the most frequently performed procedure (70.5%). Median DAP/KAP and CAK were lowest for diagnostic CAG and substantially higher for CAG + PTCA. The median fluoroscopy time was 1.9 minutes for CAG, 8.3 minutes for CAG + PTCA, and 13.1 minutes for other procedures. BMI demonstrated a significant positive correlation with DAP/KAP (r = 0.470, p < 0.001) and CAK (r = 0.469, p < 0.001). DAP/KAP and CAK demonstrated a very strong positive correlation (r = 0.941, p < 0.001). No radiation-related complications or dose alerts were documented. Conclusions Radiation exposure varied by procedure type and BMI. Systematic Cath Lab archiving and continuous monitoring of DAP/KAP, CAK, and fluoroscopy time can provide useful baseline data for radiation safety, quality assurance, and dose optimization.
title: Archiving of Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory Procedures and Records of Radiation Exposure: A Single-Center Experience.

abstract: A type 1 Brugada electrocardiographic (ECG) pattern is characteristic of Brugada syndrome but may also occur in association with reversible clinical conditions, including myocardial ischaemia. We describe a 49-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, severe hypercholesterolaemia and a strong family history of premature ischaemic heart disease who presented with crescendo angina. His admission ECG demonstrated a type 1 Brugada pattern, with subsequent ECGs showing dynamic anterior ischaemic changes. Coronary angiography demonstrated extensive multivessel coronary artery disease, and the patient underwent urgent surgical revascularisation following Heart Team discussion. Serial postoperative ECGs demonstrated complete resolution of the type 1 pattern despite continuation of his regular medication, including mirtazapine. In the absence of arrhythmic syncope, documented ventricular arrhythmia, previous cardiac arrest or a family history of sudden cardiac death, sodium-channel blocker provocation testing was not pursued. Although latent Brugada syndrome cannot be definitively excluded, the temporal relationship between myocardial ischaemia, revascularisation and ECG normalisation supports an ischaemia-associated Brugada phenotype.
title: Transient Type 1 Brugada ECG Pattern in a Patient With Severe Coronary Artery Disease.

abstract: McConnell's sign, defined as hypokinesis of the right ventricular (RV) midfree wall with preserved apical contractions, was initially considered to be highly specific for acute pulmonary embolism. However, evidence indicates that it may also appear in other conditions involving RV dysfunction. Here, we report a case of McConnell's sign associated with RV myocardial infarction in the absence of pulmonary embolism. A 74-year-old female was successfully resuscitated following cardiac arrest. Echocardiography revealed a dilated RV with moderate tricuspid regurgitation and a regional wall motion pattern characteristic of McConnell's sign. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography excluded a pulmonary embolism. Coronary angiography revealed an occluded right coronary artery, which was identified as the culprit lesion, and a chronically occluded left anterior descending artery with collateral flow. Conservative management led to gradual clinical and echocardiographic improvement. This case underscores that McConnell's sign is not pathognomonic for pulmonary embolism and should be interpreted cautiously.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery fistulas (CAFs) are rare vascular anomalies that may remain asymptomatic or present with symptoms mimicking coronary artery disease (CAD). In individuals with coexisting coronary atherosclerosis, fistulas that originate from the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and end in the pulmonary artery are extremely rare and can complicate the clinical picture.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old man, an ex-smoker with a previous non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, presented with worsening chest pain and dyspnea. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe left anterior descending artery (LAD) stenosis, diagonal artery occlusion, and a fistulous communication arising from the proximal LAD with focal aneurysmal dilatation draining into the main pulmonary artery. Cardiac computed tomography (CT) confirmed multiple fistulous tracts between the LAD and the pulmonary artery. Following a multidisciplinary discussion, the patient underwent surgical fistula ligation with double-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). The postoperative course was uneventful, with complete symptom resolution at six-month follow-up.
DISCUSSION: The coexistence of an LAD-pulmonary artery fistula with significant CAD is rare and poses diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. For precise anatomical delineation and surgical planning, multimodality imaging was crucial. Surgical ligation of the fistula, combined with CABG, allowed definitive treatment of both pathologies in a single procedure.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering CAFs as a potential coexisting pathology in adults presenting with angina and coronary artery disease. Recognition of such anomalies is essential to guide appropriate management and prevent complications.
journal: International journal of surgery case reports
keywords: left anterior descending artery–pulmonary artery fistulas
title: Beyond the usual suspects: a rare case report of left anterior descending artery to pulmonary artery fistula with concomitant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.

abstract: No-reflow is high-risk complication of PCI, associated with larger infarct size, ventricular dysfunction, and mortality. We describe a 62-year-old man with a distal RCA lesion who developed refractory no-reflow despite extensive pharmacologic therapy and thrombectomy. Supersaturated oxygen therapy, used as a bail-out strategy, restored distal perfusion and may represent an emerging option for patients with severe, treatment-resistant no-reflow.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Supersaturated Oxygen Therapy for Refractory No-Reflow Following PCI for Non-ST-Elevation ACS.

abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated serial blood cell aggregation changes after PCI in CAD patients and their 12-month outcomes.MethodsWe prospectively enrolled 120 elective PCI CAD patients and 50 frequency-matched controls. Blood was collected pre-PCI, on Days 3, 8, and Month 3. Erythrocyte aggregation index (EAI) was assessed by TAS-plus aggregometry. Patients were grouped into Group I (favorable, n = 106) and Group II (repeat PCI, n = 14).ResultsCAD patients showed higher baseline EAI (0.43 ± 0.06vs.0.29 ± 0.04, p < 0.001), fibrinogen (4.1 ± 0.6vs.2.9 ± 0.4 g/L, p < 0.001), and leukocyte aggregation (32.4 ± 5.8%vs.21.4 ± 4.2%, p < 0.001) than controls. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed a significant group-by-time interaction for EAI (F(3, 354) = 5.12, p = 0.002). Over 3 months, Group I showed progressive EAI normalization (0.42 ± 0.05 to 0.31 ± 0.03, p < 0.001), whereas Group II maintained elevated EAI (0.46 ± 0.07 to 0.44 ± 0.06, p = 0.245). Leukocyte aggregation increased transiently at Day 3 in both CAD groups (39.8 ± 6.7%vs.40.1 ± 6.5%) and returned to baseline by Month 3 (31.8 ± 5.4% vs. 32.1 ± 5.5%, p = 0.842), showing no persistent between-group differences in this cohort. ADP-induced platelet aggregation was significantly suppressed post-PCI at Day 3 (50.2 ± 7.6%vs.50.7 ± 7.4%, p < 0.001) without between-group differences.ConclusionsPersistent erythrocyte hyperaggregation post-PCI is associated with recurrent ischemia and repeat revascularization and may represent a potential biomarker for clinical risk stratification, pending validation in larger, multicenter prospective studies.
title: Blood cell aggregation as a hemorheological marker of long-term clinical outcome after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with coronary artery disease.

abstract: Cardiac surgery in patients with active thyrotoxicosis carries substantially increased perioperative risks. We report a case of urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in a 43-year-old man with severe biochemical thyrotoxicosis and critical left main coronary artery disease who presented with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Urgent off-pump CABG was performed with intra-aortic balloon pump support. Within 48 hours of surgery, the patient developed a thyroid storm characterized by fever (40 °C), tachycardia (140-180 beats/min), encephalopathy, and jaundice. The condition was successfully treated with anti-thyroid drugs and intravenous hydrocortisone. The patient recovered fully and was euthyroid at follow-up. Early recognition and prompt multidrug treatment of postoperative thyroid storm are life-saving.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary pressure pullback characterizes both the overall physiological severity and longitudinal distribution of coronary artery disease. However, the respective relationships of physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution with local and vessel-wide plaque phenotypes remain incompletely understood.
AIMS: To investigate the relationships of physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution with coronary plaque characteristics assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT).
METHODS: We studied 216 patients with left anterior descending coronary artery disease who underwent OCT and angiography-based physiological assessment. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) represented overall physiological disease severity, whereas the pullback pressure gradient (PPG) index characterized longitudinal disease distribution. Associations with local OCT characteristics and whole-vessel burden of plaque features were assessed using regression models, with physiological indices standardized per 1 SD increase.
RESULTS: Median QFR and PPG were 0.88 [0.73-0.95] and 0.76 [0.69-0.83], respectively. Lower QFR was strongly associated with greater maximum lipid arc (β per 1 SD increase, -39.16°; 95% CI, -52.01 to -26.31; p < 0.001). PPG was not associated with maximum lipid arc in univariable analysis (β, -9.18°; p = 0.19). After accounting for QFR, however, higher PPG was associated with greater lipid arc index (β, 112.26 °·mm; p = 0.012) and smaller minimum lumen area (β, -0.42 mm2; p = 0.011), with a similar association observed for maximum lipid arc (β, 16.60°; p = 0.045). Conversely, lower PPG was associated with greater whole-vessel counts of adverse plaque features in unadjusted analyses, but these associations were attenuated after accounting for QFR.
CONCLUSIONS: At comparable physiological disease severity, a more focal physiological pattern was associated with greater local lipid concentration and lumen compromise, whereas a more diffuse pattern was associated with greater whole-vessel counts of plaque features in unadjusted analyses. These findings suggest that physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution provide complementary information on the spatial phenotype of coronary atherosclerosis.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Coronary Plaque Phenotypes According to Physiological Disease Severity and Pullback Pressure Gradient.

abstract: Intramyocardial dissecting hematoma (IDH) is a rare mechanical complication following acute myocardial infarction, characterized by blood accumulation within myocardial layers without complete rupture. Clinical outcomes are highly variable, ranging from spontaneous resolution to death. The optimal management strategy remains unclear, particularly regarding the role of conservative versus surgical approaches in hemodynamically stable patients. A 79-year-old male presented 1 month after anterior myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Echocardiography revealed a large (70 × 80 mm) heterogeneous mass with scattered echolucent spaces occupying more than half of the left ventricular cavity, originating from the akinetic apex and extending along the interventricular septum. Unlike typical thrombus, no communication with ventricular cavities or color Doppler flow was detected. Cardiac computed tomography revealed a hypodense, non-enhancing lesion (91 × 70 mm), raising the possibility of an intramyocardial hematoma. Despite the massive intracardiac mass, the patient remained hemodynamically stable. Serial echocardiographic monitoring over 2 weeks documented progressive hematoma reduction without additional medical intervention, anticoagulation, or surgical management. Complete resolution of the hematoma occurred without progression to ventricular septal rupture or free wall rupture. Spontaneous resolution of post-myocardial infarction IDH can occur in hemodynamically stable patients without surgical intervention. Serial echocardiographic monitoring is essential for detecting spontaneous regression and guiding management decisions. This case highlights the potential role of conservative management with close imaging surveillance and suggests that conservative management may represent an alternative to surgery in selected patients, particularly those who are hemodynamically stable.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Spontaneous Resolution of Post-Myocardial Infarction Intramyocardial Dissecting Hematoma: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-based intravascular renal denervation produces modest, variable blood pressure reductions, partly because renal sympathetic nerves lie at variable depths within the periarterial adventitia and because accessory or early branching arteries are inaccessible to intraluminal catheters. We developed an extravascular renal denervation system (HyperQure) delivering circumferential radiofrequency energy from outside the artery and assessed its safety and efficacy. Here, we report the primary 3-month outcomes.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm, first-in-human pilot trial enrolled 10 patients with resistant hypertension (office blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥135 mm Hg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents) across 7 Korean centers. All underwent bilateral extravascular renal denervation on stable antihypertensive regimens. The primary end point was 3-month change in 24-hour ambulatory SBP; safety outcomes were assessed through 3 months.
RESULTS: All 10 patients (median age, 52.5 years; 7 men) completed follow-up. Seven patients (70%) had accessory or early branching arteries <3 mm typically ineligible for intravascular renal denervation; all were successfully ablated. Median 24-hour ambulatory SBP decreased by 25.0 mm Hg (P=0.008) and median office SBP by 39.5 mm Hg (P=0.002). Seven of 10 (70%) achieved office SBP <140 mm Hg despite a reduction in median antihypertensive burden from 6.0 to 4.5 agents. No major or procedure-related adverse events occurred; follow-up computed tomography angiography showed no vascular complications and renal function was preserved.
CONCLUSIONS: Extravascular renal denervation using the HyperQure renal denervation System warrants evaluation in a larger controlled trial, particularly in patients with complex renal arterial anatomy.
title: Extravascular Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension: First-in-Human Study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Coronary artery bifurcation lesions (CBLs) represent a complex form of coronary artery disease (CAD) and are associated with an unfavorable long-term prognosis. The triglyceride-glucose index (TyGi) has been shown to provide valuable prognostic information regarding the risk of major cardiovascular events (MACEs) in patients with CAD. This study aimed to determine whether an elevated TyGi could predict MACEs, including target lesion revascularization (TLR), myocardial infarction (MI), and all-cause mortality, over a five-year follow-up period in patients with CBLs undergoing a double-stent strategy.
METHOD: This study included 552 patients who underwent a double-stent strategy between January 2010 and December 2020.
RESULTS: Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal TyGi cut-off value of 9.2877. Patients were subsequently divided into a low-TyGi group (Group 1) and a high-TyGi group (Group 2). During the five-year follow-up period, the incidence of MACEs was recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a higher incidence of MACEs in Group 2 than in Group 1 (P = 0.008). In multivariate Cox regression analysis (CRA), ejection fraction, presence of a complex bifurcation lesion, TyGi, and SYNTAX score (Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Taxus and Cardiac Surgery) were predictors of MACEs (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: An elevated TyGi may serve as a useful predictor of MACEs in patients with bifurcation lesions undergoing a double-stent strategy.

title: Can High Triglyceride-Glucose Index Predict Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Coronary Bifurcation Lesions Undergoing a Double-Stent Strategy?

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) carry a high residual cardiovascular risk that is inadequately captured by conventional risk scores. We aimed to compare the prognostic value of ten composite blood-based indices from metabolic, inflammatory, combined, and nutritional categories for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this population.
METHOD: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 557 consecutive NSTEMI patients with T2DM who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Ten indices were calculated from admission blood samples: TyG, AIP, and METS-IR as metabolic indices; SIRI, PIV, and NLR as inflammatory indices; CTI and CAR as combined indices; and PNI and HALP as nutritional indices. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with DeLong comparison, independent predictors were identified by multivariate logistic regression, and survival separation was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: One-year MACE occurred in 118 patients (21.2%). Inflammatory indices outperformed metabolic indices in ROC analysis (SIRI AUC 0.764 vs. TyG 0.638; P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, CTI (OR 2.446; 95% CI 1.746-3.427; P < 0.001), SIRI (OR 1.242; 95% CI 1.088-1.417; P = 0.001), and PNI (OR 0.918; 95% CI 0.884-0.954; P < 0.001) remained independent predictors alongside left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), SYNTAX score, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Pure metabolic indices lost significance after CTI entered the model. SIRI yielded the widest Kaplan-Meier survival separation (29.5 percentage points; P < 0.001). CTI remained significant across all subgroups, whereas SIRI lost independence in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
CONCLUSION: In NSTEMI patients with T2DM, CTI, SIRI, and PNI independently predict one-year MACE based on routine admission blood tests. Inflammatory and combined indices outperform pure metabolic surrogates, supporting a shift toward multidimensional risk stratification in this high-risk population.
journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
title: Inflammatory and Combined Indices Outperform Metabolic Indices in Predicting One-Year MACE in NSTEMI with Type 2 Diabetes.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between preprocedural urine specific gravity (USG) and contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) and to evaluate its role in risk prediction.
METHOD: This prospective study included 191 consecutive patients undergoing CAG. USG was measured 30 minutes before the procedure. CIN was defined as a ≥25% increase from baseline or an absolute increase of ≥0.5 mg/dL in serum creatinine 48-72 hours after the procedure. Factors predicting the development of CIN were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: The median age of the study population was 63.0 years (IQR: 55.0-71.0), and CIN developed in 33 patients (17.3%). Preprocedural USG was significantly higher in the CIN(+) group than in the CIN(-) group (1020.9+-5.4 vs. 1017.7+-6.6; P =.002). Multivariate analysis identified USG (OR: 1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18; P =.010), non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (OR: 3.32, 95% CI: 1.33-8.25; P =.010), New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III/IV (OR: 15.90, 95% CI: 2.76-91.50; P =.002), and bundle branch block (OR: 6.60, 95% CI: 1.78-24.42; P =.005) as independent predictors of CIN. The area under the curve (AUC) for USG was 0.671. At a cutoff value of 1017, USG demonstrated 81.8% sensitivity, 53.2% specificity, and a 93.3% negative predictive value (NPV). Although its overall discriminatory performance was similar to that of the Mehran risk score, USG exhibited a complementary diagnostic profile.
CONCLUSION: Elevated preprocedural USG is an independent risk factor for CIN. Given its high NPV, USG may serve as a modest, noninvasive, complementary bedside tool for risk stratification. The observed independent association between bundle branch block and CIN should be regarded strictly as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

title: The Role of Urine Specific Gravity in Predicting Contrast-Induced Nephropathy in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: A Prospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) is the leading cause of primary mitral regurgitation (MR) and is increasingly managed with minimally invasive and robotic-assisted repair. Preoperative planning increasingly relies on computed tomography (CT).
CASE SUMMARIES: Here, we describe a case series of 3 patients with severe degenerative mitral regurgitation who underwent mitral valve repair (2 robotic-assisted, 1 conventional) after CT evaluation. CT findings directly influenced repair feasibility, cannulation site, and operative approach.
DISCUSSION: Preoperative imaging is essential, but current planning relies on multiple studies, including echocardiography and invasive angiography. Electrocardiographically gated, multiphase cardiac CT offers a comprehensive alternative by simultaneously assessing leaflet morphology, annular calcification, coronary artery course, vascular access, and left atrial appendage thrombus.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: We show that a standardized CT protocol can consolidate preoperative planning and optimize patient-specific surgical strategies in mitral valve repair.
title: Multiphase Cardiac CT for Integrated Planning of Mitral Valve Repair: Coronaries and Cannulation Strategies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied.
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge.
DESIGN: The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results.
SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS: Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included.
INDEX TEST: Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS: The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria.
MAIN RESULTS: Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89).
CONCLUSION: Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.
journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE.
METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model.
RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 18 studies; 24,090 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled evidence is largely non-randomised, so confounding by indication between device strategies is likely.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of mainly observational studies comparing catheter-directed thrombolysis with mechanical thrombectomy in intermediate or high-risk pulmonary embolism found no difference in mortality or major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01; major bleeding RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55; ICU stay mean difference 1.01 days, 95% CI 0.87-1.15, longer with catheter-directed thrombolysis.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the comparative evidence for the two catheter-based strategies while randomised trials of PE interventions are reporting.

title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.

abstract: A magnetic separation-assisted competitive fluorescent aptasensor based on CdTe quantum dots (CdTe QDs) and Ag⁺ for the sensitive and selective detection of heart-type fatty acid binding protein (FABP3) in clinical serum samples has been developed. CdTe QDs were first quenched by Ag⁺ to form a CdTe QDs-Ag⁺ complex in the off state. The aptamer was immobilized on magnetic beads and hybridized with poly-T to form an MB-Apt/poly-T duplex. In the presence of FABP3, the aptamer preferentially bound to FABP3, leading to the release of poly-T from the magnetic beads. After magnetic separation, the released poly-T in the supernatant bound to Ag⁺ and competed with CdTe QDs for Ag⁺, thereby removing Ag⁺ from the CdTe QDs surface and restoring the fluorescence of CdTe QDs. In the absence of FABP3, poly-T remained on the magnetic beads, and the supernatant showed no fluorescence recovery. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear response to FABP3 in the range ​ 1-20 ng/mL, with a detection limit of 0.087 ng/mL. The method also showed excellent selectivity toward FABP3 against other interfering substances. In clinical serum samples, the sensor successfully distinguished healthy individuals from patients with myocardial injury. The results showed good agreement with a commercial ELISA kit (R² = 0.98), with a mean bias of -0.16 ng/mL and 95% limits of agreement from - 1.70 to + 1.39 ng/mL. Recoveries were 97.2-104.3% in 20% serum.
title: A m​agnetic separation-assisted fluorescent aptasensor based on CdTe QDs and Ag⁺ for clinical serum detection of FABP3 in acute myocardial infarction.

abstract: Antithrombotic therapy is central to the prevention of thromboembolic and ischaemic events in patients with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and after percutaneous coronary intervention, but is accompanied by an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can reduce upper GIB, although their optimal use across different antithrombotic regimens, potential drug interactions, and inability to prevent lower GIB remain clinically relevant concerns. This structured narrative review examines PPI co-therapy in patients receiving antiplatelet agents, oral anticoagulants, or combined antithrombotic treatment. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026, supplemented by contemporary cardiology and gastroenterology guidelines. Randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large observational studies were prioritized. Evidence indicates that PPIs provide clinically meaningful protection against acid-related upper GIB, particularly in high-risk patients receiving aspirin-containing regimens, dual antiplatelet therapy, or intensified antithrombotic therapy, whereas evidence in isolated oral anticoagulation remains predominantly observational. PPI co-therapy should therefore be targeted according to gastrointestinal bleeding risk and antithrombotic intensity, with periodic reassessment as treatment changes, rather than used as universal gastrointestinal protection. KEY POINTS: • Proton pump inhibitors can reduce the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy, but their benefit is greatest in patients with additional gastrointestinal bleeding risk factors • Their use should therefore be individualized according to gastrointestinal risk and the intensity of antithrombotic treatment rather than prescribed routinely to all patients • The need for gastroprotection should be reassessed whenever the antithrombotic regimen or the patient's bleeding risk changes.
title: Proton pump inhibitors in antithrombotic therapy: gastroprotection, drug interactions, and clinical management.

abstract: Infection of the cannulae during Berlin Heart EXCOR (BHE) support is a serious complication, with refractory infections often necessitating surgical intervention to prevent their progression to mediastinitis. However, the treatment options for such infections are limited. We report the case of a 4-year-old girl with truncus arteriosus who developed severe heart failure after palliative right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction and aortic valve replacement. The patient successfully underwent a combined surgical procedure consisting of ventricular septal defect and aortic valve closure, redo right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, and BHE implantation. However, at 10 months after BHE implantation, the outflow cannula exit site was infected by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis. Gallium-67 scintigraphy revealed tracer uptake along the abdominal outflow cannula tract without mediastinal extension. Because the prior aortic valve closure prevented temporary BHE explantation, surgical cannula exchange was performed together with mediastinal irrigation, omental flap transposition, and negative-pressure wound therapy. The infection resolved completely and no recurrent infection was observed during the 1-year follow-up period. In conclusion, cannula exchange combined with omental flap transposition is an effective surgical option for treating refractory cannula infections during BHE support when device explantation is not feasible.
journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
title: Cannula exchange for refractory cannula infections during Berlin Heart EXCOR support: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.
CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays are the diagnostic standard for acute coronary syndrome but present significant implementation and workflow complexity.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether implementation of a structured, electronic health record (EHR)-integrated hs-cTn pathway was associated with changes in emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS) and serial troponin testing times.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective quality improvement study compared preimplementation conventional cTn assay (June 1, 2021, to March 31, 2022) with a postimplementation integrated hs-cTn pathway (June 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023) in 4 urban EDs within a single health system. Participants were adults (aged ≥18 years) presenting with chest pain and at least 1 troponin assay result. Data analysis was performed from April to September 2024.
EXPOSURES: Implementation of an hs-cTn assay within an EHR-integrated clinical pathway.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was ED LOS, defined as time from patient registration to ED departure. Secondary outcomes included time from first clinician evaluation to disposition (discharge or admission) and interval from the first troponin assay order to the second troponin assay result in patients with serial assays.
RESULTS: Of the 16 094 patient encounters analyzed (9151 [56.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 49.5 [17.4] years), 8486 (52.7%) were in the hs-cTn and 7608 (47.3%) were in the conventional cTn cohort. Overall, hs-cTn implementation with workflow integration was associated with decreased mean ED LOS, from 6.18 (95% CI, 6.10-6.26) hours to 5.64 (95% CI, 5.57-5.71) hours. Compared with conventional cTn, implementation of the hs-cTn pathway was associated with shorter mean ED LOS in admitted patients (9.60 [95% CI, 9.35-9.87] hours vs 10.50 [95% CI, 10.22-10.78] hours; P = .003) and discharged patients (5.02 [95% CI, 4.96-5.08] hours vs 5.33 [95% CI, 5.26-5.40] hours; P = .006). Pathway implementation was also associated with shorter time from evaluation to disposition in patients receiving 2 or more troponin measurements (5.06 [95% CI, 4.97-5.15] hours vs 6.68 [95% CI, 6.52-6.85] hours; P < .001) and time from first troponin order to second troponin result in both admitted patients (3.18 [95% CI, 3.11-3.25] hours vs 5.16 [95% CI, 5.01-5.31] hours; P < .001) and discharged patients (2.78 [95% CI, 2.75-2.82] hours vs 4.54 [95% CI, 4.46-4.62] hours; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this quality improvement study, an EHR-integrated hs-cTn pathway was associated with significantly reduced ED LOS and, in patients with serial troponin measurements, reduced time from evaluation to disposition and reduced time to serial assay results. The findings suggest this structured EHR approach may mitigate operational challenges of hs-cTn adoption and could serve as a scalable model to improve ED efficiency for patients with chest pain.
title: High-Sensitivity Troponin Pathway and Emergency Department Length of Stay.

abstract: Anomalous aortic origin of the coronary arteries (AAOCA) is an infrequent finding that may increase the risk of coronary obstruction during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We report the case of an 80-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left coronary sinus, with an interarterial course and an acute takeoff angle. Preprocedural coronary angiography showed ostioproximal occlusion. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated approximately 80% extrinsic compression, and coronary physiologic assessment confirmed hemodynamically significant ischemia. Given the high risk of myocardial ischemia during TAVR, the RCA was treated with drug-eluting stents before valve implantation. Subsequently, transfemoral TAVR with a self-expandable valve was performed successfully, with preserved coronary patency and no complications. At 4-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with a normally functioning prosthetic valve and no hospital readmissions. This case underscores the importance of detailed preprocedural imaging, coronary physiology assessment, and individualized planning to minimize the risk of coronary obstruction in patients with high-risk AAOCA undergoing TAVR.
keywords: Anomalous aortic origin of the coronary arteries
title: TAVR in anomalous origin of the right coronary artery with interarterial course and acute takeoff angle.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust long-term data on the performance and durability of novel transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) valve designs, especially in Latin America, are lacking and warrant further investigation.
OBJECTIVES: To provide a 1 year follow-up data regarding a novel TAVI device.
METHODS: A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in Latin America of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis treated with the Vitaflow prosthesis from June 2022 to June 2023. The clinical endpoints were all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, vascular and bleeding complications, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM), and heart failure admission. Echocardiographic outcomes were the transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak at 1 year of follow-up.
RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients were included. The mean age of the patients was 80.9 ± 6.13 years; 50% were men, the mean STS score was 4.64 ± 2.67, and 60.8% were in NYHA class III/IV. The most used valve size was the 27 mm (47.1%). All-cause death at 1-year follow-up occurred in 4 patients (8.7%), of which 3 were cardiovascular (6.5%). There were 2 strokes, 1 vascular event, 2 major bleeding events, 4 new PPMs, and no myocardial infarctions or heart failure admissions. The 1-year mean transvalvular gradient was 7 ± 4 mmHg, and 3 patients (6.4%) had moderate paravalvular leak, with no severe leaks.
CONCLUSIONS: In a Latin American population, the Vitaflow TAVI valve has proved good safety and efficacy outcomes at 12 months of follow-up in the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis.
title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with Vitaflow prosthesis in Latin America.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aim: To investigate the potential use of anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with acute myocardial infarction (MI).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: During December 2025, a comprehensive search was conducted in the scientometric databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar for data from peer-reviewed English-language studies on the use of anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with CAD, published over the past 10 years. The search used the following terms: anti-inflammatory drugs, MI, acute coronary syndrome, chronic coronary syndrome, CVE, CAD, atherosclerosis. Preference was given to the most relevant sources of information, results of randomized placebo-controlled trials, international recommendations, metaanalyses, and more recent literary sources. A total of 94 literary sources were analyzed.
CONCLUSION: Conclusions: Measuring levels of inflammatory markers and using anti-inflammatory agents, particularly colchicine, in addition to baseline therapy in patients with acute MI to prevent recurrent index events is justified and promising.
title: Anti-inflammatory therapy in patients with coronary artery disease: A new era in the treatment of atherosclerosis or false hopes?

abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS) is a severe infection with a rising global incidence and potentially life-threatening neonatal outcomes. We present a late preterm infant exhibiting respiratory distress, hepatosplenomegaly, and systemic inflammation. Diagnosed with congenital syphilis at 12 hours of life, targeted antimicrobial was promptly initiated. Despite maximal medical management, her clinical course rapidly deteriorated into refractory shock, severe pulmonary hypertension, and multiple organ dysfunction. This necessitated venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). The infant underwent 7 days of VA-ECMO, 19 days of renal replacement therapy and 23 days of mechanical ventilation before successfully discharging with multidisciplinary follow-up. This case underscores the devastating potential of re-emerging congenital syphilis. It also highlights VA-ECMO as a viable rescue therapy for refractory neonatal shock, emphasizing the critical need for early referral to specialized centers.
title: Congenital syphilis requiring VA-ECMO: A case report.

abstract: Coronary artery disease commonly coexists with severe aortic stenosis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) candidates, yet optimal revascularization remains debated. We meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials comparing routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before or concomitant with TAVI versus conservative management. Major databases were searched through May 2026. Random-effects models calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and evidence certainty was evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Three randomized controlled trials (1156 patients; PCI: n = 579, conservative: n = 577) were included. Routine PCI was not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; P = 0.40), cardiac death (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.51-1.08; P = 0.12), myocardial infarction (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64; P = 0.64), stroke (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.48-1.03; P = 0.07), or hospitalization (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.87-1.32; P = 0.52). However, PCI significantly increased major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P = 0.0008), while reducing urgent and repeat revascularization. In conclusion, routine PCI before or concomitant with TAVI reduces subsequent revascularization without conferring survival or ischemic benefit, while increasing bleeding complications. Given the moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, limited cumulative sample size, and clinical heterogeneity across trials, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and favor an individualized, Heart Team-guided revascularization strategy over routine PCI.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 3 randomised trials; 1156 patients (PCI n = 579, conservative n = 577).
appraisal.main_limitation: Only three trials with limited cumulative sample size, clinical heterogeneity and moderate-to-low certainty of evidence.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of three randomised trials found that routine PCI before or with TAVI did not reduce death, MI or stroke but increased major bleeding while reducing repeat revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; major bleeding RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the randomised evidence on routine PCI in TAVI candidates and supports an individualised rather than routine revascularisation strategy.

title: Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status.
METHODS: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status.
RESULTS: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.
title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Istaroxime is an inotropic and lusitropic agent tested in acute heart failure (AHF) or AHF-related cardiogenic shock (AHF-CS). We aimed to assess its efficacy and concy in a pooled analysis of all randomized trials performed to date.
METHODS: Patient-level data from four phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials were pooled. The effects of istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min for up to 48 hours vs. placebo on hemodynamics, cardiac function, and clinical outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 284 patients were included (n=200 AHF, n=84 AHF-CS). Compared with placebo, istaroxime increased systolic blood pressure through 6 hours (least square [LS] mean difference in the area under the change from baseline curve 28.9 mmHg*h, 95% CI 18.1 to 39.8 mmHg*h) and through 24 hours (LS mean difference 121.4 mmHg*h, 95% CI 63.9 to 179.0 mmHg*h). Reductions in heart rate, body weight, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and echocardiographic E/e' ratio, and an increase in echocardiographic stroke work index and stroke volume were observed with istaroxime, with a numerically greater improvement in invasive cardiac output and creatinine. Numerically, dyspnea and quality of life were improved, and length of index hospitalization, worsening HF and death were lower with istaroxime. Serious adverse events were similar between the istaroxime and placebo arms.
CONCLUSIONS: In this patient-level pooled analysis, istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min was associated with improvement in SBP and hemodynamic and echocardiographic measurements of cardiac performance, without tachycardia or serious safety concerns. These findings support a phase III program to investigate the impact of istaroxime administration on outcomes.
title: Clinical effects of istaroxime in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock: A patient-level pooled analysis of four phase II randomized clinical trials.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effect of moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe is known to be non-inferior to high-intensity statin in prevention of adverse clinical events in patients with coronary atherosclerotic disease. However, data regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque remains limited.
METHODS: In this randomized, non-inferiority trial, patients with intermediate coronary artery stenosis were randomly assigned 1:1 to either moderate-intensity rosuvastatin (10 mg) with ezetimibe or high-intensity rosuvastatin (20 mg) group. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was performed at baseline and after 12 months or longer to quantify the coronary plaque response. Primary end point was absolute changes in percent atheroma volume (PAV) between baseline and follow-up IVUS, and non-inferiority margin was as 2.5%. Secondary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which was a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned repeat revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 280 patients underwent randomization. Follow-up IVUS showed absolute changes in PAV were - 1.286 ± 3.704% and - 1.302 ± 3.586%, respectively for moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe group and high-intensity rosuvastatin group. Mean difference between 2 groups (0.017%; 95% confidence interval: -0.957% to 0.991%) did not exceed noninferiority margin (non-inferiority p < 0.001). Both groups showed acceptable side effect profiles without group differences.
CONCLUSION: Compared with high-intensity rosuvastatin monotherapy, moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe was non-inferior regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque (Supported by Hanmi Pharmaceutical co., ltd; ROSUZET-IVUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03169985).
title: Moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe combination therapy versus high-intensity statin on coronary atherosclerotic plaque.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy are at increased risk for infection and sepsis due to malignancy-related immune dysfunction, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and immunosuppression used to treat CAR T-cell toxicities; however, nationally representative estimates of sepsis burden and economic impact remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: This study uses nationally representative U.S. data to evaluate patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and healthcare utilization associated with sepsis among hospitalizations involving CAR T-cell therapy.
STUDY DESIGN: Adult hospitalizations for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or multiple myeloma in which CAR T-cell therapy was administered between 2017 and 2022 were identified from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) and stratified by sepsis status. After excluding records with missing covariates, survey-weighted analyses were performed to generate nationally representative estimates. Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate differences in mortality and secondary outcomes, with statistical significance defined as a two-sided p value < 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 10,450 weighted CAR T-cell therapy hospitalizations, 645 (6.2%) were complicated by sepsis. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in hospitalizations with sepsis (28.7% vs 1.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 33.96; 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.67-61.75). Sepsis was independently associated with higher odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 4.31), respiratory failure (aOR 11.85), acute hepatic failure (aOR 44.42), and septic shock (aOR 411.05), along with greater use of renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressors. Thrombohemorrhagic events were more frequent among hospitalizations with sepsis, including disseminated intravascular coagulation (aOR 9.30), acute venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.95), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 27.63), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 7.53), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (aOR 6.47), and intracranial hemorrhage (aOR 4.84), as well as increased need for cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma transfusion (aOR 2.70). Sepsis was also associated with longer hospital stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.96) and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted charge ratio [aCR] 1.22).
CONCLUSIONS: Sepsis was documented in approximately 6% of CAR T-cell hospitalizations and was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, organ dysfunction, critical-care utilization, longer hospitalization, and higher hospitalization charges. These findings highlight the substantial clinical and healthcare burden associated with sepsis in this population.
title: Sepsis in Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy: A Six-Year Nationwide Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Healthcare Resource Utilization in Hospitalizations for Hematologic Malignancies.
Footprints, fingerprints, and the coronary culprit in MINOCA.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Changes in pacemaker implantation indications, population ageing, the emergence of leadless pacing systems and atrioventricular block following transcatheter aortic valve implantation may have influenced recent implantation trends.
AIMS: This nationwide study aimed to describe temporal trends and patient characteristics of permanent pacemaker implantation in France between 2018 and 2024.
METHODS: All patients newly implanted with a permanent pacemaker between 2018 and 2024 were identified using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Age- and sex-standardized annual incidence rates were calculated. Patient characteristics, hospitalization settings and device types were analysed, and national pacemaker prevalence was estimated for 2024.
RESULTS: In 2024, 492,583 patients were living with a permanent pacemaker in France (standardized prevalence of 645 per 100,000 population). A total of 51,739 incident implantations were identified (61.5% men; mean age 80.1 years), with 6.8% of procedures following TAVI. The median time to pacemaker replacement was 9.0 years (interquartile range 7.7-10.5). The age- and sex-standardized incidence rate slightly declined (83-73 per 100,000) over the study period, driven primarily by a reduction in implantations performed in private healthcare facilities. Although dual-chamber pacemakers remained the most frequently implanted devices, the use of leadless pacemakers within single-chamber systems has steadily increased since 2019 and was more frequent in less socioeconomically deprived populations, even after adjustment for comorbidity burden.
CONCLUSIONS: A modest decline in incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation was observed in France between 2018 and 2024, with a more pronounced decrease in private healthcare settings. The observed disparities, especially regarding access to leadless pacing systems, suggest potential differences in healthcare access or clinical practice patterns.
title: Temporal trends in permanent pacemaker implantations in France (2018-2024).

Corrigendum to "D-limonene pretreatment attenuates acute myocardial infarction injury and modulates PPARα-associated fatty acid oxidation and inflammatory stress" [Eur. J. Pharmacol. 1037 (2026) 179397].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial shunting is a novel strategy to reduce left atrial pressure and heart-failure (HF) morbidity. The Ventura Interatrial Shunt System (V-Wave) was evaluated in the randomized, sham-controlled RELIEVE-HF trial and reviewed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Circulatory Systems Devices Panel.
OBJECTIVES: To summarize the scientific and regulatory deliberations among the sponsor, FDA, and Advisory Panel regarding the safety, effectiveness, and benefit-risk profile V-Wave.
METHODS: We reviewed publicly available FDA documents, sponsor presentations, FDA analyses, and Advisory Panel discussions from the December 2025 meeting, with emphasis on trial design, endpoint selection, subgroup interpretation, and regulatory standards.
RESULTS: The sponsor emphasized reductions in recurrent HF events among patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), supported by prespecified recurrent-event analyses and echocardiographic data, while arguing that the hierarchical win-ratio primary endpoint underestimated benefits. In contrast, the FDA highlighted the failure to meet the prespecified primary endpoint in the intention-to-treat population, the fragility of subgroup findings, lack of outcome improvement, and consistent harm in patients with preserved ejection fraction. Advisory Panel members acknowledged acceptable procedural safety but expressed concern regarding the absence of clear, reproducible efficacy, challenges in phenotype-based labeling, and the inability of post-approval registries to resolve evidence gaps.
CONCLUSIONS: The Advisory Panel unanimously concluded that, despite procedural safety, the evidence did not demonstrate a favorable benefit-risk profile for the V-Wave device. The deliberations underscore the challenges of relying on subgroup analyses, recurrent-event endpoints, and post-market data to support approval of permanent intracardiac devices in this population.
