abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-radial intervention (TRI) has become the standard of care for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, in patients on dialysis, trans-femoral intervention (TFI) remains predominant to preserve upper-limb vessels for arteriovenous fistula despite heightened hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to compare TRI and TFI in dialysis patients undergoing PCI.
METHODS: We used the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry to compare patients on dialysis who underwent PCIs with TRI versus TFI from January 2018 to June 2025. An instrumental variable analysis with the institutional proportion of TRI use was performed to assess the risk of access-site bleeding and other peri-procedural outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 137,702 dialysis patients who underwent PCI, 28.3% of patients underwent TRI (n=38,901), while 71.7% patients underwent TFI (n=98,801). TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding at the access site (adjusted risk difference [aRD]: -0.35%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.56% to -0.15%). Overall bleeding (aRD: -1.38%; 95% CI: -1.89% to -0.87%), access-site hematoma (aRD: -0.86%; 95% CI: -1.13% to -0.60%), myocardial infarction (aRD: -0.21%; 95% CI: -0.39% to -0.03%), and mortality (aRD: -1.07%; 95% CI: -1.64% to -0.51%) were also less frequently observed in TRI. Conversely, TRI was associated with a higher risk of stroke (aRD: 0.23%; 95% CI: 0.001% to 0.45%), driven primarily by ischemic stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding events, but the effect size was modest. The higher observed stroke risk highlights a potential ischemic trade-off and warrants further study.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
last_author_country: Department of Cardiology Keio University School of Medicine Tokyo Japan
title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Dialysis Patients: Insights from a Nationwide Registry Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are an established alternative to drug-eluting stents (DESs) for selected coronary lesions, offering the potential advantages of a stent-free strategy while avoiding permanent metallic implantation. This study compared real-world utilisation patterns, clinical outcomes, and patient-reported outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCBs and DESs.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up included 214 consecutive patients who underwent PCI with either a DCB (n = 64) or DES (n = 150) between January 2023 and March 2026. Baseline demographic, angiographic, procedural, and clinical characteristics were compared. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at follow-up using a questionnaire adapted from the domains of the Seattle Angina Questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with DCB utilisation.
RESULTS: The study included 214 patients (mean age 56.55 ± 11.49 years), of whom 72.9% were male. Clinical presentation differed significantly between groups (p = 0.042), the ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) group more frequently underwent DES (46.0% vs. 29.7%), whereas non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (37.5% vs. 30.7%) and Unstable Angina​ (UA) (15.6% vs. 6.0%) were more common in the DCB group. DCBs were preferentially used in patients with previous coronary revascularization, ISR, small-vessel disease and elective PCI, whereas DESs were more commonly used for acute PCI, total occlusive lesions, and lesions with calcification or thrombus (all p < 0.05). Previous coronary revascularization was associated with increased odds of DCB use, while acute PCI was associated with reduced odds of DCB use compared with elective PCI. No significant differences were observed between groups in mortality at 1, 3, or 6 months, other early clinical outcomes, or patient-reported outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: DCBs were preferentially used in specific clinical and anatomical settings while demonstrating low observed rates of short-term clinical events and no statistically significant between-group differences in patient-reported outcomes. Despite differences in lesion complexity and treatment selection, no significant differences in early outcomes were observed compared with DES. These findings describe contemporary real-world DCB utilisation in a Sri Lankan PCI centre and provide a basis for further multicentre evaluation.
journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
title: Utilisation patterns and exploratory short-term outcomes of drug-coated balloon versus drug-eluting stent in percutaneous coronary intervention: a single-centre observational cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: DAPT continuation beyond 12 months post-DES implantation in event free patients remains unresolved; prior meta-analyses pooled heterogeneous durations and used P2Y12, not aspirin, as comparator.
METHODS: Four databases were searched through August 2026 for RCTs of continued DAPT vs. aspirin monotherapy in event free patients at 1 year post-stenting, with prespecified duration and P2Y12 subgroups and TSA. Post-hoc subgroup analyses by baseline ischemic risk and patient ethnicity, and an incidence rate ratio sensitivity analysis accounting for differential follow up duration, were also performed.
RESULTS: Six RCTs (N = 28,601) were included. Extended DAPT showed no MACCE benefit (RR 0.89, 0.72-1.10) or bleeding (RR 1.19, 0.66-2.14), but reduced non-fatal MI (RR 0.60, 0.51-0.71; only outcome crossing TSA boundary), consistent across strata; a two trial P2Y12 interaction was hypothesis generating; remaining endpoints inconclusive. Incidence rate ratio sensitivity analysis confirmed these findings were not affected by differential follow up duration. Exploratory post-hoc subgroup analyses revealed significant interactions by baseline ischemic risk and patient ethnicity for all-cause mortality and MACCE, with extended DAPT trending toward benefit in higher risk and non-East Asian trials and toward a null or harmful effect in lower risk and East Asian trials.
CONCLUSIONS: Extended DAPT beyond 12 months lowers non-fatal MI risk without a confirmed net effect on ischemic or bleeding outcomes; first review with prespecified duration/P2Y12 stratification and TSA. Exploratory analyses further suggest this ischemic benefit may vary by baseline ischemic risk and patient ethnicity, a hypothesis generating signal warranting confirmation in future trials.
title: Continued dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin monotherapy beyond 12 months after drug eluting stent implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation programs have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional center-based rehabilitation, offering improved accessibility and convenience for patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation in improving clinical outcomes in this population.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, EMBASE, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Cochrane Library from July 2012 to June 2024. Randomized controlled trials and non-randomized studies evaluating telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation after PCI were included. Outcomes assessed included exercise capacity, blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), quality of life, smoking cessation, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction, and mortality. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using standardized mean differences (SMDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. Telehealth-based interventions significantly improved exercise capacity (SMD = 0.703, 95% CI: 0.382-1.023; p < 0.001) and quality of life (SMD = 0.529, 95% CI: 0.232-0.826; p < 0.001). No statistically significant effects were observed for blood pressure, BMI, smoking cessation, myocardial infarction, or mortality. A potentially clinically important but statistically non-significant trend toward reduced MACE was observed (RR = 0.487, 95% CI: 0.233-1.019; p = 0.056). Although the point estimate corresponds to an approximately 51% relative risk reduction, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because only four studies contributed to the analysis, the confidence interval crossed the null value, and MACE definitions varied across studies.
CONCLUSION: Telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation improves exercise capacity and quality of life in patients undergoing PCI. A potentially clinically important trend toward reduced MACE was also observed, although this finding remains uncertain because of the limited number of contributing studies, wide confidence interval, and variability in MACE definitions. Evidence for other cardiovascular risk factors and clinical endpoints remains limited. Further adequately powered randomized controlled trials with standardized interventions, outcome definitions, and longer follow-up are required.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID: CRD420261287216.
title: Effectiveness of telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health issues are a globally prevalent problem. Psychological distress (PD) is an emotional and behavioural response to a stressor and can even lead to mental health disease. It is also associated with cardiovascular disease including acute coronary syndrome.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted to assess psychological distress using a Kessler's psychological distress scale (K10) in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome in a primary percutaneous coronary intervention centre in Sri Lanka. Hundred and fifty-seven patients were enrolled. Data was collected from an interviewer-and self-administered questionnaires. Patient demographics, socio-economic, behavioural and clinical & therapeutic details were obtained and analysed using Chi-square tests and Polytomous Universal Model (PLUM) ordinal regression for cross comparison with varying levels of psychological distress [no distress, mild distress, moderate distress or severe distress].
RESULTS: The mean age was 52.9 ± 11.01 years and 40.8% of the sampled patients had varying levels of psychological distress. On initial bivariate analysis screening recent emotional distress, inadequate sleep, regular religious activity showed statistically significant correlation with PD (P < 0.05). However, when adjusting for confounders in the multivariate PLUM ordinal regression only recent emotional disturbance (P < 0.001) [aOR = 19.71, 95% CI:8.00-48.52) and inadequate sleep duration (P = 0.019) [aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.17-5.62] retained independent significance as predictors of distress severity. Other behavioural and clinical disease attributes became attenuated in the multivariate model.
CONCLUSION: Psychological distress is prevalent among patients with acute coronary syndrome. The immediate emotional burden after ACS is independently associated with patients' pre-existing emotional baseline and lifestyle biology rather than clinical disease and its severity.
title: Psychological distress among acute coronary syndrome patients - a descriptive cross-sectional study in patients managed at an interventional cardiology unit in Sri Lanka.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While smoking cessation reduces cardiovascular risk, the precise timeline and temporal dynamics of risk reduction using granular time intervals remain poorly characterized. We aimed to estimate the association between smoking cessation duration and cardiovascular risk using 2-year intervals in a large Asian cohort.
DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: South Korea, using the nationwide National Health Insurance Service database (2002-2023).
PARTICIPANTS: 1 349 545 adults without prior acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or AMI requiring percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) who underwent at least four biennial health examinations, comprising 1 059 469 never smokers, 60 927 quitters and 229 149 current smokers.
MEASUREMENTS: Smoking status was classified from repeated self-reported examinations; quitters were grouped by cessation duration in 2-year intervals up to ≥8 years. Outcomes were incident AMI and AMI requiring PCI, over a mean follow-up of 10.6 years. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic, clinical and lifestyle covariates including pack-years, with current smokers and never smokers as reference groups.
RESULTS: Using current smokers as reference, adjusted HRs decreased progressively with longer cessation duration. Statistically significant risk reduction was evident within 2-3 years [AMI: HR = 0.475, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.403-0.559; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.437, 95% CI = 0.359-0.532]. Quitters who maintained cessation for ≥8 years achieved risk levels comparable to never smokers (AMI: HR = 0.396, 95% CI = 0.284-0.552 vs. HR = 0.407, 95% CI = 0.386-0.429; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.321, 95% CI = 0.209-0.493 vs. HR = 0.366, 95% CI = 0.343-0.389).
SUMMARY: In a nationwide Korean cohort, the risk of acute myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction requiring percutaneous coronary intervention declined progressively with longer smoking cessation; after 8 or more years of sustained abstinence, risk was no longer distinguishable from that of never-smokers.
title: Smoking cessation duration and risk of acute myocardial infarction: A nationwide cohort study in Korea.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), one of the leading causes of death in the United States, requires rapid evaluation, diagnosis, and therapy initiation to reduce morbidity and mortality. Delayed care-seeking remains the primary reason that patients with ACS fail to receive timely treatment. Remote cardiac monitoring may supplement individuals' symptom appraisal and reduce delays. However, ACS patients' ability to remotely self-acquire an electrocardiogram (ECG) is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether hospitalized patients with suspected ACS can acquire a derived 12-lead (L) ECG using a KardiaMobile 6L remote cardiac monitoring device.
METHODS: Participants were hospitalized patients aged >21 years at high risk for ischemic events (ACS diagnosis with a History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin score >3, ie, moderate to high risk for cardiac event) who owned an iPhone. Research assistants trained participants to use mobile applications to (1) acquire an ECG at least once daily during their hospitalization and (2) document symptoms using the ACS Symptom Checklist. A cardiologist blinded to clinical data compared ischemic markers (eg, ST-elevation, ST-depression, and T-wave inversion) on KardiaMobile 6L derived 12L ECGs with hospital-based 12L ECGs.
RESULTS: We enrolled 30 participants (mean age 64.2 ± 11.2 years, 30.0% female, 73.3% White). All participants acquired at least 1 remote cardiac device ECG. A cardiologist classified 88.9% as clean and interpretable; the remainder were noisy but interpretable. Ischemic markers were present on both patient-acquired and hospital-based ECGs. All participants submitted at least 1 Symptom Checklist.
CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalized patients with suspected ACS can self-acquire a 6L ECG and self-report symptoms, and derived 12L ECGs can detect signs of ischemia (eg, ST-elevation). Future studies should examine ECG acquisition and transmission from home and remote evaluation for early ischemia detection and response.
first_author_country: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
title: Can Patients Self-Acquire Diagnostic Quality Electrocardiograms for Acute Coronary Syndrome?: A Feasibility Study of Remote Cardiac Monitoring and Symptom Reporting.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microcatheters are essential in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but their structural failure has mainly been described through passive surveillance.
AIMS: We aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and procedural impact of microcatheter structural damage during contemporary CTO PCI.
METHODS: The prospective multicentre CROSS registry included 2137 CTO PCI procedures performed at high-volume centers between 2024 and 2025. Suspected damaged microcatheters underwent centralized assessment and were classified as grade 1 (superficial deformation), grade 2 (significant deformation without complete fracture), or grade 3 (complete fracture).
RESULTS: Structural damage occurred in 109 procedures (5.1%); 58.7%, 5.5%, and 35.8% were grade 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Independent predictors of structural microcatheter damage were moderate-to-severe calcification (adjusted OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.27-2.94), retrograde approach (adjusted OR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.67), moderate-to-severe tortuosity (adjusted OR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.04-2.50), and longer procedure duration (adjusted OR per 30-min increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30). Structural damage was associated with increased periprocedural complications (25.7% vs. 7.7%; OR: 4.12, 95% CI: 2.60-6.52; p < 0.0001) and failed CTO PCI (11.0% vs. 3.1%; OR: 3.86, 95% CI: 2.01-7.39; p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: Structural microcatheter damage occurred in approximately 1 in 20 CTO PCIs and was associated with anatomical complexity, demanding procedural circumstances, and substantially worse procedural outcomes.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Structural Damage of Coronary Microcatheters During Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Interventions: The Prospective Multicenter Cross Registry.

abstract: We report a case of very severe aortic stenosis (AS) in which side-branch occlusion during elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) precipitated life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and hemodynamic collapse. The patient was a 72-year-old man with very severe AS who was scheduled to undergo a valve intervention. Preprocedural coronary angiography revealed a significant, newly developed stenosis in the right coronary artery, and an elective PCI was performed prior to valve treatment. Following intravascular lithotripsy and drug-eluting stent implantation, occlusion of the conus branch occurred, triggering recurrent ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Despite initiation of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support, the patient's hemodynamic status did not improve. Because excessive afterload due to very severe AS was considered the principal pathophysiological mechanism, emergency balloon aortic valvuloplasty was performed. This resulted in rapid hemodynamic stabilization and complete resolution of ventricular arrhythmias. This case illustrates that even a minor side-branch occlusion during PCI can lead to catastrophic outcomes in patients with very severe AS. Furthermore, it highlights that mechanical circulatory support alone may be insufficient, and that prompt relief of valvular obstruction is essential. Careful consideration of the indications and sequence of coronary intervention through discussions with a heart team is warranted for patients with very severe AS.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Electrical Storm Triggered by Conus Branch Occlusion During Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Very Severe Aortic Stenosis: Rescue With Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty Under Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.

abstract: Distal coronary artery perforation (CAP) during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is traditionally managed with embolic coils or autologous fat. However, fat embolization can be technically demanding due to complex tissue harvesting and delivery. We describe a closed-needle lower abdominal micro-suction technique enabling rapid percutaneous harvesting and direct microcatheter delivery of an autologous fat suspension without benchtop processing. An 18-gauge angiographic needle attached to a syringe pre-loaded with 2-3 mL of a 1:1 contrast-saline mixture is inserted into lower abdominal subcutaneous tissue under continuous manual negative pressure, aspirating 1-2 mL of fat-containing tissue fragments within ~10 s (total final volume ~3.5-5 mL). The resulting radiopaque suspension is delivered directly through a microcatheter using an inverted-syringe technique via small, incremental hand boluses of 0.25-0.5 mL until complete sealing is achieved. Descriptive histology confirmed mature adipose tissue fragments admixed with blood, fibrin, and clot. The technique was successfully deployed in two consecutive patients with Ellis type II and III distal CAP. Immediate angiographic sealing was achieved in both cases without open tissue processing or syringe-to-syringe transfer. At 6-month follow-up, both patients remained clinically stable without recurrent pericardial effusion or target-vessel failure. Closed-needle abdominal micro-suction is a rapid, low-resource, zero-transfer bailout technique for autologous fat embolization in high-acuity distal CAPs.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Closed-Needle Abdominal Micro-Suction Fat Embolization for Distal Coronary Perforation.

abstract:
AIMS: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, is approved for cardiovascular risk reduction in individuals with overweight or obesity and cardiovascular disease. Whether tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, has similar cardiovascular benefits remains unknown. The objective was to compare the effectiveness of semaglutide versus tirzepatide on the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in individuals with overweight or obesity and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) without diabetes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This active comparator, new user study emulated a trial using national claims data from Komodo Health. Eligible individuals had a history of ASCVD and, within 1 year prior to initiation: BMI ≥ 27 with a diagnosis of overweight or obesity, continuous insurance coverage and no diabetes or contraindications. Prior GLP-1 receptor agonist or obesity medication users were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina, coronary revascularization and mortality (revised 5-point MACE). Secondary outcomes included revised 3-point MACE and individual endpoints. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox models with inverse probability weighting.
RESULTS: There was a non-significant difference in risk of revised 5-point MACE (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.99-1.51) or secondary outcomes between semaglutide and tirzepatide. Sensitivity analyses showed directionally consistent point estimates for revised 5-point MACE but highlighted sensitivity to decisions surrounding early events, off-label use, analytic approach and outcome definition.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with overweight or obesity and ASCVD without diabetes, there was no significant difference in cardiovascular risk between semaglutide and tirzepatide.
title: Cardiovascular Outcomes in Semaglutide Versus Tirzepatide Users With Obesity and Atherosclerotic Disease: A Target Trial Emulation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery implantation of the absorb bioresorbable vascular scaffold (BVS) without intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance resulted in greater adverse events compared with metallic drug-eluting stents during 3-year follow-up.
AIMS: We assessed the 10-year outcomes of BVS implanted with routine use of IVI guidance.
METHODS: Between November 2014 and October 2016, 100 consecutive patients in whom the operator elected to implant a BVS were treated with 190 BVS devices in 171 lesions at a single center in Brazil. IVI was performed before and after BVS implantation in all patients. Clinical follow-up was complete in all patients (no losses to follow-up) for at least 8.8 years.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 9.5 years (25th percentile 9.2, 75th percentile 10.1), range 8.8-10.8 years. Through the latest follow-up, no patient experienced a cardiac death or definite scaffold thrombosis, and only one patient had a target-vessel MI (TVMI). Major adverse cardiac events (the composite of all-cause death, any MI, or any revascularization) occurred in 29 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimated 10-year rate 29.4%); target vessel failure (TVF) (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization) occurred in 15 patients (10-year rate 15.0%); and target lesion failure (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-lesion revascularization) occurred in 10 patients (10-year rate 10.0%). In the landmark analysis, TVF between 3 and 10 years occurred in 7 patients (7.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, non-randomized observational study, the long-term outcomes of BVS implantation in simple and complex coronary lesions with routine IVI guidance were favorable. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered randomized studies.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Long-Term Outcomes After Coronary Absorb BVS Implantation Guided by Intravascular Imaging.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical evidence regarding the prognostic value of the platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) for short-term outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains limited, particularly its independent predictive role for in-hospital and ICU all-cause mortality, which lacks validation in large-scale, multi-center settings. This study investigated the association between PWR and in-hospital and ICU mortality in AMI patients, aiming to evaluate its impact on short-term prognosis in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2,381 AMI patients from the MIMIC-IV database as the derivation cohort, with validation performed in 7,054 AMI patients from the multi-center eICU-CRD database and 252 AMI patients from a single-center internal cohort. Restricted cubic spline and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess nonlinearity and survival differences. Multivariable logistic regression examined the independent association between PWR and in-hospital and ICU mortality. Decision curve analysis assessed the clinical utility of PWR. Subgroup analyses, Cox regression, Fine-Gray competing-risk models, and mediation analyses were conducted for robustness assessment and mechanistic exploration.
RESULTS: In the derivation cohort of this study, 316 patients (13.3%) died during hospitalization and 237 (10.0%) died during ICU stay. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a consistent linear relationship between PWR and the risks of in-hospital and ICU mortality. Multivariable logistic regression revealed a significant inverse association between PWR and in-hospital mortality (OR = 0.976, 95% CI: 0.960-0.991, P = 0.003) as well as ICU mortality (OR = 0.977, 95% CI: 0.959-0.994, P = 0.012). The robustness of this inverse association was further supported by Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. The results were consistently reproduced in both the external eICU-CRD validation cohort and the single-center internal validation cohort. Additionally, Kaplan-Meier curves showed that patients in the higher PWR group had significantly better cumulative survival than those in the lower PWR group. Decision curve analysis further showed that PWR provided some net benefit at clinically relevant thresholds for both outcomes, supporting its clinical utility. In subgroup analyses, the inverse association between PWR and short-term mortality remained directionally consistent across all subgroups, with no significant interactions after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Mediation analysis indicated that SAPS II score and vasopressor use mediated 25.9% and 18.6% of the protective effect of PWR, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: PWR is a simple, low-cost composite marker derived from routine complete blood counts. It is significantly and inversely associated with short-term in-hospital and ICU mortality in AMI patients. Our findings suggest that PWR may serve as a convenient and inexpensive adjunctive tool for early risk stratification and identification of high-risk individuals. However, its clinical application warrants further validation in larger, multi-center prospective studies.
title: Association between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and short-term prognosis in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial enlargement (LAE) is common in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but its prognostic significance may vary according to the clinical drivers of atrial remodeling. We examined whether prognostic factors differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype in patients undergoing TAVI with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 317 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing TAVI who had preserved LVEF and LAE. Patients were classified as AS-associated LAE (no atrial fibrillation [AF] and <moderate mitral regurgitation [MR]) or AF/MR-associated LAE (AF and/or ≥moderate MR). The primary endpoint was all-cause death. During a median follow-up of 2.7 years, 69 patients (21.8%) died. The all-cause mortality rate was higher in the AF/MR-associated group than in the AS-associated LAE group (30.7% vs. 19.0%; log-rank P<0.01), but this association was attenuated after adjustment for eGFR, log-BNP, and LAVI. In the AS-associated LAE group, higher log-BNP (hazard ratio (HR) 1.45, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.98), higher E/e' (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and lower TAPSE (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.99) predicted death. In the AF/MR-associated LAE group, lower eGFR (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-1.00) and higher log-BNP (HR 1.98, 95% CI 1.09-3.59) predicted death after adjustment for age. Interactions were significant for eGFR and E/e'.
CONCLUSIONS: Prognostic markers after TAVI differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype, supporting subtype-informed risk stratification.
first_author_country: Osaka Metropolitan University Graduate School of Medicine Osaka Japan
last_author_country: Osaka Metropolitan University Graduate School of Medicine Osaka Japan
title: Prognostic Implications of Clinically Attributed Left Atrial Enlargement Subtypes in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The frequency, distribution, and optical coherence tomography (OCT) features of radial artery calcification (RAC) remain poorly defined. We assessed OCT-defined RAC and factors associated with patient-level RAC.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 461 patients with analyzable radial artery OCT (RA-OCT) between January 2021 and August 2025. RAC was assessed at the patient, segment, and lesion levels. Clinical characteristics, radial artery plaque features, coronary OCT findings, and factors associated with patient-level RAC were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 461 patients in the final analytic cohort, OCT-defined RAC was identified in 61 (13.2%). RAC involved the proximal, middle, and distal segments in 17/461 (3.7%), 25/461 (5.4%), and 52/461 (11.3%) patients, respectively. Among 214 calcified lesions, spotty calcification was the most common morphology (151/214, 70.6%). In exploratory patient-level analyses, all five radial artery plaque features were associated with RAC after multivariable adjustment, and all associations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. In multivariable analysis, older age, diabetes mellitus, and coronary calcific nodule remained associated with RAC, whereas coronary calcium score was not statistically associated with RAC after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, OCT-defined RAC was identified in 13.2% of patients, was more frequent in the distal segment, and showed heterogeneous lesion-level phenotypes. Older age, diabetes mellitus, and coronary calcific nodule were associated with RAC. Exploratory analyses also showed associations between RAC and multiple noncalcified radial artery plaque features.
title: Optical coherence tomography-defined radial artery calcification: frequency, phenotypes, and correlates in a retrospective transradial PCI cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictors of successful venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) weaning have been reported, but their integration into sequential reassessment remains unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 48 adults with cardiogenic shock receiving VA-ECMO. Exploratory stepwise models were constructed using variables available at ECMO initiation, 24, and 48 h. The 48-h model included female sex, pulse pressure, EtCO2, levels of lactate, and creatinine.
CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory stepwise models using routinely available variables may provide a framework for sequential VA-ECMO weaning assessment. External validation is required.
last_author_country: Fujita Health University School of Health Sciences Faculty of Nursing Aichi Japan
title: Stepwise Scoring Models for Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract: Coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR) remains an important limitation of percutaneous coronary intervention despite the use of drug-eluting stents. ISR is a heterogeneous process driven by neointimal hyperplasia, neoatherosclerosis, and mechanical factors such as stent underexpansion or fracture. Intravascular imaging, particularly IVUS and OCT, enables mechanism-guided lesion preparation and device selection, while metabolomics, molecular imaging, and circulating biomarkers are improving understanding of its biological heterogeneity. Adequate lesion preparation is fundamental, and drug-coated balloons and repeat drug-eluting stent implantation remain the principal treatment strategies. Adjunctive techniques such as intravascular lithotripsy may help in severely calcified or resistant underexpanded lesions. Emerging evidence also implicates sphingolipid metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, immune-inflammatory signaling, and systemic metabolic modulation in ISR, though clinical relevance requires validation. This review summarizes recent advances in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, risk factors, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of ISR, emphasizing the shift from anatomy-based management toward mechanism-guided, individualized therapy.
title: Recent advances in coronary in-stent restenosis: a comprehensive narrative review.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection in Pyridoxine-Responsive Classical Homocystinuria: Expanding the Arterial Phenotype.

abstract: Vasospastic angina (VSA) is an important and potentially treatable cause of cardiac arrest (CA) and may account for approximately 2-10% of otherwise unexplained cases of out-of-hospital CA. VSA can sometimes be diagnosed by spontaneous coronary spasm during emergency coronary angiography or by transient ST-segment elevation during a spontaneous attack after resuscitation. However, because coronary spasm is transient and may not be evident during the initial evaluation, provocation testing after clinical stabilization may be required to establish the diagnosis in otherwise unexplained cases. Once VSA is diagnosed, vasodilator therapy, particularly calcium-channel blockers, is the mainstay of treatment. Nevertheless, survivors of VSA-related CA may remain at risk of recurrent lethal ventricular arrhythmias despite medical therapy. Evaluation for alternative or overlapping arrhythmogenic disorders, including cardiomyopathies and channelopathies, should therefore be considered even after a diagnosis of VSA, and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation may be considered in selected patients according to the risk of recurrence and response to medical therapy. Further prospective studies, including randomized controlled trials, are needed to determine whether systematic provocation testing followed by targeted therapy reduces recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and CA and improves long-term outcomes.

title: Vasospastic Angina and Cardiac Arrest.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently occurs in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Kidney recovery after AKI is heterogeneous, and the prognostic significance of kidney dysfunction persisting to the 3-6-month assessment remains incompletely defined. We evaluated whether registry-defined incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) following AKI was associated with subsequent death and myocardial infarction (MI).
METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter PCI registry included STEMI patients treated with primary PCI between January 2010 and November 2020. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria. Kidney trajectory was classified as no AKI, transient AKI with recovery, or registry-defined incident CKD following AKI based on kidney function assessed at 3-6 months. To minimize guarantee-time bias, Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses began at a 6-month landmark. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, LVEF, and baseline MDRD eGFR.
RESULTS: Among 1,239 patients, 941 had no AKI, 56 had transient AKI, and 242 had incident CKD following AKI; the overall AKI incidence was 24.1%. The strict 6-month landmark cohort comprised 1,129 patients (869 no AKI, 48 transient AKI, and 212 incident CKD). Compared with no AKI, incident CKD was associated with all-cause death (multivariable Cox HR 4.06, 95% CI 1.23-13.45; P = 0.022), MI (multivariable Cox HR 4.49, 95% CI 1.79-11.30; P = 0.001), and death and/or MI (multivariable Cox HR 4.35, 95% CI 2.07-9.14; P < 0.001), whereas transient AKI was not significantly associated with these outcomes. In the two-group analysis, incident CKD was similarly associated with death (multivariable Cox HR 3.44, 95% CI 1.18-10.06; P = 0.024), MI (multivariable Cox HR 3.75, 95% CI 1.59-8.87; P = 0.003), and death and/or MI (multivariable Cox HR 3.61, 95% CI 1.83-7.14; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Registry-defined incident CKD after in-hospital AKI identified a subgroup of STEMI survivors with substantially higher post-landmark risks of death and MI. Kidney recovery trajectory may provide clinically useful prognostic information beyond the occurrence of AKI alone.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04650529. Registered on 25 January 2021. Retrospectively registered.
title: Registry-defined incident chronic kidney disease following acute kidney injury after primary PCI for STEMI and its association with long-term outcomes: a multicenter landmark analysis.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peripheral microvascular endothelial function measured by the reactive hyperemia index (RHI) with EndoPAT predicts cardiovascular outcomes, and post-procedural RHI has been associated with binary in-stent restenosis. Whether pre-procedural RHI relates to in-stent late lumen loss (LLL) measured by quantitative coronary angiography (QCA) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and whether any association depends on device caliber, has not been established.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients who underwent EndoPAT before PCI (index PCI 2009-2016). The primary endpoint was in-stent LLL at follow-up angiography (n = 91; median follow-up 9.4 months). Because in-stent LLL was highly skewed, the primary analysis used Spearman correlation and a robust (HC3) multivariable regression adjusting for age, diabetes, hypertension, number of diseased vessels, and pre-PCI minimal lumen diameter. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation (MICE, m = 20) for missing follow-up and lesion-level generalized estimating equations (GEE). Subgroup analyses by implanted stent diameter (≤2.75 versus >2.75 mm) and diabetes were exploratory.
RESULTS: RHI showed only a borderline inverse correlation with in-stent LLL (ρ = -0.19, p = 0.07) and was not independently associated with it (adjusted β = -0.11, 95% CI -0.39 to +0.18, p = 0.45); multiple imputation (β = -0.08) and GEE (β = -0.07) were concordant, and no correlation survived false-discovery-rate correction. Stratification by native reference vessel diameter showed no association, whereas stratification by implanted stent diameter revealed an inverse RHI-LLL correlation confined to small-diameter stents (≤2.75 mm, n = 33; ρ = -0.375, p = 0.032) but not larger stents (ρ = -0.055). However, the stent-diameter × RHI interaction was not significant (p = 0.48), so this caliber-dependent signal is hypothesis-generating and tracks the achieved implanted caliber rather than the native reference vessel. Inflammation explained neither result. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was unrelated to RHI (ρ = -0.02) and to in-stent LLL (ρ = +0.15), and adding it to the primary model left the RHI estimate unchanged. Small-caliber recipients had similar hs-CRP but more diabetes (57.6% versus 27.6%, p = 0.009) and worse renal function (p = 0.008), indicating a higher-risk phenotype rather than a pure caliber stratum.
DISCUSSION: Pre-procedural EndoPAT RHI was not independently associated with in-stent LLL. The exploratory signal confined to small-caliber stents is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective, device-caliber-stratified validation pairing pre- with post-procedural RHI.
title: Peripheral microvascular function and in-stent late lumen loss after percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study with an exploratory analysis by implanted stent diameter.

keywords: Recurrent myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection revealed by an iatrogenic spasm provocation test.

abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicating acute MI (AMI-CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity, despite advances in coronary revascularisation and mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Outcomes are determined not only by individual therapies, but also by the organisation of care, with current guidelines emphasising multidisciplinary, system-level approaches to enable rapid diagnosis, triage and treatment. This review examines how CS centres function within regional networks of care. We review definitions of AMI-CS, including haemodynamic, clinical and biochemical markers and their application to early identification and triage. We summarise key components of centre-based management, including revascularisation, invasive haemodynamic assessment, selective MCS use and post-percutaneous coronary intervention critical care. Contemporary data from dedicated CS centres and regionalised network models are compared, highlighting variations in transfer criteria and hub-spoke organisation alongside limitations in current evidence. The distinct phenotypic nuances of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest-associated CS are discussed and gaps in evidence with future perspectives are highlighted.
title: Role of Cardiogenic Shock Centres and Regionalised Networks for Acute MI-related Cardiogenic Shock: State-of-the-art Review on Behalf of the British Cardiovascular Interventional Society Focus Group.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and a prior history of ischemic stroke (IS) represent a high-risk population with limited prognostic tools. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting all-cause mortality in AMI patients with prior IS.
METHODS: This prospective single-center cohort included 543 consecutive patients with AMI and prior IS who underwent Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable Cox regression, Boruta, and LASSO Cox regression. Six survival models were compared: Cox, elastic-net Cox, random survival forest (RSF), GBM survival, XGBoost survival, and Survival SVM. Internal validation used 100 bootstrap resamples with out-of-bag (OOB) evaluation. Performance was evaluated using Harrell's C-index, IPCW time-dependent AUC, calibration measures, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis. SHAP-based and permutation analyses were used for model interpretation.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 3.03 years, 66 patients (12.2%) died. Six predictors were selected: age, hemoglobin, prognostic nutritional index, estimated glomerular filtration rate, atherogenic index of plasma, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio. Although RSF achieved the numerically highest OOB C-index, elastic-net Cox showed comparable discrimination, better calibration, a lower 3-year Brier score, and greater interpretability and was selected as the final model. Its OOB C-index was 0.714 (95% CI 0.616-0.790), and its 1-, 2-, and 3-year IPCW AUCs were 0.745, 0.704, and 0.701, respectively. Age and hemoglobin made the largest contributions to model predictions. Elastic-net Cox showed numerically better performance than GRACE, but statistical superiority in discrimination was not demonstrated.
CONCLUSIONS: The six-variable elastic-net Cox model provided moderate discrimination and relatively favorable calibration. Independent external validation and prospective implementation studies are required before clinical use.
title: Mortality prediction in patients with acute myocardial infarction and prior ischemic stroke: a prospective cohort study with explainable machine learning and SHAP analysis.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: Left ventricular (LV) pseudoaneurysm is an uncommon, life-threatening sequela of myocardial injury, defined by contained rupture of the ventricular free wall by pericardium or scar tissue rather than intact myocardium. Unlike true aneurysms, pseudoaneurysms carry a rupture risk of 30%-45% and a 1-week mortality of 48% in medically managed patients, making prompt diagnosis and accurate differentiation critical for patient survival. Multimodality imaging - chest radiography, echocardiography, CT and cardiac MRI (CMR) - is indispensable in assessing morphology, haemodynamic impact, tissue characterisation, thrombus burden and systemic complications. Cardiac MRI serves as the reference standard for differentiating pseudoaneurysm from true aneurysm and for risk stratification.
CONTRIBUTION: This case series highlights the pivotal role of imaging in the surgical and conservative management planning of LV pseudoaneurysm.
title: A case series on the role of multimodality imaging in the diagnosis, risk stratification and complications of left ventricular pseudoaneurysm.

abstract: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Under-preparation of calcified plaque predisposes to stent under-expansion, mal-apposition, restenosis, and stent thrombosis, while over-aggressive debulking strategies carry risk of dissection, perforation, and no-reflow. The interventional armamentarium for calcium modification has expanded from high-pressure and non-high pressure specialty balloons including intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) to dedicated atherectomy devices i.e., rotational atherectomy (RA), orbital atherectomy (OA), and excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA), each with a distinct mechanism, evidence base, and risk profile. Additionally, comprehensive assessment of coronary calcium is central to guiding lesion preparation and selecting treatment strategy, with IVUS and OCT providing detailed intravascular characterisation, and CT emerging as a complementary non-invasive tool for procedural planning. Appropriate procedural planning and judicious selection of calcium-modification tools are paramount to maximising procedural safety, minimising complications, and improving clinical outcomes. This review summarizes the pathophysiology of CAC, describes each modification technique, synthesizes the pivotal and recent randomised evidence, outlines current guideline position, and proposes a practical framework for balancing procedural innovation against patient safety. Current evidence supports an individualized, imaging-guided approach to calcium modification. Balloon-based strategies, IVL, atherectomy, and ELCA each have specific strengths and limitations, and no modality has demonstrated universal superiority across lesion subsets. Atherectomy and laser remain important for selected uncrossable, undilatable, or highly resistant lesions, whereas IVL and specialty balloons may provide effective alternatives in appropriately selected crossable lesions. Evidence for many technologies is stronger for procedural and imaging endpoints than for long-term clinical outcomes.
title: Balancing innovation and safety in percutaneous treatment of coronary artery calcification.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) reducing cardiovascular events in elderly patients with aortic stenosis (AS), the mortality rate is still high. Growth differentiation factor (GDF) 15 is reportedly a useful prognostic marker for clinical outcomes in the field of cardiovascular diseases, but it is still unclear if elevated serum GDF15 levels predict poor prognosis in patients with severe AS who undergo TAVI.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We measured the pre- and postoperative serum concentrations of GDF15 in 148 patients. The primary and secondary endpoints were all-cause death and a composite event including cardiovascular death, heart failure rehospitalization, stroke, and adverse bleeding event, respectively. There were 30 all-cause deaths and 21 composite events during a median follow-up period of 1,023 days. Both pre- and postoperative serum GDF15 levels were significantly increased with advancing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis revealed that preoperative serum GDF15 level was independently associated with the primary and secondary endpoints, and the postoperative serum GDF15 level was independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for confounding risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis for the primary endpoint showed a comparable area under the curve for the pre- and postoperative serum GDF15 levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Both the pre- and postoperative GDF15 concentration could be a feasible marker for clinical outcomes in Japanese patients undergoing TAVI.
first_author_country: Yamagata University School of Medicine Yamagata Japan
last_author_country: Yamagata University School of Medicine Yamagata Japan
title: Elevated Serum Growth Differentiation Factor 15 Levels Predict Poor Prognosis in Patients With Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.

abstract: In patients with ischaemic stroke, right-to-left shunting on a bubble study is often attributed to a patent foramen ovale (PFO) and taken as sufficient grounds for percutaneous closure. We report the case of a 60-year-old woman admitted for an ischaemic stroke, in whom transoesophageal echocardiography (TOE) showed microbubbles in the left atrium after right antecubital injection of agitated saline. A PFO was presumed, and the patient was referred for transcatheter closure. During the procedure, repeated attempts to cross the interatrial septum failed. Repeat TOE with agitated saline injected directly adjacent to the interatrial septum showed no septal transit. A subsequent left antecubital injection produced left atrial opacification as abundant as the right-sided injection, with microbubbles consistently entering through the pulmonary veins. This excluded an interatrial shunt and pointed toward a large, fixed, extracardiac right-to-left conduit between the systemic venous return and the pulmonary venous circulation. The closure procedure was therefore abandoned. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) angiography resolved the discrepancy between the positive bubble study and the absence of an interatrial communication. It showed a superior vena cava thrombosed around a long-standing central venous catheter, with extensive venous collateralisation: the left brachiocephalic vein drained through a network of collaterals into a markedly dilated azygos vein. Large-calibre collaterals anastomosed directly with the pulmonary veins, creating a haemodynamically significant right-to-left pathway into the left atrium that bypassed the pulmonary capillary filter and provided the substrate for paradoxical embolism. After multidisciplinary discussion, the patient was treated with long-term oral anticoagulation with a vitamin K antagonist. This case highlights that a positive bubble study is not synonymous with a PFO. Identifying the site of microbubble entry into the left atrium, and performing bilateral arm injections when findings are atypical or septal crossing fails, can help distinguish an intracardiac from an extracardiac shunt and prevent unnecessary intervention. In patients with a history of central venous catheterisation, superior vena cava thrombosis with collaterals draining into the pulmonary veins is a rare cause of right-to-left shunting and paradoxical embolism, and venous imaging may be considered before closure.
title: Bubbles Don't Lie: Superior Vena Cava Thrombosis With a Systemic-to-Pulmonary Venous Shunt Mimicking a Patent Foramen Ovale.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an emerging alternative to long-term anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation, but peri-device leaks remain a clinical challenge.
CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old man with permanent atrial fibrillation, heart failure, a prior ischaemic stroke history was referred for LAAO due to recurrent anticoagulation-related bleeding. Pre-procedural computer tomography (CT) showed a markedly enlarged appendage suitable for a 35-mm WATCHMAN FLX, which was implanted under intracardiac echocardiography guidance, with subsequent transition to aspirin. Three months later, CT revealed a tilted device with a peri-skirt leak; an ischaemic stroke had occurred in the interim, and anticoagulation was resumed. An Amplatzer Vascular Plug II was implanted but follow-up CT demonstrated persistent contrast passage and more but incomplete occlusion. Three months later, the patient experienced a second stroke, and CT confirmed ongoing peri-device flow. A hybrid leak-closure procedure was performed with coils in the appendage and within the device, followed by a 12-mm plug at the leak channel, achieving near-complete occlusion. At 7-month follow-up, the patient remained on rivaroxaban therapy, briefly interrupted due to haematuria associated with nephrolithiasis.
DISCUSSION: Most cases of peri-device leak after LAAO are related to suboptimal device alignment, incomplete endothelialization, or persistent peri-skirt channels. In our case, device tilt with a peri-skirt tract persisted despite initial plug-based closure. This case provides insight into the potential role of hybrid coil- and plug-based strategies in enhancing occlusion but also highlights that anticoagulation remains necessary when full occlusion is not obtained.
title: Persistent peri-device leak following left atrial appendage occlusion treated with hybrid coil- and plug-based closure: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-Ku antibodies are rare disease of overlap myositis and often signal multisystem involvement. Overt heart failure, however, is seldom reported.
CASE SUMMARY: A 60-year-old man presented with progressive exertional dyspnoea and chest tightness. Initial echocardiography showed mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF 49%), and coronary angiography was normal, leading to a diagnosis of MINOCA. One month later, he re-presented with worsening breathlessness, dysphagia, and proximal muscle weakness. Laboratory tests revealed serum creatine kinase 2154-2680 IU/L, troponin 1437 ng/L, and pro-BNP 3290 ng/L. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated dilated ventricles and LVEF 35%. During admission, he developed high-grade AV dissociation requiring dual-chamber pacing and abrupt thrombocytopenia. Cardiac MRI identified a diffuse infiltrative pattern with LVEF 18%. Myositis-specific immunoblot detected high-titre anti-Ku antibodies, and deltoid biopsy confirmed inflammatory myopathy. Despite high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, rituximab and intravenous immunoglobulin, cardiac function deteriorated to LVEF 12%. Recurrent aspiration pneumonia necessitated gastrostomy. Eight months after initial presentation, the patient died following transition to palliative care.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights the danger of assuming that an elevated troponin level is equivalent to myocardial infarction. Non-dynamic troponin elevation with global LV dysfunction and non-obstructive coronaries indicates myocardial injury and warrants investigation for inflammatory and other non-ischaemic causes. Systemic 'red flags' such as dysphagia must trigger early multidisciplinary evaluation to avoid fatal diagnostic delay.
title: Anti-Ku myositis presenting with progressive inflammatory myocarditis: diagnostic pitfalls in a fatal case-case report.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: BRASH syndrome - bradycardia, renal failure, AV nodal blockade, shock and hyperkalaemia - is a self-amplifying pathophysiological loop. Its association with severe amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism is rarely described in detail.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 79-year-old woman with permanent atrial fibrillation on long-term amiodarone and bisoprolol presented after prolonged unwitnessed floor immobilisation with extreme bradycardia (24-30 bpm), haemodynamic instability, KDIGO stage 3 acute kidney injury, hyperkalaemia (5.5 mmol/l), metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis and profound hypothyroidism (TSH 68.5 mUI/l; free T4 4.62 pmol/l) against a normal thyroid baseline 13 months prior. The Popoveniuc myxoedema coma score was 45 (high-risk zone). High-sensitivity troponin T showed flat kinetics consistent with type 2 myocardial injury. Isoproterenol was required for bradycardia refractory to initial metabolic correction, achieving a ventricular rate of 62-68 bpm with QTc shortening from 0.62 s to 0.38 s. The patient was discharged on day 8 with renal recovery and improving thyroid function. Thyroid antibody negativity at 30-day follow-up was consistent with an amiodarone-induced rather than autoimmune aetiology.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates BRASH syndrome presenting with only mild hyperkalaemia in the context of severe amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism, which may have potentiated the pathophysiological loop. Systematic thyroid monitoring during long-term amiodarone therapy and multi-target metabolic correction, including isoproterenol as a pharmacological bridge, may avert invasive pacing.
LEARNING POINTS: BRASH syndrome may occur with only mild hyperkalaemia when severe hypothyroidism potentiates AV nodal blockade - disproportionate bradycardia relative to potassium level is the key diagnostic signal.In any patient on long-term amiodarone presenting with otherwise unexplained bradycardia, profound hypothyroidism should be actively excluded before attributing the presentation to drug toxicity alone; thyroid function testing every 3-6 months is guideline-recommended during such therapy.Isoproterenol may serve as an effective pharmacological chronotropic bridge in BRASH syndrome refractory to initial metabolic correction, potentially avoiding invasive temporary pacing.
journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine
journal_abbrev: Eur J Case Rep Intern Med
title: Extreme Bradycardia in Brash Syndrome Unmasked by Severe Amiodarone-Induced Hypothyroidism.

abstract: Multimodal cardiac imaging has fundamentally reshaped the evaluation of anomalous aortic origin of the coronary artery, yet risk stratification remains challenging because anatomy, symptoms, and physiological demands vary widely across patients. This review summarizes contemporary anomalous aortic origin of the coronary artery classification and emphasizes anatomic features associated with higher risk, including interarterial and intramural courses, adverse ostial morphology, and compression related to the intercoronary pillar or myocardial bridges, which contribute to both fixed and dynamic ischemia. The complementary roles of echocardiography, coronary CT angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve, nuclear myocardial perfusion imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and hybrid anatomic-functional imaging are discussed, with attention to the specific clinical contexts in which each modality is most informative. Finally, we discuss the Vanderbilt management approach that integrates age, symptoms, detailed anatomic assessment, and functional testing to guide observation, exercise recommendations, invasive evaluation, and surgical intervention, with particular focus on individualized counseling and safe return-to-play decisions in young and athletic patients.
keywords: Anomalous aortic origin of coronary arteries
title: Multimodal Imaging in Anomalous Aortic Origin of the Coronary Arteries: Contemporary Approaches to Risk Stratification.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inaccurate measurement of lesion length during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) increases the risk of restenosis and poor clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Two interventional cardiologists evaluated angiographic images and made visual estimates of target lesion length and stent length selection. A 2 mm stent overlap of both the proximal and distal lesion edges was considered to be optimal. The target lesion was also assessed for lesion length using the millimetre controls of the CorPath®GRX system (Siemens Healthineers AG, formerly Corindus). Measurements for 10 lesions (randomly selected) were repeated to assess inter-observer variability. The primary endpoint was longitudinal geographic miss (LGM), defined as an absolute difference of 2 mm or more between visual and vascular robotics measurements.
RESULTS: A total of 21 lesions in 19 patients were evaluated. LGM was detected in 16/21 lesions. Visual lesion length measurements were short for 15 (71%), long for one lesion (5%) and appropriate for five (24%). Stent or drug-coated balloon length selections were short for 15 lesions and appropriate for six.
CONCLUSION: The CorPath GRX robotic PCI system increases the accuracy of lesion length evaluation and stent length selection compared with visual estimation.
title: Robotic Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Assessing Longitudinal Geographic Miss.

abstract: We report a rare case of a 43-year-old woman who developed severe acute left ventricular dysfunction after minimally invasive endoscopic mitral and tricuspid valve repair. Coronary angiography excluded an ischemic complication, while endomyocardial biopsy showed interstitial edema and sparse inflammatory infiltrates without definitive evidence of active myocarditis. Systemic glucocorticoid therapy was initiated after the biopsy result. Temporary mechanical circulatory support with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella CP enabled myocardial recovery and a favorable clinical outcome.
title: Fulminant myocarditis mimicking catastrophic surgical failure after mitral valve repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amniotic fluid embolism can lead to severe complications, including cardiac arrest, a significant cause of maternal mortality.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 36-year-old woman with postpartum hemorrhage was transported to our hospital. Shortly after her arrival, she experienced cardiac arrest and required immediate extracorporeal life support. A hysterectomy was performed, but persistent bleeding necessitated open abdomen management for damage control to stabilize the patient's condition. On the second day, she was successfully weaned from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, followed by catheter removal and complete abdominal closure. The patient was discharged with no neurological sequelae. Pathological examination of the hysterectomy specimen confirmed amniotic fluid embolism.
CONCLUSION: Extracorporeal life support may be effective as a last resort for cardiac arrest due to amniotic fluid embolism, and damage control surgery may be beneficial for managing intractable bleeding.
title: Amniotic Fluid Embolism Successfully Managed With Extracorporeal Life Support and Damage Control Surgery: A Case Report.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: Uterine leiomyomas, or fibroids, are the most prevalent benign tumor pathology affecting women.1 Fibroids are reportedly found in nearly 70% of Caucasian women and more than 80% of women with African ancestry.1 Rarely, fibroids progress to uterine intravenous leiomyomas (IVL), a neoplastic growth pattern characterized by intravascular proliferation of this smooth muscle cell tumor.2 This tumor is typically confined to the pelvic vasculature but can occasionally spread with venous blood flowing to the heart, ultimately penetrating the inferior vena cava, right heart chambers, and pulmonary arteries.3 If the tumor reaches the heart, this intracardiac leiomyomatosis (ICL) can result in severe cardiac symptoms including arrythmias, murmurs, and sudden death.3,4 The case presentation shows both IVL and ICL in a patient. Approximately 12 months following hysterectomy due to fibroids, the patient presented with mild dyspnea on exertion, retrosternal chest pain, and a syncopal episode. She was diagnosed with saddle embolism with extension into right ventricle and complete occlusion of the inferior vena cava (IVC). Informed by imaging from echocardiogram, computed tomography (CT) angiogram of the chest, CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the abdomen and pelvis, providers proceeded with mechanical thrombectomy followed by IVC filter, tumor debulking surgery, resection of a pelvic mass, and proximal vaginectomy. To facilitate early detection and treatment, providers should factor the risk of IVL and ICL into ongoing care and patient education post hysterectomy or fibroid diagnosis.
TOPICS: Uterine leiomyoma, fibroid, benign tumor, intravenous leiomyoma, intracardiac leiomyomatosis, neoplastic growth, pelvic vasculature, pulmonary arteries, inferior vena cava, arrhythmia, murmur, sudden death, hysterectomy, syncope, pulmonary embolism, saddle embolism, CT angiogram chest, CTA, MRI, thrombectomy, CT abdomen pelvis, MRI.
journal: Journal of education & teaching in emergency medicine
title: Case Report on Rare Presentation of Intravenous Leiomyomas with Intracardiac Leiomyomatosis.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a multifactorial condition influenced by both genetic predispositions and environmental exposures.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a pair of male monozygotic twins diagnosed with identical critical left anterior descending artery stenosis, suggesting a possible hereditary susceptibility involving this coronary segment. One twin presented with acute coronary syndrome while the other was diagnosed with CAD during screening prompted by his sibling's diagnosis.
CONCLUSION: This report underscores the importance of early screening among genetically related individuals and contributes to the understanding of phenotypic variability in genetically identical patients with CAD.
LEARNING POINTS: There is a strong genetic contribution to the anatomical distribution of CAD even when environmental risk factors differ between twins.Thorough cardiovascular risk assessment and management are warranted for asymptomatic identical twins when their co-twin presents with CAD. Early screening for subclinical disease and the consideration of advanced imaging modalities may be justified in this context.
journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine
journal_abbrev: Eur J Case Rep Intern Med
title: Identical Critical Left Anterior Descending Artery Stenosis in Monozygotic Twins.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms.
METHODS: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected.
RESULTS: Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.
title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States.
METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak.
RESULTS: A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.
title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.

abstract: Clopidogrel (CLP) remains a cornerstone of antiplatelet therapy in the management of atherothrombotic events affecting the coronary and cerebrovascular circulations. As an irreversible thienopyridine inhibitor of the platelet P2Y12 adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor, CLP reduces platelet aggregation by preventing downstream activation of the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor complex. It is a prodrug that requires hepatic bioactivation primarily via CYP2C19, resulting in susceptibility to pharmacogenomic variability and clinically significant drug-drug interactions. Current guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology (2023) and the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (2025) recommend potent P2Y12 inhibitors - ticagrelor and prasugrel - in preference to CLP for most patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, CLP retains a pivotal role when potent agents are contraindicated, in elderly patients at high bleeding risk (HBR), in cerebrovascular events, and as a de-escalation target following initial potent P2Y12 inhibition. In acute ischaemic stroke and high-risk TIA, short-course DAPT with CLP and aspirin for 21 days (not prolonged beyond this period) is the evidence-based standard of care. Major clinical trials - including CAPRIE, CURE, CHANCE, POINT, and the landmark CHANCE-2 - have defined the therapeutic boundaries and limitations of CLP-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Bleeding remains the most clinically significant adverse effect, with gastrointestinal haemorrhage the most frequent site and intracranial haemorrhage the most feared complication. This review synthesises current evidence, incorporating recent meta-analyses and guideline updates, to provide a practical, evidence-based framework for clinicians regarding the use of CLP and comparator P2Y12 inhibitors in coronary and cerebrovascular disease.
title: Clopidogrel in the Contemporary Management of Coronary and Cerebrovascular Events: Efficacy, Safety, and Decision-making Pathways.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed for severe aortic stenosis with improving procedural success rates; however, post-procedural complications remain a significant clinical challenge. Growing evidence suggests that sarcopenia may adversely affect morbidity and mortality in this patient population.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 171 patients undergoing elective TAVI (January 2018-February 2024). Muscle area (MA), visceral, subcutaneous (SATA), and total adipose tissue area (TATA) were measured at the L3 vertebral level from pre-procedural computed tomography angiography (CTA). Primary endpoints were all-cause and cardiac mortality; secondary endpoints were permanent cardiac conduction defect, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), and hospital stay.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 95 women (55.5%) and 76 men (44.5%), median age 78.9 years, society of thoracic surgeons score 6.30 (IQR = 4.37-9.33). Over 21.8 ± 17.9 months, 43 patients (25.1%) died, including 12 cardiac deaths (7.0%). Lower MA and MA/body mass index (BMI) ratio were independently associated with cardiac mortality in men (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.935, P = .016 and OR = 0.983, P = .042). Permanent cardiac conduction defect occurred in 44 patients (27.7%); lower SATA and TATA were independent predictors in women (OR = 0.990, P = .031 and OR = 0.994, P = .024). Permanent pacemaker implantation was required in 30 patients (18.6%); adipose tissue parameters were associated with PPI in women on univariate analysis but did not retain significance after multiple adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural CTA-derived body composition assessment may contribute to the prediction of mortality and morbidity in TAVI patients without additional cost or radiation exposure. The association of lower MA with cardiac mortality in men, and of reduced adipose tissue with conduction disturbances in women, suggests that sex-specific body composition parameters may provide prognostic value beyond conventional risk scores.
title: Impact of Computed Tomography-Derived Body Composition on Mortality and Conduction Disturbances After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Sex-Specific Analysis.

abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification.
