Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.
title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: De novo heart failure (HF) during the first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) hospitalization significantly increases mortality and readmission. While nutritional and inflammatory indicators like the advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) and modified Controlling Nutritional Status (mCONUT) score are gaining attention, their exact association with post-STEMI de novo HF remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective study (January 2016 to June 2025) included 1598 first-time STEMI patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. Patients were categorized into de novo HF and non-HF groups to evaluate the association of ALI and mCONUT scores with HF development.
RESULTS: The HF group exhibited significantly lower ALI and higher mCONUT scores compared to the non-HF group. Multivariate logistic regression identified lower ALI and higher mCONUT scores as independent predictors of HF risk. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that mCONUT possessed better predictive performance than ALI, with effects remaining highly consistent across subgroups. Sensitivity analyses and NRI/IDI results confirmed that mCONUT provides independent incremental predictive value beyond traditional risk models (optimism-corrected C-statistic 0.785 vs. 0.751). These associations were independent of admission hemodynamic status (Killip class) and treatment era.
CONCLUSION: Both ALI and mCONUT scores are independently associated with in-hospital de novo HF in STEMI patients. The mCONUT score demonstrates superior predictive performance, serving as a promising indicator for early risk stratification.
title: Association of ALI and mCONUT With In-Hospital De Novo Heart Failure in Patients With STEMI.

abstract: Barlow disease with bileaflet prolapse represents one of the most challenging lesions in degenerative mitral valve surgery. Multiple prolapsing segments, excess leaflet tissue, elongated chordae and annular dilatation often coexist, requiring a comprehensive repair strategy. The edge-to-edge technique, first introduced in 1991, provides a simple and reproducible method to restore leaflet coaptation in this complex setting. By approximating the free edges of the anterior and posterior leaflets at the site of regurgitation, a double-orifice mitral valve is created. This single manoeuvre effectively addresses bileaflet prolapse, reduces leaflet height, forces coaptation, restricts excessive leaflet motion and prevents systolic anterior motion of the anterior leaflet. A concomitant ring annuloplasty is strongly recommended to remodel the dilated annulus, stabilize the repair and ensure long-term durability. This video tutorial presents the key surgical steps of the double-orifice edge-to-edge repair combined with annuloplasty for the treatment of severe mitral regurgitation caused by bileaflet prolapse in Barlow disease. The procedure is performed through a anterolateral minithoracotomy at the fourth intercostal space under video assistance with peripherical cardiopulmonary bypass and cardioplegic arrest. Technical tips for patient selection, suture placement, leaflet assessment, avoidance of mitral stenosis and intraoperative competence testing are provided.
journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
title: Edge-to-edge mitral valve repair for bileaflet prolapse in Barlow disease.

journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
title: When Leaflet Thickening Becomes More Than an Imaging Finding.

abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
title: Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease: Epidemiology, Prognosis, and Management Considerations.

abstract: In developing countries, acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is becoming a more common cause of cardiovascular death. Although thrombolytic treatments and limited percutaneous coronary intervention have been introduced, in-hospital mortality from ACS is still high in sub-Saharan countries. This study aimed to evaluate the treatment outcome of ACS and its associated factors among patients attending Jimma University Medical Center, Jimma, Ethiopia. A retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 ACS patients. Patient records from admissions between November 1st, 2017, and October 31st, 2022 were reviewed, with data collected between December 1st and 31st, 2022. Data were collected using a structured checklist, entered, and analyzed using Statistical Package for Social science version 26. Descriptive analysis was used to summarize baseline characteristics and determine treatment outcomes. Bivariable and multivariable regression analyses were employed to determine factors affecting poor treatment outcomes. The odds ratio with a 95% confidence interval was computed, and a P value < .05 was considered significant. Among the 300 ACS patients included in our study, 35.3% died during hospitalization. Hypertension was the most common risk factor, present in 88.3% of the patients. In addition, 20.3% were classified as Killip class III or IV. 20.7% had a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of less than or equal to 30%, and 79.3% had an LVEF > 30%. Regarding treatment, an aspirin loading dose, clopidogrel loading dose, beta-blockers, statins, morphine, and nitrates were given to 284 (94.7%), 286 (95.3%), 227 (75.7%), 283 (94.3%), 109 (36.3%), and 80 (26.7%) patients, respectively. Factors significantly associated with in-hospital mortality were older age (P ≤ .001), history of diabetes (P = .004), ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction diagnosis (P = .003), and Killip class III and IV (P ≤ .001), whereas LVEF > 30% was associated with significantly lower odds of in-hospital death (P < .001). The proportion of in-hospital mortality attributable to ACS was found to be high. As a result, timely evidence-based therapy should be included in the setup.
title: Treatment outcomes and associated factors among acute coronary syndrome patients admitted to Jimma University Medical Centre, Jimma, Ethiopia: A 5-year retrospective study.

abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) measures atherosclerotic burden, while coronary flow reserve (CFR) measures coronary vasodilator function. The study aimed to assess the relationship between CAC burden and CFR and to define clinical and imaging factors independently associated with compromised CFR. This retrospective observational study included 467 patients aged 16 to 93 years who underwent clinically indicated CAC assessment and quantitative ^82Rb PET/computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging with pharmacological vasodilator stress between January 2024 and June 2026. CAC was categorized as 0, 1 to 99, 100 to 399, or ≥400 Agatston units. CFR was calculated as stress-to-rest myocardial blood flow, with CFR < 2.0 defined as impaired. Correlation, multivariable linear regression, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Mean age was 61.8 ± 13.7 years, with 59.1% male participants; 39.6% had impaired CFR. Mean CFR decreased progressively from 2.43 ± 0.62 in patients with CAC = 0 to 1.57 ± 0.47 with CAC ≥ 400 (P for trend < .001), while impaired CFR increased from 25.9% to 67.1%. CFR was inversely correlated with CAC (Spearman r = -0.43, P < .001). After adjustment, CAC 100 to 399 and ≥400 remained independently associated with impaired CFR (adjusted OR 2.41, 95% confidence interval 1.35 to 4.30 and OR 3.28, 95% confidence interval 1.72 to 6.25, respectively). Age, diabetes, and abnormal myocardial perfusion were also independently associated with impaired CFR. CAC was independently associated with lower CFR and a higher prevalence of impaired CFR. This association remained after multivariable adjustment, and also on sensitivity analysis, indicating that these 2 approaches to coronary assessment complement each other. The results of this study are presented as associations, due to its retrospective cross sectional design.
title: Relationship between coronary flow reserve and coronary calcium burden in patients with suspected coronary artery disease: A retrospective analysis.

abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) can be managed using different image-guided treatment modalities; however, the determinants of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently defined. This retrospective study aimed to identify clinical predictors associated with length of hospital stay and to develop a machine learning model for predicting prolonged hospitalization in patients with PFO. Clinical data from 216 patients with PFO treated at Gansu Provincial People's Hospital were retrospectively analyzed. Among them, 106 patients underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-guided treatment and 110 underwent X-ray-guided treatment. According to the median length of stay, patients were divided into a short-stay group (≤7 days) and a prolonged-stay group (>7 days). Baseline variables were compared between groups. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection. Five machine learning algorithms were then developed and compared in the training cohort, followed by validation in an independent validation cohort. Thirteen baseline variables showed significant between-group differences. LASSO regression retained 10 candidate predictors for model construction. Among the evaluated models, the random forest model showed the best overall performance. In the validation cohort, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.692, a precision of 0.708, a recall of 0.850, an F1-score of 0.773, and an AUC of 0.711, indicating moderate discrimination. The random forest model demonstrated moderate predictive discrimination for prolonged hospital stay. Given the limited sample size and single-center retrospective design, the model should be considered exploratory and requires external validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical use.
title: Exploratory clinical predictors of prolonged hospital stay in patients with patent foramen ovale undergoing transthoracic echocardiography- or X-ray-guided closure.

abstract: Electrical storm (ES), defined as at least three sustained episodes of ventricular arrhythmia within 24 h, is a life-threatening state of electrical and frequently hemodynamic instability associated with a high risk of mortality. Recurrent ventricular arrhythmias indicate prognostically relevant disease progression even before overt ES develops. Accordingly, ES often represents the culmination of a continuum of increasing electrical instability that should ideally be prevented or interrupted at an early stage. Characterization of the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate, arrhythmogenic triggers, and the arrhythmia itself, together with assessment of the overall hemodynamic status, forms the basis for risk stratification, diagnostic evaluation, and targeted treatment of ES. For the first time, the German Cardiac Society (DGK) position paper integrates these three dimensions-substrate, trigger, and arrhythmia (STA)-into the STA triad. Most episodes of ES occur in patients with structural heart disease, particularly ischemic or nonischemic cardiomyopathy with advanced heart failure; primary electrical or inherited arrhythmia syndromes are less common. The NHII-MED (neuroendocrine dysfunction, heart failure/hemodynamics, ischemia/coronary pathology, inflammation/infection, medication/metabolic factors, electrolyte imbalances, drugs/alcohol) framework was introduced to facilitate systematic trigger identification and management. Core components of specialized acute treatment include correction of reversible causes, device management including implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) reprogramming, antiarrhythmic drug therapy, sedation, catheter ablation, autonomic modulation, optimization of treatment for the underlying cardiac disease, and, when required, mechanical circulatory support. The overarching therapeutic objective is to prevent further ventricular arrhythmias and repetitive ICD therapies. This executive summary of the DGK position paper addresses the associated clinical challenges and contemporary management options.
title: [German Society of Cardiology position paper-how to treat patients with electrical storm: executive summary].

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Angina pectoris remains a common clinical manifestation, but contemporary population-based data on its long-term prognostic significance are limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term importance of angina pectoris in association with coronary artery disease (CAD) severity determined by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) in a general population.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study included participants from the Swedish Cardiopulmonary Bioimage Study who had completed the Rose Questionnaire and underwent valid CCTA from November 2013 to October 2018, excluding participants with prior myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure, or coronary revascularization. Follow-up continued through September 2024. Data analyses were conducted between August 2025 and January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Angina (defined by the Rose Questionnaire) and CAD (categorized as no findings, nonobstructive CAD [<50% stenosis], or obstructive CAD [≥50% stenosis]) according to CCTA findings.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was MI or coronary death. The secondary outcome was major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as MI, coronary revascularization, heart failure hospitalization, or death from coronary disease or heart failure. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression with sequential multivariable adjustment and stratification by CAD category and presented as hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: This study included 24 176 individuals (median [IQR] age, 57 [54-61] years; 12 225 female [50.6%]; 1615 with hyperlipidemia [6.8%]; 4374 with hypertension [18.3%]; 703 with diabetes [2.9%]). Angina was present in 720 participants (3.0%). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.7 (6.9-8.6) years, 293 primary events occurred. Angina was associated with a higher incidence of MI or coronary death compared with no angina (21 participants [2.9%] vs 272 participants [1.2%]; HR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.60-3.90). Event rates increased across CAD categories, with no evidence of interaction between angina and CAD severity. After multivariable adjustment, angina remained independently associated with the primary outcome (HR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.04-2.63). Similar associations were observed for MACE (adjusted HR, 2.34; 95% CI, 1.73-3.16).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of a contemporary general population, angina pectoris was associated with adverse cardiac outcomes, independent of CAD severity assessed by CCTA. These findings suggest that symptom assessment remains relevant in cardiovascular risk stratification because it provided incremental prognostic information that may reflect underlying coronary microvascular dysfunction or vasomotor disorders.
title: Importance of Angina Pectoris by Coronary Artery Disease Severity.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This case illustrates a percutaneous rescue of an embolized valve to the left ventricle during a transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve procedure.
KEY STEPS: Steps included: 1) maintaining wire position across the embolized valve; 2) creating a dual-wire rail by snaring guidewires through the embolized valve; 3) coordinated dual-rail tension applied to withdraw valve toward mitral annulus; 4) second valve deployment; and 5) retrieval of wires entrapped between the 2 valves using a 0.035-inch microcatheter.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Pitfalls include loss of wire position across the embolized valve, difficulty snaring wires through the embolized valve, asymmetric tension causing poor coaxial alignment, incomplete annular reapproximation, second valve embolization, paravalvular leak, and difficulty retrieving wires between the valves.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: A dual-rail system-created by snaring guidewires through the embolized valve-can provide sufficient tension to reapproximate the valve toward the mitral annulus for subsequent percutaneous rescue. Deployment of a second valve within the embolized valve is a viable rescue strategy when surgical intervention is prohibitive.
title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Complicated by Valve Embolization: Percutaneous Rescue With a Double-Rail Technique.

abstract: Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses showed no significant linear or nonlinear association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI (OR=0.999,95%CI:0.994 ~ 1.003, P = 0.534; nonlinear χ2 = 0.91, df = 3, P = 0.8223). Stratified analyses by glucose metabolism status also revealed no significant correlation in any stratum(P > 0.05). No independent association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI was identified in post‑PCI patients, even within different glucose‑metabolism strata. Relevant findings require further verification in larger prospective cohorts.
title: Association between TyG‑BMI and repeat percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) risk: exploratory stratification by glucose metabolism status.

abstract: In-hospital adverse events after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) can occur abruptly and adversely affect short-term prognosis. We developed and externally validated explainable machine learning models to predict a composite of in-hospital atrial fibrillation (AF), ventricular fibrillation (VF), cardiac arrest (CA), or death using routinely available admission data. We retrospectively analyzed 7,496 patients from the MIMIC-IV database as the development cohort and 2,776 patients from Xuanwu Hospital as the external validation cohort. Predictors included demographics, medical history, and admission laboratory tests. Logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron, and TabNet models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using discrimination, classification, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Latent class analysis identified three outcome clusters with distinct event-probability profiles. XGBoost achieved the best performance for the composite outcome in the development cohort (AUROC, 0.798). Predictive performance was moderate to good for AF and in-hospital death, with AUROCs of up to 0.834 and 0.870 in the development cohort and 0.803 and 0.849 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Discrimination was lower for VF and CA. SHapley Additive exPlanations highlighted neutrophil and leukocyte counts, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, renal function, glucose, glycated hemoglobin A1c, and prior AF as important predictors. These explainable models may support early risk stratification and help guide monitoring intensity and timely intervention in patients with AMI.
title: Development and validation of an explainable artificial intelligence model to predict in-hospital adverse events for patients with acute myocardial infarction.

abstract: Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.52% of colchicine users versus 15.03% of non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.75; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly reduced in colchicine users (8.01% vs. 11.07%; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.53-0.62; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.96-1.37; P = 0.121) or stroke (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.81-1.01; P = 0.076). In a landmark analysis at 365 days that addressed immortal time bias, the associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.62-0.73; P < 0.001) and with the composite outcome (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.71-0.81; P < 0.001) remained significant, whereas stroke (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.87-1.12; P = 0.823) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.95-1.40; P = 0.144) did not differ between the two groups. In patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease, colchicine use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The reduction in the composite outcome was driven by mortality rather than by myocardial infarction or stroke.
title: Colchicine use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic gout without prior coronary artery disease: A propensity-matched nationwide cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive coronary physiology enables comprehensive assessment of epicardial and microvascular disease, but its routine use is limited by technical complexity and prolonged acquisition time.
OBJECTIVES: The PyCath system is a rapid-exchange microcatheter engineered to simultaneously measure intracoronary pressure and thermoconvection-based flow velocity.
METHODS: First-in-human, prospective, single-arm study evaluating the safety and performance of the PyCath system in patients with a clinical indication for coronary physiology assessment. The microcatheter was advanced over a standard coronary guidewire to acquire simultaneous pressure and flow velocity at baseline and during hyperemia. The primary objectives were procedural safety, defined as device-related major adverse cardiac events, and device performance, defined as successful acquisition of pressure and velocity signals. Data were analyzed by an independent core laboratory.
RESULTS: Seventeen patients (mean age 59.3 ± 9.4 years, 76.5% males) referred for invasive coronary physiology assessment were included. Intracoronary pressure and velocity measurements were feasible in 100% and 88% of cases, respectively. The mean time required to obtain both measurements was 70.6 ± 23.6 seconds. The mean fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance were 0.84 ± 0.12, 2.28 ± 0.79, and 1.46 ± 0.77, respectively. There were no device-related major adverse cardiac events. Test-retest reproducibility was good-to-excellent with intraclass correlation coefficients for fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance of 0.979 (0.934-0.993), 0.798 (0.477-0.933), and 0.759 (0.397-0.919).
CONCLUSIONS: In this first-in-human experience, the PyCath microcatheter enabled safe and reproducible measurements of intracoronary pressure and flow velocity with excellent reproducibility.
title: First-in-Human Experience With a Novel Monorail Microcatheter for Instantaneous Coronary Pressure and Flow Velocity Measurements.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) becomes increasingly commonplace in overdose, questions about its role in various shock states remain. The application of VA-ECMO with impaired myocardial function is well established, and use in cardiogenic shock precipitated by poisoning has continued to increase. In poison-induced vasoplegia with preserved myocardial function, the role of VA-ECMO remains undefined. Many atypical antipsychotic and antidepressant agents are known to cause mild hypotension via alpha-1 adrenergic blockade. Intravenous fluids and vasopressors alone are generally effective for single-substance ingestions. In the setting of polysubstance intoxication, synergism leading to bradycardia and refractory vasoplegia refractory to conventional therapies may result, prompting consideration for extracorporeal support.
CASE REPORT: A 71-year-old woman presented to the emergency department (ED) after being found obtunded near bottles of quetiapine, olanzapine, trazodone, mirtazapine, levomilnacipran, eszopiclone, and clonazepam. She underwent prehospital intubation and received push-dose epinephrine for hypotension. In the ED, the patient remained hypotensive with a relative bradycardia, requiring escalating doses of norepinephrine, vasopressin, epinephrine, angiotensin II, and methylene blue infusions. Her extremities remained warm, and point-of-care echocardiography revealed hyperdynamic function, consistent with vasoplegic shock. She subsequently underwent VA-ECMO cannulation, which was followed by a rapid decrease in vasopressor requirements and decannulation on hospital day 3. The patient recovered and was transferred to inpatient psychiatry neurologically intact. Urine mass-spectrometry revealed large peaks for quetiapine, olanzapine, milnacipran, mirtazapine, trazodone, and zopiclone.
CONCLUSION: While overdose data are limited, levomilnacipran may precipitate or potentiate relative bradycardia with hypotension and a preserved ejection fraction. Significant ingestions and synergism with other agents causing peripheral alpha-1 antagonism may lead to hemodynamic instability refractory to conventional therapies. Extracorporeal life support may aid in recovery.
journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine
title: Polysubstance-Induced Vasoplegia Managed with Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Case Report.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with tenecteplase being a cornerstone of acute management. While tenecteplase carries a known risk of bleeding, major thrombotic events such as acute myocardial infarction (AMI) after stroke reperfusion are less commonly described.
CASE REPORT: We present the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with acute stroke symptoms. After ruling out intracranial hemorrhage and managing blood pressure, he received tenecteplase, and all neurological deficits resolved. Soon after, he developed acute chest pain, and his repeat electrocardiogram confirmed a ST-elevation myocardial infarction. He underwent emergent cardiac catheterization, revealing 100% occlusion of the left circumflex artery, which was successfully revascularized with thrombectomy and angioplasty. Intravascular ultrasound further supported the presence of embolic phenomenon. Pathology of the retrieved material identified thrombus alongside atherosclerotic plaque fragments. The patient experienced complete symptom resolution and was discharged after a short hospitalization.This case highlights the complexities encountered when a patient with acute ischemic stroke who is treated with tenecteplase subsequently develops an AMI. Potential mechanisms include a coincidental plaque rupture, possibly exacerbated by the stress of the acute stroke, a rare paradoxical prothrombotic effect of thrombolysis, or a combination thereof. The pathological finding of mixed thrombus and atherosclerotic plaque underscores the underlying disease contributing to this event.
CONCLUSION: This case accentuates the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for new cardiovascular events in post-thrombolysis patients, especially those with significant cardiovascular risk factors. Rapid and judicious diagnostic evaluation is crucial for timely management of these complex, life-threatening complications.
journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine
title: Acute Myocardial Infarction Following Tenecteplase: A Case Report of Complex Dual Pathology.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ST-elevated myocardial infarction (STEMI) is a medical emergency requiring timely revascularization to preserve myocardial injury. Rural populations often experience delays in treatment leading to increased risk of complications and mortality. Emergent treatment of STEMI in a patient on long-term direct oral anticoagulation facing delays to revascularization is a complex scenario for rural physicians.
CASE REPORT: A 55-year-old male presented to the emergency department in rural Alaska and was diagnosed with acute inferior STEMI. The patient's history was notable for pulmonary embolism with long-term direct oral anticoagulation. Thrombolytic therapy was not recommended and prompt revascularization via percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was needed; however, the nearest PCI-capable hospital was hundreds of miles away, increasing the risk of ischemic cardiomyopathy and death. The patient achieved revascularization after transport and, in the following year, experienced multiple episodes of ventricular tachycardia leading to ablation and need for implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a complex but not uncommon scenario that rural physicians face. In rural patients requiring acute STEMI treatment but without timely access to a PCI-capable hospital, systemic thrombolysis and immediate transfer of care is often the only option for revascularization. There is a need for clear STEMI management guidelines in anticoagulated patients who present in rural settings.
journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine
title: Delayed Revascularization in Rural Acute STEMI Patient on Direct Oral Anticoagulation: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.
METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.
RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.
CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.
title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.

abstract: This case-control study investigated the relationships between circulating fatty acid (FA) profiles, atherogenic indices, cardiac biomarkers, and coronary artery disease (CAD) severity in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma FA profile were quantified using gas chromatography in 314 patients with AMI and 422 controls aged ≥60 years. Compared with controls, patients had higher total saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), including total omega-3 and omega-6 PUFA, whereas linoleic acid and the omega-6/omega-3 ratio were lower. All four atherogenic indices,Castelli risk index-I (CRI-I), CRI-II, atherogenic coefficient, and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP),were independently associated with AMI, with adjusted odds ratios of 1.98, 32.94, 4.00, and 1.79, respectively. Total omega-3 PUFA and CRI-II demonstrated high discriminatory performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.904 and 0.910, respectively. Among patients with AMI, total omega-6 PUFA were highest in four-vessel disease, whereas atherogenic indices did not increase consistently with the number of affected vessels. Critical stenosis was associated with higher total saturated fatty acids, palmitic acid, arachidonic acid, and delta-5 desaturase index, alongside lower docosatetraenoic acid and omega-6 elongation index. Multivariable models revealed a novel, independent inverse correlation between AIP and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme activity (partial ρ = -0.169, q = 0.030), whereas CRI-II correlated positively with cardiac troponin I (partial ρ = 0.163, q = 0.038). These findings highlight the interest to introduce FA profiling and atherogenic indices for the biochemical characterization of AMI. Prospective studies are needed to validate these associations and their incremental value for cardiovascular risk stratification.
title: Fatty Acid Profile, Atherogenic Indices, and Cardiac Biomarkers in Older Adults With Acute Myocardial Infarction: Associations With Angiographic Coronary Disease Severity.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The shark-fin sign (SFS) is a rare, high-risk electrocardiographic pattern reported in commonly linked with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the electrocardiographic patterns, etiologies, and clinical outcomes associated with the SFS.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane from inception through May 20, 2026, including all studies with participant-level data.
RESULTS: Eighty-five papers involving 104 patients were included; 66.3% had non-obstructive etiologies. The obstructive CAD patients were predominantly male (97.1%), while other etiologies were predominantly female (60.8%). Among CAD cases, the left main coronary artery (LMCA)/proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) was the culprit in 75.0%, and SFS localization matched coronary anatomy in 91.4%. VT/VF and death each occurred in 37.1%, with adverse outcomes confined to those with LMCA/LAD lesions. Among other etiologies, Takotsubo syndrome (TTS, 31.7%), vasospasm (14.4%), myocarditis (6.7 %) and neurologic emergencies (4.8%) were the most frequently reported. VT/VF occurred in 43.4% and 27.5% died. Among patients with TTS, 63.6% experienced VT/VF or death, compared with ventricular arrhythmias in 66% of patients with vasospasm.
CONCLUSION: SFS is a high-risk ECG pattern rather than a diagnosis and warrants urgent etiologic evaluation and cardiac monitoring. Most published data are derived from patients without established CAD. LMCA/LAD disease, TTS, and coronary vasospasm were associated with particularly high-risk hospitalizations. Primary non-cardiac causes should also be considered when clinically suspected.
title: Beyond Coronary Artery Disease: Etiologies and Outcomes of the Shark-Fin ECG Pattern: A Systematic Review.

abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a major life-threatening cardiovascular disease characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and autophagic dysregulation. This study aims to investigate the cardioprotective role of AMBRA1 via mitophagy in AMI. A mouse model of AMI was established, followed by AMBRA1 overexpression and PINK1 knockdown. Cardiac function, myocardial infarct size, tissue damage, and fibrosis were assayed. LDH/cTnI/CK-MB levels were measured to assess myocardial injury. LC3-II/I, p62, PINK1, Parkin, and Tomm20 were detected by Western blot and immunofluorescence. Staining assays and biochemical assays were used to detect mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS levels, MDA content, and ATP content. Results showed that AMBRA1 expression was downregulated after AMI. AMBRA1 overexpression improved cardiac function, reduced infarct size, alleviated myocardial fibrosis and injury, and inhibited cell apoptosis. AMBRA1 overexpression enhanced mitophagic flux, with an increased LC3-II/I ratio, degradation of p62, and enhanced co-localization of LC3 and Tomm20. AMBRA1 overexpression improved mitochondrial function, with restored membrane potential, reduced ROS and MDA levels, and increased ATP levels. AMBRA1 overexpression upregulated PINK1 and Parkin. PINK1 knockdown reversed the mitophagy activation and cardioprotective effects induced by AMBRA1 overexpression. In conclusion, AMBRA1 restores myocardial functions and alleviates structural damage in AMI mice through the PINK1/Parkin axis via mitophagy.
title: AMBRA1 overexpression attenuates acute myocardial infarction injury by enhancing mitophagy via the PINK1/Parkin pathway.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) optimization remains largely driven by intravascular imaging, potentially leading to overtreatment of functionally irrelevant findings.
OBJECTIVES: To compare the impact of optical coherence tomography (OCT), angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFRangio), and the integration of imaging and physiology (OCT-FFR) on post-PCI optimization strategies.
METHODS: Among patients included in the AQVA-I and II trials, we selected those receiving post-PCI OCT (n = 79). Physiology reconstruction based on OCT traces was obtained in 76 OCT runs. One operator, blinded to the post-PCI optimization procedural plan and to final PCI result, planned the procedure according to FFRangio, OCT and OCT-FFR. The primary endpoint was the rate of any additional post-PCI optimization maneuver. Secondary endpoints included type of optimization strategy and pairwise differences between modalities.
RESULTS: Among 79 patients, 76 had complete triplet data. The rate of any additional post-PCI optimization was highest with OCT (33/76, 43.4%), followed by OCT-FFR (26/76, 34.2%) and lowest with FFRangio (5/76, 6.6%) (overall p < 0.001). The overall rate of any additional maneuver was not significantly different between OCT and OCT-FFR (absolute paired difference 2.6%; adjusted p = 0.500). Recommendations for edge dissection stenting, post-dilation for stent underexpansion, and post-dilation for malapposition were identical between OCT and OCT-FFR. In contrast, additional stenting of adjacent segments was reduced with OCT-FFR compared with OCT (4/76 [5.3%] vs 12/76 [15.8%]) and was recommended at the same rate as with FFRangio (4/76 [5.3%]).
CONCLUSIONS: OCT guidance is associated with a higher rate of post-PCI optimization maneuvers compared with FFRangio, reflecting its sensitivity to morphological abnormalities. Integration of functional assessment through OCT-FFR significantly reduces additional stenting in segments defined as 5 mm proximal and distal to the stent edges, while preserving treatment of clinically relevant mechanical complications.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Additional value of optical coherence tomography-fractional flow reserve for the optimization of percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers are common in patients referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but there is no consensus on whether they should be continued through the procedure. Continuation could worsen bradycardia or atrioventricular block in a setting already prone to conduction injury, whereas interruption may provoke adrenergic rebound, tachyarrhythmia, myocardial ischemia, or hemodynamic instability. Available evidence is observational and does not resolve this trade-off.
METHODS: BETA-TAVI is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized noninferiority trial in adults with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI while receiving chronic oral beta-blocker therapy. Participants are randomized 1:1 to continuation of their usual beta-blocker or interruption from 72 h before TAVI through day 7. The primary endpoint is new permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) within 7 days. Secondary endpoints include high-degree atrioventricular block, new conduction disturbances, atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, severe bradycardia, hemodynamic deterioration, mortality, and later PPI. The calculated sample size is 348 participants. The prespecified noninferiority margin is 6.5 percentage points on the absolute risk-difference scale; the primary conclusion requires concordant modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: BETA-TAVI tests a frequent but poorly studied medication decision using a randomized strategy comparison. The trial will determine whether chronic beta-blocker therapy can be continued through TAVI without a clinically unacceptable increase in early permanent pacing and will characterize the arrhythmic and hemodynamic consequences of both strategies.
CLINICALTRIALS: gov identifier: NCT05721170.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Beta-blocker continuation versus interruption during transcatheter aortic valve implantation: Rationale and design of the BETA-TAVI randomized trial.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The clinical impact and critical threshold of intraprocedural blood loss (BL) during large-bore aspiration thrombectomy for pulmonary embolism (PE) remain poorly defined. This study evaluates how blood loss influences major bleeding events and in-hospital mortality.
METHODS: We analysed 104 patients undergoing aspiration thrombectomy for PE in the USAT IH-PE registry with recorded intraprocedural blood loss (mL). Outcomes were major bleeding (BARC ≥3), death and a composite endpoint. Exploratory analyses were repeated, stratified by pre-procedural Hb (<11 vs ≥11 g/dL).
RESULTS: Median blood loss was 300 mL; bleeding occurred in 21%, death in 7% and the composite endpoint in 22%. Blood loss correlated only weakly with the Hb drop and not after adjustment. It was higher in patients with major bleeding (380 ± 121 mL vs 289 ± 122 mL, AUC 0.72; OR 1.74 per +100 mL) and the composite endpoint (358 ± 116 mL vs 293 ± 127 mL, AUC 0.67), but unrelated to mortality. In an exploratory subgroup analysis, the association with major bleeding appeared stronger in patients with Hb <11 g/dL (n = 22; AUC 0.93). Independent predictors of the composite endpoint were blood loss (aOR 2.18, 1.35-3.52, p = 0.001), lower pre-procedural Hb (aOR 0.65, 0.48-0.89, p = 0.006) and high-risk PE (aOR 12.01, 3.42-42.25, p < 0.001). In the full cohort, a ≥ 280 mL threshold predicted major bleeding with 91% sensitivity and 95% negative predictive value. Results were consistent after adjustment for device type.
CONCLUSIONS: Intraprocedural blood loss independently predicts bleeding and adverse outcomes after aspiration thrombectomy for PE, possibly more so in anaemic patients, and a ≥ 280 mL threshold may support risk stratification.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Clinical impact of blood loss during mechanical thrombus aspiration for pulmonary embolism intervention, a sub-analysis of the USAT IH-PE registry.

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Coronary artery implantation of the absorb bioresorbable vascular scaffold (BVS) without intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance resulted in greater adverse events compared with metallic drug‐eluting stents during 3‐year follow‐up. Aims We assessed the 10‐year outcomes of BVS implanted with routine use of IVI guidance. Methods Between November 2014 and October 2016, 100 consecutive patients in whom the operator elected to implant a BVS were treated with 190 BVS devices in 171 lesions at a single center in Brazil. IVI was performed before and after BVS implantation in all patients. Clinical follow‐up was complete in all patients (no losses to follow‐up) for at least 8.8 years. Results Median follow‐up was 9.5 years (25th percentile 9.2, 75th percentile 10.1), range 8.8–10.8 years. Through the latest follow‐up, no patient experienced a cardiac death or definite scaffold thrombosis, and only one patient had a target‐vessel MI (TVMI). Major adverse cardiac events (the composite of all‐cause death, any MI, or any revascularization) occurred in 29 patients (Kaplan−Meier estimated 10‐year rate 29.4%); target vessel failure (TVF) (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia‐driven target‐vessel revascularization) occurred in 15 patients (10‐year rate 15.0%); and target lesion failure (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia‐driven target‐lesion revascularization) occurred in 10 patients (10‐year rate 10.0%). In the landmark analysis, TVF between 3 and 10 years occurred in 7 patients (7.6%). Conclusions In this single‐center, non‐randomized observational study, the long‐term outcomes of BVS implantation in simple and complex coronary lesions with routine IVI guidance were favorable. These findings are hypothesis‐generating and require confirmation in adequately powered randomized studies.
title: Long‐Term Outcomes After Coronary Absorb BVS Implantation Guided by Intravascular Imaging

abstract: ABSTRACT Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered‐stent implantation can restore large‐bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon‐assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87‐year‐old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic‐isthmus stenosis with a peak‐to‐peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same‐session covered‐stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29‐mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18‐mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic‐valve predilation with a 23‐mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re‐expansion of the stent, a 23‐mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic‐isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon‐assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.
title: Covered‐Stent Migration During Same‐Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable‐polymer sirolimus‐eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM. Aims In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5‐year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus‐eluting stent (EES). Methods TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non‐stratified outcomes in DM versus non‐DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia‐driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis. Results Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non‐DM patients, TLF ( p < 0.001), cardiac death ( p < 0.001), TVMI ( p = 0.002), ischemia‐driven TLR ( p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis ( p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM. Conclusion This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.
title: Final 5‐Year Results of Abluminal Groove‐Filled Biodegradable‐Polymer Sirolimus‐Eluting Stent Versus Durable‐Polymer Everolimus‐Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial

abstract: ABSTRACT Distal coronary artery perforation (CAP) during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is traditionally managed with embolic coils or autologous fat. However, fat embolization can be technically demanding due to complex tissue harvesting and delivery. We describe a closed‐needle lower abdominal micro‐suction technique enabling rapid percutaneous harvesting and direct microcatheter delivery of an autologous fat suspension without benchtop processing. An 18‐gauge angiographic needle attached to a syringe pre‐loaded with 2–3 mL of a 1:1 contrast‐saline mixture is inserted into lower abdominal subcutaneous tissue under continuous manual negative pressure, aspirating 1–2 mL of fat‐containing tissue fragments within ~10 s (total final volume ~3.5–5 mL). The resulting radiopaque suspension is delivered directly through a microcatheter using an inverted‐syringe technique via small, incremental hand boluses of 0.25–0.5 mL until complete sealing is achieved. Descriptive histology confirmed mature adipose tissue fragments admixed with blood, fibrin, and clot. The technique was successfully deployed in two consecutive patients with Ellis type II and III distal CAP. Immediate angiographic sealing was achieved in both cases without open tissue processing or syringe‐to‐syringe transfer. At 6‐month follow‐up, both patients remained clinically stable without recurrent pericardial effusion or target‐vessel failure. Closed‐needle abdominal micro‐suction is a rapid, low‐resource, zero‐transfer bailout technique for autologous fat embolization in high‐acuity distal CAPs.
title: Closed‐Needle Abdominal Micro‐Suction Fat Embolization for Distal Coronary Perforation

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dual‐lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid‐exchange (RX) port and an over‐the‐wire (OTW) port, within a single low‐profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non‐CTO lesions. Methods This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non‐CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations. Results Five applications are presented: (1) aorto‐ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side‐branch re‐entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions. Conclusions DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM‐assisted strategies in complex non‐CTO lesions.
title: Dual‐Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non‐CTO Lesions

abstract: ABSTRACT Wire‐impenetrable chronic total occlusion (CTO) proximal caps cannot be penetrated with conventional guidewire escalation. They are often associated with severe calcification and proximal cap ambiguity. Wire‐impenetrable proximal caps can be approached using a “go through” or a “go around” strategy. “Go through” involves using penetrative guidewires or other plaque‐modifying equipment, such as laser and electrocautery‐assisted re‐entry (e‐CART). The “go around” approach involves getting into the extraplaque space, through which the CTO is traversed in either the antegrade or the retrograde direction, followed by re‐entry into the true lumen. Strong guide‐catheter support is required for both the “go through” and “go around” approaches. We discuss the approach to wire‐impenetrable CTO proximal caps, propose a step‐by‐step treatment algorithm, and address potential challenges and their troubleshooting.
title: Step‐by‐Step Approach to the Wire‐Impenetrable Chronic Total Occlusion Proximal Cap

abstract: ABSTRACT We report a case of very severe aortic stenosis (AS) in which side‐branch occlusion during elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) precipitated life‐threatening ventricular arrhythmias and hemodynamic collapse. The patient was a 72‐year‐old man with very severe AS who was scheduled to undergo a valve intervention. Preprocedural coronary angiography revealed a significant, newly developed stenosis in the right coronary artery, and an elective PCI was performed prior to valve treatment. Following intravascular lithotripsy and drug‐eluting stent implantation, occlusion of the conus branch occurred, triggering recurrent ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Despite initiation of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra‐aortic balloon pump support, the patient's hemodynamic status did not improve. Because excessive afterload due to very severe AS was considered the principal pathophysiological mechanism, emergency balloon aortic valvuloplasty was performed. This resulted in rapid hemodynamic stabilization and complete resolution of ventricular arrhythmias. This case illustrates that even a minor side‐branch occlusion during PCI can lead to catastrophic outcomes in patients with very severe AS. Furthermore, it highlights that mechanical circulatory support alone may be insufficient, and that prompt relief of valvular obstruction is essential. Careful consideration of the indications and sequence of coronary intervention through discussions with a heart team is warranted for patients with very severe AS.
title: Electrical Storm Triggered by Conus Branch Occlusion During Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Very Severe Aortic Stenosis: Rescue With Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty Under Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation

abstract: ABSTRACT Myocardial bridging (MB) is usually managed medically, and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is generally avoided for isolated bridging. In clinical practice, however, stent extension into a bridged segment may be difficult to avoid when proximal left anterior descending (LAD) disease reaches the bridge entrance, LAD chronic total occlusion obscures distal bridge involvement, diffuse disease leaves no bridge‐free landing region, or bailout coverage is required for edge dissection or procedural instability. Once implanted within the bridge, a stent is exposed to repetitive extrinsic compression, caliber mismatch, dynamic deformation, and abnormal local shear, creating a substrate for restenosis, deformation, fracture, perforation, and target lesion failure. This focused review addresses unavoidable bridged‐segment stenting as a distinct PCI scenario rather than as a general review of myocardial bridging. We summarize lesion‐bridge patterns, anatomic and physiologic mechanisms, the role of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)/optical coherence tomography (OCT), and invasive physiology in procedural planning, and practical strategies to minimize metal burden and optimize stent‐edge placement. We also examine drug‐coated balloons, surgical unroofing, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in selected anatomy, and emerging bioadaptor technology, while explicitly distinguishing established clinical evidence from limited observational data and hypothesis‐generating concepts.
title: Unavoidable Stent Extension Into the Bridged Segment During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Bridging: A Focused Review of Mechanisms, Pitfalls, and Treatment Strategies

abstract: ABSTRACT Background The United Kingdom–British Cardiovascular Intervention Society complex high‐risk indicated percutaneous coronary intervention (UK‐BCIS CHIP) score was developed to identify patient‐ and procedural factors to predict short‐term adverse outcomes in patients undergoing high risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The performance of the UK‐BCIS CHIP score in a patient population treated with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) for severe coronary calcification remains unknown. Aims To evaluate the prognostic performance of the UK‐BCIS CHIP score in patients undergoing IVL‐assisted PCI for severe coronary calcification, and to assess procedural and 1‐year clinical outcomes across CHIP score categories. Methods This international, multicenter, prospective study included consecutive patients undergoing IVL‐assisted PCI between May 2019 and December 2025 from the BENELUX‐IVL registry. Patients were stratified according to UK‐BCIS CHIP score categories (0, 1–2, 3–4, and ≥ 5). The primary endpoint was 1‐year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non‐fatal myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all‐cause mortality, procedural outcomes, and periprocedural complications. Discrimination of the UK‐BCIS CHIP score was assessed using the AUC for in‐hospital events and the Harrell's C‐index for 1‐year outcomes. Results A total of 911 patients were included. Higher UK‐BCIS CHIP scores were associated with increased clinical comorbidity, lesion complexity, and procedural intensity. Procedural, device, and technical success rates were comparable across UK‐BCIS CHIP score categories (85.1%, 94.4%, and 85.7% overall; p = 0.850, p = 0.813, and p = 0.781, respectively). Complications requiring intervention occurred in 5.5% of patients and did not differ significantly across CHIP score categories ( p = 0.347). The 1‐year cumulative incidence of MACE, accounting for all‐cause death as a competing risk, did not differ significantly across UK‐BCIS CHIP score categories (Gray's test p = 0.53). Conclusion In IVL‐assisted PCI, the UK‐BCIS CHIP score effectively identifies patients with increased clinical and procedural complexity but shows limited discrimination for mid‐term ischemic outcomes. IVL‐assisted PCI is safe and effective across the full spectrum of CHIP risk, while long‐term prognosis appears primarily driven by underlying comorbidity burden.
title: External Validation of the UK‐BCIS CHIP Score to Predict 1‐Year Outcomes in Patients Undergoing IVL‐Assisted PCI: Insights From the International BENELUX‐IVL Registry

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) measures angiography‐derived coronary physiology, whereas radial wall strain (RWS) characterizes cyclic lumen deformation. We investigated their complementary long‐term prognostic information in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model. Aims We investigated the complementary long‐term prognostic information of QFR and RWS in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses, and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model. Methods This single‐center retrospective cohort included 236 patients with 236 untreated index vessels and 50%–90% diameter stenosis. QFR and maximum RWS (RWSmax) were calculated offline and were unavailable to treating clinicians. Target vessel failure (TVF) comprised cardiac death, target vessel‐related myocardial infarction, or ischemia‐driven target vessel revascularization (TVR). Prespecified Cox models used multiple imputation, and four nested models underwent 1000‐bootstrap validation with repeat imputation and fitting. Fixed 3‐year analyses, calibration, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Over a median potential follow‐up of 66.8 months, 55 patients experienced TVF, including 40 TVR events. TVF occurred in 37/108 patients (34.3%) with RWSmax > 12% and 18/128 (14.1%) with RWSmax ≤12%. In the primary model, the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.06–1.23; p = 0.001) per 1% increase in RWSmax and 1.34 (95% CI: 1.08–1.67; p = 0.010) per 0.05 decrease in QFR. The combined model had an apparent C ‐index of 0.733 and an optimism‐corrected C ‐index of 0.704, compared with 0.597 for the clinical model. Its corrected 3‐year AUC was 0.733, and its corrected calibration slope was 0.90. Conclusions Joint assessment of coronary physiology and wall strain provided incremental long‐term prognostic information beyond clinical and angiographic characteristics in untreated intermediate lesions. Lower QFR and higher RWSmax were independently associated with TVF, and each added prognostic information beyond the other. The signal predominantly concerned subsequent revascularization. External validation is needed before clinical application.
title: Long‐Term Prognostic Value of Angiography‐Derived Quantitative Flow Ratio and Radial Wall Strain in Untreated Intermediate Coronary Stenoses: A Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: ABSTRACT Angiographic narrowing of a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) bypass graft does not always reflect atherosclerotic progression. Chronic or spontaneous LIMA graft dissection may be identified using optical coherence tomography (OCT). A patient with severe multivessel coronary disease and a history of coronary stenting and triple coronary artery bypass grafting presented with non‐ST‐elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated critical left main–left circumflex disease, extensive left anterior descending artery in‐stent restenosis, an occluded venous graft, and eccentric mid‐LIMA narrowing. Urgent native‐vessel revascularization restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow and relieved the patient's symptoms. During staged LIMA assessment 6 days later, OCT was performed using a Dragonfly OpStar imaging catheter. OCT identified the entry of a longitudinal intimal flap separating the true and false lumens over a long segment, without significant atherosclerosis in the imaged segment. The operators interpreted this “double‐barrel” configuration as a nonobstructive dissection of presumed chronicity. Preserved LIMA flow and clinical stability supported stent deferral; the patient remained asymptomatic and with preserved ejection fraction at the 2‐month follow‐up visit. This report offers important lessons for interventionalists: intravascular imaging can distinguish dissection from apparent atherosclerotic stenosis and significantly drive further management. Inadvertent false‐lumen stenting could expand the false channel, compress the true lumen, and compromise graft perfusion. OCT clearly elucidated lesion morphology and supported clinical restraint; however, it did not independently establish dissection age or an exact mechanism of dissection.
title: Internal Mammary Artery Bypass Graft Dissection Mimicking Atherosclerotic Stenosis: Optical Coherence Tomography to Guide Stent Deferral

abstract: ABSTRACT We report a rare case of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) catheter entrapment in which extensive twisting of the catheter shaft prevented retrieval. In this phenomenon, termed “catheter suicide,” the mechanical IVUS catheter twisted within the left main coronary artery (LMCA) and formed complex loops. Initial removal attempts were unsuccessful, and, during these bailout attempts, the imaging core of the IVUS catheter was found to be severed in its proximal portion. Subsequent imaging of another vessel confirmed extensive twisting, with associated iatrogenic dissection, as the cause of entrapment. Ex vivo experiments reproduced this rotational torque‐driven complication. The twist was eventually released incidentally when the IVUS catheter was advanced further, and a larger guiding catheter was used, thereby facilitating safe retrieval. Subsequently, a stent was placed to treat the LMCA dissection, achieving thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow, and the patient was discharged without complications. This case illustrates a severe complication specific to mechanical IVUS systems and emphasizes the importance of prevention and early surgical consultation.
title: Intravascular Ultrasound Catheter Entrapment Caused by Extensive Twisting in the Left Main Coronary Artery: A Challenging Retrieval

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) expose patients and operators to ionizing radiation, posing risks of deterministic effects such as skin injury and stochastic effects including malignancy. Although real‐time dosimetry and dose alerts have been associated with radiation‐dose reductions in prior reports, the level of patient radiation reduction associated with implementing a formal, multifaceted radiation reduction program has not previously been reported in a high‐volume catheterization laboratory. Objectives To evaluate the impact of a substantial radiation dose level (SRDL) protocol on patient radiation exposure during PCI. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 19,249 PCI procedures at a tertiary center from July 2012 to December 2021. Patients were stratified into a pre‐protocol cohort (Phase 1: 17,332 procedures) and a post‐protocol cohort (Phase 2: 1917 procedures following implementation in November 2019). The SRDL protocol included real‐time radiation monitoring, alert thresholds at 5 Gy air kerma, and structured follow‐up for high‐dose cases. Study outcomes included air kerma ( K a,r ) dose‐area product (DAP), contrast volume, and fluoroscopy time. Results The study cohort (mean age 66.3 years; 28.5% female) demonstrated significant reductions in radiation exposure after implementing the protocol. Median air kerma declined from 2.6 to 2.0 Gy (23% reduction; p < 0.0001), and median DAP decreased from 158 to 125 Gy·cm 2 (20.8% reduction; p < 0.0001). Contrast volume was reduced by 15 mL (11.1% reduction; p < 0.0001), while fluoroscopy time remained unchanged (18.1 vs. 18.3 min; p = 0.094). Despite increased procedural complexity in Phase 2 (multivessel PCI: 69.5% vs. 65.2%; p < 0.001), radiation reduction remained significant. Conclusions Implementation of an SRDL protocol was associated with significant reductions in patient radiation exposure during PCI without increasing procedure time, supporting its use as a safety intervention in high‐volume catheterization laboratories.
title: Reducing Patient Radiation Skin Dose in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using a Dedicated Protocol: A Single‐Center Experience

abstract: ABSTRACT Valve‐in‐valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73‐year‐old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre‐syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve‐in‐valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon‐expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post‐implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1‐year follow‐up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve‐in‐valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high‐risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post‐implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.
title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve‐in‐Valve Replacement Using Balloon‐Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Pseudoaneurysms of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) are a life‐threatening entity, typically developing as a complication of infective endocarditis or prior cardiac surgery. They should be repaired to reduce the risk of systemic embolization and the catastrophic risks of rupture. Surgical resection has been the gold standard; however, percutaneous transcatheter closure has emerged as an alternative for patients deemed to be at prohibitive surgical risk. The procedural access routes and technical methods for closure remain variable and patient specific. Aims This study aims to describe unique cases of percutaneous LVOT pseudoaneurysm closure in patients with mechanical valves. Methods From 2023 to 2026, 4 patients underwent percutaneous transcatheter closure of LVOT pseudoaneurysms at our center after prior mechanical aortic valve or root replacement (AVR). Results Case 1 highlights an antegrade transseptal approach to pack a wide‐necked post‐endocarditis pseudoaneurysm with coils. Case 2 demonstrates the ability of a microcatheter to engage a slit‐like orifice and utilization of coil embolization without device closure of the orifice due to proximity to the aortic valve ring. Case 3 illustrates a combined approach using devices to close 2 separate orifices and coils to pack a large aneurysm sac. Case 4 represents the first reported case of an excluded LVOT pseudoaneurysm accessed via a percutaneous, transthoracic puncture of the RV free wall and subsequent traversal of the interventricular septum. Conclusions In our experience, percutaneous transcatheter closure is a feasible option in most cases and should be considered prior to operative revision unless there is an unstable valve, active endocarditis, or other complicating circumstance that mandate prosthetic valve removal or a surgical approach for other reasons.
title: Transventricular and Transseptal Closure of Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Pseudoaneurysms After Mechanical Aortic Valve Replacement: Access‐Related and Technical Considerations

abstract: ABSTRACT The jailed balloon technique (JBT) is an effective strategy for side branch (SB) protection during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary bifurcation lesions; however, jailed balloon entrapment is a rare but serious complication. We report the case of a man in his 70s who was successfully resuscitated after out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation and underwent emergency PCI for a right coronary artery bifurcation lesion. A drug‐eluting stent was deployed from the mid right coronary artery to the posterior descending branch using JBT. The jailed SB balloon became entrapped and could not be retrieved despite repeated inflation and deflation, traction, and rotational torque. Further traction resulted in deep engagement of the guiding catheter and an accordion phenomenon of the right coronary artery, raising concern about vascular injury. A balloon was therefore inflated within the stented main vessel, and forward pressure was applied to its shaft to provide counterforce against traction on the entrapped SB balloon. Using this technique, which we termed the “reverse balloon anchoring technique,” the entrapped balloon was successfully retrieved without apparent device damage. Final angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved SB flow and adequate stent apposition. The reverse balloon anchoring technique may represent a useful bailout option for jailed balloon entrapment when conventional retrieval maneuvers fail.
title: Reverse Balloon Anchoring for Retrieval of an Entrapped Side‐Branch Balloon During the Jailed Balloon Technique

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Coronary microcatheters are essential in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but their structural failure has mainly been described through passive surveillance. Aims We aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and procedural impact of microcatheter structural damage during contemporary CTO PCI. Methods The prospective multicentre CROSS registry included 2137 CTO PCI procedures performed at high‐volume centers between 2024 and 2025. Suspected damaged microcatheters underwent centralized assessment and were classified as grade 1 (superficial deformation), grade 2 (significant deformation without complete fracture), or grade 3 (complete fracture). Results Structural damage occurred in 109 procedures (5.1%); 58.7%, 5.5%, and 35.8% were grade 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Independent predictors of structural microcatheter damage were moderate‐to‐severe calcification (adjusted OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.27–2.94), retrograde approach (adjusted OR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10–2.67), moderate‐to‐severe tortuosity (adjusted OR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.04–2.50), and longer procedure duration (adjusted OR per 30‐min increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06–1.30). Structural damage was associated with increased periprocedural complications (25.7% vs. 7.7%; OR: 4.12, 95% CI: 2.60–6.52; p < 0.0001) and failed CTO PCI (11.0% vs. 3.1%; OR: 3.86, 95% CI: 2.01–7.39; p < 0.0001). Conclusions Structural microcatheter damage occurred in approximately 1 in 20 CTO PCIs and was associated with anatomical complexity, demanding procedural circumstances, and substantially worse procedural outcomes.
title: Structural Damage of Coronary Microcatheters During Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Interventions: The Prospective Multicenter Cross Registry
