During his hospitalization, he complained of back pain and subsequent magnetic resonance imaging revealed pre-vertebral and ventral cervical epidural abscesses. TEE was repeated which demonstrated three echo-dense Watchman masses (16x5.7mm, 9.2x7.4 mm, and 6.7 mm) (Figure 2). Cardiothoracic surgery was consulted, however the patient suffered a stroke and subsequently died. Conclusion: Watchman infections are rare and its diagnosis and management prove challenging. There is high mortality with both conservative and surgical/percutaneous interventions with both approaches lacking evidence. We present a difficult case of watchman endocarditis where conservative therapy did not yield a successful outcome. Further research is required to define optimal management and timing of removal.
title: Abstract 10379: An Unlikely Culprit: A Rare Case of Watchman Endocarditis

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is prevalent among patients with acute mesenteric ischemia and may reflect embolic etiology, underlying cardiovascular disease, or both. Acute mesenteric ischemia requires urgent surgical decision-making and hemodynamic optimization, both of which may be complicated by concurrent AF. Whether AF independently worsens outcomes in this population remains unknown. Objectives: To evaluate the association between AF and in-hospital mortality and complications among adults admitted with a primary diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia. Methods: Adults admitted with a primary diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia with and without concurrent AF were identified in the 2022 National Inpatient Sample using ICD-10-CM codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, demographics, comorbidity burden, and hospital characteristics was performed. Sensitivity analyses included propensity score matching. Results: Of 2,508 unweighted admissions (weighted 12,540), 513 (20.5%) had concurrent AF. AF patients were older (76.7 vs 64.7 years; P<0.001) with higher comorbidity burden (CCI 3.04 vs 2.02; P<0.001). In-hospital mortality was 19.9% among AF patients versus 8.6% without (P<0.001). After full adjustment, AF was independently associated with higher odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.85; 95% CI 1.37-2.49; P<0.001), cardiogenic shock (aOR 4.42; 95% CI 1.68-11.63; P=0.003), acute kidney injury (aOR 1.41; 95% CI 1.11-1.78; P=0.005), and mechanical ventilation (aOR 2.29; 95% CI 1.60-3.28; P<0.001). Bowel resection rates did not differ (aOR 0.96; P=0.695). Results were consistent in propensity score matched analysis (aOR 1.57; 95% CI 1.11-2.22; P=0.010). Conclusions: Among adults admitted for acute mesenteric ischemia, concurrent AF was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality, cardiogenic shock, acute kidney injury, and mechanical ventilation. These findings identify AF as a high-risk comorbidity in acute mesenteric ischemia.
title: Abstract 10402: Atrial Fibrillation in Acute Mesenteric Ischemia

abstract: Background: A substantial proportion of patients suffering from severe mitral regurgitation (MR) are considered unsuitable for either surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair, primarily owing to prohibitive procedural risks or anatomical limitations of the mitral valve. Hypothesis: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical feasibility and outcomes of the MitraFix (MitrAssist Lifesciences) transapical mitral valve replacement system in high surgical risk populations presenting with symptomatic mitral regurgitation. Methods: This non-randomized, multicenter, prospective study investigated the safety and device performance of the MitraFix TMVR system in patients with moderate-to-severe symptomatic mitral regurgitation during a 1-year observation. All echocardiographic measurements were interpreted by an independent core laboratory. Results: A total of 62 patients (mean age 73.2 years, 51.6% female, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons score 6.7% [Q1-Q3: 4.9-8.3%]) with severe mitral regurgitation (41.9% with secondary MR, median left ventricular ejection fraction 40.3% [Q1-Q3: 38.0-43.1%]) were treated across 19 institutions. The MitraFix TMVR system was implanted successfully in 60 patients, achieving a technical success of 96.8%. The cardiovascular mortality was 8.3% at 30 days and 21.7% at 1 year, with no postoperative reintervention occurrence. Substantial MR reduction to ≤1+ was achieved in 100% of patients, and at 1 year, 68.1% were in NYHA functional class I or II, with a median 46.3 m and 24.0 points improvement in six-minute walk distance test and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary scores, respectively. Most patients had no (85.1%) or trivial (14.9%) regurgitation, with a median gradient of 4.1 mmHg and no left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (median gradient 1.0 mmHg [Q1-Q3: 1.0-1.3 mmHg]). Conclusions: The 1-year follow-up results from the MitraFix feasibility study indicated high procedural success, sustainable valve performance, optimal improvement of functional status and no reinterventions in both primary and secondary regurgitation patients. The ultrasound-guided approach was safe and practicable. Additional follow-up and clinical outcomes are essential to consolidate these results.
title: Abstract 10423: One-Year Outcomes Following Novel Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Patients with Severe Mitral Regurgitation: The MitraFix TMVR Feasibility Study

abstract: Background: Right-sided venous congestion is the dominant clinical manifestation of severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Whether bedside signs of congestion reflect hemodynamic severity and predict clinical outcomes remains uncertain. We developed an Objective Congestion Score (OCS) and evaluated its associations with invasive hemodynamics, transthoracic echocardiographic (TTE) parameters, and clinical outcomes in patients with severe TR. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that greater congestion burden is associated with higher filling pressures, worse right ventricular function, and increased risk of mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 285 patients undergoing tricuspid valve intervention at the Cleveland Clinic between 2019 and 2024. The OCS (0-5 points) was constructed from five examiner-verified bedside signs: elevated jugular venous pressure, lower-extremity edema, abdominal swelling/ascites, unintentional weight gain, and pulmonary crackles. Patients were stratified into Low (0-1; n=106), Intermediate (2-3; n=139), and High (4-5; n=40) congestion groups. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlations and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, NYHA class, prior HFH, hemoglobin, creatinine, and LVEF, with RV fractional area change included as a covariate for non-RV outcomes. Clinical outcomes were evaluated with multivariable Cox regression. Results: Increasing congestion burden was associated with worse RV function, higher right- and left-sided filling pressures, greater symptom burden, and higher TRISCORE (all p<0.05). OCS correlated with RA a-wave (ρ=0.36), PCWP mean (ρ=0.34), and RA mean pressure (ρ=0.33; all p<0.001; Figure 1). After multivariable adjustment, each 1-point increase in OCS independently predicted higher RA mean pressure (+1.11 mmHg, p<0.001), higher PCWP (+1.10 mmHg, p=0.002), and lower RV fractional area change (–1.47%, p=0.006). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated progressively lower 2-year freedom from all-cause mortality or HFH across increasing congestion groups (Figure 2, log-rank p=0.003). In multivariable Cox regression, each 1-point increase in OCS was associated with a 21% higher risk of the composite outcome (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.46; p=0.041) after adjustment for age, sex, creatinine, LVEF, and RV fractional area change. Conclusions: In patients with severe TR, bedside signs of congestion correlate with greater hemodynamic burden and worse RV function, and their cumulative burden is independently associated with 2-year mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Bedside congestion assessment provides clinically relevant information beyond conventional TTE measures and may aid risk stratification in this population.
title: Abstract 10424: Objective Congestion Burden Identifies Hemodynamic Severity and Predicts Outcomes in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation

abstract: Background: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is a frequent, prognostically important complication of myocardial infarction (MI), yet risk stratification remains limited. Left atrial volume index (LAVi) is an established predictor of AF, but the prognostic significance of right atrial volume index (RAVi) as a marker of post-MI atrial remodeling remains uncertain. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that RAVi independently predicts post-MI NOAF and provides incremental predictive value beyond established clinical and echocardiographic risk factors. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 2,091 patients admitted with MI and no prior AF who underwent index admission echocardiography. Sequential multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were constructed: Model 1 (clinical variables, including age, sex, comorbidities, STEMI, and moderate-or-greater [≥+2] mitral and tricuspid regurgitation), Model 2 (Model 1 + LAVi + LVEF), and Model 3 (Model 2 + RAVi). Discrimination was assessed by the concordance index (C-index), and incremental value was evaluated by likelihood ratio testing (LRT). Kaplan-Meier analysis was stratified by a RAVi threshold of 28 mL/m 2 , derived from maximally selected rank statistics. A prespecified sensitivity analysis was performed in the subgroup with available percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcome data. Results: NOAF occurred in 248 patients (11.9%) over 3 years. Patients who developed NOAF were older, had more prior heart failure, and lower successful PCI rates. Patients with RAVi ≥28 mL/m 2 had significantly lower NOAF-free survival over 3 years than those with RAVi <28 mL/m 2 (Figure 1). Model discrimination improved from a C-index of 0.697 for the clinical model to 0.718 after addition of LAVi and LVEF (ΔLRT p<0.001) and to 0.727 after inclusion of RAVi (ΔLRT p=0.003). In the fully adjusted model, both LAVi (HR 1.018 per mL/m 2 , 95% CI 1.007-1.029, p=0.002) and RAVi (HR 1.019 per mL/m 2 , 95% CI 1.007-1.031, p=0.003) independently predicted NOAF (Figure 2). Moderate-or-greater mitral regurgitation was also independently associated with NOAF (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.25-2.51, p=0.001). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with available PCI outcome data (n=1,295; 143 NOAF events), successful PCI was independently associated with a lower NOAF risk (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.80, p=0.001), and RAVi remained independently predictive (HR 1.020 per mL/m 2 , 95% CI 1.002-1.038, p=0.030). Conclusions: RAVi independently predicts NOAF following MI and provides incremental predictive information beyond established clinical risk factors, LAVi, and LVEF. These findings suggest that right atrial remodeling represents a distinct pathophysiologic process that is not fully captured by left atrial measurements alone. RAVi may serve as a useful echocardiographic marker for identifying patients at increased risk of NOAF following MI.
title: Abstract 10435: Right Atrial Volume Index Improves Risk Stratification for New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Acute Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) exerts beneficial cardiometabolic effects through the secretion of endocrine factors called batokines. Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF15), a stress-responsive cytokine that can be secreted from BAT, has been implicated in the regulation of energy homeostasis and cardioprotection. GDF15 mediates its metabolic effects through the hindbrain receptor GDNF family receptor α-like (GFRAL); however, whether GFRAL is required for cardioprotection remains unknown. We previously observed that myocardial infarction (MI) induces GDF15 expression in BAT and increases circulating GDF15 levels. Hypothesis: BAT-derived GDF15 is required for cardioprotection following MI through GFRAL-dependent mechanisms. Methods: Mice lacking GDF15 in thermogenic adipocytes ( Gdf15 BKO ) were generated by crossing Gdf15 floxed mice with Ucp1 -Cre mice. Global Gfral knockout ( Gfral -/- ) mice and wild-type (WT) littermate controls were used to investigate GFRAL dependence. Male mice (10-12 weeks) underwent MI or sham surgery. Circulating GDF15 levels, cardiac inflammation and fibrosis, systolic function, infarct size, and post-MI survival were assessed. Results: Gdf15 deletion in BAT significantly reduced circulating GDF15 levels after MI, whereas serum GDF15 remained elevated in Gfral -/- mice. Gdf15 BKO mice exhibited significantly reduced survival following MI compared with WT controls, while survival was unchanged between Gfral -/- and WT mice. Immunohistochemical analyses demonstrated increased cardiac macrophage infiltration in Gdf15 BKO mice after MI. Consistent with these findings, markers of inflammation and fibrosis were elevated in Gdf15 BKO hearts 3 days after MI but were unchanged in Gfral -/- mice. Despite these differences, infarct size and systolic function were similar among genotypes. Importantly, treatment of Gdf15 BKO mice with recombinant human GDF15 significantly rescued post-MI survival. Conclusions: BAT-derived GDF15 is required for survival following MI and promotes cardioprotection by limiting post-infarction inflammation and immune cell infiltration. The absence of adverse cardiac outcomes in Gfral -/- mice suggests that GDF15-mediated cardioprotection occurs independently of GFRAL signaling. These findings identify BAT-derived GDF15 as a critical endocrine mediator of the adaptive response to ischemic injury and reveal a novel BAT-heart axis regulating post-MI survival.
title: Abstract 10437: Brown Adipose Tissue-Derived Growth Differentiation Factor 15 Improves Survival Following Myocardial Infarction Through GFRAL-Independent Mechanisms

abstract: Introduction/Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains a major determinant of mortality in cardiogenic shock despite advances in mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Hemolysis is increasingly documented with contemporary MCS, however, its contribution to renal injury and clinically actionable thresholds remain poorly defined. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that hemolysis associates with AKI in patients with cardiogenic shock receiving MCS. Methods/Approach: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult ICU patients with cardiogenic shock receiving MCS. Clinical and laboratory measures were captured at 6-hour intervals. Hemolysis was defined as plasma free hemoglobin (pfHb) ≥20 mg/dL (moderate) and ≥50 mg/dL (severe). AKI was defined by creatinine-based KDIGO criteria. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between hemolysis and AKI, adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, shock etiology, LVEF, MCS type, support duration, and vasopressor burden. Results/Data: Median age was 60 years (IQR 47-68), 76% were male, and 29% had CKD; median LVEF was 25% (IQR 20-45). MCS included intravascular microaxial support (53%) and VA-ECMO (44%). Hemolysis was highly prevalent (pfHb ≥20 mg/dL: 81%; ≥50 mg/dL: 65%). AKI occurred in 88%, 50% required in-hospital dialysis, and mortality was 55%. Severe hemolysis demonstrated a strong association with AKI (unadjusted OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.39-10.6, p=0.01), which persisted after adjustment (aOR 3.38, 95% CI 1.04-11.8, p=0.046). In contrast, moderate hemolysis was not independently associated with AKI (aOR 2.32, 95% CI 0.50-9.84, p=0.30), indicating a threshold-dependent, dose-response relationship. Conclusions: In our contemporary cardiogenic shock cohort, hemolysis and AKI were common. Hemolysis is independently associated with AKI and could potentially be a modifiable mediator of kidney injury in patients supported with MCS. Clinical Implications: Targeting hemolysis—through device optimization, early detection, and tailored management—represents an immediate opportunity to reduce AKI and improve outcomes in cardiogenic shock.
title: Abstract 10448: Severe Hemolysis Identifies a Modifiable Driver of Acute Kidney Injury in Cardiogenic Shock Patients Receiving Mechanical Circulatory Support

abstract: Background: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) may be complicated by cardiovascular failure with refractory hypoxemia or circulatory collapse requiring escalation to advanced support with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or percutaneous ventricular assist device (pVAD)/intravascular microaxial flow pump (Impella). While ECMO use has grown despite uncertain mortality benefit, less is known about how heart failure (HF) phenotype and concurrent organ dysfunction influence advanced circulatory support. Research Question: In adults hospitalized with ARDS, does ECMO and Impella use differ across HF phenotypes and comorbidities? Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample from 2018-2022. Adult ARDS hospitalizations were identified using ICD-10-CM code J80 and categorized as no HF, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), or other/unspecified HF. ECMO and Impella use were identified using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was composite mechanical circulatory support (MCS), defined as ECMO or Impella use; secondary outcomes were individual devices. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographics, hospital characteristics, admission factors, comorbidities, year, and acute clinical severity. Results: Among 515,150 weighted ARDS hospitalizations, 389,680 had no HF, 52,390 HFpEF, 34,300 HFrEF, and 38,780 other/unspecified HF. After adjustment, HFrEF was associated with higher odds of composite MCS (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.21, 95% CI 1.94-2.52), ECMO (aOR 1.73, 95% CI 1.49-2.01), and Impella use (aOR 11.86, 95% CI 8.34-16.88). Other/unspecified HF: MCS (aOR 2.49, 95% CI 2.19-2.84), ECMO (aOR 2.41, 95% CI 2.10-2.77), and Impella (aOR 7.38, 95% CI 4.97-10.95). In contrast, HFpEF was not associated with increased ECMO or Impella use and had lower odds of composite MCS (aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.94). Among comorbidities, acute kidney injury (AKI) was associated with higher odds of all support types, strongest for Impella (aOR 2.23); chronic liver disease (CLD) had a similar pattern (Impella aOR 2.59). Pulmonary embolism (PE) was associated with higher odds of MCS and ECMO but not Impella use, whereas coronary artery disease (CAD) was strongly associated with Impella use (aOR 5.42). Conclusion: In this nationally representative ARDS cohort, advanced circulatory support utilization varied by HF phenotype and comorbidity burden. HFrEF and other/unspecified HF were strongly associated with ECMO and Impella, whereas HFpEF was not. Notably, HFpEF was not associated with increased advanced support use, suggesting phenotype-specific escalation patterns warranting prospective study. AKI, CLD, PE, and CAD may further identify ARDS hospitalizations likely to receive these therapies, to aid resource planning.
title: Abstract 10449: Heart Failure Phenotype and Clinical Predictors of Impella and Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Use in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Hospitalizations: An Insight from the National Inpatient Sample Database

abstract: Background: The adult mammalian heart has limited regenerative capacity, whereas the neonatal heart can regenerate almost completely following injury, a potential that is lost by postnatal day 7 (P7). Serine hydroxymethyltransferase 2 (SHMT2) is a key enzyme that converts serine to glycine and supports cell growth; however, its role in cardiomyocyte proliferation and cardiac regeneration remains unknown. Methods: We performed metabolomic profiling of mouse hearts at P1 and P7. Among the metabolic pathways altered during postnatal maturation, glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, as well as one-carbon metabolism, were markedly downregulated. SHMT2 was identified as a key regulator associated with these metabolic changes. To investigate its function, we generated cardiomyocyte-specific Shmt2 knockout ( Shmt2 -cKO) mice and established gain-of-function models through adenoviral and AAV9-mediated cardiac Shmt2 delivery. Mechanisms underlying SHMT2-mediated cardiomyocyte proliferation were investigated using targeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, and other molecular approaches. Results: SHMT2 was highly expressed in cardiomyocytes during cardiac development and immediately after birth but was markedly downregulated in adult hearts. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Shmt2 impaired neonatal heart regeneration following injury, whereas cardiac delivery of cardiomyocyte-specific Shmt2 significantly induced adult cardiomyocyte proliferation, reduced scar formation, and improved cardiac function after myocardial infarction. SHMT2 also enhanced the proliferation of human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, SHMT2 promoted serine one-carbon metabolism and reduced oxidative stress, thereby supporting cardiomyocyte proliferation. Notably, overexpression of an enzymatically inactive SHMT2 mutant partially preserved the proliferative effect, suggesting non-metabolic functions of SHMT2. We further identified IQ motif-containing GTPase-activating protein 1 (IQGAP1) as a direct binding partner of SHMT2. SHMT2 interacted with the GAP-related domain (GRD) of IQGAP1 and inhibited NEDD4-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination at lysine residues K1155 and K1230 within the GRD domain, thereby stabilizing IQGAP1. Stabilized IQGAP1 activated Rap1-ERK signaling and promoted cardiomyocyte proliferation. Conclusions: These findings identify SHMT2 as a critical regulator of cardiac regeneration through serine one-carbon metabolism and the IQGAP1-dependent signaling pathway. Targeting SHMT2 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic myocardial injury.
title: Abstract 10457: SHMT2 Promotes Cardiomyocyte Proliferation and Cardiac Regeneration Through One-Carbon Metabolism and IQGAP1 Signaling

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) increases left atrial thrombotic risk, as estimated by the CHA 2 DS 2 -VA score, which correlates well with the presence of atrial myopathy but only modestly predicts thrombotic risk (C-statistic = 0.60). Other factors, such as mitral valve regurgitation (MR), may influence thrombotic risk. Furthermore, the thrombotic effect of lone AF, without underlying atrial myopathy, is not well studied. Hypothesis: MR (high flow) has an antithrombotic effect and lone AF (low flow) has a prothrombotic effect on left atrial thrombotic risk. Methods: A total of 20 (10 male and 10 female) 16-weeks old stress-negative Piétrain pigs were randomized to severe MR, induced by selective transection of the chordae tendineae with a custom-made retractor (n = 14), or sham procedure (n = 6). High-frequency atrial tachypacing was performed to induce AF (15 min). Left atrial blood samples were obtained before and after AF induction. After four weeks, blood sampling was repeated, and the sham group underwent a longer AF tachypacing session (60 min). To explore left atrial thrombotic risk, group differences in platelet aggregation, intrinsic, extrinsic, and common coagulation pathways, fibrinolysis, and von Willebrand factor (VWF) assays were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman’s test. Results: Severe MR (grade 3.5-4/4) led to significant left atrial myopathy, with a greater increase in left atrial volume compared to the sham group (+28.1 ± 5.4 mL vs. +5.4 ± 2.0 mL; p = 0.01), and more left atrial fibrosis (25.8 ± 1.4% vs. 13.7 ± 1.0%; p <0.001). There was a significantly divergent effect of MR vs. AF on left atrial thrombotic risk (P-values for all interactions <0.05, Figure 1). MR was associated with an increase in APTT (+9.6%), PT (+9.4%), D-dimers (+43.4%), and ADAMTS13:Ag (+27.8%), and a decrease in platelet aggregation (-7.4%), fibrinogen (-24.1%), VWF collagen binding (CB) activity/Ag ratio (-14.7%), and VWF high-molecular-weight multimers (HMWM, -2.4%), indicating an antithrombotic effect. The opposite was observed for AF, with a decrease in APTT (-1.1%) and PT (-1.9%), and an increase in platelet aggregation (+1.4%), fibrinogen (+2.2%), and D-dimers (+8.8%), indicating a prothrombotic effect. No sex differences were observed. Conclusions: Lone AF, in the absence of atrial myopathy, has a prothrombotic effect on left atrial thrombotic risk. These findings emphasize the importance of rhythm control to minimize left atrial thrombogenicity and challenge the safety of withholding anticoagulation in patients with persistent AF and a low CHA 2 DS 2 -VA score. On the other hand, MR has an antithrombotic effect on left atrial thrombotic risk, despite the development of significant left atrial myopathy. Therefore, MR could be considered a protective modifying factor in thromboembolic risk assessment of AF patients and may help individualize anticoagulant treatment.
title: Abstract 10471: Mitral Valve Regurgitation and Lone Atrial Fibrillation Influence Left Atrial Thrombotic Risk: A Porcine Model of Alternating Left Atrial Flow Conditions

abstract: Introduction: Optimal myocardial protection is a critical component of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Del Nido cardioplegia (DNC) has emerged as an alternative to conventional cardioplegic solutions; however, its effectiveness and safety in adult CABG patients remain debated. Research Question: Does del Nido cardioplegia improve perioperative and postoperative outcomes compared with conventional cardioplegic solutions in patients undergoing CABG? Methods: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched for studies comparing DNC with conventional cardioplegia in adult CABG patients. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Sensitivity analyses were performed using a leave-one-out approach. Results: Thirty-six studies involving 53,021 patients were included. Compared with conventional cardioplegia, DNC significantly reduced the need for defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp removal (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.30-0.58; p<0.0001), acute kidney injury (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53-0.99; p=0.043), blood transfusion requirements (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.98; p=0.022), inotropic support (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.93; p=0.004), cardiopulmonary bypass time (MD –5.89 minutes, 95% CI –9.24 to –2.54; p=0.0006), and intensive care unit stay (MD –0.16 days, 95% CI –0.29 to –0.02; p=0.022). Return to sinus rhythm was significantly more frequent with DNC (RR 1.86, 95% CI 1.07-3.23; p=0.028). No significant differences were observed in mortality, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, low cardiac output syndrome, intra-aortic balloon pump use, ECMO requirement, mechanical ventilation duration, hospital length of stay, postoperative LVEF, CK-MB, troponin I, troponin T, mediastinitis, deep sternal wound infection, prolonged ventilation, or reoperation for bleeding. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated overall robustness of the primary findings, with only minor variations observed for acute kidney injury and ICU stay outcomes. Conclusion: Del Nido cardioplegia is a safe and effective myocardial protection strategy in CABG surgery and is associated with reduced perioperative and postoperative complication rates. These findings support the increasing adoption of DNC in adult coronary surgery.
title: Abstract 10480: Comparison of del Nido Cardioplegia versus Conventional Cardioplegic Solutions in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is widely used for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Although procedural complication rates appear similar between patients with and without heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), prior studies were limited by small samples and incomplete adjustment. Because HFpEF is associated with higher comorbidity burden and impaired atrial mechanics, a large real-world matched analysis is needed to clarify early and long-term outcomes. Objective: To compare 30-day and 1-year outcomes after LAAO in patients with and without HFpEF using a large propensity-matched cohort from the TriNetX network. Methods: Adults undergoing LAAO (2015-2024) were identified in TriNetX. Patients with and without HFpEF were propensity matched (1:1) for demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included mortality, ischemic stroke/TIA, major bleeding, pericardial effusion/tamponade, and heart failure hospitalization at 30 days and 1 year. Cox models estimated hazard ratios. Results: After matching, 8,558 patients per group were well balanced. At 30 days, HFpEF patients had higher mortality (1.4% vs 0.6%; HR 2.53; p<0.001) and more stroke/TIA (1.3% vs 0.8%; HR 1.71; p=0.002). Pericardial complications were similar (6.1% vs 6.5%), while major bleeding was numerically higher in HFpEF (5.4% vs 4.6%). HF hospitalization was markedly higher (1.9% vs 0.4%; HR 4.53; p<0.001). At 1 year, HFpEF remained associated with higher mortality and stroke/TIA, while procedural complications continued to be similar across groups. Conclusion: In this large, matched cohort, HFpEF was associated with worse early and 1-year outcomes after LAAO despite comparable procedural safety. Excess risk appears driven by HFpEF physiology rather than device-specific complications, underscoring the need for optimized HF management in patients undergoing LAAO.
title: Abstract 10488: Beyond Procedural Safety: Early and One-Year Outcomes After LAAO in HFpEF from a Large Real-World Matched Cohort

abstract: Background: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a non-atherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome that often affects young, active women. Limited evidence exists regarding exercise stress testing performance and peak exercise cardiovascular responses in patients after SCAD. Purpose: The purpose was to characterize exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake, VO 2 peak) and peak exercise cardiovascular responses in patients following SCAD. Methods: For this retrospective study, we included 206 consecutive patients with SCAD from 2006-2025 who performed a cardiopulmonary exercise stress test after SCAD. Otherwise healthy controls (CTL) who performed cardiopulmonary exercise stress tests were matched 1:1 to patients with SCAD for age, body mass index (BMI), sex, and testing modality. Results: There were no differences in age (SCAD: 50±9 vs. CTL: 50±10 years), BMI (SCAD: 28±7 vs. CTL: 28±6 kg/m 2 ), and sex distribution (SCAD: 194W/12M vs. CTL: 194W/12M) between groups (all, p>0.90). SCAD patients had higher beta-blocker, ACEI/ARB, and calcium channel blocker use than controls (all, p<0.01). The exercise stress test was performed 2.0±3.0 years following the first SCAD occurrence. There were no statistical differences in VO 2 peak (SCAD: 23.9±6.7 vs. CTL: 23.5±7.4 mL/kg/min), % predicted VO 2 peak (SCAD: 96±21 (n=193) vs. CTL: 95±26% (n=193)), or peak MET level achieved (SCAD: 6.8±1.9 vs. CTL: 6.7±2.1 MET levels) between groups (all, p>0.46). At peak exercise, SCAD patients had lower systolic blood pressure (SCAD: 153±24 vs. CTL: 162±27 mmHg) and heart rate (SCAD: 148±21 vs. CTL: 157±24 beats/min) than controls (both, p<0.02). SCAD patients had a higher frequency of chronotropic incompetence than controls (SCAD: 27 vs. CTL: 18%, p=0.04). There were no differences between groups in respiratory exchange ratio (SCAD: 1.16±0.11 vs. CTL: 1.14±0.14) or diastolic blood pressure (SCAD: 67±11 vs. CTL: 71±14 mmHg) at peak exercise (both, p>0.32). Conclusion: Our novel findings demonstrate that ~2 years following SCAD, patients exhibit exercise capacity levels similar to healthy controls. Peak exercise systolic blood pressure and heart rates were lower among SCAD patients compared to controls, likely reflecting a medication effect. However, the peak diastolic blood pressure, which determines coronary perfusion, was similar between the SCAD and control groups.
title: Abstract 10529: Peak Exercise Responses in Patients Following Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

abstract: Introduction/Background: Hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR) combines minimally invasive surgical grafting of the left anterior descending artery with percutaneous coronary intervention of remaining vessels. Whether it offers outcomes comparable to conventional coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. Research Questions/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that HCR provides mortality, stroke, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular event (MACCE) rates comparable to CABG, with a possible difference in repeat revascularization. Methods/Approach: We pooled propensity-score adjusted (matched or weighted) observational studies comparing HCR with CABG. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models, and time-to-event outcomes were evaluated using hazard ratios (HR) directly extracted from the included studies. Heterogeneity was assessed by I 2 . Sensitivity (leave-one-out), subgroup (on-pump vs off-pump; multivessel vs left main), meta-regression (by SYNTAX score difference, for mortality), and funnel-plot analyses were performed. Results: Our meta-analysis included 29 propensity-score adjusted observational studies comprising 9,755 patients (HCR: 3,773; CABG: 5,368). Repeat revascularization (22 studies) was significantly higher with HCR (OR 1.75; 95% CI 1.40–2.18; P<0.001; I 2 =20.8%), robust on leave-one-out analysis. Stroke (14 studies) was lower with HCR (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.49–0.98; P=0.040; I 2 =0%), though sensitive to individual studies on leave-one-out analysis. Across 24 studies there were no significant differences in all-cause mortality (OR 0.81; 95% CI 0.62–1.05; P=0.115; I 2 =44.2%). MACCE (17 studies) was similar (OR 0.98; 95% CI 0.71–1.34; P=0.896; I 2 =53.6%). Conclusions remained consistent on time-to-event analysis (repeat revascularization HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.47–2.41; mortality HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.66–1.31). By anatomical complexity (multivessel vs left main), no significant subgroup interactions were seen for mortality (P=0.643), MACCE (P=0.176), or stroke (P=0.452). By surgical technique (on-pump vs off-pump), no differences were seen for mortality (P=0.855) or repeat revascularization (P=0.780), whereas a significant interaction was observed for MACCE (P=0.0026), driven by a single on-pump study. Meta-regression showed baseline SYNTAX score differences did not significantly modify mortality, and funnel plots showed no major asymmetry. Conclusions: Compared with CABG, HCR showed comparable all-cause mortality and MACCE, lower stroke odds, and higher odds of repeat revascularization. Drawn from propensity-score adjusted observational data, these results suggest HCR is a reasonable alternative in selected patients but carries a greater need for repeat revascularization.
title: Abstract 10545: Real-World Comparative Outcomes of Hybrid versus Conventional CABG: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Adjusted Studies with Subgroup and Meta-Regression Analyses of Effect Modifiers

abstract: Background: Severe native aortic stenosis (sAS) can be effectively treated with elective aortic valve replacement (AVR); however, some die awaiting intervention. We aimed to identify factors associated with early post-diagnosis mortality, defined as death within 90 days of the initial diagnosis (D90d), and to develop a risk prediction model to prioritize patients for earlier intervention. Methods: Consecutive outpatients (OP) with a first diagnosis of sAS between 2010-2020 at multiple clinical sites were included. Factors associated with D90d (univariate logistic regression) were used to construct a multivariate model (stepwise forward selection). Discrimination, calibration, split-sample, and bootstrap validation were assessed. Results: Among 8,243 OP (62% male, mean age 75.3±11.7 years), 384 (4.7%) died within 90 days; 83.4% of deaths occurred before AVR. Among classifiable OP deaths (98 of 384), 56 (57.1%) were cardiovascular. Clinical (age, BMI, dyspnea, syncope, history of heart failure, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, kidney disease), echocardiographic (aortic valve area, gradient, velocity; ejection fraction; E/e’; left atrial volume index; right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular size and function), and laboratory (hemoglobin, creatinine, NT-proBNP) parameters were associated with D90d (p<0.05 for all) at univariate analysis. A 6-factor multivariable model including Hb≤12.5 g/dl, NT-proBNP≥2000 pg/mL, ≥moderate right ventricular dysfunction, history of heart failure, very severe AS (area≤0.8 cm 2 , mean gradient≥50 mmHg, or velocity ≥5.0 m/s), and age≥82y had excellent discrimination (AUC 0.81, p<0.0001; Figure). Internal validation used a random 70/30 derivation-validation split of the complete-case OP cohort and showed stable discrimination, with AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.84) and 0.80 (95% CI 0.75-0.86), respectively. Each additional multivariate model factor more than doubled odds of D90d (OR 2.30, 95% CI 2.06-2.56; p<0.001); observed mortality increased from 1.9% with 0/1 factors to 18.2% with ≥5/6 factors (Figure). A total of 1116 (13.5%) OP had more than 3 risk factors at time of initial diagnosis, with a 90-day mortality >7%. A second multivariable model that included only current ACC/AHA guideline class I (symptoms, LVEF<50%) and II (elevated BNP, very severe AS, LVEF<60%) recommendations for AVR was less performant, with AUC of 0.74. Conclusions: A 6-factor risk model based on clinical (age, history of heart failure), laboratory (hemoglobin, NT-proBNP), and echocardiographic data (very severe AS, right ventricular dysfunction) can be used to estimate 90-day mortality risk at the time of initial diagnosis of sAS, and outperformed a model based on current ACC/AHA guideline recommendations for AVR. Patients with more than 3 risk factors have 90-day mortality >7% and should be triaged to earlier interventions.
title: Abstract 10571: The EARLY-AS Score: Early Assessment of Risk for Mortality After Diagnosis of Severe Aortic Stenosis

abstract: Background: Targeted NMR metabolomics provides a scalable snapshot of circulating biochemical state and has been applied to predict general health outcomes in population cohorts, but its clinical value for cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary risk prediction in real-world health-system populations remains uncertain. Methods: We generated an NMR metabolomics resource in 54,933 Kaiser Permanente Research Biobank participants linked to longitudinal electronic health records and evaluated prediction of incident cardiovascular, cardiopulmonary, and cardiometabolic diseases in a clinical setting. Across endpoint-specific Cox models, we tested whether addition of 250 NMR biomarkers improved incident disease prediction beyond age, sex, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, and disease-relevant clinical biomarkers. Results: NMR biomarkers improved prediction of incident cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary disease beyond standard clinical predictors, including coronary heart disease, heart failure/cardiomyopathy, transient ischemic attack/stroke, atrial fibrillation, and COPD. Predictive gains were strongest for cardiorenal-metabolic endpoints, including type 2 diabetes, metabolic liver disease, and chronic kidney disease, consistent with shared metabolic architecture across cardiovascular, pulmonary, kidney, and metabolic disease. When evaluated alongside inherited genetic risk, NMR metabolomics retained its predictive benefit, whereas polygenic risk scores offered minimal incremental discrimination once metabolomic and clinical predictors were included. Improvements were preserved across demographic, anthropometric, and genetic-risk subgroups. Among participants with prevalent CKD, a population at high cardiovascular risk, NMR models predicted TIA/stroke, acute myocardial infarction/acute coronary syndrome, and heart failure beyond a comprehensive clinical biochemistry panel. NMR-enhanced models were generally well calibrated at 1-, 3-, and 5-year horizons and improved decision-curve net benefit across most endpoints, supporting potential use for risk-based follow-up, confirmatory testing, and surveillance. Externally trained NMR risk models from the UK Biobank showed directional transportability to Kaiser Permanente, although within-health-system training yielded stronger performance. Conclusion: These findings support NMR metabolomics as a deployable platform for calibrated, clinically actionable prediction of cardiovascular, cardiopulmonary, and cardiorenal-metabolic risk in real-world healthcare cohorts.
title: Abstract 10575: Targeted Metabolomics Improves Prediction of Cardiovascular, Cardiopulmonary, and Cardiometabolic Disease Across Population and Health-System Biobanks

abstract: Background: The first year after myocardial infarction (MI) represents a critical period for secondary prevention, during which sex-related differences in cardiometabolic risk factor control may influence long-term outcomes. However, longitudinal sex-specific trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors during structures follow-up programs remain insufficiently characterized. Research Question: To investigate sex differences in cardiometabolic trajectories and clinical outcomes during the first year after MI among patients enrolled in a structured follow-up program. Methods: This prospective cohort included 200 consecutive patients enrolled in a structured post-MI care pathway between June 2023 and June 2025. Clinical assessments were conducted at 1, 6, and 12 months. Baseline characteristics, lipid profile, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), blood pressure control, medication adherence, cardiovascular events, and mortality were evaluated. Longitudinal trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models incorporating time, sex, and time-by-sex interaction terms. Results: Women accounted 33% of the cohort and were older than men at presentation (65.8±12.6 vs. 61.7±12.1 years; p=0.030). Women had a higher prevalence of type 2 diabetes (48.4% vs. 27.6%; p=0.006) and higher baseline HbA1c levels (6.2% vs. 5.5%; p=0.001), whereas active smoking was more common among men (30.6% vs. 18.1%; p=0.007). A significant time-by-sex interaction was observed for LDL-C trajectories (p=0.006). Men experienced a substantial and sustained reduction in LDL-C from 116.8 mg/dL at baseline to 76.4 mg/dL at 12 months, whereas women demonstrated a partial loss of lipid control following the initial response, with LDL-C increasing from 80.3 mg/dL at 1 month to 84.1 mg/dL at 12 months. HbA1c remained consistently higher among women throughout follow-up (sex effect p=0.004), without a significant time-by-sex interaction. MACE incidence was similar between sexes (p=0.754). However, women exhibited significantly higher all-cause mortality (7.5% vs. 1.4%; OR 5.40, 95% CI 1.02-28.6; p=0.040). Conclusions: Despite similar rates of recurrent ischemic events, women exhibited persistently worse metabolic profiles and less favorable long-term lipid trajectories following MI. Higher mortality among women appeared to be driven primarily by a greater burden of baseline comorbidities rather than by recurrent cardiovascular events, underscoring the need for sex-responsive secondary prevention strategies after MI.
title: Abstract 10593: Sex Differences in Lipid Trajectories and Clinical Outcomes During the First Year After Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Case Introduction: Coronary embolism/thrombosis is an uncommon MINOCA mechanism in women without atherosclerotic risk factors. Medroxyprogesterone acetate is used for abnormal uterine bleeding; thrombotic events are recognized, but coronary arterial thrombosis is rarely reported. We describe LAD STEMI shortly after medroxyprogesterone for fibroid bleeding. Case Presentation: A 49-year-old woman presented with chest pain and profound anemia, hemoglobin 4.2 g/dL, from heavy menstrual bleeding. Pelvic imaging showed uterine fibroids. After transfusion, oral medroxyprogesterone 10 mg daily was started. Three weeks later, she returned with recurrent anemia, dyspnea, and chest discomfort. ECG showed nonspecific T-wave inversions; she received transfusions and was discharged. Two days later, she re-presented with severe chest pain. ECG showed diffuse ST elevation with troponin >5262 pg/mL. Given diffuse ST elevation and ongoing bleeding, hemorrhagic pericarditis was suspected. Catheterization was deferred due to hemorrhagic concern, and she was treated with NSAIDs and admitted. Despite therapy, she developed monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Repeat ECG showed inferior/lateral ST elevation, prompting emergent angiography. Diagnostic Assessment and Intervention: Angiography showed complete LAD occlusion with thrombus involving diagonal and marginal branches, without fixed atherosclerotic narrowing. Mechanical thrombectomy and balloon angioplasty restored partial flow, TIMI II. Hypercoagulability testing was negative, CT favored a benign uterine mass, and no alternative embolic source was found. Given the temporal relationship, negative thrombophilia workup, and absence of atherosclerosis, medroxyprogesterone-associated coronary thrombosis was suspected. Medroxyprogesterone was discontinued. Discussion: This case highlights rare nonatherosclerotic STEMI after hormonal therapy for fibroid bleeding. Although venous thromboembolism is the better-recognized progestin complication, arterial coronary thrombosis should be considered when patients receiving medroxyprogesterone develop ACS without typical risk factors or fixed stenosis. It also underscores a dilemma: bleeding and concern for hemorrhagic pericarditis may delay invasive evaluation, yet delayed reperfusion can permit malignant arrhythmia and large-territory infarction. Early multidisciplinary coordination is essential when severe uterine bleeding and suspected coronary thrombosis coexist.
title: Abstract 10599: From Fibroid Bleeding to LAD STEMI: A Rare Suspected Arterial Thrombotic Complication of Medroxyprogesterone

abstract: Background: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is an established treatment for high-riskpatients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Whether the left ventricular (LV) functional response to acute MR correction differs by underlying etiology, and how it evolves over time, remains incompletely characterised. Early post-procedural left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is often used to gauge benefit, yet its load-dependence makes this potentially misleading. Hypothesis: Degenerative MR (DMR), functional MR (FMR), and mixed MR (MMR) exhibit divergent LVEF courses over the first year after M-TEER, reflecting distinct underlying pathophysiology. Methods: We analysed 124 consecutive patients undergoing M-TEER with the MitraClip system betweenFebruary 2015 and March 2023, prospectively enrolled in an institutional registry (NCT03674788). Patientswere stratified by MR etiology: DMR (n=46), FMR (n=58), and MMR (n=20). LVEF was measured at baseline, 30days, and 1 year by transthoracic echocardiography using the biplane Simpson method. The pre-specified primary endpoint was the change in LVEF (ΔLVEF) from baseline to 1 year, compared between etiologies by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Welch pairwise post-hoc testing. Echocardiographic completeness was 97% at 30 days and 79% at 1 year; the 30-day timepoint served as a sensitivity analysis for echo attrition. Results: Mean age was 76.3±9.8 years; 31.5% were female; Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk ofmortality (STS-PROM) was 6.7±5.7%. Procedural success (post-clip residual MR ≤2) was 95.2%. At 30 days, alletiologies showed modest LVEF decline without between-group separation (DMR –2.8%; FMR –0.6%; MMR–3.0%; ANOVA F=1.15, p=0.32). By 1 year, courses diverged: DMR exhibited persistent decline (55.8% to 51.9%;ΔLVEF –4.0%, p=0.026), FMR showed reverse remodelling (30.2% to 33.5%; ΔLVEF +3.3%, p=0.024), and MMR did not change significantly (ΔLVEF +1.8%, p=0.48). Between-group ΔLVEF at 1 year was significant (ANOVAF=5.59, p=0.005), driven by the DMR-FMR contrast (Welch p=0.002). MR was substantially reduced across all etiologies (median grade 4 to 2; Wilcoxon p<0.001). Of 26 patients without a 1-year echo, 16 had died before1 year, 5 died after 1 year without follow-up imaging, and 5 were alive without 1-year echo; 23 of the 26 had a30-day study, with ΔLVEF consistent with their etiology cohort. Conclusions: M-TEER produces etiology-specific LV remodelling that emerges over time: DMR shows immediate and persistent LVEF decline consistent with afterload mismatch after acute MR correction, whereas FMR exhibits delayed reverse remodelling unmasked only by 1 year, with MMR an intermediate phenotype.These temporal patterns support etiology-specific echocardiographic surveillance and caution against using early post-procedural LVEF to gauge longer-term remodelling.
title: Abstract 10619: Etiology-Specific Left Ventricular Functional Course After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: Insights from Serial Echocardiography at 30 Days and 1 Year

abstract: Introduction: Failure of mitral bioprostheses is increasingly common, and redo surgical mitral valve replacement (redo-SMVR) carries high procedural risk. Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an emerging alternative, but comparative data are limited, especially for medium- and longer-term outcomes. Methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies comparing TMVR and redo-SMVR in patients with failed mitral bioprostheses. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central and included propensity score-matched observational studies and randomized controlled trials. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, stroke, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Effect estimates were pooled using the generic inverse variance method with a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed by I 2 . Statistical analyses were performed using R software, version 4.4.1. Results: A total of 11,518 patients from seven propensity score-matched observational studies and one randomized controlled trial were included, comprising 4,828 patients undergoing TMVR and 6,690 undergoing redo-SMVR. Mean age ranged from 58 to 77 years, and 58.6% of patients were female. Compared with redo-SMVR, TMVR was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR 0.50; 95% CI 0.33-0.76; p = 0.001; I 2 = 44.8%; Figure 1A), stroke (OR 0.57; 95% CI 0.42-0.78; p < 0.001; I 2 = 0%; Figure 1B), and AKI (OR 0.34; 95% CI 0.21-0.56; p < 0.001; I 2 = 83.5%). No difference was observed between groups in 30-day mortality (OR 0.77; 95% CI 0.34-1.75; p = 0.54; I 2 = 53.7%) or 2-year mortality (OR 0.95; 95% CI 0.73-1.24; p = 0.72; I 2 = 0%). Conclusions: In patients with failed mitral bioprostheses, TMVR was associated with lower in-hospital mortality, stroke, and AKI compared with redo-SMVR, while short- and medium-term mortality were similar. These findings support consideration of TMVR for selected high-risk patients, with further study needed on long-term durability and patient selection.
title: Abstract 10629: Transcatheter versus Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement After Bioprosthetic Failure

abstract: Background: The Glyco-Inflammatory Healing Index (GIHI), calculated as HbA1c х C-reactive protein/albumin, integrates glycemic control, systemic inflammation, and nutritional status. Its prognostic value after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains unclear, particularly according to diabetes status. Methods: We conducted a retrospective international multicenter cohort study of 6,262 adults undergoing isolated CABG between 2010 and 2025. Patients were stratified by diabetes status. GIHI was analyzed as a standardized continuous variable and descriptively categorized as high or low based on subgroup medians. The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, or repeat revascularization. The secondary outcome included long-term all-cause mortality. Associations were assessed using Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic curves. Results: Among 6,262 patients, 2,783 (44.5%) had diabetes. In diabetic patients, higher GIHI was independently associated with 30-day MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-1.65), 30-day myocardial infarction (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.00-1.60), 30-day mortality (HR 2.56, 95% CI 2.06-3.18), and long-term mortality (HR 2.57, 95% CI 2.33-2.83). In non-diabetic patients, GIHI was not associated with 30-day MACE but remained associated with 30-day mortality and long-term mortality. Adding GIHI improved discrimination for 30-day MACE in diabetic patients (AUC 0.65 to 0.69; p<0.001). Conclusions: GIHI independently predicts adverse postoperative outcomes after isolated CABG, with the strongest prognostic relevance in patients with diabetes.
title: Abstract 10632: A Novel Glyco-Inflammatory Healing Index for Risk Prediction After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study in Patients with Diabetes

abstract: Introduction: Delayed treatment escalation during weekends have been reported across acute cardiovascular conditions with variable impact on outcomes. This may be especially relevant for pulmonary embolism (PE), where multidisciplinary coordination and escalation to catheter-directed therapies (CDT) may be required. Whether weekend presentation is associated with worse outcomes among patients with acute PE referred for CDT remains uncertain. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was performed within Truveta, a multi-health system electronic health record (EHR) dataset (2018-2024), including patients receiving CDT for acute PE. Weekend status was defined by day/time of presentation (Friday 5PM - Monday 7AM and holidays). The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Secondary endpoints included in-hospital cardiac arrest, mechanical ventilation (MV), vasopressor use, mechanical circulatory support (MCS), rescue surgical embolectomy, composite bail-out therapy (composite of vasopressor use, need for MCS, MV, surgical embolectomy), International Society of Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major bleeding, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS). Multivariable logistic regression was used for binary outcomes and log-linear models for ICU LOS. Results: The cohort included 15,167 patients (weekday n=10,180; weekend n=4,987). The mean age of the total cohort was 62 years, and included 47% females. In-hospital mortality occurred in 417/10,180 (4.10%) weekday vs 236/4,987 (4.73%) weekend patients; weekend presentation was associated with higher adjusted odds of mortality (aOR 1.22, 95% CI 1.02-1.45; p=0.026). Weekend presentation was also associated with higher odds of decompensation: mechanical ventilation (0.65% vs 1.26%; aOR 1.98, 95% CI 1.37-2.86; p<0.001), MCS (0.07% vs 0.24%; aOR 3.58, 95% CI 1.25-11.1; p=0.019), vasopressor use (0.22% vs 0.70%; aOR 3.41, 95% CI 1.95-6.09; p<0.001), and composite bail-out therapy (0.91% vs 1.77%; aOR 1.94, 95% CI 1.42-2.66; p<0.001). Major bleeding did not differ by weekend status (aOR 1.01). Among ICU-admitted patients, mean ICU LOS was 3.26 days (weekday, n=1,760) vs 3.70 days (weekend, n=848), with longer adjusted ICU LOS on weekends (ratio 1.158, 95% CI 1.068-1.255; p<0.001). Conclusion: In a multi-health system EHR cohort of patients receiving advanced catheter-directed PE therapy, weekend presentation was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality and substantially greater need for rescue-level support, without increased major bleeding. These findings suggest weekend vulnerability in treated PE may manifest through acute physiologic decompensation and ICU resource utilization, supporting efforts to optimize PE care pathways.
title: Abstract 10641: Weekend versus Weekday Presentation and Outcomes Following Catheter-Directed Therapy for Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A National Electronic Health Record Analysis

abstract: Background: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) remains a common complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Existing risk stratification tools rely primarily on preoperative variables and may not adequately capture perioperative physiological stress. Objectives: To evaluate the association of a novel perioperative Cardiac Stress Score (CSS) with 30-day POAF and long-term all-cause mortality, and to assess its incremental predictive value beyond postoperative troponin. Methods: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 6,137 patients undergoing isolated CABG across four centers in Israel and the West Bank. The CSS is a simple integer-based score (range 0-6) derived from postoperative troponin, aortic cross-clamp time, and serum creatinine. Associations with outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with stepwise adjustment. Discriminative performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Kaplan-Meier curves were used for time-to-event analyses. Results: POAF occurred in 20.3% of patients. Each 1-point increase in CSS was independently associated with a higher risk of POAF (adjusted HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.33-1.42; p < 0.001) and long-term mortality (adjusted HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.47-1.62; p < 0.001). A clear graded relationship was observed, with POAF incidence increasing from approximately 10% at a score of 0 to over 50% in higher score categories. The CSS demonstrated superior discrimination for POAF compared with postoperative troponin alone (AUC 0.70 vs. 0.67; p = 0.0008). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed stepwise increases in POAF incidence and reduced long-term survival across CSS tertiles (log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusion: The Cardiac Stress Score is a simple and clinically applicable tool that integrates perioperative myocardial injury, ischemic burden, and renal dysfunction. It independently predicts POAF and long-term mortality after CABG and provides incremental prognostic value beyond postoperative troponin. Further external validation is warranted.
title: Abstract 10652: A Novel Perioperative Cardiac Stress Score for Predicting Atrial Fibrillation and Mortality After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting

abstract: Background: Optimal antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains debated, particularly regarding the benefit of aspirin in addition to a P2Y12 inhibitor. This study compared 90-day clinical outcomes of aspirin plus clopidogrel (dual antiplatelet therapy, DAPT) versus clopidogrel monotherapy in real-world patients undergoing PCI. Methods: This multicenter retrospective cohort study utilized the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients who underwent PCI and initiated antiplatelet therapy within 14 days were included. Two cohorts were defined: aspirin plus clopidogrel and clopidogrel only. Propensity score matching (1:1 greedy nearest-neighbor) balanced demographics, comorbidities, medications, and laboratory values, yielding 9,229 well-balanced patients per cohort. The index event was the PCI procedure with qualifying antiplatelet initiation. Time-to-event outcomes were assessed from day 1 to 90 days post-index using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results: After propensity score matching, cohorts were well-balanced. At 90 days, all-cause mortality was significantly lower with aspirin plus clopidogrel compared to clopidogrel monotherapy (427 vs 518 events; KM survival 95.07% vs 93.90%; HR 1.245 for monotherapy, 95% CI 1.095-1.415, log-rank p=0.001). Aspirin plus clopidogrel was associated with higher all-cause hospitalization (4,567 vs 4,159 events; KM survival 49.90% vs 54.02%; HR 0.890 favoring monotherapy, 95% CI 0.853-0.928, p<0.001), and higher MACE (4,965 vs 4,501 events; KM survival 43.78% vs 48.01%; HR 0.866 favoring monotherapy, 95% CI 0.832-0.902, p<0.001). Stroke risk was lower with aspirin plus clopidogrel (856 vs 953 events; HR 1.146 for monotherapy, 95% CI 1.045-1.257, p=0.004). Ventricular fibrillation was also lower with DAPT (148 vs 108 events; HR 0.741 favoring DAPT, 95% CI 0.579-0.950, p=0.018). No significant differences were observed for any bleeding (50 vs 64 events; HR 1.315, p=0.146), atrial fibrillation, stent thrombosis, or cardiac arrest. Conclusion: In this large propensity score-matched real-world analysis, aspirin plus clopidogrel (DAPT) was associated with significantly lower 90-day all-cause mortality and stroke compared to clopidogrel monotherapy. However, DAPT increased risks of hospitalization, and MACE. These findings suggest a mortality benefit with short-term DAPT at the expense of higher hospitalization events in this cohort. Individualized antiplatelet strategies balancing ischemic and bleeding risks are warranted. Randomized trials are needed to further define optimal regimens in contemporary PCI populations.
title: Abstract 10674: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy with Aspirin Plus Clopidogrel versus Clopidogrel Monotherapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis of 90-Day Outcomes

abstract: Background: Hemorrhagic myocardial infarction (hMI) affects ~40% of ST-elevation MIs and predicts adverse remodeling, mortality, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events. We showed that early post-reperfusion cardiac troponin-I (cTnI) kinetics distinguish hMI from nonhemorrhagic MI (non-hMI), independent of area at risk, pre-PCI TIMI flow, or infarct size. However, mechanism of cTnI surge after hemorrhagic MI is unknown. We hypothesized that intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) increases cTnI release via calcium-dependent sarcomeric proteolysis and extracellular cTnI propagates injury. Methods: Ischemia-reperfusion was induced by left anterior descending coronary occlusion in canines and Sprague-Dawley rats, followed by reperfusion. IMH was verified by cTnI kinetics and cardiac MRI in canines and by histopathology in both species. TEM, immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, RT-PCR, and RNA sequencing were employed to elucidate molecular mechanisms. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) were subjected to 90 minutes of ischemia followed by reperfusion, with or without hemin treatment. Beating cardiomyocytes received recombinant cTnI (500 pg/mL) or vehicle (n=5/group). Results: Despite matched infarct size, IMH increased circulating cTnI vs non-hMI in canines (p<0.01), consistent with patient findings and reproduced in rats. TEM in IMH heart showed sarcomeric disassembly, mitochondrial injury, and more intracellular vesicles. ER/protein-transport blockade reduced cTnI release by 23% (p<0.01) without viability loss, supporting vesicular export. In vitro, hemin disrupted sarcomeres and accelerated intracellular cTnI depletion with extracellular release at 3, 6 and 24 h. RNA-seq showed Ca2+-dependent proteolytic pathway activation, with increased CAPN5 (1.7-fold, p<0.05), CAPN15 (1.4-fold, p<0.05), MMP10 (9.2-fold, p<0.001) and MMP17 (4-fold; all p<0.05), SERCA2a downregulation (20-30%; p<0.05), and increased CAMLG/NFATC3 signaling (1.4/1.39-fold, p<0.05). Findings suggest heme-mediated Ca2+ dysregulation and activation of Ca 2 + -dependent sarcomeric proteolysis, promoting cTnI release. Recombinant cTnI altered 1,091 genes (486 upregulated, 605 downregulated), inducing ectopic sodium channels SCN10A (FC=8.96, p<0.01) and SCN7A (FC=3.33, p<0.01), suppressing SCN4A, KCNQ4, CACNB1, and ATP2A3 (p<0.05), and activating proarrhythmic calcium-signaling genes PLCB3/ADCY3 with DNA-damage/innate-immune signatures. Conclusion: IMH amplifies cTnI release via heme-driven SERCA2a impairment, Ca2+ dysregulation, calpain/MMP activation, and sarcomeric proteolysis. Extracellular cTnI injures cardiomyocytes via Ca2+ overload, electrical instability, DNA damage, and innate immunity, supporting cTnI/Ca2+ signaling axis as hMI targets. *The first two authors contributed equally.
title: Abstract 10678: Mechanism of Post-Reperfusion Cardiac Troponin I Surge in Hemorrhagic Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Ambulatory cardiac monitoring (ACM) guidelines are symptom-driven, and the 2023 AHA Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) Advisory establishes that CKM risk factors amplify arrhythmogenic substrate. Most published machine learning (ML) models for incident arrhythmia treat major arrhythmia (MA) as a single outcome. Whether risk profiles differ across arrhythmia classes and which features predict rapid versus delayed diagnosis has not been characterized. Methods: Using Symphony Integrated Dataverse open claims (Jan 2018-Dec 2025), we identified adults with a guideline-qualifying symptom and a CKM risk factor, no prevalent MA in 12-month lookback. We developed class-specific ML models to characterize distinct predictive profiles and multinomial regression to identify baseline features associated with shorter time to MA diagnosis. Four class-specific XGBoost classifiers were trained for AF/AFL, VT/VF/VFlutter, SVT/re-entry, and AV block/conduction versus no arrhythmia (N=7.4M comparators). Multinomial regression among MA patients modeled: time-to-diagnosis near-term (<90 days), intermediate (90–179 days), and delayed (≥180 days) using baseline features. All classifier models used isotonic recalibration. SHAP identified top predictors per class. Combination profiling identified prevalent co-occurring risk factors within each time interval. Results: Class-specific models achieved AUROC 0.85 (AF/AFL, N=1,031,366), 0.87 (VT, N=84,949), 0.87 (SVT, N=221,228), and 0.87 (AV block, N=188,289), all well-calibrated (O:E ~1.0; Table 1). SHAP revealed shared top predictors (time since first symptom <12 months, non-major arrhythmia, new symptoms, breathing disorder) but class-specific differentiation: age ≥65 for AF, <55 for AV block, <65 for VT and SVT. Multinomial regression for near-term diagnosis (<90 versus ≥180 days) identified cardiogenic shock (relative risk ratio [RRR] 4.21-5.84), palpitations (RRR 1.70-3.77), and myocardial infarction (RRR 1.42-1.80) as consistent predictors of near-term diagnosis (Figure 1). Bradycardia preferentially predicted early AV block (RRR 2.78) and SVT (RRR 1.99) versus AF/AFL (RRR 1.19). Chronic conditions (COPD, CKD, obesity, hypertension) were associated with delayed diagnosis. Combination profiling showed class-specific patterns: hypertension plus palpitations dominated early SVT, syncope combinations dominated early AV block, while breathing disorder plus hyperlipidemia was the top combination across all intervals for AF/AFL and VT (Table 2). Conclusions: Class-specific ML models achieved strong discrimination with good calibration across four MA types. Baseline risk profiles differentially predicted arrhythmia class and near-term diagnosis. Findings support class-stratified ambulatory monitoring strategies and motivate prospective validation of risk-tiered pathways.
title: Abstract 10689: Arrhythmia-Class-Specific Machine Learning Models to Identify Distinct Risk Profiles and Predictors of Near-Term Diagnosis Among Symptomatic Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Burden

abstract: Background: Myocardial infarction (MI) with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is increasingly recognized as a distinct clinical entity and disproportionately affects women. However, real-world data comparing in-hospital outcomes of MINOCA with PCI-treated myocardial infarction, particularly by sex, remain limited. We sought to address this gap using a large, nationally representative dataset. Methods: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2023), including adults hospitalized with STEMI or NSTEMI. Hospitalizations with COVID-19 were excluded. Patients were classified as MINOCA or PCI-treated MI using validated ICD-10-CM and PCS criteria. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, acute kidney injury, and mechanical ventilation. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression was used to adjust for demographics and comorbidities. Results: A total of 1,749,095 weighted hospitalizations were included, of which 34,505 were MINOCA cases. Women made up 78.8% of the MINOCA group compared with 31.9% in the PCI group. MINOCA patients were also younger (mean age 59.7 vs 64.8 years) and had lower comorbidity burden (Charlson Comorbidity Index 2.26 vs 2.77) compared with PCI-treated MI. Additional differences stratified by sex and MI type are described in Table 1. Overall, MINOCA was associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with PCI-treated MI (aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.62-0.85; p<0.001). However, there was strong sex-based heterogeneity. Among women, MINOCA was associated with significantly lower mortality (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.48-0.71; p<0.001) and fewer complications, including cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, and mechanical ventilation. In contrast, among men, MINOCA was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.07-1.89; p=0.014) and increased risk of acute kidney injury (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.22-1.65; p<0.001) compared with PCI-treated MI. Conclusions: MINOCA is associated with markedly different outcomes compared with PCI-treated myocardial infarction, with a striking sex-based divergence. Women with MINOCA have better in-hospital outcomes while men face higher mortality despite lower comorbidity burden. These findings underscore the need for sex-specific risk stratification in MINOCA management.
title: Abstract 10698: The MINOCA Paradox: Sex-Specific In-Hospital Outcomes Compared with PCI-Treated Myocardial Infarction- A National Inpatient Sample Analysis

abstract: Introduction: The use of dual mechanical circulatory support (MCS)—venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) and Impella (ECpella)—for left ventricular unloading has increased, yet its incremental benefit over single-device strategies remains uncertain. We compared in-hospital outcomes among ECpella, VA-ECMO without Impella, and Impella without VA-ECMO in cardiogenic shock. Research Question: In adults with cardiogenic shock requiring MCS, is dual support with concurrent VA-ECMO and Impella (ECpella) associated with different in-hospital mortality and complication rates than VA-ECMO without Impella or Impella without VA-ECMO? Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), we identified adult cardiogenic shock admissions receiving MCS, classified as Impella without VA-ECMO, VA-ECMO without Impella, or ECpella. Concurrent intra-aortic balloon pump use was not exclusionary. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were used, adjusted for demographics, etiology, severity markers, comorbidities, hospital characteristics, and year, with VA-ECMO without Impella as the reference group. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results: Among 12,620 cardiogenic shock admissions receiving MCS (~63,100 weighted), 10,029 (79.5%) received Impella without VA-ECMO, 1,936 (15.3%) VA-ECMO without Impella, and 655 (5.2%) ECpella (Table 1). ECpella was not identified in 2016-2017 and increased to 8.3% of MCS admissions by 2022 (p<0.001). After adjustment, ECpella was not associated with a significant difference in mortality versus VA-ECMO without Impella (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.87-1.29, p=0.58), which was confirmed in the propensity-matched cohort (45.9% vs 45.6%, p=0.92). Impella without VA-ECMO was associated with lower mortality than VA-ECMO without Impella (aOR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67-0.86, p<0.001). Compared with VA-ECMO without Impella, ECpella was associated with higher odds of vascular complications (aOR 1.34, p=0.031), limb ischemia (aOR 1.55, p=0.042), and cardiac arrest (aOR 1.40, p=0.003), and higher mean hospital charges ($944,713 vs. $886,519). Conclusions: In this national cohort, ECpella use increased over time but was not associated with a mortality benefit over VA-ECMO without Impella, while carrying higher rates of vascular and limb complications and higher hospital charges. These findings underscore the need for prospective data to define which patients benefit from dual MCS. Residual confounding from unmeasured hemodynamic severity cannot be excluded.
title: Abstract 10708: Outcomes of Dual Mechanical Circulatory Support (VA-ECMO + Impella, “ECpella”) versus Single-Device Strategies in Cardiogenic Shock: A National Analysis

abstract: Background: There are no approved medical therapies for calcific aortic stenosis (AS). In a post hoc analysis of the FOURIER trial, evolocumab showed a statistically nonsignificant reduction in AS events (HR 0.66, 0.40-1.09) that became significant after the first year (HR 0.48, 0.25-0.93). Risk of AS events tracked with elevated lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) rather than Lp(a)-corrected LDL-C. Hypothesis: PCSK9-targeted therapy is associated with a lower incidence of aortic valve intervention in patients diagnosed with nonrheumatic AS. Methods: In the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, adults with nonrheumatic AS (ICD-10 I35.0, 2016-2025) who received PCSK9-targeted therapy (evolocumab, alirocumab, or inclisiran) after the AS diagnosis were compared with patients receiving statin and with patients receiving ezetimibe. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity-matched on demographics, cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, the other lipid-lowering agent (ezetimibe in the statin cohort, statin in the ezetimibe cohort), the elevated Lp(a) diagnosis, and the Lp(a) lab test. The primary event was aortic valve replacement: transcatheter (TAVR) or surgical (SAVR). Three windows were prespecified: 3 years (primary), and, as sensitivity analyses, the first 90 days and a 90-day to 3-year landmark. Results: After matching, 10,352 pairs (statin cohort) and 4,525 pairs (ezetimibe cohort) were included. Baseline characteristics were well balanced (all standardized mean differences <0.05). Over 3 years, PCSK9-targeted therapy was associated with fewer aortic valve interventions than both comparators (vs statin HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.90; vs ezetimibe HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.97). This difference was limited to the first 90 days (vs statin HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.44-0.61; vs ezetimibe HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46-0.74) and was absent in the 90-day to 3-year landmark (vs statin HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.96-1.24; vs ezetimibe HR 1.13, 95% CI 0.91-1.40). Proportional hazards were violated over the full window in both comparisons (p<0.001). Conclusions: While PCSK9-targeted therapy was associated with a lower incidence of long-term aortic valve intervention, the apparent benefit came from the first 90 days and disappeared once early events were excluded. Accounting for the Lp(a) diagnosis and lab test did not alter these findings. The apparent benefit is thus more consistent with residual confounding than with a therapeutic effect. Selection bias cannot be excluded: patients usually already have moderate AS at the ICD-10 diagnosis that defines entry, so the cohort likely reflects the later disease spectrum. The FOURIER post hoc analysis also counted new AS diagnosis as an event, which might contribute to a positive finding and be more reflective of a real-world setting. A randomized trial with adequate follow-up is needed to determine whether PCSK9 inhibition affects long-term aortic valve intervention and disease progression.
title: Abstract 10722: PCSK9-Targeted Therapy and Long-Term Aortic Valve Intervention in Nonrheumatic Aortic Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Oxidative stress, inflammation, and platelet activation are interconnected processes contributing to endothelial dysfunction and myocardial injury in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). These pathways may mutually amplify each other through redox-sensitive inflammatory signaling and platelet-mediated vascular responses. Circulating biomarkers reflecting these processes may provide complementary insight into biological response to AMI and identify patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that biomarkers reflecting oxidative stress, tissue/inflammatory stress, and platelet activation are associated with adverse clinical outcomes after AMI. Methods: The analysis was conducted in a well-defined population of 476 AMI patients treated with primary PCI in a multicenter randomized trial comparing prasugrel and ticagrelor. Blood samples were obtained 24±6 h after the procedure. Selected biomarkers of oxidative stress (thioredoxin-1 [TRX-1], 8-isoprostane, superoxide dismutase-3, NADPH oxidase-2), tissue/inflammatory stress (soluble ST2 [sST2], interleukin-33 [IL-33], α-klotho, growth differentiation factor-15 [GDF-15]), and platelet activation (thromboxane B 2 , soluble P-selectin) were assessed. The study endpoints were a triple composite of cardiovascular (CV) death, MI, or stroke at 30 days and 1 year, and CV mortality at 30 days and 1 year. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for associations between biomarkers and time-to-event outcomes. Correlations among biomarkers were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Results: TRX-1, IL-33, GDF-15, and soluble P-selectin were significantly associated with the composite endpoint at both 30 days and 1 year. The strongest time-specific effects were observed for GDF-15 at 30 days (HR 1.83, p=0.004) and IL-33 at 1 year (HR 1.27, p<0.001). Among these markers, TRX-1, IL-33, and GDF-15 were related to increased CV mortality at 30 days (HR 1.006, 1.36, and 1.95, respectively; all p≤0.013) and 1 year (HR 1.005, 1.49, and 2.04; all p≤0.012). The tissue stress biomarker sST2 was significantly related to increased risk of 1-year CV mortality (HR 1.04, p=0.043) (Figure). Among all markers, only TRX-1 correlated with soluble P-selectin (Spearman r=0.59, p<0.001). Conclusions: Biomarkers of oxidative stress, tissue/inflammatory stress, and platelet activation were associated with adverse outcomes after AMI. The findings suggest that circulating biomarkers may reflect distinct biological processess following AMI and support multimarker approaches for risk assessment.
title: Abstract 10745: Oxidative Stress, Tissue Stress, and Platelet Activation Biomarkers in Relation to Outcomes After Acute Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries an in-hospital mortality of 30-40%. Acute myocardial infarction is the leading cause, and nearly 50% of related deaths occur out-of-hospital. Unlike trauma care, no nationally accepted criteria define a cardiogenic shock center, though recent consensus statements have proposed multi-tier systems. In line with these statements, we defined 'Level-1' centers as hospitals providing definitive therapies: heart transplantation and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The proportion of the U.S. population beyond reach of such centers, and whether cardiac mortality clusters in low-access areas, has not been quantified.
