The nearly two-fold higher mortality, without a corresponding rise in valve failure, indicates that these patients often die before degeneration can manifest; this finding likely reflects the competing risk of death rather than equivalent valve durability. Consistent with this, the renal effect on durability was evident at pre-dialysis (stage 4) disease but eclipsed by mortality in ESRD. Procedural and technical factors not captured here may play a larger role in early failure, and ESRD alone may not warrant withholding TAVR on early durability grounds.
title: Abstract 11399: Pre-existing End-Stage Renal Disease and Early Valve Failure After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement

abstract: Introduction: Polycythemia Vera (PV) is a JAK2-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasm in which thrombosis is the leading cause of morbidity. Acute coronary syndrome as the initial manifestation is rare, and prior reports of multi-vessel involvement describe sequential or occlusive disease treated percutaneously. To our knowledge, this is among the few reported cases of PV presenting as simultaneous multi-vessel coronary thrombosis causing ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) in the absence of atherosclerosis, managed successfully with pharmacologic therapy alone. Patient Information & Clinical Findings: A 69-year-old male with no cardiac history presented with severe non-radiating, pressure-like chest pain. Vital signs and cardiopulmonary examination were unremarkable. He reported a recently cancelled sugrery due to abnormal blood counts and a pending hematology evaluation. Diagnostic Assessment: Laboratory evaluation revealed tri-lineage elevation: leukocytosis, erythrocytosis (hemoglobin 18.5 g/dL, hematocrit 54.8%), and thrombocytosis. High-sensitivity troponin was markedly elevated at 3,222 ng/L with diffuse ST-segment elevations (II, III, aVF, V4-V6). CT angiography excluded dissection and pulmonary embolism but showed splenomegaly. Coronary angiography revealed multiple simultaneous intraluminal thrombi in the mid-right coronary artery (TIMI II) and proximal-to-mid left anterior descending artery (TIMI III) without atherosclerotic stenosis, consistent with a systemic hypercoagulable mechanism. Therapeutic Intervention: Given the high thrombus burden, hyperviscosity, and no-reflow risk, mechanical intervention was deferred in favor of intravenous heparin and the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor eptifibatide. Transesophageal echocardiography excluded a cardioembolic source; repeat angiography confirmed markedly reduced thrombus burden with restored TIMI III flow; no stents were placed. He was transitioned to time-limited triple antithrombotic therapy with aspirin, clopidogrel, and apixaban. Follow-up & Outcomes: JAK2 V617F testing confirmed PV. Therapeutic phlebotomy and low-dose aspirin were initiated, and the patient remained free of recurrent ischemic events. Discussion: This case illustrates a rare, high-risk PV phenotype in which hyperviscosity and platelet activation drove multi-vessel coronary thrombosis and STEMI without atherosclerosis. The thrombus burden resolved with platelet inhibition and anticoagulation alone, avoiding the distal embolization and no-reflow risk of mechanical intervention while bridging to hematologic optimization. Tri-lineage cytosis with severe or multi-vessel thrombosis should prompt immediate JAK2 testing and hematology involvement. In selected patients without fixed stenosis, conservative antithrombotic therapy may be preferable to revascularization.
title: Abstract 11405: Holding the Stent: Initial Presentation of Polycythemia Vera as Acute Myocardial Infarction with Multi-Vessel Coronary Thrombosis

abstract: Background: Contemporary data on the early trajectory of cardiogenic shock (CS) remain limited, particularly during the first 24 hours of hospitalization and across presenting diagnoses. Methods: Using comprehensive electronic health record data, we identified all adults hospitalized within Kaiser Permanente Northern California between 2014 and 2024 with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or worsening heart failure (WHF). Demographic and clinical characteristics were ascertained using validated algorithms, and Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI) shock stages (A-E) were assigned per consensus definitions based on hemodynamic, laboratory, and treatment parameters. We characterized the (1) epidemiology of CS, (2) baseline clinical profiles, and (3) progression of SCAI stages within the first 24 hours, overall and stratified by admitting diagnosis. Results: We identified 98,642 eligible hospitalizations (AMI: n=29,250; WHF: n=69,392). Cohort members had mean age of 74.2±13.7 years, 45.0% were women, with 13.9% Asian American/Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, 9.0% Black, and 13.3% Hispanic. Patients with WHF were older and more often female compared with those presenting with AMI. At presentation, SCAI stage distribution was: Stage A: 86.1%, Stage B: 4.2%, Stage C: 7.0%, Stage D: 1.7%, and Stage E: 0.9%. The incidence of CS presentation (SCAI C-E) was higher in WHF vs AMI: 11.3% vs 5.6%. Within the first 24 hours, 49.3% of patients experienced progression in SCAI stage, with the highest transition rates observed from Stage A→C (34.7%) and A→D (4.9%). SCAI stage progression was more frequent in those presenting with WHF vs AMI: 54.0% vs 38.1%. Median (IQR) time to first progression was 19.0 (9.0-22.0) hours, and early deterioration (≤24h) was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.65). Conclusions: In a large, contemporary, and diverse cohort of adults hospitalized for AMI or WHF, CS was common, and nearly half of patients progressed in SCAI stage within the first 24 hours. These findings highlight the dynamic nature of early CS and underscore the need for real-time risk stratification to identify patients at greatest risk of early deterioration.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective electronic health record cohort, Kaiser Permanente Northern California 2014 to 2024, 98,642 eligible hospitalizations (AMI: n=29,250; WHF: n=69,392).
appraisal.main_limitation: Stages are assigned algorithmically from routine data, so misclassification is likely, and the abstract reports no treatment-effect analysis.
appraisal.one_line: Large integrated-system cohort describing early SCAI shock stage progression in hospitalised AMI and worsening heart failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of CS presentation (SCAI C-E) was higher in WHF vs AMI: 11.3% vs 5.6%. Within the first 24 hours, 49.3% of patients experienced progression in SCAI stage; early deterioration (≤24h) was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.65).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that shock is dynamic in the first day and quantifies the window for escalation, informing shock-team triggers and trial enrichment.

title: Abstract 11445: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, and Early Trajectory of Cardiogenic Shock in a Large Integrated Healthcare Delivery System

abstract: Background: Patients with liver disease are routinely excluded from acute myocardial infarction (AMI) trials, and real-world studies rely on administrative coding alone. Whether coded liver disease and laboratory-defined liver fibrosis identify the same patients, and carry the same risk, is unknown. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that ICD-coded liver disease and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4)-defined fibrosis identify overlapping but distinct AMI populations, and that many patients without coded liver disease harbor occult advanced fibrosis with excess risk. Methods: Single-center retrospective cohort of 1,037 consecutive adults admitted with AMI (ICD-10 I21.x) to a tertiary New York center (January 2021 to December 2024). The primary exposure was ICD-defined advanced liver disease (cirrhosis, hepatic failure, or portal hypertension; n=102). The secondary exposure was admission FIB-4 (from age, AST, ALT, and platelets; computable in 99.4%), tiered as low (less than 1.45), indeterminate (1.45 to 3.25), or advanced (greater than 3.25). Co-primary outcomes were invasive management (angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention, or bypass surgery) and in-hospital mortality, modeled by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, and ST-elevation; FIB-4 trend was tested by Cochran-Armitage. Results: Patients with coded advanced liver disease received invasive management less often (12.7% vs 50.4%; adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.32) and died in hospital more often (43.1% vs 7.9%; adjusted odds ratio 8.22, 95% CI 5.02 to 13.46) than patients without coded liver disease. Outcomes worsened monotonically across FIB-4 tiers (mortality 4.4%, 9.2%, 27.5%; invasive management 55.2%, 45.6%, 33.5%; both P less than 0.001 for trend). Of 909 patients without any coded liver disease, 168 (18.5%) had FIB-4 greater than 3.25, indicating substantial occult advanced fibrosis missed by coding. Conclusions: Coded liver disease identifies a small, severely affected subgroup with markedly under-used invasive management and 6- to 8-fold higher mortality after AMI. Routine FIB-4, a free three-variable laboratory score, identifies a much larger population with occult advanced fibrosis and graded excess risk that administrative codes miss. FIB-4 warrants consideration as a routine bedside risk-stratification tool in AMI care.
title: Abstract 11447: Administrative Coding versus a Laboratory-Based Fibrosis Score for Identifying Liver Disease in Acute Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Nonrheumatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has emerged as a less invasive alternative to surgical repair (SR), yet comparative real-world data remain limited. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2017-2022. Adults with nonrheumatic TR who underwent TEER or isolated SR were included. Patients undergoing concomitant valve or coronary procedures were excluded. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality, LOS, and inflation-adjusted hospitalization costs. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury (AKI), stroke, cardiogenic shock, and mechanical ventilation. Categorical variables were compared using Rao-Scott adjusted chi-square tests and continuous variables using design-based Kruskal-Wallis tests. IPTW based on logistic regression-derived propensity scores was performed to account for non-random treatment allocation. Covariates included age, sex, race, income, hospital region, bed size, and Charlson comorbidity index. Survey-weighted IPTW-adjusted models estimated aORs and β coefficients (95% CIs). Results: A total of 3,710 weighted hospitalizations were included, with 2,320 (62.5%) undergoing SR and 1,390 (37.5%) undergoing TEER. TEER patients were older (77 ± 10 vs 60 ± 18 years) and had greater comorbidity burden, including higher Charlson comorbidity index scores (3.57 vs 2.10), congestive heart failure (93% vs 61%), chronic kidney disease (56% vs 24%), and atrial fibrillation (82% vs 55%) (all p<0.001). After IPTW-adjusted multivariable analysis, TEER was associated with significantly lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.12; 95% CI 0.04-0.37), stroke (aOR 0.43; 95% CI 0.19-0.98), AKI (aOR 0.27; 95% CI 0.15-0.48), cardiogenic shock (aOR 0.33; 95% CI 0.14-0.75), and mechanical ventilation (aOR 0.14; 95% CI 0.07-0.30) compared with SR. TEER was additionally associated with shorter LOS (β –6.9 days; 95% CI –9.5 to –4.2) and lower inflation-adjusted hospitalization costs (β –$31,770; 95% CI –$41,873 to –$21,668). Conclusions: In this national analysis of patients with nonrheumatic TR, TEER was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality, fewer peri-procedural complications, shorter hospitalization, and lower healthcare costs compared with SR.
title: Abstract 11465: Comparative Effectiveness of Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair versus Isolated Surgical Repair for Nonrheumatic Tricuspid Regurgitation: Insights from the National Inpatient Sample (2017-2022)

abstract: Background: Comprehensive data on sex-specific trajectories of cardiogenic shock (CS) remain limited, yet understanding these differences is critical for tailoring therapeutic strategies and improving clinical outcomes. Methods: Using comprehensive electronic health record data, we assembled a cohort of adults hospitalized within Kaiser Permanente Northern California between 2014 and 2024 with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or worsening heart failure (WHF). Demographic and clinical characteristics were ascertained using validated algorithms. Based on standard hemodynamic, laboratory, and treatment parameters, SCAI shock stages (A-E) were assigned at presentation and at 24 hours. Analyses were stratified by sex to compare baseline clinical characteristics and epidemiology of CS at presentation as well as progression of CS from early (SCAI stage A-B) to advanced (SCAI stage C-E) at 24 hours. Results: Among 98,642 eligible adults (mean age 74±13.7 years), 44,391 (45.0%) were women. Compared with men, women were older (mean [SD] 76.7 [13.2] vs 72.1 [13.8] years) and more likely to present with WHF than AMI (76.4% vs 65.4%, p<0.001). Women more often had atrial fibrillation or flutter, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease. Women also presented with greater shock severity, with a higher proportion in advanced stages (SCAI C-E) than men (10.4% vs 9.0%, p<0.001). Within the first 24 hours, 49.3% of patients progressed in SCAI stage. Progression from early (SCAI A-B) to advanced (SCAI C-E) shock at 24 hours was more common in women than men (45.9% vs 45.0%, p=0.006). Among patients with early progression, in-hospital mortality was similar between women and men (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.64-1.13, p=0.27). Conclusion: Sex-related differences in CS severity at presentation and early progression were evident in a contemporary cohort of adults hospitalized for AMI or WHF within a large integrated healthcare system. Despite older age and higher comorbidity burden, women who experienced early progression had no significant difference in in-hospital mortality compared with men. These findings underscore the need for further research into the sex-related factors that influence progression in CS and for more tailored, equitable strategies in its management.
title: Abstract 11486: Sex-Related Differences in Severity and Early Progression of Cardiogenic Shock: Insights from the KP-SHOCK Study

abstract: Background: Right heart thrombus-in-transit is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of venous thromboembolism associated with high mortality, particularly when accompanied by acute pulmonary embolism (PE) and right ventricular (RV) failure. Optimal management remains uncertain, especially in patients with elevated bleeding risk. Case: A 52-year-old woman with recent bowel ischemia requiring subtotal colectomy with end ileostomy and limited mobility during rehabilitation presented with 3 days of acute dyspnea and weakness. On arrival, she was hypotensive (85/66 mmHg), tachycardic (116 bpm), tachypneic, and required 6 L supplemental oxygen. Laboratory studies showed elevated troponin I (143 pg/mL), NT-proBNP (19,057 pg/mL), and lactic acid (2.8 mmol/L). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography demonstrated a saddle pulmonary embolus with extensive bilateral distal extension involving all lobar arteries and evidence of right heart strain. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed dilated right ventricle (RV) with reduced systolic function and McConnell’s sign and a large mobile right atrial thrombus prolapsing into the RV consistent with clot-in-transit (CIT). Decision-Making: Due to hemodynamic compromise, severe RV dysfunction, and right atrial thrombus-in-transit, urgent reperfusion therapy was indicated. Systemic thrombolysis was considered less favorable due to recent major abdominal surgery and prior bleeding concerns. A multidisciplinary pulmonary embolism response team (PERT) decision was made to pursue imaging -guided catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy of the CIT and PE. Intervention: Right heart catheterization revealed elevated pulmonary artery pressures (56/21 mmHg; mean 35 mmHg) and a reduced cardiac index. Echocardiography-guided aspiration thrombectomy was successfully performed for the right atrial clot-in-transit (Figure 1) and thromboemboli involving the main pulmonary trunk and bilateral pulmonary arteries. Post-procedurally, mean pulmonary artery pressure decreased to 24 mmHg with immediate hemodynamic improvement, including improvement in systemic blood pressure. Conclusion: This case highlights catheter-based aspiration thrombectomy as an effective alternative to systemic thrombolysis for high risk PE complicated by right atrial thrombus-in-transit in patients with increased bleeding risk. Rapid recognition and multidisciplinary escalation are critical to improving outcomes in this high-risk presentation.
title: Abstract 11497: Catheter-Based Extraction of Right Atrial Thrombus-in-Transit and High-Risk Saddle Pulmonary Embolism Using Aspiration Thrombectomy

abstract: Background: The optimal timing of aortic valve intervention in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains debated. Contemporary randomized trials have evaluated early surgical or transcatheter aortic valve intervention versus conservative surveillance, but the absolute clinical benefit and number needed to treat (NNT) remain incompletely defined. Research Question: Among adults with asymptomatic severe AS, what is the absolute clinical benefit of early aortic valve intervention compared with conservative surveillance or deferred intervention? Methods: We performed a meta-analysis of trials comparing early aortic valve intervention with conservative surveillance or deferred intervention in adults with asymptomatic severe AS. Pubmed, OvidSP and Cochrane Central were the databases searched. The primary analysis pooled absolute risk differences (RDs) using random-effects models to estimate NNT. The primary outcome was the trial-defined composite clinical endpoint. All data analysis was done on RStudio. PROSPERO ID: CRD420261414536 Results: Four randomized trials comprising 1,427 patients were included: RECOVERY, AVATAR, EARLY TAVR, and EVOLVED. Early intervention significantly reduced trial-defined composite clinical events compared with conservative/deferred management (pooled RD, –16.7%; 95% CI, –29.4% to –3.9%; I 2 =55.7%), corresponding to an NNT of 7. Early intervention also reduced heart failure/cardiovascular/AS-related hospitalization (pooled RD, –16.5%; 95% CI, –24.4% to –8.5%; I 2 =37.6%), corresponding to an NNT of 7. Effects on all-cause death (RD, –6.9%; 95% CI, –22.8% to 8.9%; I 2 =72.1%), stroke (RD, –2.2%; 95% CI, –5.0% to 0.6%; I 2 =0.0%), myocardial infarction (RD, –4.0%; 95% CI, –25.3% to 17.3%; I 2 =0.0%), and thromboembolic complications (RD, –1.7%; 95% CI, –45.3% to 42.0%; I 2 =41.0%) were directionally favorable but statistically uncertain. Conclusion: In randomized evidence among patients with asymptomatic severe AS, early aortic valve intervention was associated with clinically meaningful absolute reductions in composite adverse events and heart failure/cardiovascular/AS-related hospitalization, with an NNT of approximately 7 for both outcomes. Effects on mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and thromboembolic complications were directionally favorable but uncertain. These findings support individualized early intervention discussions based on absolute benefit while highlighting the need for longer-term data to clarify survival and procedural trade-offs.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 4 randomised trials (RECOVERY, AVATAR, EARLY TAVR, EVOLVED), 1,427 patients; PROSPERO CRD420261414536.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite endpoints differ between trials, heterogeneity is moderate to high, and mortality effects remain uncertain.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four randomised trials of early intervention in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis estimated absolute risk differences and numbers needed to treat.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early intervention reduced trial-defined composite clinical events (pooled RD, -16.7%; 95% CI, -29.4% to -3.9%; I2=55.7%; NNT 7) and heart failure/cardiovascular/AS-related hospitalisation (pooled RD, -16.5%; 95% CI, -24.4% to -8.5%; NNT 7). All-cause death RD, -6.9%; 95% CI, -22.8% to 8.9%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies absolute benefit for a common and rapidly changing decision in aortic stenosis (timing of TAVI or SAVR).

title: Abstract 11508: Absolute Benefit of Early versus Deferred Aortic Valve Intervention in Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: An RCT-Only Meta-Analysis of Number Needed to Treat

abstract: Introduction: Coronary involvement in fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) most commonly manifests as spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), coronary ectasia, marked vessel tortuosity, and coronary microaneurysms. In contrast, the classic angiographic string-of-beads appearance characteristic of extracoronary FMD is rarely reported in the coronary circulation. We present a unique case of coronary FMD involving the right coronary artery (RCA) with a striking string-of-beads morphology confirmed by intravascular imaging (IVUS). Case Presentation: A 62-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, infrarenal aortic dissection, and prior MI complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring single-vessel CABG to the RCA in 2009 presented with intermittent chest pressure. Coronary angiography performed in 2013 demonstrated an occluded native RCA, a patent saphenous vein graft (SVG) to the posterior descending artery (PDA), and an otherwise unremarkable left coronary system. Subsequent nuclear stress testing demonstrated mild reversible inferior wall ischemia, prompting repeat invasive coronary angiography. Coronary and graft angiography revealed spontaneous recanalization of the native RCA with a striking string-of-beads appearance, accompanied by occlusion of the SVG-PDA graft (Figure 1A). In addition, the left main and circumflex arteries demonstrated interval aneurysmal remodeling with multifocal stenotic segments (Figure 1B). Angiography-derived fractional flow reserve of the RCA was negative for physiologically significant ischemia (FFR 0.91, normal>0.8). Intravascular ultrasound of the RCA demonstrated aneurysmal vessel remodeling and marked fibrous intimal thickening within stenotic segments, without evidence of significant atherosclerotic disease (Figures 2A-B). Additional areas of fibrotic plaque with intimal disruption raised concern for prior healed SCAD versus healed plaque rupture (Figures 2C-D). Taken together, the angiographic and intravascular findings strongly supported coronary involvement by FMD. Given the absence of physiologically significant ischemia, the unusual late recanalization of the native RCA following prior CABG, and concern for an underlying arteriopathy with previous SCAD, percutaneous coronary intervention was deferred. The patient was managed conservatively with beta-blocker therapy and guideline-directed secondary prevention for coronary artery disease. Conclusion: The angiographic string-of-beads appearance is a rare but important manifestation of coronary FMD. Recognition of this characteristic pattern may facilitate diagnosis, particularly in patients with associated vascular abnormalities or a history suggestive of SCAD. Intravascular imaging can provide valuable insight into the underlying vessel pathology and may help distinguish FMD from atherosclerotic coronary disease.
title: Abstract 11523: String of Beads in the Coronary Circulation: A Rare Manifestation of Fibromuscular Dysplasia

abstract: Introduction: Streptobacillus moniliformis, the cause of rat-bite fever, is a fastidious gram-negative bacillus with only approximately 26 reported cases of native valve endocarditis. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to negative blood cultures and unrecognised rodent exposure. We present a case diagnosed by plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing. Patient Information: A 50-year-old man with alcohol use disorder and no known valvular disease presented with four days of diaphoresis, rigors, fever, polyarthralgia, vomiting, and hematemesis. No rash was present. Empiric daptomycin and meropenem were initiated. Leukocytosis was present; serial blood cultures remained sterile.Clinical Findings & Timeline:Transthoracic echocardiography revealed mitral valve vegetation. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a 1.7 х 2.0 cm vegetation with severe mitral regurgitation and pulmonary venous flow reversal. Systemic embolization occurred with bilateral renal infarcts and left superficial femoral artery stenosis. Acute hypoxic respiratory failure required intubation with elevated BNP indicating heart failure. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Blood cultures remained sterile at two facilities. Plasma microbial cell-free DNA testing, obtained after antibiotic initiation, detected Streptobacillus moniliformis, establishing the diagnosis of rat-bite fever-associated culture-negative endocarditis. Collateral history revealed residence in a rat-infested home for two years with two prior rat bites. No valve tissue culture or 16S rRNA PCR was performed on the excised valve.Therapeutic Intervention(s): Given large vegetation, severe regurgitation, heart failure, and embolic complications, he underwent bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement at a tertiary center. Antibiotics were narrowed to intravenous penicillin G for six weeks.Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: Postoperatively, progressive left foot gangrene required thrombolysis and below-knee amputation. He survived to discharge. Discussion & Synthesis: This case demonstrates a rare and severe streptobacillary endocarditis with multi-organ embolization diagnosed solely by plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing after persistently negative blood cultures, highlighting its utility in culture-negative endocarditis. Clinicians should consider S. moniliformis in culture-negative endocarditis with rodent exposure. This case also underscores the importance of valve tissue culture with 16S rRNA PCR when surgery is performed for culture-negative endocarditis.
title: Abstract 11531: Plasma Microbial Cell-Free DNA Detected Streptobacillus moniliformis Native Mitral Valve Endocarditis with Multi-Organ Embolization in a Patient with Chronic Rat Exposure

abstract: Background: Digoxin is occasionally used in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) for atrial arrhythmias or low-output right ventricular failure, although disease-specific outcome data remain limited. Aim: To evaluate the association between digoxin exposure and clinical outcomes in adults with WHO Group 1 PAH using severity-aligned matching and time-varying exposure modeling. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with WHO Group 1 PAH in the Mayo Clinic database. Inclusion required confirmed Group 1 PAH and receipt of at least one PAH-directed therapy. Patients exposed to digoxin were compared with unexposed controls. Propensity score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, atrial fibrillation, REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. Digoxin was modeled as a time-varying exposure in Cox regression, allowing patients to contribute unexposed person-time before initiation and exposed person-time thereafter. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, urgent coronary revascularization, or acute heart failure hospitalization. Results: After matching, 176 patients were included in each group, with good covariate balance across matched variables. In time-varying Cox analysis, digoxin exposure was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality compared with no digoxin exposure (hazard ratio [HR], 1.25; 95% CI, 0.77-2.03; P=0.36). Fig.1A Digoxin exposure was also not significantly associated with MACE (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.14; P=0.26). Fig.1B Conclusion: In adults with WHO Group 1 PAH, digoxin exposure was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality or MACE after REVEAL Lite 2-anchored matching and time-varying exposure modeling.
title: Abstract 11535: Digoxin Use and Clinical Outcomes in WHO Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: REVEAL Lite 2-Anchored Matching and Time-Varying Survival Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Hypoxia from an atrial septal defect (ASD) can result from right to left shunting of deoxygenated blood into systemic circulation, bypassing the lungs. Guidelines provide a tiered framework for closure in adults based on invasive hemodynamics. Case: A 40 year old male with a medical history significant for complicated infective endocarditis ultimately requiring mechanical aortic, mechanical mitral, and bioprosthetic tricuspid valve replacements, complete heart block with pacemaker placement, end stage renal disease (ESRD) on intermittent hemodialysis, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for acute on chronic hypoxic respiratory failure following creation of a left upper extremity (LUE) fistula. Initial vital signs were heart rate of 73 beats per minute, blood pressure of 205/103 millimeters of mercury (mmHg), oxygen saturation (SpO2) of 79% on bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP). On arrival, he was started on clevidipine and nitroglycerin drips to lower systemic blood pressure and inhaled nitric oxide to lower pulmonary pressures and reduce shunting. He improved on continued BiPAP and lower systemic blood pressure with oxygen saturation of 85-90%. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a right-to-left interatrial shunt and increased valve gradients. Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a large, 1.1cm secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) (Figure 1a, 1b). Right heart catheterization with oximetry and shunt assessment revealed: Right atrial pressure 16 mmHg, pulmonary vascular resistance 186 dynes/sec/cm 5 , left atrial pressure 9 mmHg, aortic SpO2 89%, mixed venous SpO2 51%, pulmonary artery SpO2 42%, pulmonary vein SpO2 98% with a calculated Qp/Qs ratio of 0.674. Post secundum ASD closure was performed (Figure 2a, 2b) with improved saturation to 90-95%. Blood pressure improved with oral isosorbide dinitrate and hydralazine. He expressed interest in discharging with plans to follow up outpatient within 4-6 weeks. Discussion: This case highlights a rare cause of hypoxemia resulting from a newly identified secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) following creation of an arteriovenous fistula. Right heart catheterization demonstrated that the right-to-left shunt was not attributable to pulmonary hypertension and a Qp/Qs ratio consistent with right to left shunting. These findings led to the hypothesis that the prosthetic tricuspid valve was unable to accommodate the increased venous return from the left upper extremity fistula, thereby promoting right-to-left atrial shunting. Importantly, ASD closure did not result in a prohibitive increase in right atrial pressure, supporting hemodynamic tolerability. This thorough evaluation of hypoxemia caused by right-to-left shunting can identify patients in whom ASD closure is both safe and effective, resulting in improved oxygen saturation.
title: Abstract 11562: Acute on Chronic Hypoxic Respiratory Failure by Novel ASD from Arteriovenous Fistula Creation

abstract: Background: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is capable of accurately identifying the composition of vascular plaque with a high-resolution. The content of lipid and the thickness of fibrous cap are critical in plaque stability and determine whether they trigger acute clinical events. Methods: In this study, 1312 patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) had performed three main vessels OCT and were undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention between 2017 to 2021. The patients were categorized into non-lipid rich plaque (NLRP), thick-cap fibroatheroma (ThCFA), and thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA) groups. The primary point was major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as the composite of cardiac death, non-culprit lesion related nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), and unplanned coronary revascularization. Results: Among 1312 patients, TCFA was detected in 487 of 1312 (37.1%) patients, who tended to have diabetes and dyslipidemia and had more severe angiographic diameter stenosis and more non-culprit lesion related MI and revascularization compared with patients containing ThCFA (2.9% vs 1.4%, P=0.034) or NLRP (2.9% vs 0.9%, P<0.001). The cumulative rate of MACEs was higher in patients with TCFA (12.0%, P=0.006) during 5 years follow-up. In 5273 non-culprit lesions identified by OCT, there were 735 TCFA (13.9%), 2760 ThCFA (52.4%) and 1778 NLRP (33.7%). Adjusted Cox proportional hazards model at lesion level showed the presence of a NLRP was a significant predictive of a lower 5 years non-culprit events rate (hazard ratio: 0.63; 95% confidence interval: 0.06 to 0.95). Conclusion: NLRP in non-culprit lesion barely triggered adverse cardiovascular events and represented relatively stable phenotypes. While, patients with LRP indicated worse clinical prognosis and increased risk of future non-culprit lesion related events, particularly with TCFA, and are mostly driven by unplanned revascularization. The more lipid the plaque contented and thinner the fibrous cap was, the unfavorable outcome would be.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort of 1312 patients with AMI who had three-vessel OCT and PCI between 2017 to 2021; 5273 non-culprit lesions analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-source observational data with events driven mainly by unplanned revascularisation, and the reported lesion-level confidence interval is implausibly wide at its lower bound.
appraisal.one_line: Three-vessel OCT cohort in AMI linking non-culprit plaque phenotype to five-year events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The cumulative rate of MACEs was higher in patients with TCFA (12.0%, P=0.006) during 5 years follow-up. Adjusted Cox model at lesion level showed the presence of a NLRP was a significant predictive of a lower 5 years non-culprit events rate (hazard ratio: 0.63; 95% confidence interval: 0.06 to 0.95).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds outcome-linked evidence for plaque-phenotype-guided preventive PCI of non-culprit lesions, a question where randomised data remain limited.

title: Abstract 11565: Morphological Phenotype of Non-Culprit Lesion in AMI Patient Identified by 3-Vessel Optical Coherence Tomography and Its Prognosis on Clinical Outcome

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has expanded from a therapy for inoperable elderly patients to a first-line option across the surgical-risk spectrum, including younger recipients. As recipients become younger, long-term valve durability assumes increasing importance, yet real world comparative data on durability-related outcomes by age remain limited. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that relatively younger (&lt;75 years) TAVR recipients would have a higher incidence of durability-related events than older (≥75 years) recipients after adjustment for comorbidity. Methods: We performed a retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study within the TriNetX Research network (110 healthcare organizations). Adults with nonrheumatic aortic stenosis within one year before an index TAVR were eligible; patients with prior surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), prior cardiac or vascular prosthetic implants, or endocarditis were excluded. Cohorts defined by age at index TAVR (&lt;75 vs ≥75 years) were matched 1:1 on sexand six comorbidities, yielding 1,380 patients per group. Outcomes, repeat TAVR, SAVR after index TAVR, coded prosthetic valve dysfunction, prosthetic valve endocarditis, and all-cause mortality, were assessed from one day after the index procedure. Risk ratios (RR) and Kaplan-Meier hazard ratios (HR) are reported as ≥75 versus &lt;75. Results: After matching, sex and all six comorbidities were well balanced (all standardized mean differences &lt;0.01). Younger recipients had a higher incidence of coded prosthetic valve dysfunction than older recipients (12.0% vs 8.6%; RR 0.711, 95% CI 0.568 0.889; HR 0.581, 95% CI 0.458-0.737; log-rank p&lt;0.001). Older recipients had higher all-cause mortality (24.7% vs 16.6%; RR 1.489, 95% CI 1.282-1.730; p&lt;0.001). Repeat TAVR (1.4% vs 1.7%; RR 0.870, 95% CI 0.480-1.576) and prosthetic valve endocarditis (5.2% vs 3.9%; RR 1.333, 95% CI 0.944-1.882) did not differ significantly. No SAVR after index TAVR was captured in either cohort. Conclusions: In a propensity-matched real-world cohort, younger (&lt;75 years) TAVR recipients had a higher incidence of coded prosthetic valve dysfunction, whereas older (≥75 years) recipients had higher all-cause mortality, consistent with greater competing mortality in the oldergroup. These findings support continued durability surveillance and lifetime valve management planning as TAVR extends to longer-lived patients.
title: Abstract 11593: Durability-Related and Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Younger versus Older Recipients: A Propensity-Matched Analysis from a Global Federated Health Network

abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The clinical benefit of routine staged percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR in patients with stable CAD remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between PCI performed within one month before TAVR and post-procedural outcomes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥65 years with stable CAD undergoing TAVR were identified using validated diagnostic and procedural codes. Patients with acute coronary syndrome or cardiogenic shock within 30 days before TAVR were excluded. Patients undergoing PCI within one month before TAVR were compared with those undergoing TAVR alone. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed for age, sex, race/ethnicity, and insurance status, yielding 2,566 patients in each cohort. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, repeat PCI, acute decompensated heart failure, left bundle branch block (LBBB), complete atrioventricular (AV) block, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Results: Median follow-up was 885 days in the PCI cohort and 867 days in the non-PCI cohort. No significant differences were observed across any prespecified outcome. All-cause mortality occurred in 29.3% versus 28.1% of patients (HR 1.04, p=0.42). Rates of acute decompensated heart failure were 64.8% versus 64.6% (HR 1.00, p=0.89), AKI 24.0% versus 25.5% (HR 0.94, p=0.08), new-onset LBBB 17.4% versus 18.2% (HR 0.95, p=0.31), complete AV block 13.7% versus 13.8% (HR 0.99, p=0.93), ischemic stroke 11.6% versus 12.4% (HR 0.93, p=0.17), recurrent MI 12.7% versus 12.3% (HR 1.03, p=0.64), and repeat PCI 2.9% versus 2.5% (HR 1.16, p=0.27). Conclusions: Among older adults with stable CAD undergoing TAVR, PCI performed within one month before valve replacement was not associated with improved clinical outcomes, including mortality, ischemic events, heart failure, conduction disturbances, or renal injury. These findings suggest that routine pre-TAVR PCI may not provide additional benefit in stable CAD and support an individualized revascularization strategy guided by clinical and anatomic considerations.
title: Abstract 11594: Staged Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Stable Coronary Artery Disease: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Fatty change of the liver is strongly associated with cardiovascular risk due to insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and systemic inflammation. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) each provide independent cardiovascular benefits. This study assesses whether combination therapy provides additional cardiovascular protection compared with GLP-1 RA monotherapy in adults with liver fatty change and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Research Question: Does combination GLP-1 RA + SGLT2i reduce MACE risk myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, heart failure (HF), and all cause mortality compared to GLP-1 RA monotherapy in patients with fatty change of liver and cardiometabolic comorbidities? Methods: This retrospective cohort study used TriNetX, a federated network that captures data from 171 healthcare organizations. Adults (≥18 years) with fatty change of liver (ICD-10: K76.0) and ≥1 cardiometabolic comorbidity (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or obesity) were included. Patients with competing liver etiologies (cirrhosis, alcoholic liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis, viral hepatitis, hemochromatosis, or Wilson’s disease) or prior MACE were excluded. Cohort 1: GLP-1 RA + SGLT2i (n=17,568); Cohort 2: GLP-1 RA monotherapy (n=17,568). Propensity score matching balanced cohorts on demographics, comorbidities, and medications. Outcomes were assessed via risk proportions, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox proportional hazards modeling. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: All-cause mortality occurred in 1.5% vs. 1.8%, MI in 1.3% vs. 1.4%, stroke in 1.2% vs. 1.3%, and HF in 2.4% vs. 2.7% (combination vs. monotherapy). Kaplan-Meier survival probabilities favored combination therapy: mortality, 94.71% vs. 88.74%; HF, 86.78% vs. 84.35%; MI, 91.46% vs. 91.62%; and stroke, 93.99% vs. 94.58%. Hazard ratios consistently favored combination therapy mortality HR 0.863 (0.732–1.017), MI HR 0.928 (0.775–1.112), stroke HR 0.966 (0.800–1.166), HF HR 0.901 (0.789–1.028) though none reached statistical significance. HF risk difference trended toward significance (p=0.071). Conclusion: Combination GLP-1 RA + SGLT2i therapy showed a consistent trend toward reduced MACE and mortality versus GLP-1 RA monotherapy in patients with fatty liver change, without reaching statistical significance. HF was the most frequent adverse outcome, underscoring the substantial cardiovascular burden in this population. Prospective randomized trials are warranted to confirm whether dual therapy offers superior cardiovascular protection in this high-risk group. Keywords Fatty change of liver · K76.0 · GLP-1 RA · SGLT2 inhibitor · MACE · Heart failure · Propensity score matching · TriNetX · Real-world evidence

register_verdicts.note: Fatty liver cohort of GLP-1 RA plus SGLT2i versus GLP-1 RA alone, not a post-MI population.

title: Abstract 11617: Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Fatty Change of Liver Treated with Combined GLP-1 RA and SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy versus GLP-1 RA Alone: A Propensity Score Matched TriNetX Analysis

abstract: Background: Concomitant left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) with catheter ablation is increasingly performed, but comparative data between pulsed field ablation (PFA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) remain limited to small single-center studies. Research Questions/Hypothesis: We evaluated whether PFA+LAAO provides comparable 1-year freedom from AF/AFL recurrence and safety outcomes compared with RFA+LAAO, hypothesizing that PFA would demonstrate similar efficacy with fewer peri-procedural complications. Methods: From a prospectively maintained single-center registry of 601 patients undergoing concomitant LAAO+ablation, 454 patients (227 PFA+LAAO vs 227 RFA+LAAO) were matched 1:1 using nearest-neighbor propensity scoring on 8 variables: age, sex, BMI, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc, HAS-BLED, AF type, redo ablation, and AFL history (caliper=0.2 SD). Primary outcome was freedom from AF/AFL recurrence at 1 year after a 90-day blanking period over 365-day follow-up. Secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause death, ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, systemic embolism), device thrombus, and significant peri-device leak (>5mm). Results: Baseline characteristics were well balanced, including age (73.7 vs 74.0 years), CHA2DS2-VASc (4.20 vs 4.00), and HAS-BLED (2.91 vs 2.89). Freedom from AF/AFL recurrence at 1 year was 67.5% in RFA+LAAO vs 62.0% in PFA+LAAO (log-rank p=0.32, Figure 1). On multivariable Cox regression, PFA+LAAO was not associated with recurrence compared to RFA+LAAO (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.85-1.66, p=0.38, Figure 2); independent predictors included redo ablation (HR 1.99, p<0.001), persistent AF (HR 1.71, p=0.004), and HAS-BLED score (HR 1.28, p=0.003). Cumulative MACE incidence at 1 year was 4.7% in RFA+LAAO vs 5.7% in PFA+LAAO (8 vs 8 events, Gray p=0.719, Figure 3). Device thrombus (2.2% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and significant leak (0.4% vs 0.4%, p=1.00) were identical between groups. Intra/postoperative complications within 5 days occurred less frequently with PFA+LAAO vs RFA+LAAO (1.3% vs 4.8%, p=0.054), driven predominantly by pericardial effusion and access site bleeding in the RFA group. Conclusions: In this large propensity-matched comparison, PFA+LAAO demonstrated equivalent efficacy to RFA+LAAO with numerically fewer peri-procedural complications. Redo ablation and persistent AF were the strongest predictors of recurrence regardless of energy modality, supporting PFA as a potentially safer and equally effective alternative to RFA in the concomitant LAAO setting.
title: Abstract 11644: Pulsed Field Ablation vs Radiofrequency Ablation Concomitant with Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: The challenge in cardiovascular medicine is no longer evidence generation, but implementation. Despite robust guideline-directed therapies, therapeutic inertia remains pervasive. Clinical decision support systems (CDSS) were developed to close this evidence-to-practice gap, yet their effectiveness remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify determinants of successful CDSS implementation. Methods: This prospectively registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD420261413315 ) followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Google Scholar, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized and cluster-randomized trials evaluating cardiovascular CDSS. Risk of bias was assessed using ROB-2. Random-effects meta-analysis using R version 4.6.0 calculated pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with prespecified subgroup analyses by clinical context and intervention design. Results: Fourteen randomized and cluster-randomized trials involving 27,187 patients were included. CDSS significantly improved adherence to guideline-directed cardiovascular care compared with standard practice ( RR 1.24, 95% CI 1.05-1.47; P=0.013 ). Heterogeneity appeared driven by clinical decision complexity rather than technology. HF-focused interventions significantly improved guideline-directed medical therapy optimization ( RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.04-2.42; P=0.031 ), while mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist initiation demonstrated the largest treatment effect ( RR 2.03, 95% CI 1.43-2.89; P<0.001 ). In contrast, AF-focused interventions did not significantly increase oral anticoagulant prescribing ( RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.99-1.11; P=0.10 ). Positive studies consistently employed workflow-integrated alerts supporting immediate action, whereas neutral studies targeted decisions requiring complex risk-benefit deliberation. CDSS effectiveness declined as clinical decision complexity increased. Conclusions: Cardiovascular CDSS interventions improve guideline-directed care, but their effectiveness is determined less by technological sophistication than by clinical actionability. The greatest benefits were observed when recommendations could be translated into immediate action, whereas complex decisions requiring risk-benefit deliberation showed little response to digital prompting. These findings challenge the assumption that more alerts improve care and identify actionability as the key determinant of CDSS success. The future of cardiovascular decision support may depend less on delivering more information and more on delivering the right recommendation at the exact moment a clinician is prepared to act.

abstract: Aims: Our study aimed to investigate the effect of renal denervation (RDN) on central hemodynamics in Chinese patients with uncontrolled hypertension. Methods: This cohort study included a subset of participants from the Iberis-HTN and Netrod TM -HTN trials previously conducted at our center. Eligible patients were randomly assigned to undergo either radiofrequency RDN or a sham procedure. Parameters of central hemodynamics and carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cf-PWV) were measured using a dedicated SphygmoCor device at both baseline and 6 months after RDN. Results: The reductions in central systolic blood pressure (BP), central pulse pressure, end systolic pressure, and mean pressure during both systole and diastole from baseline to 6 months were significantly greater in the RDN group compared to the sham group (all P < 0.05). However, the difference in central diastolic BP reduction between the two groups approached statistical significance (P = 0.068). Furthermore, the reduction in the forward wave P1 height was more pronounced in the RDN group than in the sham group (adjusted between-group difference: -4.1±1.9 mmHg, P = 0.039). No significant between-group differences were observed in the changes of reflected wave parameters (P >0.05). The changes in cf-PWV between groups did not differ significantly from baseline to 6 months (P = 0.727). Conclusion: Catheter-based RDN effectively reduced central arterial pressure, primarily through a decrease in forward wave intensity during early systole, and mitigated cardiac afterload without significantly affecting reflected wave intensity or aortic stiffness.
title: Abstract 11661: Effect of Catheter-Based Renal Denervation on Central Hemodynamics in Chinese Patients with Uncontrolled Hypertension

abstract: Background: Unlike left ventricular failure, acute right heart failure remains a clinical challenge with limited treatment options. Percutaneous right ventricular assist devices offer a minimally invasive approach, yet safe and reliable devices are scarce. Hypothesis: This study aimed to validate the safety and hemodynamic efficacy of CorVad RS, a novel percutaneous right ventricular assist device. We hypothesized that the device would demonstrate favorable hemocompatibility and device safety in vitro and in a long-term animal model, and would provide effective right ventricular unloading in an acute right heart failure model. Methods: CorVad RS is a percutaneous right ventricular assist device inserted via the femoral or internal jugular vein using a 21F sheath, featuring a microaxial dual-drive motor and ceramic bearings, with a maximum flow rate of 5.5 liters per minute. The preclinical evaluation included three components: a 30-day in vitro test of reliability, thermal performance, and hemolysis; a 30-day safety study in 6 sheep after device implantation; and a randomized controlled efficacy study in 12 pigs with cardiogenic shock induced by right coronary artery embolization (6 in the CorVad RS group vs 6 in the vasoactive therapy group). Results: In vitro, the device ran continuously for 30 days without malfunction or alarm. Thermal testing demonstrated an external pump wall temperature below 39.0 degrees Celsius under full load. In the in vitro hemolysis test, the mean hemolysis value was 0.0086 g/100L. In the 30-day ovine safety study, all 6 animals survived to endpoint, and postoperative free hemoglobin was not significantly different from preoperative values (4.5±2.7 vs 4.1±1.6, P=0.770). Histopathology revealed no thromboembolism or device-related injury in major organs (brain, heart, liver, kidney, spleen) or heart valves. In the porcine cardiogenic shock model, pressure-volume loop analysis demonstrated effective right ventricular unloading in the CorVad RS group compared with the vasoactive therapy group, with a significant reduction in right ventricular stroke work. Conclusion: CorVad RS has validated its safety and hemodynamic efficacy in vitro, in a long-term ovine safety study, and in a porcine cardiogenic shock model. The device features low thermal rise, low hemolysis, and effective right ventricular unloading, offering a promising percutaneous treatment option for refractory acute right heart failure.
title: Abstract 11664: A Novel Percutaneous Right Ventricular Assist Device for Acute Right Heart Failure: Preclinical Validation of Long-Term Safety and Acute Hemodynamic Efficacy

abstract: Introduction: Percutaneous patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure significantly reduces recurrent ischemic events in cryptogenic stroke. Device-related thrombosis (DRT) is an uncommon but clinically profound failure of therapy, occurring in approximately 1.2% of cases. We report a rare case of massive, bilateral DRT on a flexible septal occluder precipitating an acute recurrent embolic stroke despite strict compliance with standard antiplatelet therapy. Patient Information: A 32-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset slurred speech, left-sided hemiparesis, and facial droop (NIHSS = 7). Her history was notable for class III obesity, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura following a prior splenectomy, and two spontaneous miscarriages. She had undergone an elective dilation and curettage earlier that same month. Eleven months prior, she underwent percutaneous PFO closure with a 30-mm Gore Cardioform device for recurrent cryptogenic strokes. She completed a 6-month course of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT; aspirin/clopidogrel) and maintained strict compliance on aspirin monotherapy until presentation to the hospital. Brain MRI confirmed an acute right middle cerebral artery territory infarction. Urgent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) revealed the occluder in situ without a residual shunt, but visualized large, highly mobile thrombi anchored to both atrial surfaces (left atrial: 3.0 х 1.0 cm; right atrial: 2.6 х 1.0 cm). Given her hematological and recent obstetrical/surgical history, there was a high suspicion of seronegative anti-phospholipid syndrome, though a comprehensive thrombophilia and rheumatologic evaluation was completely unremarkable. Following a multidisciplinary discussion, she was initiated on continuous intravenous heparin and safely transitioned to long-term warfarin (target INR 2.0-3.0). Conclusion: This case highlights that standard antiplatelet regimens may not fully mitigate DRT risk during the critical endothelialization phase, particularly in patients with overlapping clinical risk factors for occult hypercoagulability. Integrating systematic screening frameworks like the RoPE score and PASCAL classification with comprehensive clinical judgment at baseline is essential before deciding on invasive closure. Furthermore, extended longitudinal echocardiographic surveillance should be considered in high-risk cohorts.
title: Abstract 11666: The Paradoxical Source: Recurrent Embolic Stroke from Bilateral Thrombi on a PFO Occluder

abstract: Background: Accurate characterization of aortic valve calcification is essential for evaluating the severity of aortic stenosis (AS). CT-derived aortic valve calcium (AVC) quantification is well established as a complementary diagnostic tool in equivocal or low-gradient AS, but it also provides mechanistic insight in classical high-flow, high-gradient severe AS. Using the standard 130-HU Agatston seed and higher HU thresholds (200-1000 HU), this study re-evaluated the relationship between CT-AVC and Doppler gradients to test whether denser calcium weighting provides differential or incremental hemodynamic information. Methods: We retrospectively studied 63 pre-TAVI patients with high-flow/high-gradient severe AS (April-December 2023). Non-contrast, ECG-gated CT-AVC was measured using Agatston scoring (130 HU) and prespecified higher HU thresholds (200-1000 HU), and related to AV peak and mean gradients in multivariable linear models. Diagnostic performance for identifying very severe AS (mean gradient ≥60 mmHg) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with AUC values compared across HU thresholds. Results: Higher calcium scores were independently associated with higher aortic valve peak gradient (β per 1 Agatston unit [AU]: 0.010, 95% CI 0.006-0.014 at 130 HU up to 0.144, 95% CI 0.044-0.245 at 1000 HU; all P ≤ .005) and higher aortic valve mean gradient (β per 1 AU: 0.0059, 95% CI 0.0036-0.0083 at 130 HU up to 0.073, 95% CI 0.010-0.137 at 1000 HU; all P ≤ .024). Associations with aortic valve area were not significant at any threshold. Across all HU cut-offs, AVC showed independent and directionally consistent associations with peak and mean gradients. In exploratory diagnostic analyses using very severe aortic stenosis (mean gradient ≥60 mmHg) as the reference standard, ROC curves demonstrated modest and comparable discrimination across thresholds (AUC range 0.65-0.67), with no statistically significant differences between thresholds on formal comparison (DeLong test, p = 0.68). Conclusion: In high-flow/high-gradient severe aortic stenosis, CT-derived aortic valve calcium demonstrated consistent associations with transvalvular gradients across all HU thresholds. Higher calcium density thresholds did not confer statistically superior diagnostic discrimination for identifying very severe disease (mean gradient ≥60 mmHg), but showed comparable performance to standard 130-HU scoring. CT-AVC remains a complementary imaging marker reflecting calcific burden, warranting prospective validation across broader aortic stenosis phenotypes before any diagnostic reclassification is considered.
title: Abstract 11698: CT-Based Multi-Threshold Calcium Scoring for Aortic Valve Assessment: Comparable Predictive Performance Across HU Thresholds in a Pre-TAVI Cohort

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction carries an in-hospital mortality rate approaching 50%, yet the optimal timing of temporary mechanical circulatory support remains contested. Real-world comparative data on same-day versus delayed device escalation across all support types and presentations are lacking. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that same-day mechanical circulatory support would be associated with lower mortality and a favorable safety profile compared with delayed escalation in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network spanning 171 healthcare organizations. Adults aged 18 or older with concurrent acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock receiving temporary mechanical circulatory support — including intra-aortic balloon pump, percutaneous ventricular assist device, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation — within three days of the index event were included. Patients were stratified by timing: same-day support versus delayed support on days one through three. Propensity score matching on ten demographic and clinical variables yielded 4,313 patients per group. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury, major bleeding, ischemic stroke, limb ischemia, sepsis, and ventricular arrhythmias. Results: Same-day mechanical circulatory support was associated with a clinically meaningful but statistically non-significant mortality reduction (46.4% vs. 48.1%; risk ratio 0.966; 95% CI, 0.924-1.010; p=0.126), with a directional survival benefit on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p=0.061). Same-day support significantly reduced major bleeding (31.5% vs. 35.1%; p<0.001) and limb ischemia (6.1% vs. 7.7%; p=0.003). However, it was associated with higher rates of acute kidney injury (47.8% vs. 45.4%; p=0.021) and ventricular arrhythmias (29.5% vs. 27.2%; p=0.018). Ischemic stroke and sepsis were equivalent between groups. Conclusion: In this propensity-matched real-world cohort of 8,626 acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock patients, same-day mechanical circulatory support showed a mortality trend favoring earlier escalation alongside a mixed safety profile — significantly less bleeding and limb ischemia but more acute kidney injury and ventricular arrhythmias. These findings support individualized shock-team-guided escalation over uniform timing protocols.
title: Abstract 11705: Same-Day versus Delayed Mechanical Circulatory Support in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Propensity Matched Study

abstract: Background: Circulatory collapse at hospital arrival is a severe presentation of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Statins have pleiotropic effects beyond lipid lowering that may influence early clinical severity. We evaluated the association between pre-admission statin therapy and circulatory collapse at hospital arrival in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: We retrospectively studied 551 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI at a tertiary cardiovascular center from 2019 to 2026. Pre-admission statin therapy was defined as continuous statin use for at least 30 days before admission. The primary outcome was circulatory collapse, defined as advanced-stage hemodynamic compromise broadly consistent with Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions shock stage C or higher, including persistent hypotension, vasopressor/inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, or lactate 4.0 mmol/L or higher with hypoperfusion before primary PCI. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, prior coronary artery disease, symptom-to-arrival time, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitor use. Sensitivity analyses included complete-case analysis, exclusion of pre-procedural cardiopulmonary arrest, propensity score adjustment, inverse probability of treatment weighting, and a stricter endpoint excluding lactate-based classification without pharmacologic or mechanical circulatory support. Results: Pre-admission statins were used in 160 patients (29.0%). Circulatory collapse occurred in 77 patients (14.0%) and was less frequent among statin users than non-users (7.5% vs 16.6%; P=0.005). In the primary multivariable model, pre-admission statin therapy was associated with lower odds of circulatory collapse (adjusted odds ratio 0.23; 95% confidence interval 0.10-0.50; P less than 0.001). This association was directionally consistent across prespecified subgroups and remained consistent in propensity score-adjusted analysis (adjusted odds ratio 0.27; 95% confidence interval 0.12-0.56; P=0.001), inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis (odds ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.14-0.90; P=0.030), and stricter endpoint analysis (adjusted odds ratio 0.25; 95% confidence interval 0.11-0.57; P=0.001). Thirty-day mortality did not differ significantly by statin status. Conclusions: Pre-admission statin therapy was associated with a lower risk of circulatory collapse at hospital arrival in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. These findings suggest that chronic statin therapy may be associated with a less severe early hemodynamic phenotype, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.
title: Abstract 11709: Pre-Admission Statin Therapy and Circulatory Collapse at Hospital Arrival in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Few studies have characterized contemporary population trends in P2Y12 inhibitor use, costs, and outcomes after acute myocardial infarction amid evolving evidence and clinical guideline recommendations. Methods: We identified patients initiating clopidogrel, prasugrel, or ticagrelor after acute myocardial infarction in nationally representative populations from Germany and the United States between 2011 and 2024. Trends in age- and sex-standardized use, costs, and 1-year outcomes of P2Y12 inhibitors were evaluated. We also examined payments by P2Y12 manufacturers to healthcare providers in relation to subsequent prescribing and estimated potential cost savings associated with substituting prasugrel for ticagrelor in eligible patients. Results: Among 163,015 patients in Germany and 220,971 patients in the United States who initiated P2Y12 inhibitor therapy after acute myocardial infarction, the mean age was 69 years, and 59% were men. From 2011 through 2024, clopidogrel use declined in both countries (Germany, 81% to 37%; United States, 80% to 59%). Following evidence from randomized trials favoring prasugrel over ticagrelor, prasugrel use increased by 21 percentage points in Germany (17% to 38%) and 4 percentage point in the United States (4% to 8%), whereas ticagrelor use declined by 22 and 6 percentage points (Germany, 48% to 26%; United States, 39% to 32%). Increasing prasugrel use in Germany did not meaningfully change the temporal trends in 1-year risks of major adverse cardiovascular events (-0.26; -1.08 to 0.55) or major bleeding (-0.47; -0.97 to 0.03). Industry payments related to ticagrelor exceeded those related to prasugrel by more than 15-fold and coincided with greater ticagrelor prescribing in the United States. After generic entry, prasugrel cost was 95% lower than ticagrelor in the United States and substituting prasugrel for ticagrelor in eligible patients would have reduced pharmacy cost by $1.8 billion between 2019 and 2024. Conclusions: Population trends in P2Y12 inhibitor use after acute myocardial infarction diverged substantially between two high-income countries despite shared clinical evidence. Earlier adoption of prasugrel in Germany was not accompanied with changing population trends in clinical endpoints, whereas continued ticagrelor predominance in the United States was associated with higher treatment costs. (Funded by the German Heart Foundation and the National Institutes of Health; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07610577.)
title: Abstract 11724: Population Trends in the Use of P2Y12 Inhibitors After Acute Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardio-renal outcomes in broad cardiometabolic populations, but their role in WHO Group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between SGLT2i exposure and outcomes in adults with WHO Group 1 PAH using REVEAL Lite 2 (RL2)-anchored matching and time-varying exposure modeling. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with WHO Group 1 PAH at a tertiary center. Patients prescribed SGLT2i, including empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, or ertugliflozin, were compared with PAH controls without SGLT2i exposure. Propensity score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline RL2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, urgent coronary revascularization, or acute heart failure hospitalization. Associations were assessed using both conventional fixed-exposure Cox models and start-stop time-varying Cox models. Results: The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 SGLT2i-exposed patients and 244 controls. In the fixed-exposure Cox model, SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=0.018), Fig.1 while MACE did not differ significantly (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=0.14). However, when SGLT2i exposure was modeled as time-varying, the mortality association attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=0.57). Conclusion: In an RL2-matched WHO Group 1 PAH cohort, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality after accounting for post-diagnosis treatment initiation. These findings highlight the importance of time-varying methods in PAH pharmacoepidemiology and support prospective PAH-focused trials.
title: Abstract 11770: SGLT2 Inhibitors in WHO Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A REVEAL Lite 2-Matched Cohort with Time-Varying Exposure Analysis

abstract: Background: It is well known that elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to investigate the age-specific association between elevated Lp(a) levels and coronary plaque features assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), stratified by age (<60 vs. ≥60 years). Methods: Between January 2018 and December 2021, 1144 ACS patients who underwent three-vessel OCT imaging after successful intervention were retrospectively enrolled and stratified by age (<60 years, n=632; ≥60 years, n=512). Baseline serum Lp(a) levels were measured using a latex particle-enhanced turbidimetric immunoassay (Roche Diagnostics) and categorized into elevated Lp(a) (≥75 nmol/L) and normal Lp(a) (<75 nmol/L) groups. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for baseline covariates, was used to evaluate the association between Lp(a) levels and plaque features across age groups. The primary endpoint was the presence of thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). Result: The average age of patients was 57.4±11.1 years, and 840 (73.4%) were male. Lp(a) was elevated ≥75 nmol/L in 15.6% (179/1144) of all enrolled patients. In younger ACS patients (<60 years), those with elevated Lp(a) exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of culprit-lesion plaque rupture (64.0% vs. 50.0%, P =0.010), TCFA (63.0% vs. 46.8%, P =0.003), and macrophage accumulation (92.0% vs. 84.2%, P =0.043), as well as a thinner fibrous cap (50.0 [40.0, 73.3]μm vs. 60.0 [46.7, 90.0]μm, P =0.003), compared with those with normal Lp(a). For non-culprit segments, patients with elevated Lp(a) had a higher prevalence of at least one non-culprit TCFA (43.0% vs. 28.6%, P =0.004), and macrophage accumulation (94.0% vs. 85.5%, P =0.021). The lesion-level analyses showed a higher prevalence of non-culprit TCFA (16.4% vs. 11.3%, P =0.018) and macrophage accumulation (89.1% vs. 83.2%, P =0.008), a smaller minimal lumen area (4.0[2.5-5.4] mm 2 vs. 4.3[2.8-6.3] mm 2 , P =0.002), and a thinner fibrous cap thickness (86.7 [60.0, 120.0]μm vs. 96.7 [70.0, 130.0]μm, P =0.026) in the elevated Lp(a) group. Multivariate analysis confirmed that elevated Lp(a) independently predicted culprit TCFA (OR: 1.96, 95%CI: 1.13-3.40, P =0.016) and non-culprit TCFA (OR: 1.94, 95%CI: 1.16-3.25, P =0.012). In contrast, no significant associations were observed between elevated Lp(a) and vulnerable plaque morphological features in ACS patients aged ≥60 years (all P >0.05). Conclusion: Elevated Lp(a) was significantly associated with vulnerable plaque features in both culprit and non-culprit lesions among ACS patients aged <60 years, whereas such associations were insignificant in patients aged ≥60 years. These findings highlight the importance of early Lp(a) screening and management, especially for younger patients with ACS.
title: Abstract 11829: Age-Stratified Associations Between Lipoprotein(a) and Pancoronary Plaque Vulnerability in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Three-Vessel OCT Study

abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcification impairs lesion preparation and stent deployment during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a novel calcium-modifying strategy and represents a less aggressive alternative to balloon-based preparation and rotational atherectomy (RA). However, randomized evidence comparing these approaches remains limited, and probabilistic estimates of treatment effects are scarce. Research Question: Among patients undergoing PCI for calcified coronary lesions, does IVL improve procedural and clinical outcomes compared with balloon-based strategies or RA? Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases identified randomized controlled trials comparing IVL with balloon-based strategies or RA before drug-eluting stent implantation in calcified coronary lesions. Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses were performed using vague priors for treatment effects and empirical or weakly informative priors for between-study heterogeneity. Outcomes included minimal stent area (MSA), stent expansion, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Results were reported as mean differences (MDs) or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Prediction intervals, posterior probabilities, sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-out analyses were performed. Results: Seven RCTs comprising 574 patients were included. Compared with balloon-based PCI, IVL demonstrated a 92.6% posterior probability of benefit for MSA (MD 0.91 mm 2 , 95% CrI 0.13 to 1.70) and an 86.1% posterior probability of improved stent expansion (MD 3.17%, 95% CrI –1.68 to 8.03). No clear benefit was observed for MACE (OR 0.93, 95% CrI 0.32 to 2.67). Compared with RA, IVL showed no credible differences in MSA (MD –0.28 mm 2 , 95% CrI –0.94 to 0.39), stent expansion (MD –0.89%, 95% CrI –4.55 to 2.76), or MACE (OR 3.03, 95% CrI 0.65 to 14.11). Similarly, when compared with all pooled PCI strategies, IVL was not associated with credible superiority for MSA (MD 0.44 mm 2 , 95% CrI –0.63 to 1.54), stent expansion (MD 0.88%, 95% CrI –3.84 to 4.89), or MACE (OR 1.40, 95% CrI 0.55 to 3.60). Findings were consistent across sensitivity and leave-one-out analyses. Conclusions: In patients undergoing PCI for calcified coronary lesions, IVL was associated with a favorable posterior estimate for MSA compared with balloon-based strategies, while demonstrating broadly comparable procedural and clinical outcomes to RA. These findings suggest that IVL may represent a feasible alternative for calcium modification, although larger randomized studies are needed to clarify its relative clinical benefit.
title: Abstract 11830: Intravascular Lithotripsy versus Balloon-Based and Atherectomy Lesion Preparation for Calcified Coronary PCI: A Bayesian Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) is increasingly utilized for severe tricuspid regurgitation. Approximately 25-33% of TTVR candidates have pre-existing transvenous cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) leads crossing the tricuspid valve. When TTVR is performed with leads in situ, leads become jailed between the prosthesis and annulus, precluding future extraction and creating significant risk if lead failure or device infection occurs. The incidence of lead malfunction in this setting has not been systematically quantified. Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis searching PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for studies reporting outcomes of jailed transvenous leads after TTVR. Proportional meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. The primary endpoint was strict lead failure, defined as structural or electrical failure requiring intervention or contributing to death. The secondary endpoint was broad lead malfunction, encompassing any documented parameter change on device interrogation. Meta-regression assessed the association between follow-up duration and failure rate, and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis evaluated estimate stability. Results: Six studies comprising 238 patients with jailed leads were included (TRIPLACE registry, n=104; Abbasi et al., n=32; Peigh et al., n=42; Mekary et al., n=14; Anderson et al., n=28; Braunstein et al., n=18), with median follow-up ranging from 6 to 15 months. The pooled strict lead failure rate was 6% (95% CI: 3-10%; I 2 =5.6%; prediction interval: 2-11%). The pooled broad malfunction rate was 15% (95% CI: 7-24%; I 2 =67%). Meta-regression demonstrated a non-significant trend toward higher failure rates with longer follow-up (β=0.011, p=0.25). Leave-one-out analysis confirmed stability of the strict failure estimate (range: 6.3-8.2%). Notable adverse events included two deaths among 14 jailed-lead patients in one series one from untreatable endocarditis due to lead entrapment and one sudden cardiac death in a pacemaker-dependent patient and a separate case of MRSA endocarditis with a non-extractable lead. Conclusions: Jailed transvenous leads after TTVR carry a pooled strict failure rate of 6% over short-term follow-up, substantially exceeding the less than 2% annual failure rate observed in standard settings, with potentially catastrophic consequences given the inability to extract entrapped leads. These findings provide quantitative support for lead extraction before TTVR. Early electrophysiology involvement in TTVR planning and thorough patient counseling regarding lead management strategies prior to valve implantation remain essential.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and proportional meta-analysis of 6 studies comprising 238 patients with jailed leads; median follow-up 6 to 15 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, short-follow-up, largely registry and case-series data without a comparator arm.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis suggests jailed transvenous leads after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement fail at a rate that supports lead extraction before implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pooled strict lead failure rate was 6% (95% CI: 3-10%; I2=5.6%; prediction interval: 2-11%); pooled broad malfunction rate was 15% (95% CI: 7-24%; I2=67%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a device-specific safety question that bears directly on peri-implant planning in tricuspid replacement.
