title: Abstract 11842: Lead Malfunction After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement with Jailed Transvenous Leads: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Clinical Presentation: A 43-year-old man with atopic dermatitis presented with progressive lower extremity edema and elevated brain natriuretic peptide and troponin in the setting of rapidly rising eosinophilia, increasing from 0.9 in February 2025 to 8.6 by November 2025. Earlier transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) were unremarkable. Methods: Multimodality cardiac imaging was performed serially, including TTE, TEE, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement, to evaluate structural and functional cardiac changes over time. Imaging Findings: Repeat TTE demonstrated concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, restrictive filling, and large mural thrombi in the apices of both ventricles, contrasting with normal apical morphology in February. CMR showed left ventricular apical infiltration with a 3.0 х 1.0 cm thrombus, diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement of all apical segments and mid ventricular walls, and right ventricular trabecular hypertrophy with multiple thrombi, confirming eosinophilic myocarditis in the setting of hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES). During hospitalization he developed streptococcal bacteremia from septic superficial thrombophlebitis. TEE revealed a mobile frond-like mass attached to the left ventricular thrombus concerning for superinfection. Role of Imaging in Patient Care: Serial echocardiography documented rapid progression from normal structure to restrictive cardiomyopathy with intracardiac thrombosis, prompting anticoagulation and corticosteroid therapy. CMR provided definitive tissue characterization. TEE altered management by identifying possible infected thrombus, leading to prolonged intravenous antibiotic therapy. Discussion: This case demonstrates the fulminant evolution of cardiac involvement in HES and highlights the critical role of multimodality imaging in detecting restrictive physiology, ventricular thrombi, and superimposed infection, enabling timely life-saving therapy.
title: Abstract 11851: Eosinophilic Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Biventricular Apical Thrombus and Infective Endocarditis

abstract: Background: Ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is inherent to donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation and remains a major contributor to primary graft dysfunction. Regenerative cell-based therapies exert much of their benefit through paracrine signaling rather than cellular engraftment. We investigated whether administration of a stromal adipose-derived secretome which contains growth factors, antiapoptotic factors and anti-inflammatory factors could attenuate IRI in murine DCD transplanted hearts. Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (4-6 weeks) were anesthetized with ketamine/xylazine and mechanically ventilated. Following carotid artery cannulation, systemic heparin was given, and vecuronium was administered for neuromuscular blockade. Five minutes later, ventilatory support was withdrawn to initiate the DCD process. After 25 minutes of in vivo warm ischemia, a thoracotomy was performed, and the aorta was clamped distal to the innominate artery.In the treatment group, 1 mL of secretome mixed with 9 mL of University of Wisconsin (UW) cardioplegia solution was administered via the carotid artery cannula. Untreated DCD hearts received 10 mL of UW solution alone. Continuous beating-heart donation (CBD) hearts without ischemia, receiving UW solution only at procurement, served as controls. Hearts were procured and stored in cold UW solution prior to heterotopic abdominal transplantation. Recipient rats were anesthetized with 2-3% isoflurane, and donor hearts transplanted heterotopically in the abdomen by anastomosing aorta to the aorta and pulmonary artery to the inferior vena cava. After 24 hours, graft function was assessed using a balloon-tipped catheter placed in the left ventricle to measure developed pressure, rate pressure product, positive and negative dP/dt. Hearts were then procured for histologic evaluation and infarct size analysis. Results: Left ventricular developed pressure in untreated DCD hearts was 63 mmHg compared with 153 mmHg in CBD control hearts (p< 0.001). Secretome-treated DCD hearts demonstrated improved developed pressure (132 mmHg) compared with untreated DCD hearts (63 mmHg) (p< 0.01). Infarct size was 34% in untreated DCD hearts versus 7% in CBD controls (p< 0.05) and was reduced to 18% (p< 0.05) in secretome-treated DCD hearts. Conclusions: DCD hearts exhibit significant ischemia-reperfusion injury following transplantation. Administration of a paracrine secretome at the time of donor heart procurement appears to mitigate functional impairment and myocardial injury. Further studies in larger animal models are warranted to evaluate the translational potential of this strategy for DCD heart transplantation.
title: Abstract 11906: Paracrine Modulation of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in a Murine DCD Heart Transplant Model

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a major cause of stroke and cardiovascular mortality. Although oral anticoagulation remains the standard strategy for stroke prevention, long-term treatment may be limited by bleeding risk, contraindications, and adherence challenges. Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative approach, but randomized evidence remains mixed. Research Question: Does percutaneous LAAC provide comparable efficacy and safety to oral anticoagulation in patients with AF? Methods: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing percutaneous LAAC with oral anticoagulation in adults with AF. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were systematically searched. Bayesian random-effects models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) and posterior probabilities of benefit (OR <1.00) or harm (OR >1.00). Results: Six randomized controlled trials and one pooled analysis comprising 7,004 patients were included. For the primary composite outcome, LAAC demonstrated an OR of 0.83 (95% CrI 0.58-1.16), corresponding to an 88.72% posterior probability of benefit. No clear differences were observed for all-cause mortality (OR 0.90; 95% CrI 0.69-1.18) or cardiovascular mortality (OR 0.94; 95% CrI 0.65-1.33). Major bleeding favored LAAC (OR 0.87; 95% CrI 0.67-1.14), with an 85.86% probability of benefit. Stroke outcomes remained uncertain (OR 1.06; 95% CrI 0.73-1.54), with a 63.35% posterior probability of harm. Conclusions: In patients with AF, LAAC demonstrated a high probability of benefit for composite clinical outcomes and major bleeding, while mortality outcomes were comparable to oral anticoagulation. However, uncertainty regarding stroke risk persists, supporting a selective and individualized approach to patient selection.
title: Abstract 11947: Left Atrial Appendage Closure vs Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Contemporary Bayesian Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the standard strategy for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF), but long-term anticoagulation may be unsuitable for some patients because of bleeding risk or intolerance. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative approach; however, comparative data between LAAC and DOACs remain limited. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis incorporating recently reported randomized trial data to compare clinical outcomes between LAAC and DOAC therapy. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and major cardiovascular meeting databases were systematically searched for studies comparing LAAC with DOACs in patients with non-valvular AF. Randomized and observational studies reporting clinical outcomes of interest were included. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), clinically relevant bleeding, stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), systemic embolism, and cardiovascular death. Results: Nineteen studies, including five randomized trials and fourteen observational cohorts, comprising more than 25,000 patient-years of follow-up were analyzed. Compared with DOAC therapy, LAAC was associated with lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.56-0.79; p<0.0001), reduced MACE (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.57-0.94; p=0.01), and lower clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65-0.83; p<0.0001). Rates of stroke/TIA (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.83-1.12; p=0.63), systemic embolism (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.77-1.17; p=0.62), and cardiovascular death (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.69-1.17; p=0.43) were similar between groups. In randomized-trial-only analyses, reductions in mortality and bleeding were attenuated and no longer statistically significant. Conclusions: Among patients with non-valvular AF, LAAC was associated with lower all-cause mortality, MACE, and clinically relevant bleeding compared with DOAC therapy, while maintaining similar protection against stroke, systemic embolism, and cardiovascular death. The attenuation of benefit in randomized-trial analyses suggests that residual confounding may contribute to observed differences and highlights the need for additional adequately powered randomized studies.
title: Abstract 11954: Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is traditionally planned with angiography, yet angiographic stenosis severity may not reflect lesion-specific ischemia. Fractional flow reserve (FFR), including invasive and angiography-derived approaches, may improve conduit selection and reduce unnecessary grafting. We evaluated whether FFR-guided CABG improves short- and long-term clinical and procedural outcomes compared with angiography-guided CABG, with prespecified subgroup analyses by study design, surgical procedure, and follow-up duration. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis compared FFR-guided versus angiography-guided CABG in patients with coronary artery disease undergoing isolated CABG or CABG with concomitant valve surgery. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for nonrandomized studies; certainty was assessed with GRADE. Results: Nine studies were included. Across outcomes, pooled sample sizes ranged from 524 to 2072 patients. Compared with angiography guidance, FFR guidance was associated with lower rates of major adverse cardiac events (MACE; 193/920 [21.0%] vs 304/1152 [26.4%]; RR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71-0.97) and myocardial infarction (28/920 [3.0%] vs 64/1152 [5.6%]; RR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.34-0.80). There were no statistically significant differences in all-cause death (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.67-1.02), repeat revascularization (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.81-1.40), target revascularization (RR, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.67-2.00), or stroke (RR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.94-2.59). FFR guidance was associated with shorter hospital length of stay (MD, -1.02 days; 95% CI, -1.50 to -0.55), fewer grafts (MD, -0.63; 95% CI, -0.93 to -0.33), fewer anastomoses (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -0.47 to -0.01), shorter aortic clamp time (MD, -4.97 minutes; 95% CI, -9.57 to -0.38), and shorter cardiopulmonary bypass/perfusion time (MD, -12.48 minutes; 95% CI, -20.30 to -4.67). In study-design subgroups, MACE estimates remained directionally favorable in randomized trials (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.62-1.00) and nonrandomized studies (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.70-1.06). Conclusion(s): In patients undergoing CABG, FFR-guided surgical planning was associated with lower MACE and myocardial infarction and reduced procedural burden, without clear differences in mortality, repeat revascularization, target revascularization, or stroke. Larger randomized studies, particularly in patients undergoing concomitant valve surgery, are warranted to confirm long-term clinical benefit.
title: Abstract 11963: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided versus Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Skin sympathetic nerve activity (SKNA) is a noninvasive measure of sympathetic nerve activity recorded from the skin over extended periods. Because sympathetic nerve signals contain higher-frequency components than electrocardiographic signals and myopotentials, SKNA can be isolated using band-pass filtering. Increased sympathetic nerve activity has been implicated in the pathophysiology of orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension, and these hypertension phenotypes have been reported to be associated with a favorable response to renal denervation. Research Question: We hypothesized that increased SKNA is associated with increased prevalence of orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension among patients with hypertension. Methods: The current study enrolled outpatients with hypertension. SKNA was extracted from body surface electrical signals using a band-pass filter and was measured for at least 5 minutes each in the supine and standing positions. Average SKNA (aSKNA) during supine, stand, and standing-to-supine aSKNA ratio were used in the current analysis. Orthostatic blood pressure (BP) change, measured in the supine position and at 1 and 3 minutes after standing, was assessed simultaneously with SKNA measurement. Nighttime BP was measured using a wrist-type nocturnal home BP device at 2:00, 3:00, and 4:00 AM for 7 consecutive days. Orthostatic hypertension was defined as an increase in systolic BP (SBP) of ≥20 mmHg or diastolic BP of ≥10 mmHg after standing, or as standing BP ≥140/90 mmHg among participants with supine BP <140/90 mmHg. Nocturnal hypertension was defined as mean nocturnal BP ≥120/70 mmHg. Correlations between SKNA indices and BP parameters were assessed. The associations of SKNA tertiles with each hypertensive phenotype were examined using multivariable logistic regression models. Results: Among 141 patients (mean age 67.6 years; 53.9% men), orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension were 49.6% and 29.0%, respectively. The standing-to-supine aSKNA ratio was positively correlated with standing SBP (r=0.221) and nighttime home SBP (r=0.271) (Figure). In multivariable logistic regression models, compared with the first tertile of the standing-to-supine aSKNA ratio, the third tertile showed higher odds of orthostatic hypertension (adjusted OR 2.22; 95%CI 0.91 to 5.57, P=0.084) and nocturnal hypertension (adjusted OR 2.60; 95%CI 0.93 to 7.65; P=0.074). Conclusion: In the current analysis, a higher standing-to-supine aSKNA ratio tended to be associated with orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension. SKNA may serve as a noninvasive marker for identifying hypertensive phenotypes characterized by increased sympathetic nerve activity.
title: Abstract 12624: Associations of Skin Sympathetic Nerve Activity with Orthostatic Hypertension and Nocturnal Hypertension Among Japanese Outpatients with Hypertension

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is strongly associated with mortality. Studies exploring the impact of social determinants of health (SDoH) on CS outcomes are limited. We sought to examine sociodemographic factors associated with outcomes in CS. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of CS patients admitted to University of Pittsburgh Medical Center from 2019 to 2026. The study cohort included patients from cardiac and cardiothoracic intensive care units who were individually screened and confirmed to have CS without mixed shock. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Independent variables included race, type of insurance, income and area deprivation index (ADI). Covariates included age, sex, race, income, ADI, insurance type, Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stage, Elixhauser comorbidity scores and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use. Baseline characteristics were compared using t-tests or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for continuous variables and chi-squared tests for categorical variables (Table 1). Multivariable logistic regression model was used to evaluate predictors of in-hospital mortality after adjusting for covariates. Results: We identified 992 patients with CS. The mean age was 59.4 ± 14.4 years; 70.5% were male and 15.1% were Black. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that in-hospital mortality did not differ by sex, race, ADI quintiles, insurance type, income categories, Elixhauser comorbidity scores and MCS use. Age (OR: 1.02, CI: 1.00-1.04, P = 0.025) and SCAI stage E, compared with SCAI A-C (OR: 4.94, CI: 1.91-12.82, P = 0.001) were independently associated with increased odds of in-hospital mortality (Table 2). Conclusion: In a cohort of patients with CS, age and SCAI stage E were related to mortality while race, ADI, insurance and income did not have a significant association.
title: Abstract 13289: Impact of Social Determinants of Health on Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Human genome-wide association studies have implicated ADAMTSL4 as a putative susceptibility locus for spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD). Although biallelic ADAMTSL4 variants cause ectopia lentis via impaired fibrillin microfibril assembly, the vascular consequences of heterozygous ADAMTSL4 deficiency remain unknown. Methods: We sequenced the ADAMTSL4 gene in 568 SCAD cases in the Canadian SCAD registry and 1123 healthy controls from the Michigan Genomics Initiative and conducted gene-burden association testing. Following an ADAMTSL4 molecular interaction network analysis, in vitro functional analysis experiments focused on the effects of lysyl oxidase (LOX) abundance and activity following ADAMTSL4 -knockdown in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (CASMC). In vivo studies were performed to assess arterial integrity in a murine model of Adamtsl4 deficiency. Results: Rare coding variants in ADAMTSL4 that were predicted to be deleterious were enriched in SCAD cases compared to healthy controls (OR=2.4[Cl:1.1-5.5],P=0.018) and compared to gnomAD non-Finnish European individuals N=56,885 (OR=5.0[Cl:2.8-8.2,P=9.4x10 -6 ). In vitro , LOX protein abundance and activity were reduced 24% and 26%, respectively (Fig. 1). Adamtsl4 tvrm267/+ / Adamtsl4 tvrm267/tvrm267 aortas exhibited reduced stiffness and failure strength in ex vivo biomechanical testing (Fig. 2A). Following angiotensin II infusion, Adamtsl4 deficiency was associated with decreased elastin thickness and tortuosity, with increased elastin fragmentation (Fig. 2B). Angiotensin II exposure also resulted in excess aortic ruptures and persistent non-ruptured dissections in mutant mice (Fig. 2C). Conclusions: These findings define ADAMTSL4 as a critical regulator of arterial extracellular matrix integrity. Genetic deficiency impairs LOX activity, promotes matrix-mediated biomechanical arterial fragility, and increases susceptibility to arterial dissection, providing a mechanistic link between ADAMTSL4 -associated genetic risk and vascular disease.

abstract: Background: Infants listed for heart transplantation are at highest risk for waitlist mortality despite advances in allocation policy and mechanical circulatory support. The impact of the 2016 United Network for Organ Sharing pediatric heart allocation revision on diagnosis-specific outcomes in infants has not been well characterized. Methods: Using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients, we identified children younger than 2 years listed for primary heart transplantation between October 11, 2008, and August 31, 2023. Patients were categorized by diagnosis as congenital heart disease (CHD), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), or hypertrophic/restrictive cardiomyopathy (H/RCM). Outcomes were compared between pre-policy and post-policy eras. The primary outcome was waitlist death or removal for clinical deterioration, with transplantation treated as a competing event. Multivariable cause-specific hazards models were used to evaluate associations between diagnosis and outcomes. Results: The cohort included 3,699 infants: 2,345 (63%) with CHD, 1,189 (32%) with DCM, and 165 (4.5%) with H/RCM. In the post-policy era, infants with CHD and H/RCM had a significantly higher cumulative incidence of waitlist mortality or clinical deterioration compared with DCM (p<0.0001). After adjustment for demographic and clinical covariates, CHD (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.9-3.4; p<0.0001) and H/RCM (aHR 3.4, 95% CI 2.0-5.6; p<0.0001) remained independently associated with increased waitlist mortality risk relative to DCM. Likelihood of transplantation did not differ significantly across diagnosis groups. Ventricular assist device utilization increased significantly over time across all diagnoses (p<0.0001), with the greatest increase observed among patients with DCM (4% to 49%). Ventricular assist device support was associated with a higher likelihood of transplantation (aHR 1.2, 95% CI 1.04-1.5; p=0.014) without increased waitlist mortality risk. In contrast, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (aHR 2.5, 95% CI 1.9-3.3; p<0.0001) and mechanical ventilation (aHR 1.9 (95% CI 1.5-2.4; p<0.0001) were associated with increased waitlist mortality. Conclusions: Significant diagnosis-related disparities in waitlist outcomes persist among infants listed for heart transplantation despite the 2016 pediatric allocation policy revision. Infants with CHD and H/RCM remain at substantially increased risk of waitlist mortality compared with those with DCM. Expansion of durable mechanical circulatory support strategies and continued refinement of pediatric allocation policy may improve outcomes for these high-risk populations.
title: Abstract 13325: Impact of the 2016 UNOS Pediatric Heart Allocation Policy on Waitlist Mortality and Mechanical Support Use in Infants

abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) models may improve early detection of occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI), but non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) often evolves dynamically. Whether serial ECG acquisition adds value beyond the initial AI-ECG risk estimate remains uncertain. Purpose: To evaluate the incremental value of serial ECGs in NSTE-ACS by characterizing longitudinal AI-ECG risk patterns and determining whether trajectory-based features improve OMI prediction compared with the initial ECG alone. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of patients with NSTE-ACS admitted from 2019-2023 at a U.S. tertiary academic medical center. Serial 12-lead ECGs obtained from presentation through 72 hours of hospitalization were linked to the American College of Cardiology Chest Pain Registry. A multimodal fusion AI-ECG algorithm generated OMI probabilities for each ECG. Probabilities were aggregated into 6-hour windows to construct longitudinal risk trajectories. Trajectory features captured central tendency, variability, temporal change, cumulative risk burden, and timing of peak probability. Logistic regression models compared the initial ECG probability alone with a serial trajectory model incorporating longitudinal features. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), likelihood ratio testing, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and DeLong testing. Uncertainty was estimated using 1,000 bootstrap-refit resamples. Results: Among 829 patients with NSTE-ACS, mean age was 66±12 years and 68.6% were male. Most patients underwent serial ECG testing (82.0%), with a median of 3 ECGs per patient (IQR 2-5). Compared with the initial ECG probability alone, the serial trajectory model significantly improved OMI discrimination (AUC 0.693, 95% CI 0.666-0.748 vs. 0.593, 95% CI 0.545-0.641; DeLong p<0.001). The absolute AUC increase was 0.100 (95% CI 0.070-0.164). Continuous NRI was 0.488 (95% CI 0.369-0.696), reflecting improved classification among both OMI events (event NRI 0.285, 95% CI 0.130-0.429) and non-events (non-event NRI 0.203, 95% CI 0.133-0.362). Conclusion: In patients with NSTE-ACS, serial ECG-derived AI-ECG trajectories provided significant incremental value beyond the initial ECG probability alone. Longitudinal features of ECG risk dynamics improved discrimination and reclassification for OMI, supporting continued use of serial ECGs even in the AI-ECG era. These findings suggest that integrating temporal ECG information with AI-based diagnostics may enhance risk stratification in NSTE-ACS.
title: Abstract 13347: Serial AI-ECGs Are Clinically Useful in NSTE-ACS

abstract: Background: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) often lacks diagnostic ST-segment elevation on the initial ECG, requiring repeat ECGs to identify evolving ischemia. Machine learning models may improve detection of occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI), but their performance in NSTE-ACS and the incremental value of serial ECG data remain unclear. Purpose: To compare three models for predicting OMI in patients with NSTE-ACS and to evaluate whether additional ECGs improve diagnostic performance compared with the initial ECG alone. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with NSTE-ACS admitted from 2019-2023 at a U.S. tertiary academic medical center. Serial 10-second, 12-lead ECGs obtained from presentation through the first 72 hours of hospitalization were linked to the American College of Cardiology Chest Pain Registry. OMI was defined based on stenosis. Three models—a convolutional neural network (CNN), random forest (RF), and multimodal fusion model—were applied to each ECG to generate OMI probabilities. Model performance was evaluated using the initial ECG alone and serial ECG data, summarized as the maximum predicted probability across 6-hour intervals during the 72-hour window. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). AUCs were compared using DeLong’s test, and AUPRC differences were assessed using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Results: The cohort included 829 patients with NSTE-ACS (mean age 66±12 years; 68.6% male; 87.4% White), of whom 21.6% had OMI. Most patients (82.0%) underwent serial ECG testing, with a median of 3 ECGs per patient (IQR 2-5). Among patients with repeat ECGs, 50.6% (344/680) had new ischemic changes not present on the initial tracing, including isolated ST-segment elevation in 5.4%, ST-segment depression in 32.5%, T-wave inversion in 31.3%, and combined ST-segment/T-wave abnormalities in 0.6%. Initial ECG model performance was modest across all models (AUC range, 0.570-0.593). Incorporating serial ECG data improved discrimination for all models. Using maximum predicted probability over 72 hours, the fusion model had the highest performance (AUC 0.622; AUPRC 0.303), followed by the CNN (AUC 0.620; AUPRC 0.302) and RF model (AUC 0.614; AUPRC 0.274). Differences between models were not statistically significant for serial ECG performance (fusion vs. CNN: ΔAUC 0.002, p=0.908; fusion vs. RF: ΔAUC 0.008, p=0.730; CNN vs. RF: ΔAUC 0.006, p=0.745) or initial ECG performance. Conclusion: In patients with NSTE-ACS, serial ECG acquisition was common and frequently identified new ischemic changes. Incorporating serial ECG data improved OMI prediction across model architectures, although overall discrimination remained modest and differences between models were not statistically significant.
title: Abstract 13351: Comparing Three Different AI-ECG Models for OMI Detection in NSTEACS

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac metastases occur in fewer than 10% of all malignancies and are exceedingly rare in testicular cancer. When present, they introduce a layered clinical problem: the mass carries embolic risk, yet the patient's oncologic and surgical context may render anticoagulation dangerous or impossible. We present a case of metastatic testicular cancer with intracardiac tricuspid valve involvement and new arrhythmia, managed in the immediate post-craniotomy period under strict anticoagulation contraindication. Patient Information (De-identified): An 18-year-old male with metastatic testicular cancer, status post craniotomy for brain metastasis resection, developed new-onset premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) postoperatively. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Electrocardiogram demonstrated sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs. Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed a 3.2 x 2.6 x 2.9 cm spherical, solid mass at the lateral tricuspid annulus, without features consistent with vegetation or thrombus. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed an intracardiac mass with morphology and signal characteristics suggestive of metastatic disease rather than primary cardiac tumor or organized clot. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The mass location raised concern for tricuspid valve obstruction, right-sided thrombus, and pulmonary embolism. Anticoagulation was contraindicated due to prohibitive intracranial hemorrhage risk following recent neurosurgery. Surgical resection was deferred given metastatic disease burden and perioperative risk. Therapeutic Intervention(s): Following multidisciplinary discussion among oncology, cardiology, and neurosurgery, anticoagulation was deferred and systemic chemotherapy initiated for tumor reduction. Radiation therapy was planned concurrently. The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout hospitalization. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient was discharged in stable condition to begin outpatient chemotherapy and radiation. Cardiac surveillance was incorporated into the oncologic follow-up plan. Discussion & Synthesis: This case illustrates the therapeutic tightrope clinicians must walk when intracardiac metastasis presents in a surgically vulnerable patient. Testicular cancer rarely involves the heart and when it does, the stakes are high. Competing risks of thromboembolism from the intracardiac mass and intracranial hemorrhage from anticoagulation create a genuine therapeutic impasse. Treating the underlying malignancy became the primary harm-reduction strategy. Multidisciplinary coordination and early cardiac imaging are essential in any young oncologic patient with new arrhythmia.
title: Abstract 13353: A Delicate Balance: Intracardiac Metastasis in Testicular Cancer with Contraindication to Anticoagulation

abstract: Background: Hepatic steatosis reflects systemic metabolic dysfunction and is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. On routine cardiac CT, steatosis is conventionally defined using fixed liver attenuation thresholds. However, attenuation primarily captures average liver density and may miss early, heterogeneous, or spatially subtle hepatic fat accumulation. Research Question: To determine whether an AI-derived liver fat fraction measure (QuLF-CT) identifies discordant subclinical hepatic adiposity phenotypes associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, or revascularization) but not captured by conventional CT attenuation. Methods: QuLF-CT is a radiomic-based tool developed to quantify hepatic steatosis from partial-view liver regions captured incidentally on cardiac CT imaging and was previously validated against proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) and liver biopsy. We applied QuLF-CT to the independent prospective CLARIFY registry (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04075162), which enrolled 43,340 individuals undergoing coronary artery calcium CT screening. Median follow-up was 4.03 years (IQR 3.01-5.38). Among participants with conventionally normal hepatic attenuation (>40 HU [N=25,316; E=2,726], >50 HU [N=19,806; E=1,967], and >58 HU [N=8,439; E=725]; i.e., no steatosis by standard CT criteria), QuLF-CT positivity (>5% liver fat fraction) identified a discordant subclinical phenotype: HU-normal yet QuLF-CT-positive. This group represents individuals with early hepatic adiposity undetected by conventional thresholds. Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations with MACE. Results: Agreement between QuLF-CT and attenuation-based steatosis definitions was modest (Cohen’s κ = 0.37-0.65 across established CT attenuation thresholds), identifying a substantial discordant subgroup. Among attenuation-defined normal individuals, QuLF-CT positivity was consistently associated with increased MACE risk across all HU thresholds. Compared with HU-normal and QuLF-CT-negative individuals, HU-normal and QuLF-CT-positive participants had higher MACE risk, with hazard ratios ranging from 1.21 (95% CI 1.08-1.36) to 1.69 (95% CI 1.45-1.97) across thresholds (all p < 0.01). Among individuals with HU-normal liver attenuation (>40 HU), 29.2% were identified as QuLF-CT positive, corresponding to 8.5 additional MACE cases per 1,000 HU-normal individuals screened. Conclusion: QuLF-CT identifies a discordant subclinical hepatic adiposity phenotype among individuals classified as normal by conventional CT attenuation, revealing adiposity-related cardiovascular risk missed by fixed HU thresholds and supporting its potential role in routine risk stratification.
title: Abstract 13365: AI-Derived Liver Fat Identifies Subclinical Cardiovascular Risk Missed by Conventional CT Attenuation

abstract: Background: Leukogram-derived biomarkers have been associated with cardiovascular risk in the general population. However, no longitudinal study has yet evaluated their prognostic value in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). We investigated whether leukocyte counts and derived indices predict cardiovascular events in genetically confirmed HeFH. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed the Hipercol Brasil cohort (2010-2025), including adults with genetically confirmed HeFH and baseline leukograms. We evaluated differential leukocyte counts, as well as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII = platelets х neutrophils / lymphocytes), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI = monocytes х neutrophils / lymphocytes). The primary outcome was MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or stroke, unstable angina, or coronary revascularization. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality (ACM) and ASCVD, including MACE, carotid and peripheral arterial disease, significant aortic stenosis, and chronic coronary disease. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) per 1-SD increase, adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, BMI, prevention status, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, and lipid-lowering therapy. Results: The study included 549 participants (40% male; median age 49 [35-60] years; 76% White), of whom 74% were in primary prevention, 40% had hypertension, 16% diabetes, 37% were current/former smokers, and 82% had prior lipid-lowering therapy. Over a median follow-up of 8.1 [3.6-12.1] years, 82 participants experienced MACE (incidence 1.93/100 PY) and 106 developed ASCVD (incidence 2.59/100 PY). Those with MACE were older and more likely to be male, smokers, hypertensive, and diabetic, and had higher monocyte counts and SIRI values (all p<0.01). Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by monocyte count and SIRI tertiles showed different event-free survival for both MACE and ASCVD (log-rank p<0.05). In unadjusted analyses, monocyte count (HR 1.47, 95%CI 1.23-1.74), platelet count (HR 0.78, 95%CI 0.62-0.98) and SIRI (HR 1.38, 95%CI 1.11-1.72) were associated with MACE; after full adjustment, only monocyte count independently predicted MACE (HR 1.29, 95%CI 1.06-1.56). For ASCVD, total leukocyte (HR 1.28, 95%CI 1.04-1.57), neutrophil (HR 1.23, 95%CI 1.01-1.50), and monocyte counts (HR 1.31, 95%CI 1.10-1.55), as well as SIRI (HR 1.29, 95%CI 1.05-1.59), independently predicted risk after adjustment. No leukogram-derived marker independently predicted ACM after adjustment. Conclusions: Only monocyte count independently predicted incident MACE, whereas multiple leukocyte-derived measures were associated with ASCVD in HeFH. These findings support the prognostic value of leukocyte-derived measures in HeFH.
title: Abstract 13386: Leukogram-Derived Biomarkers and Cardiovascular Risk in Genetically Confirmed Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia

abstract: Background: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) are genetically correlated non-atherosclerotic arteriopathies that share susceptibility at the chromosome 6 PHACTR1 locus. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying this shared genetic risk remain incompletely understood. We sought to identify long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) that may contribute to shared FMD-SCAD susceptibility and evaluate their expression in patients with severe FMD. Methods: Multi-trait analysis of FMD and SCAD genome-wide association study summary statistics was performed, followed by colocalization with arterial tissue expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) to identify candidate regulatory transcripts. Candidate lncRNAs were subsequently evaluated in peripheral blood RNA-sequencing data from an independent cohort of adults with FMD (N=73) and healthy controls (N=22). Severe FMD was defined by the presence of arterial aneurysm and/or dissection. Results: Integrative genetic analyses prioritized RP1-257A7.4 , a long non-coding RNA antisense to PHACTR1 , at the shared chromosome 6 susceptibility locus. RP1-257A7.4 demonstrated arterial tissue eQTL colocalization and evidence of a shared association across FMD and SCAD. In peripheral blood RNA-seq analyses, RP1-257A7.4 expression was significantly increased 2.2-fold in individuals with severe FMD compared with controls (P adj =5.90x10 -3 ). PHACTR1 expression was similarly increased 3.1-fold in severe FMD (P adj =9.23x10 -3 ). The coordinated upregulation of RP1-257A7.4 and PHACTR1, and their positive expression correlation in severe patients (rho= 0.69, P adj =1.24x10 -9 ) supports a shared regulatory relationship at this locus. Conclusions: Integrative genetic and transcriptomic analyses implicate RP1-257A7.4 as a candidate regulatory lncRNA at the PHACTR1 susceptibility locus shared by FMD and SCAD. Differential expression of RP1-257A7.4 in patients with severe vascular manifestations supports a potential role in disease-associated vascular remodeling and provides a rationale for future functional studies of lncRNA-mediated regulation at this locus.
title:
Abstract 13392: Long Non-Coding RNA
                    RP1-257A7.4
                    is Associated with Severe Vascular Manifestations in Fibromuscular Dysplasia

abstract: Background: The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock classification is widely used for risk stratification in cardiogenic shock (CS). While individual studies have reported mortality differences between acute myocardial infarction-related CS (MI-CS) and heart failure-related CS (HF-CS), the magnitude of etiology-specific mortality differences within each baseline SCAI stage has not been pooled across studies. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify stage-specific mortality differences between MI-CS and HF-CS across baseline SCAI stages. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that baseline SCAI stage-specific mortality differs between HF-CS and MI-CS. Methods: We performed a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of observational studies reporting in-hospital mortality by both CS etiology and baseline SCAI shock stage. Studies were included if they reported both HF-CS and MI-CS mortality within the same baseline SCAI stage. Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RR) for in-hospital mortality comparing HF-CS with MI-CS within each baseline SCAI stage. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Results: Three observational registry-based studies contributed to the primary analysis. Baseline SCAI stage was associated with a stepwise increase in mortality across both etiologies. HF-CS was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality than MI-CS at baseline Stage D (pooled RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.65-0.80, I 2 =6.8%). At baseline Stage C, HF-CS showed a trend toward lower mortality (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.59-1.03, I 2 =45.1%). At baseline Stage E, the mortality difference was borderline (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.79-1.00, I 2 =14.6%). At baseline Stage B, the difference was not statistically significant (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.54-1.09, I 2 =0%). The test for subgroup differences across stages did not reach conventional statistical significance but suggested possible variation in effect size (p=0.057). Conclusions: In this pooled analysis, HF-CS was associated with lower or numerically lower in-hospital mortality than MI-CS across baseline SCAI stages, reaching statistical significance at Stage D. These findings highlight that baseline SCAI stage alone may not equally predict mortality across CS etiologies. Further studies should explore whether etiology-specific interpretation of SCAI stages improves prognostic accuracy.
title: Abstract 13422: Etiology-Specific Mortality Within Baseline SCAI Stages in Heart Failure versus Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Clinical guidelines recommend ambulatory blood pressure (BP) monitoring (ABPM) to diagnose hypertension and assess chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Hypothesis: ABPM-derived asleep systolic BP (SBP) mean and/or sleep-time relative SBP decline towards the non-dipper/riser 24-hr SBP pattern are significant markers of a study endpoint among enrollees in the Sleep-Time Blood Pressure and Chronic Kidney Disease Progression Study. The study endpoint was combined outcome of progression towards end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) or a major CVD event (CVD death, myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, heart failure, vascular surgery for peripheral artery disease, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke). Methods: At enrollment and every 3 months, office BP and 48-hour ABPM, with a sleep diary, was conducted to derive 48-hr, awake and asleep systolic and diastolic BP (SBP, DBP), and their sleep-time relative decline ([awake mean - asleep mean]/awake mean x100). Cox survival analysis modeled final office BP and ABPM parameters that preceded having a study endpoint as predictors of study endpoint. Results: The cohort was 180 adult men and women with moderate (CKD stage G3b, n= 80) to severe (CKD stage G4, n= 100) decreased glomerular filtration rate. Enrollees were elderly (mean age 70±11.1), male (66.7%), with less than high school education (60.6%) who were followed for a median of 2.31 years. Sixty-five enrollees progressed toward ESKD or had a major CVD event. Analyses supported study hypothesis. Models showed that 1 SD elevation in SBP asleep mean (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.45, 95%CI 1.17, 1.79) was associated with higher hazards of having a study endpoint, while 1 SD elevation in SBP sleep-time relative decline, indicating an increase in SBP dipping, was associated with lower hazards (HR 0.74, 95%CI 0.59, 0.93). Adjusting for SBP asleep mean, SBP 48-hr and SBP awake means were not significantly associated with study endpoint. Office SBP and DBP were not associated with study endpoint in the unadjusted nor adjusted models. Conclusion: ABPM-derived parameters were predictive of renal or CVD risk with SBP asleep mean being the most relevant. ABPM should be periodically assessed in CKD patients to capture these risk biomarkers and inform individualized therapeutic schemes. title: Abstract 13426: Office versus 48 Hour Ambulatory Derived Blood Pressure Parameters as Prospective Predictors of Cardiovascular and Renal Events in Patients with Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery perforation (CAP) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Successful management requires rapid identification and treatment of the bleeding source, however, localization may be challenging when perforations propagate or persist despite covered stent implantation. We describe a novel Balloon-Assisted Visualization (BAV) technique for localization of an active coronary perforation during complex PCI. Case Presentation: An 88-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and coronary artery disease with a chronic total occlusion (CTO) of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery presented with refractory Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III angina despite optimal medical therapy. He underwent Impella-supported PCI of a heavily calcified LAD CTO. Following sequential balloon dilatation, an Ellis type III coronary perforation developed, resulting in hypotension. Immediate balloon tamponade was performed, mechanical circulatory support was established, and a covered stent was deployed across the presumed perforation site. The patient subsequently developed pericardial tamponade requiring drainage. Despite placement of an additional covered stent, persistent contrast extravasation suggested ongoing bleeding. Diagnostic Assessment and Intervention: To localize the active bleeding source, we employed the BAV technique, consisting of sequential balloon occlusion at progressively distal coronary segments with repeat angiographic assessment of contrast extravasation. This maneuver identified persistent bleeding distal to the previously treated segment, suggesting perforation propagation. Guided by these findings, a final covered stent was deployed at the newly localized site. Outcome: Definitive closure of the perforation was achieved with restoration of TIMI 3 flow and a residual stenosis of approximately 5%. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and was transferred to the intensive care unit for post-procedural management. Discussion: CAP remains a serious complication of complex CTO PCI, and failure of covered stents may occur when perforation propagation leads to inaccurate localization of the bleeding source. This case introduces the BAV technique, a practical and reproducible method that uses sequential coronary balloon occlusion to map the site of active extravasation. BAV enabled identification of a propagated perforation and facilitated successful definitive treatment. This approach may serve as a useful adjunctive strategy when persistent bleeding remains despite apparently adequate covered stent deployment.
title: Abstract 13434: Balloon-Assisted Visualization a Novel Technique for Localization of a Propagated Coronary Perforation During Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

abstract: Introduction: The Ross procedure is an aortic valve replacement strategy for pediatric patients with congenital aortic valve disease. There is limited data on the perception of and need for subsequent reinterventions on female Ross patients as they consider pregnancy. Research Questions: This study aims to describe female Ross procedure patient outcomes and perceptions on pregnancy. Methods: We conducted a single-center study consisting of a retrospective chart review and a cross-sectional survey of adult female patients who underwent the Ross procedure before December 31 st , 2024. Patients lost to follow-up before 18 years of age were excluded. Clinical and demographic data were extracted from electronic medical records and subjects were invited to complete a REDCap questionnaire. Descriptive statistics were generated and differences were assessed by pregnancy history. Results: Retrospective chart review yielded 41 patients who underwent the Ross procedure at a median age of 11 (IQR 5, 17) years. Clinical indications included aortic stenosis (27, 66%), left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (4, 10%), and other (10, 24%). Median years between Ross and reintervention was 8.8 (IQR 7.5, 12.4). Ten patients underwent a total of 17 pregnancies at a median age of 25.2 (IQR 19.9, 27.1) years, with a median of 17.2 (IQR 8.7, 18.4) years between Ross and first pregnancy. There was no significant difference (p = 0.091) in median years between Ross and reintervention for women who underwent post-Ross pregnancy (11.3, IQR 8.8, 15.3) compared to those who did not (8.6, IQR 6.3, 10.3). Of the 26 patients who completed the survey, having children was important to 20 (77%), including all six survey patients with a history of pregnancy. Ten women (38%) reported no plans to have biological children. A total of 15 (58%) reported that their congenital heart disease (CHD) impacted their decision to get pregnant. Pregnancy concerns included passing CHD to their children (10, 67%) and “stressing their heart” (5, 33%). Reinterventions after Ross procedure were not associated with patients reporting that their CHD impacted their decision to pursue pregnancy. Conclusion: For female Ross patients, the number and frequency of post-Ross reinterventions does not impact their decision to undergo pregnancy. Patients reported a variety of concerns regarding post-Ross pregnancy including the fear of passing CHD to their children.
title: Abstract 13440: Pregnancy Perceptions and Reintervention Outcomes in Female Patients Who Underwent the Ross Procedure

abstract: Background: Previous retrospective research displayed similar safety and efficacy between 1 and 2 Perclose devices (Abbott, Abbott Park, Ill.) used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), potentially reducing associated complications and healthcare costs. We identified a lack of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Aim: To investigate the differences in postoperative health outcomes between 1 and 2 Perclose devices in an RCT. Methods: Our ongoing single-center, prospective, single vs. dual large-bore access closure TAVR (SOLO-TAVR) RCT is currently enrolling adult patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transfemoral TAVR with the CoreValve (Medtronic, Minneapolis, Minn.) using 14-French sheaths (ClinicalTrial.gov ID: NCT06871774). Participants are randomly assigned to 1 or 2 Perclose devices for pre-closing TAVR. Primary outcomes are life-threatening bleeding, major or minor bleeding without threat to life (within 24 hours post-procedure), major or minor vascular complications (within index hospitalization), and time to hemostasis (post-procedure). Secondary outcomes include the use of additional closure devices (within 24 hours post-procedure), in-hospital serious vascular complications requiring percutaneous or surgical interventions, and limb ischemia related to TAVR (30-days post-procedure). Outcomes were recorded intra-operatively, during index hospitalization, and 30 days postoperatively. Outcomes were defined according to the 2021 Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC-3) criteria. The composite endpoint was composed of all the categorical complications. We used Fisher’s exact test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test with an intent-to-treat analysis approach. Results: A total of 81 patients were enrolled successfully based on eligibility criteria from August 14, 2025, through March 16, 2026. Sample characteristics and results are shown in Table 1 and Figure 1. There was no significant difference between 1 and 2 Perclose device use when comparing the composite endpoint (p=1.00), time to hemostasis (p=0.24), and time to compression (p=0.14). Conclusion: Thus far, our study demonstrates that one Perclose device may be as safe as 2 Perclose devices for TAVR.
title: Abstract 13474: Single versus Dual Large-Bore Access Closure in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Interim Analysis of the SOLO-TAVR Trial

abstract: Background: Intravenous tirofiban, a short-acting reversible glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor, targets platelet-mediated re-thrombosis after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Despite two recent phase 3 trials substantially expanding the evidence base, no tirofiban-specific meta-analysis incorporating contemporary data exists. Methods: A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov through May 2026, comparing adjunctive intravenous tirofiban initiated within 24 hours of IVT versus placebo or standard care in adults with AIS. The primary outcome was excellent functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1 at 90 days). Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using random-effects models. A pre-specified subgroup stratified by indication, prophylactic versus response-guided, was conducted to explore heterogeneity. GRADE certainty was assigned for each outcome. Results: Seven RCTs enrolling 1,869 patients (tirofiban n=1,011; control n=858; 2016-2026) were included. Adjunctive tirofiban significantly improved mRS 0-1 at 90 days (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.11-1.37; I 2 =11%; GRADE moderate). The prophylactic subgroup, anchored by ASSET-IT 2025 and comprising three RCTs (n=1,134), demonstrated a consistent, heterogeneity-free benefit (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.35; I 2 =0%). Functional independence (mRS 0-2; 6 RCTs) was similarly improved (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.06-1.29; I 2 =46%; GRADE low). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage trended higher with tirofiban but did not reach significance (RR 1.81, 95% CI 0.66-5.00; I 2 =0%; GRADE low). Any intracranial hemorrhage did not differ (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.76-1.70; I 2 =0%; GRADE low). Mortality was equivalent between groups (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.52-1.82; I 2 =0%; GRADE low). Conclusions: Adjunctive intravenous tirofiban following IVT significantly improves excellent 90-day functional outcomes in AIS, with a consistent, heterogeneity-free effect in prophylactically treated patients and no significant increase in symptomatic hemorrhage or mortality. Driven by two adequately powered phase 3 trials, these findings support tirofiban as a clinically meaningful adjunct to IVT in noncardioembolic AIS. The sparse safety event data and predominantly Chinese evidence base necessitate geographically diverse confirmatory trials before universal adoption.
title: Abstract 13497: Adjunctive Intravenous Tirofiban After Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and end-stage kidney disease. Routine cardiac screening is widely performed in patients undergoing kidney transplant evaluation to reduce post-transplant risk and inform organ allocation decisions. Traditionally, this approach has emphasized detection of obstructive coronary disease to guide revascularization. However, contemporary evidence demonstrates limited benefit of revascularization over guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), alongside a low prevalence of actionable coronary disease. Despite this, blanket screening practices persist and contribute to delays in transplant access, increased healthcare costs, and patient burden.Hypothesis Can transitioning from routine, anatomy-based screening to a risk-based, multidisciplinary, and patient-centered evaluation model improve decision-making and reduce unnecessary testing in kidney transplant candidates? Approach: This educational initiative synthesizes evidence from randomized trials, meta-analyses, and guideline recommendations to critically evaluate current screening practices. Key gaps were identified, including variability in ischemia interpretation, overuse of downstream and invasive testing, and limited implementation of multidisciplinary team (MDT)-based decision-making. We propose a conceptual framework integrating risk-based evaluation, GDMT optimization, and MDT-guided care. Results: Evidence from ISCHEMIA-CKD trial demonstrates no significant reduction in mortality or myocardial infarction with invasive strategies compared with GDMT in stable coronary disease among CKD patients. Meta-analytic data reveal a low prevalence (~2%) of coronary anatomy meeting Class 1 indications for revascularization in asymptomatic transplant candidates. Nevertheless, current practice remains highly variable, with frequent downstream testing and limited integration of MDT-based decision-making into clinical workflows. Conclusion: Routine cardiac screening in asymptomatic transplant candidates yields low clinical value and does not improve outcomes, supporting a paradigm shift toward risk-based, individualized evaluation strategies.Clinical Implications : A multidisciplinary care model integrating transplant nephrology, cardiology, and surgical expertise is essential to guide complex decision-making and reduce practice variability. Adoption of targeted evaluation strategies alongside cardiometabolic risk optimization has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing, improve efficiency, and facilitate timely and equitable access to kidney transplantation.
title: Abstract 13502: Transforming Cardiac Evaluation in Kidney Transplant Candidates, Toward Risk-Based and Multidisciplinary Care

abstract: Background: Hemodynamic-guided strategies incorporating microaxial flow pumps have been associated with improved hemodynamics and, in some studies, clinical outcomes in acute myocardial infarction cardiogenic shock (AMICS). However, limited availability and technical complexity restrict widespread adoption. Whether a standardized approach using an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) as the initial device, with selective escalation to veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), is effective remains uncertain. Methods: As part of a national cardiogenic shock initiative at a high-volume primary PCI center, we implemented a standardized, hemodynamic-guided algorithm for AMICS. Patients in SCAI stage E or undergoing ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation received immediate VA-ECMO. All others were initially treated with IABP, with escalation to VA-ECMO guided by hemodynamic and clinical response. We analyzed prospectively collected data on 218 consecutive AMICS patients from January 2024 to December 2025. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Results: The mean age was 54±11 years; 84% presented with STEMI. At baseline, 48% were SCAI stage C and 28% stage D/E; 48% had cardiac arrest before PCI. The mean lactate was 5.4±4 mmol/L. All patients required vasoactive support, and 74% required mechanical ventilation. Hemodynamic parameters included CPO 0.57±0.21, LVEDP 29±9 mmHg, and PAPI 1.2. The median door-to-MCS time was 60 minutes.IABP alone was sufficient in 62% of patients; 16% required escalation to VA-ECMO, and the remainder received upfront VA-ECMO. Access-site bleeding occurred in 12%. In-hospital mortality was 34%, with approximately 66% of deaths due to cardiac causes.. Conclusions: In AMICS, an IABP-first, hemodynamic-guided strategy with selective escalation to VA-ECMO is feasible and yields outcomes within the range reported in contemporary reports. This approach may reduce the need for advanced mechanical circulatory support while maintaining an acceptable safety profile. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.
title: Abstract 13507: An IABP-First, Hemodynamic-Guided Strategy with Selective VA-ECMO Escalation in AMI Cardiogenic Shock: Results from the Qatar National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative

abstract: Background: Time to treatment is critical for the prognosis of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). While guidelines are clear on the timing for treatment for patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), optimal timing for invasive coronary angiography (ICA) remains undefined for non-STE-ACS. A recently updated meta-analysis of 17 RCTs found no mortality benefit of early ICA. However, these RCTs comparing early vs. delayed ICA consistently measured the timing from hospital arrival. Whether measuring ICA timing from symptom onset (representing the total ischemic time) is associated with patient outcomes remains unknown. Hypothesis: ICA timing measured from symptom onset is significantly associated with all-cause mortality among NSTE-ACS patients. Methods: Retrospective cohort study using EHR data from NSTE-ACS patients admitted in 2016-2019 to an academic medical center who underwent ICA. Symptom onset was manually extracted from clinical notes. Primary exposure was symptom onset-to-ICA time (continuous, hrs). The primary outcome was 5-year mortality. Time zero was symptom onset, and patients without recorded death were censored in February 2024. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were adjusted for age, sex, smoking, prior MI, prior PCI, prior CABG, diabetes, hypertension, BMI, creatinine, and peak pre-ICA troponin (log-transformed; assay type included as covariate). Non-linearity was assessed using restricted cubic splines (3-knots). Sensitivity analysis used a categorical cutoff of 24 hrs. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted. Results: Among 732 patients: 67% male, median age 66 years (58-74), median symptom onset-to-ICA 24 hrs (14-37), 137deaths occurred at 5 years (18.7%). In the adjusted Cox model, symptom onset-to-ICA time showed a trend toward significance for 5-year mortality (HR 1.00 per hour, 95% CI 1.00-1.00, p =0.057). Restricted cubic spline analysis (Fig. 1) demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between symptom onset-to-ICA time and 5-year mortality (overall p =0.023; non-linearity p =0.046). In the categorical sensitivity analysis, early ICA (within 24 hrs of symptom onset) was associated with significantly lower 5-year mortality than delayed ICA (log-rank p =0.049; Fig. 2). Conclusions: Symptom-onset-to-ICA time, a metric not captured in prior trials, shows a significant nonlinear association with 5-year mortality in NSTE-ACS. Early ICA within 24 hrs of ACS symptom onset was associated with improved 5-year survival. These findings suggest that total ischemic time may be a more relevant measure of ICA timing than in-hospital system delay alone, and that measuring ICA timing from hospital arrival may have underestimated the mortality benefit of early ICA.
title: Abstract 13515: Symptom Onset-to-Invasive Coronary Angiography Time and Long-Term Mortality in Non-ST-Elevation ACS

abstract: Background: The Impella 5.0/5.5 axillary microaxial pump provides durable temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock, frequently as bridge to heart transplantation (OHT) or durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD). Whether baseline left ventricular internal diastolic dimension (LVIDD) predicts disposition and bridge success is not well defined. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective analysis of 108 patients supported with Impella 5.0 (n=5) or 5.5 (n=103). Four patients presenting with acute aortic dissection were excluded, leaving 104 patients. Baseline LVIDD was stratified into three clinical ranges: <6 cm, 6-6.5 cm, and >6.5 cm. Outcomes were in-hospital death or transition to comfort care, discharge to home, and successful bridge to OHT or LVAD. Associations were assessed by chi-square testing and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and device flow index (insertion flow indexed to body surface area), with LVIDD <6 cm as the reference. Results: The cohort was predominantly male (91/104, 88%) with a median age of 61 years (IQR 55-68), median LVEF of 20% (IQR 15-25), and median LVIDD of 6.3 cm. Successful bridge to OHT/LVAD increased progressively across LVIDD ranges: 45% (14/31) at <6 cm, 59% (19/32) at 6-6.5 cm, and 71% (25/35) at >6.5 cm (chi-square p=0.096). After adjustment for age, LVEF, and device flow index, LVIDD >6.5 cm remained independently associated with higher odds of successful bridge versus LVIDD <6 cm (adjusted OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.09-14.35, p=0.037). In-hospital death rates did not differ significantly across ranges (41%, 27%, 33%; p=0.46). Neither LVEF, device flow index, nor age independently predicted death, bridge, or home discharge. Conclusions: Among patients supported with Impella 5.0/5.5, greater left ventricular dilation (LVIDD >6.5 cm) was independently associated with a nearly fourfold increase in the odds of successful bridge to transplant or durable LVAD. This effect persisted after adjustment for ejection fraction and insertion flow. LVIDD appears to mark chronic heart-failure physiology, favoring advanced-therapy candidacy rather than in-hospital survival, and may aid early identification of patients likely to reach durable destination therapy. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.
title: Abstract 13516: Left Ventricular Internal Diastolic Dimension as a Predictor of Bridge Success and Outcomes in Patients Supported with Impella 5.0/5.5

abstract: Background: Ambulatory cardiac monitoring (ACM) is widely used for the detection of arrhythmias, including atrial fibrillation, a recognized stroke risk factor. ACM typically involves extended-wear Holter monitoring for 3-7 days (EWH7) or 8-15 days (EWH15), and mobile cardiac outpatient telemetry (MCOT) for up to 30 days. Despite the frequent use of ACM, the relationship between modality and subsequent diagnostic and therapeutic outcomes remains unclear. Research Question How does therapeutic yield—defined as the rate of new arrhythmia diagnoses accompanied by a targeted intervention—compare across ACM modalities and durations? Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 100% Medicare Fee-for-Service claims (2020-2023). Cases were identified using corresponding technical ACM CPT components. Patients were included only if no arrhythmia treatment, inpatient diagnosis, or monitoring were reported in the 12 months preceding ACM initiation. We compared 6-month therapeutic yield across EWH7, EWH15, and MCOT cohorts. Therapies included implantable devices (pacemaker, ICD, CRT, LAAO), non-implantable interventions (ablation, cardioversion), and pharmacologic treatment. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and baseline clinical risk factors. Residual confounding related to patient selection and modality-specific differences may persist despite adjustment. Results: The study included 445,241 patients (median age 75 years; 61% female). Cohort distribution was EWH7: 122,819 (28%); EWH15: 179,005 (40%); and MCOT: 143,417 (32%). Overall therapeutic yield was 15.1% (67,239/445,241). By treatment type (patients could be treated with >1 type), 5.8% of the monitored population received a cardiac implant, 1.6% underwent non-implantable interventions, and 10.5% initiated pharmacologic treatment. Adjusted analyses showed that MCOT was associated with 19% higher odds of arrhythmia diagnosis accompanied by clinical intervention compared with EWH15 (OR 1.19, 95% CI [1.18-1.22], P < .001) and 39% higher odds compared with EWH7 (OR 1.39, 95% CI [1.35-1.41], P < .001). Differences were most pronounced among patients receiving a cardiac implant, for whom MCOT was associated with 25% higher odds of intervention compared with EWH15 (OR 1.25, 95% CI [1.22-1.30], P < .001) and 54% higher odds compared with EWH7 (OR 1.54, 95% CI [1.47-1.59], P < .001). Conclusion: In this analysis of national Medicare beneficiaries, longer ACM monitoring durations were associated with higher rates of actionable arrhythmia diagnoses and targeted clinical treatment. The association was most pronounced among patients who received long-term cardiac implants. These findings suggest that extended monitoring may identify additional clinically significant arrhythmias in patients who then undergo targeted therapeutic management.
title: Abstract 13522: Retrospective Comparison of Arrhythmia Diagnosis and Interventions Following Ambulatory Cardiac Monitoring in Medicare Beneficiaries

abstract: Introduction: Infarct size (IS) is a key endpoint for evaluating therapeutic efficacy in preclinical models of myocardial infarction (MI) and ischemic stroke. Current quantification approaches are typically organ-specific and rely on manual delineation, which is time-consuming and operator-dependent. While automated methods have been developed for individual organs, a generalized framework applicable across different injury models remains lacking. Methods: We analyzed two preclinical injury models. For MI, n=165 Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats (165 images) (150-300 g, 1-2 months, 69% female) underwent left coronary artery occlusion for 30 minutes followed by 3 hours of reperfusion. For ischemic stroke, n=48 SD rats (96 images) (250-350 g, 1-2 months, all male) underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion for 1 hour followed by 3 hours of reperfusion. Hearts/brains were excised, sectioned, and stained with 1% TTC to delineate infarcted (pale white) and viable (red) tissues. Manual IS was quantified by expert contouring using ImageJ (NIH, USA). A unified cross-organ deep learning pipeline was developed for automated infarct quantification. Following automated slice detection, a U-Net segmentation model was used to simultaneously predict infarcted and total tissue areas across both heart and brain images. Ground truth (GT) masks were generated from expert annotations. The U-Net model was trained using n=133 MI rats and n=38 stroke rats. We further tested the model on a blinded set of n=32 MI rats and n=10 stroke rats. Model’s performance was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (Dice score) and agreement with manual IS measurements. Results: The proposed cross-organ U-Net model achieved high segmentation accuracy on the combined heart and brain blind test data, with a Dice score of 0.96 (Figures 1 and 2). Automated infarct size measurements showed strong agreement with expert manual quantification from TTC-stained heart and brain slices (R 2 =0.98, P<0.0001, blind test, Figure 3). Conclusions: We developed a cross-organ deep learning framework for automated infarct quantification that achieves robust performance across both heart and brain images. Despite substantial differences in tissue morphology and slice appearance, the framework achieved high segmentation accuracy and strong agreement with expert manual annotations. By integrating slice detection, infarct segmentation, and infarct size calculation into a fully automated workflow, this approach reduces manual analysis time, standardizes infarct assessment, improves reproducibility, and minimizes operator-dependent variability. This approach provides a robust and unbiased tool for preclinical evaluation of ischemic injury.
title: Abstract 13551: A Cross-Organ Deep Learning Segmentation Framework for Infarct Quantification in Cerebral and Cardiac Injury Models

abstract: Introduction: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is essential after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk, prompting frequent proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use. Concerns regarding PPI-mediated attenuation of clopidogrel efficacy persist, while contemporary DAPT strategies increasingly utilize ticagrelor and prasugrel. We evaluated cardiovascular and bleeding outcomes associated with PPI co-therapy in ACS patients receiving DAPT. Methods: A systematic search of various databases was performed from inception through June 2026. Randomized studies comparing DAPT with versus without proton pump inhibitors after ACS were included. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.0 Results: A total of 7 randomized controlled trials encompassing 6,708 patients with acute coronary syndrome receiving dual antiplatelet therapy were included. The pooled population had a mean age of 63.4 years, with 74% men and 26% women. Baseline rates of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, smoking, and prior myocardial infarction were comparable across treatment groups. Concomitant proton pump inhibitor therapy was not associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.69-1.10), myocardial infarction (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.75-1.14), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.24), stroke (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.34-2.02), stent thrombosis (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.72-1.75), repeat revascularization (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78-1.19), or hospitalization for unstable angina (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63-1.25). All-cause mortality was significantly lower with PPI co-therapy (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.27-0.80). PPI use substantially reduced upper gastrointestinal bleeding (RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25-0.60) and clinically significant bleeding events (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.40-0.84). Overall, heterogeneity was low and risk of bias was low across included trials. Conclusion: Among patients with acute coronary syndrome receiving dual antiplatelet therapy, concomitant proton pump inhibitor use was not associated with increased major adverse cardiovascular events or ischemic complications. PPI therapy significantly reduced gastrointestinal bleeding and all-cause mortality, supporting its cardiovascular safety and clinical benefit in appropriately selected high-risk patients.
title: Abstract 13553: Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: While ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation improves arrhythmia control in many patients, a subset experiences early adverse outcomes related to advanced heart failure despite successful ablation. Identifying these patients before the procedure may improve risk stratification and guide clinical decision-making. Objective: To develop and validate a practical clinical risk score to identify patients at increased risk of early adverse outcomes following VT ablation. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 2,489 consecutive patients undergoing VT ablation between 2005 and 2025 at a tertiary referral center. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, heart transplantation, or device shock within 3 months after ablation. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, which were weighted to create a bedside risk score. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results: Early high-risk outcomes occurred in 346 patients (13.9%). Among these, 156 patients (6.3%) died, 16 (0.6%) underwent LVAD implantation, 34 (1.4%) underwent heart transplantation, and 175 (7.0%) experienced ICD shocks within 3 months following VT ablation. Six variables independently predicted the primary endpoint and were incorporated into the risk score: prior intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) use, VT storm, intubation at presentation, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III/IV, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤25%, and prior cardiogenic shock (Table2). Weighted points generated a 0-8 score. Patients were stratified into four risk groups: low risk (score 0; n=1350), intermediate-low risk (scores 1-2; n=651), intermediate-high risk (scores 3-4; n=371), and high risk (scores 5-8; n=117). Rates of the composite endpoint and its individual components increased progressively across risk-score groups. Composite endpoint incidence rose from 6.6% in patients with a score of 0 to 49.0% in those with scores of 5-8 (AUC=0.72). Individual outcomes such as death increased from 2.2% to 31.6%, early device shock from 4.6% to 12.0%, LVAD implantation from 0% to 4.3%, and heart transplantation from 0.2% to 5.1%, one patient could have more than one outcome, hence percentages don’t add up to the combined endpoint(figure1). Conclusion: We developed a simple clinical risk score that predicts early adverse outcomes following VT ablation using readily available preprocedural clinical variables. This tool may help identify higher risk patients for counseling, procedural planning and earlier advanced HF evaluation.
title: Abstract 13561: Risk Score to Identify High Risk Patients Following Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation

abstract: Introduction: Clot-in-transit (CIT) is a mobile thrombus in the right atrium (RA) or right ventricle (RV) that carries a high risk of embolization and cardiopulmonary collapse. Approximately 4% of patients with pulmonary embolism (PE) present with free-floating CIT and is associated with a mortality rate exceeding 30%. Despite this, no established guidelines exist for a defined escalation threshold beyond anticoagulation. We present a case of a RA CIT leading to bilateral PE and RV failure, who was bridged to successful thrombectomy on venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Case: A 67-year-old man with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and atrial fibrillation (AF) presented with progressive dyspnea and acute hypoxic respiratory failure. 12-lead ECG demonstrated AF with rapid ventricular response (Fig 1). Initial laboratory studies were notable for an elevated high-sensitivity troponin-I (58 ng/L) and NT-proBNP (3155 pg/mL). He was admitted for presumed acute decompensated heart failure. Diagnostic Assessment: A TTE revealed evidence of a large, highly mobile RA mass intermittently entering the RV and crossing into the inferior vena cava (Fig 2A-C). Anticoagulation was initiated, the PE response team (PERT) was activated, and the patient was transferred to the cardiac ICU. A stat CTA chest revealed bilateral PE and multifocal RA thrombi (Fig 3A-B). Following a multidisciplinary discussion, thrombus aspiration and pulmonary thrombectomy were planned. Management & Outcome: An intraoperative TEE was performed, showing that the RA thrombus was no longer visualized with now evidence of severe RV failure; the procedure was aborted and he was cannulated for emergent VA-ECMO. The following day, successful ECMO-supported bilateral pulmonary artery thrombectomy was performed with restoration of perfusion (Fig 4A-B). He was subsequently decannulated, transitioned to oral anticoagulation, and discharged on GDMT with close follow-up. Discussion: This case offers a rare, real-time demonstration of CIT physiology and its hemodynamic consequences: a directly visualized RA thrombus that embolized on serial imaging, precipitating extensive PE and abrupt RV failure requiring ECMO stabilization as bridge to successful thrombectomy. The optimal management of CIT remains undefined, but anticoagulation alone fares the worst (mortality 28-36% vs 11-18% with reperfusion). Early PERT activation (Class 1) is paramount to guiding escalation of advanced therapies (e.g. thrombolysis and catheter-based thrombectomy). For acute PE with free-floating RA/RV CIT in ACC/AHA Categories C3-E2, advanced therapies over anticoagulation alone should be considered (Class 2a). As in our patient, VA-ECMO is reasonable (Class 2a) in instances of cardiopulmonary failure and/or persistent shock state, alongside continued anticoagulation, as a bridge to recovery and definitive treatment.
title: Abstract 13562: Gone in Transit: A Migrating Right Atrial Thrombus Leading to Right Ventricular Failure and Pulmonary Embolism Bridged with VA-ECMO to Mechanical Thrombectomy
