Bipolar voltage was acquired from seven predefined ventricular regions (21 measurements per animal per time point; n=210 paired observations). Complementary unipolar voltage mapping was performed and surface ECG leads were continuously monitored and reviewed for acute ischemic injury patterns. Systemic perfusion was maintained at systolic arterial pressure ≥80 mm Hg throughout. Linear mixed-effects modeling analyzed voltage changes from pre-VF to post-VF. Results Sustained VF (10 ± 1 minutes) was reproducibly induced and maintained with consistent hemodynamics (SAP 90 ± 5 mm Hg; ECMO flow 2.5 ± 0.5 L/min). All animals were successfully defibrillated with external biphasic shocks. High-density mapping was feasible in all experiments with stable electrograms (1000 ± 300 points per chamber). Bipolar voltage showed no statistically significant change from pre-VF (5.86 ± 2.56 mV) to post-VF (6.53 ± 2.22 mV; mean difference 0.67 mV, 95% CI [-0.31, 1.65], p=0.15). Both left (p=0.17) and right ventricular (p=0.08) chambers demonstrated voltage preservation. Regional analysis found no significant voltage changes (all p>0.05), with post-VF voltages well above viable myocardium thresholds (>1.5 mV). Unipolar voltage maps recovered toward baseline following defibrillation in all animals, and no electrocardiographic acute injury pattern was identified in any subject post-defibrillation. Conclusion Dual mechanical circulatory support with VA-ECMO and Impella CP enables reproducible, high-fidelity electroanatomic mapping and preserves myocardial electrical substrate characteristics after sustained VF in a large-animal model. This platform addresses critical technical barriers in VF research and provides a physiologically relevant, non-ischemic foundation for mechanistic substrate investigation and future translational studies.
title: Abstract 14845: Ventricular Fibrillation Mapping in a Large-Animal Model Using Dual Mechanical Circulatory Support: Electroanatomic Substrate Preservation Without Ischemic Changes

abstract: Introduction: External iliac artery endofibrosis (EIAE) affects avid cyclists who undergo repetitive hip flexion during high endurance activity. Increased mechanical stress and blood flow lead to intimal thickening and non-atherosclerotic stenosis, resulting in exercise-induced claudication. Unlike atherosclerotic peripheral artery disease, EIAE occurs in otherwise healthy athletes and is frequently missed due to its resting-asymptomatic nature, making incidental discovery during vascular imaging an unusual diagnostic pathway. Case: A 52-year-old female with hyperlipidemia and lacunar infarcts presented with recent cryptogenic stroke. Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a patent foramen ovale (PFO) with right-to-left shunting, and she underwent successful percutaneous closure. Post-procedural groin bleeding prompted abdominal aortogram with runoff to exclude dissection, fistula, and perforation. Incidentally, significant stenosis of the external iliac artery was identified. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed a minimal lumen area of 3.7 mm 2 , below the 4.0 mm 2 hemodynamic significant threshold, alongside the pathognomonic "perfect circle appearance" — circumferential intimal thickening with preserved outer wall architecture. This imaging finding is distinctly absent in atherosclerotic disease. Directed history confirmed she was a long-time avid cyclist. Discussion: Repetitive hip flexion causes arterial stretching, kinking, and elevated shear stress, driving smooth muscle proliferation and subintimal fibrosis without lipid deposition. Symptoms are classically exertional and rapidly resolve with rest, a pattern easily attributed to musculoskeletal etiology, underscoring the diagnostic challenge. Untreated, complications include thrombosis, dissection, and secondary atheroma. Management options include endarterectomy, endofibrosectomy, or endovascular stenting, selected based on lesion severity and patient activity demands. Conclusion: This case highlights the unique imaging features of EIAE, a peripheral vascular disease seen in athletes. IVUS is the modality of choice, demonstrating circumferential intimal thickening and constrictive remodeling in the absence of traditional atherosclerotic risk factors. Clinicians should maintain awareness of EIAE in physically active patients, as early recognition enables targeted intervention and return to full activity.
title: Abstract 14852: Cycling-Related External Iliac Artery Endofibrosis Uncovered During PFO Closure

abstract: Introduction: There are few interventions shown to improve outcomes in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is commonly used to treat CS despite limited evidence beyond microaxial flow pump use in patients with STEMI-CS. Nationwide contemporary data on CS and MCS outcomes across centers are not well characterized. Research Question: We aimed to characterize annual CS and MCS center volume across the U.S. and evaluate their association with in-hospital mortality. Methods: Using the Vizient® Clinical Data Base, we identified adults aged ≥18 years hospitalized with CS from 2015 to 2023. Annual CS volume was defined as the total number of CS admissions at each center per year. Annual MCS volume was defined as the number of CS admissions receiving any MCS at each center per year. Patients were categorized separately into tertiles (low, intermediate, and high-volume) or binary (low vs high volume centers) based on annual CS or MCS per center, respectively. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations between center volume and mortality were evaluated using propensity match inverse probability weighting including hospital characteristics, demographics, and comorbidities expressed as adjusted absolute risk differences in mortality. Continuous volume-mortality relationships were evaluated using restricted cubic splines. Results: We identified 497,330 hospitalizations for CS across 376 centers in the US. Most patients were categorized as SCAI C (48.7%), followed by SCAI D (26.7%) and SCAI E (16.8%). The mean age was 65.3±15.0 years, and 37.6% were female. Annual center volume was highly heterogeneous, with 65% managing <100 CS cases per year and 70% of centers performing <25 MCS cases per year. MCS on admission ranged from 3.3%, 6.6%, and 7.3% in low, middle, and high CS volume centers. Mortality was lower for high vs low volume CS centers (33.1% vs 35.1%; p<0.001) as well as for high vs low volume MCS centers (33.2 vs 37.8 %; p<0.001). After propensity matching, for annual CS volume, high-volume centers (>140 cases per year) were associated with a 2.9% absolute reduction in in-hospital mortality compared with low-volume centers (<55 cases per year) (95% CI 0.1% to 5.0%; p=0.004). High-volume MCS centers (>17 MCS per year) were associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with low-volume centers, with absolute risk reductions in in-hospital mortality of 1.5% (95% CI 0.3% to 3.8%; p=0.008). Increasing CS and MCS volumes were associated with progressively lower in-hospital mortality, with a potential threshold of ~150 MCS per year (Figure). Conclusion: In this nationally representative, contemporary cohort of patients with CS, higher institutional CS and MCS volume was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. These findings may support the development of regional CS systems of care and formalized referral centers of excellence.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective nationwide analysis of 497,330 hospitalisations for cardiogenic shock across 376 US centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with limited adjustment for shock severity and for transfer selection.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide analysis associated higher cardiogenic shock and MCS centre volumes with lower in-hospital mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: High-volume CS centres (>140 cases per year) were associated with a 2.9% absolute reduction in in-hospital mortality versus low-volume centres (95% CI 0.1% to 5.0%); high-volume MCS centres had a 1.5% reduction (95% CI 0.3% to 3.8%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports centralisation and shock-team systems of care, where natural-experiment designs are feasible.

title: Abstract 14857: Mechanical Circulatory Support and Cardiogenic Shock Center Volumes and In-Hospital Mortality: A Nationwide Real-World Analysis

abstract: BACKGROUND: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapies are increasingly used for hematologic malignancies and require complex inpatient care. However, contemporary data describing cardiovascular (CV) complications and their relationship to resource utilization remain limited. Understanding the balance between clinical risk and healthcare intensity is essential in this high-cost population. We used the 2023 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) to evaluate CV outcomes and healthcare utilization across CAR T-cell products. METHODS: Adult CAR T-cell hospitalizations across five FDA-approved products were identified in the 2023 NIS. Outcomes included mortality, major CV events, mechanical circulatory support (MCS), atrial fibrillation (AFib), length of stay (LOS), and hospital charges. AFib was assessed using both a broad definition (all I48.x) and a strict definition (new onset only). Survey-weighted multivariable models estimated adjusted LOS and charges. Propensity score matching (1:1) compared axicabtagene with tisagenlecleucel. RESULTS: Among approximately 865 weighted admissions (Figure 1), cardiogenic shock, new onset AFib, and MCS events were not identified. The composite CV endpoint occurred in 1.2% of admissions, all acute heart failure. Mortality ranged from 1% to 4.5% (Figure 1). Despite low acute CV event rates, baseline AFib was identified using broader definitions (27 cases vs 0 with strict criteria), with prevalence varying across products: lisocabtagene (23%), idecabtagene (20%), axicabtagene (15%), tisagenlecleucel (9%), and brexucabtagene (4%) (Figure 2A). LOS was prolonged across all therapies: 19.0 days (brexucabtagene), 18.4 (axicabtagene), 15.1 (lisocabtagene), 13.9 (tisagenlecleucel), and 12.9 (idecabtagene) (Figure 2B). Charges ranged from $1.42M to $2.07M (Figure 2C). Adjusted LOS was shorter for tisagenlecleucel (aRR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48-0.96) and idecabtagene (aRR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.98), with no significant differences in adjusted charges. Matched analyses showed no acute CV differences between products. CONCLUSIONS: Acute CV complications during CAR T-cell hospitalizations appear uncommon, while hospitalizations are characterized by prolonged LOS and high costs. This divergence suggests that resource utilization may be more strongly influenced by non-cardiovascular factors such as monitoring protocols and discharge complexity. Variability in AFib identification across coding definitions highlights challenges in accurately assessing arrhythmic burden in administrative data. These findings support the need for standardized CV assessment strategies and coordinated care pathways in CAR T-cell populations.
title: Abstract 14862: Silent Arrhythmias, Loud Costs: Hidden Atrial Fibrillation Burden and Minimal Cardiovascular Events in CAR-T Hospitalizations Using 2023 NIS Database

abstract: Background: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) has gained increasing adoption as a guidance modality for LAAC, yet rigorous long-term comparative data against transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) across periprocedural and clinical outcomes remain limited. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that ICE-guided LAAC achieves equivalent periprocedural safety and one-year clinical outcomes compared to TEE-guided LAAC. Methods: Using the TriNetX federated real-world network, we identified adults with AF undergoing LAAC with ICE or TEE guidance from January 2021 onward, reflecting the contemporary ICE-guided LAAC era. After propensity score matching on demographic, clinical, and pharmacologic variables, balanced cohorts of 1,536 patients per arm were analyzed. Periprocedural safety outcomes including bleeding, pericardial effusion/tamponade, device-related thrombus (DRT), and device embolization were assessed at 7 and 45 days. One-year outcomes included stroke, Thromboembolic disease, bleeding, all-cause mortality, and hospital admissions. Results: ICE was associated with lower bleeding risk at 7 days (2.1% vs 3.2%, OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38-1.19, p=0.168) and 45 days (3.0% vs 4.5%, OR 0.65, 95% CI 0.40-1.06, p=0.082), though neither reached statistical significance. Pericardial effusion/tamponade trended lower with ICE at both periprocedural timepoints without reaching significance. Device-related thrombus and device embolization were similar between groups, with the latter precluding formal comparison due to limited event counts. At one year, no significant differences were observed in thromboembolic events (3.3% vs 2.7%, OR 1.22, 95% CI 0.76-1.96, p=0.417), bleeding (4.6% vs 6.1%), or all-cause mortality (HR 1.26, 95% CI 0.92-1.73, p=0.496). Hospital admissions were higher in the ICE group (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.04-1.80, p=0.026). Conclusion: ICE-guided LAAC demonstrated comparable periprocedural safety and one-year clinical outcomes to TEE guidance, supporting its feasibility as an alternative imaging modality for LAAC
title: Abstract 14870: Periprocedural Safety and One Year Outcomes of Intracardiac versus Transesophageal Echocardiography Guided Left Atrial Appendage Closure

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery aneurysms are uncommon and may be discovered during evaluation of chest pain. Their clinical significance depends not only on size and anatomy, but also on whether they impair myocardial perfusion. We report a rare case of a large left main (LM) coronary aneurysm causing inducible ischemia. Case: A 49-year-old woman with hyperlipidemia presented with episodic chest pressure, palpitations, neck tightness, and arm discomfort. Electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with right bundle branch block, and troponin was normal. Exercise stress echocardiography was equivocal, showing 2 mm inferior and inferolateral ST depression without stress induced wall motion abnormality. Transthoracic echocardiogram showed preserved left ventricular systolic function with left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) showed calcium score 0 and a 39 x 39 x 34 mm partially calcified thrombosed aneurysm in the expected left atrial appendage location, supplied by a small left coronary artery, with a normal dominant right coronary artery (RCA). Coronary angiography showed the LM artery terminating into a large aneurysmal mass without antegrade flow into the left anterior descending (LAD) or left circumflex (LCx). Both territories filled retrograde from RCA collaterals. Stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) showed moderate inducible ischemia in the anterior, anteroseptal, anterolateral, and distal lateral walls, without infarction or scar. After specialized evaluation, she underwent elective LM aneurysm repair with saphenous vein grafting to the intraaneurysmal LAD ostium and LCx. At follow up, she had returned to work and cardiac rehabilitation with resolution of her symptoms. Discussion: The decision for elective repair was not driven by refractory symptoms or aneurysm enlargement alone. Her symptoms improved with antianginal therapy, and surveillance CCTA showed stable aneurysm size at 6 months follow up. However, angiography demonstrated absent antegrade left coronary flow with LAD and LCx perfusion dependent on RCA collaterals, while stress CMR showed viable myocardium with inducible ischemia in the left coronary territory. In a young active patient, this combination suggested persistent ischemic vulnerability despite clinical stability. Multidisciplinary evaluation therefore favored surgical reconstruction to exclude the aneurysm and restore direct perfusion to the left coronary territory. Conclusion: Giant coronary aneurysms with unusual coronary anatomy require careful multimodality assessment. In this case, integrated CCTA, angiography, and stress CMR clarified the clinical significance of a rare LM aneurysm and guided successful complex surgical repair with favorable early recovery.
title: Abstract 14875: When Collaterals Are Not Enough: Left Main Coronary Aneurysm with Inducible Ischemia

abstract: Background: Cocaine-associated acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is associated with heightened platelet activation, coronary vasospasm, and a prothrombotic state that may differ from traditional ACS. Whether more potent P2Y12 inhibition with ticagrelor provides incremental benefit over clopidogrel in this unique population remains uncertain. We compared cardiovascular and bleeding outcomes among patients with cocaine-associated ACS treated with clopidogrel or ticagrelor. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified adults with cocaine-associated ACS treated with clopidogrel or ticagrelor. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, and prior cardiovascular disease. Outcomes were assessed from 1 to 180 days following the index ACS event. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or coronary revascularization. Secondary outcomes included individual MACE components and major bleeding. Results: After propensity matching, 1,664 patients were included in each cohort. Clopidogrel was associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with ticagrelor (58.4% vs 67.0%; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.72-0.85; p<0.001). Acute myocardial infarction occurred less frequently among clopidogrel-treated patients (50.2% vs 61.0%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.68-0.81; p<0.001). Rates of all-cause mortality were similar between groups (6.2% vs 6.7%; HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.71-1.22; p=0.60). No significant differences were observed in ischemic stroke or major bleeding. Kaplan-Meier analyses demonstrated sustained separation in favor of clopidogrel for MACE and recurrent myocardial infarction throughout follow-up. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched analysis of patients with cocaine-associated ACS, clopidogrel was associated with lower MACE and recurrent myocardial infarction without an increase in major bleeding compared with ticagrelor. These findings challenge the assumption that more potent platelet inhibition necessarily improves outcomes in cocaine-associated ACS and warrant prospective validation.
title: Abstract 14880: Clopidogrel versus Ticagrelor in Cocaine-Associated Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Propensity-Matched Real-World Analysis

abstract: Background: Post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect (VSD) is a rare, catastrophic mechanical complication. Its recognition is challenging in late-presenting ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), where confounding hemodynamic data can be misattributed to isolated ventricular failure. Case Presentation: A 71-year-old male with diabetes and hypertension presented with one week of fatigue, dyspnea, and vague back pain, presented to the emergency department in cardiogenic shock (systolic blood pressure ~60 mmHg). ECG showed inferior STEMI. Emergent coronary angiography revealed a subtotal distal right coronary occlusion and elevated filling pressures (left ventricular end-diastolic pressure 30). Due to persistent shock and concerns for right heart involvement, a right heart catheterization (RHC) was also performed. Hemodynamics revealed a stark paradox: markedly elevated filling pressures (right atrial pressure 25-28 mmHg, pulmonary artery wedge pressure 30 mmHg, V-wave 40 mmHg), which coexisted with a supranormal cardiac output (11.3 L/min) by Fick’s equation and pulmonary artery oxygen saturation (SvO 2 ) of 84%. This pattern, inconsistent with isolated left ventricular failure, pointed towards a left-to-right intracardiac shunt. Intraprocedural echocardiography confirmed a postinfarction VSD. An intra-aortic balloon pump was placed for stabilization, and PCI was deferred, given the late presentation. Echocardiogram revealed an initial VSD of 2.4 cm during systole and 1.4 cm in diastole with a left-to-right shunt. LVEF remained preserved at 65-70%. Cardiothoracic surgery was taken on board, support was escalated to VA ECMO for persistent shock, and an emergent VSD repair was deferred until scar stabilization. The VSD stabilized at 3.3 cm on repeat echocardiography and was successfully repaired with a bovine pericardial patch eight days after admission. Postoperative echocardiography following weaning of cardiac support revealed an LVEF of 50-55%, with no VSD leak. Discussion and Conclusion: In cardiogenic shock, the coexistence of a supranormal cardiac output and elevated pulmonary artery oxygen saturation is diagnostic of a left-to-right shunt rather than a reassuring hemodynamic state. This paradox is the telltale signature of a post-infarction VSD masquerading behind falsely favorable indices. Early RHC in hemodynamically unstable, late-presenting STEMI patients is critical for prompt diagnosis, targeted mechanical support, and surgical survival. Subacute repair of a post-infarct ventricular septal defect/rupture (PIVSD) should be considered if adequate support is available for better scar anchorage.
title: Abstract 14882: The Hemodynamic Paradox: Supranormal Cardiac Indices Masking Ventricular Septal Defect in Late-Presenting STEMI

abstract: Background: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are detected in 18-43% of infective endocarditis (IE) cases, most commonly as anti-proteinase-3 (PR3) antibodies. This immunologic phenomenon creates a dangerous diagnostic pitfall: misattribution to ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) can prompt immunosuppression in the setting of active infection, a potentially fatal error. We present a case of enterococcal IE with positive anti-PR3 antibodies following urologic surgery, initially raising suspicion for AAV, ultimately complicated by severe native valve destruction, heart failure, and septic emboli. Case: A 70-year-old male with history of prostate cancer, status post holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), presented with five months of persistent gross hematuria and symptomatic anemia. Workup revealed positive anti-PR3 antibodies, prompting initial concern for AAV, concurrent with Enterococcus urinary tract infection and intermittent fevers. Progressive dyspnea, a new diastolic murmur, and lower-extremity edema shifted clinical focus toward a cardiovascular etiology. Blood cultures confirmed Enterococcus species. Echocardiography demonstrated aortic valve vegetation with moderate-to-severe regurgitation, preserved LVEF (65%), and elevated filling pressures. CT imaging excluded mycotic aneurysm but revealed multiple splenic abscesses from septic emboli. The patient underwent image-guided abscess drainage and combination antimicrobial therapy with ceftriaxone and ampicillin-sulbactam, achieving sustained culture clearance. He is currently undergoing hemodynamic optimization for definitive aortic valve replacement. Discussion: The heart team faced a patient caught between a failing valve and an uncontrolled infection. Operating too early risked seeding a new prosthesis, waiting too long risked irreversible hemodynamic collapse. Recognizing the anti-PR3 as infection-driven rather than primary vasculitis avoided a catastrophic pivot to immunosuppression. Coordinated source control, culture clearance, and careful timing of surgery defined the path forward. Conclusions: ANCA positivity with fever, new valvular regurgitation, or recent genitourinary instrumentation mandates aggressive IE exclusion before considering primary vasculitis. Urologic procedures including HoLEP represent underrecognized portals for enterococcal bacteremia and subsequent endocarditis in elderly males. Multidisciplinary collaboration integrating cardiology, surgery, infectious disease, and interventional radiology is essential for managing the complex interplay of valvular destruction, embolic complications, and infection eradication in high-acuity IE.
title: Abstract 14886: A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: ANCA-Positive Enterococcal Infective Endocarditis Masquerading as Vasculitis Following Holmium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate. A Case Report

abstract: Background New-onset left bundle branch block (LBBB) is the most frequently observed conduction disturbance following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, its long-term clinical and functional implications remain incompletely characterized. We performed a contemporary systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the association of post-TAVR LBBB with mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, ventricular function, and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). Methods A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was performed from inception through June 2026 according to PRISMA guidelines. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Randomized, registry-based, and observational studies comparing outcomes after TAVR in patients with and without new-onset LBBB were included. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular mortality, HF hospitalization or readmission, PPI, and change in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) from baseline to 1 year following TAVR. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled risk ratios (RR) and mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Results Eighteen studies comprising 162,622 patients were included: 28,857 with new-onset LBBB and 133,765 without LBBB. New-onset LBBB was associated with higher 1-year all-cause mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.16-1.48; P<0.00001; I 2 =42%) and cardiovascular mortality (RR 1.48, 95% CI 1.23-1.78; P<0.0001; I 2 =26%). Patients with LBBB had a higher risk of HF hospitalization or readmission (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.19-1.24; P<0.00001; I 2 =0%). The strongest observed association was with PPI, with a more than twofold increase in risk among patients who developed LBBB (RR 2.28, 95% CI 1.67-3.11; P<0.00001). Although baseline LVEF was comparable between groups (MD –1.62%, 95% CI –3.76 to 0.52; P=0.14), patients with LBBB demonstrated a greater decline in LVEF at 1 year (MD –3.12%, 95% CI –4.37 to –1.88; P<0.00001; I 2 =40%), consistent with adverse ventricular remodeling and impaired functional recovery following TAVR. Conclusions New-onset LBBB after TAVR is associated with a distinct high-risk clinical profile characterized by increased mortality, greater HF burden, progressive ventricular dysfunction, and substantially higher rates of pacemaker implantation. These findings suggest that conduction system injury following TAVR may carry clinical consequences that extend beyond the periprocedural period. These findings emphasize the need to develop techniques and TAVR designs that minimize conduction system injury.
title: Abstract 14907: New-Onset Left Bundle Branch Block After TAVR Is Associated with Increased Mortality, Heart Failure Burden, and Progressive Ventricular Dysfunction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 162,622 Patients

abstract: Background: Microvascular obstruction (MVO) remains a major contributor to adverse outcomes following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis was trialed to reduce residual thrombi following primary PCI in STEMI, and initial trials showed benefit. The publication of STRIVE, the largest randomized trial of intracoronary alteplase to date- with a negative result, prompted this updated meta-analysis with fibrin-specificity stratification of agents to determine whether a biological efficacy-gradient exists and whether any agent class confers meaningful clinical benefit. Methods: A meta-analysis of trials in databases searched from inception through February 2026 was performed. Eligible RCTs enrolled STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI randomized to intracoronary thrombolytic versus placebo/standard care. Trials were classified a priori as non-fibrin-specific (streptokinase, urokinase), moderately specific (prourokinase), or highly specific (alteplase, tenecteplase). Subgroup interaction was tested by chi-square test across strata. Results: Sixteen RCTs enrolling 2,598 patients met inclusion criteria. A statistically significant subgroup interaction for composite MACE was identified (χ 2 =8.08, df=2, P=0.018), proving the hypothesized efficacy-specificity gradient. Composite MACE was reduced in the non-fibrin-specific (OR 0.36; 95% CI 0.17-0.79; P=0.010) and moderately fibrin-specific tiers (OR 0.56; 95% CI 0.38-0.81; P=0.002), with no effect in the highly fibrin-specific tier (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.70-1.61; P=0.77). No individual clinical endpoint (cardiovascular mortality, reinfarction, or heart failure hospitalization) reached statistical significance in any tier, including those where composite MACE was reduced. This dissociation reflects substantial heterogeneity in MACE definitions, obscuring the true efficacy of these agents. TIMI 3 flow and MBG grade 3 significantly favored intracoronary thrombolysis in the moderately fibrin-specific tier (OR 2.46 and 2.36; both P<0.001), with a significant interaction for impaired myocardial perfusion across tiers (χ 2 =14.97, P=0.0006). In the highly fibrin-specific tier, absent MACE benefit was concordant with absent angiographic benefit across all measures. Conclusions: Adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis confers no individually significant clinical benefit across any fibrin-specificity tier, and composite MACE reductions in less fibrin-specific tiers are not supported by individual endpoints. IC alteplase demonstrates no benefit on any clinical or angiographic measure and should be considered a closed avenue for investigation. Future trials should prioritize moderately fibrin-specific agents and incorporate cardiac MRI endpoints to directly judge microvascular injury.
title: Abstract 14912: Exploring the Role of Adjunctive Intracoronary Thrombolysis During Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction with High Clot Burden: A Meta-Analysis of Clinical and Angiographic Outcomes in Randomized Controlled Clinical Trials

abstract: Background: Current patch materials for mitral valve repair often suffer from structural degeneration, chronic inflammation, and calcification, particularly in younger patients. A novel, partially resorbable hybrid bioscaffold (HBS) has demonstrated favorable biological performance in vascular and early cardiac applications, presenting a promising candidate for advanced mitral valve reconstruction. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that implantation of HBS or a structurally modified HBS (MOD) in a juvenile porcine mitral valve model would achieve preserved valve function with minimal calcification and a limited inflammatory response at mid-term follow-up. Methods: In a preclinical porcine model, surgical patch augmentation of the A2 segment of the anterior mitral leaflet was performed using either HBS or MOD. Animals underwent postoperative surveillance for 6 months. Valve function was serially assessed via echocardiography. Explanted valves were evaluated macroscopically, histologically, and via micro-computed tomography μCT) to quantify tissue integration, inflammation, and calcification. Results: In total, 8 animals were enrolled; 4 (50%) survived to the planned 6-month endpoint (median follow-up: 181 days). Echocardiography demonstrated preserved mitral valve competence, with all surviving animals exhibiting none-to-trivial regurgitation despite rapid somatic growth, which entailed a ~ 60% increase in annular diameter. Macroscopic assessment confirmed well-integrated, completely endothelialized patches without structural failure. Histological analysis revealed a mild inflammatory response confined strictly to the suture sites. Minimal calcium deposition was observed in the specimens (4/4), with μCT detecting only minor generalized calcification alongside micro-focal deposits. Animals that died before the endpoint demonstrated partial re-endothelialization and limited inflammation, consistent with an active, ongoing healing process. Conclusions: In this challenging juvenile porcine model, hybrid synthetic patch materials successfully maintained mitral valve competence, demonstrated excellent tissue integration, and exhibited minimal calcification at mid-term follow-up. These findings strongly support the therapeutic potential of hybrid bioscaffold-based mitral valve reconstruction and warrant further evaluation in larger, comparative preclinical studies.
title: Abstract 14926: A New Synthetic Bioscaffold for Mitral Valve Repair: Achieving Excellent Valve Function and Biocompatibility - A Chronic Porcine Study

abstract: Introduction: Type 2 Myocardial infarction (T2MI) occurs due to myocardial oxygen supply-demand mismatch without acute atherothrombotic plaque rupture. T2MI is a heterogeneous condition which can be caused by acute non atherothrombotic coronary artery disease or other non coronary illnesses, and must be distinguished from nonischemic myocardial injury. Research Questions: Among adults hospitalized with T2MI in the 2022-2023 National Inpatient Sample, what are the contemporary national rates of coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and what factors are associated with receipt of coronary angiography? Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the 2022-2023 National Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalizations with T2MI (ICD-10-CM I21.A1) were identified; coronary angiography and PCI were defined by ICD-10-PCS codes. Survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, primary payer, Charlson comorbidity index, and hospital characteristics identified factors independently associated with angiography. Discharge weights generated national estimates. Results: Among 234,282 hospitalizations with T2MI (weighted average annual national estimate, 585,705; 95% CI, 566,234-605,176), 9.9% (95% CI, 9.6-10.2%) underwent coronary angiography and 1.25% (95% CI, 1.20-1.31%) underwent PCI; PCI occurred in 12.5% (95% CI, 12.0-13.0%) of those evaluated invasively. Diagnostic angiography without revascularization occurred in 8.6% (95% CI, 8.4-8.9%) and any revascularization in 1.53% (95% CI, 1.46-1.60%). Angiography increased from 9.4% (95% CI, 9.1-9.8%) in 2022 to 10.3% (95% CI, 9.9-10.7%) in 2023. In multivariable analysis, independent predictors of angiography included younger age (adjusted OR, 0.985 per year; 95% CI, 0.984-0.986), lower Charlson comorbidity index (aOR, 0.899 per point; 95% CI, 0.892-0.905), private insurance versus Medicare (aOR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.34-1.48), large versus small hospital size (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.34-1.55), urban teaching versus rural location (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.28-1.61), and 2023 admission (aOR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.05-1.18); Medicaid versus Medicare was associated with lower odds (aOR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.84-0.93). Female sex was not independently associated with angiography (aOR, 1.03; 95% CI, 1.00-1.05; P=0.09). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality was lower among patients who underwent angiography (2.7% vs 9.1%). Conclusions: Fewer than 1 in 10 adults hospitalized with T2MI undergo coronary angiography and approximately 1 in 80 undergo PCI, reflecting predominantly noninvasive management. Invasive evaluation is strongly patterned by age, comorbidity burden, and hospital infrastructure rather than by sex, suggesting clinical and systemic determinants of access. These contemporary benchmarks underscore the need for trials defining which T2MI patients benefit from an invasive strategy.
title: Abstract 14927: Rates of Coronary Angiography and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Among Patients Hospitalized with Type 2 Myocardial Infarction: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis

abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease (CAD) carries a 30-50% recurrence rate ndwithin 6 months of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Standardised group-based discharge education fails to account for individual patient knowledge levels and risk profiles, limiting its efficacy in sustaining secondary prevention behaviours. Purpose: To evaluate whether an individual supportive nursing (ISN) programme — initiated during cardiac intensive care unit (CCU) admission and maintained over 8 weeks — improves CAD knowledge, sick-role behaviour, and self-efficacy in post-PCI patients compared with standard care. Methods: A prospective, parallel-group randomised controlled trial enrolled adults admitted to the CCU following stent implantation, randomised 1:1 to ISN (n=26) or standard care (n=24). The ISN programme comprised: (1) individualised bedside consultation during CCU stay; (2) six structured telephone follow-up calls over 4 weeks post-discharge; and (3) two face-to-face consultations at outpatient visits. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and 8 weeks using validated instruments: CAD Knowledge (32 items; α=.84), Sick-Role Behaviour (15 items; α=.78), and Self-Efficacy (16 items; α=.86). Between-group change scores were compared using independent-samples t-tests; effect sizes are reported as Cohen's d. Results: Both groups were well-matched at baseline (all p>.05). The ISN group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in CAD Knowledge (Δ=+0.20±0.11 vs +0.04±0.09; t=5.56, p<.001; d=1.59, large effect), Sick-Role Behaviour (Δ=+0.66±0.46 vs –0.04±0.52; t=5.05, p<.001; d=1.43, large effect), and Self-Efficacy change (t=–2.45, p=.018; d=0.69, medium effect). Within sick-role behaviour, significant gains were observed in dietary therapy (d=1.13), stress management (d=1.44), and weight management (d=0.79). Smoking cessation, exercise adherence, and hospital-visit/medication adherence did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion: An ISN programme initiated during CCU hospitalisation and sustained through structured multi-contact follow-up produces large, clinically meaningful improvements in CAD knowledge and sick-role behaviour, and a moderate gain in self-efficacy, in post-PCI patients. These findings support systematic integration of individualised nurse-led education into routine post-PCI care pathways. Future adequately powered, multicentre trials should examine long-term clinical outcomes.
title: Abstract 14933: Individual Supportive Nursing After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Improves Disease Knowledge, Sick Role Behavior, and Self Efficacy: A Randomized Controlled Trial

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become a widely used treatment for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis across a broad range of surgical risk groups. Common indications for permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation following TAVR are complete heart block (CHB) and left bundle branch block (LBBB) progressing to CHB. Research Questions: Among adults undergoing TAVR in the 2022-2023 Nationwide Inpatient Sample, is permanent pacemaker implantation during the index hospitalization associated with greater in-hospital clinical and economic burden? Methods: We identified adult TAVR hospitalizations in the 2022-2023 HCUP Nationwide InpatientSample (NIS) using ICD-10-PCS codes and excluded patients with a pre-existing cardiac implantable electronic device. Same-admission PPM was identified by ICD-10-PCS codes, and the TAVR-to-PPM interval was derived from procedure-day variables. Survey-weighted logistic and generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, primary payer, Charlson Comorbidity Index, hospital characteristics, and year. Results: Among an estimated 88,005 annual adult TAVR hospitalizations (unweighted n=35,202), 6.9% underwent index-hospitalization PPM (≈6,033/year). Among patients with valid timing, mean time from TAVR to PPM was 1.64 days (95% CI 1.55-1.74), and median time was 1 day. PPM occurred on the same day as TAVR in 27.2%, post-TAVR day 1 in 35.6%, day 2 in 16.5%, and day ≥3 in 20.7%. Each 1-year increase in age was associated with higher odds of PPM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.04, 95% CI 1.03-1.05), as was each 1-point increase in Charlson comorbidity index (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.05-1.12). PPM was associated with longer stay (5.5 vs 2.8 days), higher charges ($315k vs $228k), and more frequent non-home discharge (34.7% vs 17.8%; aOR 2.42) and acute kidney injury (aOR 2.01, 95% CI 1.64-2.45). PPM was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality or ischemic stroke. Complete heart block was coded in 75.6% of PPM recipients compared with 3.3% of patients without PPM, supporting its role as a major conduction diagnosis linked to pacing Conclusions: In a contemporary national cohort, approximately 1 in 14 TAVR patients received a pacemaker during the index admission. 62.8% occurred by the end of day 1, but roughly 1 in 5 occurred on or after the third post-procedure day. PPM marked a longer, costlier hospitalization and more non-home discharge without higher in-hospital mortality. The persistent day-3-and-beyond tail argues against uniformly early discharge and supports risk-stratified post-TAVR rhythm monitoring.
title: Abstract 14949: Permanent Pacemaker Implantation During Index Hospitalization After TAVR: National Rates, Timing, Predictors, and In-Hospital Outcomes in the 2022-2023 NIS

abstract: Introduction: Atrial fibrillation is a major cause of cardioembolic stroke, and oral anticoagulants (OAC) remain the cornerstone of stroke prevention. However, long-term anticoagulation is limited by bleeding risk, drug discontinuation, adherence issues, cost, and patient preference. The left atrial appendage is the major source of thrombus formation in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, making percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion/closure (LAAO/LAAC) a non-pharmacologic alternative for stroke prevention. Research Questions: In adults with atrial fibrillation requiring stroke prevention, how does percutaneous LAAO/LAAC compare with OAC for death, stroke, systemic embolism and bleeding? Methods: We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar from inception to May 20, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing percutaneous LAAC with OAC in adults (≥18 years) with AF requiring stroke prevention were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2.0. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Knapp-Hartung adjustments. Results: Six RCTs enrolling 7,004 patients (LAAC n=3,681; OAC n=3,323) were included: CLOSURE-AF, OPTION, CHAMPION-AF, PRAGUE-17, PREVAIL and PROTECT AF. Compared with OAC/medical therapy, LAAC was not associated with a statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.15; I 2 =37.6%), stroke or systemic embolism (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.85-1.42; I 2 =0.0%), overall stroke (RR 1.13, 95% CI 0.74-1.74; I 2 =10.5%), systemic embolism (RR 1.40, 95% CI 0.28-6.89; I 2 =0.0%), major bleeding (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.77-1.13; I 2 =0.0%), or hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.24-1.41; I 2 =30.5%). Ischemic stroke showed a numerically higher risk with LAAC that did not reach statistical significance (RR 1.40, 95% CI 0.97-2.00; I 2 =0.0%). Conclusion: In adults with atrial fibrillation requiring stroke prevention, LAAC showed comparable risks of all-cause mortality, stroke or systemic embolism, overall stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with OAC/medical therapy. Hemorrhagic stroke was numerically lower and ischemic stroke numerically higher with LAAC, but neither reached statistical significance. These findings support LAAC as a reasonable alternative in carefully selected patients who are unsuitable for long-term OAC.
title: Abstract 14952: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Oral Anticoagulant in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Background Structural valve degeneration (SVD) of surgical bioprosthetic aortic valves represents a growing clinical challenge. While redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo SAVR) has historically been the standard of care, it carries substantial perioperative morbidity and mortality risks. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (ViV-TAVR) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative; however, direct comparative data regarding their long-term clinical outcomes, hemodynamic performances, and safety profiles remain poorly defined. Methods A systematic search of major electronic databases was conducted from inception to May 2026 to evaluate studies comparing redo SAVR with ViV-TAVR. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using the RevMan, version 5.4, providing pooled estimates as risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Heterogeneity among studies was assessed using the I 2 statistics. Results A total of 33 studies comprising 23902 patients (12922 (ViV-TAVR);10980 redo SAVR) were analyzed. ViV-TAVI was associated with a significantly lower risk of 30-day mortality (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.47-0.66; p < 0.00001) and 1-year mortality (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.76-0.97; p = 0.01). However, long-term mortality was significantly higher in the ViV-TAVI group compared to redo-SAVR (RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.08-2.05; p = 0.02). ViV-TAVI significantly reduced the risk of stroke (RR 0.67, p = 0.03), major bleeding (RR 0.47, p < 0.00001), acute kidney injury (RR 0.47, p < 0.00001), new-onset atrial fibrillation (RR 0.37, p < 0.00001), and the need for new permanent pacemakers (RR 0.68, p = 0.004). There were no significant differences in myocardial infarction (p = 0.94), major vascular complications (p = 0.17), or re-hospitalization (p = 0.39). ViV-TAVI also resulted in a significantly shorter length of hospital stay (SMD -1.24; p < 0.00001). On the other hand, ViV-TAVI resulted in a higher mean transprosthetic gradient (SMD 0.67; p < 0.00001) and higher rates of severe patient-prosthesis mismatch (RR 1.86; p < 0.0001), paravalvular leak (RR 2.91; p < 0.00001), and a significantly higher risk of reintervention (RR 2.59; p = 0.001) as compared to redo-SAVR. Conclusion: In patients with degenerated surgical bioprosthetic aortic valves, ViV-TAVI is associated with superior short-term outcomes, including lower mortality, stroke, and perioperative complications, as well as shorter hospitalization. However, redo-SAVR appears to confer improved long-term durability with lower late mortality and reduced reintervention. These findings suggest that while ViV-TAVI offers favorable short-term clinical outcomes, redo-SAVR may provide superior long-term benefit, underscoring the importance of an individualized treatment plan.
title: Abstract 14966: Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter versus Redo Surgical Replacement of a Failing Surgical Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Tc-99m pyrophosphate (PYP) scintigraphy has transformed the noninvasive diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR), often obviating endomyocardial biopsy (EMB). However, false-positive uptake may occur in nonamyloid conditions. We describe a case of longitudinal progression from Perugini grade 0 to grade 3 uptake in a patient with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis (HD), highlighting an important diagnostic pitfall in the evaluation of suspected ATTR. Case Description: A 63-year-old woman with ESRD on hemodialysis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (EF 60-65%), hypertension, hyperphosphatemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism was evaluated for suspected cardiac amyloidosis. Two years before presentation, PYP scintigraphy performed prior to HD initiation showed Perugini grade 0 uptake. Baseline echocardiography showed moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) without infiltrative features. Over the ensuing two years, she developed recurrent intradialytic hypotension and atrial fibrillation. Echocardiography revealed severe concentric LVH with interventricular septal thickness of 1.85 cm, dynamic mid-left ventricular cavity obstruction (peak gradient 70 mmHg with Valsalva), and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. EKG showed atrial fibrillation and low-voltage QRS complexes disproportionate to LVH severity. Cardiac MRI demonstrated diffuse late gadolinium enhancement involving the mid-myocardium, epicardium, and posterior right ventricular wall. Repeat PYP scintigraphy with SPECT confirmed Perugini grade 3 uptake (Figure 1). Serum immunofixation was negative, and kappa/lambda ratio was normal. Phosphorus was 7.2 mg/dL, and PTH was 292 pg/mL. ATTR genetic testing was negative. EMB revealed cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, minimal interstitial fibrosis, and no amyloid deposition on Congo red staining (Figure 2). Subsequent mitral valve replacement for significant MR revealed valvular calcification. Discussion: The progression from a negative scan to strongly positive uptake paralleled HD initiation, metabolic derangements, and structural remodeling, suggesting that non-amyloid cardiac processes can mimic ATTR on scintigraphy (Figure 3). Hyperphosphatemia and hyperparathyroidism likely promoted myocardial calcium-phosphate deposition, while chronic mechanical stress, reflected by marked LVH, may have driven fibrosis and microcalcification, providing an additional substrate for tracer uptake. Although EMB showed no calcification, microscopic calcium-phosphate deposits below the resolution of light microscopy cannot be excluded and may account for Tc-99m PYP uptake. This case underscores the value of EMB when significant metabolic or structural confounders accompany a positive scan, thereby preventing misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.
title: Abstract 14970: From Perugini Grade 0 to Grade 3: Biopsy-Proven False-Positive Technetium-99m Pyrophosphate Uptake in End-Stage Renal Disease Following Hemodialysis Initiation

abstract: Background: Intracoronary acetylcholine (ACh) is used to assess coronary vasomotor function but there are wide variations in dosage protocols compounded by uncertainty about how to assess response. We aimed to characterize the effects of 3 common ACh administration protocols on epicardial resistance, microvascular resistance and coronary blood flow (CBF) in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries. Methods: Aortic pressure (Pa), intracoronary pressure (Pd) and CBF (derived from average peak flow velocity and cross sectional vessel area) were measured in the left anterior descending artery using a combined Doppler and pressure sensor-tipped guidewire under the following conditions: rest, ACh infusion at 18mcg.min -1 for 3 mins ( ACh INF ) and ACh 100mcg bolus over 20 seconds ( ACh 100 ). A subset of consecutive patients underwent a higher dose ACh 200mcg bolus over 20 seconds ( ACh 200 ). Epicardial resistance was defined as (Pa-Pd)/CBF and microvascular resistance as Pd/CBF. Coronary vasomotor dysfunction (CVD) was defined as a composite of ≥20% vessel caliber reduction, angina or ischemic ECG changes in response to ACh. Non-parametric data are presented as median (IQR); continuous variables are compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and binary variables using the Chi-squared test. Results: 80 patients were enrolled (60±10 years old, 58% female) with median fractional flow reserve 0.92 (0.88, 0.94). ACh 100 led to augmentation of CBF (p=0.015) and a trend towards attenuation of microvascular resistance (p=0.068) without altering epicardial resistance (p=0.585) compared to rest. No significant differences were observed between ACh INF and rest. ACh 100 led to greater augmentation of CBF (p=0.036) compared with ACh INF , but no significant differences were observed in epicardial resistance (p=0.108) or microvascular resistance (p=0.197) (Figure 1). ACh 200 increased epicardial resistance (p=0.014) without any differences in CBF (p=0.169) or microvascular resistance (p=0.332) compared with ACh 100 (Figure 2). CVD was diagnosed in 29%, 55% and 79% of patients in response to ACh INF , ACh 100 and ACh 200 , respectively (ACh INF vs ACh 100 odds ratio 3.04, 95% CI 1.73-5.33; p<0.001; ACh 100 vs ACh 200 odds ratio 3.10, 95% CI 0.95-10.12; p=0.053). Conclusions: Commonly used ACh protocols are not physiologically interchangeable. ACh 100 was associated with coronary flow augmentation without changes in epicardial resistance, whereas ACh 200 increased epicardial resistance without further augmentation of flow. This suggests that ACh 100 should be used to assess coronary endothelial function and to detect underlying epicardial spasm with a high specificity, whereas ACh 200 should be reserved for detection of epicardial spasm where sensitivity is prioritized over specificity.
title: Abstract 14972: The Physiological Basis of Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing with Acetylcholine

abstract: Atrial fibrillation affects approximately 60 million people globally and is associated with a 2-fold increase in cardiovascular mortality. EAST-AFNET 4 showed that early rhythm control reduces major adverse cardiovascular events by 21% compared with rate control, but nearly one in five patients in that trial's rhythm control arm underwent catheter ablation. Whether antiarrhythmic drugs alone confer independent outcome benefit remains unresolved. We sought to quantify the pharmacologic component of this effect in isolation.We performed a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies comparing antiarrhythmic drug-based early rhythm control, without ablation, versus rate control in atrial fibrillation diagnosed within one year. Primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, or acute coronary syndrome. A random-effects model with REML estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment was fitted. Where multiple publications from the same national registry database were identified, the largest non-overlapping cohort per distinct analytic population was retained to avoid double-counting of patients.After applying the registry overlap exclusion rule, 2 studies were retained: Kim et al. (Annals of Internal Medicine 2022; KNHIS general cohort, N=54,216) and Kim et al. (JACEP 2022; KNHIS EAST-AFNET 4-eligible cohort, N=31,220). Three additional Korean NHIS publications were excluded as overlapping subsets of these same two cohorts. Pharmacologic-only early rhythm control reduced the primary composite outcome versus rate control (HR 0.85 [95% CI 0.79-0.92]; P=0.023). Between-study heterogeneity was absent (I 2 =0%; Q=0.08, P=0.78). With k=2, a prediction interval was not estimated.Antiarrhythmic drugs alone, without any procedural rhythm control component, reduce composite cardiovascular outcomes in recently diagnosed atrial fibrillation. After restricting the analysis to non-overlapping Korean NHIS cohorts, the direction and significance of benefit are preserved (HR 0.85; P=0.023). These data isolate the pharmacologic contribution from ablation in the EAST-AFNET 4 framework and confirm that drug-first rhythm control carries independent prognostic value. The two-study evidence base limits definitive conclusions and reinforces the case for a dedicated non-Korean external replication dataset.
title: Abstract 14975: Drug-Based Early Rhythm Control versus Rate Control in Recently Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: Isolating the Pharmacologic Effect

abstract: Background: Fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography angiography (FFR-CT) is a promising tool to non-invasively assess the hemodynamic severity of coronary lesions. However, real-world uptake and accessibility in the US are not well-characterized Research Question: How often is FFR-CT performed in the US, where is it performed, and how accessible is it? Methods: Using 2024 data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Part B datasets, we quantified, as a proportion of computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA), the adoption of FFR-CT as well as provider-level and state-level variability in FFR-CT adoption. Additionally, we assessed geographical proximity to centers with FFR-CT capabilities in the US. CTCA was identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 75574 and FFR-CT was identified using CPT code 75580. Data on the provider-level utilization of FFR-CT as a percentage of CTA was limited to providers with ≥11 CTCA and CT-FFRs. Results: From 210,289 CTCAs performed in the US in 2024 for Medicare beneficiaries, a total of 29,270 FFR-CT procedures were performed (13.9%). Out of 7,480 providers reading CTCA, 2,421 (32.4%) performed FFR-CT. Provider-level FFR-CT adoption as a % of CTCA varied widely (IQR among providers performing ≥11 CTCA and CT-FFRs: 19.7% to 44.9%), with 18.3% using FFR-CT in >50% of CTA reads. States with the highest adoption of FFR-CT (as % of CTA) included West Virginia (428 FFR-CT out of 1,211 CTCA; 35.3%), Delaware (199 FFR-CT out of 653 CTCA; 30.5%), and North Carolina (1,559 FFR-CT out of 6,082 CTCAs). The weighted-median distance to the nearest FFR-CT-capable facility (with ≥11 FFR-CT procedures in 2024) was 23.3km, with 52.7 million persons in the US (16%) living >100km away from the nearest facility. Conclusion: Nationwide adoption of FFR-CT shows considerable provider-level and state-level heterogeneity, with one-third of those performing CTCA additionally performing FFR. Large swathes of the US have minimal access to FFR-CT-capable facilities.
title: Abstract 15009: Regional Heterogeneity and Provider-Level Variability in Adoption of Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve

abstract: Background: Microaxial flow pump (mAFP) support is increasingly used as mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock. However, its high rotational speed and direct blood exposure to the impeller may increase hemolysis and subsequent acute kidney injury (AKI). Plasma free hemoglobin (PFHb) measurement enables quantitative assessment of hemolysis during mAFP support. However, the determinants of PFHb burden and its association with AKI requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT) remain unclear. Objective: We aimed to determine the associations of pump intensity and right ventricular function with PFHb burden and AKI requiring RRT in patients receiving mAFP support. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 239 patients who received Impella CP support from July 2019 to May 2026. After excluding 3 patients without PFHb measurements and 19 receiving chronic hemodialysis, 217 patients were included. PFHb was measured twice daily during mAFP support. PFHb burden was assessed using trapezoidal PFHb area under the curve (AUC) during Days 1-7 and log-transformed for regression analyses. Peak PFHb was defined as the maximum value during Days 1-7. Pump intensity was assessed by cumulative P-level. Right ventricular function was assessed using pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). The outcome was AKI requiring RRT. Models were adjusted for age, baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate, initial lactate, and concomitant VA-ECMO. Exploratory analyses evaluated net volume balance, vasoactive-inotropic score, and RBC transfusion volume. Results: AKI requiring RRT occurred in 51 patients (23.5%). Patients with AKI requiring RRT had higher PFHb AUC and peak PFHb than those without RRT (PFHb AUC, 0.42 [0.24-0.71] vs 0.18 [0.10-0.32] g/dL-day; peak PFHb, 0.12 [0.08-0.25] vs 0.06 [0.05-0.13] g/dL; both P<0.001). In adjusted models, greater cumulative P-level exposure and lower minimum PAPi were both associated with higher PFHb AUC (P=0.025 and P=0.034, respectively). Patients with AKI requiring RRT had greater positive net volume balance and higher RBC transfusion volume. Positive net volume balance was associated with higher PFHb AUC, whereas RBC transfusion volume was not independently associated with PFHb AUC after adjustment, suggesting severity-related confounding. Vasoactive-inotropic score showed no consistent association. Log-transformed PFHb AUC was strongly associated with AKI requiring RRT (odds ratio per doubling, 2.47; 95% CI, 1.68-3.62; P<0.001). Conclusions: During mAFP support, greater cumulative pump intensity and impaired right ventricular function were associated with higher PFHb burden. PFHb AUC was strongly associated with AKI requiring RRT, suggesting that cumulative hemolysis exposure may represent a clinically relevant pathway linking pump management, right ventricular function, and AKI during mAFP support.

title: Abstract 15015: Plasma Free Hemoglobin Burden and Acute Kidney Injury During Microaxial Flow Pump Support: Associations with Pump Intensity and Right Ventricular Function

abstract: Background: Prasugrel is preferred over ticagrelor after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), a position reinforced by a recent network meta-analysis of 15 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) reporting fewer major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with prasugrel. Its applicability to diabetes remains unresolved: in the ISAR-REACT 5 trial, the prasugrel advantage was restricted to patients without diabetes (significant treatment-by-diabetes interaction), and no prior meta-analysis has pooled all the available contemporary RCTs in diabetes. Hypothesis: Prasugrel’s ischemic advantage in the overall PCI population is absent in patients with diabetes, in whom ticagrelor and prasugrel confer comparable ischemic and bleeding outcomes. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane through May 2026 and identified three RCTs comparing prasugrel with ticagrelor in patients with diabetes undergoing PCI. These included the prespecified diabetic substudy of ISAR-REACT 5, the diabetic stratum of PRAGUE-18, and TUXEDO-2, the first trial restricted to diabetes. Endpoints, assessed at 12 months, were the ischemic composite of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (MACE) and major bleeding (BARC types 3-5). Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models with prediction intervals; heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and robustness was evaluated with leave-one-out analysis. Results: Among 2,942 patients with diabetes (1,488 ticagrelor, 1,454 prasugrel), MACE did not differ between agents (pooled HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.78-1.33; P =.90; I 2 =0%) and was unchanged on leave-one-out analysis. Major bleeding (BARC 3-5) was numerically higher with ticagrelor but nonsignificant (pooled HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.93-1.81; P =.12; I 2 =0%). Conclusions: Consistent with our hypothesis, ticagrelor and prasugrel were comparable for ischemic events in patients with diabetes undergoing PCI, with no significant difference in major bleeding. The prasugrel advantage evident in the overall population does not extend to diabetes, where antiplatelet selection may instead be governed by bleeding risk, tolerability, and cost.
title: Abstract 15025: Ticagrelor versus Prasugrel in Patients with Diabetes Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Randomized trials of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) have consistently shown improvements in tricuspid regurgitation severity, symptoms, and health status, whereas early analyses of death or first heart-failure hospitalization (HFH) have shown limited clinical-event separation. Severe tricuspid regurgitation represents a chronic right-sided heart-failure phenotype, therefore treatment effects may emerge over longer follow-up period. Objectives: To evaluate whether T-TEER may reduce longer-term recurrent HFH burden and to quantify the probability of clinically meaningful benefit using Bayesian sparse-trial synthesis. Methods: We performed an aggregate-data meta-analysis of randomized T-TEER trials reporting longer-term recurrent HFH outcomes. The primary estimate was the treatment-to-control recurrent HFH effect ratio, synthesizing randomized trial-reported recurrent-event rate ratios or hazard ratios on the log scale. Random-effects synthesis incorporated a skeptical Bayesian normal prior centered at no effect [log(RR)=0, SD=0.35]. Absolute recurrent-HFH reductions were calculated per 100 patient-years and used to estimate the number of patients requiring treatment over 2 years to prevent one HFH event. Given that post-1-year crossover may attenuate intention-to-treat estimates, a prespecified mixture-based crossover-contamination sensitivity analysis was applied. Results: Two randomized T-TEER datasets contributed longer-term recurrent-HFH evidence. TRILUMINATE Pivotal reported recurrent HFH rates of 0.19 versus 0.26 events/patient-year with T-TEER + OMT versus OMT (optimal medical therapy), corresponding to a joint frailty hazard ratio of 0.72. TRI.FR extended follow-up, with no crossover and prespecified recurrent-event analysis, reported 37 versus 64 total HFH events for T-TEER + OMT versus OMT, with a rate ratio of 0.52. The pooled recurrent-HFH effect favored T-TEER (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.87). The mean absolute reduction was 7.1 fewer HFH events per 100 patient-years, corresponding to approximately 7 patients requiring T-TEER + OMT rather than OMT alone over 2 years to prevent one HFH event. Bayesian analysis yielded a posterior median RR of 0.69, 95% credible interval 0.53-0.91, with posterior probabilities of 99.5% for any benefit, 84.7% for at least 20% reduction, and 52.9% for at least 30% reduction. Crossover-contamination sensitivity shifted the TRILUMINATE recurrent-HFH RR from 0.73 toward approximately 0.66 under plausible assumptions. Conclusions: Longer randomized follow-up suggests that the clinical benefit of T-TEER emerges over time and is recurrent-event based, as shown by reduced HFH burden rather than early separation in mortality or first-event endpoints. Recurrent HFH burden and crossover-aware estimates should be prioritized in future tricuspid intervention trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Aggregate-data Bayesian meta-analysis of 2 randomised T-TEER datasets (TRILUMINATE Pivotal and TRI.FR) with recurrent-event outcomes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials contribute, with crossover contamination and a sceptical prior that drive the estimate.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled randomised data suggest tricuspid TEER reduces recurrent heart failure hospitalisation over longer follow-up.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The pooled recurrent-HFH effect favoured T-TEER (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.87); Bayesian posterior median RR 0.69, 95% credible interval 0.53-0.91.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the case for tricuspid TEER on a hard-adjacent endpoint and the evidence base available for guideline update.

title: Abstract 15047: Delayed Clinical Benefit After Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Recurrent-Event, Crossover-Sensitive Bayesian Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Advances in mapping and ablation approaches have improved the safety and efficacy of catheter-based ablation (CA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF) historically have poor ablation outcomes; however, they are underrepresented in contemporary reports and modern outcomes are poorly defined. Research Question: To evaluate ablation approaches and long-term rhythm control following contemporary catheter ablation for LSPAF. Methods: A single-center, retrospective analysis of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF between 2021 and 2025 was performed. Demographic and procedural characteristics were analyzed; one-year arrhythmia free survival and atrial arrhythmia (AA) burden were assessed. Results: One hundred and six patients were included (median age was 68 years (IQR 63-74), male 79%, BMI 32[92.0-35.37], ejection fraction 55[46-60] %, prior CA 43%) and followed for 18.6[10.2-28.8] months. Ablation modality included radiofrequency n=86(81%), pulsed field ablation n=13(12%), or both n=7(7%). All patients underwent pulmonary vein isolation, 99(94%) underwent additional ablation (including linear ablation n=99(94%), posterior wall isolation n=87(82%), vein of Marshall ethanol infusion n=30(28%), coronary sinus ablation n=30(28%), and cavotricuspid isthmus n=25(24%). Major complications included stroke n=2, major bleeding n=2, cardiogenic shock n=1, and air-embolism n=1. Nineteen patients remained on anti-arrhythmic at follow up. Among patients undergoing a first time ablation (n=57), one year arrhythmia free survival was 39.3% (95% CI 27.8-55.4%). Allowing for multiple procedures, one-year arrhythmia free survival was 52.0% (95% CI 42.2-64.1%). Among patients with continuous monitoring, median arrhythmia burden decreased from 90.1%[37.5-98.5%) to 0.0%[0.0-3.3%) at 6 months and 0.0%[0.0-10.0%) at 12 months. Conclusion: Among a contemporary cohort of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF, one year-arrhythmia free survival was attained in 52% of patients; among patients with implanted cardiac devices, AA burden was markedly reduced (arrhythmia burden 0.0%[0.0-10.0%) and may better reflect procedural efficacy.
title: Abstract 15059: Contemporary Outcomes of Catheter Ablation of Long-Standing Persistent Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Background: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is a revascularization strategy for patients with high-risk spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), particularly those with left main or multivessel SCAD; failed percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); or hemodynamic instability. However, contemporary data on early procedural outcomes, graft patency, and long-term clinical outcomes remain limited. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of Mayo Clinic SCAD Registry patients who underwent CABG for acute SCAD between 1996 and 2020. Baseline clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, procedural details, graft characteristics, and outcomes were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as death, recurrent SCAD, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke/transient ischemic attack, or repeat revascularization. Results: This cohort included 72 patients treated with CABG for acute SCAD. Mean age was 42±9 years, and 97% were women. Upon presentation, 68% had STEMI, 31% had NSTEMI; and 26% had cardiac arrest/ventricular arrhythmia. Left main SCAD was present in 35%, and multivessel SCAD in 46%. CABG was emergent in 99% and performed after failed PCI in 40%. Mechanical circulatory support was required in 54%. A total of 142/143 grafts were successfully performed as planned. Left internal mammary artery grafts were used in 53 patients (76%), and saphenous vein grafts were used in 54 patients (76%), while radial artery and right internal mammary artery grafts were infrequent (1.4% each). On-pump CABG was performed in 74%. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass time and mean aortic cross-clamp time were 75±37 and 56±21 minutes, respectively. Thirty-day postoperative complications occurred in 40%, including bleeding requiring re-exploration, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe left ventricular dysfunction. Angiography after CABG in 21 (29%) patients showed with graft occlusion in 9/21 (42.9%) at median time of 4 years (IQR 2.4-7.3). Causes of graft failure included competitive native LAD flow after vessel healing (most frequent in 88%), thrombotic occlusion, and graft obstruction. The estimated 5-year MACE rate was 32%. Conclusions: CABG remains an important revascularization strategy for high-risk SCAD, achieving high procedural success, but also high risk of early complications. Long-term graft patency is limited, and patients have a notable risk of future MACE. These findings provide one of the largest contemporary assessments of CABG outcomes in SCAD and support the need for careful surveillance following surgical revascularization.
title: Abstract 15067: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Acute Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: Procedural Success, Graft Patency, and Long-Term Outcomes

abstract: Background: Alzheimer disease (AD) and other nonvascular neurodegenerative dementias represent a growing global health burden. Increasing evidence links cardiovascular and metabolic dysfunction to cognitive decline, suggesting that therapies targeting vascular risk may influence neurodegenerative outcomes. Statins, widely used in cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, may confer neuroprotective effects beyond lipid lowering; however, their association with dementia risk in patients with established CVD remains uncertain. Objective: To examine the association between statin therapy and the risk of all-cause dementia and AD among adults with known CVD. Methodology: Design, Setting, and Participants: This observational cohort study used data from the PITTHeart-Brain Registry curated using a multihospital electronic health record (EHR) review. Adults with coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) within the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center health system between 2010 and 2020 were included. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were extracted from the electronic health record. Exposures: Statin therapy categorized by intensity (high-intensity, moderate/low-intensity, or no statin therapy). Main Outcomes and Measures: Incidence of all-causeand ADdementia, defined using ICD-9/ICD-10codesand AD-specific pharmacologic therapywas assessed. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusting fortraditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Results: Among 47,210 patients (33,822 [71.6%] PCI; 13,388 [28.4%] CABG), female sex was independently associated with higher dementia risk (HR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.13-1.39;P< .001). Increasing age, diabetes, hypertension, anemia, elevatedB-type natriuretic peptide, and greater comorbidity burden were independently associated with dementia incidence. Statin use demonstrated a graded protective association: moderate/low-intensity statins (HR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.64-0.91) and high-intensity statins (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.45-0.64) were associated with significantly lower risk of dementia compared with no statin therapy. Similar associations were observed for AD. Interaction analyses suggested that the excess dementia risk among women was most pronounced at lower HDL-C levels. Conclusions and Relevance: In patients with established CAD, statin therapy-particularly high-intensity treatment-was associated withsubstantially lowerrisk of incident dementia and AD, supporting a potential neuroprotective effect beyond lipid lowering.
title: Abstract 15072: Impact of Statin Therapy on Dementia Risk Following Coronary Revascularization: A Multi-Hospital Heart-Brain Registry

abstract: Background: Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS) is a common, often clinically silent perioperative complication associated with mortality. Although ECG foundation models have emerged, they were developed mainly from diagnostic 12-lead ECGs, leaving their applicability to continuous intraoperative single-lead monitoring unclear. Whether such embeddings improve MINS prediction beyond clinical variables, and whether full-surgery modeling outperforms brief ECG snapshots, remains unknown. Methods: We retrospectively studied adults undergoing intra-abdominal or intrathoracic non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia lasting >1 h at a tertiary center from 2016 to 2021. The primary outcome was MINS, defined as postoperative cardiac troponin elevation within 3 days. Intraoperative lead-II ECG was encoded with a 1-lead variant of ECGFounder, producing a 1,024-dimensional embedding for each 10-second segment. We compared snapshot embeddings from early and late 10-minute surgical windows modeled by linear probe, and full-surgery embeddings modeled by a bidirectional Simplified State-Space (S5) sequence model. Each strategy was fused with 16 clinical variables spanning demographics, preoperative laboratory values, ASA classification, surgical context, comorbidities, and intraoperative transfusion. Models were evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Pairwise differences in AUROC and AUPRC were estimated using paired bootstrap with 2,000 replicates. Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, and expected calibration error (ECE). Results: Among 2,966 surgical cases (2,807 patients), 14.7% developed MINS. Adding intraoperative ECG embeddings to clinical variables improved prediction compared with clinical variables alone. The full-surgery S5 plus clinical model achieved an AUROC of 0.778 (95% CI, 0.754-0.802) and an AUPRC of 0.448 (95% CI, 0.405-0.492), compared with 0.758 and 0.367 for the clinical-only model (∆ AUROC, +0.020; p=0.049; ∆ AUPRC, +0.081; p<0.001). The snapshot plus clinical model showed similar discrimination to the S5 plus clinical model, with an AUROC of 0.778 and an AUPRC of 0.432 (versus S5: ∆ AUROC 0.000; ∆ AUPRC, +0.016; both not significant). Calibration was better with the snapshot plus clinical model than with the S5 plus clinical model, with lower Brier score (0.104 vs. 0.128), calibration slope closer to 1 (0.92 vs. 1.89), and lower ECE (0.017 vs. 0.146). Conclusions: Intraoperative ECG foundation-model embeddings fused with clinical variables significantly improved MINS prediction over clinical variables alone. Full-surgery temporal modeling did not outperform snapshot embeddings from early and late operative windows, suggesting that change between induction and emergence ECG captures the prognostic signal.
title: Abstract 15103: Foundation-Model Embeddings of Intraoperative Electrocardiogram for Prediction of Myocardial Injury After Non-Cardiac Surgery

abstract: Introduction: Despite advances in preventive cardiology, acute coronary syndrome frequently occurs in individuals without prior cardiovascular events and remains inadequately predicted by conventional clinical risk factors. Current risk assessment models fail to capture underlying plaque vulnerability. Accurate identification of high risk coronary plaque phenotypes before clinical rupture remains a major unmet need in cardiovascular medicine. Methods: We conducted a global multicenter retrospective study of 60,000 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography across 12 international centers. PHOENIX AI, a multimodal foundation model, integrated automated deep learning-derived plaque phenotypes, clinical variables, and inflammatory biomarkers. The model was developed in 45,012 patients and externally validated in 14,988 patients. Results: Among 60,000 patients (mean age 62.0±10.5 years; 58.0% male), 3,026 incident acute coronary syndrome events occurred during 26.8±14.5 months of follow-up. Low attenuation plaque burden independently predicted future ACS (OR 1.16 per 1% increase; 95% CI 1.15-1.17; p<0.001), as did positive remodeling (OR 9.29; 95% CI 6.38-13.53; p<0.001), napkin ring sign (OR 3.35; 95% CI 3.05-3.67; p<0.001), hs-CRP (OR 1.06; 95% CI 1.03-1.09; p<0.001), and age (OR 1.02; 95% CI 1.02-1.03; p<0.001).
