ACS rates increased from 2.19% (95% CI 2.00-2.38) in patients without high-risk plaque features to 4.11% (95% CI 3.86-4.36), 10.46% (95% CI 9.89-11.03), and 20.29% (95% CI 18.40-22.18) in those with one, two, and three features, respectively (p-trend<0.001). In external validation, PHOENIX AI significantly outperformed the clinical model (AUROC 0.741, 95% CI 0.723-0.759 vs 0.589, 95% CI 0.567-0.611), yielding a ΔAUROC of 0.152 (95% CI 0.123-0.181). Conclusion: PHOENIX AI accurately identified vulnerable coronary plaque phenotypes and substantially improved prediction of future acute coronary syndrome beyond traditional clinical risk factors. The strong stepwise association between high-risk plaque burden and adverse outcomes, coupled with robust external validation, supports its potential role in personalized cardiovascular risk stratification and prevention.
title: Abstract 15113: PHOENIX AI: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Coronary Plaque Phenotyping and Prediction of Future Acute Coronary Syndrome Using Coronary CT Angiography, A Global Multicenter Retrospective Study

abstract: Background: Post-myocardial infarction secondary prevention requires optimization of multiple objectives: reducing major adverse cardiovascular events, minimizing bleeding, preserving quality of life and ensuring cost-effectiveness. Traditional meta-analyses assess single outcomes, failing to identify strategies that achieve optimal trade-offs. Clinicians face choices when interventions that reduce ischemic events increase bleeding risk or when effective therapies are costly. We applied Pareto frontier optimization to identify non-dominated strategies that maximize net clinical benefit across four dimensions. Methods: We conducted a systematic search of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed, identifying 248 papers. We extracted data from 22 randomized trials and meta-analyses (N=843,272 participants) covering 9 intervention categories: antiplatelet regimens, high-intensity statins, PCSK9 inhibitors, cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation, ACE inhibitors/ARNI, beta-blockers, and digital monitoring. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis was performed for each outcome domain. Pareto optimization evaluated four objectives: MACE reduction, bleeding minimization, QoL maximization (EQ-5D), and cost-effectiveness (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio). Strategies were classified as Pareto-optimal if no alternative strategy improved one objective without worsening another. Results: Five of nine strategies achieved Pareto optimality. Smoking cessation demonstrated the strongest composite performance (MACE HR=0.65 [95% CI: 0.58-0.74], bleeding HR=1.01, QoL gain=0.120, ICER=$1,302/QALY). Cardiac rehabilitation showed robust benefit (MACE HR=0.74 [0.68-0.81], QoL gain=0.084, ICER=$4,551/QALY). Genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy achieved cost-dominance (ICER=–$725/QALY) with reduced bleeding (HR=0.78 [0.61-0.98]) without MACE penalty. High-intensity statins (MACE HR=0.86 [0.75-0.98], ICER=$15,706/QALY) and digital monitoring (MACE HR=0.86 [0.75-0.97], ICER=$1,595/QALY) completed the Pareto frontier. Standard intensive antiplatelet therapy was dominated due to excess bleeding (HR=1.34 [1.05-1.71]). PCSK9 inhibitors, despite MACE reduction (HR=0.80), were cost-prohibitive (ICER=$450,000/QALY). Conclusions: Pareto analysis reveals that smoking cessation, cardiac rehabilitation, genotype-guided antiplatelet selection, high-intensity statins, and digital monitoring constitute the optimal bundle for secondary prevention, maximizing MACE reduction, safety, QoL, and cost-effectiveness. these five interventions represents an efficient approach to secondary prevention. This optimization framework provides a rigorous method to prioritize interventions that achieve superior outcomes across clinical and economic dimensions, moving beyond single-endpoint decision-making.
title: Abstract 15125: Pareto Frontier Analysis in Multi-Component Meta-Analysis: Balancing Reduction in Recurrent Events, Bleeding Risk, Quality of Life, and Cost-Effectiveness in Post-Myocardial Infarction Secondary Prevention

abstract: Background: The optimal mechanical circulatory support strategy for patients undergoing high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. Randomized trials evaluating elective intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), Impella, and standard care have reported conflicting results and have not been synthesized within a unified comparative framework. Research Question/Hypothesis: We evaluated the comparative efficacy and safety of elective IABP, Impella, and standard care in planned high-risk PCI. Methods: We systematically identified randomized controlled trials enrolling patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction undergoing planned high-risk PCI. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis compared elective IABP, Impella, and standard care. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included periprocedural myocardial injury, major bleeding, vascular complications, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and stroke. Results: Three randomized trials (BCIS-1, PROTECT II, and CHIP-BCIS3) comprising 1,053 patients formed a closed triangular evidence network. Model convergence was excellent (all R̂<1.01), with low estimated between-study heterogeneity (posterior median τ=0.346). For all-cause mortality, elective IABP demonstrated the most favorable treatment profile. Compared with standard care, IABP was associated with a 40% reduction in mortality odds (OR 0.60, 95% CrI 0.24-1.31) and an 89.7% posterior probability of benefit. This signal remained consistent across prespecified sensitivity analyses, including long-term follow-up data (OR 0.64, 95% CrI 0.29-1.30; probability of benefit 91.4%). Impella was associated with a directionally unfavorable mortality profile compared with standard care (OR 1.14, 95% CrI 0.47-2.24), with a 63.7% posterior probability of harm. Indirect comparison between Impella and IABP demonstrated an OR of 1.88 (95% CrI 0.69-5.06), with a 91.5% posterior probability that Impella was associated with higher mortality than IABP. Treatment ranking strongly favored IABP. IABP had an 85.1% probability of being the optimal strategy for survival (SUCRA 0.906), compared with 8.0% for standard care (SUCRA 0.370) and 6.9% for Impella (SUCRA 0.224). Rankings remained stable across sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were observed for secondary outcomes, although event rates were low and certainty of evidence was limited. Conclusions: Among randomized trials of mechanical circulatory support during high-risk PCI, elective IABP demonstrated the highest probability of survival benefit and consistently ranked as the preferred strategy. Impella did not demonstrate a mortality advantage and showed a directional signal toward increased mortality compared with IABP and standard care. These findings highlight the need for adequately powered head-to-head randomized trials.
title: Abstract 15126: Elective Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Ranks Highest for Survival in High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in DSP -encoded desmoplakin cause a distinct form of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) with extensive subepicardial-predominant left ventricular (LV) fibrosis, ventricular arrhythmias, and recurrent acute myocardial injury/myopericarditis. Case: A 30-year-old African American male with recurrent troponin-positive myopericarditis over 8 years presented with severe chest pain precipitated by acute emotional distress, shortly after a clinic. Cardiac troponin T rose from 8 to 4500 ng/L; C-reactive protein and leukocyte counts were normal. Electrocardiography showed diffuse ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography showed LVEF 45-50% with mild noncoronary regional wall-motion abnormalities. CT coronary angiography excluded epicardial disease; PET obtained just before presentation showed sequelae of prior myocarditis without active inflammation. Cardiac MRI demonstrated extensive new subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of anterior and inferior LV segments with mild edema and pericardial enhancement (Figure 1A). Endomyocardial biopsy and rheumatologic workup were unremarkable. Ambulatory monitoring captured sustained slow monomorphic VT during the flare (Figure 1B), with recurrent non-sustained VT on telemetry. Paternal family history included unspecified cardiomyopathy in his uncle and grandfather. Decision-making: An 83-gene cardiomyopathy panel identified a heterozygous in-frame deletion ( DSP c.3374_3376del; p.Arg1125del). It affects a highly conserved arginine within the desmoplakin nuclear localization signal, is extremely rare (1/730,841 public exomes/genomes), and is predicted to disrupt nuclear import, raising concern for pathogenicity in this clinical context. Acute therapy—corticosteroids, steroid-sparing immunosuppression (mycophenolate mofetil), and a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator—was initiated before genomic results, based on the clinical and imaging phenotype. The genetic findings supported a unifying diagnosis of desmoplakin-associated cardiomyopathy. At 1 month he remained stable with normalized troponin and preserved low-normal LVEF; cascade family screening and segregation analysis are ongoing. Conclusion: Recurrent troponin-positive myopericarditis with a subepicardial LGE pattern should prompt consideration of desmoplakin-associated cardiomyopathy. Notably, this flare was triggered by acute emotional stress rather than the exertion classically described in DSP cardiomyopathy, suggesting emotional stress may be an under-recognized precipitant of hot phases relevant to counseling. Integrating phenotype, imaging, and genomic results is critical for risk stratification and management.
title: Abstract 15136: Idiopathic Recurrent Myopericarditis and Ventricular Tachycardia in a Patient with a Rare Nuclear Localization Signal Variant in the Desmoplakin (DSP) Gene

abstract: Background: The use of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation in the management of advanced heart failure has become a cornerstone treatment option, associated with improved prognosis and quality of life. However, patients undergoing LVAD implantation are often in a physiologically precarious state, making frailty a critical yet frequently underappreciated vulnerability. We aimed to evaluate the impact of frailty on in-hospital perioperative outcomes following LVAD implantation. Methods: We analyzed LVAD procedures among adults from 2016 to 2023 using the National Inpatient Sample, excluding COVID-19 patients. Frailty was defined per the Johns Hopkins ACG criteria. Multivariable regression models were used to estimate the odds of perioperative complications and all-cause in-hospital mortality associated with frailty. Results: A total of 29,435 LVAD implantation patients were identified, of whom 11,865 (40.31%) were frail. Frail patients were older (mean age 58.64 vs 55.89 years, p<0.001) with a slightly lower Charlson Comorbidity Index score (3.70 vs 3.81, p=0.040). Both groups had comparable sex distribution, and were heavily dependent on Medicare (49.89% frail vs 46.48% non-frail) followed by private insurance. Frail patients had longer lengths of stay (46.67 vs 31.94 days, p<0.001) and higher total charges ($1,641,858 vs $1,214,223, p<0.001).Frail LVAD recipients had significantly higher odds of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, hemopericardium, cardiac tamponade, cardiogenic shock, pneumothorax/hemothorax, post-operative respiratory failure, other iatrogenic respiratory complications, prolonged mechanical ventilation, acute kidney injury, pulmonary embolism, post-hemorrhagic anemia, reopen surgery for bleeding, septicemia, aspiration pneumonia, superficial wound complications, vascular repair, and in-hospital mortality compared to non-frail patients. Myocardial infarction, acute pericarditis, pacemaker implantation, pulmonary insufficiency, respiratory arrest, venous thromboembolism, fever/device infection, sepsis, and deep wound complications did not differ significantly between groups(Table 1). Conclusions: Our findings confirm the significant impact of frailty on perioperative outcomes following LVAD implantation, with frail patients experiencing higher odds of multiple adverse events including in-hospital mortality. Pre- and periprocedural frailty risk stratification and targeted interventions to mitigate these outcomes warrant further exploration.
title: Abstract 15140: The Hidden Burden of Frailty: Unraveling Its Impact on Perioperative Complications and In-Hospital Mortality Among 29,435 Left Ventricular Assist Device Recipients

abstract: Introduction: Saphenous vein grafts (SVGs) remain widely used in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), yet graft failure requiring percutaneous coronary intervention is frequently reported. Despite contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) use, clinical outcomes remain suboptimal, and the mechanisms of stent failure remain incompletely understood. Methods: From the CVPath stent registry (n=814 patients, 1344 stents), we analyzed 46 stents from 38 patients with stented SVG, excluding lesions <30 days. Lesions were categorized as second-generation DES (2nd-DES, n=12 lesions), first-generation DES (1st-DES, n=17 lesions), or bare metal stents (BMS, n=17 lesions). Results: Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups, and stent duration was not significantly different between groups (median [interquartile range (IQR)], 2nd-DES 2.8 [1.7-3.9] years vs. 1st-DES 2.0 [1.0-2.8] years vs. BMS 2.8 [1.4-3.0] years, p =0.226). Maximum % area stenosis was lowest in 2nd-DES lesions (median [IQR], 2nd-DES 20 [10-50] % vs. 1st-DES 50 [30-100] % vs. BMS 100 [35-100] %, p =0.047). The prevalence of in-stent restenosis was lowest in 2nd-DES lesions (2nd-DES 2/12 [17%] vs. 1st-DES 8/17 [47%] vs. BMS 11/17 [65%], p =0.038, Figure panel A ). The prevalence of CTO was also lowest in 2nd-DES lesions (2nd-DES 1/12 [8%] vs. 1st-DES 5/17 [29%] vs. BMS 9/17 [53%], p =0.039). In contrast, no significant differences were observed in the prevalence of stent thrombosis (2nd-DES 2/12 [17%] vs. 1st-DES 3/17 [18%] vs. BMS 1/17 [6%] vs, p =0.507). Stent fracture was most prevalent in 1st-DES lesions (1st-DES 12/17 [71%] vs. 2nd-DES 2/12 [17%] vs. BMS 2/17 [12%], p =0.025). Importantly, neoatherosclerosis was most prevalent in 1st-DES lesions (1st-DES 12/17 [71%] vs. 2nd-DES 6/12 [50%] vs. BMS 4/17 [24%], p =0.023, Figure panel B ). Conclusions: 2nd-DES in SVG lesions demonstrated improved luminal patency and lower prevalence of restenosis and CTO compared with BMS and 1st-DES. However, neoatherosclerosis remains frequent, suggesting persistent adverse vascular responses despite contemporary DES technology.
title: Abstract 15146: Vascular Response to Second-Generation Drug-Eluting Stents in Saphenous Vein Grafts

abstract: Introduction: The myocardial contraction fraction (MCF) is a novel, dimensionless measure that normalizes the stroke volume to a unit of myocardium. It has become particularly appealing for predicting survival across different subtypes of heart failure, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, cardiac amyloid, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. However, the prevalence and prognostic value of depressed MCF across the spectrum of severe low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG AS) remains unknown. Research Question: This study aimed to assess whether a specific subtype of LFLG AS is more associated with depressed MCF and whether there is any prognostic value of MCF in predicting post-TAVR mortality outcomes across both subtypes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 402 patients with LFLG AS who underwent TAVR at a single tertiary center. Patients were stratified by subtype: classical LFLG (cLFLG) AS (LVEF <50%, n=140) and paradoxical LFLG (pLFLG) AS (LVEF ≥50%, n=262). MCF was calculated as the ratio of stroke volume to myocardial volume, and myocardial volume was defined as LV mass divided by the mean density of the myocardium (1.05 g/mL). Sex-specific thresholds were used to define normal MCF (>0.68 in males; >0.82 in females). Multivariate logistic regression models assessed odds of depressed MCF, and Cox models evaluated its association with post-TAVR mortality, adjusted for confounders. Results: Across the spectrum of LFLG AS, depressed MCF was associated with increased mortality (adjusted HR 2.223, p = 0.002). In subgroup analyses, cLFLG AS patients had higher odds of depressed MCF (adjusted OR 5.102, p<0.001), but depressed MCF was not associated with increased mortality (adjusted HR 1.365, p=0.482). In contrast, pLFLG AS patients had lower odds of depressed MCF (adjusted OR 0.196, p<0.001), but depressed MCF was associated with increased mortality (adjusted HR 2.018, p=0.029). Conclusion: Depressed MCF is more frequent in classical LFLG AS but is not clearly associated with higher mortality, whereas though less common, its presence in paradoxical LFLG AS is associated with worse outcomes. These divergent patterns likely reflect differences in remodeling and hemodynamics and underscore the need for tailored approaches to risk stratification and management.
title: Abstract 15162: Prevalence and Prognostic Value of Myocardial Contraction Fraction on Outcomes in Classical and Paradoxical Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is increasingly used in older patients with intermediate-risk aortic stenosis (AS), but contemporary real-world data comparing TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), particularly in frail patients, remain limited. Hypothesis: The relative benefit of TAVR over SAVR would be preserved across frailty strata. Methods: We analyzed elective hospitalizations for isolated TAVR or SAVR among adults aged ≥65 years with AS in the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2016-2022). To focus on intermediate-risk patients, we excluded those with extreme-risk features and patients undergoing additional cardiac procedures. Frailty was identified using the Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups frailty indicator. Multivariable models adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, index complications, length of stay, and 30-day readmission. Interaction testing assessed whether frailty modified the association between procedure type and outcomes. Results: Among 93,093 weighted procedures, 83,348 were TAVR and 9,745 were SAVR. Frailty was present in 5.96% of patients, similarly distributed between groups (6.03% vs 5.33%, p=0.058). There was no significant procedure-by-frailty interaction for in-hospital mortality (p-interaction=0.495) or 30-day readmission (p-interaction=0.890), indicating that the relative benefit of TAVR was similar regardless of frailty status (Image 1a-1b). Among complications, a significant procedure-by-frailty interaction was observed only for hemorrhage/hematoma (p-interaction=0.0003) (Image 1c). Length of stay was shorter with TAVR in non-frail (1.8 vs 6.5 days) and frail patients (2.5 vs 8.5 days; both p<0.001). Thirty-day readmissions after adjustment were consistent regardless of frailty (non-frail aHR 0.700; frail aHR 0.658; p-interaction=0.890). Among non-frail patients, TAVR was associated with significantly lower adjusted odds of in-hospital death, stroke, acute kidney injury (AKI), hemorrhage requiring transfusion, mechanical ventilation (MV), pericardial tamponade (PT), and post-procedural heart failure than SAVR, with no significant difference in pacemaker implantation. Among frail patients, TAVR showed a similar pattern across most outcomes, except stroke and pacemaker implantation, which did not differ significantly (Image 2). Conclusions: In intermediate-risk patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower mortality, fewer complications, shorter hospital stays, and fewer readmissions than SAVR. These benefits were seen in both frail and non-frail patients, with no significant procedure-by-frailty interaction for mortality and readmission. Frailty alone should not limit consideration of TAVR in appropriately selected intermediate-risk patients.
title: Abstract 15164: Impact of Frailty on Comparative Outcomes of Transcatheter versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Intermediate-Risk Aortic Stenosis: A U.S. Population-Based Analysis of 93,093 Hospitalizations

abstract: Abstract and Introduction: Eosinophilic myocarditis (EM) is a rare cause of acute heart failure. The focal nature of cell infiltrates on endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) can lead to misdiagnosis. We present a case of EM first diagnosed as resolving lymphocytic myocarditis. Clinical decompensation and rising peripheral eosinophilia prompted re-review of biopsy slides, uncovering eosinophilic infiltrates that fundamentally changed the diagnosis and management. Clinical Findings & Diagnostic Assessment: A 23-year-old female with asthma and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis presented with one week of malaise. Heart rate was in the 150s with O2 saturation 90% on HFNC. POCUS showed a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, confirmed at 20-25% on TTE. Troponin was 6,780 ng/L, BNP 2,500 pg/mL, WBC 16х10 9 /L with 15% eosinophils, and CRP 84 mg/L. Chest x-ray showed bilateral infiltrates. EMB showed sparse lymphocytic infiltrate with interstitial fibrosis, suggestive of a resolving myocarditis. She was treated for CAP and diuresed. She required intubation as her respiratory status worsened. Bronchoscopy with BAL revealed 75% eosinophils, and peripheral eosinophils rose to 50% by day 10. Re-examination of the EMB slides was requested, revealing eosinophilic infiltration consistent with EM (Image 1). Workup including ANCA, BCR-ABL, flow cytometry, and stool Strongyloides was negative. Final diagnosis was idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome with EM. Therapeutic Interventions: Pulse-dose methylprednisolone 1g IV daily for three days was initiated on day 10, followed by 80mg IV daily for two weeks, then a prednisone taper. Eosinophils dropped to 2% within 48 hours of pulse-dose steroids. GDMT was started as tolerated. Follow-up & Outcomes: Serial TTEs showed persistently reduced LVEF at 25%. She discharged to inpatient rehab on day 34 and completed a month of rehab with cardiology, rheumatology, and hematology follow-up arranged. Discussion: This case demonstrated that early EMB results can misclassify EM as resolving myocarditis, which delayed treatment. The pivot point was a BAL finding of 75% eosinophils, prompting a re-review of biopsy slides that revealed eosinophilic infiltrates not seen initially. Rapid response to steroids confirmed the diagnosis. The persistently reduced LVEF is likely from myocardial injury, highlighting the consequences of this diagnostic pitfall. Conclusion: A negative initial EMB shouldn’t exclude EM when the course suggests an eosinophilic process. Clinicians should re-review biopsy specimens when the clinical trajectory is discordant with the initial pathologic results, as early steroid initiation is vital. Patient Perspective: The family expressed guilt over a delay in seeking care, as they thought symptoms were from a viral illness. They were reassured that this was a highly atypical presentation unlikely to have been diagnosed earlier.
title: Abstract 15167: Eosinophilic Myocarditis Misclassified as Resolving Lymphocytic Myocarditis on Endomyocardial Biopsy: A Case Report

abstract: Background: As survival among patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) continues to improve, an increasing number develop atrial fibrillation requiring stroke prevention strategies. Data regarding the safety of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) in this population remain limited. We evaluated temporal trends and in-hospital outcomes of CHD patients undergoing LAAO in the United States. Methods: Adult patients undergoing LAAO for atrial fibrillation/flutter were identified using procedural and diagnostic codes between 2016-2023 and were queried from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS), excluding COVID-19 cases. Temporal trends in the prevalence of CHD among LAAO recipients were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between CHD and in-hospital complications after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics. Results: Among an estimated 278,740 patients undergoing LAAO, 6,840 (2.45%) had CHD. The prevalence of CHD among LAAO recipients remained stable throughout the study period (trend p=0.13). Compared with non-CHD patients, those with CHD were younger (75.6 vs. 76.3 years, p<0.001), had higher comorbidity burden (Charlson index 2.18 vs. 2.03, p=0.005), and were more likely to have prior stroke (27.4% vs. 20.8%, p<0.001), heart failure (42.1% vs. 37.7%, p=0.001), COPD (20.0% vs. 15.9%, p<0.001), and prior valve replacement (6.7% vs. 5.4%, p=0.037). After multivariable adjustment, CHD was associated with significantly higher odds of pericardial effusion (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.93, 95% CI 1.37-2.71), pericardiocentesis (aOR 1.98, 95% CI 1.12-3.49), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 3.80, 95% CI 1.82-7.97), major bleeding (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.55), mechanical ventilation (aOR 2.89, 95% CI 1.50-5.53), sepsis (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 1.20-11.07), and in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.94, 95% CI 1.06-8.20; all p<0.05). Conclusions: Despite increasing utilization of LAAO, CHD patients experience significantly higher rates of periprocedural complications, stroke, and in-hospital mortality compared with non-CHD patients. These findings highlight the need for careful patient selection, procedural planning, and dedicated studies evaluating LAAO outcomes in the growing adult CHD population.
title: Abstract 15190: In-Hospital Outcomes of Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in Patients with Congenital Heart Disease: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2016-2023

abstract: Patients aged ≥80 years or weighing ≤60 kg with atrial fibrillation are frequently deemed ineligible for standard-dose oral anticoagulation due to high bleeding risk, frailty, or renal impairment. Edoxaban 15 mg once daily is the only dose evaluated in a randomised trial specifically designed for this group (ELDERCARE-AF), yet whether this signal is consistent across the broader population of OAC-ineligible patients including the extreme-low-body-weight subgroup has not been formally quantified. We sought to pool available pairwise evidence for the pre-specified ELDERCARE-AF anchor comparison.We performed a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of studies comparing edoxaban 15 mg versus placebo or no anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation patients aged ≥80 years or with body weight ≤60 kg who were ineligible for standard oral anticoagulation. Primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism. A random-effects model with REML estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment was applied per protocol.We performed an analysis of 2 studies (Okumura 2020 ELDERCARE-AF ITT; Akao 2024 ≤45 kg subgroup). Edoxaban 15 mg significantly reduced stroke or systemic embolism versus placebo or no anticoagulation (HR 0.35 [95% CI 0.25-0.49]; P=0.016). Between-study heterogeneity was absent (I 2 =0%; Q=0.01, P=0.91). With k=2, a prediction interval was not estimated.Edoxaban 15 mg reduces stroke or systemic embolism by approximately 65% versus placebo in OAC-ineligible elderly and low-body-weight atrial fibrillation patients, with a consistent effect across the parent ELDERCARE-AF trial and the extreme-low-body-weight subgroup. These findings reinforce the clinical value of very-low-dose edoxaban in patients traditionally excluded from anticoagulation trials and establish a quantitative efficacy anchor for this underserved population.
title: Abstract 15204: Edoxaban Dosing Strategies in Older Adults and Low Body Weight Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Pre-Specified Pairwise Meta-Analysis with Falls-Related Bleeding Assessment

abstract: Background: Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve implantation is an established option for degenerated surgical bioprostheses in patients at high surgical risk. Late bioprosthetic valve thrombosis is a potentially life-threatening complication, and the optimal treatment is not established. Case Presentation: A 71-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, prior coronary artery bypass grafting, paroxysmal atrial flutter, and a degenerated surgical mitral bioprosthesis underwent transfemoral transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve implantation with a 26-mm balloon-expandable prosthesis in September 2023. He was discharged in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I on a vitamin K antagonist (warfarin; target international normalized ratio 2.0 to 3.0) and antiplatelet therapy. In October 2025, two years later, he developed exertional dyspnea (NYHA class II) despite a therapeutic target range. Echocardiography showed increased transprosthetic gradients and reduced leaflet mobility, and transesophageal echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography demonstrated hypoattenuated thrombotic material on the ventricular aspect of the leaflets with restricted motion, consistent with obstructive thrombosis. Management and Outcome: Anticoagulation was intensified (international normalized ratio 2.5 to 3.5) with continued antiplatelet therapy. After 60 days, symptoms progressed to NYHA class III with persistent obstruction (mean transprosthetic gradient of 9 mmHg, pressure half-time of 240 ms, effective orifice area of 0.9 cm 2 ). The Heart Team deemed reoperation prohibitive. Ultra-slow low-dose fibrinolysis with alteplase, 25 mg infused over 25 hours, was administered in a single cycle without bleeding or embolic complications. After treatment, the mean gradient fell to 4 mmHg, the pressure half-time to 120 ms, and the effective orifice area rose to 1.7 cm 2 , with restored leaflet mobility. Follow-up cardiac computed tomography confirmed complete thrombus resolution. Conclusion: To our knowledge, this is among the first reported cases of late obstructive thrombosis after transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve implantation in which complete resolution was confirmed by both transesophageal echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography after a single ultra-slow, low-dose alteplase cycle. In this patient at prohibitive operative risk, prolonged low-dose fibrinolysis reversed prosthetic obstruction without surgery, and cardiac computed tomography was useful for confirming the treatment response.
title: Abstract 15209: Late Obstructive Bioprosthetic Valve Thrombosis After Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve Implantation

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac arrest during labor is rare, the differential includes amniotic fluid and pulmonary embolism, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, peripartum cardiomyopathy, local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST), and primary arrhythmic disease. We present a term pregnant patient with ventricular fibrillation (VF) arrest after epidural ropivacaine dosing, in whom LAST was the leading diagnosis and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) was considered but felt less likely. Patient Information: A 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks' gestation with no cardiac history apart from syncopal episode at 16 thought to be neurocardiogenic was admitted for elective induction of labor. The pregnancy was complicated by anemia, fetal macrosomia, and preeclampsia without severe features. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Induction was begun on Hospital Day 1. On Hospital Day 2, about 15 minutes after a second epidural ropivacaine bag, she developed acute dyspnea and became pulseless; the monitor showed VF, and she was defibrillated at 200 J with epinephrine and amiodarone over two further cycles to ROSC, with intravenous lipid emulsion given for presumed LAST. An emergent perimortem cesarean delivered the infant, after which she sustained a PEA arrest with ROSC and seizure-like activity treated with midazolam. She was extubated on Hospital Day 3, weaned off pressors on Hospital Day 4, and discharged on Hospital Day 9. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The temporal link to ropivacaine made LAST the leading diagnosis. Post-arrest ECG showed sinus tachycardia and right bundle branch block (RBBB) without ischemic changes. Echocardiography showed a hyperdynamic left ventricle without wall-motion abnormality and mild-to-moderate RV dilation. CTA chest excluded pulmonary embolism and aortic dissection, and preserved LV function made acute coronary syndrome unlikely. Therapeutic Intervention: Treatment included ACLS, intravenous lipid emulsion for presumed LAST, perimortem cesarean delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage control. Follow-up & Outcomes: The patient made a complete neurologic recovery. No arrhythmia was captured during the event, and outpatient cardiac MRI was recommended to exclude ARVC. Discussion: The sudden collapse minutes after ropivacaine suggested LAST and prompted lipid rescue. RBBB with a dilated right ventricle briefly raised concern for ARVC, but the lack of a documented arrhythmia, her benign fainting history, no family history of sudden death, and a plausible physiologic basis for the RV findings made it unlikely. Conclusion: A VF arrest in labor demands weighing obstetric, anesthetic, and cardiac causes together. LAST deserves early recognition as a reversible, treatable culprit, while incidental findings such as mild RV dilation in pregnancy warrant caution before attributing an arrest to inherited heart disease.
title: Abstract 15210: Ventricular Fibrillation Arrest During Labor: Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity from Epidural Ropivacaine

abstract: Introduction: A coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) is rare, and a CAA with a coronary sinus fistula is a distinct subset of coronary anomaly, with an incidence of less than 1 percent. We present a rare case of acute thrombotic STEMI occurring two years after repair of a right coronary artery (RCA) aneurysm with a coronary sinus fistula, likely triggered by temporary interruption of apixaban and aspirin for an elective surgery. Case: A 71-year-old patient with prior RCA aneurysm and coronary sinus fistula repair, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea presented with two hours of severe substernal chest pain and was found to have an inferoposterior STEMI at an outside rural hospital. The admission electrocardiogram (EKG) demonstrated new inferoposterior ST-segment elevation compared with the prior tracing (Image 1); tenecteplase was given en route, and high-sensitivity troponin increased from 5,245 ng/L to >50,000 ng/L. Earlier that day, the patient underwent bilateral carpal tunnel release after holding aspirin and apixaban for three days. Coronary angiography showed severe acute thrombotic occlusion of an aneurysmal distal right coronary artery. Manual and mechanical aspiration thrombectomy using a guide extension catheter and Penumbra system restored TIMI 2 flow, with some residual thrombus burden seen on coronary angiography images (Image 2). A transthoracic echocardiogram showed a preserved left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% with no regional wall-motion abnormalities, mild left ventricular hypertrophy, and reduced right ventricular systolic function. Heparin infusion was started for high thrombus burden but stopped overnight due to persistent bleeding from fresh bilateral carpal tunnel surgical sites, with an acute drop in hemoglobin from 14.7 to 11.0 g/dL. GPIIb/IIIa inhibitors were avoided as our patient had received thrombolytics and developed bleeding after thrombectomy. The coronary CT angiography confirmed a markedly aneurysmal RCA and a small fusiform proximal left anterior descending aneurysm (Image 3). Antithrombotic therapy was tailored to clopidogrel plus apixaban without aspirin based on the patient's high bleeding risk profile, and proton-pump inhibitor therapy was added. The patient was discharged with close follow-up and was later switched to ticagrelor after CYP2C19 testing. Conclusion: This case highlights the thrombotic vulnerability of aneurysmal coronary anatomy following fistula repair and the technical challenges of reperfusion therapy in these cases, with postprocedural bleeding further limiting optimal antithrombotic therapy to prevent recurrent thrombosis. In such rare cases, the optimal management requires tailored balancing of thrombosis, bleeding, and anticoagulation risk, informed by coronary angiography findings and procedural expertise.
title: Abstract 15218: Aneurysm, Thrombus, and Bleeding Collision: A Case of Inferoposterior STEMI in a Previously Repaired Aneurysmal Right Coronary Artery-Coronary Sinus Fistula

abstract: Introduction: Heart rate response (HRR) during vasodilator stress testing reflects chronotropic and autonomic reserve. While blunted HRR has been associated with adverse outcomes during exercise stress testing, its prognostic significance beyond myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) findings in patients undergoing vasodilator SPECT (Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography) is frequently overlooked. Hypothesis: Abnormal HRR (<20% increase from resting to peak heart rate) during vasodilator stress provides incremental prognostic information beyond SPECT perfusion findings for adverse cardiovascular events. Methods: We analyzed 1,292 patients from the PROMISE trial who underwent vasodilator pharmacologic SPECT (adenosine, regadenosone, or dipyridamole). Abnormal HRR was defined as <20% increase from resting to peak heart rate. Nuclear stress test results were categorized as normal or abnormal. Patients were stratified into four groups based on HRR status (abnormal vs. normal) and SPECT findings (abnormal vs. normal). The composite endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or unstable angina hospitalization over a median follow-up of 48 months. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were constructed adjusting for age, BMI, diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease equivalents, beta-blocker use, sex, smoking, heart failure, and nuclear imaging severity. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared cumulative event rates across groups (log-rank test). Results: Abnormal HRR was present in 152 patients (11.8%). After adjustment for nuclear imaging results and clinical covariates, each 10% increase in HRR was independently associated with a 19% reduction in risk of the composite endpoint (adjusted HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.72-0.91, p<0.001). Abnormal nuclear imaging results independently predicted adverse outcomes (adjusted HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.28-1.86, p<0.001; C-index 0.78). When stratified by combined HRR and SPECT results, patients with both abnormal HRR and abnormal SPECT had the highest event rates, while those with normal HRR and normal SPECT had the lowest risk. Patients with discordant findings exhibited intermediate event rates. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant differences across the four groups (log-rank p<0.0001; Figure 1). Conclusions: In patients undergoing vasodilator SPECT, abnormal HRR provides incremental prognostic information beyond perfusion imaging findings, even after adjustment for imaging results and clinical risk factors. The combination of abnormal HRR and abnormal SPECT identifies a particularly high-risk subgroup, while normal findings in both confer the most favorable prognosis. These results support incorporating HRR as a complementary prognostic marker during pharmacologic stress testing.
title: Abstract 15220: Abnormal Heart Rate Response During Vasodilator Stress SPECT Provides Incremental Prognostic Value Beyond Myocardial Perfusion Findings: A PROMISE Subgroup Analysis

abstract: Background: Randomized trials of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation span warfarin- and direct oral anticoagulant-based comparator frameworks, distinct clinical settings, and heterogeneous endpoint constructs, limiting interpretation of prior pooled analyses. We therefore performed an era-structured systematic review and meta-analysis of contemporary randomized evidence. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials comparing percutaneous LAAO with anticoagulation-based medical therapy in adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. The prespecified primary quantitative outcome was clinically relevant nonprocedural bleeding in contemporary trials. Time-to-event effects were summarized as hazard ratio (HR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis when appropriate. Thromboembolic efficacy was summarized by trial-level synthesis because efficacy composites were not directly comparable across studies. Results: Six randomized trials involving 7,028 patients were included. The extended contemporary bleeding analysis comprised 3 trials and 5,002 randomized patients. Left atrial appendage occlusion was associated with significantly lower nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (pooled HR 0.51, 95% CI, 0.37-0.70; I 2 =0%; Figure 1). Across contemporary trials, thromboembolic efficacy appeared preserved relative to anticoagulation-based therapy, supported by trial-level noninferiority rather than a pooled superiority model. Warfarin-era trials provided historical proof of concept for efficacy preservation, whereas CLOSURE-AF, conducted in a very high-risk population with physician-directed best medical care, did not demonstrate noninferiority for its primary composite endpoint and was interpreted as contextual mixed-comparator evidence (Table 1). Conclusion: Across randomized evidence, the clearest contemporary advantage of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion is reduction in clinically relevant nonprocedural bleeding, whereas thromboembolic efficacy appears preserved at the trial level. These findings support left atrial appendage occlusion as a selective bleeding-sparing strategy in appropriately chosen patients rather than a universal replacement for anticoagulation. Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261357386
title: Abstract 15231: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion versus Anticoagulation in Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation Across Therapeutic Eras: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Penetrating cardiac trauma caused by high-velocity projectiles is typically associated with catastrophic complications, including tamponade, major hemorrhage, valvular injury, and death. Retained intracardiac foreign bodies are uncommon and often prompt surgical extraction because of concerns regarding migration, embolization, infection, and arrhythmias. We present an unusual case of a chainsaw tooth embedded within the interventricular septum that remained clinically silent despite documented myocardial injury. Case: A previously healthy 26-year-old man was referred for cardiology evaluation after sustaining penetrating precordial trauma while cutting wood. Five days earlier, a chainsaw chain fractured, projecting a metallic tooth toward his chest. Despite the mechanism of injury, he remained asymptomatic, denying chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, or syncope. Physical examination revealed only a small sutured precordial wound without evidence of heart failure. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated troponin I levels (2178 ng/L) and inflammatory markers. Point-of-care ultrasound excluded tamponade but identified a hyperechoic intracardiac structure. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography with three-dimensional reconstruction confirmed a metallic foreign body embedded within the mid-apical interventricular septum. No pericardial effusion, active bleeding, or migration was identified. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function without valvular abnormalities. The principal management challenge involved determining whether surgical extraction was warranted despite the absence of symptoms and structural complications. Following multidisciplinary discussion, conservative management was selected because the anticipated risks of surgery outweighed the potential benefits. The patient received intravenous antibiotics and close clinical and imaging surveillance. He remained asymptomatic throughout hospitalization, with normalization of inflammatory markers and stable imaging findings. He was discharged in good clinical condition with planned outpatient follow-up. Conclusion: Retained intramyocardial foreign bodies may occasionally remain clinically silent even when located within critical cardiac structures. Multimodality imaging was essential for anatomical characterization and risk stratification. In carefully selected hemodynamically stable patients without structural complications, conservative management may represent a safe alternative to high-risk surgical intervention.
title: Abstract 15233: When Not to Operate: Conservative Management of a Retained Intracardiac Chainsaw Tooth

abstract: Introduction: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high morbidity and mortality despite increasing use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices such as intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella, and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. While ischemic cardiomyopathy(ICM) is the most common cause of CS, outcomes of patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) requiring MCS remain poorly characterized. We compared in-hospital outcomes and 30-day readmission rates between NICM and ICM patients presenting with CS on temporary MCS. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD) from 2018 to 2022. Patients were stratified into NICM and ICM cohorts. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed to evaluate in-hospital outcomes and 30-day readmission, respectively, after adjustment for demographic, clinical, and hospital-level characteristics Results: Among an estimated 48,155 patients with CS requiring temporary MCS, 32,465 (67.4%) had ICM and 15,690 (32.6%) had NICM. NICM patients were younger (60.9 vs. 66.5 years), more often female (30.8% vs. 24.3%), and had longer hospital stays with higher costs, while ICM patients had a higher prevalence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes (Table 1). After multivariable adjustment, ICM was associated with significantly lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.75, 95% CI 0.70-0.81), mechanical ventilation (aOR 0.82, 95% CI 0.76-0.87), acute kidney injury (aOR 0.63, 95% CI 0.59-0.68), renal replacement therapy (aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.65-0.80), and sepsis (aOR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.65) compared with NICM. Stroke and cardiac arrest rates were comparable between groups(Table 2). Thirty-day readmission rates were similar (19.1% vs. 19.1%, p=0.980), with no significant difference in readmission risk between groups (adjusted HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.89-1.05, p=0.392). Conclusion: NICM was associated with worse in-hospital outcomes, including higher mortality, organ failure, and resource utilization compared with ICM, likely reflecting a more refractory shock phenotype less amenable to targeted intervention. Despite these differences, 30-day readmission rates were similar, suggesting persistently high post-discharge vulnerability irrespective of etiology.
title: Abstract 15247: 30-Day Readmission Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Requiring Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support: A Comparative Analysis of Ischemic versus Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease is common among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but whether planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVI improves hard ischemic outcomes remains uncertain. We evaluated whether planned PCI before TAVI is associated with lower time-to-event all-cause death and myocardial infarction compared with conservative treatment or PCI deferral. Methods: We performed a focused meta-analysis of randomized trials comparing planned PCI with conservative treatment or deferral among patients with severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease undergoing TAVI. Across three randomized trials, 1,156 patients were assigned to PCI (n=579) or conservative treatment/deferral (n=577). Individual patient time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves using the Guyot method. Reconstruction was feasible for NOTION-3 and PRO-TAVI, which provided randomization-anchored curves for all-cause death and myocardial infarction; ACTIVATION was excluded from the reconstructed analysis because comparable curves were unavailable. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated from the reconstructed dataset. Results/Data: The reconstructed analysis included 921 patients from NOTION-3 and PRO-TAVI. For all-cause death, planned PCI was not associated with improved survival compared with conservative treatment/deferral (HR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.63-1.46; P=0.84), with substantial overlap of the reconstructed curves through 12 months. For myocardial infarction, the point estimate favored planned PCI but remained statistically inconclusive (HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.39-1.26; P=0.24). Conclusions: In this reconstructed time-to-event meta-analysis of randomized evidence, planned PCI before TAVI was not associated with a significant reduction in all-cause death or myocardial infarction. These findings support a selective, heart-team-based revascularization strategy rather than routine PCI before TAVI, while emphasizing the need for longer follow-up and adequately powered trials to identify patients most likely to derive net clinical benefit.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials (3 trials, 1,156 patients); reconstructed individual patient data from NOTION-3 and PRO-TAVI (921 patients) using the Guyot method.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials were reconstructable, follow-up was short, and the analysis is underpowered for individual outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Reconstructed time-to-event analysis found no clear benefit of planned PCI before TAVI for death or myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For all-cause death, planned PCI was not associated with improved survival (HR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.63-1.46; P=0.84). For myocardial infarction, HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.39-1.26; P=0.24.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears directly on management of coronary disease in TAVI candidates, a common and guideline-contested decision.

title: Abstract 15250: Planned Coronary Revascularization Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Reconstructed Time-to-Event Evidence from Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (AF) is increasingly prevalent worldwide and can lead to fatal cardioembolic stroke. Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as a promising alternative to life-long anticoagulation with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), the current standard of care. Previous data demonstrated conflicting outcomes and heterogenous comparators across studies. Therefore, a focused meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) is needed to compare LAAC versus DOACs in nonvalvular AF. Research Question: Does percutaneous LAAC provide an effective and safe alternative to direct oral anticoagulation in adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation? Methodology: We systematically searched major databases through May 1st, 2026. We included RCTs comparing LAAC to DOACs in adults with nonvalvular AF. Statistical analysis was conducted via Cochrane’s Review Manager using the Mantel-Haenszel random effects model and pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated. Outcomes assessed included incidence of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, cardiovascular (CV) death, all cause mortality, and major bleeding. Trial-defined composite efficacy endpoints and net adverse clinical events (NACE) were assessed descriptively because outcome definitions varied across studies. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROB-2.0 tool. Sensitivity and leave-one-out influence analyses were conducted to identify sources of heterogeneity. Results: A total of 4 RCTs involving 5,890 patients were included in the final analysis. The risk of ischemic stroke was numerically higher (RR 1.30, 95% CI 0.94-1.78; I 2 =0%) in the LAAC arm, although it did not reach statistical significance, whereas hemorrhagic stroke tended to be less frequent (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.45-1.51; I 2 =0%). There were no significant differences in cardiovascular death (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.73-1.40; I 2 =49%, 0% after exclusion of PRAGUE-17) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.16; I 2 =1%). LAAC significantly reduced major bleeding by 31% (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-0.99; I 2 =84%, 37% after exclusion of CLOSURE-AF), with CLOSURE-AF being the probable contributor towards observed heterogeneity due to its stricter bleeding endpoints (BARC ≥3). Descriptive assessment of trial-defined composite efficacy and net adverse clinical event outcomes demonstrated broadly comparable overall efficacy between LAAC and DOAC therapy, although CLOSURE-AF did not meet its prespecified noninferiority criterion. Conclusion: In patients with nonvalvular AF, LAAC was associated with lower major bleeding and comparable hemorrhagic stroke and mortality outcomes, although ischemic stroke was numerically higher. These findings support LAAC as a potential alternative to DOAC therapy in selected patients and underscore the importance of individualized assessment of thromboembolic and bleeding risk.
title: Abstract 15263: Contemporary Randomized Evidence Comparing Left Atrial Appendage Closure with Direct Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) remains uncertain. Although oral anticoagulants (OACs) and antiplatelet therapy (APT) are commonly used, comparative real-world data on long-term outcomes are limited. We aimed to compare the long-term effectiveness and safety of OACs versus APT-based antithrombotic strategies following percutaneous LAAO. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that post-percutaneous LAAO management with OACs provides comparable thromboembolic protection but differs in cumulative bleeding complications compared with APT over a 2-year follow-up. Methods: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who underwent percutaneous LAAO were identified. Patients initiated on OACs (rivaroxaban, apixaban, dabigatran, warfarin, or edoxaban) (Cohort 1) versus APT (Cohort 2) within one month post-procedure were compared. Patients with mechanical valves, venous thromboembolism, or thrombophilia were excluded. A 1:1 propensity score matching was performed. . The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of cerebral infarction and arterial embolism/thrombosis. The primary safety endpoint was a composite of intracranial hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding. Outcomes were assessed at 2 years follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: Following propensity score matching, 6,980 patients were analyzed (n=3,490 per cohort). At 2 years, no significant difference was observed in the efficacy composite between OAC and APT (HR 1.21; 95% CI 0.89-1.63; p=0.94). For the safety composite, OAC demonstrated significantly lower cumulative major bleeding risk compared with APT (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.57-0.92; p=0.008). Kaplan-Meier curves are shown in Figure 1. Conclusion: In this large propensity-matched real-world analysis, post-percutaneous LAAO OAC achieved comparable thromboembolic protection, but significantly lower long-term bleeding risk compared with APT from 6 months onward. These findings challenge conventional assumptions regarding OAC-related haemorrhage in post-percutaneous LAAO patients and suggest OAC may offer superior net clinical benefit over prolonged antiplatelet strategies.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective TriNetX cohort; 6,980 patients analysed after 1:1 propensity matching (3,490 per cohort), 2-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Confounding by indication and coded outcomes; the safety composite is defined as intracranial and gastrointestinal haemorrhage only.
appraisal.one_line: TriNetX matched cohort associated oral anticoagulation after LAAO with less major bleeding than antiplatelet therapy and similar efficacy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Efficacy composite HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.89-1.63; safety composite (major bleeding) HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.57-0.92 for OAC vs antiplatelet therapy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It runs against the premise of antiplatelet-only therapy after LAAO and adds to uncertainty over the optimal post-implant regimen.

title: Abstract 15271: Oral Anticoagulation versus Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Real-World Comparative Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Aortic valve infective endocarditis (IE) carries high morbidity and mortality, especially with prosthetic valves. Coronary obstruction by a vegetation is a rare, lethal complication. We describe aortic valve IE with dynamic right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion causing inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and shock. Patient Information: A 67-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and aortic stenosis, status post bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement one year prior, presented with fever, dyspnea, and fatigue after missing two dialysis sessions. Clinical Findings and Timeline: He had methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia complicated by septic shock and acute hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Echocardiography showed moderate aortic stenosis and a large aortic valve vegetation. He developed bradycardia (heart rate in the 20s) from atrial flutter with slow ventricular response, which responded to intravenous dopamine. Diagnostic Assessment: Recurrent hypotension prompted a repeat ECG showing inferior ST-segment elevation with troponin rise. Urgent coronary angiography revealed a large vegetation occluding the RCA with slow, stagnant mid-to-distal flow, mimicking thrombotic acute coronary syndrome. Therapeutic Interventions: After multidisciplinary discussion between interventional cardiology and cardiovascular surgery, balloon angioplasty and mechanical aspiration were performed with minimal flow improvement. Patient was cannulated for venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for mixed septic and cardiogenic shock with a cardiac index of 1.6. Follow-up and Outcomes: Despite multiple vasopressors, antiarrhythmics, full-flow VA-ECMO, and CRRT, shock persisted. He developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia refractory to magnesium and defibrillation, attributed to recurrent vegetation-related RCA occlusion. The family elected for comfort care, and he died the following day. Discussion: Coronary ostial obstruction by an aortic valve vegetation is rare but highly lethal, particularly with aggressive pathogens such as MSSA, where septic and cardiogenic shock coexist. Coronary involvement should be considered in IE with new conduction abnormalities, hypotension, or ischemic ECG changes. Percutaneous angioplasty and aspiration offer only transient benefit because the mechanical obstruction persists; surgical excision is preferred but may be precluded by profound shock. VA-ECMO offers temporary support, yet recurrent obstruction can drive ongoing ischemia and malignant arrhythmias. This case underscores the value of rapid multidisciplinary decision-making and the poor prognosis of large aortic valve vegetations causing dynamic coronary occlusion.
title: Abstract 15273: Circulatory Collapse in Infective Endocarditis: Coronary Occlusion from an Aortic Valve Vegetation

abstract: Introduction: Paradoxical embolism occurs when venous thromboemboli enter the systemic arterial circulation through an intracardiac shunt, most commonly a patent foramen ovale (PFO). We present a young patient with massive pulmonary embolism (PE), severe right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, and acute limb ischemia associated with a PFO. Patient Information: A 23-year-old man with obesity and schizoaffective disorder presented with progressive dyspnea and chest discomfort. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Evaluation demonstrated extensive right lower extremity deep venous thrombosis involving the popliteal and posterior tibial veins and bilateral PE with a large right main pulmonary artery thrombus measuring 2.3 х 2.8 cm. TTE demonstrated severe RV dilation and dysfunction consistent with RV pressure overload. The patient underwent catheter-directed pulmonary embolectomy via right femoral venous access and therapeutic anticoagulation. Several hours later, he developed acute ischemia of the contralateral left lower extremity with pain, sensory loss, and limb coolness. Bedside Doppler examination revealed absent arterial signals. CTA demonstrated acute occlusion of the left common femoral, superficial femoral, and profunda femoris arteries with additional bilateral popliteal arterial occlusions. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Emergent thrombectomy restored perfusion and limb viability. Given concomitant venous thromboembolism and acute arterial occlusion, further investigation was pursued. TEE demonstrated a PFO with bidirectional shunting on color Doppler and a positive agitated saline study. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated normalization of RV function. The combination of extensive venous thromboembolism, severe RV pressure overload, acute arterial occlusion, and bidirectional intracardiac shunting was highly suggestive of paradoxical embolization. Discussion: Acute PE may transiently elevate right-sided cardiac pressures, promoting right-to-left shunting across a PFO and permitting venous thrombi to enter the systemic arterial circulation. In this case, severe PE with RV dysfunction was followed by acute limb ischemia, creating a compelling clinical scenario for suspected paradoxical embolism. The coexistence of extensive venous thromboembolism, severe RV pressure overload, acute arterial occlusion, and a PFO with bidirectional shunting provided a plausible pathophysiologic explanation. Recognition of this entity is critical, as management may include consideration of PFO closure to reduce future embolic risk. Conclusion: Acute limb ischemia occurring in the setting of massive PE should prompt consideration of paradoxical embolization through a PFO. This case illustrates how severe PE-associated RV pressure overload can convert an otherwise silent PFO into a conduit for systemic arterial embolization.
title: Abstract 15282: When Venous Becomes Arterial: Acute Limb Ischemia Following Massive Pulmonary Embolism in a Patient with Patent Foramen Ovale

abstract: Introduction: The optimal antithrombotic strategy for non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on dialysis remains uncertain. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate and compare the real-world efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin, and antiplatelet agents in patients with NVAF with ESRD on dialysis. Hypothesis: DOACs and warfarin are associated with superior thromboembolic protection compared with antiplatelet therapy in NVAF patients with ESRD on dialysis, without a significant increase in bleeding risk. Methods: Using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network, we identified patients (≥18 years) with NVAF and ESRD on dialysis. Patients with valvular heart disease or prosthetic heart valves were excluded. Three pairwise propensity score-matched (PSM) analyses were performed: (1) warfarin vs. DOAC (n=2,286 per cohort), (2) warfarin vs. antiplatelet (n=2,129 per cohort), and (3) DOAC vs. antiplatelet (n=4,884 per cohort). PSM covariates included age, sex, race/ethnicity, diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, atherosclerosis, liver disease, tobacco use, alcohol-related disorders, and NSAID use. The primary efficacy outcome was a composite of cerebral infarction and systemic embolism. The primary safety outcome was a composite of major bleeding events, including intracranial, gastrointestinal, and other hemorrhagic complications. Outcomes were assessed at a 5-year follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: After PSM, baseline covariates were well balanced (all SMD <0.08). Warfarin vs. DOAC showed no significant difference in efficacy (Hazard ratio (HR) 0.93; 95% CI 0.64-1.36; p=0.721) or safety (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.69-1.09; p=0.216). Warfarin vs. antiplatelet demonstrated a significantly lower primary endpoint (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.36-0.66; p<0.001) and lower bleeding risk (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.65-0.99; p=0.043). DOAC vs. antiplatelet showed a significantly lower primary endpoint (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.45-0.74; p<0.001), with comparable bleeding risk (HR 0.94; 95% CI 0.80-1.11; p=0.483). Conclusions: In NVAF patients with ESRD on dialysis, both warfarin and DOACs were associated with significantly lower rates of the composite of ischemic stroke or systemic embolism compared with antiplatelet therapy, with comparable or lower bleeding risk. Warfarin and DOACs demonstrated similar long-term efficacy and safety profiles to each other. These findings support the use of oral anticoagulation over antiplatelet therapy alone in this population and suggest DOACs may be a reasonable alternative to warfarin, consistent with evolving guideline recommendations.
title: Abstract 15300: Warfarin vs. DOACs vs. Antiplatelet Therapy in Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation with End-Stage Renal Disease on Dialysis

abstract: Background: The retroaortic anomalous coronary (RAC) sign is an uncommon echocardiographic finding that may indicate the presence of an anomalous circumflex artery with a retroaortic course. Although often considered a benign anatomical variant, recognition of this sign can prompt further investigation and reveal clinically significant coronary pathology. We present a case in which identification of the RAC sign during routine transthoracic echocardiography led to the diagnosis of both a coronary artery anomaly and severe obstructive coronary artery disease.Case: A 56-year-old man with hypertension and dyslipidemia was admitted for evaluation of an acute ischemic stroke involving the left middle cerebral artery territory. He denied chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, or prior cardiovascular symptoms. Routine transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function and mild left atrial enlargement. Importantly, a linear echogenic structure posterior to the aortic root was identified in the apical four-chamber view, consistent with the retroaortic anomalous coronary (RAC) sign.Recognition of this finding prompted dedicated coronary imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography confirmed an anomalous circumflex artery arising from the proximal right coronary artery and coursing posterior to the aortic root. Subsequent invasive coronary angiography further characterized the anomaly and unexpectedly revealed severe obstructive coronary artery disease, including a 75% proximal-to-mid left anterior descending artery stenosis and an 80% posterolateral branch lesion. The anomalous circumflex artery itself demonstrated only mild non-obstructive disease.The patient underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent implantation, achieving complete revascularization with TIMI 3 flow and no procedural complications. He remained neurologically and cardiovascularly stable and was discharged on guideline-directed secondary prevention therapy.Conclusion: The RAC sign is an important but frequently overlooked echocardiographic marker of anomalous circumflex artery origin. Recognition of this simple imaging finding may trigger further multimodality evaluation and uncover clinically significant coronary pathology. This case highlights the diagnostic value of transthoracic echocardiography beyond structural heart disease and emphasizes how incidental imaging findings can meaningfully influence patient management.
title: Abstract 15302: The RAC Sign: An Underrecognized Echocardiographic Clue Unmasking Coronary Anomaly and Severe Coronary Artery Disease

abstract: Background: Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome arises from the recurrent de novo heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Fewer than five cases have been reported, none with severe valvular or high-grade conduction disease, leaving it unclear whether the heart is spared.Case: A 30-year-old man with short stature (height 1.42 m), low body weight (30 kg), facial dysmorphism, and recurrent skeletal fractures presented with recurrent syncope. Electrocardiography showed complete (third-degree) atrioventricular block with a junctional escape rhythm at 31 bpm. Laboratory tests revealed evidence of insulin resistance, with elevated glycemic parameters (glycated hemoglobin, 10.5%) and an abnormal lipid profile (total cholesterol, 321 mg/dL; triglycerides, 1115 mg/dL). Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (56%), concentric hypertrophy, reduced global longitudinal strain (-13.1%), and calcific degeneration of the aortic and mitral valves with moderate to severe aortic stenosis (mean gradient 34 mmHg, aortic valve area 0.8 cm 2 ). Cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed preserved biventricular function without late gadolinium enhancement. Computed tomography showed valvular calcification without coronary atherosclerosis. Serology for Chagas disease was negative. Whole-genome sequencing identified the heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant, classified as likely pathogenic by American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria, confirming the diagnosis.Management and Outcome: A permanent pacemaker was implanted for the high-grade conduction disease. Over six months the aortic stenosis progressed (mean gradient 41 mmHg, aortic valve area 0.57 cm 2 ), and the patient underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation with symptomatic improvement.Conclusion: To our knowledge, this is the first description of severe valvular heart disease and high-grade atrioventricular block in Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome. These findings align the heterozygous Ser479Phe variant with the cardiovascular involvement of homozygous LEMD2 disease and support consideration of electrocardiographic and echocardiographic surveillance in affected individuals.
title: Abstract 15334: Cardiac Phenotype of the LEMD2 c.1436C>T Variant in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome

abstract: Background Residual inflammatory risk (RIR) persists in post-acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients despite optimal lipid-lowering therapy. While interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a validated biomarker of cardiovascular inflammation, the dose-response relationship between continuous IL-6 levels and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remains incompletely characterized. We hypothesized that a non-linear "inflammatory ceiling" exists, below which marginal risk reduction becomes negligible. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to March 2026 to identify relevant studies and conducted a dose-response meta-analysis of seven landmark trials encompassing 57,521 post-ACS patients. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression modeled the continuous association between log-transformed IL-6 and MACE hazard ratios. Pooled log(HR) per unit log(IL-6) was estimated using random-effects models. Publication bias was assessed via Egger's test. Results The pooled log(HR) per unit log(IL-6) was 0.300 (95% CI 0.216-0.384), confirming a strong log-linear association. RCS analysis revealed a critical "inflammatory floor" at IL-6 ≈ 1.8 pg/mL (HR = 1.49 vs reference), below which further reductions yielded minimal incremental benefit. In the CANTOS IL-6 substudy (n=4,833), on-treatment IL-6 below the median (1.65 pg/mL) conferred a 32% MACE reduction (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.83), whereas levels above the median showed no benefit (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.87-1.20). Anti-inflammatory therapies demonstrated consistent efficacy: CANTOS (IL-1β inhibition, HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74-0.98), COLCOT (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.96), and LoDoCo2 (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56-0.86). In CIRT, each unit increase in log(IL-6) conferred a 31% higher MACE risk (HR 1.31). CLEAR Outcomes demonstrated a nearly two-fold MACE risk in the highest hsCRP quartile (HR ≈ 1.97). Romeo et al. meta-analysis (n=13,604) confirmed that hsCRP ≥2 mg/L predicted 64% higher MACE risk (RR 1.64, 95% CI 1.33-2.03) Conclusion An inflammatory floor at IL-6 ≈ 1.8 pg/mL defines a therapeutic threshold for targeted IL-6 inhibitor therapy in post-ACS secondary prevention, optimizing patient selection and resource allocation.
title: Abstract 15371: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Continuous High-Sensitivity IL-6 and the Non-Linear Risk of Recurrent MACE Post-Acute Coronary Syndrome

abstract: Introduction: Development of right heart failure (RHF) in pulmonary hypertension (PH) represents an advanced stage of disease and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Understanding the burden of RHF in hospitalized PH patients may facilitate risk stratification and identify opportunities for targeted interventions. Using the Nationwide Readmissions Database(NRD)(2018-2022), this study examines the impact of concomitant PH on in-hospital outcomes, complications, and 30-day readmission rates among patients hospitalized with acute-on-chronic RHF. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the NRD from 2018 to 2022. Patients were stratified based on the presence or absence of concomitant PH. The primary outcome was a 30-day readmission rate. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate in-hospital complications and mortality, and Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed for 30-day readmission, after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics. Results: A total of 5,762 patients were hospitalized with acute-on-chronic RHF, of whom 4,188 (72.68%) had concomitant PH and 1,574 (27.32%) did not. Patients with PH were younger (60.4 vs 63.1 years), more frequently female (60.8% vs 50.8%), and had a higher comorbidity burden (CCI 3.28 vs 3.06)(Table 1). During the index admission, PH was associated with significantly higher adjusted odds of acute respiratory failure (aOR 1.73, 95% CI 1.45-2.07, p <0.001), while cardiac dysrhythmias were less frequent in the PH group (aOR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56-0.84, p <0.001). No significant differences were observed in cardiogenic shock, acute kidney injury, dialysis, mechanical ventilation, intubation, MCS use, or VTE. In-hospital mortality was higher in the PH group (7.82% vs 5.54%) but did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (aOR 1.45, 95% CI 0.96-2.19, p = 0.080)(Table 2). Patients with PH had a lower 30-day readmission rate (20.87% vs 25.08%), corresponding to a 23.7% lower adjusted hazard of readmission (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.92, p = 0.004). Among readmitted patients, 25.44% carried a diagnosis of acute-on-chronic RHF, which was notably higher in the PH group (32.05% vs 13.36%, p <0.001), with PH associated with nearly three times the odds of this diagnosis during readmission (aOR 2.81, 95% CI 1.59-4.96, p <0.001). Conclusion: Among patients hospitalized with acute-on-chronic RHF, concomitant PH was associated with higher odds of acute respiratory failure and markedly increased likelihood of RHF-related readmission, despite no significant increase in adjusted mortality. These findings highlight the need for targeted discharge planning, pulmonary vascular optimization, and early post-discharge monitoring in this population.
title: Abstract 15378: 30-Day Readmissions After Hospitalization for Acute-on-Chronic Right Heart Failure: The Role of Pulmonary Hypertension on Demographics, In-Hospital Outcomes, Complications, and Readmission Rates, A Nationwide Readmissions Database Analysis (2018-2022)

abstract: Background: Severely calcified coronary lesions impair lesion preparation and stent expansion, predisposing to under-expansion, restenosis, and target-vessel failure. Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) modifies calcium and aids stent delivery, but its incremental benefit over balloon-based strategies is uncertain, and randomized and observational data appear to disagree. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that IVL provides superior stent optimization (maximal stent area and stent expansion) and procedural success versus balloon-based lesion preparation, and that the treatment effect is modified by study design. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 2026 for studies comparing IVL with balloon-based calcium modification in calcified coronary PCI. Primary outcomes were maximal stent area (MSA) and stent expansion; secondary outcomes were procedural success and safety. Random-effects models pooled mean differences (MD) and risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs; study design was a prespecified subgroup with a formal interaction test. Results: Eight studies (1,321 patients; five RCTs, three observational) were included; 578 underwent IVL and 743 balloon-based preparation (OCT 24.1%, IVUS 35.8%). IVL did not improve MSA (MD 0.26 mm 2 ; 95% CI –0.03 to 0.56; p=0.082; I 2 =8.8%) or stent expansion (MD 1.19%; –2.84 to 5.21; p=0.563; I 2 =51.6%), and findings were unchanged in RCTs (MSA MD 0.22, –0.09 to 0.52, p=0.160, I 2 =0%; expansion MD –0.87, –3.36 to 1.62, p=0.494, I 2 =0%) (Figures 1 and 2). Procedural success was comparable but heterogeneous (RR 1.10; 0.98-1.22; p=0.100; I 2 =78.9%), explained by a significant design interaction (p<0.001): observational studies favoured IVL (RR 1.26; 1.14-1.39; p<0.001; I 2 =0%) while RCTs showed no difference (RR 0.99; 0.96-1.02; p=0.608; I 2 =0%); a concordant interaction occurred for expansion (p=0.015). Safety did not differ: in-hospital MACE (RR 1.48; 0.34-6.38; p=0.600; I 2 =0%), 30-day MACE (RR 1.74; 0.78-3.88; p=0.179; I 2 =0%), dissection (RR 0.74; 0.51-1.09; p=0.130; I 2 =0%), and perforation (RR 1.74; 0.51-5.95; p=0.375; I 2 =0%) (Figure 3). Conclusions: In calcified coronary PCI, IVL did not improve MSA, stent expansion, procedural success, or short-term clinical outcomes versus balloon-based preparation. The advantage observed in observational studies was not reproduced in RCTs, consistent with confounding by indication and supporting selective rather than routine use of lithotripsy.
title: Abstract 15380: Intravascular Lithotripsy versus Balloon-Based Lesion Preparation in Calcified Coronary PCI: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicating non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction(NSTEMI) in young adults represents a high-stakes, understudied clinical entity. UnlikeSTEMI-related CS, NSTEMI-associated CS is often driven by cumulative comorbidityburden and may follow a less predictable clinical trajectory. Using a nationally representativeinpatient database, we sought to characterize contemporary trends, management patterns, andin-hospital outcomes in this vulnerable population.
