Methods: Using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS), we identified adults aged 18–45with a primary diagnosis of NSTEMI and a secondary diagnosis of CS. Exclusions includedSTEMI, septic shock, hypovolemic shock, obstructive shock, elective admissions, COVID-19-positive encounters, and admissions with missing mortality data. The primary outcomewas in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiac arrest, AKI, ventriculartachycardia (VT), ventricular fibrillation (VF), stroke, mechanical ventilation, and resourceutilization. Multivariable logistic regression compared outcomes across treatment strategies(PCI, CABG, and medical management), with medical therapy as the reference group.Race/ethnicity data were restricted to 2016–2022 due to coding changes. Results: Of 167,160 NSTEMI hospitalizations, 2,905 (1.74%) were complicated by CS.Mean age was 39.74 years (95% CI: 39.33–40.16); 66.78% were male. The cohort carriedsubstantial comorbidity burden, most notably congestive heart failure (74.70%), coronaryartery disease (70.57%), and hypertension (68.16%), with a mean Charlson ComorbidityIndex of 3.48 (Figure 1). Treatment distribution was 29.26% PCI, 29.78% CABG, and40.96% medical management. In-hospital mortality was 12.39%; additional outcomesincluded cardiac arrest (13.25%), AKI (42.86%), VF (21.51%), VT (16.18%), stroke(3.96%), and vasopressor use (13.60%). On adjusted analysis, CABG was associated withsignificantly lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.278; 95% CI: 0.123–0.630;p=0.002), cardiac arrest (aOR 0.196; 95% CI: 0.077–0.495; p=0.001), AKI (aOR 0.544; 95%CI: 0.321–0.920; p=0.023), and VF (aOR 0.363; 95% CI: 0.185–0.711; p=0.003) comparedwith medical management. PCI was associated with greater Impella (aOR 4.744; 95% CI:2.143–10.501; p<0.001) and IABP utilization (aOR 2.659; 95% CI: 1.429–4.950; p=0.002)(Table 1). Mortality and vasopressor use did not differ significantly between PCI and medicalmanagement. Conclusions: NSTEMI-related cardiogenic shock in young adults carries over 12% in-hospital mortality with high comorbidity burden. CABG was associated with lower odds ofmortality and complications versus medical management. Prospective studies are needed todefine optimal strategies in this underrepresented population.
title: Abstract 15383: Contemporary Outcomes of NSTEMI-Related Cardiogenic Shock in Young Adults: Mechanical Circulatory Support, Vasopressor Use, Mortality, and Complications - A Nationwide Inpatient Sample Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) such as pembrolizumab have dramatically impacted the clinical outcomes of malignancies but are associated with several immune-related adverse events. Among these is myopericarditis, which is rare but carries a high reported mortality. Thus, prompt recognition is crucial as early treatment can significantly impact outcomes. We present a challenging case of acute myocardial infarction initially suspected to be ICI induced myopericarditis. Case: A 48-year-old patient with a history of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer complicated by recurrent pericardial effusions and recent initiation of pembrolizumab was admitted from outpatient oncology clinic with lab work concerning for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). She was started on a heparin infusion. On hospital day 2, she had an episode of sharp, centrally located chest pain with a significant high sensitivity troponin elevation from 1,744 to 8,273. On serial ECG, she developed ST elevation in I and aVL that did not meet STEMI criteria. Repeat troponin at the time of ECG was 19,949. Given that she was on pembrolizumab, there was concern that her troponin elevation with abnormal ECG was in the setting of ICI induced myopericarditis, and she was subsequently started on high dose steroids. Cardiac MRI showed a late gadolinium enhancement consistent with transmural infarct in the left ventricular apical region. It was believed that this infarct was caused by an embolic event in the setting of DIC. Coronary angiography was considered but ultimately not performed due to resolution of chest pain, stability of ECG changes, down-trending troponin as well as significant thrombocytopenia. Discussion: This case emphasizes the diagnostic complexity of cardiac presentations in patients receiving ICI. Increased awareness of and clinical suspicion for ICI induced myocarditis is important however, premature attribution of cardiac symptoms to ICI related complications may lead to diagnostic anchoring. Though rare, coronary embolism can occur in patients in DIC, even when on therapeutic anticoagulation. It is likely that coronary angiography would have been performed if clinical suspicion was higher earlier in the patient’s course, though it is unknown whether an actionable lesion existed or not.
title: Abstract 15387: Not Every Troponin Elevation on Pembrolizumab is Myopericarditis

abstract: Permanent pacemaker implantation is required in 5-25% of patients after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, depending on valve platform and pre-existing conduction disease. Right ventricular apical pacing induces dyssynchronous left ventricular contraction that causes pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in 10-20% of patients with high pacing burden. Conduction system pacing, via His bundle or left bundle branch area capture, preserves normal ventricular activation and is increasingly used as an alternative, but comparative evidence specifically in the post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement population with concurrent structural disease remains limited. We sought to pool available comparative data for left ventricular function outcomes.We performed a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of studies comparing conduction system pacing versus right ventricular pacing in patients requiring permanent pacemaker after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Primary outcome was left ventricular ejection fraction at follow-up, reported as mean difference. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalisation at 12 months. A random-effects model with REML estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment was fitted.We performed an analysis of 4 studies. Conduction system pacing was associated with significantly higher left ventricular ejection fraction compared with right ventricular pacing (mean difference +4.49% [95% CI 0.50-8.48]; P=0.037). Between-study heterogeneity was high (I 2 =75.8%). The prediction interval [-3.59, 12.57] crossed zero, reflecting uncertainty in the treatment effect at the individual study level. Secondary endpoints of mortality and heart failure hospitalisation showed directional trends favouring conduction system pacing that did not reach conventional significance.Conduction system pacing is associated with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction versus right ventricular pacing in patients requiring permanent pacemaker after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High between-study heterogeneity and a prediction interval that crosses zero indicate that individual study replication is uncertain. These data support the preferential use of conduction system pacing in this population pending results from randomised controlled trials such as CONDUCT-TAVR.
title: Abstract 15388: Conduction System Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Requiring Permanent Pacemaker After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Pooled Analysis of Left Ventricular Function

abstract: Introduction: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is frequently used in patients with cardiogenic shock, though successful weaning and survival remain challenging. Levosimendan, a calcium-sensitizing inotrope, has been proposed as an adjunctive therapy to facilitate myocardial recovery and improve ECMO outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of Levosimendan during VA-ECMO support in cardiogenic shock patients. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis included 14 studies involving 2,120 adults receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock. Secondary outcomes included short- and long-term mortality (30-day, in-hospital/discharge, under 6 months, and over 6 months), ECMO duration, ICU and hospital length of stay, adverse events including renal replacement therapy (RRT) incidence, bleeding events, arrhythmia, infection, ischemia, stroke, thrombosis. Pooled odds ratios (OR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects model. Results: Levosimendan was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of successful weaning from VA-ECMO compared with control (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.27-3.80). However, this benefit did not translate into statistically significant reductions in 30-day mortality (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.38-1.19), in-hospital or discharge mortality (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.12-1.61), mortality< 6 months (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.06-7.27), or mortality> 6 months (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.37-2.24). Levosimendan was associated with longer ECMO duration (MD 1.81 days, 95% CI 0.54-3.07), while ICU length of stay (MD +3.57 days, 95% CI –0.27 to 7.42) and hospital length of stay (MD 2.17 days, 95% CI –5.29 to 9.63) did not differ significantly between groups. There was no statistically significant difference between groups in RRT incidence (OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.68-2.02), infection (OR 1.55, 95% CI 0.94-2.57), bleeding events (OR 1.84, 95% CI 0.52-6.53), or arrhythmia (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.24-3.99). Similarly, no significant differences were observed in ischemia (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.14-4.15), stroke (OR 2.39, 95% CI 0.74-7.67), or thrombosis (OR 2.28, 95% CI 0.31-16.74), although stroke and thrombosis estimates warrant further study. Conclusion: Levosimendan improved successful VA-ECMO weaning in cardiogenic shock but did not significantly reduce mortality, with comparable safety outcomes between groups. Given limited randomized evidence and substantial heterogeneity, large randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify its role during VA-ECMO support.
title: Abstract 15406: Levosimendan as an Adjunct During Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock requires rapid risk stratification, but invasive cardiac output is often unavailable at support decisions. Objectives: To test whether admission estimated cardiac power output (eCPO) from cuff vitals is associated with in-hospital mortality after Impella support and externally validate the findings in MIMIC-IV. Methods: We analyzed 276 institutional Impella recipients with complete admission HR, SBP, and DBP, then validated findings in MIMIC-IV v3.1 using first adult Impella plus cardiogenic-shock ICU stays with complete noninvasive HR/SBP/DBP in the first 6 ICU hours. Internal eCPO used restricted cubic spline Firth logistic regression; MIMIC-IV used adjusted logistic regression and repeated cross-validated index comparison. Results: Internal in-hospital death occurred in 101 patients (36.6%); median eCPO was 3.97 (IQR: 2.88-5.61). Internal adjusted mortality at eCPO 0.6 W vs 1.0 W differed by +2.9 percentage points. MIMIC-IV included 139 patients, with 72 deaths (51.8%), median eCPO 2.91 (IQR: 2.09-4.17), adjusted OR 1.01 per 0.2 W lower eCPO, and eCPO AUROC 0.679. In both cohorts, Shock Index or Modified Shock Index outperformed eCPO. Conclusions: Admission eCPO was feasible but did not outperform simpler admission-vitals indices. MIMIC-IV validation supports the main conclusion and reinforces the need for calibration before using invasive-CPO thresholds.
title: Abstract 15417: Admission Estimated Cardiac Power and Mortality After Impella for Cardiogenic Shock: MIMIC-IV Validation

abstract: Background: In patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS), peak high-sensitivity troponin-T (hsTnT) has been associated with an increased risk of heart failure; however, whether hsTnT is independently associated with subsequent heart failure regardless of the final diagnosis is currently unknown. Purpose: To examine the short- and long-term associations between peak hsTnT and subsequent hospitalization or outpatient contact for heart failure in subjects with suspected ACS stratified by final diagnosis, i.e., myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or suspected myocardial infarction. Methods/Approach: We used Danish nationwide registry data from 2012 through 2019 to identify individuals with no prior history of heart failure who had two hsTnT measurements (99th percentile: 13.5 ng/l) taken at presentation, 1-7 hours apart, during hospitalization for suspected ACS. First, we stratified the population according to the final diagnosis made during hospitalization (i.e., myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or suspected myocardial infarction). We then grouped individuals per peak quartiles (Q1-Q4) based on the first two hsTnT measurements (Q1: <=9 ng/l, Q2: 10-19 ng/l, Q3: 20-263 ng/l, Q4: >=264 ng/l). Finally, we calculated the standardized absolute risk of hospitalization or outpatient contact for heart failure at 0-30 days and 31-365 days within each hsTnT peak quartile category, using multivariable Cox regression with average treatment effect modeling. Results: We included 26,835 individuals; 38.8% received a diagnosis of myocardial infarction, 5.1% unstable angina, and 56.1% suspected myocardial infarction. The median age was 64.2 years, 59.5% were male, 18.1% had coronary artery disease, and 7.2% had undergone prior revascularization. A total of 1,122 individuals were diagnosed with heart failure within the first 30 days, and 707 individuals were diagnosed between days 31-365. The absolute risk of heart failure was positively associated with peak hsTnT concentrations in each group, at both 0-30 days and 31-365 days. The final diagnosis modified the prognostic implications of peak hsTnT (P-interaction=0.03), but a relative gradient across the peak hsTnT quartiles remained. Individuals with suspected myocardial infarction in the Q4 group had a very high standardized absolute risk of incident heart failure (0-30 days: 14.28%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.66 to 17.91; 31-365 days: 8.53%, 95% CI: 5.24 to 11.82). The results are shown in Table 1. Conclusions: In individuals presenting with suspected ACS, higher peak hsTnT concentrations were associated with higher risks of subsequent heart failure within both 0-30 days and 31-365 days. This risk gradient was observed irrespectively of whether individuals were discharged with a final diagnosis of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or suspected myocardial infarction.
title: Abstract 15431: The Association Between Peak High-Sensitivity Troponin-T Concentration and Risk of Heart Failure in Patients with Myocardial Infarction, Unstable Angina, and Suspected Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: The optimal percutaneous coronary intervention strategy for coronary bifurcation lesions remains uncertain. Drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty offers a stent-less approach that may preserve vessel physiology and reduce metal burden. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing DCB with drug-eluting stents (DES) for coronary bifurcation interventions. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420261417555), PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to June 2026. Randomized and observational studies comparing DCB and DES in coronary bifurcation lesions were included. Random-effects meta-analyses generated pooled risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), target vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), target lesion revascularization (TLR), target vessel revascularization (TVR), restenosis, cardiovascular death, late lumen loss (LLL), and minimal luminal diameter (MLD). Results: Seven studies involving 3,723 patients (DCB: 1,768; DES: 1,995) were included. DCB significantly reduced TV-MI (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34-0.83; I 2 =0%; p=0.006) and MACE (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52-0.80; I 2 =0%; p<0.001). No significant differences were observed for TLR (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.26-1.48; I 2 =73.1%; p=0.287), restenosis (RR 0.34, 95% CI 0.07-1.55; I 2 =58.3%; p=0.163), or cardiovascular death (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.70-1.34; I 2 =0%; p=0.851). Side-branch MLD was similar between groups (MD 0.06 mm, 95% CI –0.27 to 0.39; I 2 =95.5%; p=0.729), whereas side-branch LLL was significantly lower with DCB (MD –0.29 mm, 95% CI –0.54 to –0.04; I 2 =83.4%; p=0.022). Main-vessel MLD (MD 0.13 mm, 95% CI –0.34 to 0.60; I 2 =98.3%; p=0.558) and main-vessel LLL (MD –0.07 mm, 95% CI –0.18 to 0.04; I 2 =77.2%; p=0.210) were comparable. TVR was higher with DCB (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.19-5.52; I 2 =0%; p=0.016), although this finding was based on only two studies. Conclusions: In coronary bifurcation lesions, DCB angioplasty was associated with lower rates of MACE and TV-MI, similar rates of TLR, restenosis, cardiovascular mortality, and comparable main-vessel angiographic outcomes versus DES. DCB also reduced side-branch late lumen loss, supporting its role as a promising alternative to DES in selected bifurcation lesions. Larger randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed.
title: Abstract 15440: Clinical Outcomes of Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty Compared with Drug-Eluting Stents in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction Left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus is a major barrier to rhythm-control procedures and LAA closure. Yet dense spontaneous echo contrast, sludge, complex anatomy, and extremely slow flow may mimic thrombus, creating high-stakes uncertainty when embolic and bleeding risks coexist. Case A 78-year-old woman with longstanding persistent atrial fibrillation, rheumatic mitral valve disease status post commissurotomy, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and prior LAA thrombus while on apixaban was evaluated for rhythm-control therapy for persistent symptoms and recurrent HFpEF decompensation. After transition back to warfarin, serial transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) continued to suggest LAA thrombus with very slow appendageal flow. Intensification with aspirin and a higher INR target was complicated by gastric ulcer bleeding, prompting aspirin discontinuation and highlighting the need for a nonpharmacologic stroke-prevention strategy. Although TEE findings initially limited procedural options, delayed-phase cardiac computed tomography (CCT) showed no LAA thrombus, allowing reconsideration of combined catheter ablation and percutaneous LAA occlusion. On the procedure day, preprocedural TEE demonstrated echodense material at the LAA tip, highly suggestive of thrombus with sludge. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) confirmed distal echodensity. Contrast injection resulted in progressive appendage opacification, arguing against occlusive thrombus and supporting severe blood stasis. After multidisciplinary discussion and intraprocedural imaging, the team proceeded with percutaneous LAA occlusion. A 31-mm Watchman device was implanted, meeting PASS criteria for position, anchor, size, and seal, with no residual leak or instability. Concomitant ICE-guided pulsed-field pulmonary vein isolation was performed, followed by cardioversion to sinus rhythm, without device shift, embolic event, or procedural complications. Discussion This case highlights a rare LAA imaging dilemma: a thrombus-like echodensity on TEE and ICE, absent on delayed-phase CCT, clarified by contrast opacification. Severe LAA stasis can mimic thrombus, while complete contrast filling argues against an occlusive clot. When conventional TEE suggests thrombus, but diagnostic uncertainty persists, additional imaging strategies should be considered, including contrast echocardiography and, in selected cases, pharmacologic augmentation with isoproterenol to increase LAA flow and improve thrombus discrimination. For patients trapped between embolic risk, failed or intensified anticoagulation, and major bleeding, multimodality imaging can transform an apparent contraindication into a selected procedural strategy, enabling LAA occlusion and rhythm-control therapy when anticoagulation alone becomes unsafe or ineffective.
title: Abstract 15451: The Phantom of the Left Atrial Appendage: A Multimodality Imaging-Guided Strategy for Suspected Thrombus

abstract: True coronary bifurcation lesions, defined by significant disease in both the main vessel and side branch, account for 15-20% of all percutaneous coronary interventions and carry higher rates of target lesion failure than non-bifurcation disease. The provisional stenting approach, treating the side branch only if necessary, has historically been favoured for simplicity, while the DK crush two-stent technique addresses ostial side branch disease systematically. Prior DKCRUSH trials demonstrated superiority of DK crush over provisional stenting in complex true bifurcations; DKCRUSH-VIII, the most recent anchor trial, examined this relationship in a refined population. We sought to provide an updated pooled estimate incorporating all available randomised data.We performed a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing systematic two-stent techniques versus provisional stenting in true coronary bifurcation lesions (Medina 1,1,1 or 0,1,1 classification). Primary outcome was target lesion failure or major adverse cardiovascular events at 12 months. A random-effects model with REML estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment was applied.We performed an analysis of 2 randomised trials (NordicBalticIV2020 and EBCMAIN2021) contributing the composite major adverse cardiovascular event endpoint. Systematic two-stent strategy showed a directional trend toward lower major adverse cardiovascular events versus provisional stenting that did not reach conventional significance (HR 0.73 [95% CI 0.16-3.22]; P=0.22). Between-study heterogeneity was absent (I 2 =0%; Q=0.38, P=0.54). With k=2, a prediction interval was not estimable. Data from DKCRUSHV2017 and DEFINITIONII2020 contributed separately to the target lesion failure endpoint and were consistent in direction with the MACE result.Systematic two-stent strategy shows a consistent directional signal toward lower major adverse cardiovascular events across contemporary randomised bifurcation trials, with target lesion failure benefit established in DKCRUSHV2017 and DEFINITIONII2020. The pooled MACE estimate across NordicBalticIV2020 and EBCMAIN2021 is directionally consistent but does not reach significance with the current evidence base (HR 0.73, P=0.22, k=2). These data support systematic two-stent implantation as a preferred strategy in complex true coronary bifurcation lesions while acknowledging that a larger pooled MACE signal requires further trial evidence.
title: Abstract 15464: Systematic Two-Stent versus Provisional Stenting in True Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: An Updated Pairwise Meta-Analysis Incorporating Recent Trial Data

abstract: Background: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) affects up to 1.6 million Americans and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Multiple interventional strategies now exist transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER), transcatheter valve replacement (T-TVR), surgical repair (STVr), and surgical replacement (STVR) but no trial has compared all modalities simultaneously, and the optimal strategy remains undefined. Methods: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) of studies comparing two or more interventions for TR. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality (ACM); secondary outcomes included heart failure hospitalisation (HFH), new permanent pacemaker implantation (PM), major bleeding (BL), and renal complications (REN). Medical therapy (MT) was the reference node. SUCRA was used to rank treatments. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE and CINeMA. MCMC was implemented with gemtc/JAGS (4 chains х 50,000 iterations) and cross-verified with PyMC. Results: Forty-three studies (5 RCTs, 8 PSM, 30 observational/registry; N ≈ 34,000) were included. For ACM (24 studies, 5 nodes), T-TEER significantly reduced mortality versus MT (OR 0.62, 95% CrI 0.42-0.91; SUCRA 82%); STVr showed a significant benefit (OR 0.52, 95% CrI 0.31-0.88; SUCRA 74%); T-TVR was non-significant (OR 0.80, 95% CrI 0.44-1.46); STVR showed a neutral-to-harmful signal (OR 1.18, 95% CrI 0.78-1.79; SUCRA 23%), driven by TRIGISTRY registry data (overall HR 1.45 in mixed TRI-SCORE cohort). T-TEER and T-TVR both significantly reduced HFH. T-TVR carried markedly elevated pacemaker risk (OR 9.12 vs MT). T-TEER demonstrated the most favourable cross-outcome profile (SUCRA: mortality 82%, HFH 89%, renal 84%). Heterogeneity was moderate for ACM (τ 0.34). Global and local inconsistency tests were non-significant. All models converged (R̂ max 1.003). Conclusions: T-TEER demonstrated the most consistent benefit across efficacy and safety outcomes. T-TVR reduced hospitalisation and renal events but carries substantial pacemaker and bleeding burden. STVR did not improve survival overall and may harm selected patients with advanced disease. These findings support T-TEER as the preferred intervention for eligible patients with severe TR while reinforcing the need for TRI-SCORE risk stratification to guide surgical referral. Randomised trials comparing transcatheter strategies head-to-head are urgently needed.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian network meta-analysis of Forty-three studies (5 RCTs, 8 PSM, 30 observational/registry; N approximately 34,000).
appraisal.main_limitation: Predominantly observational and registry inputs, so estimates are exposed to confounding and selection.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian network meta-analysis ranks T-TEER most favourably across outcomes among interventions for tricuspid regurgitation.

title: Abstract 15468: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Transcatheter and Surgical Interventions for Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Distal embolization and microvascular obstruction remain important limitations of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), contributing to impaired myocardial reperfusion and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis during primary PCI for STEMI. Methods: A systematic literature search through Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was performed through May 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis versus placebo or conventional PCI in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI were included. Thrombolytic agents included prourokinase, urokinase, alteplase, and tenecteplase. Outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial reperfusion parameters, and bleeding complications. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed according to thrombolytic agent. Results: Eleven randomized controlled trials comprising 2,457 patients were included. Adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis reduced MACE at 3-6 months (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.45-0.91; p=0.01), with no difference in 30-day MACE (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.60-1.67; p=0.99). Compared with placebo/conventional PCI, intracoronary thrombolysis improved post-PCI TIMI 3 flow (RR 1.06, 95% CI 1.01-1.12; p=0.02), myocardial blush grade 2-3 (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.07-1.41; p=0.004), and ST-segment resolution >70% at 60-90 minutes (RR 1.24, 95% CI 1.12-1.38; p<0.0001). The reduction in intermediate-term MACE was driven primarily by prourokinase/urokinase-based strategies (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.36-0.78). Major bleeding was not increased (RR 1.23, 95% CI 0.55-2.74; p=0.62). Conclusions: Adjunctive intracoronary thrombolysis during primary PCI improved myocardial reperfusion and reduced intermediate-term cardiovascular events without increasing major bleeding. The greatest benefit was observed with prourokinase/urokinase-based strategies. Further randomized studies are needed to identify the optimal thrombolytic agent and define the role of intracoronary thrombolysis in contemporary STEMI reperfusion practice.
title: Abstract 15469: Clinical and Procedural Outcomes of Adjunctive Intracoronary Thrombolysis During Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 2,457 Patients from Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: Balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve replacement (BE-TAVR) via the SAPIEN platform has been evaluated against surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) across the surgical risk spectrum in four randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A systematic synthesis of echocardiographic and cardiac remodeling outcomes across all four SAPIEN-platform RCTs and valve generations has not been performed. Objectives: To compare echocardiographic outcomes and cardiac remodeling following BE-TAVR versus SAVR, with prespecified subgroup analysis by valve generation (early-generation SAPIEN/SAPIEN XT versus contemporary-generation SAPIEN 3/SAPIEN 3 Ultra). Methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of four RCTs (PARTNER 1A, 2A, 3, RHEIA; n=4,101). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. The primary outcome was moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation (PVR). Secondary outcomes included mean transprosthetic gradient, aortic valve area (AVA), LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and LV mass index (LVMI). RV function and valvular pathology were exploratory outcomes. Results: BE-TAVR was associated with significantly higher moderate/severe PVR at 30 days (RR 8.33, 95% CI 3.83-18.13) and 1 year (RR 4.02, 95% CI 1.59-10.17), with no significant difference by valve generation at either timepoint (subgroup P = 0.596 and P = 0.204, respectively). A marked valve-generation interaction was identified for transprosthetic hemodynamics (P < 0.0001 at both timepoints): early-generation devices demonstrated lower gradients and larger AVA than SAVR (MD -1.15 mmHg at 30 days; -0.76 mmHg at 1 year), whereas contemporary-generation devices demonstrated higher gradients and smaller AVA (MD +2.08 mmHg at 30 days; +2.13 mmHg at 1 year), with a null pooled estimate obscuring these opposing effects. No between-group difference in LVEF was observed. BE-TAVR was associated with persistently higher LVMI at 30 days (MD +7.49 g/m 2 , 95% CI 4.55-10.43) and 1 year (MD +7.17 g/m 2 , 95% CI 2.73-11.60), alongside higher LV hypertrophy rates (RR 1.35 at 30 days; 1.40 at 1 year; P < 0.01). BE-TAVR was also associated with better preservation of RV function (TAPSE MD +0.66 cm at 30 days; +0.45 cm at 1 year; P < 0.0001) and lower rates of moderate/severe tricuspid and mitral regurgitation at both timepoints. Conclusion: Despite advances in device technology, BE-TAVR remains associated with higher PVR irrespective of valve generation. Contemporary-generation devices carry higher transprosthetic gradients and smaller AVA than SAVR, findings concealed when generations are pooled, while early-generation devices showed the opposite. The sustained LVMI elevation and higher LV hypertrophy rates constitute a prespecified remodeling signal. Future TAVR trials should report echocardiographic outcomes according to valve generation.
title: Abstract 15473: Echocardiographic Outcomes and Cardiac Remodeling After Balloon-Expandable TAVR versus SAVR: A Generation-Stratified Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Radiofrequency (RF) or ultrasound (US) mediated renal denervation (RDN) have emerged as catheter-based device treatment for resistant hypertension. Both approaches effectively reduce blood pressure (BP) compared with sham, however, there are no randomized trials comparing the two modalities. Methods: A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed using second-generation sham-controlled randomized trials evaluating RDN in patients receiving antihypertensive medications. Five trials were included (SPYRAL HTN-ON MED Pilot, RADIANCE-HTN TRIO, REQUIRE, RADIOSOUND-HTN, and IBERIS-HTN; n=676). The primary outcome was change in 24-hour ambulatory systolic BP (SBP). Secondary outcomes included daytime SBP, nighttime SBP, office SBP, and 24-hour ambulatory diastolic BP (DBP). Results: In the primary analysis, neither RF (MD -5.3 mmHg, 95% CI -11.9 to 1.3) nor ultrasound RDN (MD -5.6 mmHg, 95% CI -12.4 to 1.2) reached significance versus sham, with high heterogeneity (I 2 =82.5%) and significant network inconsistency (p<0.0001), driven by the REQUIRE trial. The RF versus ultrasound difference was 0.3 mmHg (95% CI -7.5 to 8.1), indicating equivalence. On sensitivity analysis excluding REQUIRE, both RF (MD -6.3 mmHg, p=0.048) and ultrasound (MD -8.6 mmHg, p=0.029) were significant. For secondary outcomes, RF significantly reduced nighttime SBP (MD -8.9 mmHg, p<0.0001), office SBP (MD -7.5 mmHg, p<0.0001), and 24-hour DBP (MD -4.4 mmHg, p<0.0001) with zero heterogeneity. Ultrasound significantly reduced daytime SBP (MD -9.1 mmHg, p=0.029). Conclusions: In patients on antihypertensive therapy, the efficacy of BP reduction was similar between RF and US renal denervation in second-generation sham-controlled randomized trials with neither modality being superior. When methodologically robust trials are considered, second-generation RDN demonstrates consistent BP reduction as adjunct to antihypertensive therapy, with no basis for preferring one modality over the other.
title: Abstract 15480: Radiofrequency versus Ultrasound Renal Denervation as Adjunctive Therapy for Hypertension: A Network Meta-Analysis of Second-Generation Sham-Controlled Randomized Trials

abstract: Keywords: multiple myeloma; MINOCA; cardiac amyloidosis; ST-segment elevation; global longitudinal strain; thrombocytopenia Introduction : Persistent ST-segment elevation with troponin elevation usually suggests acute coronary occlusion. Infiltrative cardiac disorders may mimic STEMI despite non-obstructive coronaries. Cardiac involvement in multiple myeloma (MM) is uncommon and may reflect amyloid deposition, myocardial infiltration, or microvascular dysfunction. We report a case of newly diagnosed IgA-kappa MM with a STEMI-like phenotype, troponin elevation, preserved systolic function, abnormal global longitudinal strain (GLS), and non-obstructive coronaries. Patient Information: A man in his 70s with newly diagnosed IgA-kappa MM, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, aortic stenosis, and tobacco use was referred after a preoperative ECG showed new anterior ST-segment elevation. Clinical Findings & Timeline: He was stable and denied chest pain or dyspnea. ECG showed persistent anteroseptal ST-segment elevation with Q waves in V1-V4. High-sensitivity troponin I peaked at 1,766 ng/L. Platelets decreased to 19,000/mcL, attributed to marrow involvement from MM. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Urgent angiography showed non-obstructive coronary disease, excluding type 1 myocardial infarction. Echocardiography revealed hyperdynamic LV function (ejection fraction >65%), mild concentric hypertrophy, severely reduced GLS (-9.2%), RV hypertrophy with RA dilation, and a small pericardial effusion without tamponade. Bone marrow biopsy showed 70-80% plasma cell involvement; Congo red staining was negative. The combination of abnormal strain imaging, biventricular remodeling, pericardial effusion, and troponin elevation raised concern for occult cardiac involvement. Cardiac MRI and PYP scintigraphy were recommended. Therapeutic Interventions: Aspirin was initiated, and heparin was stopped due to thrombocytopenia. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation during catheterization was converted with amiodarone. Anticoagulation was deferred. Dexamethasone was started with acyclovir and allopurinol prophylaxis. Follow-up & Outcomes: He remained asymptomatic and was discharged with cardiology and hematology-oncology follow-up. Discussion & Synthesis: This case highlights a rare STEMI mimic in a newly diagnosed MM patient. Persistent anterior ST-segment elevation, Q waves, and marked troponin elevation suggested acute myocardial infarction, yet angiography revealed no culprit lesion. Abnormal GLS, right-sided cardiac remodeling, and pericardial effusion raised suspicion for occult cardiac involvement related to the plasma cell disorder. Recognition of infiltrative diseases should be considered when ECG abnormalities and biomarker elevation occur with non-obstructive coronaries. Advanced cardiac imaging may guide diagnosis and management.
title: Abstract 15490: Persistent Anterior ST-Segment Elevation and Troponin Elevation with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma

abstract: Background: Center-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains underutilized due to geographic, financial, and scheduling barriers, particularly among older adults and underserved populations. Mobile health (mHealth) and home-based telerehabilitation are emerging alternatives, but the magnitude of benefit on functional capacity and how it varies by age remains unclear. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that mHealth or home-based telerehabilitation improves functional capacity in adults with ischemic heart disease (IHD) compared with center-based CR and usual care, and that the effect is moderated by participant age. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Web of Science for randomized controlled trials published January 2023 to February 2026 evaluating digitally delivered or monitored exercise rehabilitation in adults post-myocardial infarction or post-percutaneous coronary intervention. Primary outcomes were six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and peak oxygen uptake (VO2 peak). Random-effects models with REML estimation pooled Hedges' g and weighted mean differences. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 , robustness with leave-one-out analyses, age effects with mixed-effects meta-regression, and certainty with GRADE. Results: 12 trials enrolling 1,631 participants from 8 countries were included. Pooled walking distance increased by 38.82 m (95% CI, 15.83 to 61.81; p<0.001; k=5; I 2 =89.3%; GRADE moderate), exceeding the accepted minimal clinically important difference for 6MWD. VO2 peak improved by 1.56 mL/kg/min (95% CI, 0.51 to 2.61; p=0.004; k=5; I 2 =63.4%; GRADE low). Versus center-based CR, telerehabilitation yielded a moderate standardized benefit (g=0.70; 95% CI, 0.07 to 1.33; p=0.028; I 2 =83.1%), which remained significant after excluding the most influential study (g=0.34; 95% CI, 0.09 to 0.60; p=0.009; I 2 =17.1%). Versus usual care, the pooled effect was g=1.82 (95% CI, 0.00 to 3.64; p=0.049), attenuating to g=0.91 (95% CI, 0.60 to 1.22; p<0.001) when an extreme outlier was removed. Meta-regression showed adults under 65 years gained 57.30 m (95% CI, 30.84 to 83.75; p<0.001), with older adults gaining 37.32 m less (p=0.051); age explained 40.9% of between-study variance for walking but did not moderate VO2. Conclusions: Digital and home-based CR produces clinically meaningful improvements in walking-based functional capacity in adults with IHD, comparable to center-based programs in younger adults but smaller in those aged 65 and older. However, cardiorespiratory fitness improved similarly across age groups, suggesting physiological benefit is preserved in older adults despite smaller walking gains. Heterogeneity across protocols and technologies warrants standardization before broad implementation.
title: Abstract 15501: Mobile and Home-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation Compared with Center-Based Care for Functional Capacity in Adults with Ischemic Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Introduction: Environmental exposure to toxic heavy metals like lead and cadmium promotes systemic inflammation and accelerated atherogenesis. Clinical trials show these toxicants drive secondary cardiovascular events, especially in vulnerable populations. We evaluated whether family income-to-poverty ratio (PIR) is associated with a disproportionate heavy metal body burden among US adults with established ischemic heart disease (IHD). Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional cohort analysis using pooled data from recent NHANES cycles. This was split between pre -Covid (2017-2020) and post Covid (2021-2023). The study was restricted to adults aged 40 and older with a verified history of IHD, defined by self-reported prior myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization (PCI or CABG). Socioeconomic status was categorized via PIR: Low Income (PIR less than 1.0), Middle Income (PIR 1.0 to 3.0), and High Income (PIR greater than 3.0). Primary endpoints were whole-blood lead concentrations (ug/dL) and urinary cadmium concentrations (ug/g creatinine). Multivariable linear regression models calculated adjusted geometric means, controlling for age, sex, race, active smoking status, and occupational exposures. Results: The final sample included 2,114 participants with established IHD. Graded socioeconomic disparities were observed in heavy metal bioaccumulation. Low-income patients (PIR less than 1.0) had significantly higher adjusted geometric mean blood lead levels compared to high-income patients (PIR greater than 3.0) (2.04 vs 1.12 ug/dL, p less than 0.001). Urinary cadmium was also significantly elevated among low-income patients (0.61 vs 0.29 ug/g, p less than 0.001). In fully adjusted multivariable regression models, low income remained a powerful independent predictor of toxicant load, associated with a 45 percent relative increase in blood lead (p less than 0.001) and a 34 percent relative increase in urinary cadmium (p = 0.002). Conclusions: Socioeconomically disadvantaged US adults with established IHD carry a significantly higher body burden of atherotoxic heavy metals. This disparity persists independent of smoking or occupational history. Environmental screening and mitigation in resource-limited neighborhoods may serve as an essential structural intervention in secondary prevention.
title: Abstract 15504: Income-Based Disparities in Toxic Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation Among US Adults with Established Ischemic Heart Disease: An NHANES Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Long IVC filters may become part of the thrombotic substrate rather than remaining passive protection against embolization. We report an intermediate-high-risk PE in which venography confirmed thrombus attached to and filling a decades-old IVC filter, managed with a source-first mechanical thrombectomy strategy targeting both the caval thrombus and bilateral pulmonary emboli. Patient Information: A 53-year-old man with recurrent VTE, bilateral PE eight months prior, chronic DVT status post IVC filter placement in 1997 and unrevealing hypercoagulable evaluation presented with progressive exertional dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and worsening left lower-extremity pain. He had discontinued apixaban and insulin two weeks earlier because of medication access barriers. Diagnostic Assessment: Admitted to the ICU with DKA. ECG showed sinus tachycardia with RBBB and T-wave inversions. Troponin peaked at 37.4 pg/mL and BNP was 72 pg/mL. CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated extensive bilateral PE. He was classified as PESI class III. Abdominal radiography confirmed an IVC filter at L3. Venous duplex demonstrated acute proximal left DVT. Therapeutic Interventions: The patient received systemic anticoagulation and ICU-level of care for DKA. On hospital day two, catheter-based thrombectomy was performed. IVC venography revealed a large filling defect attached to and filling the chronic IVC filter. Suction thrombectomy of the IVC thrombus was performed first with two aspiration passes, achieving complete resolution of filter-associated thrombus on repeat venography. Bilateral pulmonary mechanical thrombectomy was then performed. Repeat pulmonary angiography showed near-complete resolution of thrombus burden with excellent arterial blush. The IVC filter was left in place. Follow-up & Outcomes: Dyspnea and chest pain improved after thrombectomy. DKA resolved. He was transitioned to apixaban and basal-bolus insulin and discharged home. Discussion: This case highlights a critical gap in long-term IVC filter management. Existing data on filter-related thrombotic risk are limited beyond 9 years of follow-up, while this patient’s approximately 28-year time represents an extreme duration. Venographic confirmation of thrombus filling the filter, combined with simultaneous proximal DVT, extensive superficial venous thrombosis, and bilateral PE, suggests that the filter functioned less as a protective barrier and more as part of a central thrombotic source. Combined IVC and pulmonary thrombectomy has been described. However, the source-first approach, clearing the caval nidus before treating PE, is not well documented in the setting of a 28-year-old filter. This case underscores the need to evaluate chronically indwelling IVC filters and to consider source-directed mechanical thrombectomy when recurrent PE occurs in their presence.
title: Abstract 15515: Twenty-Eight Years Later: Filter-Associated Caval Thrombus and Bilateral Pulmonary Embolism Treated with Source-First Thrombectomy

abstract: Introduction: Lipoprotein(a) is a genetic, oxidised phospholipid-rich particle driving premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, fixed Lp(a) thresholds poorly capture heterogeneous phenotypes. Many with moderate elevations suffer early events while others with extreme levels do not. Artificial intelligence can identify these high-risk Lp(a) phenotypes to guide preventive therapy. Methods: Retrospective cohort of 10,000 adults with baseline Lp(a) measurement. Primary endpoint: premature myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or coronary revascularization. Patients stratified into four Lp(a) phenotypic tiers (<75, 75-125, 125-250, >250 nmol/L). XGBoost machine learning with SHAP analysis identified high-risk phenotypes. Adjusted Cox proportional hazards models quantified event risk. Results: Among 10,000 patients (44.5% female, 55.5% male) followed for a median of 8.4 years, 1,150 primary premature ASCVD events occurred (incidence 14.3 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI: 13.5-15.1). Events comprised 420 premature MIs (36.5%; 95% CI: 33.7-39.4), 280 ischemic strokes (24.3%; 95% CI: 21.9-26.9), and 450 coronary revascularizations (39.1%; 95% CI: 36.3-42.0). Compared with Lp(a) <75 nmol/L, adjusted HRs for composite premature ASCVD were: 1.34 (95% CI: 1.26-1.42) for 75-125 nmol/L, 1.78 (95% CI: 1.65-1.92) for 125-250 nmol/L, and 2.45 (95% CI: 2.22-2.71) for >250 nmol/L (all P<0.001). In the extreme-risk tier (>250 nmol/L, n=500), event rates were: MI 11.8% (95% CI: 9.2-14.9), stroke 6.2% (95% CI: 4.4-8.7), revascularization 12.6% (95% CI: 9.9-15.8). The XGBoost model achieved a C-statistic of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.784-0.801). SHAP analysis showed hs-CRP>3.0 mg/L multiplied Lp(a) risk by 1.62 (95% CI: 1.48-1.78). For Lp(a)>125 nmol/L with hs-CRP>3.0 mg/L or ApoB>100 mg/dL, aHR for premature MI was 3.12 (95% CI: 2.80-3.48). NRI was 22.4% (95% CI: 19.8-25.0; P<0.001). Conclusion: AI-guided phenotyping identifies graded Lp(a)-associated risk for premature ASCVD, with extreme elevations conferring a 2.45-fold hazard. Machine learning outperforms fixed thresholds, revealing synergistic amplification by inflammation and ApoB. These high-risk phenotypes inform targeted allocation of emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies to prevent early myocardial infarction and stroke.
title: Abstract 15517: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Identification of High-Risk Lipoprotein(a) Phenotypes Associated with Premature Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 10,000 Patients

abstract: Introduction: Chest pain with troponin elevation prompts evaluation for acute coronary syndrome (ACS). It is important to consider alternate causes when presentation is atypical. Myeloid sarcoma, an extramedullary neoplasm of immature myeloid cells, is a rare cause of a mediastinal mass and a deceptive ACS mimic. Patient Information: A 71-year-old woman with COPD, hypertension, complete heart block with pacemaker, and severe aortic stenosis status-post transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) 3 years prior who presented with one week of constant 10/10 chest pain at rest and exertion, dyspnea, and night sweats. Clinical Findings and Timeline: Physical examination demonstrated hypoxemia (SpO2 88% on 3 L) and sinus tachycardia. Labs revealed leukocytosis, normocytic anemia, acute kidney injury, elevated NT-proBNP of 2313 pg/mL, elevated D-Dimer of 2.19, and high-sensitivity troponin of 74 ng/L, peak 84 ng/L. No ischemic changes on EKG. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Coronary angiography and nuclear stress testing were normal. Echocardiography showed no regional wall motion abnormalities. SPEP negative. A CT obtained for suspected pulmonary embolism (elevated D-dimer) excluded PE but revealed a large subcarinal mass encasing the right pulmonary artery and compressing both mainstem bronchi. Prior CT had shown only stable mediastinal adenopathy, which enlarged into this mass within approximately one month, with a new pulmonary nodule. Myeloid sarcoma with monocytic differentiation was confirmed on endobronchial ultrasound-guided needle aspiration. Peripheral flow cytometry showed a circulating abnormal monocytic population with rare myeloblasts, consistent with aggressive acute myeloid leukemia. Therapeutic Interventions and Outcomes: After bronchoscopy, she could not be extubated due to development of hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure. Progressive encephalopathy, fevers, and septic shock precluded extubation. Patient was transferred to MICU. Discussion and Synthesis: Myeloid sarcoma infrequently presents as a mediastinal mass mimicking ACS. Pulmonary artery encasement and bronchial compression can produce chest pain, dyspnea, and modest troponin elevation without coronary disease. Therefore, negative coronary evaluation should raise concern for non-coronary thoracic pathology.
title: Abstract 15525: Myeloid Sarcoma Mimicking Acute Coronary Syndrome: Rapidly Progressive Mediastinal Mass Encasing the Pulmonary Artery

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains the leading cause of mortality following acute myocardial infarction despite advances in cardiovascular care. Older adults comprise an increasing proportion of patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) complicated by CS, yet outcomes across elderly age groups remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the impact of age on outcomes among patients with NSTEMI-CS. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified adults with NSTEMI who developed CS within 7 days of the index event. Patients were stratified into three age groups: 65-74 years (n=14,876), 75-84 years (n=16,604), and 85-100 years (n=14,015). A propensity score-matched analysis compared patients aged 65-74 and 85-100 years, adjusting for demographics, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, heart failure, atrial fibrillation/flutter, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pulmonary hypertension, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea (Table 1). After matching, 10,435 patients remained in each cohort. Outcomes were assessed at 180 days. Results: Mortality increased progressively with age. Among unmatched cohorts, all-cause mortality was 12.5% in patients aged 65-74 years, 14.1% in those aged 75-84 years, and 17.0% in those aged 85-100 years. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly higher survival among patients aged 65-74 years compared with those aged 85-100 years (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.61-0.73; p<0.001) (Figure 1). Conversely, the younger cohort experienced higher rates of ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation/cardiac arrest (3.37% vs 1.66%; HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.20-1.92; p<0.001), heart failure hospitalization (2.96% vs 1.91%; RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.17-2.07; p=0.002), and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation (0.80% vs 0.27%; HR 2.38, 95% CI 1.54-3.67; p<0.001) (Table 2). Rates of percutaneous coronary intervention, cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation, permanent pacemaker implantation, and palliative care utilization were similar . Conclusions: Among patients with NSTEMI-CS, advancing age was associated with progressively higher mortality, with the greatest risk observed in those aged 85-100 years. Despite lower mortality, patients aged 65-74 years experienced greater long-term cardiovascular morbidity, including ventricular arrhythmias, heart failure hospitalization, and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation. These findings may aid risk stratification and post-discharge management of elderly patients with NSTEMI-CS.
title: Abstract 15532: Age-Stratified Outcomes Following Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis, leading to a significant increase in procedures over the last 10 years. Despite this growth, there has not been a thorough review of Medicare reimbursement trends under the Inpatient Prospective Payment System. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that Medicare reimbursement for transcatheter aortic valve replacement has declined over the past decade, despite increased procedure volume. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of Medicare Inpatient Prospective Payment System reimbursement from 2015 to 2025. We looked at payments for MS-DRG 266 (Endovascular Cardiac Valve Replacement and Supplement Procedures with Major Complication or Comorbidity) and MS-DRG 267 (without Major Complication or Comorbidity). To calculate annual payments, we multiplied national standardized operating and capital base rates from CMS Tables 1A through 1E by the MS-DRG relative weights from Table 5, using data from the Inpatient Prospective Payment System Final Rule files. We adjusted all amounts for inflation to 2025 dollars using the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index calculator. All calculations were performed and verified in Microsoft Excel. For each diagnosis-related group, we calculated the compound annual growth rate and the total percentage change. Results: We found that nominal reimbursement dropped steadily, even though base rates increased each year. For MS-DRG 266, payments fell from $52,742 in 2015 to $42,637 in 2025, a 19.2% decrease (compound annual growth rate: -2.10%). For MS-DRG 267, payments went from $39,602 to $33,483, a 15.5% decrease (compound annual growth rate: -1.66%). When adjusted for inflation, the declines were even greater: MS-DRG 266 dropped by 41.1% in real terms, with a per-case shortfall of $29,759. MS-DRG 267 dropped by 38.4%, with a per-case shortfall of $20,876. The main reason for these declines was a steady reduction in MS-DRG relative weights, which went from 8.99 to 5.99 for MS-DRG 266 and from 6.75 to 4.70 for MS-DRG 267. Conclusions: Medicare reimbursement for transcatheter aortic valve replacement has dropped by 41.1% in real terms over the past ten years, mainly because MS-DRG relative weights have been steadily reduced. Hospitals now receive $29,759 less per complex case than they did in 2015. These findings raise serious concerns about the sustainability of these programs, especially for hospitals with lower volumes, and may affect patient access, fellowship training in structural heart procedures, and fair access to advanced cardiovascular care.
title: Abstract 15540: Trends in Medicare Reimbursement for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement, 2015 to 2025: Financial and Clinical Implications for Structural Heart Programs

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is increasingly used in high-risk patients; however, a subset remains at substantial hemodynamic risk due to severe left ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, or catastrophic procedural complications. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides full cardiopulmonary support and is used prophylactically or as rescue therapy during TAVR, though available evidence remains fragmented across the medical literature. Objectives: To systematically summarize evidence on VA-ECMO use during TAVR, characterize outcomes by ECMO timing, and appraise certainty using GRADE. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review with a pre-registered protocol on PROSPERO. Five databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane, Google Scholar) were searched for studies from January 2000 to December 2025. Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) undergoing TAVR with VA-ECMO support, regardless of timing (prophylactic, rescue, bridge) or cannulation strategy. Two reviewers independently performed screening, full-text review, and data extraction, resolving disagreements by consensus. Risk of bias was assessed using Newcastle-Ottawa, NIH tools, and AMSTAR-2. Certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Results: Thirty-three studies (12 case reports, 2 case series, 16 cohorts, 3 reviews/meta-analyses) from 11 countries (2013-2025), including approximately 1800 patients, were analyzed. Patients were uniformly high-risk (mean age 74-88 years, LVEF 20-55%, elevated STS/EuroSCORE). All used VA-ECMO; a subset used LAVA-ECMO. In-hospital mortality ranged 0-45.5%, consistently lower in prophylactic cohorts (often 0%) vs rescue (22-45.5%). Thirty-day mortality followed a similar gradient. Procedural success ranged 54.4-100%, higher with prophylactic ECMO (90-100%) vs rescue (54-72%). Rescue ECMO was associated with higher stroke, AKI, major bleeding, vascular complications, and longer ICU stay. A prior meta-analysis showed higher odds of stroke and AKI with ECMO-supported vs non-ECMO TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low to very low due to study design, inconsistency, and imprecision. Conclusions: VA-ECMO-supported TAVR is increasingly used in highly selected high-risk patients and appears technically feasible. Observational data suggest more favorable short-term outcomes with prophylactic ECMO; however, these findings are likely driven by confounding by indication, as patients receiving rescue ECMO are often more critically ill, as well as selection and center-level biases. Substantial heterogeneity in patient selection, ECMO timing, and outcome definitions further limits comparability. Standardized criteria for ECMO initiation, complication reporting, and prospective studies, including LAVA-ECMO, are needed.
title: Abstract 15543: Venoarterial Extracorpeal Membrane Oxygenation Support During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review

abstract: Background: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) is defined by complete or near-complete coronary occlusion with Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 0-1 flow which includes a subset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients without ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Conventional STEMI criteria frequently misclassify these patients, delaying timely reperfusion. Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may improve recognition of OMI beyond standard interpretation, but existing evidence remains limited and a systematic diagnostic synthesis is required. Hypothesis: AI-ECG based deep learning algorithms provide improved diagnostic accuracy for OMI compared to conventional STEMI-based interpretation, enabling earlier identification of patients eligible for reperfusion therapy. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through June 3, 2026. Eligible studies included adults with suspected ACS, applied machine learning or deep learning electrocardiography algorithms, and used coronary angiography TIMI 0-1 flow as reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. A bivariate random-effects model and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. Included models comprised Queen of Hearts (QoH) family algorithms including QoH_aOMI, QoH_eOMI, QoH_mACS, and PMcardio architectures, plus a non-QoH model. Results: Eight studies with 7,358 patients were included from 796 records after deduplication. Risk of bias for index tests was low across studies, while overall bias was low in two, high in four, and unclear in two. The primary pooled analysis demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.865 (95% confidence interval 0.745-0.934), specificity 0.815 (0.741-0.869), and area under the curve 0.890. Hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic analysis showed stable performance across thresholds. Sensitivity analysis excluding ECG-SMART-NET reduced heterogeneity to I 2 = 0%, with sensitivity 0.875 (0.723-0.950), specificity 0.781 (0.750-0.809), and AUC 0.818. These suggest that heterogeneity was largely driven by model-specific effects, while overall diagnostic performance remained robust. Conclusions: Deep learning-based AI-ECG shows strong diagnostic accuracy for OMI, outperforming conventional STEMI-based classification and improving identification of reperfusion-eligible patients. Sensitivity analysis confirmed robustness of pooled estimates, while residual variability reflects algorithm-dependent performance. Findings support potential clinical integration of validated AI-ECG tools for early triage of suspected OMI; however, limited study numbers and heterogeneity warrant prospective validation and real-world studies.
title: Abstract 15546: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiography for Detecting Occlusion Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Before the era of reperfusion therapy for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), an early peak in cardiac biomarker levels was associated with less coronary artery occlusion and better prognosis. On the other hand, in the current era of reperfusion therapy, an early peak has been reported to be associated with impaired chronic-phase cardiac function. The association with timing of peak in cardiac biomarker and the quantity of myocardial salvage remains unclear. Purpose: To assess the hypothesis that timing of peak in cardiac biomarker is associated with myocardial salvage and chronic-phase myocardial function. Methods: Between 2018 and 2025, patients with STEMI who presented to our hospital within 24 hours of symptom onset and underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) on day 4 and 6 months after primary PCI were included. The area at risk was calculated from high-signal areas on T2-weighted images at day 4, and infarct size on late gadolinium enhancement images at 6 months. The myocardial salvage index (MSI) was calculated from both. Troponin T (TnT) measurements were obtained on admission and every three hours after reperfusion. Statistical comparisons were performed using Mann-Whitney U test, Fisher’s exact test, or Chi-square test, as appropriate. A p-value < 0.05 was defined as statistically significant. Results: Among 50 patients (median age 72 years [interquartile range: 65 - 77], 82% male), the culprit vessel was the left anterior descending artery in 26 (52%), the right coronary artery in 18 (36%), the left circumflex artery in 3 (6%) and the left main trunk in 3 (6%). The onset-to-door time as median 124 minutes [71 - 248] and door-to-reperfusion time 55 minutes [47 - 63]. The area at risk was median 30% [25 - 35], infarct size 20% [12 - 26], MSI 0.34 [0.14 - 0.56], left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in the acute-phase 47% [36 - 52] and LVEF in the chronic-phase 50% [43 - 57]. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) in the acute-phase was detected in 14 patients (28%). The time from reperfusion to peak TnT was median 6 hours [3 - 9] and the peak value of TnT 6.0 ng/mL [3.2 - 14.4]. The TnT release pattern was classified into two groups: an early-peaking group (0-3 hours after reperfusion) and a delayed-peaking group (>=6 hours after reperfusion). TnT levels were higher in the early-peaking group than in the delayed-peaking group (Figure1). The incidence of acute-phase MVO (53% vs 13%, P < 0.05) and infarct size (25% [21 - 29] vs 15% [8.5 - 23], P < 0.05) were significantly larger in the early-peaking group (Figure 2). Moreover, chronic-phase LVEF (43% [33 - 52] vs 51% [48 - 60], P < 0.05) and MSI (0.15 [0.1 - 0.28] vs 0.44 [0.26 - 0.68], P < 0.05) were significantly lower in the early-peaking group (Figure 3). Conclusion: The earlier peak in cardiac biomarker release after reperfusion was associated with impaired myocardial salvage and reduced chronic-phase cardiac function.
title: Abstract 15547: The Early Peak Catches the Scar: Peak Troponin Timing as a Surrogate Marker for Quality of Reperfusion Therapy in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Solid organ transplant recipients represent a high-risk population for aortic valve replacement because of their comorbidity burden and perioperative vulnerability. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may offer a less invasive alternative to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), but comparative outcomes in this population remain incompletely defined. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 studies including 3,688 patients undergoing aortic valve replacement after solid organ transplantation. Outcomes assessed were acute kidney injury, in-hospital stay, length of stay, pacemaker implantation, postprocedural bleeding, and stroke. Pooled odds ratios were calculated using a random-effects model. Results: TAVR was associated with significantly lower acute kidney injury (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.18-0.58; p=0.0002; I 2 =90.1%), in-hospital stay-related events (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.15-0.58; p=0.0004; I 2 =46.5%), shorter length of stay (MD -7.38, 95% CI -12.66 to -2.09; p=0.0063; I 2 =97.8%), lower postprocedural bleeding (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.26-0.66; p=0.0002; I 2 =20.9%), and lower stroke risk (OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.19-0.73; p=0.0041; I 2 =40.1%). Pacemaker implantation did not differ significantly between groups (OR 1.18, 95% CI 0.42-3.28; p=0.7529; I 2 =67.1%). Conclusions: In this meta-analysis of 3,688 solid organ transplant patients, TAVR was associated with more favorable short-term outcomes than SAVR, particularly for acute kidney injury, bleeding, stroke, and hospital stay. Given the observational nature of the available evidence and the substantial heterogeneity for some endpoints, larger prospective studies are needed to clarify long-term comparative outcomes. Clinical Implications: TAVR appears to be the preferred short-term strategy when anatomically feasible in solid organ transplant recipients, but procedural selection should remain individualized within a multidisciplinary heart-team approach.
title: Abstract 15551: Transcatheter versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Pregnancy-associated spontaneous coronary artery dissection (P-SCAD) is the leading cause of myocardial infarction in pregnant and postpartum women, yet remains underdiagnosed due to atypical presentations. We present a case of Impella-assisted, IVUS-guided PCI for suspected peripartum LAD SCAD. Patient Information: A 28-year-old G7T5A2L5 woman presented 10 days following uncomplicated vaginal delivery with no prior medical history and no traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Initial ECG showed no ST-elevation. High-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 1,318 ng/L within 2 hours. Bedside POCUS demonstrated severely reduced LV systolic function with anterior wall hypokinesis. Serial ECGs evolved to anterior and anterolateral ST-elevations with reciprocal inferior changes, meeting STEMI criteria. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Rising troponin, anterior wall dysfunction on POCUS, and evolving STEMI in a young postpartum woman without atherosclerotic risk factors made P-SCAD the leading diagnosis. Coronary angiography revealed TIMI 0 flow at the LAD ostium. IVUS confirmed proximal LAD dissection with intramural hematoma, thrombus burden, and false lumen compression — findings not reliably identified by angiography alone. Therapeutic Interventions: Given TIMI 0 proximal LAD occlusion and severe LV dysfunction, an Impella was placed for hemodynamic support. IVUS-guided PCI was performed with true lumen wire position confirmed prior to stent deployment. Two overlapping drug-eluting stents were deployed from the ostial to mid-LAD with restoration of TIMI-3 flow. Outcomes: The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout with no procedural complications. She was transferred to a tertiary care center for ongoing management. Discussion: This case illustrates three key lessons. First, a normal initial ECG does not exclude P-SCAD — serial monitoring is essential as intramural hematoma propagation can cause abrupt occlusion. Second, bedside POCUS identified severe anterior LV dysfunction before ECG evolution, bridging the gap to emergent catheterization. Third, IVUS was indispensable for confirming the diagnosis, verifying true lumen wire position, and guiding stent coverage. High multiparity (G7) represents an underrecognized predisposing factor. Clinicians should maintain high suspicion for P-SCAD in postpartum patients with chest pain regardless of initial ECG findings.
title: Abstract 15555: Impella Assisted IVUS Guided PCI for Suspected Peripartum LAD Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

abstract: Introduction: In rare cases of bilateral subclavian artery stenosis (SAS), cuff pressures may substantially underestimate true systemic blood pressure (BP), resulting in pseudo-normotension or pseudo-hypotension. The effects of SAS-related pseudo-hypotension on dialysis and hypertensive management are poorly described. Patient Information: A 71-year-old woman with peripheral artery disease and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on maintenance hemodialysis experienced recurrent dyspnea and hypervolemia, resulting in nine emergency room visits over nine months. BP measurements obtained during dialysis consistently suggested hypotension, prompting progressive de-escalation of antihypertensive therapy and premature termination of dialysis sessions due to presumed intradialytic hypotension. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Despite apparent hypotension, she demonstrated no evidence of hypoperfusion. Recurrent dyspnea and hypervolemia suggested underdialysis and masked hypertension. Following a positive stress test, the patient was transferred for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). During PCI, invasive monitoring revealed severe asymptomatic hypertension with systolic pressures of 220-260 mmHg. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Femoral arterial pressure measured 185/54 mmHg, while cuff pressures were 92/60 mmHg in the left arm, 92/63 mmHg in the right arm, 98/63 mmHg in the left leg, and 133/68 mmHg in the right leg. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed severe bilateral subclavian artery stenosis. Peripheral cuff measurements underestimated systemic pressure by 60-100 mmHg. Therapeutic Intervention: Antihypertensive therapy was cautiously reintroduced, and dialysis was performed under arterial-line guidance. Correlation of invasive and noninvasive measurements identified the right leg as the preferred monitoring site. A surrogate outpatient BP target of approximately 100/50 mmHg using right-leg measurements was established. Follow-Up & Outcomes: Outpatient management was guided by right-leg BP measurements. Improved volume control and more effective dialysis sessions were achieved following recognition of pseudo-hypotension and optimization of antihypertensive therapy. Discussion & Synthesis: This case highlights bilateral SAS as a rare but clinically significant cause of pseudo-hypotension leading to chronic undertreatment of severe hypertension, recurrent hypervolemia, and inadequate dialysis. In patients with advanced vascular disease and discordant BP measurements, assessment in multiple extremities and correlation with invasive measurements may be necessary. Identifying a reliable surrogate BP site can optimize dialysis and antihypertensive management.
title: Abstract 15558: When Hypotension Was Hypertension: Pseudo-Hypotension Causing Severe Hypertension and Inadequate Dialysis in a Patient with Bilateral Subclavian Artery Stenosis

abstract: Background: Patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remain at risk for infarct expansion, unfavourable ventricular remodelling, and heart failure despite prompt percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Several anti-inflammatory therapies have been attempted to reduce this inflammatory harm but the relative efficacy and safety is uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of anti-inflammatory therapies and identify the optimal treatment strategy in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI. Methods: We searched major databases for relevant randomized controlled trials. A frequentist network meta-analysis using random-effect model was performed to compare eligible interventions. Effect estimates were expressed as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs for continuous outcomes. Treatments were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) probability. All statistical analyses were conducted in R Studio. Results: Twenty-four randomized controlled trials involving 15,245 patients were included. For all-cause mortality, bolus plus infusion pexelizumab was associated with a significantly lower risk compared with placebo (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.11-0.86; p = 0.025) and ranked as the most effective intervention (SUCRA = 0.87). For new-onset heart failure, anakinra was ranked the best (SUCRA = 0.95) and associated with a significant reduction in risk compared with placebo (OR 0.14, 95% CI 0.02-0.75). For CMR-measured infarct size, methylprednisolone ranked highest (SUCRA = 0.82) but did not significantly reduce infarct size (SMD –0.13, 95% CI –0.33 to 0.06). Conversely, doxycycline monotherapy significantly increased infarct size compared with placebo (SMD 0.40, 95% CI 0.01-0.79). While anakinra and cyclosporine ranked highest for LVEF, neither demonstrated a statistically significant benefit compared with placebo. Likewise, bolus plus infusion pexelizumab was the top-ranked for composite MACE, although the effect was not statistically significant. Safety outcomes were generally comparable across treatment strategies, with no consistent evidence of an increased risk of adverse events relative to placebo or standard care. Conclusion: This network meta-analysis suggests that anti-inflammatory therapies may confer outcome-specific benefits following acute myocardial infarction. Bolus plus infusion pexelizumab was associated with reduced all-cause mortality, whereas anakinra significantly lowered the risk of new-onset heart failure. However, most interventions did not show significant improvements in LVEF, and composite MACE. Further large-scale randomized trials are needed to validate these findings and define the role of targeted anti-inflammatory therapy in contemporary post-myocardial infarction care. .
title: Abstract 15562: Comparative Effectiveness of Anti-Inflammatory Therapies in Adults with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Frequentist Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background Approximately 50% of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) deaths occur outside the hospital, yet national data characterizing which populations face the greatest risk of pre-hospital cardiac death remain limited. Place of death (POD) may serve as a proxy for prehospital emergency care access: DOA (Dead on Arrival) and ER (Emergency Room) deaths reflect probable failures in EMS response and STEMI network reach, while nursing home/LTC and hospice deaths reflect frailty and goals-of-care trajectories. Despite this, Sociodemographic determinants of POD in AMI remain poorly characterized. Methods Using CDC WONDER, we analysed POD among 2,532,610 adults ≥20 years with AMI (ICD-10 I21) from 2003-2023. POD categories included inpatient, outpatient/ER, DOA, home, nursing home/LTC, and hospice. Multinomial logistic regression examined sociodemographic predictors of POD using inpatient death as the reference. Independent variables included age (20-44 [Ref]), sex (female [Ref]), race (White [Ref]), Hispanic origin (Hispanic [Ref]), and urbanization. Results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% CIs. Analyses were performed in R v4.3.1. Results Rural residence was the strongest predictor of pre-hospital death: rural residents had nearly 3-fold higher odds of DOA (aOR: 2.91 [2.71-3.12]), along with elevated odds of home (aOR: 1.89 [1.86-1.91]) and outpatient death (aOR: 1.58 [1.55-1.61]) versus large metropolitan residents. Black decedents had higher odds of outpatient death (aOR: 1.25 [1.23-1.28]) and DOA (aOR: 1.16 [1.06-1.26]) versus White decedents. Younger adults (20-44 years) had the highest relative odds of DOA and ER death, decreasing progressively with age. Male sex was independently associated with higher DOA (aOR: 1.39 [1.31-1.48]), outpatient (aOR: 1.25 [1.23-1.27]) compared to females. Hispanic decedents showed consistently lower odds of out-of-hospital death compared to non-Hispanics. Adults ≥65 years were markedly more likely to die in nursing home/LTC (aOR: 6.38 [5.52-7.38]) and hospice (aOR: 2.14 [1.76-2.61]), while rural and Hispanic decedents demonstrated reduced hospice utilization. (Table 1, Figure 1) Conclusions In this 20-year national analysis of 2.5 million AMI decedents, rural residence was the strongest independent predictor of pre-hospital death. Black decedents faced significantly higher odds of out-of-hospital death versus White decedents, reflecting racial inequities in prehospital EMS. Young adults disproportionately died outside the hospital, consistent with delayed AMI recognition. Priority targets include: (1) expansion of rural EMS infrastructure and STEMI training; (2) equitable access to regional STEMI receiving networks; and (3) improved AMI recognition in younger and minority populations. Reduced hospice utilization among rural and Hispanic decedents signals unmet palliative care needs.
title: Abstract 15578: Sociodemographic Disparities in Place of Death and Emergency Care Access in Acute Myocardial Infarction in the United States: Insights from CDC Wonder

abstract: Introduction: Histidine-Tryptophan-Ketoglutarate (HTK) cardioplegia provides single-dose myocardial protection during adult valve surgery, yet its comparative effectiveness against standard blood cardioplegia across perioperative outcomes is not well established.Research Question: Among adults undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, does single-dose HTK cardioplegia differ from standard blood cardioplegia in perioperative mortality, myocardial injury, and major clinical outcomes?
