A proximal LAD myocardial bridge was identified, but no stent was placed. Blood cultures grew Streptococcus sanguinis, and intravenous ceftriaxone was initiated. Transthoracic echocardiography showed an ejection fraction (EF) of 35-40%, apical akinesis, and mild mitral regurgitation. Diagnosis and Management: Cardiac CT demonstrated a myocardial bridge involving the mid-LAD and evidence of prior infarction. Given positive blood cultures and absence of significant coronary disease, transesophageal echocardiography was performed, revealing mitral valve vegetations and moderate mitral regurgitation, confirming infective endocarditis. The patient completed six weeks of intravenous ceftriaxone with clearance of bacteremia. Follow-Up: Repeat TEE demonstrated persistent large mitral and aortic valve vegetations, anterior mitral leaflet perforation, and worsening mitral regurgitation despite antibiotic therapy. He underwent successful mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacement with concomitant myocardial bridge unroofing. Conclusion: This case highlights a rare presentation of infective endocarditis as STEMI in a patient with myocardial bridging and underscores the importance of considering septic coronary embolization when acute coronary syndrome occurs in the setting of bacteremia.
title: Abstract 16991: Infective Endocarditis Presenting as ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction in a Patient with Myocardial Bridging

abstract: Background: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is a unique cause of right ventricular pressure overload and right heart failure (RHF). While RHF is frequently associated with adverse arrhythmic and hemodynamic outcomes, the electrical phenotype of CTEPH-associated RHF remains poorly characterized. Objective: We evaluated arrhythmic burden and clinical outcomes among patients hospitalized with acute RHF with and without CTEPH. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2021-2023). Adult hospitalizations with acute RHF were identified using ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes and stratified by the presence of CTEPH. The primary outcome was sudden cardiac arrest (SCA). Secondary outcomes included atrial arrhythmias, malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA), complete heart block (CHB), cardiogenic shock, in-hospital mortality, mechanicalventilation, acute kidney injury, length of stay (LOS), and hospitalization charges. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was performed to determine the independent association between CTEPH and outcomes. Results: Among 200,345 weighted RHF hospitalizations, 4,610 (2.3%) had concomitant CTEPH. Patients with CTEPH were younger (58.0 vs 66.4 years, p<0.001) and more frequently had prior venous thromboembolism (38.7% vs 8.8%, p<0.001) and long-term anticoagulation use (51.2% vs 24.1%, p<0.001). The CTEPH group had longer LOS (10.1 vs 8.3 days) and greater hospitalization charges ($203,218 vs $133,410), both with p<0.001. Atrial arrhythmias were significantly less common among CTEPH hospitalizations (25.2% vs 43.4%, p<0.001), whereas rates of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (1.8% vs 2.8%, p=0.076) and complete heart block (0.9% vs 1.6%, p=0.061) were similar. Despite higher rates of cardiogenic shock (15.4% vs 9.1%, p< 0.001), patients with CTEPH experienced lower in-hospital mortality (7.8% vs 11.4%, p=0.002). In adjusted analyses, CTEPH was independently associated with lower odds of SCA (adjusted OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.88; p=0.015), malignant ventricular arrhythmias (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.15-0.83), atrial arrhythmias (aOR 0.63, 95% CI 0.49-0.80), and in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.44-0.89). CTEPH demonstrated a trend toward increased cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.87). The association between CTEPH and lower mortality persisted after additional adjustment for arrhythmic events. Conclusions: Among patients hospitalized with acute RHF, concomitant CTEPH was associated with a distinct electrical phenotype characterized by lower risks of sudden cardiac arrest, ventricular arrhythmias, and atrial arrhythmias despite a greater burden of cardiogenic shock. These findings suggest CTEPH-associated RHF may differ fundamentally from other RHF etiologies with respect to arrhythmogenic risk.
title: Abstract 16997: Distinct Arrhythmic and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Right Heart Failure with Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension: A Nationwide Analysis

abstract: Background: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a nonatherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome, predominantly affecting young and middle-aged women. The COL4A1/COL4A2 locus has been implicated in SCAD risk through genome-wide association studies and rare-variant enrichment analyses. Although COL4A1 -related disease has a recognized systemic arteriopathy phenotype (cerebrovascular, renal, ocular, muscular), SCAD has not been systematically characterized as a coronary manifestation of monogenic COL4A1 -related disease. Objectives: To describe the prevalence, severity, management, and extra coronary phenotype among individuals with SCAD and pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) COL4A1 variants, using reverse phenotyping from a COL4A1 -related disease cohort. Methods: We queried the Mayo Clinic institutional database for all records referencing COL4A1 , yielding 1,447 patients. After excluding benign/likely benign findings and individuals without reportable COL4A1 variants, the analytic cohort included 110 COL4A1 variant carriers, of which 37 were P/LP and 73 were variants of uncertain significance (VUS). SCAD was confirmed by chart review and coronary presentation, territory, angiographic flow, management, extra-coronary arteriopathy, renal involvement, musculoskeletal symptoms, and follow-up were abstracted. Results: SCAD occurred in 3/37 P/LP carriers (8.1%; 95% CI, 1.7%-21.9%) and 0/73 VUS carriers (0%; Fisher exact P=0.036). All three SCAD cases were women presenting at ages 32, 35, and 42 years. All carried heterozygous LP COL4A1 variants spanning distinct mutational mechanisms: a collagenous-domain glycine substitution c.1484G>T (p.Gly495Val), a nonsense variant c.2437C>T (p.Gln813Ter), and a canonical splice-site variant c.388-1G>C. Presentations included pregnancy-associated left circumflex/obtuse marginal dissection managed conservatively, left anterior descending dissection requiring extensive percutaneous coronary intervention, and right coronary artery (RCA) dissection ultimately treated with off-pump right internal mammary artery-to-RCA by-pass. During follow-up, left ventricular ejection fraction was preserved or recovered in all. Extra coronary arterial abnormalities were common including cranial/cervical arterial abnormalities in all three and renal/visceral/iliac abnormalities in two, consistent with a systemic COL4A1 arteriopathy phenotype ( Table 1 ). Conclusions: In this COL4A1 -enriched cohort, SCAD occurred in 8.1% of P/LP COL4A1 carriers, with all cases accompanied by systemic arteriopathy, identifying SCAD as a coronary manifestation of monogenic COL4A1 -related arteriopathy. Multicenter studies are needed to define penetrance, recurrence risk, and optimal surveillance strategies.
title: Abstract 17014: Expanding the Vascular Phenotype of COL4A1-Related Arteriopathy: A Novel Association with Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

abstract: Introduction: Alveolar hemorrhage is a known but rare complication of ablation, previously described with thermal techniques. Adverse events have declined since the advent of pulse field ablation (PFA) with no alveolar hemorrhage reported. We describe a case of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) after PFA and the complexities of management. Patient Information: 72 year old woman with history of symptomatic paroxysmal atrial flutter and fibrillation on Apixaban, coronary artery disease with drug eluting stent, obstructive sleep apnea. Clinical Findings: The patient underwent 3D electroanatomical mapping using CARTO sound. Multipolar veripulse PFA catheter was used to target pulmonary veins for isolation with total 22 PFA lesions. Q DOT force sensing ablation catheter was used to map right atrium and radiofrequency ablation was done at Cavo tricuspid isthmus and base of coronary sinus, without intraoperative complications with conversion to normal sinus rhythm. She was discharged home the same day. In a few hours, she had 3 episodes of small volume hemoptysis. On arrival of EMS, oxygen saturation was 70%. On ICU admission, she required 40 L oxygen via high flow nasal cannula. Diagnostic Assessment: Chest Xray showed diffuse interstitial infiltrates. CT chest showed extensive ground glass infiltrates in both lung fields. Apixaban was reversed with Prothrombin Complex Concentrate. She became progressively hypoxic and was intubated with DAH confirmed on bronchoalveolar lavage. Therapeutic Intervention: She received pulse dose steroids and broad spectrum antibiotics. With worsening oxygenation, she was paralyzed and proned. She was started on epoprostenol and tranexamic acid nebulization. Follow up Autoimmune workup was negative. She weaned off steroids, had improvement of bloody secretions and was successfully extubated. After 2 days of no hemoptysis, prophylactic anticoagulation with heparin was started and transitioned to dabigatran at discharge. Discussion: Our patient underwent extensive AF ablation using PFA without any intraprocedural complications. The close temporal relation between the procedure and symptom onset raised suspicion for DAH. Although extensive diagnostic evaluation was initially pursued, the clinical presentation and exclusion of alternative etiologies supported PFA related vascular injury as most likely mechanism. While PFA is generally regarded as a predominantly nonthermal energy, local thermal effects and direct tissue injury may contribute to rare complications such as DAH. Prompt recognition and supportive management like airway protection, mechanical ventilation, and measures to limit ongoing bleeding, resulted in significant clinical improvement. As PFA continues to gain widespread adoption for AF ablation, awareness of potentially serious complications is important with further studies to better define these complications.
title: Abstract 17019: Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage Following Pulsed Field Ablation: A Case Report and Management Considerations

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) reduces thromboembolic risk for selected patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulation, but its downstream inpatient utilization impact remains poorly defined. We evaluated 1-year changes in hospitalization-related charges, admissions, length of stay (LOS), bleeding-related readmissions, and post-LAAO utilization trajectories. Methods: A prospectively maintained UNC Health LAAO registry (2017-2024) was analyzed. Among patients with ≥365 days of follow-up, annual hospitalization-related charges, inpatient admissions, and inpatient LOS were compared during the year before versus after LAAO. Bleeding-related inpatient records were classified by ICD-defined phenotype. Pre- and post-LAAO utilization charges, admissions, and LOS were standardized after charge log-transformation and clustered using prespecified k-means clustering (k=3). Baseline comorbidities were withheld from clustering and evaluated separately as predictors of trajectory membership using logistic regression. Results: Among 1,080 LAAO recipients, 821 had ≥1 year of follow-up. Median annual hospitalization-related charges decreased from $8,594 (IQR $2,477-$64,736) before LAAO to $4,866 (IQR $2,655-$28,490; p<0.001). Patients with ≥1 inpatient hospitalization decreased from 29.8% to 19.9% (p<0.001), and mean inpatient LOS declined from 2.05 to 1.68 days per patient-year. Among 200 bleeding-related inpatient admissions, 75% occurred before LAAO vs. 25% after. Gastrointestinal bleeding accounted for 72% of post-LAAO bleeding readmissions. Clustering identified three utilization phenotypes: sustained low-burden (n=670, 82%), utilization reduction (n=116, 14%), and utilization escalation phenotype (n=35, 4%). Median change in annual hospitalization-related charges was -$1,025 in the sustained low-burden, -$78,589 in the utilization reduction, and +$111,277 in the utilization escalation phenotype (p<0.001). Bleeding-related readmission rates were 11.9%, 51.7%, and 42.9% (p<0.001), and mortality was 16.1%, 22.4%, and 31.4% (p=0.024). Bleeding predisposition, heart failure, prior stroke/TIA, and pre-LAAO hospitalization identified the reduction phenotype; escalation was poorly explained by baseline clinical variables. Conclusions: In this real-world LAAO registry, inpatient utilization decreased after implantation and separated into distinct trajectories. Patient-level administrative utilization data identified a large sustained low-burden group, a marked utilization-reduction group, and a small escalation phenotype associated with higher mortality. These findings suggest that routinely captured utilization metrics add clinically meaningful context beyond aggregate pre- and post-procedure comparisons.
title: Abstract 17042: Impact of Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion on Healthcare Utilization and Bleeding-Related Readmissions: A Large Retrospective Registry Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) are at high residual cardiovascular risk, requiring intensive lipid-lowering therapy (LLT), including high-intensity statins (HIS), to achieve low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets. Research Question: In a large contemporary registry of patients with CAD treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), what are the temporal trends of LDL-C levels and LLT intensity? Methods: We included consecutive patients with available LDL-C measurement at admission for PCI between January 2012 and December 2023 at a large US tertiary center. Patients with cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, active cancer, or dialysis were excluded. Patients were stratified by admission LDL-C levels (<55,55-69,70-99,≥100 mg/dL) and statin intensity (high intensity statin [HIS]: rosuvastatin 20-40 mg or atorvastatin 40-80 mg; low to moderate intensity statin; and no statin). Mean LDL-C levels and LLT distribution are reported annually to assess temporal trends. Logistic regression was performed to estimate the odds ratio (OR) of LLT prescription per one-year increment in time. Results: Among 24,003 patients included (mean age 67±11 years; 29% women), 8,952 (37.3%) were on HIS, 8,222 (34.3%) on low to moderate intensity statin, and 6,829 (28.5%) not on statin at admission. Ezetimibe was prescribed in 1,210 (5.0%) patients. The use of PCSK9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) was at 1.5% between 2018 and 2023. Patients with the highest levels of LDL-C (≥100 mg/dL) compared with those with LDL-C<55 mg/dL were more frequently women (35% vs. 22%) and younger (63.8 vs. 68 years). LLT intensity increased over time for statin use (OR 1.15/year, 95%CI 1.14-1.16), ezetimibe (OR 1.19/year, 95%CI 1.01-1.12), and PCSK9i (OR 1.43/year, 95%CI 1.35-1.52 since 2017) ( Figure 1 ). Despite LLT intensification, more than 50% of patients had LDL-C levels above the target of 70 mg/dL, and mean LDL-C levels remained above this threshold throughout the study period ( Figure 2 ). Overall, 5,468 patients (22.9%) were eligible for PCSK9 inhibitors with a Class I indication according to the 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines. Conclusions: Despite increasing statin intensity over time, mean LDL-C levels remained stable and above 70 mg/dL, supporting greater use of non-statin lipid-lowering therapies, including PCSK9 inhibitors, for which 1 in 5 patients were eligible. Moreover, 30% of patients were not receiving statins at admission, suggesting undervaluation of cardiovascular risk, particularly in women and younger patients.
title: Abstract 17054: Temporal Trends of Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels and Lipid Lowering Therapy Intensity in a Large Registry of Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

abstract: Background: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) in degenerative mitral valve disease has been associated with ventricular ectopy and arrhythmic risk. Whether robotic mitral valve repair modifies premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden in patients with MAD remains poorly defined. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that robotic mitral valve surgery in patients with MAD is associated with favorable perioperative outcomes and reduced PVC burden among patients with elevated preoperative PVC burden. Methods: We retrospectively identified 161 consecutive patients with MAD who underwent robotic mitral valve surgery between 2009 and 2025. Baseline characteristics, operative variables, and postoperative outcomes were obtained from chart review. Paired preoperative and postoperative PVC burden was available in 40 patients. Postoperative ambulatory rhythm monitoring was performed at a median of 21.9 months after surgery (IQR 8.4-33.5). Elevated PVC burden was defined as ≥5%. The primary arrhythmic outcome was change in PVC burden after surgery. Secondary outcomes included operative mortality, stroke, renal failure, prolonged ventilation, reoperation, postoperative atrial fibrillation, and survival. Results: Among 161 patients, median age was 58.1 (IQR 45.9, 66.3) years, 43.5% were female. There was no operative mortality, stroke, or renal failure. One patient required prolonged ventilation, and one underwent early re-repair for valve dysfunction. Postoperative atrial fibrillation occurred in 21.1%. During a median follow-up of 2.4 years, Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 95.5%. In the paired PVC cohort, median PVC burden changed from 1.4% (IQR 0.5-3.7) preoperatively to 0.93% (IQR 0.5-3.3) postoperatively (P=0.313). Among patients with elevated preoperative PVC burden ≥5% (n=9), PVC burden decreased in 89% of patients (8/9), with median absolute reduction of 5.4 percentage points (IQR 1.1,8.6; P=0.028). In patients with preoperative PVC burden <5% (n=31), no significant change was observed (P=0.545). The magnitude of PVC reduction was greater in patients with elevated versus low baseline PVC burden (P=0.002). Conclusions: In patients with MAD, robotic mitral valve repair was associated with excellent repair results, favorable perioperative outcomes, and great mid-term survival. In the paired rhythm analysis, patients with elevated preoperative PVC burden showed a significant postoperative reduction, suggesting potential benefit in these patients.
title: Abstract 17074: Premature Ventricular Contraction Burden After Robotic Mitral Valve Repair in Patients with Mitral Annular Disjunction

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) planning relies heavily on computed tomography for annular sizing, valve selection, and procedural risk assessment. Manual CT analysis is time-intensive and subject to interobserver variability, potentially contributing to patient-prosthesis mismatch and adverse outcomes. Methods: This multicenter retrospective validation study included 7,000 consecutive patients undergoing preprocedural TAVR computed tomography. TITAN-AI automatically segmented aortic root anatomy, quantified annular dimensions, coronary heights, and calcification burden, and generated valve-sizing recommendations. Performance was evaluated against expert structural heart team assessments using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Results: Among 7,000 patients undergoing preprocedural TAVR CT analysis, the mean age was 78.4±7.9 years, 46.8% were female, and 53.2% were male. Mean annular area was 492.8±118.6 mm 2 , area-derived annular diameter was 24.9±2.8 mm, and annular perimeter was 78.3±8.6 mm. Mean left coronary artery height measured 13.8±3.1 mm, while median aortic valve calcification burden was 2,420 Agatston units (IQR 1,640-3,520). High-risk anatomical features included low coronary height (<10 mm) in 8.4%, severe leaflet calcification in 15.2%, and predicted patient-prosthesis mismatch in 12.8% of cases. TITAN-AI achieved sensitivity of 99.53% (95% CI 99.31-99.75), specificity of 100.00% (95% CI 99.95-100.00), positive predictive value of 100.00% (95% CI 99.90-100.00), and negative predictive value of 99.79% (95% CI 99.60-99.92), with an ROC-AUC of 1.000 (95% CI 0.999-1.000). Automated valve-sizing recommendations demonstrated 99.4% concordance with expert heart teams. Median planning time decreased from 42.1 to 2.9 minutes, representing a 93.1% reduction. AI-guided planning was associated with a projected 42% reduction in patient-prosthesis mismatch and a 31% reduction in moderate-to-severe paravalvular regurgitation risk. Conclusion: TITAN-AI provides highly accurate automated TAVR CT planning with near-perfect diagnostic performance, rapid valve-sizing recommendations, and reliable identification of high-risk anatomy. By substantially reducing analysis time and predicted patient-prosthesis mismatch, the platform may improve procedural efficiency, standardize decision-making, and enhance outcomes across contemporary structural heart programs.
title: Abstract 17079: TITAN-AI: Automated CT-Based TAVR Planning and Valve Sizing Reduces Patient-Prosthesis Mismatch and Planning Time A Multicenter Retrospective Validation Study of 7,000 Patients

abstract: Background: Despite technically successful transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), persistent left ventricular hypertrophy driven by renin-angiotensin system activation contributes to excess long-term mortality. Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASi) are biologically plausible post-TAVR therapies; however, major guidelines carry no specific recommendation, and real-world prescribing remains low. Hypothesis: Post-TAVR RASi use is associated with lower all-cause mortality and rehospitalization without increasing acute kidney injury or stroke risk. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, stratifying TAVR recipients (2012-2025) by post-procedural RASi prescription. One-to-one propensity score matching (PSM) was performed across demographics, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and laboratory parameters. Pre-specified falsification outcomes (acute appendicitis, malignant melanoma, myopia) were used to assess residual confounding. Survival analyses employed Kaplan-Meier estimation and Cox proportional hazards modeling. A 30-day landmark sensitivity analysis addressed immortal-time bias. Results: Following PSM, 27,010 matched pairs were identified (n=54,020; mean age 78.2 years; 56.9% male; 86.1% White). Over a median follow-up of 713 days, RASi use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (21.9% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72-0.77; p<0.001) and all-cause rehospitalization (59.7% vs. 67.6%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.70-0.73; p<0.001). Median time to first rehospitalization was 349 days in RASi users versus 83 days in non-users. Risks of acute kidney injury (HR 0.960; 95% CI 0.927-0.993; p=0.019) and stroke (HR 0.974; 95% CI 0.930-1.019; p=0.223) were comparable between cohorts. All falsification outcomes were uniformly null (HRs 0.95-1.18; all p>0.17), providing no evidence of systematic confounding bias. Conclusions: In this largest propensity-matched real-world analysis of post-TAVR RASi use to date, RASi therapy was associated with significant reductions in mortality and rehospitalization with no meaningful increase in renal or cerebrovascular risk. These findings support a large, adequately powered randomized trial of RASi initiation after TAVR to establish guideline-level evidence.
title: Abstract 17080: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Patients with Ebstein’s anomaly (EA) have a higher risk of atrial arrhythmias (AA) including atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter. Tricuspid valve surgery is an opportune moment to perform concomitant AA ablation; both in patients with pre-existing arrhythmias and potentially as prophylaxis. We hypothesized that concomitant AA ablation procedures would reduce postoperative arrhythmias, and we present our findings from a large single-center cohort of EA patients. Methods: All consecutive patients with EA who underwent tricuspid valve surgery between 2010-25, were included. Clinical, surgical and echocardiographic data were obtained via retrospective chart review. Sustained atrial flutter or atrial fibrillation > 30 d after surgery was the primary end point. Wilcoxon rank-sum, chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests compared patients who underwent surgical AA ablation versus those who did not. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed freedom from sustained postoperative AA. Multivariable Cox-regression analysis described predictors for postoperative sustained AA. Results: Of 745 patients (median age 22.5, 54% female) who underwent tricuspid valve surgery, 172 (23%) underwent concomitant atrial ablation: 67 RA MAZE, 83 CTI ablation, 11 LA MAZE and 11 bi-atrial MAZE. Patients with and without surgical ablation are compared in Table1. Over a median follow-up of 2.7 (IQR 0.2-7.1) years, 12.3% of patients experienced sustained atrial arrhythmia; 20.9% in the ablation cohort and 9.8% in the no-ablation cohort. Atrial flutter was the most common (7.2%), followed by atrial fibrillation (5.6%). Univariable Cox regression demonstrated older age, previous tricuspid surgeries, valve replacement surgery, lower LVEF, lower TAPSE, and history of pre-operative atrial arrhythmias as predictors of post-operative sustained atrial arrhythmias. Right reduction atrioplasty was associated with a reduced risk (Table 2). On multivariable Cox regression, older age, previous atrial arrhythmia ablations and valve replacement surgery were independent predictors of AA. Surgical ablation did not significantly reduce the post-operative arrhythmia risk (p=0.221). A subgroup analysis of patients with and without pre-operative sustained atrial arrhythmias demonstrated no significant difference in post-surgical AA risk in either group (Figure 1B). Conclusion: AAs are common after tricuspid valve surgery in EA and the risk increases with age and history of tricuspid valve replacement. Surgical ablation was not associated with significantly improved arrhythmia-free survival. Further studies are needed to assess the role of surgical atrial ablation in targeted populations to reduce the risk of post-operative AA.
title: Abstract 17084: Surgical Atrial Arrhythmia Ablation During Tricuspid Valve Surgery in Ebstein's Anomaly: Predictors of Postoperative Arrhythmias and the Impact of Concomitant Ablation

abstract: Background: The hemoglobin-to-serum creatinine ratio (Hb/Cr) integrates anemia and renal dysfunction into a simple bedside index and lower values have been associated with ischemic and bleeding events in patients with ACS. However, its prognostic value in a broader all-comers PCI population, including patients undergoing PCI for CCS, has not been systematically investigated. Hypothesis: We evaluated whether baseline Hb/Cr is independently associated with ischemic and bleeding risk after PCI and whether this association is consistent across ACS and CCS presentations. Methods: In this observational cohort study, we analyzed prospectively collected data from a PCI registry at a large tertiary US center, including patients undergoing PCI between January 2012 and December 2024. Patients with active malignancy, dialysis, or cardiogenic shock at presentation were excluded. Baseline Hb/Cr was categorized into quartiles, with the highest quartile (Q4) used as the reference. The primary ischemic outcome was 1-year MACE, defined as all-cause death, MI, or stroke and major bleeding at 1-year was the primary safety outcome. Cumulative event rates across Hb/Cr quartiles were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and compared with the log-rank test. Adjusted hazard ratios were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, AF, clinical presentation, multivessel disease, coronary calcification, and prior MI. Results: Among 23,891 patients, those in the lowest Hb/Cr quartile were older and less frequently female than those in the highest quartile (age 71.4±10.9 vs 63.3±11.0 years; female sex 27.9% vs 37.6%). They also more frequently had anemia (71.5% vs 12.5%), CKD (77.7% vs 1.0%), and multivessel disease (70.6% vs 57.9%). At 1 year, Kaplan-Meier estimated MACE rates were higher in Q1 than in Q4 (8.4% vs 2.3%; unadjusted HR, 3.76; 95% CI, 3.08-4.60; P <0.001; P for trend <0.001). Major bleeding was also more frequent in Q1 than in Q4 (7.5% vs 3.4%; unadjusted HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.87-2.61; P<0.001; P for trend <0.001). After multivariable adjustment, Q1 remained associated with higher risks of MACE (adjHR, 2.52; 95% CI, 2.05-3.11), all-cause death (adjHR, 3.48; 95% CI, 2.55-4.74), and major bleeding (adjHR, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.62-2.32), with significant trends across Hb/Cr quartiles (P for trend <0.001 for all). The association between lower Hb/Cr and MACE was consistent across ACS and CCS presentations (P for interaction=0.71). Conclusion: Lower baseline Hb/Cr was independently associated with higher 1-year ischemic and major bleeding risk after PCI, consistently across ACS and CCS presentations. Hb/Cr may serve as a simple, low-cost, routinely available marker of patient vulnerability to inform follow-up intensity and individualized post-PCI management.
title: Abstract 17096: Hemoglobin-to-Creatinine Ratio and One-Year Outcomes in an All-Comers Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Population

abstract: Background: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is common and can result from ischemic coronary mechanisms or non-ischemic mimics (e.g., myocarditis or takotsubo syndrome). Multimodality imaging with multivessel optical coherence tomography (OCT) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) identifies an etiology in ~80% of MINOCA cases. However, this approach is invasive, resource-intensive, and not universally accessible. Electrocardiography (ECG) is inexpensive and routinely used in the initial evaluation of acute coronary syndromes. It is unknown whether ECG findings can provide meaningful diagnostic insights into the mechanisms of a MINOCA presentation or to localize the territory of injury to guide targeted intracoronary imaging. Research Question: Are ECG findings at presentation associated with multimodality imaging findings in MINOCA? Methods: Adults with MINOCA enrolled in the prospective, multicenter, international Heart Attack Research Program (HARP) had 12-lead ECG at presentation. ECG findings and localization using standard lead distributions were evaluated. Multivessel OCT and CMR findings were analyzed at core laboratories to categorize the underlying cause of MINOCA as MI, non-ischemic MINOCA mimic, or idiopathic (no identifiable cause). The OCT culprit territory was defined based on the vessel containing a culprit lesion, and ischemic patterns on CMR were defined as ischemic-pattern late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) or regional myocardial edema in a coronary distribution in the presence of a regional wall motion abnormality. We compared ECG findings by diagnosis and assessed the agreement between the territory of ECG abnormalities and imaging findings in cases with final diagnosis of MI. Ischemic ECG abnormalities included ≥2 contiguous leads of ≥1 mm ST-segment elevation (STE), ST-segment depressions (STD), T-wave inversions (TWI); or Q waves. Results: Among 281 MINOCA patients with OCT, CMR and ECG available for central review, 59% had a final diagnosis of MI, 20% had a MINOCA mimic, and 21% were idiopathic. Ischemic ECG abnormalities were present in 98/165 (59%) of patients with MI or ischemic injury, compared with 31/56 (55%) with MINOCA mimics and 33/60 (55%) with idiopathic MINOCA (p=0.779). The frequency of STE, STD, TWI, and Q waves did not differ by final diagnosis. CMR abnormalities and OCT culprit lesions were not more common in patients with vs. without ECG ischemic abnormalities. Overall, ischemic ECG changes had 59.4% sensitivity and 44.8% specificity to identify a final diagnosis of MI in patients with a clinical diagnosis of MINOCA. Conclusion: Presenting ECG findings did not distinguish imaging-defined MI from MINOCA mimics or idiopathic cases. These findings support the continued role of multimodality imaging with OCT and CMR for defining MINOCA mechanism and territory.
title: Abstract 17113: Electrocardiography and Etiologies of Myocardial Infarction with Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries (MINOCA)

abstract: Introduction: Lidocaine remains an important anti-arrhythmic agent for the management of ventricular tachycardia (VT) and ventricular fibrillation (VF). Because lidocaine and its active metabolites may accumulate in patients with organ dysfunction, concern exists that patients requiring renal replacement therapy may be at increased risk of neurologic toxicity. Few studies have evaluated neurologic outcomes among patients receiving lidocaine therapy and renal replacement therapy, and the relationship between renal replacement therapy and lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity remains poorly understood. Research Question: Among hospitalized patients with ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation receiving lidocaine therapy, is exposure to renal replacement therapy associated with an increased risk of neurologic adverse events? Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network. Adult hospitalized patients with VT/VF who received lidocaine were identified and stratified by exposure to renal replacement therapy (CRRT or hemodialysis). Propensity score matching was performed using age, sex, acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, liver disease, ECMO use, cardiac arrest, and cardiogenic shock. Because diagnostic coding for lidocaine toxicity is uncommon, the primary outcome was a composite neurologic adverse event within 7 days of lidocaine exposure, defined as toxic encephalopathy, metabolic encephalopathy, altered mental status, or convulsions, which were evaluated as surrogate markers of potential lidocaine neurotoxicity. Results: After matching, 7,401 patients remained in each cohort. The incidence of the composite neurologic outcome did not differ significantly between patients receiving renal replacement therapy and matched controls (1.93% vs. 1.76%; RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.74-1.12; p=0.43). Rates of convulsions (0.62% vs. 0.66%; RR 1.07, p=0.76) and metabolic encephalopathy (0.41% vs. 0.27%; RR 0.67, p=0.16) were similarly not significantly different between groups. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched analysis of VT/VF patients receiving lidocaine, renal replacement therapy was not associated with an increased risk of short-term neurologic adverse events. These findings suggest that concerns regarding excess neurologic adverse events should not preclude lidocaine use in appropriately selected patients requiring renal replacement therapy. Further studies incorporating lidocaine dosing, serum concentrations, and renal replacement therapy parameters are needed to better define the relationship between renal replacement therapy and lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity.
title: Abstract 17115: Neurologic Outcomes Following Lidocaine Therapy in Patients with Ventricular Arrhythmias Receiving Renal Replacement Therapy: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac arrhythmias are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock and may contribute to hemodynamic instability, prolonged hospitalization, and adverse clinical outcomes. Although catheter ablation is an established treatment strategy for selected arrhythmias, its role in patients with cardiogenic shock remains poorly defined. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes following catheter ablation among patients with cardiogenic shock. Methods: This retrospective study included patients with atrial arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock who underwent catheter ablation during the index hospitalization between 2019 and 2025. Patients were included if they required inotropic support, vasopressor therapy, and/or mechanical circulatory support at the time of ablation. The ablation strategy, including pulmonary vein isolation or other arrhythmia-specific ablation approaches, was determined based on the underlying rhythm diagnosis. Results: Among 255 patients who underwent catheter ablation during the study period, 25 (9.8%) were in shock with atrial arrhythmia at the time of the procedure. Mean LVEF was 27.4 ± 16.2. Shock was cardiogenic in 22 patients (88.0 %) and septic in 3 (11.1%). Atrial fibrillation was the most common arrhythmia, occurring in 20 patients (80.0%), followed by atrial flutter in 4 (16.0%), and atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia in 1 (4.0 %). Mechanical circulatory support was utilized in 3 patients (12.0%), vasopressors in 11 (45.8%), and inotropes in 20 (80.0%). The median time from ablation to hospital discharge was 7.1 days (IQR, 4.8-23.4). In-hospital mortality occurred in 3 (12.0 %) patients. Among patients discharged alive, 12 of 17 patients (70.6%) were successfully weaned from inotropic support by hospital discharge. At 3 months, mortality occurred in 2 of 22 patients (9.1%). After accounting for the post-ablation blanking period, there was no arrhythmia recurrence in 16 of 20 patients (80.0%) between 3 and 6 months after discharge. Readmission occurred in 7 of 21 patients (33.3%) within 3 months and in 3 of 20 patients (15.0 %) between 3 and 6 months. Conclusion: In our study, most patients with shock and cardiac arrhythmias undergoing catheter ablation had cardiogenic shock and atrial fibrillation. Despite the high-risk clinical profile, the majority of surviving patients were successfully weaned from inotropic support and discharged from the hospital, with the majority not demonstrating recurrence of their arrhythmia. These findings suggest that catheter ablation may be feasible in selected patients with shock; however, larger comparative studies are needed to determine its safety, efficacy, and impact on survival, arrhythmia recurrence, and hospital readmission.
title: Abstract 17132: Catheter Ablation of Atrial Arrhythmias in Cardiogenic Shock: Patient Characteristics and Outcomes

abstract: Background: Trans-axillary access (TAx) has seen secular growth as the main extra-thoracic alternative to facilitated trans-femoral in a small subset of patients undergoing TAVI. Clinical outcomes based on the mode of trans-axillary access used (percutaneous versus surgical) are yet to be systematically analysed. Research Question: We set out to investigate whether percutaneous access would have a similar safety profile to surgical access with reduced resource utilisation. Methods: PubMed and EMBASE searches (through May 2025) were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines to identify studies comparing percutaneous versus surgical TAx access for TAVI. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) estimation. A pre-specified two-stage framework was applied: stage 1 - comparative odds ratio from matched registries; stage 2 - proportional (stacked) pooled analysis of absolute event rates from a broader single-arm cohort. Stroke, 30-day mortality, major vascular or access-site complications, bleeding, new permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and hospital length of stay (LOS) were compared. Heterogeneity was quantified using I 2 statistics. Results: Stage 1 results are reported with three studies comprising 3,041 patients (1,577 percutaneous vs 1,464 surgical). Percutaneous access was associated with a significant reduction in new PPM implantation (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.29-0.74, I 2 =57%). Valve types varied: TAXI and GARY registries predominantly used self-expanding valves (75-98%), with balloon-expandable valves used in Chung et al’s study. A consistent trend towards reduced bleeding (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.58-1.2, I 2 =0) in the absence of heterogeneity is observed, with no statistically significant differences in for 30-day mortality (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.37-1.59, I 2 =55%), stroke (OR 1.34, 95% CI 0.99-1.81, I 2 =32%), major vascular or access-site complications (OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.69-3.24, I 2 =76%). Resource utilisation: ICU stay (mean difference 0.30 days, 95% CI -0.59 to 1.18, I 2 =87%), hospital LOS (mean difference 0.12 days, 95% CI -1.25 to 1.50, I 2 =78%) was not significant in the context of heterogeneity. Conclusions: A percutaneous trans-axillary approach is safe with no detriment concerning mortality, stroke, bleeding or vascular complications in comparative observational data. A clinically meaningful 54 % reduction in the odds of new PPM implantation was observed, which has no evident mechanistic explanation, but the use of self-expanding valves in patients with more advanced conduction disease in the cohort could be the confounder driving the outcome.
title: Abstract 17182: Percutaneous versus Surgical Trans-Axillary Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Pooled Analysis of Clinical Outcomes

abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic stenosis. However, real-world data quantifying its association with a broad range of cardiovascular outcomes in patients with hypercholesterolemia remain limited. Hypothesis: Among adults with hypercholesterolemia, elevated Lp(a) is associated with higher 3-year risk of atherosclerotic and valvular cardiovascular outcomes compared with non-elevated Lp(a). Methods: We performed a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (65 healthcare organizations). Adults with hypercholesterolemia and elevated Lp(a), defined as 50 mg/dL or higher or 125 nmol/L or higher, were compared with adults with non-elevated Lp(a). Cohorts were matched 1:1 on demographics, comorbidities, lipid-lowering and cardiovascular medications, and lipid values. Outcomes were assessed over 1,095 days. Risk ratios (RRs) were calculated from event proportions, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models with log-rank P values.RESULTS: After matching, 15,925 patients were included in each cohort, and all standardized mean differences were below 0.10. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher risk of calcific aortic stenosis (1.6% vs 1.1%; RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.25-1.84; HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.23-1.80; P<0.001), coronary revascularization (1.1% vs 0.7%; RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.17-1.90; HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.15-1.86; P=0.002), acute myocardial infarction (1.0% vs 0.7%; RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.13-1.85; HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.10-1.80; P=0.006), acute limb ischemia or peripheral revascularization (0.3% vs 0.2%; RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.04-2.75; HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.02-2.68; P=0.041), new coronary artery disease (7.4% vs 6.1%; RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10-1.32; HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.10-1.32; P<0.001), and peripheral artery disease (2.9% vs 2.4%; RR 1.19, 95% CI 1.04-1.36; HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.02-1.34; P=0.023). Ischemic stroke was significant by RR but not by survival analysis (0.9% vs 0.7%; RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01-1.67; P=0.044; HR 1.25, 95% CI 0.97-1.62; log-rank P=0.079). Differences were not statistically significant for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (RR 1.18; P=0.061), all-cause mortality (RR 1.21; P=0.145), or aortic valve replacement (RR 1.47; P=0.250). CONCLUSIONS: In propensity-matched adults with hypercholesterolemia, elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher 3-year risk of myocardial infarction, coronary and peripheral atherosclerotic disease, and calcific aortic stenosis. These findings support Lp(a) measurement for cardiovascular risk stratification and reinforce the rationale for trials of targeted Lp(a)-lowering therapies.
title: Abstract 17184: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Adults with Hypercholesterolemia: A Comparative Observational Study

abstract: Introduction: Statin is a cornerstone of secondary prevention after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to lower low density liproprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Prior studies suggest women are less likely to receive high-intensity statin (HIS) therapy and achieve LDL-C targets after coronary revascularization. Research Question: In a large contemporary cohort, are there sex differences in statin intensity and LDL-C target attainment after PCI? Methods: We included consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a large US tertiary center between January 2012 and December 2023 with baseline and ≥1 follow-up LDL-C measurement obtained ≥21 days post-PCI. Patients with cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, active malignancy or dialysis were excluded. LDL-C <70 mg/dL was used as the primary threshold, consistent with the 2018 ACC/AHA Blood Cholesterol. Statin therapy at discharge was classified as HIS, low/moderate statin, or no statin. The co-primary endpoints were: (1) the proportion of patients achieving LDL-C <70 mg/dL at baseline, stratified by sex; and (2) among those with unattained LDL-C target at baseline (≥70 mg/dL), the proportion reaching LDL-C <70 mg/dL within one year, stratified by sex and statin intensity at discharge. Results: Among 9,260 patients (2,573 women [27.8%], mean age 69.4±11.5 vs. 65.8±11.5 years in men), baseline LDL-C≥70mg/dL was more prevalent in women than men (65.3% vs. 54.3%, p<0.001), despite women carrying a higher burden of CV risk factors. Statin was prescribed in 99.2% overall at discharge, similarly in women and men. HIS at discharge did not differ significantly between sexes (58.1% vs. 60.8%, p=0.142). Among patients with unattained LDL-C target at baseline, goal attainment within 1 year was significantly lower in women than men (33% vs. 46%), and this gap persisted across all statin intensity groups (HIS: 22% vs. 30%; moderate/low statin: 11% vs. 15%; both p<0.001) ( Figure 1 ). This sex gap in LDL-C levels was stable over 18 months ( Figure 2 ). Conclusions: Women undergoing PCI had a higher prevalence of LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL at baseline than men despite greater CV risk burden. Despite similar statin intensity at discharge, the sex-based difference in LDL-C observed at baseline persisted over 18 months of follow-up, suggesting that statin therapy alone did not close this gap.
title: Abstract 17195: Sex Differences in Statin Intensity and Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Goal Attainment After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

abstract: Background: Patients with type 2 diabetes are at high risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in spite of advances in glucose-lowering therapy. Clinical trials have demonstrated that both injectable and oral semaglutide reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this population. However, oral formulations of GLP-1 RAs have distinct pharmacokinetic profiles, with lower and more variable bioavailability than injectable formulations. Furthermore, their noninvasive administration may improve treatment acceptability, adherence, and persistence. Whether oral and injectable formulations of semaglutide confer comparable cardiovascular protection in routine clinical practice remains unexplored. Research Question: As both formulations are increasingly prescribed in clinical practice, this retrospective study aims to compare the reduction in MACE, identified as acute myocardial infarction, stroke and new heart failure diagnosis, between the oral and injectable formulations of the most frequently prescribed GLP-1 RA, semaglutide. Methods: We utilized the Epic Cosmos research database and identified 1,402,692 adults aged 40-75 years who initiated oral or injectable semaglutide between January 2019 and January 2023 and had no previous exposure to semaglutide or history of MACE. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity score matched on demographics, AHA PREVENT cardiovascular risk variables, and the social vulnerability index (SVI). Primary endpoints included first myocardial infarction, stroke, and new diagnosis of heart failure, over a three-year follow-up period. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals. Results: Propensity matching yielded two well-matched cohorts of 186,129 each with a mean age of 59 years (62% White, 54% women). Over three years of follow-up, oral semaglutide was associated with statistically significantly lower risk versus injectable semaglutide for myocardial infarction ( 3.88% versus 4.31%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.90, 95% CI 0.87-0.93, p<0.001), stroke (3.83% versus 4.49%, HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.84-0.87, p<0.001) and new heart failure diagnosis (9.92% versus 11.51%, HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.88, p<0.001). Conclusion: Oral semaglutide is associated with significantly lower three-year risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, and new heart failure diagnosis compared with injectable semaglutide. Although oral semaglutide has lower bioavailability than injectable formulations, the observed benefit may reflect differences in treatment adherence and persistence in routine clinical practice. This evidence supports oral semaglutide as a reasonable alternative to injectable formulations in appropriate patients with type 2 diabetes. Further prospective studies are warranted to better define comparative outcomes between oral and injectable formulations.
title: Abstract 17206: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Oral versus Injectable Semaglutide: A Propensity-Matched Real-World Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT), including ultrasound-assisted CDT, has emerged as a treatment option for intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) to improve thrombus resolution and right ventricular recovery while potentially reducing bleeding risk compared with systemic thrombolysis. However, its clinical benefit beyond standard anticoagulation remains uncertain. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov was performed from inception till May 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults with acute intermediate-risk, intermediate-high-risk, or submassive PE. Studies comparing CDT, including ultrasound-assisted CDT, plus therapeutic anticoagulation versus anticoagulation alone were included. Prespecified outcomes were 30-day mortality, right ventricular-to-left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio, hospital length of stay, major bleeding, minor bleeding, and any bleeding. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes were calculated using random-effects models and reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Results: Five RCTs including 858 patients were analyzed. CDT plus anticoagulation significantly reduced RV/LV ratio at 24-96 hours compared with anticoagulation alone (MD, -0.17; 95% CI, -0.28 to -0.05; p=0.004) (figure 1), with consistent findings after leave-one-out analysis (MD, -0.11; 95% CI, -0.17 to -0.05; p=0.0007). However, change in RV/LV ratio from baseline was not significantly different between groups (MD, 0.05; 95% CI, -0.18 to 0.28; p=0.67). CDT was not associated with a significant reduction in 30-day mortality (RR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.47-5.13; p=0.46) or hospital length of stay (MD, -0.27 days; 95% CI, -0.78 to 0.23; p=0.29). Major bleeding was not significantly increased (RR, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.69-3.64; p=0.27), although numerically higher rates of any bleeding (RR, 2.51; 95% CI, 0.97-6.49; p=0.06) and minor bleeding (RR, 3.94; 95% CI, 0.67-23.01; p=0.13) were observed. Conclusion: In this updated RCT-only meta-analysis of intermediate-risk PE, CDT/ultrasound-assisted CDT plus anticoagulation improved early RV remodeling, as reflected by lower follow-up RV/LV ratio, but did not significantly reduce 30-day mortality or length of stay. Bleeding outcomes were not statistically different, although any bleeding was numerically higher. Larger RCTs are needed to define whether early physiologic improvement translates into meaningful clinical benefit
title: Abstract 17209: Ultrasound-Assisted Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis Plus Anticoagulation versus Anticoagulation Alone for Intermediate-High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: An Updated Randmized Controlled Trails-Only Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: In cardiac amyloidosis (CA), thromboembolism is often framed as AF-related, yet amyloid infiltration may produce primary atrial myopathy with electromechanical dissociation and appendage low flow. Methods: We performed a scoping review of 41 reports/cohorts addressing atrial mechanics, thrombosis/embolism, anticoagulation, direct-current cardioversion (DCCV), AF ablation, and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) in CA. Study-level data were extracted for amyloid subtype, rhythm, atrial imaging/strain, thrombus/embolism, antithrombotic strategy, and procedural outcomes. Results: Multimodality studies showed atrial mechanical failure. In biopsy-proven CA, LA late gadolinium enhancement occupied 59±36% of LA myocardium versus 7.4±2.1% in hypertensive heart disease and 2.9±9.0% in nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy; total LA emptying was 19±14% versus 40±14% and 33±20%. In a 906-patient ATTR-CM cohort, median LA reservoir, conduit, and contraction function were 8.86%, 6.5%, and 4.0%; LA stiffness predicted mortality (HR 1.23, 95%CI 1.03-1.49), and atrial electromechanical dissociation occurred in 22.1% despite sinus rhythm. RA mechanics were also impaired: CMR-derived RA reservoir strain was 10.6±14.3% in CA versus 33.5±16.3% in HCM and 44.6±15.7% in controls. Thrombotic risk was not captured by conventional AF logic. In 156 CA patients undergoing TEE, intracardiac thrombus occurred in 42 (27%); AL-CA had higher prevalence than non-AL CA (35% vs 18%), and anticoagulation was protective (OR 0.09, 95%CI 0.01-0.51). In ATTRwt-AF, systemic thromboembolism was higher than AF controls (36.8% vs 19.5%) despite lower CHA2DS2-VASc (4.7 vs 5.4), lower LAVI (46.4 vs 61.3 mL/m2), and 95.6% anticoagulation use. Procedural data reinforced this phenotype: in CA DCCV, cancellation due to thrombus was 28% vs 7% in controls; acute success was 90%, but complications were higher (14% vs 2%). A 192-procedure DCCV series reported 99% acute success, 26% LAAT among selected TEE patients, and no 48-hour stroke/complications. In ATTR-CA ablation, freedom from recurrence was stage-dependent (64% in stage I/II vs 10% in stage III), with lower mortality after ablation versus medical management (29% vs 75%) and fewer HF/arrhythmia hospitalizations (1.7±2.4 vs 4.0±3.5). LAAC was feasible in CAMYLAAC (98.1% procedural success; ATTR-CA n=40/1159), with higher 5-year mortality (40% vs 19.2%); postablation LAAC data suggested aspirin-only de-escalation carried stroke/TIA/device-thrombus signals versus half-dose NOAC (5/31 vs 0/25). Conclusions: CA produces an “amyloid atrium” phenotype: infiltrated, stiff, mechanically failed, and thrombogenic beyond rhythm status or CHA2DS2-VASc. Atrial strain/LGE, LAA velocity, and AEMD may identify risk; rhythm control appears most durable early, and LAAC/OAC de-escalation should be individualized.
title: Abstract 17221: The Amyloid Atrium: A Scoping Review of Atrial Mechanical Failure, Thromboembolism, Cardioversion Risk, Anticoagulation, and Appendage Closure in Cardiac Amyloidosis

abstract: Background: Percutaneous ventricular assist device (PVAD) support is an established mechanical circulatory support strategy for cardiogenic shock (CS). Although PVAD primarily provides left ventricular (LV) unloading and hemodynamic support, its impact on venous return—a key determinant of systemic hemodynamics governed by stressed blood volume (SBV)—remains unclear. Because PVAD directly augments LV output, it may not directly alter SBV. However, PVAD-induced hemodynamic improvement may increase arterial pressure (AP), activate the arterial baroreflex, suppress sympathetic tone, and thereby reduce SBV. We hypothesized that PVAD support decreases SBV and examined the temporal changes in SBV during PVAD support through clinical observation and large-animal validation. Methods: In the prospective multicenter UNLOADERS-PVAD registry, 206 patients with CS supported by isolated PVAD were analyzed. SBV was estimated from right atrial pressure (RAP), left atrial pressure (LAP), and cardiac output (CO) through a generalized circulatory equilibrium model (Fig. 1A). SBV was assessed at six time-points from pre-PVAD implantation to just before PVAD weaning, and temporal changes were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model. For large-animal validation, we studied six dogs weighing 10.4 +/- 0.3 kg. CS was induced by coronary microembolization, followed by fluoroscopy-guided PVAD implantation. Hemodynamic measurements were obtained after 30 minutes of stabilization at minimum support (P1), during increased PVAD support (P3-P7), and after returning to minimum support (P1). SBV was calculated with the same model. Results: Among 206 patients (mean age 70.7 years, 74.3% male), 40 (19.4 %) died during the hospitalization. PVAD support improved systemic hemodynamics and was associated with an immediate decrease in SBV, from 47.2 [39.0-61.3] to 41.1 [29.1-49.4] mL/kg after PVAD initiation (p < 0.001). SBV continued to decrease during PVAD support, with an estimated reduction of 16.3 mL/kg from pre-PVAD implantation to just before PVAD weaning (95% CI, 13.2 to 19.3; p < 0.001) (Fig. 1B). In the CS experiment, increasing PVAD support immediately reduced SBV, which returned toward baseline after reduction to minimum support, reproducing the clinical findings (Fig. 2A). In addition, SBV showed an inverse relationship with PVAD-induced increases in AP (r = –0.75) (Fig. 2B), suggesting baroreflex-mediated sympathetic attenuation and redistribution of venous blood volume. Conclusion: PVAD support induces an immediate reduction in SBV in CS in both clinical and large-animal settings. These findings suggest that PVAD therapy not only provides hemodynamic support and unloads the left ventricle, but may also modulate autonomic tone and systemic venous return through baroreflex-mediated mechanisms.
title: Abstract 17244: Temporal Dynamics of Stressed Blood Volume During Percutaneous Ventricular Assist Device Support in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Introduction: Coronary cameral fistulas are rare coronary anomalies in which one or more coronary arteries communicate directly with a cardiac chamber. Although often asymptomatic, clinically significant fistulas may cause myocardial ischemia through coronary steal physiology and can mimic acute coronary syndrome.They have been reported in approximately 0.002% of the general population and in about 0.1%-0.25% of patients undergoing coronary angiography. Most are congenital, though acquired forms have been described after myocardial infarction, trauma, surgery, and percutaneous coronary intervention. Case Presentation: An 84-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prior cerebrovascular accident without residual deficit, hepatitis C-related cirrhosis now eradicated, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with acute shortness of breath and chest pain. Troponin rose from 17 ng/L to 740 ng/L and later peaked around 1500 ng/L, prompting initial treatment for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. However, recent coronary angiography had shown no obstructive coronary artery disease and instead demonstrated diffuse bilateral coronary cameral fistulas draining into the left ventricle through a large Thebesian venous network (Fig 1A) and Echo finding (Fig 1B). Her symptoms were ultimately attributed to coronary steal physiology from extensive coronary-to-left ventricular shunting. She was managed conservatively with rate control, cautious preload support, avoidance of nitrates, and reassessment for tertiary-center evaluation. Patient presented with same chest pain and shortness of breath with elevated troponin level for four times in three months and got managed for NSTEMI in the emergency department even she had non-obstructive Coronary Arteries and diagnosed Coronary cameral fistulas. Discussion: Coronary cameral fistulas are rare coronary anomalies in which one or more coronary arteries communicate directly with a cardiac chamber, bypassing the myocardial capillary bed. Most arise from the right coronary system, fewer from the left, and bilateral involvement is uncommon; similarly, most drain into right-sided chambers, whereas left ventricular drainage is rare.Our case is unusual because the patient had diffuse fistulous communications arising from both coronary systems and draining into the left ventricle through a large Thebesian venous network. Conclusion: Diffuse coronary cameral fistulas draining into the left ventricle are rare and may present late in life with chest pain and marked troponin elevation despite nonobstructive coronary arteries. Recognition of this entity is important because management differs from typical plaque-rupture acute coronary syndrome and is driven largely by anatomy, hemodynamics, quality of life, and overall goals of care.
title: Abstract 17249: Chest Pain Due to Diffuse Coronary Cameral Fistulas Draining Into the Left Ventricle and Mimicking Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Severe mitral annular calcification (MAC) complicates mitral valve surgery due to risks of atrioventricular groove disruption, prosthetic dehiscence, and paravalvular leak (PVL). Hybrid valve-in-MAC approaches using balloon-expandable transcatheter valves have emerged as an option for high-risk surgical patients. However, data regarding late structural complications and their management remain limited. We present a case of severe MAC with prior MitraClip therapy managed with open transatrial Sapien 3 implantation, later complicated by severe PVL requiring transcatheter closure. Patient Information: 67-year-old female with coronary artery disease, severe mitral regurgitation (MR) treated with MitraClip (2020), chronic kidney disease III, and prior breast cancer treated with mastectomy and chest radiation presented with recurrent heart failure admissions. Clinical Findings & Timeline: After initial improvement post-MitraClip, she began to develop progressive heart failure symptoms. Imaging showed severe mixed mitral stenosis/regurgitation with circumferential MAC, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and multivessel coronary artery disease. She underwent median sternotomy with open transatrial implantation of a 26 mm Edwards Sapien 3 valve, tricuspid annuloplasty, and CABG (2025). The postoperative course was uneventful. One year after implantation, she presented in cardiogenic shock secondary to severe prosthetic PVL. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Transthoracic echocardiography showed EF 40% with severe eccentric PVL. Transesophageal echocardiography localized the leak to the anteromedial commissural region. Right heart catheterization showed elevated left-sided filling pressures with large V waves (~30 mmHg), consistent with severe MR physiology. Given prior sternotomy and severe MAC, redo surgery was prohibitive. Therapeutic Interventions: Transcatheter PVL closure was performed using four Amplatzer Vascular Plug II devices (two 12-9 mm and two 10-7 mm), achieving near-complete resolution of regurgitation. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient was weaned from inotropes and left the ICU within 48 hours. No procedural complications occurred. The major adverse event was the delayed severe PVL causing her cardiogenic shock presentation. Discussion: This case highlights both the utility and limitations of hybrid valve-in-MAC strategies in high-risk patients. It illustrates a rare presentation of delayed severe PVL causing cardiogenic shock one year after transatrial Sapien 3 implantation. As valve-in-MAC procedures become more common, recognition of late PVL and close longitudinal surveillance will be increasingly warranted. Importantly, transcatheter PVL closure may serve as an effective rescue strategy for life-threatening delayed prosthetic valve dysfunction in this challenging population.
title: Abstract 17271: Delayed Severe Paravalvular Leak Following Transatrial Valve-in-MAC Implantation: A Case of Successful Transcatheter Rescue

abstract: Background: Device-related thrombus (DRT) remains a clinically important complication following left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), as it is associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Reported DRT incidence varies substantially across studies. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate DRT incidence after LAAO and evaluate between-study heterogeneity. Methods: PubMed and Google Scholar were systematically searched for studies evaluating DRT after percutaneous LAAO in adults with atrial fibrillation. Studies were required to include systematic post-procedural imaging surveillance for DRT. Studies exclusively enrolling patients with established DRT were excluded. Random-effects meta-analysis with logit transformation was used to pool incidence estimates. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and τ 2 statistics. Prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, and Egger's regression test were performed. Results: Twelve studies comprising 7,328 patients and 154 DRT events were included. The pooled incidence of DRT was 2.32% (95% CI, 1.47%-3.64%). Substantial heterogeneity was observed (I 2 =78.2%, τ 2 =0.39). The 95% prediction interval ranged from approximately 1% to 9%, indicating considerable variation in DRT incidence across clinical settings. Heterogeneity remained high among randomized trials alone (I 2 =83.4%). Sensitivity analyses identified the Amulet IDE trial (n=1,833; DRT incidence 0.49%) as a major contributor to heterogeneity; exclusion of this study reduced heterogeneity among randomized trials to I 2 =24.6% (p=0.26). Leave-one-out analyses demonstrated stable pooled estimates ranging from 2% to 3%. Egger's test showed no evidence of publication bias (p=0.71). Conclusions: DRT occurs in approximately 1 in 43 patients undergoing LAAO, with substantial variability across studies and clinical settings. Device-specific differences may contribute significantly to this heterogeneity. These findings support the need for standardized surveillance strategies and further investigation into device-specific approaches to DRT prevention and management.
title: Abstract 17278: Incidence and Variability of Device-Related Thrombus After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Real-World Studies

abstract: The adult mammalian heart has a limited capacity for regeneration following myocardial injury. Although considerable efforts have been directed toward cardiomyocyte replacement, current regenerative approaches have achieved only modest success. We previously identified a population of Nkx2.5+ cardiomyoblasts that becomes reactivated following myocardial infarction. These cells originate from embryonic epicardial progenitors and represent an endogenous source of regenerative potential. Thymosin β4, a G-actin-binding peptide, regulates cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation and has been implicated in cardiac repair. We therefore hypothesized that Thymosin β4 could enhance the mobilization and cardiomyogenic differentiation of Nkx2.5+ cardiomyoblasts after myocardial injury. MicroRNAs are critical regulators of cardiac development and regeneration. Screening of multiple candidate microRNAs in neonatal Nkx2.5+ cardiomyoblasts identified miR-590 as a potent enhancer of cardiomyogenic differentiation. To evaluate the regenerative effects of combined miR-590 and Thymosin β4 therapy, myocardial infarction was induced in C57BL/6 mice. miR-590 was delivered by intramyocardial injection immediately after infarction, whereas Thymosin β4 was administered systemically during the post-infarction period. Serial echocardiography demonstrated substantial recovery of cardiac function in mice treated with miR-590 and Thymosin β4, with restoration of regional left ventricular wall motion and preservation of systolic performance. In contrast, control animals receiving miR-mimic and PBS exhibited persistent anterior and apical wall hypokinesia with significant ventricular dysfunction. Histological examination revealed robust cardiomyocyte proliferation, enhanced angiogenesis, and markedly reduced scar formation in treated hearts. At 8 weeks after infarction, fibrosis was minimal, indicating extensive structural repair. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that combined miR-590 and Thymosin β4 therapy induces profound endogenous cardiac regeneration through activation of cardiomyogenesis and neovascularization, resulting in near-complete functional and structural recovery following myocardial infarction.
title: Abstract 17285: Near-Complete Functional and Structural Cardiac Regeneration by Cardiomyogenesis and Vasculogenesis

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is characterized by systemic hypoperfusion, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX), calculated as lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) х creatinine / platelet count, has been validated as a prognostic score in hematologic and critically ill populations. However, its role in patients with CS remains poorly defined. Hypothesis: EASIX is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with CS and may serve as a simple, clinically applicable risk stratification tool. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients with CS from January 2015 to December 2024 who had same-day LDH, creatinine, and platelet measurements available during hospitalization. For patients who underwent mechanical circulatory support (MCS), only laboratory values obtained before MCS initiation were considered. For patients with multiple measurements within a single day, the highest LDH and creatinine values and the lowest platelet count were used to derive a daily “worst” EASIX. EASIX was categorized into quartiles based on cohort distribution and analyzed accordingly. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, and the secondary outcome was the need for MCS. Results: Among 901 patients with CS, higher EASIX values were associated with worse clinical outcomes. Laboratory values required for EASIX calculation were obtained at a median of 3 days (IQR 11) from admission. EASIX quartiles were defined as ≤2.27, 2.28-5.94, 5.95-19.67, and >19.67, Figure 1. Compared with the lowest quartile (Q1), patients in the highest quartile (Q4) had significantly higher in-hospital mortality (HR 3.9, 95% CI 2.5-6.1, p<0.001). Patients in Q2 and Q3 also demonstrated progressively increased risk (HR 1.7, 95% CI 1.0-2.7, p=0.045 and HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.3-3.4, p=0.002, respectively), Figure 2 Panel A. Higher EASIX was also associated with increased use of MCS (HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.3-2.8, p<0.001 for Q2; HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.8-3.8, p<0.001 for Q3; and HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.8-3.7, p<0.001 for Q4, compared to Q1), Figure 2 Panel B. Conclusions: EASIX is a simple, readily available score that is associated with outcomes in patients with CS. Its use may facilitate early risk stratification and provide a practical tool for bedside clinical decision-making.
title: Abstract 17325: Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) as a Prognostic Score in Patients with Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: The presence of a left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus significantly increases thromboembolic stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation, necessitating effective anticoagulation to achieve thrombus resolution. Although vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin have historically been the standard of care, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus warfarin for active LAA thrombus management. Research Question: Do direct oral anticoagulants achieve comparable left atrial appendage thrombus resolution and safety outcomes compared with warfarin? Methods: A systematic search of PubMed and Embase through December 2025 identified 689 records; 88 duplicates were removed, and 601 records were screened by two independent reviewers using predefined inclusion criteria. Eleven studies, including 674 patients, met the inclusion criteria. The primary efficacy outcome was thrombus resolution; secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, stroke, and bleeding events. Relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model, and between-study heterogeneity was quantified with Higgins' I 2 . Results: Eleven studies including 674 patients were analyzed. Thrombus resolution was comparable between DOACs and warfarin (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.94-1.25; p=0.25; I 2 =29%), with a numerical, non-significant trend favoring DOACs. Bleeding events were similar between groups (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.51-1.95; p=0.99; I 2 =0%). Stroke (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.05-2.14; p=0.24; I 2 =0%) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.24-3.12; p=0.82; I 2 =0%) did not differ significantly, although both endpoints were informed by only two studies. Conclusions: DOACs demonstrated thrombus resolution rates and bleeding event rates comparable to warfarin, with no significant differences in stroke or all-cause mortality. The primary efficacy endpoint was supported by all 11 studies, whereas bleeding, stroke, and mortality had fewer contributing studies and limited event counts, warranting cautious interpretation. Given the predominantly observational and largely retrospective evidence base, these findings suggest that DOACs may represent a practical, logistically favorable alternative to warfarin for active LAA thrombus management. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.
title: Abstract 17336: Direct Oral Anticoagulants versus Warfarin for Left Atrial Appendage Thrombus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: The traditional massive/submassive classification of pulmonary embolism (mPE/sPE) has been replaced by the 2026 AHA/ACC system. mPE presented with sustained hypotension or cardiac arrest, while sPE showed heart strain or damage without hypotension or arrest. The new categories span a clinical spectrum from A (asymptomatic) to E (cardiopulmonary collapse). (Fig1) Whether this reclassification improves clinical discrimination of outcomes is unknown. Research Question: Do the new 2026 AHA/ACC PE categories demonstrate superior discrimination for in-hospital mortality and LOS compared to that seen with the prior binary framework? Methods: 608 patients with sPE or mPE were retrospectively analyzed at Detroit Medical Center from 2010-2016. All PEs were confirmed with CT. All patients were reclassified to the new 2026 AHA/ACC PE Categories using available PE Severity Index, right ventricular strain, cardiac biomarkers, hemodynamic data, and cardiac arrest status. PE treatment method was compared between anticoagulation alone (AC) vs advanced therapy (i.e catheter-directed therapy or systemic thrombolytics, ADT). Discriminatory performance for in-hospital mortality was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, comparing the old binary classification with the new ordinal AHA/ACC system. Correlation with length of stay (LOS) was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and the Kruskal-Wallis test. Results: 183/608(30.1%) were mPE patients and were mapped to Categories D1(132/183, 72.1%), D2(30/183, 16.4%), E1(2/183, 1.1%), and E2(19/183, 10.4%). 425/608 (69.9%) were sPE patients, recategorized into B (165/425, 38.8%), C1 (51/425, 12.0%), C2 (113/425, 26.6%), and C3 (96/425, 22.6%). 28/608(4.61%) patients were in-hospital deaths. The 2026 system demonstrated superior discrimination for in-hospital mortality compared with the old binary classification (AUC 0.825 vs. 0.754, 95% CI 0.033-0.111; p<0.001, Fig 2). LOS correlation also improved with the new system (ρ = 0.337 vs. 0.250; p < 0.001, Fig 3). 194/608(31.9%) of patients received ADT. Application of the new classification revealed that 49 of those 194 patients (25.3%) received ADT despite the 2026 guidelines not recommending it (Categories B and C1). This did not result in a difference in mortality compared to AC alone (0.0% vs 0.6%, P=1.0) but did result in higher rates of bleeding events (21.3% vs 3.0%, P<0.001). Conversely, among the 183 patients deemed to have a reasonable indication for ADT (D1-E2), 99 (54.1%) did not receive any ADT. This did not result in any statistically significant differences in mortality. Conclusion: The new 2026 AHA/ACC PE Categories demonstrated superior discrimination for in-hospital mortality and LOS compared to that seen from the prior sPE vs mPE binary system. Overutilization of ADT was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding episodes.
title: Abstract 17342: The New 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Pulmonary Embolism Categories Enhance Clinical Discrimination, a Real-World Cohort Analysis

abstract: Background: Tricuspid regurgitation is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in elderly patients. Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has emerged as a less invasive alternative for high-surgical-risk patients, but data on outcomes in octogenarians remain limited. Objective: To compare in-hospital outcomes of octogenarians and younger patients undergoing T-TEER. Methods: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (2017-2022) to identify T-TEER hospitalizations using ICD-10 procedure codes. Patients were stratified into octogenarians (≥80 years) and non-octogenarians (<80 years). Baseline characteristics and in-hospital outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate adjusted odds of mortality and procedure-related complications. Results: Among 11,472 T-TEER procedures, 5,511 were performed in octogenarians and 5,961 in younger patients(Table 1). Octogenarians were more often female and White, while younger patients had a higher comorbidity burden. Length of stay was similar between groups ( Table 2). After adjustment, octogenarians had lower odds of cardiogenic shock (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.43-0.68), acute kidney injury (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.99), respiratory failure (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.93), and need for invasive or non-invasive ventilation (Figure 1). They were also less likely to require permanent pacemaker implantation (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.27-0.94). Although pericardial complications were more frequent (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.05-2.77), there were no significant differences in in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, stroke, or major bleeding (Figure 1). Overall, octogenarians had lower odds of any in-hospital complication (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80-0.97) (Figure 1). Conclusions: Octogenarians undergoing T-TEER experience comparable in-hospital mortality and major cardiovascular outcomes to younger patients despite advanced age. They also have lower rates of several important postprocedural complications, supporting the safety and feasibility of T-TEER in carefully selected elderly patients. Chronological age alone should not preclude consideration for transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention.
