Annual in-hospital mortality declined from 26.9% (2022) to 26.6% (2023), 20.7% (2024), and 21.3% (2025; through November). The unadjusted odds of in-hospital death decreased 4% per calendar quarter (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-1.00, p=0.033). After adjustment for age, sex, and SOFA, the per-year reduction was significant (adjusted OR 0.85 per year, 95% CI 0.74-0.98, p=0.029). The composite of death or hospice discharge also decreased (OR 0.87 per year, 95% CI 0.76-0.99, p=0.036). Discharge home increased from 36.5% to 44.9% (OR 1.13 per year, 95% CI 1.00-1.27, p=0.053). Conclusions: Over 3.5 years following implementation of a structured 24/7 cardiogenic shock program with surgical mechanical circulatory support availability, in-hospital mortality at a single quaternary center fell by approximately 22% in relative terms, with a statistically significant per-year reduction after risk adjustment and an accompanying rise in discharge-home rates. These findings support a coordinated systems-of-care approach to CS and warrant multicenter confirmation.
title: Abstract 17948: Temporal Trends in In-Hospital Mortality Following Implementation of a Structured 24/7 Cardiogenic Shock Program at a Quaternary Center

abstract: Introduction/Background: The SMART-CHOICE 3 trial demonstrated improved ischemic outcomes with clopidogrel versus aspirin monotherapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in Korean patients. However, the generalizability of these findings to a diverse United States population, especially among females, elderly (>75 years old), and minority races, remains uncertain. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that clopidogrel monotherapy would be associated with lower rates of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) without increased bleeding compared with aspirin monotherapy among high-risk US patients following PCI. Methods/Approach: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of adults undergoing PCI who completed dual antiplatelet therapy for 6months-1year and subsequently transitioned to clopidogrel or aspirin monotherapy. High ischemic risk was defined by prior myocardial infarction, diabetes mellitus, or chronic kidney disease. Patients receiving oral anticoagulation, alternative P2Y12 inhibitors, active malignancy, or prior intracranial hemorrhage were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching was performed using demographic, clinical, and treatment-related variables (Table 1). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack, or cardiac arrest. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding and all-cause mortality. Results/Data: After propensity score matching, 10,712 patients were included in each treatment group. Clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a lower risk of MACCE compared with aspirin monotherapy (29.8% vs. 32.9%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-0.92; log-rank p<0.001; Figure 1). Major bleeding occurred less frequently with clopidogrel (4.1% vs. 8.0%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.43-0.54; p<0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower among patients receiving clopidogrel (5.5% vs. 8.6%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.57-0.70; p<0.001). Directionally consistent reductions in MACCE, bleeding, and mortality were observed among women (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p=0.002), patients aged >75 years (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.78-0.91; p<0.001), and patients with chronic kidney disease (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78-0.87; p<0.001). Conclusion: In a large, diverse US population-based real-world target-trial emulation, clopidogrel monotherapy following 6-12 months of DAPT in patients undergone PCI was associated with lower risks of MACCE, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality compared with aspirin monotherapy among high-risk patients. These findings extend the external validity of SMART-CHOICE 3 and support further evaluation of clopidogrel as a long-term antiplatelet strategy following PCI.

appraisal.design_and_n: After propensity matching, 10,712 patients in each treatment group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective EHR data with residual confounding; the 29.8% vs 32.9% event rates imply broad outcome definitions including all-cause mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Target trial emulation in TriNetX of clopidogrel versus aspirin monotherapy after PCI, testing external validity of SMART-CHOICE 3.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Clopidogrel was associated with a lower risk of MACCE than aspirin (29.8% vs. 32.9%; HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests transportability of a monotherapy trial to a diverse US population including women and older patients.

title: Abstract 17953: External Validation of SMART-CHOICE 3: Clopidogrel versus Aspirin Monotherapy Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in a Diverse US Population

abstract: Background: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is a high-risk thromboembolic substrate driven by atrial arrhythmias and amyloid-related atrial mechanical dysfunction. In practice, anticoagulation status guides the need for thrombus-exclusion imaging before cardioversion or other rhythm-control strategies. However, intracardiac and left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombi have been reported despite oral anticoagulation, raising concern that anticoagulation alone may be insufficient to exclude thrombus risk in CA. Objective: To evaluate the prevalence of intracardiac and LAA thrombus in adults with CA and characterize thrombus detected despite oral anticoagulation. Methods: We performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for adult studies of confirmed CA reporting imaging- or pathology-confirmed intracardiac, left atrial, or LAA thrombus with extractable event counts and denominators. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was performed for imaging-based studies. Pre-cardioversion cohorts were analyzed as a prespecified subgroup. Thrombus despite anticoagulation and autopsy/pathology cohorts were summarized separately. Study quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Results: Five imaging-based studies including 631 CA patients assessed for thrombus were included. Intracardiac/LAA thrombus was identified in 92 patients, with a pooled prevalence of 16.7% (95% CI, 9.8%-27.2%; I 2 =89.9%). In pre-cardioversion cohorts, pooled prevalence was 19.9% (95% CI, 13.6%-28.2%; I 2 =43.6%). Sensitivity analysis excluding a procedure-level cohort yielded a similar pooled prevalence of 16.1%. In studies with extractable anticoagulated denominators, thrombus was detected in 12.8% of anticoagulated patients undergoing assessment. Among studies reporting anticoagulation status of thrombus cases, at least 49.1% occurred despite documented anticoagulation. Imaging-based studies were generally at low to moderate risk of bias, mainly due to selective thrombus assessment and clinical-setting heterogeneity. Conclusion: Intracardiac and LAA thrombi are clinically common in CA, occurring in anticoagulated patients and pre-cardioversion settings where a missed thrombus may alter management. These findings support amyloid atrial myopathy as a distinct thrombotic substrate not reliably mitigated by conventional anticoagulation strategies. A lower threshold for imaging-based thrombus exclusion before cardioversion/rhythm-control procedures may be warranted in selected CA patients, even when anticoagulation appears adequate. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal thrombus-exclusion strategies, identify predictors of thrombus despite anticoagulation, and test whether CA-specific anticoagulation or rhythm-control pathways reduce thromboembolic events.
title: Abstract 17954: Intracardiac and Left Atrial Appendage Thrombus in Cardiac Amyloidosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prevalence and Occurrence Despite Anticoagulation

abstract: Introduction: Sotorasib is a KRAS G12C inhibitor used in advanced non-small cell lung cancer, with cardiovascular complications remaining poorly characterized. We describe a probable sotorasib-associated myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries phenotype presenting with acute heart failure shortly after treatment initiation. Patient Information: An 80-year-old man with metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer presented with progressive dyspnea and acute hypoxic respiratory failure six days after initiation of sotorasib therapy. Pre-treatment transthoracic echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% without regional wall motion abnormalities. Clinical Findings and Timeline: High-sensitivity troponin showed a marked dynamic rise from 4,840 to 6,565 to 9,797 to 9,924 ng/L. B-type natriuretic peptide was 1,607 pg/mL. Electrocardiography demonstrated sinus rhythm with anterolateral ischemic changes, including ST-segment depression and T-wave inversion in leads V2 to V4. Repeat echocardiography revealed newly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% to 40%, grade II diastolic dysfunction, moderate aortic stenosis, atrial septal aneurysm, and new lateral and apical wall akinesis. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Coronary angiography demonstrated non-obstructive coronary artery disease without a culprit lesion. The combination of myocardial injury, ischemic electrocardiographic abnormalities, new systolic dysfunction, new regional wall motion abnormalities, and absence of obstructive coronary disease was consistent with a myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries-like presentation. Infectious evaluation, including viral testing, was unrevealing, and no alternative trigger adequately explained the abrupt deterioration. Therapeutic Intervention and Outcome: Given the close temporal relationship between sotorasib initiation and symptom onset, drug-associated cardiotoxicity was suspected. Sotorasib was discontinued and supportive management was initiated. The patient subsequently died, precluding assessment of ventricular recovery. Discussion and Synthesis: This case highlights a probable early signal of sotorasib-associated cardiotoxicity. Although causality cannot be established from a single case and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging could not be completed, before-and-after imaging, objective myocardial injury, non-obstructive coronary angiography, and absence of an alternative explanation support a probable drug-associated cardiovascular event. As use of KRAS G12C inhibitors expands, clinicians should maintain awareness for new cardiac symptoms, biomarker elevation, or ventricular dysfunction shortly after treatment initiation.
title: Abstract 17964: Sotorasib-Associated MINOCA Phenotype Presenting with Acute Heart Failure: A Probable Early Pharmacovigilance Signal

abstract: Introduction: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare but increasingly recognized cause of acute coronary syndrome, most commonly affecting women with few traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Although chest pain is the typical presenting symptom, SCAD can rarely manifest with neurologic or systemic phenomena. We present a case in which multivessel SCAD initially presented with an episode of transient global amnesia (TGA). Patient Information: A 69 year-old woman with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, hyperlipidemia, prior myopericarditis, and a prior TGA episode presented as a code stroke activation. Her husband noted she had awakened with acute amnesia, disorientation, and an inability to retain new information. He reported the episode as strikingly similar to her TGA three years prior. Clinical Findings and Timeline: She denied chest pain and dyspnea on presentation. Troponin rose to a peak of 8,376 ng/L. Initial EKG showed nonspecific ST changes. CT head and CT perfusion were unremarkable. CTA head showed vertebral artery beading consistent with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD). Brain MRI was negative for stroke. EEG during the amnestic episode excluded seizure. TGA was confirmed as the neurologic diagnosis. On the third day of hospitalization she developed nausea and substernal chest discomfort. Repeat EKG showed new T wave inversions in inferior leads. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Echocardiogram showed preserved LVEF (65%) with no wall motion abnormalities. Cardiac MRI demonstrated anterolateral delayed enhancement, raising concern for myocarditis versus infarction. Coronary angiography revealed multivessel SCAD: 99% stenosis of the right posterior descending and posterolateral arteries, 70% distal LAD stenosis, and 80% third marginal stenosis. Therapeutic Interventions: Conservative management was pursued given hemodynamic stability and preserved LVEF. Clopidogrel was started. She was continued on rosuvastatin, metoprolol succinate and dapagliflozin. Anticoagulation was continued for atrial fibrillation. Follow-up and Outcomes: The patient was referred to vascular surgery and a tertiary FMD specialist at outpatient follow-up and remained clinically stable. Discussion and Synthesis: TGA is considered a once-in-a-lifetime event in the vast majority of patients. Recurrence is estimated at under 10% and should prompt consideration of an alternative or concurrent etiology. When a patient presents with cardiac biomarker elevation and incidental imaging findings concerning for systemic arteriopathy, SCAD should be on the differential. The absence of chest pain does not exclude an acute coronary etiology, and acute coronary syndrome can present with neurological manifestations.
title: Abstract 17987: Multivessel Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection in a Patient with Fibromuscular Dysplasia Presenting as Transient Global Amnesia

abstract: Background: HIV infection is associated with cardiovascular disease, including coronary artery disease, cardiomyopathy, and heart failure. As survival has improved in the modern antiretroviral era, HIV-positive patients are increasingly presenting with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). Whether HIV independently affects in-hospital outcomes in this population remains incompletely understood. Research Question: Is HIV infection independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes among patients hospitalized with ADHF? Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (2016-2020). Adult hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of ADHF were identified using ICD-10 codes and stratified by HIV status. Propensity-score matching (1:1) yielded 5,463 hospitalizations in each group. Continuous variables were compared using two-sample t-tests and categorical variables using chi-square tests. Multivariate logistic regression, adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, and disease severity, evaluated associations between HIV and clinical outcomes including acute kidney injury (AKI), acute respiratory failure, hemodialysis initiation, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, and in-hospital mortality, as well as length of stay, charges, and discharge disposition. Results: The matched groups were well balanced in age, sex, and most comorbidities. HIV-positive patients had higher rates of AKI (41.17% vs 37.32%, p<0.001), acute respiratory failure (28.65% vs 25.24%, p<0.001), and hemodialysis initiation (18.78% vs 16.95%, p=0.013), and lower MCS use (1.19% vs 1.79%, p=0.009). Rates of mechanical ventilation and in-hospital mortality were similar. After adjustment, HIV was associated with higher odds of AKI (aOR 1.22; 95% CI 1.13-1.33), acute respiratory failure (aOR 1.18; 95% CI 1.08-1.29), and hemodialysis initiation (aOR 1.20; 95% CI 1.02-1.42), and lower odds of MCS use (aOR 0.65; 95% CI 0.47-0.90). HIV was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.12; 95% CI 0.95-1.33). Length of stay (8.63±11.15 vs 8.27±12.70 days, p=0.116) and total charges ($114,961 vs $111,983, p=0.499) were similar, whereas HIV-positive patients were less frequently discharged home (15.58% vs 18.20%, p<0.001). Conclusion: Among ADHF hospitalizations, HIV infection is associated with greater end-organ complications without higher in-hospital mortality, and with lower MCS use, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring and equitable escalation of care.
title: Abstract 17996: Impact of HIV on In-Hospital Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: A Propensity-Matched Nationwide Analysis

abstract: Background: Regionalized surgical programs centralize procedural expertise but may fragment post-discharge care, particularly as community-care options expand. Non-index readmission after cardiac surgery, including SAVR, is common and associated with worse outcomes. We tested whether referral catchment was associated with documented readmission after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) at a regional VA cardiac surgery center. Methods: We studied 347 consecutive veterans undergoing SAVR from 2009 to 2024. Patient ZIP code centroids were geocoded to the nearest VA medical center in the regional network and collapsed into index-center local and three non-local referral catchments. The primary endpoint was 30-day documented VA readmission; any-time documented VA readmission was a sensitivity endpoint. Seven readmitted patients without classifiable timing were retained only in any-time analyses. Logistic regression adjusted for STS predicted morbidity/mortality (PROMM), age, and TAVR availability; sex was excluded due to zero readmissions among 9 women. Results: Thirty-day documented VA readmission occurred in 24/340 (7.1%). Baseline predicted STS PROMM was similar locally versus non-locally (median 8.2% [6.3-12.6] vs 8.5% [6.2-13.6]; p=0.802). Non-local referral catchment had lower 30-day documented readmission than the index-center local catchment (index-center local 12/88 (13.6%) vs non-local 12/252 (4.8%); OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.74; p=0.008). Results were similar for any-time documented VA readmission (index-center local 20/91 (22.0%) vs non-local 27/256 (10.5%); OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.22-0.80; p=0.008). Four-region 30-day rates showed a similar gradient (p=0.052). Among 30-day readmissions, leading documented reasons were infection/wound 46%, pericardial effusion/tamponade-related 21%, heart failure 8%, arrhythmia/PPM 4%, other 21%; cause distribution did not differ by local vs non-local catchment (p=0.800). Observed operative mortality (index-center local 1/91 (1.1%) vs non-local 7/256 (2.7%); p=0.686) and observed STS major morbidity (index-center local 20/91 (22.0%) vs non-local 44/256 (17.2%); p=0.393) were similar locally versus non-locally. Bleeding, LOS, ICU LOS, and VARC-3 composites did not significantly differ by catchment. Conclusions: In a regional VA surgical network, non-local referral catchments were associated with lower documented VA readmission after SAVR despite similar operative risk and clinical outcomes. Although readmissions were documented within VA records, the specific VA facility of readmission was unavailable, therefore, this gradient is consistent with differential post-discharge pathways and readmission capture across VA sites rather than true differences in surgical quality. Post-discharge surveillance across VA referral catchments warrant investigation as VA community-care options expand.
title: Abstract 17997: Readmission Capture Across Referral Catchments After Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in a Regional Veterans Affairs Network

abstract: Introduction Fluoropyrimidines, including 5-fluorouracil, are widely used in gastrointestinal malignancies and are among the most common non-anthracycline chemotherapies associated with cardiotoxicity. We present a case of fluorouracil-associated vasospastic angina presenting as a STEMI mimic. Patient Information A 71-year-old man with locally advanced gastric adenocarcinoma and no prior cardiac history began first-cycle modified FLOT with fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, docetaxel, and durvalumab. He received fluorouracil through a 46-hour infusion pump. Near completion, he developed intermittent substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm with dyspnea, diaphoresis, and nausea. Clinical Findings and Diagnostic Assessment In the emergency department, he was asymptomatic. ECG showed sinus rhythm without ischemic changes (figure 1), and high-sensitivity troponin T was 27 ng/L (normal <=15 ng/L). CT pulmonary angiography showed no pulmonary embolism. During observation, he developed severe chest pain with sinus tachycardia to the 130s. Repeat ECG showed anterolateral and inferior ST elevations (figure 2), and troponin increased to 44. The temporal association with fluorouracil, episodic symptoms, multi-territory ST elevations, and modest troponin elevation raised concern for coronary vasospasm. Therapeutic Intervention A STEMI alert was activated, and he received aspirin 324 mg and clopidogrel 600 mg. Given suspected vasospasm, IV nitroglycerin and diltiazem were initiated, with intracoronary nitroglycerin considered. His chest pain resolved, and repeat ECG 30 minutes later demonstrated resolution of ST-segment elevations, prompting cancellation of the STEMI alert. He was admitted for telemetry monitoring and continued on IV nitroglycerin. TTE demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function, ejection fraction of 57%, and no regional wall motion abnormalities. He had no recurrent angina or ischemic telemetry changes and was transitioned to oral isosorbide mononitrate. Follow-up and Outcomes He was discharged on oral isosorbide mononitrate with close cardio-oncology follow-up. Amlodipine was added for additional prophylaxis. After multidisciplinary discussion, fluorouracil rechallenge was planned with antianginal prophylaxis and close monitoring. Discussion Fluoropyrimidine-associated coronary vasospasm is an important STEMI mimic. Reported mortality ranges from 2.2-13% and recurrence after rechallenge has been reported in up to 90% of cases. Diagnosis is clinical and supported by temporal proximity to exposure, episodic angina, dynamic ischemic ECG changes, limited troponin rise, and rapid response to vasodilators. Although fluorouracil rechallenge has traditionally been discouraged, it may be considered in carefully selected patients when oncologic benefit is substantial, and alternatives are limited.
title: Abstract 18009: Fluorouracil-Associated Coronary Vasospasm Presenting as a Reversible STEMI Mimic

abstract: Purpose: Premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) are among the most common findings on exercise treadmill testing (ETT). They are usually benign, but exercise-induced PVCs, particularly frequent or recovery-phase ectopy, have been linked in other populations to increased cardiovascular risk and mortality. In tactical athletes, such findings can affect fitness-for-duty decisions and health. We examined whether overall or stage-specific PVC incidence was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in tactical athlete candidates. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 596 tactical athletes undergoing occupational ETT at a single center from 2016 to 2025. PVC incidence was defined as one or more PVCs during the duration of the test. MACE was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke or transient ischemic attack, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and atrial fibrillation, ascertained from clinical records. PVC-positive and PVC-negative candidates were compared using chi-square and Fisher exact tests, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). A secondary analysis compared MACE among candidates with recovery-phase PVCs, other-stage PVCs, and no PVCs. Results: Among 596 candidates, PVCs were present in 189 (31.7%) and MACE in 26 (4.4%). MACE was similar in PVC-positive and PVC-negative candidates (3.2% vs 4.9%; OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.25-1.61; p=0.40). A broader definition counting any documented cardiovascular diagnosis was concordant (6.3% vs 8.8%; OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.35-1.38; p=0.34). By PVC timing (n=520), MACE was similar across recovery-phase PVCs (2.6%), other-stage PVCs (4.9%), and no PVCs (6.4%; p=0.48). No comparison reached statistical significance. Conclusion: In this tactical athlete cohort, neither PVC incidence nor timing on ETT was associated with MACE. These findings suggest that PVCs identified on occupational screening may not, in isolation, justify automatic disqualification or reflexive downstream cardiac testing, supporting a more individualized, risk-factor-based approach that could help identify at risk-patients. Given the retrospective, single-center design and modest event count, prospective multi-center studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to define which PVC characteristics carry prognostic weight in tactical athletes.
title: Abstract 18012: Incidence and Timing of Premature Ventricular Contractions on Exercise Treadmill Testing and Cardiovascular Events in Tactical Athletes

abstract: Background: Sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) is commonly attributed to ischemic scar in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). However, concomitant CAD may create diagnostic anchoring and obscure additional arrhythmogenic substrates. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) can differentiate ischemic from nonischemic myocardial injury and identify coexisting cardiomyopathies. Case: A 70-year-old man with hypertension presented with chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, and near-syncope. Electrocardiography demonstrated sustained monomorphic VT (>200 bpm), successfully terminated with direct-current cardioversion. Subsequent ECGs revealed alternating left anterior and left posterior fascicular block. Troponin peaked to 25.5 ng/mL. Echocardiography showed EF 40-45% with inferolateral hypokinesis. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe distal LAD disease and moderate circumflex/obtuse marginal disease with negative physiologic assessment (iFR 0.98). The distal LAD was successfully stented.Given the severity of VT and conduction abnormalities, CMR was obtained. EF was 44% with three distinct late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) patterns: transmural inferolateral enhancement consistent with ischemic infarction; extensive mid-myocardial enhancement involving the basal-mid septum; and subepicardial enhancement of the apical lateral wall. These latter findings did not conform to a coronary distribution. No edema, pericardial disease, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy was present. Decision-Making: Although obstructive CAD and elevated troponin provided an apparent explanation for presentation, CMR identified both ischemic and nonischemic scar patterns. The coexistence of transmural, mid-myocardial, and subepicardial LGE, together with VT and alternating fascicular block, suggested a second arrhythmogenic substrate. Cardiac sarcoidosis was considered the leading diagnosis, and FDG-PET was recommended. Conclusion: CMR revealed concurrent ischemic and nonischemic myocardial injury despite an apparently sufficient ischemic explanation for VT. Recognition of dual scar pathology prevented diagnostic anchoring and redirected evaluation toward suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, highlighting the value of advanced tissue characterization in ventricular arrhythmias.
title: Abstract 18019: Beyond the Culprit Lesion: Cardiac MRI Revealing Concurrent Ischemic and Nonischemic Myocardial Injury Following Ventricular Tachycardia:

abstract: Background: Complete revascularization (CR) following percutaneous coronary intervention(PCI) is standard of care for patients presenting with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel coronary artery disease (CAD). However, the optimal timing of CR remains uncertain. This study examined clinical outcomes following immediate versus staged PCI among patients with STEMI and multivessel CAD without cardiogenic shock. Methods: We updated our March 2025 meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing staged and immediate CR. MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to April 30, 2026. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at ≥12 months. Secondary outcomes included individual components of MACE. Risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using random-effects models. We conducted two sensitivity analyses. First, we conducted a stratified analysis with trials categorized as 1) early staged CR (during index hospitalization) or 2) late staged CR (post-discharge). Second, we used meta-regression to examine timing to staged PCI and MACE. Results: We included nine reports from eight trials (n=4,129); four reports from three trials were published since our previous meta-analysis. Overall, no differences in MACE were observed between staged and immediate CR (11.5% vs 10.6%; RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.78-1.41). However, all-cause mortality was lower in the staged group (3.8% vs 5.0%; RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.97). Pooled estimates for all outcomes are presented in Table 1 . The first sensitivity analysis indicated a lower risk of MACE in trials with early staged CR compared with immediate CR (9.3% vs 11.7%; RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67-0.94) but not in trials with late staged CR (12.7% vs 10.0%; P-interaction=0.02) ( Table 2 ). There was no difference in all-cause mortality in trials with early or late staged CR compared to immediate CR. In the second sensitivity analysis, meta-regression suggested a trend toward lower MACE with shorter delays to staged PCI (β=0.0078 per day; 95% CI -0.0068-0.0224) ( Figure 1 ). Conclusion: Among patients with STEMI and multivessel CAD, a pooled analysis shows that staged PCI is associated with lower all-cause mortality compared to immediate CR. A reduction in overall MACE was only seen in a sensitivity analysis limited to trials of early staged CR. These results suggest improved clinical outcomes with early staged CR done during the index hospitalization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nine reports from eight trials (n=4,129).
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, and mortality difference arises from secondary outcomes with heterogeneous timing definitions.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of immediate versus staged complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE did not differ between staged and immediate complete revascularisation (11.5% vs 10.6%; RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.78-1.41); all-cause mortality was 3.8% vs 5.0% in the staged and immediate groups respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Timing of complete revascularisation in STEMI is an active guideline question.

title: Abstract 18039: Immediate versus Staged Complete Revascularization in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: The DOREMI (Milrinone as Compared with Dobutamine in the Treatment of Cardiogenic Shock [CS]) trial found no difference in outcomes or adverse effects between milrinone and dobutamine in CS. A post-hoc analysis showed that acute kidney injury (AKI) may modify treatment effect, with potential benefit of milrinone over dobutamine only in patients without AKI. Whether outcomes differ between these agents in patients with AKI remains unclear. Despite limited clinical evidence, many clinicians favor dobutamine in AKI due to milrinone’s renal clearance and the risk of hypotension and arrhythmia. In this retrospective study, we analyze a large cohort of CS patients with AKI treated with milrinone or dobutamine and assess their 30-day relative risk of all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiac events (MACE; stroke, AMI, and death), any tachyarrhythmia, AMI, and stroke. Methods: All Icahn Mount Sinai Health System patients were searched using TriNetX from 1/1/2005-5/1/2026. Identified by ICD codes, adult patients with CS and AKI were included. Those who did not meet inclusion criteria, had other shock types, or who had any outcome of interest prior to indexing were excluded. Split into those receiving milrinone or dobutamine, the cohorts were propensity matched and balanced for baseline demographics, comorbidities and antiarrhythmics. Statistical analysis was performed via Cox regression using the built-in TriNetX calculator. Results are reported as hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: After propensity matching, 1100 patients were included (milrinone n=550, dobutamine n=550). Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between groups. Patients on milrinone had a significantly reduced risk of mortality (HR 0.708, 95% CI 0.572-0.876, p=0.0013) and MACE (HR 0.792, 95% CI 0.658-0.954, p=0.0130), but a higher risk of arrhythmias (HR 1.485, 95% CI 1.192-1.851, p=0.0004) compared to dobutamine. Risk of stroke (HR 1.632, 95% CI 0.91-2.927, p=0.0966) or AMI (HR 0.776, 95% CI 0.548-1.1, p=0.1517) did not differ significantly. Conclusion: In this large propensity-matched cohort of patients with CS and AKI, milrinone was associated with lower risk of mortality and MACE but a higher arrhythmia risk compared to dobutamine. While prior randomized studies have not demonstrated differences between these inotropes in CS, our findings suggest that milrinone remains a viable option in CS with AKI and support further prospective studies to define optimal inotrope strategy in this high-risk population.

register_verdicts.note: Retrospective propensity-matched milrinone versus dobutamine comparison in an AKI subgroup, which does not replace a randomised first-line inotrope comparison.

title: Abstract 18081: Outcomes of Milrinone vs. Dobutamine in Cardiogenic Shock with Acute Kidney Injury

abstract: Background: B-type natriuretic peptides and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) reflect distinct biological pathways of cardiovascular risk, but the comparative prognosis of patients whose risk is dominated by one versus the other is not well characterized in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Hypothesis: Among adults with ASCVD, a BNP-dominant biomarker phenotype is associated with different 3-year cardiovascular outcomes than an hs-CRP-dominant phenotype. Methods: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (67 healthcare organizations). Adults with ASCVD and LDL-C of at least 130 mg/dL were classified as BNP-dominant (BNP at least 100 pg/mL or N-terminal pro-BNP at least 300 pg/mL with hs-CRP at most 2 mg/L) or hs-CRP-dominant (the inverse pattern). After 1:1 matching on demographics, diagnoses, medications, and laboratory values, 11,133 patients per group were analyzed over 1,095 days. Risk ratios (RR) were derived from event proportions; hazard ratios (HR) used Cox models with log-rank p-values. Results: All standardized mean differences were below 0.10 after matching. Compared with the hs-CRP-dominant phenotype, the BNP-dominant phenotype was associated with higher risk of heart failure (10.2% vs 6.5%; RR 1.56, 95% CI 1.43-1.70; HR 1.57, 1.43-1.73; P<0.001), acute myocardial infarction (13.4% vs 10.0%; RR 1.34, 1.25-1.44; HR 1.36, 1.26-1.47; P<0.001), new-onset atrial fibrillation/flutter (27.4% vs 20.7%; RR 1.32, 1.26-1.39; HR 1.37, 1.30-1.45; P<0.001), coronary revascularization (4.2% vs 3.3%; RR 1.29, 1.13-1.48; HR 1.29, 1.13-1.48; P<0.001), major adverse cardiovascular events (37.6% vs 31.3%; RR 1.20, 1.16-1.25; HR 1.25, 1.20-1.31; P<0.001), and ischemic stroke (13.4% vs 12.0%; RR 1.12, 1.04-1.20; HR 1.12, 1.04-1.20; P=0.003). No significant differences were observed for all-cause mortality (RR 1.05; P=0.290), acute kidney injury (RR 1.04; P=0.326), all-cause hospitalization (RR 0.99; P=0.518), or troponin elevation (RR 1.02; P=0.657). Conclusions: In propensity-matched adults with ASCVD, a BNP-dominant biomarker phenotype was associated with higher 3-year risk of heart failure, myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation, revascularization, MACE, and stroke than an hs-CRP-dominant phenotype, while mortality and hospitalization were similar. These findings support natriuretic peptide elevation as a marker of adverse cardiovascular risk in ASCVD.
title: Abstract 18084: Comparative Prognosis of BNP-Dominant and hs-CRP-Dominant Biomarker Profiles in ASCVD: A Propensity Score Matched Retrospective Study

abstract: Background: Conduction abnormalities are common complications following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Real-world utilization of ambulatory rhythm monitoring after TAVR and its association with heart block detection needing pacemaker or ICD implantation remain poorly characterized. We evaluate ambulatory rhythm monitoring practices post-TAVR using a large multicenter electronic health record database. Methods: Using the TriNetX database through May 31, 2026, we identified adults undergoing TAVR who survived to discharge and had ≥12 months of prior healthcare data. Patients with prior pacemakers, ICDs, implantable loop recorders, or pre-existing high-grade atrioventricular block were excluded. We characterized post-TAVR ambulatory rhythm monitoring utilization and assessed rates of permanent pacemaker/ICD implantation within 30 days and conduction abnormality detection within 30-90 days. Results: Among 42,398 adults undergoing TAVR who met eligibility criteria, ambulatory rhythm monitoring was used in a minority of patients. The most commonly utilized modalities were mobile cardiac telemetry (9.4%, n=3,971), patient-activated event monitors (8.7%, n=3,697), and 8-14-day patch monitors (7.8%, n=3,148), followed by 24-48-hour Holter monitors (6.7%, n=2,642) and extended (>48-hour-7-day) patch monitors (4.0%, n=1,614). Implantable loop recorders were used least frequently (1.5%, n=628).Within 30 days of TAVR, permanent pacemaker or ICD implantation occurred in 7.2% of patients monitored with 24-48-hour Holter devices, 6.7% with extended patch monitors, 5.4% with event monitors, 5.3% with 8-14-day patch monitors, 4.3% with mobile cardiac telemetry, and 4.2% with implantable loop recorders. Documented conduction abnormalities within 30-90 days post-TAVR were most frequently identified among implantable loop recorder recipients (42.1%), followed by extended patch monitors (39.6%), 24-48-hour Holters (39.2%), event monitors (37.0%), 8-14-day patch monitors (36.0%), and mobile cardiac telemetry (28.8%). Conclusions: Ambulatory rhythm monitoring after TAVR remains underutilized despite the high burden of post-procedural conduction disturbances. More intensive monitoring, particularly implantable loop recorders and extended patch monitors, was associated with greater detection of clinically significant abnormalities. These findings demonstrate substantial variability in post-TAVR surveillance and support further study to define optimal monitoring strategies for early arrhythmia and conduction disease detection.
title: Abstract 18093: Ambulatory Rhythm Monitoring After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Database Observational Study Using TriNetX Through May 2026

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an alternative therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in patients who are not candidates for long term systemic anticoagulation. PDL defined as a continuous stream of contrast between the Watchman device and the left atrial appendage (LAA) wall doubles the risk of stroke. Contrast may still enter the LAA through the fabric of the Watchman device, incomplete endothelialization, contributing a second cause of LAA “patency” post implant. Intraprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) is a novel technique for real-time LAAO validation with hitherto unreported peri-device leak (PDL) and device patency outcomes. Hypothesis: Intraprocedural CT guidance improves device deployment accuracy, resulting in lower PDL and patency rates compared to standard imaging techniques. Method: This is a retrospective, single-center, observational study. Patients underwent intraprocedural CTA-guided LAAO with Watchman FLX and FLX Pro from August 2020 to May 2025 using the Canon Aquilion ONE scanner. Post-implantation surveillance via CTA was conducted at 45 days, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year. Frequency of PDL and LAA patency were compared to data shared from authors of the SWISS APERO trial reporting 13-month CTA follow up for Watchman FLX implantation. Results: A total of 745 patients underwent LAAO with 414 Watchman FLX, 331 Watchman FLX Pro. Patient characteristics included mean age of 75.8 ± 7.8 years with 64% male, BMI 31.42 ± 11.53 and a CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score of 4.61 ± 1.47. AF was classified as paroxysmal (55%), persistent (34.8%), and long-standing persistent (9.8%) in the study cohort. At the 1-year CTA surveillance, the overall patency rate was 36.5% (272/745), with 28.1% (209/745) incomplete endothelialization and 8.4% (63/745) with visible leaks. The 1-year patency rates for Watchman FLX from the SWISS-APERO trial was 46.8% (29/62) with PDL at 27.4% (17/62), notably the SWISS APERO trial published patency rate of 48.8% for combined Watchman 2.5 and FLX devices but isolated Watchman FLX data was provided directly by the investigators. Intraprocedural CTA cohort demonstrated a lower 1-year patency (36.5% vs. 46.8%) and PDL rates (8.3% vs. 27.4%) compared to standard approach. Conclusion: intraprocedural CTA guidance prior to device release in watchman implantation optimize device deployment, leading to reduced PDL and LAA patency rates compared to standard deployment and emerging as a potential new standard of care.
title: Abstract 18114: Intraprocedural Computed Tomography Angiography for Optimization of Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Impact on Residual Patency

abstract: Background: AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) carries high early mortality despite rapid reperfusion. Reperfusion during severe hemodynamic instability may not adequately correct low cardiac output or end-organ hypoperfusion. Early Impella support before PCI may provide ventricular unloading and circulatory stabilization prior to revascularization; however, optimal implantation timing remains uncertain. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that Impella implantation before PCI would be associated with lower mortality and complication rates than implantation during or after PCI in patients with AMI-CS. Methods: We performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science through February 2026. Eligible studies included adults with AMI-CS treated with Impella, reporting outcomes by timing: pre- or during/post-PCI. The primary outcome was short-term mortality (≤30 days). Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, limb ischemia, vascular complications, acute kidney injury (AKI), stroke, and device-related complications. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models. Results: Seven studies (789 patients) were included; 320 received Impella pre-PCI and 469 during/post-PCI. Pre-PCI Impella was associated with significantly lower short-term mortality (36.3% vs. 53.1%; RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.55-0.80; p<0.0001; I 2 =12%) and fewer vascular complications (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.92; p=0.02; I 2 =0%). No significant differences were observed in major bleeding (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.23-1.19; p=0.12; I 2 =0%), limb ischemia (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.60-1.39; p=0.67; I 2 =29%), AKI (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.55-1.29; p=0.43; I 2 =23%), stroke (RR 0.70, 95% CI 0.09-5.25; p=0.73; I 2 =0%), or device-related complications (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.60-1.39; p=0.67; I 2 =29%). Conclusions: In AMI-CS patients undergoing Impella-supported PCI, pre-PCI implantation was associated with lower short- and intermediate-term mortality than during/post-PCI implantation, without increased major bleeding, limb ischemia, or vascular complications, supporting early mechanical unloading and stabilization before revascularization.
title: Abstract 18123: Impella Before PCI vs After PCI in Acute Myocardial Infarction with Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Timing Strategy in the Door-to-Balloon Era

abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) frequently coexist, presenting significant management challenges, particularly due to autonomic dysregulation. Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT) enhances parasympathetic activity and restores autonomic balance in HFrEF; however, its effect on AF burden remains uncertain. Case presentation A 70-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy and advanced heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was referred for evaluation due to persistent symptoms despite maximally tolerated medical therapy (GDMT). His past medical history included chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure (NYHA class III), paroxysmal AF, non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, stage 2 chronic kidney disease, percutaneous coronary intervention in 2009, three-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting in 2020, and dual-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation in 2014. The patient reported progressive exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, lower extremity edema, abdominal bloating, intermittent dizziness, and palpitations. At the time of evaluation, his medications included metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, empagliflozin 10 mg daily, sotalol 25 mg daily, rivaroxaban 10 mg daily, and furosemide as needed. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 17%, decreased from 22% the previous year. Device interrogation revealed an AF burden of 6.6% and episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia. The patient was diagnosed with advanced symptomatic HFrEF with concomitant paroxysmal AF and ventricular arrhythmias despite optimized GDMT. Catheter ablation was considered but the patient was previously deemed ineligible due to hemodynamic instability. Given the clinical suspicion of autonomic imbalance contributing to his symptoms and arrhythmia burden, BAT using the Barostim system was selected as adjunctive therapy. At follow-up, the patient exhibited marked functional improvement and increased daily exercise tolerance. He was able to perform daily exercise without limitation. Repeat clinical assessment demonstrated a substantially reduced arrhythmia burden. Discussion Autonomic modulation represents a potential therapeutic target for selected patients with concomitant HFrEF and AF, warranting further prospective investigation. Further investigation is needed to explore the role of autonomic modulation as a target therapy in patients with concomitant HFrEF and AF.
title: Abstract 18130: Beyond Heart Failure: Baroreflex Activation Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation A Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Cutibacterium acnes ( C. acnes ) is a rare cause of prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE), typically identified via blood culture or echocardiographic findings. We describe C. acnes mitral annuloplasty ring endocarditis presenting with embolic stroke and only discovered exclusively intraoperatively during third-time sternotomy having satisfied zero Duke criteria pre-operatively. Patient Information: An 80-year-old male with mitral valve repair (1994 with redo-sternotomy in 1996 for thrombus on valve), ventricular tachycardia with implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, permanent atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presented with NYHA class IV heart failure and multi-territory embolic strokes. He denied fever, chills, or constitutional symptoms. Clinical Findings: TTE demonstrated severe prosthetic mitral stenosis (mean gradient 21 mmHg, valve area 1.24 cm 2 ), massively dilated left atrium (volume index 822 mL/m 2 ), severe tricuspid regurgitation, and PASP 52 mmHg. Brain MRI confirmed acute embolic infarcts in multiple vascular territories. Blood cultures were negative. Three pre-operative echocardiograms including two transesophageal echocardiograms (TEE) showed no vegetations or perivalvular abnormality. Diagnostic Assessment: CT identified LAA thrombus and annular geometry precluding transcatheter mitral valve-in-ring (TMViR); open redo surgery was elected. Embolic strokes were attributed to atrial fibrillation and LAA thrombus; endocarditis was not suspected. Intraoperatively, a mitral ring abscess and gross vegetations were discovered, absent on all prior imaging. Operative cultures confirmed C. acnes at seven days. In retrospect, multi-territory emboli may represent unrecognized septic embolization. Therapeutic Intervention: Third-time sternotomy: redo mitral valve replacement, tricuspid valve repair, and LAA thrombectomy. Empirical antibiotics narrowed to ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for six weeks per AHA PVE guidelines. Follow-up and Outcomes: Post-operative echocardiography confirmed normalized mitral gradients (mean 4 mmHg) and PASP reduction from 52 to 27 mmHg. At six months, the patient was NYHA class II, exercising four days weekly in cardiac rehabilitation. Discussion: Four lessons emerge: (1) C. acnes PVE can satisfy zero Duke criteria masquerading as prosthetic stenosis; (2) multi-territory embolic stroke with a prosthetic valve should prompt suspicion for occult PVE even without fever or echocardiographic findings; (3) LAA thrombus contraindicated TMViR and paradoxically ensured surgical source control for unrecognized PVE; (4) intraoperative culture of explanted prosthetic material may be the sole diagnostic modality. Patient Perspective: Patient expressed relief the infection was discovered and treated, noting sustained improvement in energy and daily function.
title: Abstract 18133: Occult Cutibacterium acnes Prosthetic Mitral Valve Endocarditis Discovered Intraoperatively During Third-Time Sternotomy: A Case Report

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries devastating mortality and consumes extraordinary healthcare resources. Its comprehensive national economic burden stratified by mechanical circulatory support (MCS) strategy, insurance type, and socioeconomic status remains uncharacterized in the contemporary era. Methods: We analyzed the 2021 National Inpatient Sample to identify adult CS hospitalizations (ICD-10: R57.0). Costs were derived using hospital-level cost-to-charge ratios. Primary outcomes were total national cost burden and in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression with Rao-Scott survey adjustment identified independent predictors of extreme cost (top quartile ≥$132,277) and mortality, adjusting for demographics, CS etiology, MCS type, organ failure burden, and hospital characteristics. Results: Among 211,380 weighted CS hospitalizations, the total national economic burden reached $24.3 billion - mean $116,134 and median $63,959 per hospitalization. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 33.7%. HF-CS comprised 69.5% of admissions with lower mortality than AMI-CS (27.2% vs 36.4%, p<0.001). MCS strategy was the dominant cost driver — median costs escalated from $54,080 (no MCS) to $98,192 (IABP), $160,109 (Impella), and $282,205 (ECMO). On multivariable analysis, ECMO independently predicted extreme cost (aOR 7.49, 95% CI 6.10-9.20), followed by Impella (aOR 6.92, 6.14-7.80) and IABP (aOR 2.75, 2.49-3.05; all p<0.001). Higher income independently predicted both lower mortality (Q4 vs Q1: aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.74-0.85, p<0.001) and higher cost (aOR 1.28, p<0.001). Uninsured patients faced the highest adjusted mortality (aOR 1.64, 95% CI 1.43-1.87, p<0.001), while Medicaid patients also carried excess mortality risk (aOR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01-1.20, p=0.032) compared with Medicare. Privately insured patients had the lowest mortality (28.0%) with no significant adjusted excess risk. Conclusions: CS imposes a $24.3 billion annual national burden. In line with increase use of MCS and their associated cost, mortality in HFCS was lower than AMI-CS, while insurance status and socioeconomic position independently determined survival. Uninsured patients face dramatically higher mortality a stark and urgent marker of healthcare inequity in CS management.
title: Abstract 18135: The Cost of Healthcare Inequality in the US, a $24 Billion Crisis in Cardiogenic Shock Hospitalizations: A 2021 NIS Analysis

abstract: Background: Valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is limited by residual transvalvular gradients, particularly in small surgical bioprostheses. Bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) has emerged as an adjunct to optimize transcatheter heart valve (THV) expansion, but its net clinical benefit remains uncertain. Methods: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science; through May 2026) identified comparative and single-arm BVF cohorts. Comparative outcomes were pooled using random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I; certainty of evidence with GRADE. Subgroup analyses were pre-specified by valve size (≤21 vs >21 mm) and BVF timing (before vs after THV implantation). Results: Seven studies (n=3,627) were included. BVF was associated with lower Doppler-derived residual gradients vs no BVF (pooled mean difference –3.8 mmHg [95% CI –5.8, –1.7]; I 2 =71%; k=2 comparative datasets). Discharge aortic valve area was higher with BVF (1.6 vs 1.4 cm 2 ) and VARC-2 device success was higher (93% vs 68%). In a contemporary single-registry analysis (n=2,975), BVF was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 2.51 [1.30-4.84]) and life-threatening bleeding (OR 2.55 [1.44-4.50]); stroke rates were similar. Subgroup point estimates were numerically larger for pre-THV BVF (mortality OR 2.90 [1.21-6.94]; bleeding OR 4.48 [2.07-9.72]) than post-THV BVF (mortality OR 2.10 [0.80-5.10]; bleeding OR 2.00 [0.99-4.04]); no formal interaction testing was reported, and subgroup estimates remained directionally concordant. Single-arm cohorts showed within-patient gradient reduction of –8.0 to –32.9 mmHg and aortic valve area gain of +0.3 to +1.0 cm 2 . GRADE certainty was very low to low across outcomes. Conclusions: BVF reduces echocardiographically-derived residual gradients during ViV-TAVR but is associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality and life-threatening bleeding in single-registry data. The clinical significance of Doppler gradient reduction in ViV-TAVR is challenged by contemporary randomized data (LYTEN) showing no association between echocardiographic gradients and clinical outcomes; mechanistic concerns with incomplete THV expansion (altered leaflet kinematics, sinus washout, subclinical leaflet thrombosis) remain to be defined. BVF should not be considered a routine adjunct; prospective randomized trials are needed to identify which patients, if any, derive net clinical benefit.
title: Abstract 18139: Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture in Valve-in-Valve TAVR: Hemodynamic Gain vs Procedural Risk — A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Baseline lactate is widely used for early mortality risk stratification in cardiogenic shock, but its prognostic performance may be altered by high-grade mitral regurgitation (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) due to their distinct hemodynamic effects. Whether this attenuation is specific to lactate or extends to broader illness-severity scores is unknown. Methods: We analyzed 1,532 cardiogenic shock hospitalizations from the MIMIC-IV critical care database (v3.1) with baseline lactate, echocardiographic assessment of MR and TR, and in-hospital mortality data. Baseline lactate was defined as the first lactate measurement recorded within 4 hours of ICU admission. Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) and APACHE III were derived from data collected during the first 24 hours of ICU admission. MR and TR severity were categorized as none-to-mild, moderate, or high-grade, with none-to-mild serving as the reference group. Discrimination for in-hospital mortality was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for baseline lactate, SOFA, and APACHE III. AUCs were compared between the reference and high-grade MR/TR groups using DeLong testing. Results: Baseline lactate was a weaker predictor of in-hospital mortality in patients with high-grade regurgitation. For MR, lactate AUC declined from 0.645 in the reference group to 0.563 in the high-grade group (p=0.030). For TR, lactate AUC declined from 0.661 to 0.565 (p=0.009). Notably, in-hospital mortality was nearly identical between TR reference and high-grade TR groups (38.6% vs 38.9%), yet lactate predicted mortality significantly less effectively in the high-grade TR group than in the reference group. In contrast, SOFA maintained similar mortality discrimination in reference and high-grade groups for both MR (AUC 0.773 vs 0.756, p=0.592) and TR (AUC 0.783 vs 0.766, p=0.587). APACHE III demonstrated an intermediate pattern, with lower discrimination in high-grade MR that approached significance (0.754 vs 0.690, p=0.056) and significantly lower discrimination in high-grade TR (0.764 vs 0.680, p=0.013). Conclusions: In cardiogenic shock, high-grade MR and TR attenuated the mortality discrimination of baseline lactate, while SOFA-based discrimination remained preserved. APACHE III showed partial attenuation, particularly in high-grade TR. These findings suggest that high-grade MR and TR selectively reduce the prognostic performance of lactate and APACHE III, while SOFA remains more robust for mortality risk assessment in cardiogenic shock.
title: Abstract 18155: High-Grade Mitral and Tricuspid Regurgitation Selectively Attenuate Lactate-Based Mortality Risk Discrimination in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries a persistent 30-50% in-hospital mortality despite advances in mechanical circulatory support. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly deployed in refractory CS, yet hemodynamic monitoring strategies remain unstandardized. Pulmonary artery catheterization (PAC) offers precise measurement of filling pressures, cardiac output, and mixed venous oxygen saturation — parameters critical for titrating vasopressors and managing right ventricular failure on ECMO — but its independent effect on survival in this population has not been established in a large real-world cohort. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (174 healthcare organizations), we identified adults (≥18 years) with CS (ICD-10 R57.0) who underwent ECMO and stratified them by PAC use. Patients were matched 1:1 via propensity scoring across 54 covariates, including age, sex, race/ethnicity, cardiovascular and renal comorbidities, medication classes, and index laboratory values (troponin, BNP, creatinine). The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality, evaluated by risk analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival, and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: The unmatched cohort comprised 8,960 patients in the no-PAC group and 3,456 in the PAC group. At baseline, the PAC group had significantly higher rates of ischemic heart disease (79.0% vs. 65.3%), hypertension (81.3% vs. 65.6%), chronic kidney disease (43.1% vs. 29.3%), and greater metabolic and hematologic comorbidity burden — indicating that PAC was preferentially used in higher-risk patients. After propensity matching (3,281 pairs, all standardized differences <0.10), the no-PAC group had significantly higher 30-day mortality (40.8% vs. 37.2%; risk difference 0.036, 95% CI 0.012-0.060; p=0.003; OR 1.163, 95% CI 1.053-1.285). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed inferior survival at 30 days in the no-PAC group (56.8% vs. 61.9%; HR 1.176, 95% CI 1.088-1.271; log-rank p<0.001), with proportional hazards assumption satisfied (p=0.514). Conclusions: In this large propensity-matched real-world analysis, PAC-guided monitoring in ECMO-supported CS was independently associated with a 17.6% relative reduction in 30-day mortality hazard. Notably, the survival benefit persisted despite the PAC group carrying greater baseline comorbidity burden before matching, strengthening the causal inference. These data challenge the notion that PAC monitoring is dispensable in ECMO-supported CS and support its prospective evaluation within standardized resuscitation protocols for this high-mortality population.
title: Abstract 18176: Pulmonary Artery Catheter Use in Cardiogenic Shock Patients on ECMO: A Propensity-Matched Analysis from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network

abstract: Background: Recent Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) classification of myocardial injury severity have suggested that the outcome of reperfused myocardial infarction (MI) is determined not only by infarct size, but also by the presence of microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH). However, the gold standard for comprehensive assessment of these elements using Cardiac MRI (CMR) currently requires multiple breath-held, ECG-gated acquisitions, resulting in prolonged examinations (>40 mins). To address this limitation, we developed an 8-minute free-breathing whole-heart CMR framework that enables comprehensive characterization of myocardial injury severity. We tested this in a porcine model with MI and compared it to the clinical standard 1-hour procedure. Methods: A free-breathing, non-ECG-gated 3D inversion-recovery prepared free-running acquisition was implemented at 3T and reconstructed using a low-rank tensor framework. The acquisition continuously sampled contrast kinetics and relaxation dynamics following gadolinium administration, enabling retrospective generation of time-resolved enhancement images. Reperfused porcine MI models (n = 6) were imaged at 5-7 days of MI and underwent both conventional clinical CMR and the proposed free-running protocol. Conventional 2D cine, T2* and LGE images were acquired at diastole during end-expiration breath-holds. left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), Myocardial Infarction (MI) size, microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) were computed from conventional CINE, LGE, T2*-w images (TE = 11.10 ms), respectively. Delayed-phase dynamic enhancement models was developed to enhance lesion contrast and identify persistent MVO. The agreement was evaluated between the conventional and the proposed methods. Results: The proposed framework successfully generated whole-heart cine, delayed enhancement, and T2*-weighted images from a single 8-minute acquisition. LVEF demonstrated strong agreement with conventional cine imaging (Fig 1 y = 0.95x + 2.51, R 2 = 0.91, P = 0.015). Proposed 8-min delayed enhancement images showed strong agreement with conventional methods in MI volume (Fig. 1, y = 1.11x - 2.83, R 2 = 1.00, P = 0.006), while 8-min MVO volume showed intermediate agreement (Fig. 2, y = 0.77x + 0.00, R 2 = 1.00, P = 0.008). Synthetic LGE images accurately delineation of MVO volume, showing strong agreement with conventional LGE (Fig. 2, y = 0.96x + 0.04, R 2 = 1.00, P = 0.008). IMH binary agreement analysis from reconstructed T2*-weighted images demonstrated 100% concordance with conventional T2* imaging. Conclusions: An 8-minute free-running whole-heart CMR framework enables CCS staging of myocardial injury, providing simultaneous assessment of cardiac function, MI, MVO, and IMH with strong agreement to conventional CMR.
title: Abstract 18183: Rapid Whole-Heart Staging of Myocardial Injury Using an 8-Minute Free-Running Cardiac MRI Acquisition

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) reduces mortality and recurrence, yet centre-based programme uptake remains below 30% globally. Telemedicine/digital CR platforms may overcome access barriers, but their long-term efficacy versus standard care has not been systematically quantified. This meta-analysis evaluates the effect of telemedicine/digital CR on clinical outcomes at ≥12 months post-AMI. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and CINAHL (2000-2025) identified randomised controlled trials and prospective cohort studies enrolling adults (≥18 years) with confirmed AMI (STEMI/NSTEMI) within 12 weeks post-event, comparing telemedicine/digital CR (≥12 weeks) against centre-based or standard care, with ≥12-month follow-up. Pooled estimates were calculated using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed via I 2 and Cochran's Q. GRADE was applied to all outcomes. Results: Twelve studies (N=3,123; follow-up 12-60 months) were included. Telemedicine CR significantly reduced all-cause readmission (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.48-0.77; I 2 =34%) and MACE (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54-0.86; I 2 =41%). GDMT adherence at ≥12 months was more than doubled (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.62-2.82; I 2 =29%). Exercise capacity improved substantially, with VO 2 peak SMD +0.71 (95% CI 0.44-0.98; I 2 =52%) and 6-minute walk distance increasing by 38 m (95% CI +24 to +52 m), both exceeding established minimal clinically important differences. SF-36 Physical Component Score improved by 4.8 points (95% CI 2.9-6.7) and the Seattle Angina Questionnaire by 6.1 points. CR programme completion was nearly three times higher versus control (OR 2.89, 95% CI 2.01-4.15). No significant subgroup interactions were identified across MI type, digital platform, age group, or T2DM comorbidity. Meta-regression identified programme duration as a significant moderator of VO 2 improvement (β=+0.018 SMD/week; p=0.04). GRADE certainty was moderate for readmission, MACE, and GDMT adherence, and low for quality of life and CV mortality. Conclusion: Telemedicine/digital CR produces consistent, clinically meaningful improvements in readmission, MACE, GDMT adherence, and exercise capacity after AMI, with moderate certainty of evidence. Integration into post-MI care pathways is warranted, particularly where centre-based access is limited.
title: Abstract 18191: Effect of Telemedicine/Digital Cardiac Rehabilitation on Long-Term Outcomes After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Early identification of recurrent thrombotic events remains challenging in ACS pts`. Hypoxanthine (Hx), a purine metabolite released during tissue hypoxia, may rise earlier than high-sensitivity troponin-I (cTnI). We evaluated Hx and cTnI trajectories, associations with hypercoagulability and inflammation, and ischemia recovery after intervention in a racially diverse ACS cohort. Methods: In this M-BRACE substudy, serial Hx and cTnI were analyzed in MI patients with cTnI >500 ng/L indicating myocardial necrosis. Hx was measured by HPLC-UV with ischemia threshold >5.3 μM. Hypercoagulability was defined as platelet fibrin clot strength (PFCS) ≥67 mm measured using thromboelastography (TEG). Platelet reactivity was assessed by light transmittance aggregometry with agonists arachidonic acid, collagen, and ADP. Results: The analysis included 29 MI patients (13 STEMI, 16 NSTEMI; mean age 65 ± 12 years; 60% male, 52% Blacks). Hx was elevated above the ischemic threshold in all pts vs. 59% for cTnI at baseline (Figure). Hypercoagulable patients (64%) had significantly higher baseline and peak Hx levels and exhibited slower overall clearance with higher residual Hx at 24 hours (7.24 μM vs 3.54 μM). STEMI pts had a greater Hx decline from peak (2-6h) to the 16-24h window compared to NSTEMI pts (-6.1 vs -0.3 μM, p=0.002). By 24 hours, both groups achieved substantial reduction (~84% from peak) whereas cTnI remained elevated in all pts. Ticagrelor/prasugrel therapy was associated with lower platelet reactivity (p≤0.05 by all agonists) and lower mean 24-hour Hx levels (4.94 μM) compared to clopidogrel or no P2Y12 therapy (8.91 μM, p=0.031). Hypercoagulability was strongly correlated with hsCRP (ρ=0.494, p=0.002) and 61% had elevated functional fibrinogen by TEG, indicating fibrinogen as a major driver of hypercoagulability. Conclusions: Hypoxanthine demonstrates clear superiority to troponin-I for early detection of myocardial ischemia and favorable dynamic response to reperfusion. Hypercoagulability, often driven by elevated fibrinogen, is linked to greater ischemic burden and slower Hx clearance, while potent antiplatelet agents accelerate resolution of tissue hypoxia. These findings support Hx as a promising biomarker for real-time reperfusion assessment and personalized antithrombotic strategies in diverse ACS populations. Larger validation studies are warranted.
title: Abstract 18203: Hypoxanthine as an Early and Dynamic Biomarker of Myocardial Ischemia in Acute Coronary Syndrome: M-BRACE Prospective Observational Study

abstract: Introduction: Bioprosthetic valve thrombosis (BPVT) recurs in ~23% of patients despite anticoagulation. DOACs have limited efficacy in prosthetic valve settings, and warfarin sensitivity poses a unique challenge when VKA therapy is the guideline-recommended treatment. We present recurrent prosthetic valve thrombosis across four valve surgeries and three anticoagulation strategies, highlighting low-dose warfarin with aspirin in a warfarin-sensitive patient and a novel hybrid transapical-transfemoral thrombectomy approach. Clinical Presentation: A 60-year-old male with mitral valve prolapse underwent two mitral valve repairs followed by mechanical MVR. Warfarin caused extreme INR lability (INR >17) with depressed vitamin K-dependent factors (II, VII, IX, X) and normal factor V, consistent with warfarin sensitivity. After transition to enoxaparin, he developed mechanical prosthetic valve thrombosis causing cardioembolic left M1 occlusion requiring thrombectomy. A fourth surgery replaced the mechanical valve with bioprosthetic MVR and AVR. He was maintained on apixaban for concurrent DVT with an IVC filter. Thrombophilia workup was negative. On 4/23/2026, he presented with aphasia, right facial droop, and right-sided weakness. Diagnosis and Intervention: CTA showed left M1 occlusion; thrombectomy achieved TICI 2B reperfusion. TEE (4/28/2026) revealed two large mobile masses on the bioprosthetic aortic valve (14х11mm and 15х6mm) with elevated transvalvular velocity (3.5 m/s), confirmed on cardiac CT. Blood cultures were negative, excluding endocarditis. Given prohibitive redo sternotomy risk, a hybrid approach was adopted: left anterior thoracotomy with transapical access for large-bore aspiration thrombectomy under TEE guidance, with Sentinel cerebral embolic protection via the right radial artery. The thrombus embolized during catheter advancement, occluding the left common iliac artery, requiring conversion to transfemoral aspiration thrombectomy with successful retrieval. Outcomes: Pathology confirmed fibromyxoid tissue and fibrin without infection. Given warfarin sensitivity, the patient was bridged with IV heparin to low-dose warfarin (1.25mg daily, target INR 2.0-3.0) plus aspirin 81mg, balancing VKA-based anticoagulation against high bleeding risk (HAS-BLED 3). Conclusion: This case highlights three novel aspects of recurrent BPVT management. First, DOAC failure reinforces that VKA therapy remains preferred for BPVT. Second, low-dose warfarin with aspirin represents a viable individualized strategy when DOACs and enoxaparin have both failed in a warfarin-sensitive patient. Third, hybrid transapical-transfemoral aspiration thrombectomy with cerebral embolic protection offers a less invasive alternative for patients with prohibitive surgical risk, though procedural embolization remains a significant complication.
title: Abstract 18224: Repair, Replace, Re-Thrombose: Recurrent Valve Thrombosis Across Sequential Valve Interventions Despite Anticoagulation Therapy

abstract: Introduction: Acute decompensation of chronic degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) by ischemic papillary muscle dysfunction — without frank rupture — is an underrecognized mechanism of cardiogenic shock. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has emerging evidence in acute MR but is underexplored in mixed ischemic-on-degenerative pathology in patients with prohibitive surgical risk. Patient Information: A 74-year-old woman with advanced Friedreich ataxia, muscular dystrophy, chronic severe MR from mitral valve prolapse, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). Reduced-dose apixaban had been discontinued for hematuria during urinary tract infection with urolithiasis, then withheld for fall risk. Clinical Findings & Timeline: The patient presented with acute dyspnea and hypotension requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressors. Electrocardiography showed inferolateral ST-segment elevation. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Coronary angiography revealed distal embolic occlusion of a terminal right coronary posterolateral branch without proximal culprit, consistent with cardioembolic mechanism. Hemodynamics demonstrated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure 19 mmHg and cardiac index 1.2 L/min/m 2 . Transesophageal echocardiography showed flail P1 and P2 leaflets, effective regurgitant orifice area 0.49 cm 2 , and systolic pulmonary venous flow reversal — interpreted as ischemic posteromedial papillary muscle dysfunction superimposed on degenerative prolapse. EuroSCORE II predicted mortality was 40.69%. Therapeutic Intervention(s): An intra-aortic balloon pump was placed. Emergent TEER was performed with staged deployment of two PASCAL ACE devices (A2/P2 then A1/P1), reducing MR to trace-mild with mean transmitral gradient 2-3 mmHg. The balloon pump was discontinued intraprocedurally. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient was extubated on hospital day 4 and discharged on day 7. At 30 days, left ventricular ejection fraction recovered to 54%, with mild residual MR (mean gradient 4-5 mmHg) and return to pre-hospitalization functional status; no device instability or adverse events occurred. Discussion & Synthesis: This case illustrates a less-recognized mechanism of acute decompensated MR — ischemic posteromedial papillary muscle dysfunction triggered by distal cardioembolic coronary occlusion in AF off anticoagulation, superimposed on a chronic degenerative substrate. Staged TEER achieved rapid hemodynamic stabilization with preserved low gradients in extensive flail anatomy. Decisions to withhold anticoagulation for perceived bleeding or fall risk warrant careful balance against thromboembolic risk. Patient Perspective: At 30-day follow-up, the patient expressed gratitude for her recovery and return to independent baseline function, despite living with progressive neuromuscular disease.
title: Abstract 18250: Rescue Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Cardioembolic Acute-on-Chronic Mitral Regurgitation in a Patient with Friedreich Ataxia

abstract: Background: Physiology-guided deferral using fractional flow reserve (FFR) and related indices is well validated for identifying coronary lesions without flow-limiting ischemia. However, physiology does not assess plaque composition, lipid-core burden, fibrous cap morphology, or vessel wall remodeling. Whether imaging-defined high-risk plaque (HRP) features identify residual biologic risk in physiology-negative lesions has not been systematically evaluated. Methods: We performed a systematic review and study-level meta-analysis of published studies evaluating HRP features and clinical outcomes in physiology-negative coronary lesions. Physiology-negative lesions were defined as FFR >0.80, quantitative flow ratio (QFR) >0.80, or coronary computed tomography angiography-derived FFR (FFRCT) ≥0.80. Eligible studies used OCT, IVUS, or coronary CTA to characterize plaque risk and reported hazard ratios comparing HRP-positive versus HRP-negative physiology-negative lesions, vessels, or patients. Overlapping cohorts were identified, and only the most comprehensive independent dataset from each registry was included. Hazard ratios were pooled using a random-effects model on the log-HR scale. Sensitivity analyses restricted the dataset to invasive FFR-only and invasive imaging-only studies. Results: Six independent studies met inclusion criteria, including OCT (n=1), grayscale IVUS (n=2), and coronary CTA (n=3), across post-MI, diabetic, and mixed coronary artery disease populations. Despite heterogeneity in HRP definitions and composite endpoints, imaging-defined HRP features were associated with higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes among physiology-negative lesions (pooled HR 3.20, 95% CI 2.06-4.96; I 2 =31.57%; p<0.001). Results remained significant when restricted to invasive FFR-only studies (HR 2.89, 95% CI 1.82-4.61; I 2 =34.96%; p<0.001) and invasive imaging-only studies (HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.66-3.25; I 2 =0.00%; p<0.001). Leave-one-out analyses remained significant, with pooled HRs ranging from 2.69 to 4.03. Conclusions: Across OCT, IVUS, and CTA studies, imaging-defined HRP features in physiology-negative coronary lesions were associated with a more than threefold higher risk of adverse cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that physiology-guided deferral, while effective for identifying lesions without flow-limiting ischemia, may not exclude residual biologic risk conferred by vulnerable plaque morphology, including thin-cap fibroatheroma, elevated lipid-core burden, and high plaque burden. Physiology and plaque imaging may therefore capture complementary dimensions of coronary risk, and future studies should evaluate whether integrating both strategies improves outcomes, particularly in high-risk populations such as post-MI and diabetic patients.
title: Abstract 18254: Imaging-Defined High-Risk Plaque Features Are Associated with Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes in Physiology-Negative Coronary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are increasingly deployed in healthcare to automate telephonic encounters. While Large Language Models (LLMs) enable scalable outreach, patient sentiment and communication patterns during AI-augmented pre-procedural clinical calls remain unexplored. Purpose: To quantify patient sentiment, characterize communication categories, and identify independent predictors of communication outcomes during AI-augmented pre-procedural cardiac catheterization calls. Methods: We analyzed 2,034 calls with assessable patient speech between February and December 2025. Sentiment was classified as positive, neutral, or negative using a hierarchical rules-based Natural Language Processing framework, in a fixed priority order: negative (profanity or hostility, refusal requests) was assessed first; positive (warm closings or approval) second; neutral (transactional exchanges) third. Two hundred calls were manually validated by two independent analysts. Ten communication categories were predefined: confirmations, voicemail, logistics, medication, callback, transportation, hospitalization, cancellation, insurance, and other. Six outcomes were evaluated via multivariable logistic regression with 12 predictors: age, ejection fraction, number of treated vessels, prior PCI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention), prior MI (Myocardial Infarction), prior CABG (Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting), multi-vessel CAD (Coronary Artery Disease), sex, race, diabetes, hypertension. Results: Sentiment was neutral in 1,243 calls (61.1%), positive in 719 (35.3%), and negative in 72 (3.5%), suggesting cooperative engagement. Older patients (OR 1.21), those with prior MI (OR 1.41), and Asian (OR 2.03) and Other race patients (OR 1.54) were more likely to express positive sentiment.
