Negative sentiment was more common in older patients (OR 1.52) and those with severe coronary disease (OR 2.16); men and patients with better cardiac function were less likely to express negative sentiment (OR 0.46; OR 0.77). Older and prior MI patients were less likely to respond neutrally (OR 0.79; OR 0.72); more treated vessels predicted neutral responses (OR 1.13); Asian and Other race patients were less likely to be neutral (OR 0.53; OR 0.60), reinforcing their positive sentiment. Diabetes was significantly associated with hospitalization queries, callback, and long call duration models, notably doubling the likelihood of callback requests (OR 1.95). Conclusion: Patient sentiment and communication patterns during AI-augmented calls are shaped by distinct demographic and clinical factors. These findings suggest that AI-driven sentiment and communication analytics can help optimize targeted pre-procedural outreach, warranting prospective evaluation of their impact on patient experience and procedural safety.
title: Abstract 18259: Characterizing Patient Sentiment and Communication Patterns During AI-Augmented Cardiac Catheterization Pre-Procedural Calls: A Real-World Observational Study

abstract: Background: Metabolic syndrome (MetS, defined per NCEP ATP III criteria) is independently associated with accelerated bioprosthetic structural valve degeneration (SVD). The goal of our study was to investigate in a large retrospective surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) population whether the composite MetS or a specific component drives bioprosthetic SVD and/or reintervention rates. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 8,853 patients undergoing primary bioprosthetic SAVR at two centers (2004-2024), with follow-up to 20 years. MetS was defined as ≥3 of 4 components: obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m 2 ), hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia. Outcomes were severe bioprosthetic SVD on echocardiography (multivariable logistic regression) and aortic valve reintervention, defined as valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (ViV-TAVR) or redo SAVR (Fine-Gray models with death as a competing risk), adjusted for age, sex, and clinical covariates. Results: MetS was present in 2,950 patients (33%) in our population, and the two groups were similar in age and sex. MetS was only borderline associated with SVD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.76, P=0.057) and not associated with higher rates of reintervention (subdistribution hazard ratio [subHR] 1.08, 0.88-1.33, P=0.4). In contrast, higher BMI independently predicted both outcomes: SVD aOR 1.22 per 5 kg/m 2 (1.10-1.40, P=0.001) and reintervention subHR 1.10 per 5 kg/m 2 (1.05-1.16, P<0.001), consistent across age strata for SVD. On sensitivity analysis, BMI was the only MetS component associated with reintervention; hypertension (subHR 1.12, 0.90-1.40, P=0.3) and dyslipidemia (0.98, 0.79-1.22, P=0.9) were null, and diabetes was inversely associated (0.72, 0.55-0.95, P=0.019), consistent with higher competing mortality. Reintervention rose stepwise across BMI categories (11.1% to 17.0% for ≥40 kg/m 2 ; log-rank P=0.021), with severe obesity conferring the highest risk (subHR 1.64, 1.09-2.47); this gradient was concentrated in patients ≥65 years (P=0.0007) and absent in those <65 (P=0.9). Conclusions: After bioprosthetic SAVR, obesity -not MetS as a composite- appears to be the driver of risk for SVD and reintervention. BMI showed a consistent, dose-dependent association with both outcomes, while the syndrome's other components were null or confounded by competing mortality. We conclude that routinely captured BMI may be a more informative and actionable biomarker than MetS for long-term durability risk stratification in SAVR.
title: Abstract 18265: Impact of Metabolic Syndrome on Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve Durability: A 20-Year Bi-Center Analysis

abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) age has emerged as a digital biomarker of biologic aging. While AI-ECG age gap has been associated with mortality in various cardiovascular populations, its role in surgical risk stratification among patients with mitral valve (MV) disease remains poorly defined. Hypothesis: We sought to evaluate the association between preoperative AI-ECG age gap and both long-term mortality and postoperative outcomes among patients undergoing MV surgery. We hypothesized that increasing AI-ECG age gap would identify patients at higher risk for adverse postoperative events and long-term mortality. Methods: We identified 13640 patients who underwent MV surgery at our institution between 1993 and 2025. After excluding patients with prior cardiac surgery, age <18 years, active endocarditis, urgent/emergent procedures, and concomitant CABG, SAVR, aortic surgery, or myectomy, 6097 patients comprised the final cohort. Of these, 5435 had a valid preoperative AI-ECG age estimate from an ECG obtained within 30 days before surgery. AI-ECG age gap was defined as AI-ECG age minus chronological age. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to evaluate the association between AI-ECG age gap and all-cause mortality. Multivariable spline models were additionally used to evaluate associations with postoperative atrial fibrillation, blood transfusion, operative mortality, and hospital length of stay. Models were adjusted for chronological age, sex, body mass index, MV replacement, concomitant tricuspid valve repair, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension, and ejection fraction. Results: Among 5,435 patients (mean chronological age 61.8 years, mean AI-ECG age 62.1 years), 1,444 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 8.5 years. Overall, 54% of patients demonstrated a positive AI-ECG age gap. Adjusted spline analyses demonstrated a graded increase in mortality risk with increasing AI-ECG age gap and each 5-year increase in AI-ECG age gap was independently associated with a 12% higher risk of long-term mortality (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.07-1.16; P<0.001). Higher AI-ECG age gap was also associated with postoperative atrial fibrillation (adjusted OR per 5-year increase 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.12; P<0.001), blood transfusion (adjusted OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10; P=0.026), longer hospital length of stay (P=0.007) and operative mortality (adjusted OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.02-2.14; P=0.040). Conclusions: Preoperative AI-ECG age gap is independently associated with long-term mortality following MV surgery and demonstrates a graded relationship with adverse postoperative outcomes. These findings support AI-ECG age gap as a marker of biologic aging and may enhance preoperative risk stratification beyond chronological age alone.
title: Abstract 18275: Artificial Intelligence-ECG Age Gap Predicts Postoperative Outcomes and Long-Term Mortality Following Mitral Valve Intervention

abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have emerged as an important therapy for heart failure and have favorable effects on myocardial remodeling, fibrosis, and inflammation. The overlap between aortic stenosis (AS) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction provides a rationale for evaluating SGLT2i in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR). However, data evaluating outcomes associated with SGLT2i therapy after AVR are limited. Methods: Population-based cohort study of patients with severe AS undergoing AVR in Western Denmark between January 1, 2016 and April 11, 2022. Patients treated with SGLT2i before or within 6 months after AVR were compared with untreated controls. Propensity score matching was performed using age, sex, AVR approach (SAVR vs TAVI), Charlson comorbidity index, left ventricular ejection fraction, body surface area, EuroSCORE II, smoking status, creatinine clearance, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, and non-elective surgery. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reintervention. Results: Among 5,259 patients undergoing AVR, 225 received SGLT2i therapy. Propensity score matching yielded 146 well-balanced pairs. During follow-up, the primary endpoint occurred in 52 (35.6%) SGLT2i-treated patients and 73 (50.0%) controls (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.45-0.92; p=0.015). SGLT2i therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality (28.1% vs 40.4%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.94; p=0.022). In multivariable analysis, SGLT2i therapy remained independently associated with lower risk of the primary composite outcome (adjusted HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.38-0.80; p=0.002) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.98; p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reintervention, stroke, myocardial infarction, chronic kidney disease, or incident atrial fibrillation. Conclusions: In this propensity score-matched cohort of patients undergoing AVR, SGLT2i therapy was independently associated with lower risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality.
title: Abstract 18296: Association of SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy with Long-Term Outcomes Following Aortic Valve Replacement: A Danish Registry Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Red man syndrome (RMS) is a known reaction that can occur with vancomycin infusions and has also been associated with other medications that stimulate histamine release. While sildenafil has not been reported to be associated with RMS, it is commonly used as a vasodilator for pulmonary hypertension and may induce vasodilation in a way that resembles the anaphylactoid reaction seen in classic vancomycin-induced RMS. Case Presentation: A 38-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 10%, secondary pulmonary hypertension, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and prior methamphetamine use presented to our emergency department with progressive fatigue and worsening dyspnea on exertion. He was on four pillar GDMT as an outpatient. Prior echocardiography estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure exceeding 50 mmHg. During this hospitalization a right heart catheterization was performed while on milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min for progressive shock that demonstrated a BP of 88/64 mmHg, RA pressure of 6 mmHg, PA of 46/30 mmHg with a mean of 35 mmHg, and wedge pressure of 23 mmHg, TPG of 12 mmHg, Thermodilution cardiac output of 2.99 L/min, and cardiac index of 1.42 L/min/m 2 . The patient was initiated on intravenous diuretics and maintained on milrinone at 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Despite this, he required Impella 5.5 placement for refractory shock. The following day, sildenafil 10 mg three times daily was initiated for optimization of pulmonary hypertension. Shortly following initiation of sildenafil, the patient developed symptoms concerning for RMS, with erythema and pruritus without hypotension. His symptoms progressed to blanchable erythema involving his chest and bilateral upper and lower extremities Sildenafil was discontinued, resulting in complete resolution of all symptoms without hemodynamic instability. He underwent successful orthotopic heart transplantation on hospital day 10. Discussion RMS is a well-recognized anaphylactic reaction, not exclusive to vancomycin. To our knowledge, this case represents a rare and clinically significant report of an RMS-like reaction attributable to sildenafil in the setting of heart failure cardiogenic shock with WHO group 2 pulmonary hypertension.
title: Abstract 18306: An Unexpected Reaction: Red Man Syndrome Following Sildenafil A Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to long-term anticoagulation for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation who are unable to tolerate oral anticoagulation. Coronary artery fistulas (CAFs) are rare anomalies, and communication between a coronary artery and the left atrial appendage (LAA) is exceptionally uncommon. Persistent LAA perfusion through a CAF after WATCHMAN implantation raises important questions regarding stroke prophylaxis, contrast flow into the left atrial appendage despite occlusion, and long-term anticoagulation management. Case Presentation: A 77-year-old man with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 40-45%) and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation underwent WATCHMAN implantation in 2021 after a life-threatening gastrointestinal bleed rendered long-term anticoagulation contraindicated. He subsequently developed progressive heart failure symptoms despite guideline-directed medical therapy. Stress testing demonstrated inferior ischemia, prompting coronary angiography. Angiography revealed an abnormal vascular structure arising from the left circumflex coronary artery. Coronary computed tomography angiography further characterized the finding as a fistulous connection between the left circumflex artery and the LAA. Despite the presence of the WATCHMAN device, contrast opacification of the LAA was observed, demonstrating persistent appendage perfusion through the fistula. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and underwent multidisciplinary evaluation to assess ischemic burden, residual thromboembolic risk, and potential management strategies. Discussion: Coronary artery-to-LAA fistulas are exceedingly rare and have only rarely been described in association with LAA occlusion devices. This anatomy introduces a potential pathway for continued LAA perfusion despite successful device implantation, raising questions regarding residual thromboembolic risk and the completeness of mechanical stroke prevention. Multimodality imaging with coronary angiography and coronary CTA was essential for diagnosis and anatomical characterization. Management remains individualized and may include surveillance, antithrombotic therapy, or consideration of transcatheter fistula closure depending on symptoms, ischemia, and stroke risk. Conclusion: This case highlights an uncommon coronary-to-LAA fistula discovered after WATCHMAN implantation and demonstrates a previously underrecognized mechanism of persistent appendage perfusion. Recognition of this entity is important because it may influence post-LAAO surveillance, stroke prevention strategies, and decisions regarding fistula closure. Further study is needed to define the clinical significance of persistent LAA filling from coronary sources.
title: Abstract 18330: Coronary Artery to Left Atrial Appendage Fistula Identified After Watchman Device Implantation: Diagnostic and Management Considerations

abstract: Introduction: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent, genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor increasingly recognized in secondary prevention guidelines, yet testing remains inconsistent in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Whether outcome differences between tested and untested patients reflect residual biologic risk, care-process intensity, or both remains uncharacterized at scale. Hypothesis: Among patients with established ASCVD, those who undergo Lp(a) measurement will have different downstream clinical and utilization outcomes than comparable untested patients, even after matching on comorbidity and care-intensity variables, reflecting both residual biologic risk and differential care-process effects. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (174 healthcare organizations), adults with established ASCVD who had Lp(a) measured after diagnosis (Cohort 1, n=99,208) were compared to untested patients (Cohort 2, n=8,716,557). After 1:1 propensity score matching on age, sex, race, diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, cerebral infarction, obesity, and chronic ischemic heart disease, cohorts of 94,613 per group were analyzed for MACE (myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or cardiac arrest), MI, ischemic stroke, coronary revascularization, and all-cause hospitalization at 1-, 3-, and 5-year follow-up. Results: After matching, the cohorts were well balanced (median age 65 years in both; chronic ischemic heart disease 77.5% in each). Across all time windows, Lp(a)-tested patients had significantly lower event rates than untested patients for every outcome (all p<0.001). At 1 year: MACE risk ratio (RR) 0.581 (95% CI 0.551-0.614), MI RR 0.580 (0.543-0.620), ischemic stroke RR 0.701 (0.650-0.756), revascularization RR 0.744 (0.718-0.771), hospitalization RR 0.584 (0.559-0.610). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed lower event-free survival probability in untested patients at all time windows; hazard ratios for MACE were 0.672 (1-year), 0.718 (3-year), and 0.709 (5-year), all p<0.001. The protective association was consistent and durable, with absolute risk differences widening substantially at 5 years: MACE RD -0.070, hospitalization RD -0.118. Conclusions: In propensity-matched adults with established ASCVD, Lp(a) testing is associated with substantially lower rates of MACE, MI, stroke, revascularization, and hospitalization across 1-, 3-, and 5-year follow-up. These findings likely reflect that Lp(a) testing occurs in the context of more intensive cardiovascular risk management rather than a direct protective effect of the test itself. They highlight Lp(a) measurement as a marker of proactive care and support broader guideline-driven adoption of Lp(a) testing in secondary prevention.

register_verdicts.note: Lp(a) testing study with no incretin exposure.

title: Abstract 18332: Lipoprotein (a) Testing as a Marker of Care Intensity and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Established Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Propensity-Matched Real-World Cohort Study

abstract: Introduction: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality.Although statins remain the foundation of lipid-lowering therapy, some patients need add-on agents such as ezetimibe or PCSK9 inhibitors to reach guideline LDL-C targets. However, real-world data comparing the long-term effectiveness of these two strategies are limited. Research Question: What are the long-term real-world outcomes of PCSK9 inhibitor-based versus ezetimibe-based regimens in patients with ASCVD on statin therapy? Methods Using the TriNetX Research Network, we identified patients with ASCVD on statin therapy prescribed ezetimibe (N=176,169) or a PCSK9 inhibitor (N=16,150). Propensity score matching generated two well-balanced cohorts (N=16,145 per group). Primary and secondary outcomes; all-cause mortality, all-cause readmission, myocardial infarction (MI), revascularization, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), ischemic stroke, and heart failure (HF) exacerbation-were analyzed over 3-year and 5-year follow-ups. Results: Baseline mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol was higher in the PCSK9 inhibitor group than the ezetimibe group (114.2±54.5 mg/dL vs 98.9±41.1 mg/dL). The PCSK9 inhibitor regimen demonstrated a significant reduction in all-cause mortality at 3 years (OR: 0.78, p<0.001; HR: 0.785, p<0.001) and 5 years (OR: 0.777, p<0.001; HR: 0.79, p<0.001). Diminished risks of all-cause readmission were observed with PCSK9 inhibitors at 3 years (OR: 0.901, p=0.03) and 5 years (OR: 0.889, p=0.012). Conversely, the PCSK9 inhibitor cohort experienced a higher risk of MI at 5 years (OR: 1.109, p=0.002; HR: 1.101, p=0.03) and revascularization at 3 years (OR: 1.22, p=0.01; HR: 1.202, p=0.002) and 5 years (OR: 1.194, p=0.002; HR: 1.182, p=0.002). No significant differences were noted for composite MACE, ischemic stroke, or HF exacerbation. Conclusion: PCSK9 inhibitor-based regimens are associated with a significant long-term survival advantage and lower readmission rates compared to ezetimibe-based regimens in high-risk ASCVD patients. Higher risks of MI and revascularization in the PCSK9 inhibitor group likely reflect residual confounding given their higher baseline lipid levels and clinical severity. These findings support expanding intensive PCSK9 inhibitor utilization for secondary prevention.
title: Abstract 18344: Beyond Statins: Real-World Long-Term Effectiveness of PCSK9 Inhibitors versus Ezetimibe in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease

abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, largely driven by maladaptive cardiac remodeling characterized by fibrosis and hypertrophy following myocardial injury. Although transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tDRs) have recently emerged as important regulators of cellular stress adaptation, their roles in cardiac remodeling are largely unknown. We recently established a stress-specific tDR atlas in cardiac cells and reported hundreds of ischemia-regulated tDRs, while their functions remain to be explored. Here, we identified Asp-GTC-3′tDR, a tRNA-derived small RNA generated from the 3′ end of tRNA-Asp-GTC, as a key ischemia-responsive regulator of cardiac homeostasis. Asp-GTC-3′tDR generation was markedly enhanced following acute ischemia in cultured cardiac fibroblasts (CFs), cardiomyocytes, and mouse hearts, but was suppressed in activated myofibroblasts, hypertrophic cardiomyocytes, and failing hearts. Exogenous Asp-GTC-3′tDR delivery inhibited CF activation and suppressed pathological cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in cell culture models. Cardiac delivery of Asp-GTC-3’tDR significantly attenuated adverse cardiac remodeling and preserved cardiac function in both myocardial infarction (MI) and pressure-overload models. Conversely, silencing endogenous Asp-GTC-3′tDR in healthy hearts promotes both fibrotic and hypertrophic remodeling. Importantly, administration of three doses of Asp-GTC-3′tDR within the first week after ischemia/reperfusion provided long-term cardiac protection. Mechanistically, we discovered that Asp-GTC-3′tDR exerts cardioprotection through distinct cell-type-specific RNA regulatory pathways. In CFs, Asp-GTC-3′tDR directly promoted stress granule assembly, resulting in the condensation and degradation of translating profibrotic transcripts. In cardiomyocytes, Asp-GTC-3′tDR attenuated hypertrophic remodeling through sequestering pseudouridine synthase 7 (PUS7), altering histone mRNA pseudouridylation, and activating RNA autophagy. Together, these findings identify Asp-GTC-3′tDR as a previously unrecognized ischemia-induced cardioprotective tDR that coordinates anti-fibrotic and anti-hypertrophic responses through distinct molecular mechanisms in different cardiac cell types. Furthermore, Asp-GTC-3′tDR was significantly induced in human heart tissues upon ischemia, underscoring its clinical relevance. These findings establish Asp-GTC-3′tDR as a promising novel therapeutic target for treating maladaptive cardiac remodeling and HF progression across diverse etiologies.
title: Abstract 18350: A Stress-Responsive tRNA-Derived Small RNA Orchestrates Cell-Specific Cardioprotection Through Distinct RNA Regulatory Pathways

abstract: Background: Heart Team decision making represents a cornerstone of contemporary valvular heart disease (VHD) management. Current guidelines increasingly emphasize age-based treatment allocation, particularly in aortic valve (AV) disease, while recommendations for coronary revascularization in transcatheter patients have become more restrictive. Aim: To evaluate whether guideline-based age categories reflect real-world clinical outcomes and assess the impact of coronary artery disease (CAD) and revascularization strategies. Methods: Consecutive patients discussed by the institutional Heart Team between August 2021 and April 2025 were analyzed (1,940 patients). Patients were stratified by valve, treatment strategy, age, and STS-PROM risk. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, disabling stroke, or new dialysis at 30 days and 1 year; secondary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier estimates, log-rank tests, Fisher’s exact test, and Cox models adjusted for age, STS-PROM, and treatment were used. Results: Among patients undergoing mitral valve (MV) intervention, high STS risk (transcatheter treatment only) was associated with increased mortality vs intermediate risk (26% vs 6%; HR 4.33, 95% CI 1.30-14.39; p=0.017) and higher composite event rates (27% vs 11%; HR 2.77, 95% CI 1.03-7.43; p=0.044). Outcomes increased stepwise with STS risk in TAVI patients. Mortality increased from 3% to 11% and 19%, while composite events increased from 4% to 14% and 24% across low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups; all age-adjusted comparisons were significant (HR 3.50; 95% CI 2.17-5.65; p <0.001). In surgical AV patients, intermediate/high STS risk was associated with higher unadjusted mortality than low risk (14% vs 2%), but not after adjustment. Outcomes in AV patients were not associated with age. CAD was not independently associated with outcomes after adjustment. Revascularization was more frequent with surgery (AV: 39.7% vs 3.3%, p<0.001; MV: 17.3% vs 0%, p=0.004). Among CAD patients, revascularization was associated with lower unadjusted mortality (0% vs 8%; p=0.010) and lower composite event rates (2% vs 10%; p=0.016). In AV patients with CAD, surgery was associated with lower unadjusted mortality than transcatheter treatment (2% vs 7%; p=0.020). After adjustment, this association was attenuated (HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.02-1.08; p=0.059). Conclusions: Objective risk stratification showed greater prognostic value than age-based treatment allocation. High STS risk identified MV patients with substantially increased adverse event rates. Although CAD was not associated with outcomes, more frequent surgical revascularization may have contributed, alongside baseline risk selection, to favorable outcomes in CAD patients undergoing AV surgery, highlighting the importance of coronary treatment strategies in Heart Team decision making.
title: Abstract 18374: Beyond Age-Based Treatment Categories: Risk Stratification and Coronary Treatment Patterns in Contemporary Heart Team Decision Making

abstract: Background: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS) carries high mortality, yet evidence on mechanical circulatory support (MCS) outcomes in this population remains sparse. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to characterize outcomes of MCS strategies in PPCM-CS. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that MCS strategy selection might be associated with differences in in-hospital mortality and LV recovery in women with PPCM-CS. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were systematically searched for studies reporting MCS use in PPCM-CS. Studies were stratified by support strategy: venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), and mixed-strategy MCS. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included bleeding, stroke, and left ventricular (LV) recovery. Single-arm proportion meta-analysis was performed using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed by I 2 statistics. Statistical analysis was performed using R version 4.5.2. Results: Thirteen studies comprising 829 patients were included. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 16.4% (95% CI 10.5-24.6%; I 2 =24%), with significant subgroup differences by device (p<0.01): VA-ECMO 33.6% (95% CI 18.7-52.6%), durable LVAD 5.5% (95% CI 1.6-17.3%), and mixed-strategy 13.9% (95% CI 11.6-16.5%). Pooled bleeding rate was 27.0% (95% CI 11.8-50.5%; I 2 =68%). VA-ECMO and mixed-strategy cohorts showed similar bleeding rates, and no significant differences were observed between subgroups (p = 0.75). Stroke occurred in 13.6% (95% CI 9.8-18.6%; I 2 =21%). Durable LVAD cohorts demonstrated the highest stroke rates, while mixed-strategy cohorts had the lowest. Unlike bleeding, stroke incidence differed significantly between MCS strategies (p = 0.02). LV recovery was achieved in 31.9% (95% CI 17.7-50.5%; I 2 =81%), highest with VA-ECMO (57.4%; 95% CI 48.2-66.1%) versus durable LVAD (13.5%; 95% CI 5.8-28.1%). Conclusion: MCS in PPCM-CS is associated with an overall in-hospital mortality of 16.4%, with marked variation by support strategies. VA-ECMO cohorts demonstrated higher acute mortality but greater LV recovery rates compared with durable LVAD cohorts. These findings support individualized device selection in this high-risk obstetric population.
title: Abstract 18378: Mechanical Circulatory Support Outcomes in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) creates non-thermal myocardial injury. While chronic lesion dimensions are determined by energy dose, the temporal evolution of focal PFA lesion dimensions remains incompletely characterized. Objective: To quantify longitudinal changes in focal PFA lesion volume using LGE-MRI. Methods: In a swine model, 27 ventricular lesions were created using a focal FARAPOINT™ catheter with a FARASTAR generator. Lesions were assessed with serial 3 Tesla LGE-MRI at four time points: acutely (2-4 hours post-ablation), 2 weeks, 1 month, and 2 months post-ablation. Lesion volumes were segmented using semi-automated CorView software with the GrowCut tool and three segmentation thresholds: Conservative, Moderate, and Aggressive. Moderate segmentation was used as the primary analysis, with Conservative and Aggressive segmentations used as sensitivity analyses. Paired t-tests compared lesion volume between consecutive imaging timepoints. Results: In the Moderate segmentation, mean lesion volume decreased from 0.55±0.41 cm 3 acutely to 0.20±0.15 cm 3 at 2 weeks, representing a 63.6% reduction ( p=0.0017 ). There was no differences from 2 weeks to 1 month, 0.20±0.15 to 0.23±0.16 cm 3 ( p=0.562 ), or from 1 month to 2 months, 0.23±0.16 to 0.22±0.15 cm 3 ( p=0.796 ). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses: Conservative volumes decreased from 0.32±0.28 to 0.10±0.08 cm 3 from acute imaging to 2 weeks ( p=0.0035 ), and Aggressive volumes decreased from 0.71±0.49 to 0.29±0.21 cm 3 ( p=0.0015 ), with no significant subsequent changes from 2 weeks to 1 month or from 1 month to 2 months. Conclusion: Serial LGE-MRI demonstrates substantial early changes in LGE-defined lesion volume within the first two weeks following focal PFA, with relative stability thereafter through 2 months. These findings could reflect changes in contrast kinetics over time, recovery of an edemic response, or represent underlying structural changes such as recovery of the PFA reversible zone.
title: Abstract 18443: Longitudinal Assessment of Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Lesion Volume in a Swine Model Using LGE-MRI

abstract: Background: The optimal timing of intervention in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains controversial. While current guidelines support clinical surveillance until symptom onset or ventricular dysfunction, recent randomized trials have suggested potential benefit from earlier aortic valve replacement (AVR). Objectives: To evaluate the efficacy of early AVR, including surgical AVR (SAVR) and transcatheter AVR (TAVR), compared with conservative surveillance in patients with asymptomatic severe AS. Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing early AVR versus conservative management in asymptomatic severe AS. Four trials were included: RECOVERY long-term follow-up, AVATAR long-term follow-up, EARLY TAVR, and EVOLVED. Random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models were used to pool hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included composite cardiovascular events, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and stroke. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Results: Four randomized trials comprising 1,427 patients were included (719 early AVR/TAVR and 708 surveillance). The weighted mean age was 73.3 years, approximately two-thirds were male, and the weighted mean follow-up duration was 49.8 months. Participants were predominantly low surgical risk with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and severe or very severe AS. Follow-up ranged from 3.8 years in EARLY TAVR to 10 years in RECOVERY. Early AVR/TAVR was associated with a numerically lower risk of all-cause mortality that did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.42–1.13; P=0.137; I 2 =63.4%). However, early intervention significantly reduced composite cardiovascular events (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37–0.72; P<0.001; I 2 =34.9%), cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.26–0.63; P<0.001; I 2 =0%), heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.26–0.59; P<0.001; I 2 =0%), and stroke (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35–0.93; P=0.026; I 2 =0%). Conclusions: Among randomized trials, early AVR in asymptomatic severe AS significantly reduced major cardiovascular events, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and stroke compared with conservative surveillance. Although a statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality was not observed, the overall treatment effect consistently favored earlier intervention. These findings support consideration of an early AVR strategy in carefully selected asymptomatic patients and further reinforce the evolving role of valve intervention before symptom onset.
title: Abstract 18447: Early Aortic Valve Replacement versus Conservative Surveillance in Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: Hypertension exposes the coronary arteries to sustained mechanical wall stress, radial stretch, and perivascular injury. Similar forms of acute coronary mechanical disruption occur during procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention, where balloon inflation and vessel expansion can damage the vascular wall. These mechanical insults can promote perivascular inflammation, fibrosis, and vascular stiffening. The early cellular and molecular programs that link coronary barotrauma to perivascular inflammation remain unexplored. Recently, we discovered mechanically-induced type I interferon response after myocardial infarction. Whether a similar response occurs in the mechanically injured vasculature is unknown. Hypothesis: hypothesize that coronary artery barotrauma induces a spatially restricted type I interferon response that contributes to the formation of pathological coronary perivascular injury niche and may represent a target for therapy. Methods: Adult male C57BL/6J mice underwent transverse aortic constriction (TAC) to model hypertension-induced mechanical injury to the coronaries. At 7 days, perivascular fibrosis of left and right coronary arteries was assessed by Masson’s trichrome staining. Spatial transcriptomics (Xenium, 5050 probes) and duplex RNAscope (Ifit1, Nppa) defined cell-type organization, cardiac stress programs, and expression of interferon-stimulated gene (ISGs). To test pathway determinants, experiments were repeated in IRF3-/- and cGAS -/- mice. To assess therapeutic modulation, TAC mice received anti-IFNAR antibody from day –1 to +4 and analyzed at day 7. Results: TAC induced focal coronary perivascular injury characterized by increased fibrosis around left (n=6, P<0.0001) and right (n=4, P<0.0001) coronary arteries. Spatial transcriptomics identified a distinct post-TAC perivascular niche with altered endothelial, immune, and stromal programs in both ventricles. Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) were spatially clustered adjacent to vessels and absent in distant myocardium (data on control vs TAC ifit1%). IRF3 and cGAS deficiency significantly reduced ISGs after TAC (P<0.0001). Anti-IFNAR treatment completely suppressed perivascular ISG expression, demonstrating the response is pharmacologically modifiable in vivo. Conclusion: Hypertension induces coronary artery barotrauma and a multicellular perivascular inflammatory niche marked by spatially restricted cGAS- and IRF3-dependent type I interferon signaling, suggesting a cytosolic DNA sensing mechanism. This genetically and pharmacologically targetable pathway may offer new opportunities to limit perivascular inflammation and adverse cardiac remodeling.
title: Abstract 18463: Hypertension Induces Coronary Barotrauma and Activates a Targetable Perivascular Type I Interferon Response

abstract: Introduction: Right-sided infective endocarditis from methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is frequently complicated by persistent bacteremia and progressive septic pulmonary embolism. When antibiotic therapy fails to achieve source control, surgical debulking remains standard of care, yet many critically ill patients are not operative candidates. The INARI FlowTriever has emerged as a novel endovascular platform for percutaneous vegetation debulking, though published experience remains limited. Case: A 39-year-old woman with intravenous drug use presented with septic shock, acute hypoxic respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, and multi-organ failure. MRSA bacteremia was confirmed on admission. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated a large tricuspid valve vegetation measuring up to 3.3 x 2.7 cm. CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multifocal cavitary pulmonary lesions consistent with bilateral septic emboli, pleural effusions with right-sided empyema requiring drainage, and soft tissue infection with intramuscular gas of the gluteal and iliopsoas regions. Despite broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, blood cultures remained positive for MRSA for approximately seven days with persistent fevers and ventilator dependence. Despite eventual clearance of bacteremia, ongoing septic embolization precluded recovery and open cardiac surgery was deemed prohibitively high-risk.Intervention: On hospital day 14, percutaneous transcatheter debulking was performed under general anesthesia via right common femoral venous access. A coaxial 24-Fr INARI FlowTriever outer catheter and curved 20-Fr inner catheter were advanced to the right atrium under transesophageal echocardiographic and fluoroscopic guidance. Multiple aspiration passes successfully debulked the giant tricuspid vegetation, with near-complete removal confirmed on imaging. Vegetectomy specimens confirmed MRSA. Results: The patient was extubated to high-flow nasal cannula within 48 hours, with resolution of fevers and marked clinical improvement. Blood cultures remained negative, and she completed a prolonged intravenous antibiotic course. Conclusion: In critically ill patients with large tricuspid vegetations driving septic pulmonary embolism who are not operative candidates, percutaneous debulking with the INARI FlowTriever can achieve endovascular source control and facilitate recovery, supporting catheter-based aspiration in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 18483: Transcatheter Inari FlowTriever-Assisted Debulking of a Giant Tricuspid Valve Vegetation in Surgically Ineligible MRSA Endocarditis Complicated by Disseminated Septic Embolization

abstract: BACKGROUND: Comparative data between left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at moderate-to-high risk for stroke remain limited. We performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the efficacy and safety of both strategies. METHODS: Two RCTs were included: PRAGUE-17 (Osmancik 2020, n=402, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc 4.7±1.5; HAS-BLED 3.0±0.9; median follow-up 19.9 months) and CLOSURE-AF (Landmesser 2026, n=888, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc 5.2±1.5; HAS-BLED 3.0±0.9; median follow-up 36 months). The primary outcome was total stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic). Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding and systemic embolism. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% CI were calculated using the Mantel-Haenszel method with Hartung-Knapp correction. Analyses were performed in R using the meta package. RESULTS: A total of 1,290 patients were included (647 LAAC, 643 DOAC). No significant differences were found for total stroke (RR 1.02; 95% CI 0.65-1.62; I 2 =0%), ischemic stroke (RR 1.17; 95% CI 0.67-2.05; I 2 =0%), hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.71; 95% CI 0.32-1.58; I 2 =0%), or major bleeding (RR 1.10; 95% CI 0.82-1.47; I 2 =0%). Heterogeneity was minimal across all outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: LAAC demonstrated comparable rates of stroke and major bleeding relative to DOAC-based therapy in high-risk AF patients, supporting its role as a viable alternative in carefully selected patients. Results should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials and small event counts for several outcomes.
title: Abstract 18490: Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Atrial Fibrillation at Moderate-to-High Stroke and Bleeding Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) carries in-hospital mortality of 20-40%, with surgery as the standard of care. Many patients are inoperable due to comorbidities, prior sternotomies, or clinical instability. Percutaneous mechanical aspiration (PMA) is established in right-sided endocarditis, but left-sided applications remain anecdotal. We describe transseptal Penumbra vegectomy with Sentinel cerebral embolic protection for active prosthetic mitral valve endocarditis in a surgically inoperable patient with a transcatheter valve-in-valve prosthesis. Case presentation: A 62-year-old woman with neurofibromatosis type 1, gastrointestinal stromal tumor history, and CKD stage 3 presented with three weeks of fevers, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. She was septic with leukocytosis, elevated lactate and procalcitonin. Cardiac history included mechanical mitral valve replacement (2001), redo bioprosthetic replacement for PVE (2010), and valve-in-valve implantation with a 26-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (2025).Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus epidermidis. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated a large, mobile vegetation on the prosthetic mitral valve. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) confirmed the vegetation and excluded paravalvular abscess or prosthetic dehiscence. A fourth sternotomy was deemed prohibitively high risk, and after multidisciplinary discussion percutaneous vegectomy was pursued for source control.Under general anesthesia with TEE guidance, radiofrequency transseptal puncture was performed via the VersaCross system. A Sentinel device was deployed via right radial access for cerebral protection. A 12-French Penumbra catheter was advanced through a Watchman FLX sheath into the left atrium: multiple aspiration passes achieved marked vegetation reduction. All material was sent for microbiological and pathological analysis.There were no complications, embolization, effusion, or hemodynamic instability. The patient was extubated in the catheterization laboratory and transferred to the CVICU in stable condition. Discussion This is among the first reported Penumbra uses for left-sided mitral endocarditis and, to our knowledge, the first in a valve-in-valve prosthesis. As transcatheter valve populations grow, many patients will lack surgical options even when reoperation is indicated. PMA may serve as a bridge or definitive source-control strategy, though it does not address abscesses or structural leaflet destruction. Multidisciplinary selection remains essential. Conclusion: Transseptal Penumbra aspiration with Sentinel cerebral embolic protection is feasible and acutely safe for vegetation debulking in carefully selected, surgically inoperable patients with prosthetic mitral valve endocarditis.
title: Abstract 18496: Transseptal Vegectomy for Prosthetic Mitral Valve Endocarditis in a High-Risk Surgical Candidate

abstract: Background: Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) has two predominant forms, atrial (AFMR; annular dilation) and ventricular (VFMR; leaflet tethering). Whether atrial fibrillation (AF) and left bundle branch block (LBBB) worsen them differentially is untested and first requires a calibrated baseline model. Purpose: To build patient-indexed mitral-valve twins, classify AFMR-/VFMR-predominant phenotypes, calibrate a geometric EROA estimator against PISA, and define what must be validated before AF/LBBB experiments. Methods: Twenty-seven patients with predominantly mild-to-moderate FMR (mild 13, moderate 12, severe 2 by integrated echo grade) underwent 3D transthoracic echocardiography and ECG. Phenotype used operational criteria (LVEF, LAVI, tenting, LVEDV; thresholds below). For each patient a digital twin was constructed from 3D-echo-derived geometry, a parametric saddle-shaped annulus, an anisotropic Holzapfel-Gasser-Ogden bileaflet with per-vertex circumferential fibre direction, chordal apparatus, and papillary muscles, in diastolic and systolic states, with dimensions provenance-flagged as measured or nominal (Figure A). Electromechanical timing was derived from the Kors vectorcardiogram. EROA was estimated by a geometric coaptation model driven by tenting and annular size; performance against PISA was estimated by leave-one-out cross-validation. An exploratory reserve-depletion index was compared with the phenotype label. Results: Twenty-one patients were AFMR-predominant, 5 VFMR-predominant, 1 discordant. On cross-validation the model showed moderate concordance with PISA, an imperfect FMR comparator (Figure B; r=0.65; mean difference –0.01 cm 2 [model–PISA], 95% limits –0.15 to +0.13). It appeared to compress the high-EROA range (high-EROA performance uncertain; n=2 severe MR). The reserve-depletion index explained more cross-validated variance than the phenotype label (Figure C-E; R 2 0.42 vs no better than chance, ≈0; similar for grade); no annulus-tenting interaction was detected (power limited), describing MR severity, not vulnerability to load. Simulated annular dilation (AF) and tethering (LBBB-dyssynchrony) gave graded EROA increases (Figure F). Conclusions: We present a pilot patient-indexed mitral-valve twin framework, a transparent operational classifier for AFMR- versus VFMR-predominant phenotypes, and an internally cross-validated geometric estimator of EROA. This pilot identifies geometric reserve, reflected by tenting and annular diameter, as a cross-sectional severity signal that may be more informative for current MR severity than phenotype of origin. With further validation, this framework could support preprocedural prediction of MR response to atrial rhythm restoration, ventricular resynchronization, or mitral repair strategies targeting annular and coaptation geometry.
title: Abstract 18501: A Mitral-Valve Digital-Twin Framework for Functional Mitral Regurgitation

abstract: Background: Frailty is highly associated with adverse outcomes in cardiogenic shock (CS) patients. Sarcopenia is a key component of frailty and while sarcopenia can be estimated by psoas muscle index (PMI), the ideal lumbar vertebral level to measure PMI has not been firmly established. We conducted a comparative analysis of the association between PMI and mortality in CS patients at the level of L1 vs L4. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 170 patients admitted with CS at a single center. PMI was measured using CT abdomens performed within 72 hours of hospital admission. Axial slices at L1 and L4 were used to measure the cross-sectional area of the right and left psoas muscles. PMI was calculated using the formula: (Right Psoas Area + Left Psoas Area) / [Height in meters 2 ]. Adjusted multivariable Cox proportional hazard ratios were used to assess the association between PMI and mortality. Results: In the multivariable Cox model adjusting for age, sex, SCAI stage, and peak VIS, each 1-SD decrease in L4-PMI raised the hazard of death by 53% (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.01, p=0.002). Age was the only other significant covariate (HR 1.50, p=0.001); sex, SCAI stage, and VIS were not. Sorting patients into L4-PMI tertiles, mortality was 74% in the lowest-muscle third, 41% in the middle third, and 37% in the highest third (log-rank p<0.001). Lower L4-PMI predicted in-hospital death (logistic OR 1.54 per 1-SD decrease, p=0.019) and 1-year mortality (unadjusted OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.20 to 2.37, p=0.003; adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.03 to 2.31, p=0.036). L1-PMI did not predict mortality in the same patients. The unadjusted Cox HR was 1.14 for L1-PMI (95% CI 0.90 to 1.44, p=0.27) and fell further after adjustment (HR 1.09, p=0.48). L1 tertiles did not separate (mortality 55%, 53%, 45%; log-rank p=0.44). Conclusions: This study provides evidence that low PMI at L4 can identify CS patients at higher mortality risk independent of shock severity. However, this signal is anatomically specific to L4 and cannot be captured from L1-PMI on chest CT imaging that these patients often undergo. This positions L4-PMI as a potential tool for risk stratification that could inform treatment decisions in cardiogenic shock.
title: Abstract 18507: L4 Psoas Muscle Index is Associated with Mortality in Cardiogenic Shock: A Comparative Analysis of L1 and L4 Measurements

abstract: Background: Severe hyperkalemia can mimic STEMI on ECG and trigger life-threatening arrhythmias. Early recognition is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions. Case: A 62-year-old woman presented unresponsive with Kussmaul respirations. ECG showed wide-complex tachycardia with apparent ST elevations. Bedside echo initially revealed no wall motion abnormalities. Labs confirmed diabetic ketoacidosis (glucose 1,371 mg/dL, bicarbonate 6 mmol/L, anion gap 38) and hyperkalemia (7.3 mmol/L). She experienced recurrent ventricular tachycardia requiring resuscitation, calcium, bicarbonate, vasopressors, insulin, and intubation. ST changes resolved after potassium correction. Two days later, TTE showed new cardiomyopathy with LVEF 33%, global LV hypokinesis, akinetic inferior wall, and severe RV dysfunction. Troponin, initially modestly elevated (341 ng/L), rose progressively, peaking at 26,179 ng/L, consistent with NSTEMI and new ischemic cardiomyopathy. Discussion: This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of pseudo-STEMI from hyperkalemia followed by true ischemic injury. Bedside echocardiography and serial biomarkers are essential to distinguish reversible metabolic changes from evolving ischemic cardiomyopathy. Conclusion: Hyperkalemia in DKA may mimic STEMI and precipitate malignant arrhythmias, but evolving inferior wall dysfunction and troponin rise can reveal concurrent ischemic cardiomyopathy. Prompt recognition and correction of metabolic abnormalities remain lifesaving. Clinical Implications: Clinicians should distinguish pseudo-STEMI from true ischemia so that it guides prompt management.
title: Abstract 18535: Hyperkalemia Induced ST Elevation and Ventricular Tachycardia Mimicking STEMI in the Setting of Diabetic Ketoacidosis

abstract: Background: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the standard treatment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolytic therapy has been proposed to improve microvascular perfusion and clinical outcomes, particularly in patients with high thrombus burden; however, its overall efficacy and safety remain uncertain. Objectives: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolytic therapy compared with primary PCI alone in patients with STEMI, with emphasis on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial reperfusion, left ventricular function, and bleeding outcomes. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolytic therapy (alteplase, tenecteplase, urokinase, streptokinase, and prourokinase) versus PCI alone in adult STEMI patients was conducted. Outcomes included MACE, mortality, myocardial reperfusion parameters, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and bleeding events. Pooled risk ratios or mean differences were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed to explore heterogeneity and robustness of evidence. Results: Thirteen randomized controlled trials comprising 2,122 patients were included. Adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolysis significantly reduced MACE compared with PCI alone (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53-0.86; p=0.001; I 2 =4%), with consistent findings across sensitivity analyses. Trial sequential analysis supported the robustness of this reduction, as the cumulative Z-curve crossed both conventional and sequential monitoring boundaries. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differential treatment effects according to fibrin specificity and timing of administration, while meta-regression identified fibrin specificity as a significant effect modifier.Intracoronary fibrinolysis improved myocardial reperfusion, including higher rates of TIMI grade 3 flow (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.14), TIMI myocardial perfusion grade 3 (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.13-1.68), and complete ST-segment resolution (RR 1.14, 95% CI 1.06-1.23), and reduced corrected TIMI frame count (MD -4.48, 95% CI -6.23 to -2.72). LVEF was also improved (MD 1.87%, 95% CI 1.07-2.67). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, major bleeding, or minor bleeding. Conclusions: Adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolytic therapy is associated with reduced MACE and improved angiographic, microvascular, and functional outcomes without an increase in bleeding in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. Further large-scale trials are needed to define optimal patient selection, fibrinolytic agent, and timing of administration.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 randomised controlled trials comprising 2,122 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Conference abstract without full methods; the included trials are small and heterogeneous in agent and timing, and the MACE definitions may vary.
appraisal.one_line: Conference abstract: meta-analysis of randomised trials of adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolysis during primary PCI in STEMI, with trial sequential analysis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolysis significantly reduced MACE compared with PCI alone (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53-0.86; p=0.001; I 2 =4%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, major bleeding, or minor bleeding.

title: Abstract 18568: Intracoronary Fibrinolytic Therapy During Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction A Systematic Review Meta Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a condition that predominantly affects women, for which conservative management is generally favored in clinically stable patients. Despite the lower overall prevalence of SCAD among men, real-world data show that men with SCAD are more frequently represented among patients treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This discordance raises important questions about whether PCI use reflects differences in clinical presentation, comorbidity burden, or treatment selection. This study compared baseline characteristics between women and men with SCAD and examined sex-specific factors associated with PCI use. Methods: Data were drawn from the TriNetX Research Network from 2015 to the present. Adults with SCAD were identified using ICD-10 code I25.42 and stratified by sex. Early PCI was defined as PCI performed within 3 days of the index SCAD diagnosis; patients with any prior PCI were excluded. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, presenting symptoms, and cardiac biomarkers were compared between women and men overall, between women and men treated with PCI, and within each sex according to early PCI versus no early PCI. Results: Among 16,219 patients with SCAD, 9,968 (61.5%) were women and 6,251 (38.5%) were men. Despite this higher prevalence of SCAD among women, early PCI was performed more frequently in men (48.1% vs. 25.2%, respectively). Compared with women, men had higher rates of hypertension, arterial disease, venous/lymphatic disease, pulmonary circulation disease, metabolic disorders, and diabetes, whereas women had higher rates of obesity, thyroid disease, muscle disorders, systemic lupus erythematosus, chest pain, and malaise/fatigue. Among PCI-treated patients, men had higher rates of hypertension and diabetes, while women had higher rates of chronic rheumatic heart disease, pulmonary circulation disease, obesity, thyroid disease, fatigue, syncope, muscle disorders, and systemic autoimmune disease. Within both sexes, PCI-treated patients had greater cardiometabolic and symptom burden than conservatively managed patients. PCI-treated women had higher natriuretic peptide levels, whereas PCI-treated men had higher troponin I levels. Conclusions: In this large real-world cohort, SCAD was more common among women; however, early PCI was disproportionately concentrated among men. The higher use of PCI among men may reflect differences in cardiovascular risk profile, clinical presentation, and biomarker evidence of myocardial injury. Further studies incorporating angiographic severity, hemodynamic status, and longitudinal clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether these observed patterns reflect variations in disease severity, procedural selection, or sex-specific management strategies.
title: Abstract 18579: Sex Differences in Baseline Characteristics and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Use Among Patients with Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

abstract: Introduction/Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but concerns about perioperative euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) prompted guideline recommendations to hold these agents before surgery. Their association with outcomes after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains incompletely defined. Research Questions/Hypothesis: We evaluated whether SGLT2i exposure within 90 days before isolated CABG was associated with 5-year mortality, perioperative complications compared with matched T2DM patients without SGLT2i exposure. Methods/Approach: We performed a multicenter retrospective TriNetX cohort study of adults with T2DM undergoing isolated CABG. Patients with SGLT2i exposure within 90 days before surgery were compared with no SGLT2i controls after 1:1 propensity score matching. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality through 5 years. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, atrial fibrillation, stroke or transient ischemic attack, pneumonia, respiratory failure, sepsis, perioperative DKA, a 30-day composite outcome (all listed 30-day outcomes except DKA and the late coronary ischemic event endpoint), and a late coronary ischemic event endpoint (repeat CABG, PCI, myocardial infarction, or angina). Results/Data: Matched cohorts included 2,170 SGLT2i-exposed and 2,170 no SGLT2i patients. Five-year mortality was lower in the SGLT2i cohort (139/2,160 [6.43%] vs 279/2,157 [12.94%]; RD –6.50%, 95% CI –8.25% to –4.75%; RR 0.498, 95% CI 0.410-0.604; HR 0.566, 95% CI 0.461-0.694; log-rank p<0.0001). Thirty-day mortality was numerically lower without conventional significance (1.20% vs 1.81%; OR 0.662; p=0.1030). The 30-day composite was similar by risk analysis (OR 0.892; p=0.0663) with a favorable Kaplan-Meier signal (HR 0.905; log-rank p=0.0396). Acute kidney injury, atrial fibrillation, stroke or TIA, pneumonia, respiratory failure, sepsis, and the late coronary ischemic event endpoint did not differ between groups. Perioperative DKA was rare, with fewer than 10 total events across the matched cohort lmiting comparative estimates according to database policy. Conclusion(s): Among matched T2DM patients undergoing isolated CABG, SGLT2i exposure within 90 days before surgery was associated with substantially lower 5-year mortality. Perioperative DKA was uncommon, with fewer than 10 total events across both matched groups, supporting that this safety signal was rare in the observed cohort while precluding reliable between-group inference. These findings support prospective evaluation of preoperative SGLT2i use in cardiac surgery.
title: Abstract 18580: Preoperative Sodium Glucose Cotransporter Inhibitor Exposure and Outcomes After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Type 2 Diabetes

abstract: Introduction: Immune checkpoint inhibitor -associated myocarditis (ICI-M) carries mortality rates exceeding 20%. Diagnosis relies on cardiac MRI (cMR) criteria that can be confounded by pre-existing structural heart disease. We report a novel case of ICI-M in a patient with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HOCM) and a recent acute coronary syndrome where overlapping imaging and biomarker abnormalities confounded the diagnosis. Case Presentation: 74 year old male with metastatic urothelial carcinoma initiated on pembrolizumab 14 days prior to admission, prostate adenocarcinoma, HOCM, and coronary artery disease (CAD) with recent non-ST segment myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) presented with diffuse abdominal and chest pain and diarrhea 4 days following percutaneous coronary intervention to the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries. High-sensitivity troponin T on admission was 440 ng/L, higher than at prior discharge. C-reactive protein (CRP) was significantly elevated to 253 mg/L. One day after admission, he developed mixed shock requiring vasopressor support and ICU transfer. Management: Shock physiology was thought to be consistent with LVOT obstruction related to hypovolemia. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed vigorous LV systolic function (LVEF 70%) and LVOT peak gradient of 59 mmHg at rest. He was treated with aggressive intravenous fluid repletion and intravenous esmolol. Colonoscopy demonstrated findings consistent with ICI colitis. cMR demonstrated intraventricular septal thickening up to 17mm, delayed myocardial enhancement that was predominantly mid-myocardial at the apex with additional subendocardial and subepicardial foci, and T2 hyperintensity at the apex and anterolateral segments (Figure 1). These imaging findings in view of the elevated HS-troponin T and CRP argued for concurrent myocarditis in the setting of underlying HOCM and recent infarct. The patient was treated empirically with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone for presumed concurrent ICI colitis and ICI-M which led to resolution of shock physiology and improvement in high-sensitivity troponin. Outcome: The patient was discharged on a prolonged steroid taper 1 week after initiating high dose steroids with resolution of GI symptoms, stable hemodynamics, and preserved systolic function. Immunotherapy was discontinued indefinitely. Discussion: To our knowledge, there are no published case reports specifically describing ICI-M in patients with pre-existing HOCM. The coexistence of HOCM, ischemic heart disease, and ICI-M raises unique clinical challenges including the diagnostic conundrum where every major cMR criterion for myocarditis is already abnormal at baseline. We speculate that a baseline cMR among patients beginning ICI therapy may be useful in cases of preexisting structural or ischemic heart disease.
title: Abstract 18604: Obstruction of Diagnosis: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis Hidden Behind the Hypertrophic Heart

abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but frequently life-threatening immune-related adverse event of cancer immunotherapy. Despite its high mortality, effective targeted therapies remain limited. Colchicine exerts broad anti-inflammatory effects and has demonstrated benefit in several inflammatory cardiovascular disorders; however, its role in ICI-associated myocarditis remains unknown. We investigated the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of colchicine in a transgenic mouse model of ICI-associated myocarditis. Methods: Mice were assigned to three groups: wild-type controls (WT), transgenic Pdcd1-/-Ctla4+/- mice receiving saline (ICI-myocarditis model), and transgenic Pdcd1-/-Ctla4+/- mice receiving colchicine. Colchicine was administered intraperitoneally every other day for 30 days. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. Myocardial injury, inflammation, and fibrosis were evaluated using histological and immunofluorescence analyses, plasma biomarker measurements, multiplex cytokine profiling, and unbiased cardiac proteomic analysis. Results: Compared with WT controls, Pdcd1-/-Ctla4+/- mice developed progressive myocarditis characterized by increased mortality, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and impaired global longitudinal strain, elevated plasma troponin I levels, extensive myocardial fibrosis, and marked infiltration of CD8 + T cells and macrophages. Colchicine treatment significantly improved survival, preserved cardiac function, reduced myocardial injury biomarkers, attenuated myocardial fibrosis, and decreased inflammatory cell infiltration. Multiplex cytokine profiling demonstrated suppression of key inflammatory mediators, including IFN-γ and CXCL9. Proteomic analysis revealed substantial normalization of disease-associated molecular pathways with colchicine treatment and identified endoplasmic reticulum membrane complex subunit 10 (EMC10) as a potential mediator of both disease pathogenesis and therapeutic response. Conclusions: Colchicine mitigates the functional, histological, inflammatory, and molecular manifestations of ICI-associated myocarditis in a clinically relevant murine model. These findings support further investigation of colchicine as a therapeutic and potentially preventive strategy for ICI-associated myocarditis, particularly in patients at increased risk for this complication. Furthermore, EMC10 emerges as a promising candidate mediator and potential therapeutic target warranting further mechanistic investigation.
title: Abstract 18622: Colchicine Attenuates Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis and Identifies EMC10 as a Novel Therapeutic Target

abstract: Introduction: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) is an immune-mediated prothrombotic disorder of heparin exposure. DVT and PE are its most common complications; simultaneous venous, intracardiac, and cerebral thrombosis after PCI is rare. Case: A 55-year-old man underwent PCI to the LAD and LCx for NSTEMI, complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring Impella support, with resultant HFrEF (LVEF 30-35%). He received unfractionated heparin during NSTEMI management. His platelet count, normal through hospital day 9, fell on day 10 (102 K/uL), and he was discharged at 83 K/uL, with thrombocytopenia not investigated or attributed to HIT (Figure 1). Four days later, he presented with pleuritic chest pain; D-dimer was 17 mcg/ml and CT angiography showed extensive bilateral PE with RV strain (Figure 2-A and B). Heparin was restarted, then stopped for persistent thrombocytopenia. Doppler confirmed left-leg DVT; echocardiography revealed a left ventricular (LV) apical thrombus (Figure 2-C); he underwent bilateral pulmonary artery thrombectomy. HIT was confirmed (PF4 antibody OD 2.604; positive serotonin release assay; nadir 72 K/uL). Due to left arm weakness that developed during hospitalization, an MRI brain showed multifocal infarcts attributed to cardioembolism from the LV thrombus (Figure 3). He was treated with argatroban, then fondaparinux, then was kept on apixaban. Hematology and cardiology agreed that indefinite anticoagulation was not required for the cardiac thrombus; a 3-6 month anticoagulation course was planned. By a follow-up echocardiogram after 4 months, the LVEF had recovered to 50% with normal right ventricular size and function and resolution of the LV thrombus. Discussion: This case illustrates HIT driving thrombosis possibly across three vascular compartments after PCI: venous (DVT/PE), intracardiac (LV thrombus), and cerebral (cardioembolic stroke), where systemic hypercoagulability compounds procedural endothelial injury and post-infarct apical akinesis. The DVT/PE and LV thrombus are clearly distinct events driven by HIT, while the multilobar infarcts could represent a sequela to the LV thrombus or a primary vascular thrombosis secondary to HIT. The platelet trajectory indicates HIT very likely began during the index admission (day-10 fall) and went unrecognized at discharge, with thrombosis dominating while thrombocytopenia remained modest. Prompt heparin cessation and non-heparin anticoagulation were decisive: on follow-up, platelets normalized (294 K/uL), LVEF recovered to 50%, and the LV thrombus resolved by 4 months. Clinicians should scrutinize platelet trends during and after any heparin exposure and maintain a high index of suspicion for HIT in post-PCI patients with unexpected thrombosis. The favorable trajectory — platelet normalization, LVEF recovery, and thrombus resolution — further underscores the value of early recognition.
title: Abstract 18644: The Unholy Triad: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia After PCI Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism, Left Ventricular Thrombus, and Embolic Stroke

abstract: Background: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has emerged as an important treatment option for severe tricuspid regurgitation. However, factors associated with prolonged postprocedural hospitalization and their clinical implications remain poorly characterized.Methods Adult T-TEER hospitalizations were identified using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016-2023. Postprocedural length of stay was calculated as total length of stay minus procedure day. Late discharge was defined as postprocedural hospitalization >48 hours. Survey-weighted analyses were performed to compare baseline characteristics, postprocedural complications, and temporal trends. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of late discharge. Results: Among 2,650 T-TEER hospitalizations, 1,555 (58.7%) were discharged within 48 hours and 1,095 (41.3%) experienced late discharge. Patients with late discharge had a greater comorbidity burden (median Elixhauser Comorbidity Index 21 vs 16; p<0.001) and were less likely to undergo elective admission (67.1% vs 87.1%; p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, increasing Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, female sex, and treatment at medium- or large-sized hospitals were independently associated with greater odds of late discharge, whereas elective admission was associated with lower odds of prolonged hospitalization.Patients with late discharge experienced substantially higher rates of acute kidney injury (29.7% vs 5.8%; p<0.001), major bleeding (19.2% vs 1.9%; p<0.001), heart block (5.9% vs 2.6%; p=0.034), cardiogenic shock (6.8% vs 0.3%; p<0.001), and mechanical ventilation (4.6% vs 0.0%; p<0.001). Median hospitalization costs were significantly greater among patients with late discharge ($273,154 vs $167,193; p<0.001). Nationally, early discharge increased while late discharge declined substantially between 2016 and 2023. Conclusions: More than two in five patients undergoing T-TEER remain hospitalized beyond 48 hours. Greater comorbidity burden and nonelective presentation are associated with prolonged hospitalization, while late discharge identifies a population with markedly higher postprocedural complication rates. Contemporary T-TEER practice has demonstrated a substantial shift toward earlier discharge over time.
title: Abstract 18646: Late Discharge Following Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair: Predictors, Temporal Trends, and Clinical Consequences from a National Analysis

abstract: Background: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) due to coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) represents a distinct and underrecognized clinical entity with limited evidence-based therapeutic guidance. Verapamil, a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker, and carvedilol, a non-selective beta-blocker with alpha-1 antagonism, are both mechanistically plausible agents for managing CMD-related vasospasm and sympathetic overdrive, yet no real-world comparative data exist to guide selection between these agents. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that verapamil would be associated with lower rates of heart failure, angina recurrence, stroke, and mortality compared to carvedilol in patients with MINOCA-CMD over a one-year follow-up period. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified adults (≥18 years) with a confirmed diagnosis of myocardial infarction with coronary microvascular dysfunction (ICD-10-CM: I21.B) prescribed either verapamil (n=879) or carvedilol (n=420). Propensity score matching (PSM) on demographics, comorbid diagnoses, and medication classes yielded balanced cohorts of 389 patients each. Outcomes were assessed from day 1 through 365 days post-index event and included all-cause mortality, heart failure, stroke, angina pectoris, atrial fibrillation, and hypotension. Results: After PSM, mean age was 64.9 ± 13.0 years in both cohorts, with approximately 57-58% female. Verapamil was associated with a significantly lower risk of heart failure compared to carvedilol (46.5% vs. 55.0%; RR 0.846, 95% CI 0.736-0.972; p=0.018; HR 0.805, 95% CI 0.661-0.982), with a longer median time to heart failure (358 vs. 100 days; log-rank p=0.029). All-cause mortality trended lower with verapamil (3.1% vs. 4.9%; RR 0.632, 95% CI 0.311-1.283; p=0.199; HR 0.634, 95% CI 0.308-1.305) but did not reach significance. Rates of stroke (7.2% vs. 10.5%; RR 0.683, 95% CI 0.431-1.081; p=0.101; HR 0.680, 95% CI 0.420-1.099), atrial fibrillation (13.1% vs. 17.5%; RR 0.750, 95% CI 0.537-1.048; p=0.090; HR 0.739, 95% CI 0.514-1.063), and hypotension (16.2% vs. 15.4%; RR 1.050, 95% CI 0.759-1.452; p=0.768; HR 1.066, 95% CI 0.748-1.518) were comparable between groups. Notably, verapamil was associated with a higher angina burden (17.2% vs. 12.6%; RR 1.367, 95% CI 0.973-1.922; p=0.070; HR 1.408, 95% CI 0.974-2.035), though this did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched real-world analysis of MINOCA-CMD patients, verapamil was associated with a significantly lower risk of heart failure and a longer time to heart failure hospitalization compared to carvedilol. These findings underscore the need for prospective randomized trials to validate these findings.
title: Abstract 18652: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes of Verapamil and Carvedilol in MINOCA-Related Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction - A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study

abstract: Background: In patients with continuous-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) for end-stage heart failure, low-flow alarms driven by arterial hypertension are difficult to manage, owing to the narrow therapeutic window for oral antihypertensive therapy. Case Summary: A 57-year-old man with a HeartMate 3 LVAD as destination therapy for end-stage non-ischemic cardiomyopathy developed refractory low-flow alarms beginning on postoperative day (POD) 50 in the setting of renal dysfunction. The low-flow alarms persisted despite serial hemodynamic evaluations with right heart catheterization and volume repletion, exclusion of pump thrombosis or outflow obstruction, and escalation to 5 simultaneous oral agents. Several oral agents were poorly tolerated, and despite the use of intravenous vasodilator therapy, he developed acute kidney injury (peak creatinine 5.3 mg/dL). After multidisciplinary discussion and shared decision-making, he underwent transcatheter-based bilateral radiofrequency renal arterial sympathetic denervation (RDN). Over the subsequent 2 weeks, intravenous vasodilator requirements fell and renal function normalized, permitting stabilization and discharge on a 3-drug oral antihypertensive regimen (Figure 1). Discussion: To our knowledge, this is the first reported use of RDN to treat refractory hypertension and its hemodynamic consequences of recurrent low-flow alarms in a patient supported by a continuous-flow LVAD. Because continuous-flow support devices are afterload-dependent, uncontrolled systemic hypertension directly impairs left ventricular unloading and reduces flow, manifesting as low-flow alarms, as seen with our patient. The systemic hypertension that accompanies continuous-flow support is also mechanistically distinct. Continuous-flow support reduces arterial pulsatility and produces sustained elevation in sympathetic nerve activity, with subsequent persistent activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. Thus, RDN, which ablates the afferent and efferent renal sympathetic nerves, may offer as an adjunctive strategy to attenuate the neurohormonal drivers of refractory hypertension in this patient population.
title: Abstract 18653: Renal Denervation for Recurrent Low-Flow Alarms from Uncontrolled Hypertension in a Left Ventricular Assist Device Patient

abstract: Background: Mental health disorders are prevalent in the general cardiovascular population. Their impact on in-hospital outcomes among patients admitted with cardiogenic shock remains unclear at a national level. Research Question: Are mental health comorbidities independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes among patients with cardiogenic shock? Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (2016-2020). Cardiogenic shock hospitalizations were stratified by the presence or absence of mental health comorbidity. ICD-10 codes were used to identify the variables. Continuous variables were compared using two-sample t-tests, and categorical variables were analyzed using chi-square tests. Multivariate logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, race, comorbidities, and disease severity, assessed the associations between mental health disorders (e.g., depression, anxiety) and clinical outcomes (e.g., AKI, mortality) and non-clinical outcomes (e.g., length of stay, discharge disposition) Results: Of 170,937 cardiogenic shock hospitalizations, 6,202 (3.63%) had concurrent mental health comorbidity. Despite comparable ages (66.37 ± 16.38 vs. 65.57 ± 15.97 years, p<0.001), patients with mental illness had markedly longer lengths of stay (19.65 ± 18.80 vs. 11.15 ± 14.40 days, p<0.001) and higher total hospital charges ($411,687 ± $546,978 vs. $243,216 ± $370,956, p<0.001). Mental illness patients had higher rates of atrial fibrillation/flutter (47.02% vs. 42.24%), VTE (10.54% vs. 8.01%), and stroke (9.09% vs. 6.77%; all p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, mental illness was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.55; 95% CI 0.51-0.58, p<0.001). It was independently associated with higher odds of acute respiratory failure (aOR 1.18; 95% CI 1.12-1.25), need for mechanical ventilation (aOR 1.30; 95% CI 1.23-1.37), sepsis/septic shock (aOR 1.40; 95% CI 1.33-1.49), and mechanical circulatory support use (aOR 1.21; 95% CI 1.13-1.29; all p<0.001). It was not significantly associated with AKI (aOR 1.01, p=0.846) or hemodialysis initiation (aOR 0.71, p=0.055). Patients with mental illness were frequently discharged to skilled nursing facilities (40.70% vs 21.82%, p<0.001). Conclusion: Mental health comorbidities affect approximately 1 in 28 cardiogenic shock hospitalizations and are associated with double the length of stay, higher hospital charges, higher rates of respiratory failure and sepsis, MCS utilization, and significantly worse discharge disposition.
