The paradoxically lower in-hospital mortality likely reflects selection bias or differences in resuscitation goals rather than a true protective effect. These findings highlight the importance of integrated psychiatric co-management and tailored care pathways in cardiogenic shock patients with mental illness.
title: Abstract 18660: Impact of Mental Health Comorbidities on In-Hospital Outcomes Among Patients Admitted with Cardiogenic Shock: A Nationwide Analysis

abstract: BACKGROUND: Cognitive decline affects 30-40% of patients within 12 months of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), driven by cerebral hypoperfusion, neuroinflammation, and cardioembolic microembolism — yet cognitive outcomes are absent from all ACS and cardiac rehabilitation (CR) guidelines. Structured CR plausibly attenuates post-ACS neurodegeneration via aerobic conditioning and anti-inflammatory metabolic effects. Whether CR independently reduces cognitive decline or dementia incidence post-ACS has not been established by pooled evidence. This is the first systematic review examining CR as a neuroprotective intervention post-ACS. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, PsycINFO, and ClinicalTrials.gov through April 2025. Eligible studies were RCTs and prospective cohorts comparing structured CR versus usual care in adults with confirmed ACS, reporting validated cognitive outcomes (MoCA, MMSE, MCI incidence, or dementia) at ≥6 months. Primary outcomes: MoCA score change and incident MCI or dementia. Secondary outcomes included executive function, processing speed, depression, and quality of life. Pooled SMDs and RRs used random-effects models. RESULTS: Twenty-one studies (n=8,847; mean age 61.4 ± 9.3 years; CR completion 74%) were included. CR significantly attenuated cognitive decline versus usual care (SMD +0.48, 95% CI 0.34-0.62; p<0.0001; I 2 =29%), equating to a 2.1-point MoCA advantage at 12 months. CR reduced incident MCI (RR 0.61, 95% CI 0.49-0.76; p<0.0001; NNT=11) and dementia (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.42-0.80; p=0.001). Executive function showed greatest benefit (SMD +0.54; p<0.0001). Effects were consistent across age and ACS subtype (p-interaction=0.43). CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac rehabilitation reduces post-ACS cognitive decline, MCI incidence by 39% (NNT=11), and dementia risk by 42% — consistently across age and ACS subtype. The brain-heart neuroprotective axis of CR is entirely absent from ACC/AHA ACS and CR guidelines. These data provide the first pooled evidence supporting cognitive preservation as a formal Class I CR indication post-ACS and mandate neurocognitive assessment as a standard CR outcome metric.
title: Abstract 18662: Cardiac Rehabilitation and Prevention of Cognitive Decline Following Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established alternative to surgical aortic valve replacement for patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Myval has shown favourable outcomes; however, comparative evidence against established THVs remains limited. Hypothesis: We evaluated the comparative effectiveness and safety of Myval versus contemporary THVs in severe aortic stenosis. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through March 2026 for studies comparing Myval with contemporary THVs. Random-effects network meta-analysis was performed. Primary outcomes included PPI, 30-day mortality, stroke, major bleeding, and major vascular complications. Secondary outcomes included technical success, transvalvular aortic regurgitation, mean aortic valve gradient, and 1-year mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and NOS, and certainty of evidence using CINeMA. Pooled RRs or MDs with 95% CIs were calculated. Results: Twelve studies (2 RCTs and 10 observational studies) comprising 5,444 patients across six THV platforms were included. Compared with Myval, Portico (RR 2.59, 95% CI 1.52-4.42, P-score =0.05) and Allegra (RR 1.99, 95% CI 1.08-3.69, P-score=0.22) were associated with significantly higher PPI rates, while Evolut showed a borderline increase (RR 1.62, 95% CI 0.99-2.66, P-score=0.36). No significant differences were observed between Myval and Sapien or Acurate valves for PPI. 30-day mortality, stroke, major bleeding, and major vascular complications were largely comparable across valves. Evolut showed higher transvalvular aortic regurgitation compared with Myval (RR 2.52, 95% CI 1.35-4.71, P-score=0.01). Technical success was lower with Evolut compared to Myval, whereas Sapien exhibited comparable technical success. For haemodynamics, Allegra (MD –2.26 mmHg, 95% CI –3.10 to –1.42, P-score=1.00) and Evolut (MD –1.37 mmHg, 95% CI –1.99 to –0.75, P-score=0.79) showed significantly lower mean aortic valve gradients than Myval, whereas Sapien had higher gradients (MD +2.70 mmHg, 95% CI +1.90 to +3.50, P-score=0.00). Mortality at 1-year did not differ significantly among valves. No significant publication bias or network inconsistency was detected; overall confidence was low by CINeMA. Conclusion(s): Myval showed a favourable safety and procedural profile compared with contemporary THVs. It had lower permanent pacemaker implantation rates than Portico and Allegra, while maintaining comparable short- and intermediate-term clinical outcomes. Although some supra-annular valves showed lower mean aortic valve gradients, Myval was associated with favorable conduction outcomes while maintaining acceptable haemodynamic performance. Further adequately powered head-to-head randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.
title: Abstract 18663: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Myval versus Contemporary Transcatheter Aortic Valves: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac re-transplantation accounts for about 3% of heart transplants. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV), rejection, and other mechanisms of graft dysfunction drive late mortality after transplantation, and select patients with a failing graft may benefit from re-transplantation. We present a patient who underwent four orthotopic heart transplants (OHT), a rare course in which serial re-transplantation has produced a favorable long-term outcome despite recurrent severe complications over three decades. Patient Information: A 34-year-old woman who underwent neonatal OHT for hypoplastic left heart syndrome has since undergone three further OHTs for distinct causes of graft failure. She also developed end-stage renal disease from calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, requiring two renal transplants. Clinical Course: Prior to establishing care in adult transplant clinic, she had undergone her first re-transplant in childhood for CAV. In her late teens she was treated for 2R acute cellular rejection (ACR). At age 20 she presented with worsening tachycardia and volume overload; echocardiography showed biventricular graft dysfunction with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 43%, endomyocardial biopsy showed 2R ACR with diffuse C4d positivity indicating antibody-mediated rejection (AMR), and coronary angiography revealed near-total loss of the left anterior descending artery with diffuse three-vessel distal disease (grade 3 CAV). With concurrent AMR and graft dysfunction, she was listed for re-transplantation and underwent a third OHT. Over the next 12 years, she developed progressive tricuspid regurgitation (TR) from a flail tricuspid leaflet. Two transcatheter repairs failed, culminating in single-leaflet device attachment and severe TR. Despite medical management, she progressed to NYHA class IV, stage D heart failure and developed stage IV chronic kidney disease of her renal allograft. She was re-listed and underwent combined heart-kidney transplantation at age 32. Outcomes: At two-year follow-up, she has normal cardiac allograft function with no subsequent rejection or CAV, and her renal function is stable. She currently works as a registered nurse. Discussion: Re-transplantation is the only definitive therapy for end-stage graft failure and offers favorable outcomes in carefully selected candidates. This case demonstrates several indications for re-transplantation: cardiac allograft vasculopathy, rejection, and structural graft failure. Although repeat transplantation carries escalating risks of allosensitization, infection, and perioperative complications, she achieved a remarkable outcome across four heart transplants. Ultimately, her course suggests that prior re-transplantation alone should not preclude candidacy, and supports individualized evaluation of serial re-transplantation in carefully selected patients.
title: Abstract 18665: A Change of Heart, and Another, and Another: Four Orthotopic Heart Transplants in One Patient

abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is prevalent among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) complicated by cardiogenic shock and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, the impact of CKD severity on outcomes among patients requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS) remains incompletely characterized. Research Question: To evaluate the association between CKD severity and in-hospital outcomes among STEMI hospitalizations complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring MCS. Methods: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2023) to identify adult hospitalizations with STEMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and were complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, or venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Hospitalizations were stratified into advanced CKD, CKD stages 1-3, and no CKD. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, palliative care utilization, mechanical ventilation, acute limb ischemia, acute blood loss anemia, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT). Propensity score matching was performed using 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching. Results: Among 72,865 weighted hospitalizations, 18,840 (25.8%) had CKD, including 6,010 (8.2%) with advanced CKD and 12,830 (17.6%) with CKD stages 1-3. In the crude analyses, mortality increased with worsening kidney dysfunction (39.0% vs. 35.3% vs. 29.8%; p<0.001). Advanced CKD was associated with higher prevalence of AKI (91.0% vs. 82.9% vs. 47.2%; p<0.001), RRT (26.6% vs. 10.7% vs. 4.8%; p<0.001), acute blood loss anemia (25.4% vs. 19.2% vs. 17.0%; p<0.001), and palliative care utilization (18.1% vs. 17.5% vs. 12.6%; p<0.001). After propensity matching, CKD stages 1-3 remained associated with higher mortality than no CKD (35.9% vs. 32.7%; p=0.033), whereas mortality differences between advanced CKD and no CKD (39.2% vs. 36.0%; p=0.137) and between advanced CKD and CKD stages 1-3 (39.2% vs. 35.0%; p=0.050) were attenuated. Renal complications persisted despite matching, with advanced CKD associated with a higher prevalence of AKI (91.9% vs. 54.9%; p<0.001) and RRT utilization (27.9% vs. 6.8%; p<0.001) compared with no CKD. Conclusions: Among STEMI hospitalizations complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring MCS, although mortality differences were largely attenuated after adjustment for baseline comorbidity burden, adverse renal outcomes remained pronounced across CKD strata. These findings identify CKD as an important modifier of outcomes in STEMI-related cardiogenic shock requiring MCS.
title: Abstract 18666: Chronic Kidney Disease and Outcomes in STEMI-Related Cardiogenic Shock Requiring Mechanical Circulatory Support

abstract: Background: Management options are limited when left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction persists despite septal reduction therapy in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM). Pacing strategies may offer an adjunctive, physiology-guided approach in selected patients. Case Presentation: An 85-year-old woman with HOCM and second-degree heart block with dual-chamber pacemaker implantation presented with worsening dyspnea. One month earlier, she was admitted with non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and underwent coronary revascularization. At that time, she also underwent Alcohol Septal Ablation (ASA) of the largest septal branch. Echocardiography on this admission showed preserved ejection fraction, significant LVOT turbulence with a peak gradient of approximately 100 mmHg, and severe mitral regurgitation. She was treated with metoprolol succinate and diltiazem to reduce the LVOT gradient; however, recurrent hypotension limited medication uptitration. Given persistent obstruction despite medical therapy and recent ASA, electrophysiologic evaluation was performed to assess different pacing strategies. Under echocardiographic guidance, septal pacing and RV apical pacing were compared. During RV apical pacing, the peak LVOT gradient decreased to 9 mmHg, and mitral regurgitation improved from severe to mild (Figures 1 and 2). Based on this response, her device was upgraded to a cardiac resynchronization therapy pacemaker (CRT-P) with pacing from her RV apical lead. After CRT-P implantation, her dyspnea resolved. At 1-month follow-up, she remained asymptomatic with stable echocardiographic findings. Discussion: This case highlights the importance of pacing site selection in patients with HOCM and persistent LVOT obstruction after septal reduction therapy. Despite recent ASA and maximally tolerated medical therapy, the patient remained symptomatic with a severe residual gradient. Intraprocedural echocardiographic assessment demonstrated that switching from septal pacing to RV apical pacing produced immediate improvement. This case highlights that RV apical pacing may alter ventricular activation in a way that reduces dynamic obstruction in select patients.
title: Abstract 18684: From Septal to Apical, Pacing Optimization for Refractory Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction

abstract: Introduction / Background: Timely reperfusion via Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) is the gold standard for reducing mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). International guidelines recommend a strict travel threshold under 120 minutes from symptom onset to device activation, with an optimal "golden hour" of 60 minutes. However, specialized cardiovascular infrastructure in developing countries is often unevenly distributed. In Mexico, the real-world geographic coverage of these centers and the structural disparities between institutional healthcare sectors remain poorly quantified. Research Questions: What is the actual geographic coverage area of PCI centers in Mexico within clinical time windows of 60, 90, and 120 minutes? Methods / Approach: We conducted a nationwide geospatial network analysis evaluating a comprehensive sample of 86 active PCI centers across Mexico. Facilities were geocoded and categorized by institutional sector (Private, Public, Public-Military, or Unclassified). To move beyond theoretical geometric buffers, real-world driving network data was simulated utilizing the HERE API in R (using the hereR and sf packages). Cumulative isochrone service areas were modeled based on three clinical travel time thresholds: 60, 90, and 120 minutes under standardized driving conditions. Overlapping polygons were spatially dissolved using metric projections (EPSG:6362) to calculate the exact, non-duplicated effective coverage in square kilometers (km2). Results / Data: Of the 86 analyzed PCI centers, the sample is almost equally split between the private and public domains: 45.3 % (n = 39) are private facilities, 44.2% (n = 38) belong to the public sector, 2.3% (n = 2) belong to the military public sector, and 8.1% (n = 7) were unclassified. Network isochrone modeling demonstrated an effective cumulative geographic coverage of 111,661 km2 within the optimal 60-minute window. Spatial expansion analysis showed a coverage of 218,130 km2 at 90 minutes, reaching a maximum national footprint of 331,451 at the critical 120-minute threshold. Spatial clustering was prominently observed; despite private centers accounting for nearly half of the nation's total PCI capacity, their service areas heavily overlap within major urban economic hubs, failing to extend coverage to vulnerable populations. Conclusion(s): Profound structural and geographic disparities exist within Mexico's cardiovascular emergency care network. Although the private sector holds a massive share of the country's catheterization laboratories, its commercial clustering limits its utility for national emergency coverage. Consequently, extensive geographic "PCI deserts" persist across remote and rural regions, leaving significant portions of the population entirely outside the recommended travel safety limits.
title: Abstract 18692: Spatial Distribution and Temporal Accessibility Analysis of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) Centers in Mexico

abstract: Introduction: Atrial septal aneurysm (ASA) is a saccular deformity of the interatrial septum associated with patent foramen ovale (PFO), intracardiac shunting, and thromboembolic events including cryptogenic stroke. Giant ASA is exceedingly rare and may have heightened clinical significance in patients with malignancy-associated hypercoagulability. We present a case of giant ASA discovered during evaluation of acute dyspnea in a patient with advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Case Description: A 69-year-old woman with prior right upper lobe adenocarcinoma status post lobectomy, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, remote cerebrovascular accidents, and newly diagnosed stage IIIB right upper lobe SCC presented with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. She had a >40 pack-year smoking history. On presentation, she was tachycardic and hypoxemic. High-sensitivity troponin rose from 47 to 250 ng/L. Electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia without ischemic changes. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography demonstrated a 10.0 х 8.5 cm right upper lobe mass with right pulmonary artery invasion, complete superior vena cava occlusion with collateralization, and progressive satellite nodules. Pulmonary embolism could not be excluded. Cardiology was consulted for rising troponin. Bedside echocardiography showed right ventricular dilation and dysfunction. Transthoracic echocardiography with contrast and agitated saline demonstrated ejection fraction 50-55%, severe apical hypokinesis, a giant ASA, and possible right-to-left shunting. Venous duplex revealed chronic right axillary and acute left subclavian deep vein thrombosis, prompting therapeutic anticoagulation. The patient underwent rigid bronchoscopy with tumor debulking, cryotherapy, and stent placement, complicated by hypercapnic respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. She subsequently received palliative radiation and carboplatin/etoposide with clinical improvement and was discharged on supplemental oxygen. Discussion: ASA is associated with interatrial shunting and increased risk of cardiogenic embolism, particularly when accompanied by PFO. In patients with cancer, hypercoagulability further amplifies thromboembolic risk. This patient's history of stroke, active malignancy, upper-extremity thromboses, and giant ASA with possible shunting represented a convergence of risk factors for paradoxical embolization. Further evaluation with transesophageal echocardiography was recommended. Conclusion: Giant ASA is a rare finding with important thromboembolic implications, particularly in patients with malignancy. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive cardiac evaluation and consideration of transesophageal echocardiography when ASA is identified on transthoracic imaging.
title: Abstract 18698: Incidental Giant Atrial Septal Aneurysm in a Cancer Patient Presenting with Acute Dyspnea

abstract: Introduction: Acquired Gerbode defects are rare left ventricle-to-right atrium (LV-RA) shunts associated with infective endocarditis, prosthetic valve dysfunction, & prior cardiac surgery. Diagnosis is often challenging because findings are frequently obscured by coexisting valvular pathology. Case: 66-year-old man with chronic heart failure & mechanical aortic & mitral valve replacements (2006) presented with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, abdominal pain, & worsening heart failure symptoms for 1 month. Initial evaluation demonstrated acute decompensated heart failure with LVEF 15-20%. TEE revealed severe paravalvular aortic regurgitation (AR), partial dehiscence of the mechanical aortic valve, & moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) secondary to perforation of the mitral-aortic continuity. Despite medical therapy, he developed worsening cardiogenic shock & was transferred for evaluation of structural or transcatheter options for severe prosthetic valve dysfunctionMultimodality imaging was performed to clarify anatomy & guide management. Repeat TEE demonstrated severe AR with holodiastolic flow reversal & a paravalvular leak adjacent to the left coronary cusp. Cardiac MRI identified a small LV-RA shunt near the membranous septum consistent with a Gerbode defect & confirmed severe paravalvular AR (regurgitant volume 71 mL; regurgitant fraction 63%). Right heart catheterization showed elevated filling pressures (RA 12 mmHg, PCWP 24 mmHg) & pulmonary hypertension. PET/CT & CT showed no evidence of active infection or aortic root abscess.A multidisciplinary structural heart, advanced heart failure, imaging, & cardiothoracic surgery team reviewed the case. Given severe prosthetic valve dehiscence, torrential paravalvular AR, complex LV-RA shunt physiology, & severe ventricular dysfunction, the patient was deemed prohibitively high risk for redo surgery or transcatheter intervention. The patient was listed as Status 2 by exception for orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT) He subsequently underwent successful OHT without major complications. Discussion: This case highlights the value of multimodality imaging in identifying an acquired Gerbode defect concealed within complex prosthetic valve pathology. While severe paravalvular AR initially appeared to explain the presentation, advanced imaging demonstrated additional septal destruction with LV-RA shunting. The combination of prosthetic valve dehiscence, severe regurgitation, & Gerbode physiology resulted in end-stage heart failure not amenable to surgical or percutaneous repair. Recognition of this rare constellation was critical in guiding referral for OHT, illustrating how multimodality imaging can fundamentally alter management in complex structural heart disease.
title: Abstract 18716: When the Left Ventricle Finds a New Exit: Multimodality Imaging Uncovers an Acquired Gerbode Defect Leading to Heart Transplantation

abstract: Background: The optimal revascularization strategy in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) receiving Impella or percutaneous left ventricular assist device (pLVAD) support remains uncertain. While culprit-only percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is generally recommended in unselected AMI-CS populations, the applicability of this strategy to mechanically supported patients is unclear. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies comparing complete or multivessel revascularization with culprit-only or incomplete revascularization in adults with Impella/pLVAD-supported AMI-CS. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through May 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury, renal replacement therapy, bleeding, stroke, and vascular complications. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Three observational studies involving 11,835 patients met the inclusion criteria. Four mortality comparisons comprising 22,714 observations and 10,301 events were included in the quantitative synthesis. No significant difference in all-cause mortality was observed between culprit-only/incomplete and multivessel/complete revascularization strategies (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.00-1.12; p=0.055; I 2 =48.8%). Subgroup analyses according to follow-up duration demonstrated no significant differences for either in-hospital or 30-day mortality. Similarly, no significant differences were observed for acute kidney injury (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.94-1.23), blood transfusion (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.83-1.03), ischemic stroke (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.70-1.74), hemorrhagic stroke (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.73-1.06), or vascular complications (OR 1.28, 95% CI 0.83-1.99). Access-site hematoma was less frequent in the culprit-only/incomplete revascularization group (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.37-0.77). Conclusions: Among patients with Impella/pLVAD-supported AMI-CS, current observational evidence does not demonstrate a significant difference in mortality between culprit-only/incomplete and multivessel/complete revascularization strategies. Given the limited number of available studies and the very low certainty of evidence, adequately powered prospective studies are needed to determine the optimal revascularization strategy in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 18717: Complete versus Culprit-Only Revascularization in Impella/pLVAD-Supported Acute Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Conduction disturbances remain a common complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), resulting in new left bundle branch block (LBBB), high-grade atrioventricular block, and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). The proximity of the His-Purkinje system to the membranous septum (MS) suggests that septal anatomy may influence susceptibility to conduction injury. Methods: Data were evaluated from the Membranous Septum Depth Alignment Study (MIDAS), the INTERSECT registry, a meta-analysis of MS anatomy and conduction outcomes (18 studies; n=5,740), and a meta-analysis of persistent LBBB outcomes after TAVR (12 studies; n=7,792). Results: In MIDAS (n=248), new PPI occurred in 9.7% of patients undergoing self-expanding TAVR. Implantation depth exceeding MS length independently predicted PPI (OR 8.04, 95% CI 2.58-25.04; p<0.001). After implementation of a prospective MS-guided strategy (n=100), PPI decreased to 3.0% (p=0.035) and new LBBB decreased from 25.8% to 9.0% (p<0.001). In INTERSECT (n=1,811), new PPI occurred in 15.2% of patients, and those requiring PPI had shorter MS length than those without PPI (3.7 mm vs 4.1 mm; p<0.01). In the largest quantitative synthesis available (18 studies; n=5,740), each 1-mm decrease in MS length was associated with higher odds of conduction abnormality or PPI (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.28-1.99; p<0.001). A smaller difference between MS length and implantation depth was similarly associated with conduction injury (OR 1.75 per 1-mm decrease, 95% CI 1.32-2.31; p<0.001). In a separate meta-analysis (12 studies; n=7,792), persistent LBBB was associated with increased 1-year all-cause mortality (RR 1.32, 95% CI 1.17-1.49; p<0.001), cardiac mortality (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.20-1.78; p<0.001), heart failure hospitalization (RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.05-1.72; p=0.02), and subsequent PPI (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.58-2.27; p<0.001). Conclusions: Across MIDAS, INTERSECT, and pooled analyses involving more than 13,000 patients, shorter MS length and deeper implantation relative to septal anatomy were consistently associated with post-TAVR conduction disturbances. The reduction in PPI and LBBB observed with MS-guided implantation supports incorporation of CT-derived septal measurements into procedural planning and provides a rationale for prospective anatomy-guided strategies to reduce conduction complications.
title: Abstract 18756: Membranous Septum Anatomy and Implantation Depth as Determinants of Conduction Injury After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement

abstract: Background: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and liver cirrhosis represent a high-risk population in whom stroke prevention is challenging due to competing thromboembolic and bleeding risks. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) may offer an alternative to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC), but comparative real-world outcomes in cirrhosis remain limited. Objective: To compare clinical outcomes after LAAC versus OAC in patients with AF and liver cirrhosis. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults with AF and cirrhosis who underwent LAAC were compared with patients treated with OAC without LAAC. Propensity score matching was performed across 91 baseline characteristics, including demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, liver disease severity markers, bleeding history, medications, and laboratory values. After matching, 1,379 patients were included in each cohort. Outcomes were assessed from 1 day to 1,095 days after the index event. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed, and p values were derived from log-rank testing. Results: In the matched cohorts, LAAC was associated with a lower rate of the composite adverse outcome compared with OAC (25.7% vs 40.9%; HR 0.638, 95% CI 0.509-0.799; log-rank p<0.001). Stroke or systemic embolism was lower after LAAC (3.6% vs 6.6%; HR 0.526, 95% CI 0.358-0.772; log-rank p=0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower in the LAAC cohort (20.2% vs 33.6%; HR 0.585, 95% CI 0.504-0.679; log-rank p<0.001). Major bleeding was reduced with LAAC compared with OAC (13.1% vs 22.2%; HR 0.588, 95% CI 0.436-0.793; log-rank p<0.001). Conclusions: Among patients with AF and liver cirrhosis, LAAC was associated with lower risks of composite adverse outcomes, stroke or systemic embolism, all-cause mortality, and major bleeding compared with OAC. These findings support LAAC as a potential alternative stroke-prevention strategy in selected patients with cirrhosis and warrant prospective validation.
title: Abstract 18759: Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation Patients with Liver Cirrhosis

abstract: BACKGROUND: Women with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are underrepresented in landmark cardiovascular trials, yielding guideline recommendations derived predominantly from male cohorts. Sex-based differences in platelet reactivity, pharmacokinetics, and thrombotic biology may substantially alter antiplatelet efficacy. Whether novel antiplatelet agents confer differential benefit in women with ACS remains unestablished. This is the first sex-stratified meta-analysis to examine treatment-specific outcomes of novel antiplatelet therapy in women with ACS. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines , we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov through December 2024. Eligible studies were RCTs and prospective cohort studies enrolling women with ACS (STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina) treated with novel antiplatelet therapy versus standard-of-care, with sex-disaggregated outcomes. Quality was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The primary endpoint was MACE (cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke). Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, stent thrombosis, and major bleeding (BARC ≥3). Pooled estimates used random-effects models (DerSimonian-Laird); sex-treatment interaction was formally tested. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies enrolling 31,847 women (mean age 64.3 ± 9.1 years) were included. Novel antiplatelet therapy significantly reduced MACE in women (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.87; p<0.0001; I 2 =31%), representing an absolute risk reduction of 4.2 events per 100 patient-years. A significant sex-treatment interaction was identified (p-interaction=0.03), with women deriving greater benefit than men (HR 0.78 vs. 0.94). All-cause mortality (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.71-0.93; p=0.002) and stent thrombosis (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.45-0.88; p=0.007) were also significantly reduced. Major bleeding did not differ by sex (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.91-1.31; p=0.34). CONCLUSIONS: Novel antiplatelet therapy confers preferentially greater cardiovascular benefit in women with ACS, with no excess bleeding risk. These findings provide the first class-level evidence of a sex-specific therapeutic advantage and directly challenge male-derived antiplatelet guidelines. Current ACC/AHA recommendations do not incorporate sex-stratified antiplatelet guidance; these data support urgent revision. Mandatory sex-disaggregated reporting in future ACS trials is imperative.
title: Abstract 18771: Sex-Specific Outcomes of Novel Antiplatelet Therapy in Women with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac metastases can mimic primary cardiac tumors and cause obstruction, embolization, arrhythmia, or pericardial disease. Melanoma has high propensity for cardiac involvement, though right atrial metastasis is rarely the initial diagnostic clue. Multimodality imaging helps define tumor attachment and hemodynamic risk. Case Description: A 46-year-old man with hypertension, prediabetes, tobacco use, and former alcohol use disorder presented after developing fluctuating, nontender fullness along the left side of his neck. He perceived the area as intermittently pulsatile and also reported throat pressure when lying supine, along with several days of bilateral lower-extremity edema. Computed tomography angiography of the neck showed no stenosis or soft tissue mass. Transthoracic echocardiography showed an irregular right atrial mass measuring 3.7 x 1.6 cm (Figure 1). Transesophageal echocardiography showed a large right atrial mass attached to the lateral wall without a stalk, protruding through the tricuspid valve, measuring 8.0 x 5.3 cm (Figure 2). Agitated saline study was positive for interatrial shunting. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed a 5.4 x 7.0 x 7.8 cm irregular right atrial mass with broad-based attachment to the cranial, posterior, and lateral right atrial free wall. The mass extended from the distal superior vena cava, which appeared nearly occluded, to the tricuspid valve orifice (Figure 3). Tissue characterization favored malignancy. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography showed the right atrial mass with subcutaneous and intramuscular nodules, concerning for angiosarcoma or metastatic disease. He underwent right atrial mass resection with bovine patch reconstruction and tricuspid valve repair. Pathology demonstrated melanoma, with tumor cells positive for S100, SOX-10, and PRAME. Postoperative echocardiography showed trace tricuspid regurgitation and no residual mass. He was started on relatlimab and nivolumab. Discussion: This case highlights metastatic melanoma presenting as a giant right atrial mass with near-occlusion of the superior vena cava and tricuspid valve involvement. The presentation was subtle, with intermittent neck fullness and dyspnea rather than overt heart failure, arrhythmia, or shock. The mass mimicked a primary cardiac tumor, but broad-based sessile attachment, malignant cardiac magnetic resonance imaging features, extracardiac nodules, and immunohistochemistry established metastatic melanoma. In right atrial tumors, echocardiography identifies mobility and valve involvement, while cardiac magnetic resonance imaging defines tissue characteristics and obstructive risk. Early recognition is critical because malignant right atrial masses may progress rapidly to caval or valvular obstruction and require coordinated surgical and oncologic management.
title: Abstract 18789: Giant Right Atrial Metastatic Melanoma Presenting with Intermittent Neck Fullness

abstract: Background: Type 2 myocardial infarction (T2MI), caused by myocardial oxygen supply-demand mismatch rather than plaque rupture, is a poorly characterized complication of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB). Hemorrhage-driven hypotension, acute anemia, and reflex tachycardia create a substrate for demand ischemia, yet the true incidence, clinical predictors, and prognostic impact of T2MI in UGIB remain incompletely defined. Hypothesis: T2MI occurs in a clinically significant proportion of UGIB hospitalizations and is an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality beyond established comorbid risk factors. Methods: We analyzed the MIMIC-IV v3.1 ECG-ICD-10 dataset (800,035 ECG records; BIDMC, 2008-2022). UGIB was identified by ICD-10 codes covering peptic ulcer, esophageal varices, and unspecified upper GI hemorrhage; T2MI by code I21.4. One ECG per patient (first recorded) was used; 7,490 unique patients comprised the analytic cohort. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of T2MI (Model 1) and its association with in-hospital mortality (Model 2). A prespecified sensitivity analysis restricted to ED-obtained ECGs was performed. Results: T2MI occurred in 401 patients (5.4%). T2MI patients were older (median 76 vs. 66 years) and had higher rates of heart failure (HF; 56.1% vs. 22.0%), atrial fibrillation (AF; 42.1% vs. 24.3%), and chronic kidney disease (CKD; 42.1% vs. 22.9%). Incidence rose sharply with age, from 0.9% in patients aged 18-49 to 8.1% in those aged ≥80 years. On multivariable analysis, independent predictors of T2MI were HF (adjusted OR [aOR] 3.04; 95% CI 2.40-3.85), coagulopathy (aOR 1.56; 1.22-1.99), male sex (aOR 1.46; 1.17-1.81), CKD (aOR 1.26; 1.00-1.58), and older age (aOR 1.02/year; 1.02-1.03); cirrhosis was independently protective (aOR 0.57; 0.35-0.90). In-hospital mortality was 61.6% vs. 44.0% (crude OR 2.04; 1.66-2.51). After full covariate adjustment, T2MI remained independently associated with death (aOR 1.33; 95% CI 1.06-1.66; p=0.012). Results were directionally consistent in the ED subgroup (n=3,728; T2MI rate 4.0%; mortality 63.5% vs. 38.0%). Conclusions: T2MI complicates roughly 1 in 18 UGIB hospitalizations and is independently associated with 33% higher adjusted odds of in-hospital death based on our data findings. Pre-existing cardiac disease, coagulopathy, and advanced age are the dominant risk factors. These findings support systematic cardiac monitoring and individualized risk stratification in UGIB patients with relevant comorbidities.
title: Abstract 18826: Type 2 Myocardial Infarction Complicating Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Incidence, Clinical Predictors, and Impact on In-Hospital Mortality

abstract: Background: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) depends on autologous conduits: the left internal mammary artery (LIMA) is considered the gold standard for bypass grafting to the left anterior descending artery (LAD). However, many patients lack suitable vessels. The Coronary Tissue Engineered Vessel (CTEV) is an acellular bioengineered human artery designed as an off-the-shelf biologic alternative for surgical revascularization. Positive preclinical evaluation in a primate CABG model, together with clinical experience demonstrating safety and feasibility of the related acellular tissue-engineered vessel across multiple vascular indications (>600 patients; >1200 patient-years), supported FDA Investigational New Drug authorization for human evaluation. Research Question: This study is designed to assess whether CTEV can be safely implanted as a coronary bypass and maintain graft patency in patients undergoing CABG. Methods: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase 2a study is the first-in-human evaluation of CTEV in CABG. Enrollment will be conducted initially at one U.S. site using a staged design. An initial 3 subject cohort will undergo CABG with a LIMA to the LAD and a CTEV graft to the right coronary artery or left circumflex territory. The initial cohort (n=3) will be enrolled one subject at a time, with each subsequent subject enrolled only after completion and review of the prior subject's 2-month clinical assessment, including coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) and transthoracic echocardiography. Following review of the initial cohort data and confirmation of acceptable graft performance, a second cohort (n=3) will be enrolled using a 1-week stagger between subjects. Enrollment of the final cohort (n=4) will proceed following review of the 2-month CTA assessments from Cohort 2, for a total of 10 subjects. Eligible subjects are adults with multivessel coronary artery disease undergoing first-time isolated CABG with ≥80% target vessel stenosis (or FFR ≤0.8), target vessel diameter ≥2.5 mm, and suitable runoff. Subjects will be followed through 12-14 months, with extension to 36 months. Primary objectives include graft patency and safety. Major adverse cardiac events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or repeat revascularization) will be assessed. Analyses will include all implanted grafts and treated subjects; safety will be reported as observed. Results: This study will generate the first clinical data evaluating CTEV for coronary revascularization. Serial imaging and clinical assessments will provide longitudinal characterization of graft patency, remodeling, and safety. Conclusions: This study marks the first U.S. clinical investigation of a bioengineered human artery in CABG and may advance the development of off-the-shelf biologic conduits for coronary revascularization.
title: Abstract 18840: First-in-Human Phase 2a Study Design of a Bioengineered Human Coronary Artery for Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting

abstract: Introduction/Background: Despite contemporary lipid-lowering therapy and increasingly aggressive LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) targets following acute coronary syndrome (ACS), many high-risk patients fail to achieve guideline-directed LDL-C goals. We sought to identify factors associated with persistent LDL-C elevation following ACS and evaluate predictors of successful LDL-C goal attainment among patients with severe baseline dyslipidemia. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that baseline lipid burden and longitudinal treatment patterns would be associated with LDL-C goal attainment following ACS. Methods: We performed a retrospective single-center study of patients admitted with STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina who underwent left heart catheterization at Loyola University Medical Center from 2022–2024. In an exploratory longitudinal analysis, patients with ≥3 follow-up lipid panels over 2 years were categorized as persistently uncontrolled if LDL-C remained >70 mg/dL on ≥50% of follow-up measurements. Baseline demographics, comorbidities, and lipid-lowering treatment patterns were compared. Given baseline LDL-C emerged as the dominant predictor of persistent LDL-C elevation, a focused analysis was subsequently performed among patients with baseline LDL-C >100 mg/dL and longitudinal lipid follow-up. Patients were stratified by latest LDL-C ≤70 mg/dL versus >70 mg/dL. Results: Among patients with ≥3 follow-up lipid panels, 33% remained persistently uncontrolled despite longitudinal management. Baseline LDL-C was the strongest predictor of persistent LDL-C elevation (102±28 vs 81±38 mg/dL, p=0.006), while comorbidities and rates of therapy intensification were similar between groups. In the severe dyslipidemia cohort (n=78), only 32 patients (41%) achieved LDL-C ≤70 mg/dL. Controlled patients demonstrated substantially greater LDL-C reduction at latest follow-up compared with uncontrolled patients (55%±9% vs 19%±29%, p<0.001), were more likely to remain on high-intensity statin therapy (78% vs 52%, p=0.034), and were less likely to undergo statin de-escalation or discontinuation (3% vs 20%, p=0.041). Rates of ezetimibe use, PCSK9 inhibitor use, and statin intensification were not significantly different between groups. Conclusion: Failure to achieve guideline-directed LDL-C goals after ACS remains common, particularly among patients with severe baseline dyslipidemia. Persistent LDL-C elevation appeared more strongly associated with baseline lipid burden and inability to sustain intensive lipid-lowering therapy than with differences in comorbidity burden or isolated treatment escalation events. These findings highlight ongoing challenges in longitudinal lipid optimization following ACS.
title: Abstract 18848: Persistent Challenges in Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Control Following Acute Coronary Syndrome Despite Longitudinal Lipid-Lowering Therapy

abstract: Background: Delta ECG age is a metric calculated by subtracting a patient's chronological age from the age estimated by a machine learning algorithm applied to the patient’s ECG. A positive delta ECG age has been associated with an increased risk of mortality, heart failure, and stroke. However, the factors associated with acute fluctuations in delta ECG age remain unknown. We investigated whether acute events leading to hospital admission are associated with acute changes in delta ECG age. Methods: This retrospective cohort study used the MIMIC-IV ECG-linked cohort, a de-identified single-center dataset of emergency department and ICU encounters in Boston, MA, from 2008-2022. ECG age was estimated using the Resnet-based CODE model. Delta ECG age was defined as the predicted ECG age minus the actual age at the time of the ECG. Delta-delta ECG age was defined as post-admission minus pre-admission delta ECG age, using the nearest ECG 7-365 days before admission and the ECG closest to 24 hours after admission within a ±12-hour window. We applied a linear age-bias correction to delta ECG age by regressing delta ECG age on actual age and subtracting the fitted age-dependent offset. Among admissions with a single incident diagnosis (HF, STEMI, hip fracture, or gastroenteritis), we compared delta-delta ECG age across diagnosis groups using one-way ANOVA and adjusted subject-level random-intercept mixed models with hip fracture as the reference group. Results: Among 9,927 admissions from 6,270 subjects, mean±SD delta-delta ECG age was -0.52±8.97 years for HF (n=9,176), 0.47±9.01 for STEMI (n=498), -0.23±9.86 for hip fracture (n=102), and -0.02±9.57 for gastroenteritis (n=151); corresponding bias-corrected values were -0.14±8.96, 0.81±9.01, 0.10±9.85, and 0.33±9.60. Diagnosis groups did not differ by ANOVA for raw (p=0.104) or bias-corrected (p=0.131) delta-delta ECG age. In adjusted mixed models versus hip fracture, HF was not associated with delta-delta ECG age in raw or bias-corrected analyses (raw and corrected β=-0.12 years, 95% CI -1.63 to 1.39) nor was STEMI (raw and corrected β=-0.28, 95% CI -1.92 to 1.37). Conclusion: In the MIMIC-IV ECG cohort, hospitalization for HF or STEMI was not associated with clinically meaningful acute shifts in ECG-age gap, and findings were unchanged after ECG-age bias correction. These results suggest that ECG-predicted age is relatively stable across selected acute illness states.
title: Abstract 18853: Acute Changes in Machine Learning Estimated ECG Age After Hospital Admission in the MIMIC-IV Cohort

abstract: Background: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on dialysis have higher risks of stroke/systemic embolism (SSE), major bleeding, and mortality. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) increases bleeding risk, while left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a non-pharmacologic alternative. Currently, there is limited and conflicting data. Methods: We systematically searched Embase, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through June 2026. Four observational cohorts comparing LAAO versus OAC in AF patients with advanced CKD (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m 2 ) or ESRD were identified. Three studies with extractable data (total N=2,747; LAAO n=480, OAC n=2,267) were included. The primary outcome was SSE; secondary outcomes were major bleeding and all-cause mortality. Outcome definitions varied modestly across studies. Risk ratios (RR) were pooled from raw event counts using a restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects model. Sensitivity analyses included fixed-effect models and pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HR). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I; robustness was evaluated by leave-one-out analysis. Results: A total of 2,747 patients were included (LAAO n=480, OAC n=2,267). The pooled population was dialysis-predominant. LAAO showed no significant difference in SSE compared with OAC (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.58-1.25, p=0.41, I 2 =0%). Major bleeding was numerically lower but not significant, with substantial heterogeneity (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.50-1.22, p=0.27, I 2 =74.6%; one study diverged). All-cause mortality was lower with LAAO in the primary analysis (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.97, p=0.016, I 2 =4.8%), but this finding was not significant in sensitivity analyses using adjusted HRs (e.g., 0.60, 95% CI: 0.33-1.10) and was sensitive to single-study exclusion in leave-one-out analysis. Conclusion: In our meta-analysis of observational studies, in patients with AF and advanced CKD or ESRD, LAAO was associated with stroke/systemic embolism rates comparable to OAC and a non-significant reduction in major bleeding. The apparent mortality advantage with LAAO was not robust to adjustment for confounding or single-study exclusion. The small number of available observational studies, modest overall sample size, and some heterogeneity in outcome definitions highlight the need for randomized controlled trials to define the role of LAAO in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 18869: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion versus Oral Anticoagulation for Stroke Prevention in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease or End-Stage Renal Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Patients with concurrent atrial fibrillation (AF) and malignancy face disproportionately elevated thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risks. Long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) is frequently contraindicated due to malignancy-related coagulopathy, visceral neoplasms, and chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) offers a non-pharmacological alternative, yet its safety and efficacy in this population remain insufficiently characterized. Research Question: We hypothesized that LAAO in patients with malignancy provides non-inferior stroke prevention and comparable bleeding outcomes relative to patients without malignancy, and that LAAO confers superior bleeding and survival outcomes compared to long-term OAC in this high-risk cohort. Methods: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Embase, and Scopus (inception through January 2026). Studies reporting LAAO outcomes in patients with active or historical malignancy were included. Primary outcomes were ischemic stroke, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality (malignancy vs. non-malignancy LAAO). Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and pericardial complications. Pooled hazard ratios (HR) and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Heterogeneity was quantified using I 2 . Results: Eighteen studies encompassing 5,058 patients with malignancy undergoing LAAO were included. Compared to non-malignancy LAAO patients, those with malignancy demonstrated comparable ischemic stroke risk (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.19–1.47, p=0.226, I 2 =0%) and major bleeding (HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.64–2.11, p=0.624, I 2 =0%). All-cause mortality was higher in the malignancy cohort (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09–2.08, p=0.013, I 2 =0%), attributable to underlying neoplastic progression. In-hospital mortality (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.01–2.45, p=0.044) and pericardial complications (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.40–2.54, p<0.001) were modestly elevated. Critically, propensity-matched analysis (N=1,228 pairs) demonstrated that LAAO reduced major bleeding by 20% (26.4% vs. 33.0%, p<0.001) and all-cause mortality by 37% (aHR 0.63, p<0.001) compared to OAC. Conclusion: LAAO provides effective stroke prevention in patients with malignancy-associated AF without increasing bleeding risk and demonstrates clear superiority over OAC with significant reductions in hemorrhage and mortality. These findings support LAAO as a first-line strategy in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 18881: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in Malignancy-Associated Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Patients with concomitant tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and heart failure (HF) represent a high-risk population with limited therapeutic options. Although tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has emerged as a less invasive treatment for severe TR, real-world outcomes in patients with coexisting HF remain poorly characterized. Research Questions: In patients with concomitant TR and HF, is T-TEER associated with improved 1-year and 3-year clinical outcomes, and do these associations differ by HF phenotype or acuity? Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, identifying adults with TR and HF between January 2020 and March 2026. Patients undergoing T-TEER were compared with those not undergoing T-TEER using 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). Analyses were stratified by HF phenotype (HFpEF and HFrEF) and acuity (chronic HF and acute-on-chronic HF). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality (ACM) or tricuspid valve surgery/reintervention. Secondary outcomes included ACM, HF exacerbation, acute kidney failure, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, RV dysfunction, all-cause hospitalization, and ischemic stroke. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses, and reported as adjusted hazard ratios (aHR). Results: Among 257,433 patients with TR and HF, 580 underwent T-TEER. After 1:1 PSM, 578 patients were included in each cohort (mean age: 78.9±11.3 years, women: 61.1%). Among matched patients, 39.4% had HFpEF, 8.7% had HFrEF, and the remainder had other or unspecified HF phenotypes; 22.1% had chronic HF and 72.1% had acute-on-chronic HF. At 1 year, T-TEER was associated with significantly lower risks of the primary composite endpoint (aHR 0.61 [0.46-0.81]), ACM (aHR 0.45 [0.32-0.61]), HF exacerbation (aHR 0.69 [0.57-0.84]), acute kidney failure (aHR 0.73 [0.59-0.92]), and all-cause hospitalization (aHR 0.70 [0.55-0.89]) compared with control (all p<0.05). Findings remained consistent at 3 years ( Figures 1-2) . Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent benefits of T-TEER in patients with acute-on-chronic HF, including reductions in the primary endpoint, ACM, HF exacerbation, acute kidney failure, major bleeding, and all-cause hospitalization. Similarly, among patients with HFpEF, T-TEER was associated with lower risks of the primary endpoint, ACM, HF exacerbation, and acute kidney failure. Analyses in HFrEF and chronic HF were underpowered. Conclusions: In a large, real-world cohort of patients with concomitant TR and HF, T-TEER was associated with a reduced risk of the primary composite endpoint, ACM, HF exacerbation, and acute kidney failure. These benefits extended to high-risk subgroups, including patients with HFpEF and acute-on-chronic HF, highlighting the therapeutic potential of T-TEER in this complex population.
title: Abstract 18885: Real World Outcomes of Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Patients with Tricuspid Regurgitation and Heart Failure

abstract: Introduction: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) is a rare laminopathy causing premature fibrocalcific cardiovascular disease with median survival of 14-15 years. Transcatheter valve experience in HGPS is essentially unreported, limited to isolated surgical valve replacements and a single transapical TAVR. Patient Information: A 25-year-old man with clinically diagnosed HGPS (non-diagnostic chromosomal microarray; LMNA sequencing not performed), on chronic rosuvastatin. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Progressive dyspnea decompensated into cardiogenic shock requiring intravenous milrinone. Examination revealed elevated JVP, harsh systolic ejection murmur radiating to carotids, holosystolic apical murmur, and bibasilar crackles. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: TEE showed severe calcific bicuspid AS (AVA 0.9 cm 2 ), moderate-to-severe AR, mixed MS with severe eccentric MR (bilateral PV systolic flow reversal), severe pulmonary hypertension (RVSP 95 mmHg), and LVEF 40%. The diffuse fibrocalcific phenotype at age 25 was attributed to accelerated valvular aging from HGPS rather than rheumatic or metabolic disease. CT showed annular area 350 mm 2 with asymmetric bicuspid calcification, prohibitive iliofemoral anatomy, and favorable left common carotid access. Therapeutic Intervention: Multidisciplinary heart team (structural cardiology, vascular surgery, cardiac anesthesia) supported urgent TAVR given young age and instability. A 20 mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 was selected over self-expanding Evolut to avoid coronary obstruction risk during anticipated future valve-in-valve TAVR. Transcarotid TAVR was performed via surgical left common carotid cutdown using a 14 Fr expandable sheath, deployed at +1 cc above nominal under rapid pacing without pre/post-dilation or cerebral embolic protection. Peak ACT 233 sec, reversed with protamine. Follow-up & Outcomes: Weaned from inotropes and discharged hospital day 6 on aspirin, sacubitril/valsartan, dapagliflozin, and furosemide. At 5 months, LVEF improved 40→54% and RVSP fell 95→40 mmHg. The prosthetic mean gradient rose 17→31 mmHg in proportion to flow recovery, consistent with flow-mediated rise rather than valve deterioration. Severe MR persisted, reflecting intrinsic fibrocalcific leaflet involvement rather than functional MR. Discussion & Synthesis: First reported transcarotid TAVR in HGPS. Three teaching points: (1) anatomy-guided transcarotid access enables structural intervention when iliofemoral anatomy is prohibitive; (2) lifetime valve management drives valve selection in young patients—supra-annular self-expanding designs may compromise future valve-in-valve coronary access; (3) post-TAVR gradient rise should be interpreted alongside flow recovery, as flow-mediated rise is more likely than early structural deterioration in this milieu.
title: Abstract 18918: Transcarotid TAVR for Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis in a 25-Year-Old with Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome: First Reported Case

abstract: Background: Frailty is a powerful predictor of adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and women undergoing TAVR have distinct baseline and procedural risk profiles. Whether sex modifies the association between frailty and in-hospital outcomes after TAVR remains unclear. Methods: We performed a cross-sectional, survey-weighted analysis of the National Inpatient Sample from 2016-2023. Adult hospitalizations undergoing isolated TAVR were identified using ICD-10-PCS codes, excluding concurrent open aortic valve replacement or coronary artery bypass grafting. Frailty was measured using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), analyzed continuously and categorically. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. Survey-weighted logistic regression tested the sex х HFRS interaction, adjusted for age, race, payer, income quartile, hospital region, teaching status, bed size, elective admission, and year. Additive interaction was assessed using marginally standardized risks. Results: The final cohort included 116,187 TAVR hospitalizations, representing approximately 580,935 national hospitalizations. Frailty was more common among women than men, with intermediate/high frailty present in 24.0% of women versus 21.2% of men. In adjusted models, each 1-point increase in HFRS was associated with higher mortality in both sexes, but the relative effect was modestly attenuated among women compared with men (sex х HFRS interaction OR, 0.956; 95% CI, 0.936-0.977). Using binary frailty, adjusted standardized mortality was 0.34% in non-frail men, 2.97% in frail men, 0.63% in non-frail women, and 3.27% in frail women. The absolute frailty-associated mortality increase was similar in men and women: 2.63% versus 2.64%, respectively, with no additive interaction detected (difference-in-differences, 0.01%; 95% CI, –0.45% to 0.48%; P=0.958). Among secondary outcomes, only acute kidney injury demonstrated a significant sex х HFRS interaction after false-discovery-rate adjustment. Conclusion: In this nationally representative TAVR cohort, frailty was strongly associated with in-hospital mortality in both sexes. Female sex modestly attenuated the relative frailty-mortality association, but the absolute mortality increase associated with frailty was nearly identical in women and men. These findings suggest that frailty carries clinically important prognostic value after TAVR regardless of sex, while emphasizing the importance of reporting interaction effects on both relative and absolute scales.
title: Abstract 18932: Sex Differences in Frailty Burden and Prognostic Impact After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2016-2023

abstract: Introduction/Background: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality despite effective preventive therapies. Although statins reduce cardiovascular risk, many patients who ultimately experience ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are not receiving appropriate primary prevention. The recently developed PREVENT risk equation was designed to provide a broader assessment of cardiovascular risk than the traditional Pooled Cohort Equation (PCE). This study compared PCE and PREVENT risk estimates among patients presenting with STEMI and evaluated missed opportunities for primary prevention. Research Question/Hypothesis: Among patients who ultimately experienced STEMI, would PREVENT identify more patients at elevated cardiovascular risk and eligible for primary prevention compared with PCE? It was hypothesized that PREVENT would identify a greater proportion of high-risk patients. Methods/Approach: A retrospective case series of 12 patients admitted with STEMI at a community teaching hospital was conducted. Demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, laboratory values, medication histories, and healthcare utilization data were obtained through chart review. PCE and PREVENT 10-year risk estimates were retrospectively calculated using pre-STEMI clinical data. Statin eligibility, statin use, and healthcare encounters within one year preceding STEMI were reviewed. Descriptive analyses compared risk estimates and treatment patterns. Results/Data: Mean age was 59 years. Mean PCE-estimated 10-year risk was 27.6% compared with 23.4% using PREVENT. Eleven patients (91.7%) met PCE-based statin eligibility criteria versus eight (66.7%) using PREVENT. Despite elevated cardiovascular risk, only six patients (50.0%) were receiving statin therapy before STEMI. Four patients (33.3%) had a documented missed opportunity for primary prevention. Patients averaged 3.5 healthcare encounters during the preceding year. Conclusion(s): PREVENT generated lower risk estimates and identified fewer statin-eligible patients than PCE despite all patients in this cohort subsequently experiencing STEMI. These findings suggest that PREVENT may reclassify some high-risk individuals into lower-risk categories, potentially reducing opportunities for preventive intervention. Furthermore, only 50% of eligible patients were receiving statin therapy before STEMI, underscoring persistent gaps in primary prevention. Larger studies including NSTEMI populations are needed to further evaluate PREVENT risk stratification and its impact on preventive treatment decisions.
title: Abstract 18938: Could We Have Prevented STEMI? A Real-World Comparison of PREVENT and Pooled Cohort Equation Risk Assessment for Primary Prevention

abstract: INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic Multicentric Castleman disease (iMCD) is a rare IL-6-driven lymphoproliferative disorder. During advanced heart failure (HF) evaluation, active iMCD can complicate transplant candidacy and defer durable LVAD implantation until disease control is achieved. PATIENT INFORMATION: A 34-year-old woman with presumed familial nonischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 15%) and chronic hypokalemia presented after out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest with serum potassium 1.6 mEq/L. CLINICAL FINDINGS AND TIMELINE: Milrinone was initiated and an intra-aortic balloon pump provided hemodynamic stability. An inherited cardiomyopathy panel returned no pathogenic variants. CT chest identified mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy (LAD), with bulky bilateral progression on repeat imaging three weeks later, coinciding with recurrent fevers. Infectious workup was unrevealing. Hematology-oncology was consulted and an excisional supraclavicular lymph node biopsy was performed. DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT: Lymph node biopsy showed Castleman-like germinal center regression, polytypic plasmacytosis, negative HHV-8, and no lymphoma. PET-CT confirmed diffuse hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy with splenomegaly and increased marrow uptake. IL-6 was elevated at 22 pg/mL (ref <6.4) and VEGF was normal, ruling out POEMS syndrome. Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow without a clonal B-cell process. iMCD was confirmed by consensus criteria, meeting both major and at least five minor criteria. THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION AND OUTCOMES: On milrinone, PCWP was 31 mmHg and cardiac index (CI) 1.7 L/min/m2. Despite the addition of dobutamine, PCWP was 36 mmHg, CI 2.84 L/min/m2, and SvO2 45.7%. Hematology-oncology recommended corticosteroids and siltuximab. Active iMCD limited transplant consideration or durable LVAD placement given malignancy risk under immunosuppression. The patient was transferred 18 days after the first siltuximab dose on continuous milrinone, with goals-of-care discussions ongoing. DISCUSSION: Lymphoproliferative disease found during advanced HF evaluation can require systemic therapy while limiting advanced therapies. The absence of a confirmed pathogenic variant and pre-treatment IL-6 elevation leaves open the question of cytokine-mediated myocardial dysfunction. While iMCD is not an absolute contraindication to solid organ transplantation, active disease raises concern for malignant transformation under immunosuppression, complicating candidacy in this setting. In young patients with advanced HF and unexplained lymphadenopathy or fever, evaluation for lymphoproliferative disease may inform advanced therapy eligibility and guide goals-of-care discussions.
title: Abstract 18940: Idiopathic Multicentric Castleman Disease as a Barrier to Advanced Heart Failure Therapy in a Young Woman

abstract: Background: Depression is a common but frequently under-recognized comorbidity after myocardial infarction (MI) and is associated with poor recovery, reduced treatment adherence, recurrent cardiovascular events, and increased mortality. Early identification of depression in post-MI patients may improve both psychological and cardiovascular outcomes. Objective: To determine the prevalence of depression among patients with myocardial infarction and evaluate its association with selected cardiovascular risk factors. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore, over six months. A total of 302 patients diagnosed with MI were enrolled using non-probability consecutive sampling. Patients with a prior history of depression, advanced heart failure, chronic kidney disease, active malignancy, or planned coronary artery bypass grafting were excluded. Depression was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8), with a score of ≥10 considered clinically significant. Demographic data and cardiovascular risk factors, including smoking, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia, were recorded. Associations between depression and clinical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test, with p≤0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: The mean age of participants was 52.8±5.2 years, and 196 patients (64.9%) were male. STEMI was present in 178 patients (58.9%), while 124 patients (41.1%) had NSTEMI. Overall, depression was identified in 70 patients, giving a prevalence of 23.2%. Depression was significantly more frequent among smokers compared with non-smokers (47.0% vs. 16.2%, p<0.001), patients with diabetes compared with those without diabetes (53.6% vs. 16.2%, p<0.001), and patients with hyperlipidemia compared with those without hyperlipidemia (33.3% vs. 18.8%, p=0.006). No statistically significant association was observed between depression and gender or age group. Conclusion: Nearly one-quarter of patients with myocardial infarction had clinically significant depression. Smoking, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia were significantly associated with depression in this population. These findings support routine depression screening in post-MI patients, particularly among those with cardiovascular risk factors, to enable early intervention and improve long-term patient outcomes.
title: Abstract 18944: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Depression Among Patients with Myocardial Infarction: A Cross-Sectional Study

abstract: Background: Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is performed in contemporary practice, yet whether in-hospital outcomes associated with combined PCI-TAVR differed before versus during the COVID-19 pandemic is incompletely understood. Methods: Using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (2018-2022), we identified 76,026 adult TAVR hospitalizations, including 25,681 pre-COVID (2018-2019) and 50,345 during the COVID era (2020-2022). Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations between concomitant PCI and in-hospital mortality and complications, adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, hospital characteristics, and calendar year. Length of stay (LOS) and total hospitalization charges were analyzed using linear regression, with log-transformed charges. Results: Among 76,026 TAVR hospitalizations (pre-COVID n=25,681; COVID era n=50,345; PCI 3% vs 2.4%), concomitant PCI was associated with higher in-hospital mortality both pre-COVID (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.98, 95% CI 1.16-3.39) and during the COVID era (aOR 2.95, 95% CI 2.01-4.35). PCI was also associated with higher odds of major complications in both periods, including acute kidney injury (pre-COVID aOR 2.09; COVID aOR 2.17), cardiogenic shock (3.02 vs 2.90), mechanical ventilation (1.98 vs 2.13), cardiac arrest (2.55 vs 2.92), and bleeding (1.66 vs 1.76). Stroke was not significantly associated with PCI in either era.Concomitant PCI was associated with longer LOS, while COVID-era hospitalization itself was not. Total hospitalization charges were higher with PCI (55%) and during the COVID era (32%), reflecting greater resource utilization during pandemic-era admissions. Conclusions: Concomitant PCI during TAVR was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, morbidity, and resource utilization both before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, with a more pronounced mortality association during the COVID era. Higher hospitalization charges associated with concomitant PCI and COVID-era admissions underscore the importance of thoughtful procedural planning when considering combined PCI-TAVR strategies during periods of healthcare system disruption.
title: Abstract 18945: In-Hospital Outcomes of Concomitant PCI During TAVR Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Nationwide Analysis

abstract: Background: Recovery and progression following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) with left ventricular dysfunction are heterogeneous, and environmental exposures may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk. Air pollution is an increasingly recognized contributor to adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but its impact among patients with ACS and left ventricular dysfunction remains poorly understood. We evaluated the association between ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure and all-cause mortality following ACS. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with ACS in the Myocardial Infarction Registry who had available PM2.5 exposure data. Annual ambient PM2.5 exposure was assigned using tract-level estimates and analyzed by quartiles and as a continuous variable. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between PM2.5 exposure and mortality after adjustment for demographic, clinical, and treatment factors. We also tested whether the association differed between STEMI and non-STEMI. Results: Among 1,266 patients with available PM2.5 data, the mean age was 67.3 ± 13.6 years, 36.6% were female, and 24.5% were Black. Over a mean follow-up of 3.2 ± 2.6 years, 322 deaths occurred (25.4%). Median PM2.5 exposure was 9.18 μg/m 3 , with an interquartile range of 7.97 to 9.64 μg/m 3 . Mortality rates across PM2.5 quartiles were 21.5%, 28.4%, 26.3%, and 25.6% from Q1 to Q4, respectively. In unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis, survival differed numerically across PM2.5 quartiles, although the log-rank test was not statistically significant (p=0.152). After multivariable adjustment, higher PM2.5 exposure was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality. For every 1 μg/m 3 increase in PM2.5 exposure, mortality risk increased by 17% (HR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.04-1.32, p=0.009). Similarly, each interquartile range increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 30% higher mortality risk (HR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.07-1.59, p=0.009). When analyzed by quartiles, patients in the highest exposure quartile had a significantly greater risk of mortality compared with the lowest quartile (HR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.09-2.18, p=0.013). There was no significant interaction by acute coronary syndrome subtype (p-interaction=0.768). Conclusions: In this cohort of patients with ACS, higher ambient PM2.5 exposure was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality after adjustment for demographic, clinical, and treatment factors. The association did not significantly differ between ST-elevation myocardial infarction and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. These findings suggest that ambient particulate exposure may represent an important environmental determinant of long-term mortality following ACS with left ventricular dysfunction.
title: Abstract 18983: Ambient PM2.5 Exposure and Mortality Following Acute Coronary Syndrome with Left Ventricular Dysfunction

abstract: Background: Pregnancy associated spontaneous coronary artery dissection (P-SCAD) represents a high risk SCAD phenotype and poses unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges when recurrent ischemia occurs during pregnancy. Case: A 31 year old woman at 33 weeks gestation presented with chest pain, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and 2 mm ST segment elevations in V2-V3 concerning for myocardial infarction. Given her demographic profile, absence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and bedside echocardiogram findings, spontaneous coronary artery dissection was suspected and initial management was conservative. Five days later, she developed recurrent chest pain with dynamic anterior ST segment elevations and anterior wall motion abnormalities, raising concern for early extension of presumed P-SCAD. Following multidisciplinary discussion among cardiology, maternal fetal medicine, and interventional cardiology, coronary angiography was performed. The left anterior descending artery demonstrated severe diffuse narrowing with an atretic appearance and no evidence of thrombus, concerning for Type 2 SCAD. Given preserved hemodynamics and the known risks of coronary intervention in SCAD, conservative management with aspirin and beta blockade was pursued. Expert SCAD consultation supported continued conservative management and close monitoring. The patient subsequently underwent successful delivery of a healthy infant without maternal cardiovascular complications. Follow up coronary CTA demonstrated persistent but stable diffuse narrowing of the left anterior descending artery. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function with improving apical wall motion abnormalities and no left ventricular thrombus. Conclusion: This case highlights the challenges of diagnosing and managing recurrent ischemia occurring five days after presumed pregnancy associated Type 2 SCAD. Multidisciplinary collaboration, multimodality imaging, and careful patient selection allowed successful conservative management through delivery despite concern for early SCAD extension.
title: Abstract 19012: Recurrent Ischemia in Late Pregnancy: Multidisciplinary Management of Mid to Distal LAD Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

abstract: Background: Current guidelines recommend dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients not requiring oral anticoagulation despite limited TAVR-specific evidence. Prior randomized trials suggest increased bleeding with DAPT without clear reductions in ischemic events but did not evaluate clopidogrel monotherapy and were underpowered for mortality. Given the advanced age and high comorbidity burden of TAVR recipients, optimizing antiplatelet therapy is particularly important. We compared clopidogrel monotherapy versus DAPT following TAVR in a large real-world cohort. Hypothesis We hypothesized that aspirin adds net harm rather than benefit after TAVR and that clopidogrel monotherapy provides sufficient ischemic protection. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (174 healthcare organizations). Adults undergoing TAVR and prescribed clopidogrel within six months were stratified into clopidogrel monotherapy (no-DAPT; no aspirin or oral anticoagulation) or DAPT (aspirin plus clopidogrel; no oral anticoagulation). Patients on oral anticoagulants were excluded. Baseline cohort sizes were 4,058 (no-DAPT) and 36,275 (DAPT). After 1:1 propensity score matching using demographics and comorbidities, two balanced cohorts of 4,058 patients each were analysed. Outcomes were assessed 180-365 days post-TAVR. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and stroke; secondary outcomes were major bleeding and myocardial infarction. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Results: After propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were balanced between cohorts. All-cause mortality was significantly lower with no-DAPT than DAPT (3.3% vs. 4.7%; RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.87; p=0.001), with consistent findings on time to event analysis (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.93; log-rank p=0.009). Stroke rates were similar between groups (1.1% vs. 1.0%; HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.70-1.76; p=0.655). Major bleeding was numerically lower with no-DAPT but did not reach significance (2.0% vs. 2.3%; HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64-1.27; p=0.561). Myocardial infarction rates were also comparable (1.5% vs. 1.2%; HR 1.25, 95% CI 0.81-1.91; p=0.310). Conclusions: In this large propensity score-matched real-world analysis of over 8,000 TAVR recipients, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a 26% relative reduction in all-cause mortality compared with DAPT during the 6-12 month post-procedural period, without increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, or major bleeding. These findings challenge the routine use of DAPT after TAVR in patients not requiring anticoagulation and suggest limited additional benefit from aspirin.
