Our results support reassessment of post-TAVR antiplatelet strategies and the potential role of clopidogrel monotherapy as a safer alternative.

abstract: Background: Catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy with the Inari FlowTriever system has seen rapid adoption for intermediate- and high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE), yet comparative real-world data against medical anticoagulation remains limited. Whether Inari thrombectomy has a mortality advantage - and how composite endpoints capture that benefit - is unclear in large real-world cohorts. We compared 30-day mortality, a morbidity composite, and bleeding outcomes between Inari thrombectomy and medical anticoagulation in a large national database. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (January 2021-December 2024). Patients with PE undergoing Inari FlowTriever thrombectomy (n=2,642 pre-match) were compared to those receiving medical anticoagulation alone (n=300,101 pre-match). Propensity score matching (PSM; 1:1 nearest-neighbor, 47 covariates, caliper 0.10) yielded 2,523-2,803 matched pairs per arm. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were: (1) a 30-day composite of death, cardiac arrest, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor use; and (2) 30-day bleeding complications (Day 0-7). Results: After PSM, Inari thrombectomy was associated with significantly lower 30-day all-cause mortality versus medical anticoagulation (2.4% vs. 3.7%; OR 0.647, 95% CI 0.466-0.898; p=0.009). Kaplan-Meier survival at 30 days was 97.6% (Inari) versus 96.2% (anticoagulation); HR 0.637, 95% CI 0.461-0.879; log-rank p=0.006. For the secondary composite endpoint, anticoagulation was favored (22.7% vs. 35.9%; OR 1.904, 95% CI 1.694-2.142; p<0.0001), driven by higher peri-procedural mechanical ventilation and vasopressor use in the Inari arm rather than excess mortality. Bleeding complications were also significantly more frequent with Inari thrombectomy (14.9% vs. 11.1%; OR 1.404, 95% CI 1.190-1.657; p<0.0001). Conclusions: In this large propensity-matched real-world analysis, Inari FlowTriever thrombectomy was associated with a significant reduction in 30-day mortality versus medical anticoagulation in PE patients, despite higher peri-procedural composite event and bleeding rates. Composite endpoints inclusive of vasopressor and ventilator use may obscure the true mortality benefit of Inari thrombectomy by capturing expected procedural intensity rather than true harm. Mortality should be prioritized as the primary endpoint in future comparative PE trials.
title: Abstract 19049: 30-Day Outcomes of Inari FlowTriever Thrombectomy versus Medical Anticoagulation in Pulmonary Embolism: A Real-World Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Patients with active malignancy undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) represent a complex population with competing high bleeding and prothrombotic risks. Because patients with malignancy are systematically excluded from most antiplatelet trials, the optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remains uncertain. Research Question: Is short-duration DAPT (1 to 3 months) associated with reduced major bleeding without increased ischemic events compared to standard-duration DAPT (6 to 12 months) in patients with active malignancy undergoing PCI? Methods: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis searching PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception through January 2026. Studies reporting clinical outcomes in patients with malignancy undergoing PCI were included. The analysis was structured in two parts: Part A compared outcomes between patients with and without malignancy to establish baseline risk, and Part B compared short-duration DAPT (1 to 3 months) versus standard-duration DAPT (6 to 12 months) specifically within malignancy and high-bleeding risk (HBR) cohorts. Overlapping registries were rigorously excluded. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models were used to calculate pooled hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Fifteen non-overlapping primary studies were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. Results: From 2,847 screened records, 15 non-overlapping primary studies comprising over 500,000 patients were included in the quantitative synthesis. In Part A, compared with patients without malignancy, those with active malignancy experienced significantly higher all-cause mortality (HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.72–2.38; p<0.001; I 2 =78.0%), major bleeding (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.40–1.66; p<0.001; I 2 =0.0%), and stent thrombosis (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.01–2.49; p=0.047; I 2 =35.1%). In Part B, short-duration DAPT (1 to 3 months) was compared to standard-duration DAPT (6 to 12 months) in malignancy/HBR cohorts. Short DAPT was associated with a significant 22% reduction in major bleeding (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.69–0.89; p=0.0002; I 2 =21.5%) with no significant increase in ischemic events or myocardial infarction (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.87–1.06; p=0.43; I 2 =0.0%). Conclusions: Patients with active malignancy undergoing PCI face a two-fold increase in mortality and a 50% higher risk of major bleeding compared to patients without malignancy. In this high-risk population, an abbreviated DAPT strategy of 1 to 3 months significantly mitigates bleeding risk compared to standard 6-to-12-month DAPT without incurring an ischemic penalty. These findings strongly support the routine adoption of de-escalated antithrombotic therapy in cardio-oncology patients following PCI.
title: Abstract 19075: Less is More: Short Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After PCI in Patients with Active Malignancy — A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Coronary septic embolization is a rare complication of infective endocarditis. We present a case of Gemella morbillorum endocarditis with vegetation embolization to the LAD, requiring double-valve surgery and revascularization via CABG. Patient Information: A 65-year-old male with a history of alcohol use disorder presented to his PCP with several months of unintentional weight loss, dysphagia, palpitations and back pain. Clinical Findings and Diagnostic Assessment: Labs showed elevated inflammatory markers and moderately elevated troponin. He subsequently underwent a TTE which showed LVEF 60-65%, severe aortic regurgitation with a mobile aortic valve mass, and severe mitral regurgitation. Multiple blood cultures grew Gemella morbillorum. TEE confirmed a 1.8 х 0.8 cm aortic vegetation with severe aortic regurgitation and a 1.0 х 0.7 cm mitral vegetation with chordal rupture and severe mitral regurgitation. Coronary angiography showed a large filling defect in the mid-LAD with TIMI 3 flow and no obstructive coronary disease, concerning for septic embolization. A post-angiogram TEE did not demonstrate any new wall motion abnormalities, favoring stable embolization over plaque rupture. Therapeutic Interventions: Subsequently he underwent bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement and CABG with saphenous vein to the LAD. The postoperative course was complicated by reduced LVEF of 30%, necessitating an intra-aortic balloon pump. He was initiated on antiplatelet therapy and ceftriaxone. Follow-up, Outcomes and Adverse Events: Subsequent TEE post-op showed normally functioning aortic and mitral bioprostheses, yet persistently reduced LVEF, requiring initiation of heart-failure GDMT. His course was further complicated by recurrent atrial fibrillation, failure to thrive, and poor intake requiring PEG placement. He was discharged with planned rehabilitation, amiodarone taper and a six-week course of IV ceftriaxone. Conclusion: Coronary septic embolization may mimic ACS but presents unique challenges. Unlike obstructive CAD, PCI and stent placement are generally avoided because of the risk of infection and seeding. Although preserved flow as seen in this patient is typically favorable in obstructive CAD, septic emboli carry additional risks of sudden coronary occlusion and ongoing infectious injury. Multimodality imaging, microbiologic identification, and multidisciplinary collaboration were critical for diagnosis and management. Prompt double-valve replacement, coronary artery bypass grafting, and prolonged antimicrobial therapy achieved source control and clinical stabilization. This case underscores coronary embolization as a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of left-sided infective endocarditis.
title: Abstract 19088: From Valve to Vessel- Suspected Left Anterior Descending Coronary Artery Septic Embolization in Gemella morbillorum Endocarditis

abstract: Background : Right heart catheterization (RHC) and pulmonary artery catheterization (PAC) are commonly used management of cardiogenic shock (CS). However, their value when mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is initiated remained uncertain. Prior randomized trials such as ESCAPE and PAC-Man showed no mortality benefit in PAC-guided management, but patients requiring MCS were largely excluded. We hypothesized that peri-MCS RHC/PAC is associated with improved survival outcomes and fewer major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) . Methods: Using TriNetX, a federated electronic health record network of 110 U.S. health care organizations, we identified adults ≥18 years old hospitalized with CS who underwent MCS with a microaxial flow pump or VA-ECMO between 2018 and 2025. The exposure was RHC/PAC use within 3 days of MCS initiation. Exclusion criteria include prior heart transplantation or pre-existing durable LVAD. Patients were propensity-score-matched (PSM) 1:1 using demographics, comorbidities, vasopressor or inotrope use, and biomarkers reflecting illness severity. Post-match balance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models at 30 days and 1 year after MCS initiation (index date). A pre-specified non-AMI CS subgroup excludes patients with acute myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization before the index event. Results: Among 8,552 matched pairs cohorts were were well balanced by mean age 63.6±13.6 versus 63.6±14.2 years, and other demographic information, comorbidities, and vasoactive medication use (SMDs <0.10) but lactate, BNP, and NT-proBNP remained higher in the RHC/PAC arm (each SMD 0.12), suggesting residual illness severity differences. At 1 year, peri-MCS RHC/PAC was associated with higher risk of ACM (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.22, 95% CI 1.16-1.28; p<0.001) and higher risk of MACE (aHR 1.28, 95% CI 1.23-1.33; p<0.001). Concordant results found at 30-day time point (ACM HR 1.28, 1.21-1.35; MACE HR 1.31, 1.25-1.36; both p<0.001). Subgroup analysis in the non-AMI cohort (1,775 matched pairs, 1-year mortality was no longer significant, aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.90-1.12; p=0.96, although MACE remained higher, aHR 1.43, 95% CI 1.28-1.60; p<0.001. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched real-world analysis, peri-MCS RHC/PAC was associated with higher 1-year mortality and MACE in the overall MCS-supported CS cohort, contrary to our hypothesis. Persistent post-match differences in biomarkers representing disease severity may indicate selection of sicker patients rather than procedural harm. The non-significant mortality difference in the non-AMI CS subgroup utility of invasive hemodynamic assessment may differ by CS phenotype. These findings should be viewed as hypothesis-generating and support prospective studies or further analysis with variables like SCAI staging are needed

title: Abstract 19092: Peri-MCS Invasive Hemodynamic Assessment and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Pacing after recent bioprosthetic tricuspid valve replacement poses unique challenges. Ideally, patients receive permanent epicardial pacing wires at the time of surgery, to be connected with permanent pacing devices if the heart block proves to be persistent. Transvenous pacing with a coronary sinus lead is also a feasible solution; however, transvenous wires may be contraindicated in certain patients. Paroxysmal atrial arrhythmias are very common after cardiac surgery, due to the inflammatory milieu, and usually managed conservatively. Rarely, atrial flutter can be refractory, fail antiarrhythmic therapy and repeated cardioversion, and a more permanent solution becomes necessary. Case: A 33-year-old man with ESRD on peritoneal dialysis and severe tricuspid regurgitation secondary to infective endocarditis underwent sternotomy with debulking of the tricuspid annulus and bioprosthetic tricuspid valve replacement. His postoperative course was complicated by transient heart block and recurrent rapid atrial flutter, refractory despite amiodarone loading and repeated cardioversion. Atrial flutter was associated with significant hemodynamic instability, and long post-conversion pauses with syncope when flutter terminated. After multidisciplinary discussions between electrophysiology, cardiac critical care, and cardiac surgery, we proceeded with flutter ablation and placement of a leadless ventricular pacemaker (MICRA AV) for backup pacing. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) was used to identify the tricuspid valve suture ring and avoid catheter placement on the suture line. Entrainment maneuvers demonstrated typical counterclockwise cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI)-dependent flutter, which slowed and terminated during ablation. Pacing on each side confirmed bidirectional block. With ICE guidance, a MICRA AV was advanced without interaction across the new tricuspid valve to the mid septum, achieving favorable pacing morphology with QRS complexes positive in inferior leads, similar to physiologic pacing. Discussion/Conclusion: This case highlights a paradigm shift in the management of patients who may require transient ventricular pacing after recent tricuspid valve surgery. While leadless pacemakers were previously contraindicated in this situation and were thought to carry a high-risk of valve injury, we demonstrate how the use of high-resolution ICE can guide safe and effective leadless pacemaker deployment through the new valve and achieve a favorable pacing morphology. Furthermore, while CTI ablation is generally avoided after a recent tricuspid valve surgery, in this case it was very poorly tolerated hemodynamically and there was no other alternative but ablation. We demonstrate how ablation can be safely performed when guided by intracardiac echocardiography.
title: Abstract 19128: Intracardiac Echocardiography-Guided Leadless Pacemaker Implantation and Cavo-Tricuspid Isthmus Ablation Across a Recently Implanted Bioprosthetic Tricuspid Valve

abstract: Background: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is being rapidly adopted for atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Theoretical concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) between PFA energy and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) have led to cautious adoption in this population, but real-world safety data remain limited. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with a pre-existing CIED who underwent PFA-based AF ablation between June 2024 and December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically significant EMI, defined as intraoperative lead dislodgement requiring procedural intervention. Secondary outcomes included acute lead noise on day-of device interrogation and subsequent noise within 30 days. Peri-procedural safety outcomes were captured per institutional protocol. Results: 123 patients were included (mean age 73.1 ± 8.9 years; 69.1% male; CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc median 4 [IQR 3-5]; prior catheter ablation 40.7%). CIED types: PPM 65.0%, ICD 19.5%, CRT-D 10.6%, CRT-P 3.3%, ILR 1.6%. The Medtronic Affera system was used in 74.8% and Boston Scientific FaraPulse in 19.5%. Pulmonary vein isolation was performed in 96.7%; concomitant LAAO in 34.1%. Clinically significant EMI occurred in 2 patients (1.6%), both atrial-lead dislodgements requiring extraction/reimplantation. Day-of device interrogation was documented in 81 patients (65.9%); acute lead noise was identified in 16/81 (19.8%). Among 76 with follow-up interrogation, subsequent noise occurred in 5 (6.6%). No patient with transient noise required device revision. No intraoperative ST elevation, coronary vasospasm, or ventricular arrhythmias occurred. Peri-operative stroke/TIA occurred in 2 (1.6%); vascular complications in 4 (3.3%). Median length of stay was 1 day [IQR 1-1]; same-day discharge 23.6%. There were no in-hospital deaths. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort of CIED patients undergoing PFA-based AF ablation, clinically significant EMI was infrequent (1.6%) and no patient suffered a fatal or unrecoverable device complication. Although acute lead noise was identified in approximately one-fifth of patients with day-of interrogation, these findings were largely transient and did not mandate device revision. PFA appears safe in this population; systematic peri-procedural device interrogation remains warranted.
title: Abstract 19137: Safety of Pulsed Field Ablation in Patients with Pre-Existing Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices: A Single-Center Real-World Experience

abstract: Background: Optimal anticoagulation for intracardiac thrombus (ICT) remains uncertain. Warfarin has been standard therapy, yet DOACs are increasingly used off-label despite limited randomized evidence. Prior studies were underpowered or conflicting; whether findings persist in a larger cohort is unknown. Hypothesis: DOAC therapy is associated with comparable or improved thromboembolic and safety outcomes versus warfarin. Methods: We performed a retrospective propensity score-matched analysis using TriNetX. Adults with ICT (ICD-10 I51.3) identified in temporal association with transthoracic echocardiography (CPT 93306-93308) and treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin were included. Matching balanced demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, heart failure severity, prior MI, cardiogenic shock, atrial fibrillation, prosthetic valves, cirrhosis, CKD, antiplatelet therapy, and guideline-directed medical therapy (all standardized mean differences <0.1). The primary outcome was persistent or recurrent thrombus between 90-180 days. Secondary outcomes through 365 days included ischemic stroke, TIA, arterial embolism, GI bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, all-cause mortality, and acute MI. Results: After matching, 10,684 patients remained per cohort. DOACs were associated with lower rates of persistent/recurrent thrombus (18.5% vs. 24.2%; HR 0.789, 95% CI 0.744-0.836; p<0.001), arterial embolism (2.0% vs. 3.0%; HR 0.706, 95% CI 0.588-0.846; p<0.001), GI bleeding (3.8% vs. 4.8%; HR 0.854, 95% CI 0.744-0.982; p=0.026), acute MI (8.1% vs. 11.9%; HR 0.708, 95% CI 0.629-0.797; p<0.001), and intracranial hemorrhage (0.9% vs. 1.4%; HR 0.671, 95% CI 0.515-0.875; p=0.003). Ischemic stroke (3.4% vs. 3.6%; HR 1.031; p=0.717) and TIA (1.1% vs. 1.3%; HR 0.914; p=0.920) were similar. Cumulative mortality was similar (17.4% vs. 17.1%; RR 1.016; p=0.608), although time-to-event analysis favored warfarin (HR 1.101, 95% CI 1.032-1.175; p=0.009). Conclusions: In this large propensity score-matched real-world analysis, DOAC therapy was associated with lower rates of persistent or recurrent ICT, arterial embolism, gastrointestinal bleeding, acute MI, and intracranial hemorrhage compared with warfarin, while rates of ischemic stroke and TIA were similar. Although cumulative mortality risk was comparable, time-to-event analysis demonstrated a modest difference favoring warfarin, highlighting the need for prospective validation. Given the observational design and reliance on documented outcomes, these findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal. Nevertheless, the favorable thrombotic and bleeding profile associated with DOAC therapy supports consideration of DOACs as an alternative to warfarin for ICT and provides a foundation for future randomized trials and guideline development.
title: Abstract 19139: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Direct Oral Anticoagulants versus Warfarin for Intracardiac Thrombus: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis of 21,368 Patients

abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but potentially fatal complication of cancer immunotherapy. Diagnosis can be challenging when presentation mimics acute coronary syndrome (ACS), particularly in patients with marked troponin elevation and ischemic electrocardiographic changes. Case Presentation: A 73-year-old woman with metastatic renal cell carcinoma receiving lenvatinib and pembrolizumab presented with acute chest pain. Electrocardiogram demonstrated lateral ST-segment elevations and T-wave inversions. High-sensitivity troponin I was 13,600ng/L on presentation and increased to > 125,000ng/L within 12 hours; high-sensitivity troponin T measured 2,430ng/L. Creatine phosphokinase was 354U/L. She was treated for suspected ACS and underwent emergent coronary angiography, which demonstrated non-obstructive coronary disease. Recurrent chest pain prompted repeat angiography with unchanged findings. Persistently rising biomarkers despite two negative angiograms raised concern for anon-ischemic etiology. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 44%), extensive non-ischemic late gadolinium enhancement, and myocardial edema, consistent with ICI-associated myocarditis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and BNP increased from 53 to 645pg/mL. High-dose intravenous corticosteroids were initiated; however, troponin continued to rise, prompting escalation to abatacept therapy. Biomarkers subsequently stabilized, and high-sensitivity troponin I normalized. Following recovery from myocarditis and heart failure, repeat imaging demonstrated a profound oncologic response, allowing the patient to become a surgical candidate. Discussion: This case highlights the diagnostic value of troponin kinetics inpatients receiving ICI therapy. Extreme and progressive biomarker elevation (>125,000ng/L) despite recurrent ischemic symptoms and two negative coronary angiograms prompted evaluation for myocarditis, which was confirmed by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Persistent biomarker elevation despite high-dose corticosteroids identified steroid-refractory disease and supported escalation to abatacept. Integration of serial biomarker assessment with advanced imaging was critical for establishing the diagnosis, guiding immunosuppressive therapy, and avoiding additional unnecessary invasive ischemic evaluation. Conclusion: In oncology patients with persistent troponin elevation and non-obstructive coronary arteries, ICI-associated myocarditis should remain a key diagnostic consideration. Early recognition using troponin kinetics and multimodality imaging may improve diagnostic accuracy, expedite initiation of life-saving immunosuppressive therapy, and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.
title: Abstract 19141: Troponin Kinetics Unmask Steroid-Refractory Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis Presenting as STEMI

abstract: Background: Surgical myectomy and alcohol septal ablation (PTSMA) are the principal septal reduction therapies for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), yet contemporary head-to-head outcome data remain limited, particularly for conduction-related complications. Methods: Within the TriNetX federated network (110 healthcare organizations), adults (≥18 yr) with oHCM (ICD-10 I42.1) undergoing surgical myectomy were compared with those undergoing alcohol septal ablation (PTSMA). The index event was the procedure date. To limit indication bias, cohorts were 1:1 propensity-score matched on approximately 40 variables spanning demographics, comorbidities, procedures, medications, and laboratory values. Three-year outcomes (1-1095 days) were evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis: all-cause mortality, atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), an atrioventricular block (AVB) composite, MACCE, cardiogenic shock, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Hazard ratios (HR) are expressed for myectomy relative to PTSMA. Results: After matching, 575 patients per arm were analyzed. Three-year all-cause mortality was similar between myectomy and PTSMA (HR 1.06; 95% CI 0.70-1.62). Myectomy was associated with a significantly lower risk of permanent pacemaker implantation (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.48-0.85; p=0.002) and the AVB composite (HR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.79; p=0.001), and a nonsignificant trend toward lower MACCE (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.50-1.06). AF (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.52-1.18), HF (HR 1.36; 95% CI 0.85-2.17), and cardiogenic shock (HR 1.16; 95% CI 0.52-2.58) did not differ significantly. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched real-world analysis, myectomy and PTSMA yielded comparable 3-year survival, but myectomy was associated with significantly fewer atrioventricular conduction events, including a lower rate of permanent pacemaker implantation. These data reinforce conduction risk as a key differentiator between septal reduction strategies and support individualized therapy selection. Prospective confirmation is warranted.
title: Abstract 19142: Surgical Myectomy versus Alcohol Septal Ablation in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Propensity-Matched Comparison of Long-Term Outcomes

abstract: Background: The Amulet and Watchman platforms are the two dominant LAAO devices used in concomitant ablation + LAAO procedures, yet head-to-head procedural comparisons in this specific setting are lacking. Methods: We retrospectively compared patients undergoing concomitant CA + LAAO with the Amulet (n=59) vs. Watchman FLX/FLX Pro (n=46) at a single center. Lariat cases (n=6) were excluded from this analysis. Co-primary endpoints were implant success and PASS criteria achievement. Secondary safety endpoints included pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, and periprocedural stroke/TIA. Results: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups (Amulet vs. Watchman: age 74.7 ± 7.5 vs. 74.6 ± 7.9 years; CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc 4.3 ± 1.6 vs. 4.1 ± 1.6). Implant success was 93.2% (55/59) for Amulet vs. 95.7% (44/46) for Watchman (p=NS). PASS criteria were met in 93.2% vs. 95.7% respectively (p=NS). No residual intraprocedural leak was detected in either group. Pericardial effusion occurred in 10.2% (6/59) Amulet vs. 15.2% (7/46) Watchman patients (p=NS). Cardiac tamponade occurred in 0% vs. 2.2% (0 vs. 1 patient; p=NS). Periprocedural stroke/TIA was seen in 1.7% (1/59) Amulet vs. 4.3% (2/46) Watchman patients (p=NS). Prior stroke/TIA was more prevalent in the Amulet group (29% vs. 13%, p=0.05), which may reflect operator selection bias toward Amulet in higher-risk patients. Conclusions: In the concomitant CA + LAAO setting, both Amulet and Watchman platforms demonstrate comparable implant success and periprocedural safety profiles. No statistically significant differences were observed in major outcomes. Larger multicenter data are needed to confirm these findings and elucidate any device-specific advantages in this combined procedural context.
title: Abstract 19172: Amulet vs. Watchman FLX/FLX Pro in Concomitant Catheter Ablation and LAAO — A Device Comparison

abstract: Background: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) can require advanced cardiac care not available at all delivery hospitals, necessitating interhospital transfer. Whether transferred patients experience different in-hospital outcomes reflecting appropriate regionalization or residual excess risk has not been characterized nationally. Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample 2016-2023, we identified hospitalizations with PPCM (ICD-10-CM O90.3, any of DX1-DX40) and flagged interhospital transfer-in (ATYPE=2) and transfer-out (DISPUNIFORM=2). Survey-weighted (DISCWT) multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for All-Patient-Refined DRG (APR-DRG) illness-severity and mortality-risk subclass, age, payer, income quartile, hospital characteristics, and comorbidities, compared transfer-in with non-transfer PPCM admissions on in-hospital mortality (primary), cardiogenic shock, mechanical circulatory support (MCS), and mechanical ventilation. Cells <11 were suppressed. Results: Among 7,288 PPCM hospitalizations (weighted N ≈ 36,440), 946 (13.0%) were transfer-in and 329 (4.5%) were transfer-out. Transfer-in patients had higher acuity: cardiogenic shock (18.7% vs 4.6%, aOR 2.05, 95% CI 1.60-2.62, p<0.001, E-value 3.52) and any MCS (10.3% vs 2.1%, aOR 2.03, 95% CI 1.50-2.76, p<0.001, E-value 3.48). Despite this higher acuity, in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between transfer-in and non-transfer (3.2% vs 1.5%; adjusted OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.56-1.39, p=0.59). Mechanical ventilation (aOR 1.21, 95% CI 0.95-1.54) and severe maternal morbidity (aOR 1.19, 95% CI 0.92-1.55) were not significantly elevated. Conclusions: One in eight PPCM hospitalizations involves transfer-in, and transferred hospitalizations show more than twice the odds of cardiogenic shock and MCS yet in-hospital survival is comparable to non-transferred hospitalizations. This mortality-neutral profile, despite markedly higher presenting acuity, may be consistent with appropriate regionalization of PPCM care, though selection bias cannot be excluded. These findings suggest a potential role for referral-center models that warrants further study. Limitations: Encounter-level (NIS cannot link admissions); transfer-in designation captures receiving-hospital perspective only; residual confounding possible; retrospective cross-sectional; the unit of analysis is the hospitalization, not the unique patient.
title: Abstract 19193: Interhospital Transfer and In-Hospital Outcomes in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2016-2023

abstract: Background: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a key mediator of inflammation, myocardial injury, and adverse remodeling in acute coronary syndromes (ACS), including ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Tocilizumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-6 receptor, has emerged as a potential adjunctive therapy aimed at reducing inflammatory injury and improving myocardial salvage. This systematic review synthesizes current clinical and mechanistic evidence evaluating the effects of IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab in ACS. Research Question: In adult patients presenting with acute coronary syndromes (STEMI or NSTEMI), does interleukin-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab, compared with placebo or standard care, reduce inflammatory activity and myocardial injury while improving myocardial salvage and clinical outcomes without increasing adverse events? Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a PROSPERO-registered protocol. Eligible studies included adult patients with STEMI or NSTEMI receiving tocilizumab during the acute or early post-myocardial infarction phase, compared with placebo or standard care. Data on inflammatory biomarkers, cardiac injury markers, imaging outcomes, and adverse events were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. Due to heterogeneity in study design, timing of intervention, and reported outcomes, a narrative synthesis was performed. Results: Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria. Tocilizumab consistently reduced systemic inflammation, as demonstrated by marked reductions in leukocytes, neutrophils, and C-reactive protein (CRP), and attenuated troponin release in several trials. Imaging studies showed improved myocardial salvage index and reduced microvascular obstruction in STEMI populations. Proteomic analyses demonstrated broad modulation of inflammatory and endothelial pathways. Adverse events were comparable between groups, with no major safety concerns identified. Conclusion: IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab demonstrates promising anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects in ACS. While current evidence supports biological efficacy, larger outcome-powered trials are needed to determine its impact on mortality, recurrent myocardial infarction, and long-term ventricular remodeling.
title: Abstract 19194: Interleukin-6 Receptor Blockade with Tocilizumab in Acute Coronary Syndromes (STEMI and NSTEMI): A Systematic Review

abstract: Keywords: cyclic vomiting syndrome; Sato variant; takotsubo cardiomyopathy; stress-induced cardiomyopathy; pediatric cardiology Introduction: The Sato variant of cyclic vomiting syndrome (CVS) features hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis hyperactivation with episodic catecholamine surges, hypertension, and lethargy. Catecholamine-mediated cardiovascular complications have not been previously characterized in this population. Patient Information: A 6-year-old girl with vomiting episodes since infancy presented with headache, abdominal pain, and emesis. Clinical Findings & Timeline: She developed cardiogenic shock with hypothermia, tachycardia, and syncope. Echocardiography revealed severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction 11%) with elevated troponin (258→533 ng/L; reference <14) and proBNP (2,138 pg/mL; reference <178). Over the following year, recurrent stereotypical vomiting episodes were complicated by hypertensive crises exceeding 200 mmHg systolic. Diagnostic Assessment: Ventricular function recovered within two weeks. Cardiac MRI showed no late gadolinium enhancement, excluding myocarditis, consistent with stress-induced (takotsubo) cardiomyopathy. Evaluation for secondary hypertension, including pheochromocytoma, was unrevealing. The clinical picture was recognized as the Sato variant of CVS, with cardiogenic shock retrospectively attributed to catecholamine-induced stress cardiomyopathy. Therapeutic Intervention(s): Management included propranolol for CVS prophylaxis and sympathetic attenuation, on-demand antihypertensives, and mitochondrial-targeted supplements (riboflavin, coenzyme Q10, magnesium). Follow-up & Outcomes: Cardiac function remained normal over nearly two years despite ongoing CVS exacerbations. No recurrence of ventricular dysfunction was observed. Discussion: This is, to our knowledge, the first report of stress-induced cardiomyopathy complicating the Sato variant of CVS without an arrhythmogenic substrate. The Sato variant functions as a physiologic analog to pheochromocytoma, with episodic catecholamine excess capable of inducing myocardial stunning. This case supports incorporating cardiovascular monitoring into Sato-variant CVS management and highlights the dual role of beta-blockade for CVS prophylaxis and cardioprotection.
title: Abstract 19202: Catecholamine-Induced Cardiogenic Shock Unmasking Sato-Variant Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome in a Child

abstract: Background: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm (AIVR) is a hallmark of early post-myocardial infarction (MI) recovery, yet its complete temporal profile remains obscured by the limitations of intermittent electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring in prior studies. Defining the precise trajectory of AIVR is essential to characterize the electrically unstable post-MI substrate. Continuous implanted ECG telemetry now allows for uninterrupted, beat-level quantification of these dynamics. Objective: To define the temporal burden and trajectory of AIVR across the first 6 days post-MI using implanted ECG telemetry in a large-animal model. Methods: Sixteen canines (8F/8M, 28 ± 3 kg) underwent permanent left anterior descending coronary artery ligation, followed by 6-day continuous ECG telemetry and serial serum Troponin-I monitoring. A validated classifier quantified minute-level AIVR burden, verified by QRS morphology and duration. Resulting temporal trajectories were characterized using a linear mixed-effects (LME) model to account for inter-subject variability. Results: AIVR burden increased rapidly after MI, peaked on postoperative Day 2 (Figure A), and declined thereafter (LME β≈–0.36 beats/hour, p<0.0001; Figure B), becoming <1 beats/hour by Day 6. Electrophysiologic validation identified ventricular origin, with QRS duration significantly prolonged during AIVR compared with sinus rhythm (ΔQRS +25 ± 5 ms, p<0.001). Notably, AIVR resolved while myocardial injury markers remained elevated (Troponin-I >8 ng/mL through Day 6). Conclusion: AIVR exhibits a consistent post-MI pattern, with a Day-2 peak followed by rapid resolution. Its transient course—despite ongoing biochemical evidence of myocardial injury—indicates that AIVR reflects a distinct, time-limited component of early ventricular electrical remodeling.
title: Abstract 19221: Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm Shows an Early Peak and Predictable Post-Myocardial Infarction Time Course in a Preclinical Model

abstract: Background: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) affects approximately 1 in 250 individuals and is most commonly caused by LDLR variants. With 2000 unique pathogenic variants, frameshift variants account for a particularly rare and severe phenotype. LDLR c.933delA (p.E312Sfs*58) is considered ultra-rare with no established prevalence data. Carriers of LDLR null variants have approximately 2-fold higher risk of MACE. Case: We present a 35-year-old male with HeFH on no lipid-lowering medications due to statin and evolocumab intolerance and payer denial of lipoprotein apheresis who presented with an out of hospital cardiac arrest. Two rounds of CPR were performed. Upon ROSC, patient was found to have an acute anterior STEMI. Patient underwent Impella assisted PCI with two DES to a 100% thrombotic occlusion of the proximal LAD. His course was complicated by refractory VT/VF and SCAI stage C cardiogenic shock, requiring Impella support, VA-ECMO, and milrinone. Lipid panel on hospital day 2 revealed total cholesterol 218 mg/dL, LDL-C 159 mg/dL, and TG 109 mg/dL. Post-discharge testing revealed lipoprotein(a) of 193 nmol/L. Post-arrest, echocardiogram showed LVEF 35% with hypokinesis to akinesis of the apical, anteroseptal, and anterior segments, with progressive recovery in subsequent echocardiograms. He also developed a right atrial thrombus along the Impella catheter requiring systemic anticoagulation and was discharged with a LifeVest. Post discharge, genetic testing revealed LDLR gene c.933delA (p.E312Sfs*58) consistent with monogenic HeFH. Patient was started on alirocumab and GDMT for HFrEF. At 1-month follow-up, echocardiography showed LVEF 50%, and the LifeVest was removed. Post-discharge testing revealed lipoprotein(a) of 193 nmol/L. Discussion: Untreated FH carries high premature coronary event risk i.e., up to 50% in men by age 50 and 30% in women by age 60. Monogenic FH carries approximately twice the cardiovascular risk of polygenic hypercholesterolemia at similar LDL-C levels. Notably, this patient also had a markedly elevated lipoprotein(a) of 193 nmol/L, an independent risk factor for ASCVD. Only 47% of PCSK9 inhibitor prescriptions are reported to be approved by payers. Lipoprotein apheresis may be limited by reimbursement variability with annual costs of $50,000-150,000, and prolonged preauthorization. These systemic barriers to evidence-based therapy can result in catastrophic cardiovascular events, as illustrated by this case with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, anterior STEMI from 100% LAD occlusion, refractory VT/VF, cardiogenic shock requiring Impella and VA-ECMO, and RA thrombus. Conclusion: This case highlights the devastating consequences of delayed access to guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy in a young patient. Early recognition and aggressive lipid lowering in high-risk FH is not optional but lifesaving.
title: Abstract 19222: When Insurance Barriers Become Life Threatening: A Preventable Cardiac Arrest in a 35-Year-Old with an Ultra-Rare Low-Density Lipoprotein Receptor Null Variant and Elevated Lipoprotein(a)

abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) is an established marker of cardiovascular risk. However, CAC primarily reflects atherosclerotic burden and may not capture inflammatory and metabolic pathways contributing to adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has emerged as a promising imaging biomarker that can be automatically quantified using artificial intelligence (AI) from routine non-contrast chest CT. Objective To evaluate the prognostic value of AI-derived EAT compared with CAC and develop a practical CT-based cardiovascular risk score. Methods: A total of 3,077 patients undergoing routine non-contrast chest CT were included. EAT volume was quantified using a fully automated AI algorithm, and CAC was assessed using the Agatston score. Patients were followed for 5 years.Clinical outcomes included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, atrial fibrillation (AF), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Logistic regression and ROC analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and assess discriminative performance. Results: The mean age was 62.7 ± 18.6 years. During follow-up, all-cause mortality occurred in 714 patients (23.2%), ischemic stroke in 372 (12.1%), MI in 283 (9.2%), AF in 704 (22.9%), and PCI in 412 (13.4%).EAT demonstrated strong prognostic performance across multiple outcomes. For MI, EAT showed higher discrimination than CAC (AUC 0.787 vs. 0.773). For AF, EAT substantially outperformed CAC (AUC 0.820 vs. 0.724). EAT also demonstrated superior discrimination for all-cause mortality (AUC 0.795 vs. 0.770). CAC remained the strongest predictor of PCI (AUC 0.854 vs. 0.819 for EAT). For ischemic stroke, predictive performance was comparable for CAC (AUC 0.744), age (AUC 0.743), and EAT (AUC 0.715).In multivariable analyses, age, EAT, and CAC remained independently associated with adverse outcomes. An EAT threshold of 90 cm 3 was identified as the optimal cutoff for MACE prediction.A CT-based risk score integrating age, EAT, and CAC demonstrated good discrimination for MACE (AUC 0.80). The score was derived from multivariable regression coefficients and included age (<55=0, 55-64=1, 65-74=2, ≥75=3 points), EAT ≥90 cm 3 (1 point), and CAC categories (0=0, 1-100=1, 101-400=2, >400=3 points). Total scores ranged from 0 to 7 and stratified patients into low- (0-1), intermediate- (2-3), high- (4-5), and very-high-risk (≥6) categories, corresponding to estimated MACE risks of ≤30%, 30-45%, 45-60%, and ≥60%, respectively. Conclusions: AI-derived EAT provides prognostic information beyond CAC and predicts a broad spectrum of cardiovascular outcomes. Integration of EAT, CAC, and age enables opportunistic cardiovascular risk assessment from routine chest CT and may support large-scale personalized prevention strategies.
title: Abstract 19249: AI-Derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue Improves Long-Term Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Beyond Coronary Artery Calcium: Development of a Practical CT-Based Risk Score

abstract: Background: Sex-based differences in cardiogenic shock management and outcomes are recognized, but whether disparities vary across hospital practice patterns remains unclear. We evaluated sex differences in temporary mechanical circulatory support use, in-hospital outcomes, and the modifying effect of hospital-level support intensity among patients with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock. Methods: We analyzed adult hospitalizations for heart failure-related cardiogenic shock in the 2022 to 2023 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitals were categorized into quartiles based on temporary mechanical circulatory support utilization intensity. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations between sex, temporary mechanical circulatory support use, and in-hospital mortality, with formal testing for sex-by-hospital intensity interaction. Results: Among 66,961 hospitalizations, temporary mechanical circulatory support was used in 16.8%. Women had higher crude in-hospital mortality than men (30.9% versus 26.2%). After adjustment, female sex was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval 1.11 to 1.20) and lower odds of temporary mechanical circulatory support use (adjusted odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.68 to 0.75). Utilization increased across hospital intensity quartiles, with widening sex disparities at higher-intensity centers. In the highest-intensity hospitals, temporary mechanical circulatory support use was 29.9% in men versus 23.2% in women. Higher hospital intensity was associated with modestly lower adjusted mortality, whereas temporary mechanical circulatory support use itself was not associated with lower mortality after adjustment. A significant sex-by-hospital intensity interaction was observed (P for interaction <0.001). Conclusions: Women hospitalized with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock had lower use of temporary mechanical circulatory support despite higher adjusted mortality. These disparities were amplified in higher-intensity centers, suggesting that access to advanced therapies alone may not ensure equitable care. Standardized, objective escalation pathways may be needed to reduce sex-based variation in cardiogenic shock management.
title: Abstract 19256: Sex Differences in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support Use Across Hospital Intensity in Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Heart failure-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) carries persistently high mortality despite contemporary management. Although AKI is frequent in this setting, its prognostic significance has been defined primarily in AMI-CS and may not generalize to HF-CS, leaving a critical gap in risk stratification. Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for cohort studies through November 2025. Eligible studies enrolled adults with HF-CS comparing outcomes with vs. without AKI; CS primarily related to AMI or post-cardiotomy were excluded, and cohorts excluding these etiologies by original design were considered HF-CS. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30, 90, and 180 days. Crude HRs were pooled using a random-effects inverse-variance model. When HRs were unavailable, time-to-event individual patient data (IPD) were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves using the IPDfromKM algorithm and analyzed via Cox regression; IPD were reconstructed separately for each time horizon to minimize violations of the proportional hazards assumption, and pooled Kaplan-Meier survival curves were fitted using reconstructed IPD in a 1-stage approach. Leave-one-out analyses were used to evaluate heterogeneity. AKI stage-specific mortality was explored in a pre-specified subgroup analysis. All analyses were performed in R 4.5.2. Results: Of 4,926 screened studies, four cohort studies (N=1,333) met inclusion criteria. QUIPS-based risk of bias ranged from low to high, driven by confounding. AKI was associated with higher all-cause mortality at 30 days (cHR 2.31; 95% CI 1.44-3.71; p=0.0005), 90 days (cHR 2.34; 95% CI 1.33-4.14; p=0.003), and 180 days (cHR 2.14; 95% CI 1.16-3.96; p=0.01). Pooled Kaplan-Meier curves fitted from reconstructed IPD confirmed early and sustained survival divergence favoring No AKI at 30 days (HR 1.72; 95% CI 1.46-2.04; p<0.001) and 90 days (HR 2.48; 95% CI 1.47-4.17; p<0.001). Substantial 30-day heterogeneity (I 2 ≥50%) was driven by Sundermeyer et al.; its exclusion resolved heterogeneity (I 2 =0%) and strengthened the pooled estimate. In stage-stratified exploratory analyses, AKI stage 3 showed the highest pooled mortality risk (cHR 3.26; 95% CI 0.68-15.65; p=0.14), directionally consistent with Sundermeyer et al., where stage 3 was the only stage independently associated with mortality (aHR 1.97; 95% CI 1.56-2.48; p<0.001), while stages 1 and 2 were not, likely reflecting limited power. AKI patients required CRRT more frequently (25.7% vs. 0%; p=0.01), with no significant difference in the use of invasive mechanical ventilation. Conclusions: AKI is associated with higher all-cause mortality across multiple follow-up periods in HF-CS, supporting its role as a prognostic marker in this population. Prospective studies are warranted to evaluate organ-protective strategies and define optimal AKI management in HF-CS.
title: Abstract 19279: Prognostic Impact of Acute Kidney Injury on Mortality in Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Using Reconstructed Individual-Participant Survival Data

abstract: Background: Regional-level evidence comparing stress perfusion modalities against invasive physiology remains limited, particularly as scanner and detector technology has evolved. Research Question: We evaluated whether modality and technology generation modify regional diagnostic performance for hemodynamically significant coronary artery disease. Methods: We performed a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of vessel- or territory-level studies using invasive reference standards centered on fractional flow reserve ≤0.80, with or without severe angiographic stenosis criteria. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and summary receiver-operating-characteristic curves were estimated with bivariate random-effects models. Comparative analyses were conducted using random-effects meta-regression on log diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) and on logit sensitivity/specificity with adjustment for disease prevalence and reference-standard threshold. We compared computed tomography perfusion (CTP), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), positron emission tomography, and single-photon computed tomography. Prespecified technology sub-analyses included dual-source vs single-source CTP, cadmium-zinc telluride (CZT) vs conventional SPECT, and 3T vs 1.5T CMR. Results: Sixty-six studies comprising 5,496 patients, 13,735 regions were included. Pooled sensitivity/specificity were 0.829/0.843 for CTP, 0.767/0.885 for CMR, 0.771/0.796 for PET, and 0.652/0.856 for SPECT. Compared with SPECT, CTP had higher adjusted DOR (DOR ratio 2.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.25-3.38; P=0.006) and highest pooled sensitivity, whereas CMR had the highest pooled specificity. PET also showed higher sensitivity but lower specificity. Technology generation materially modified performance. CZT SPECT had higher DOR than conventional SPECT (DOR ratio 4.09, 95% confidence interval 1.85-9.02; P=0.003), and 3-T CMR showed higher DOR than 1.5-T CMR (DOR ratio 4.96, 95% CI 1.08-22.88; P=0.042). Dual-source CTP showed directional improvement over single-source systems. In analyses restricted to advanced platforms, 3-T CMR had higher DOR than CZT SPECT (DOR ratio 2.70, 95% CI 1.03-7.05; P=0.044). Conclusions: Stress perfusion imaging modalities showed distinct regional diagnostic operating profiles rather than a uniform hierarchy. CTP had the highest pooled sensitivity, whereas CMR had the highest pooled specificity, while technology generation was associated with difference in performance within-modality, particularly for CZT-SPECT. These findings support modality- and technology-aware selection of noninvasive ischemia testing.
title: Abstract 4216: Technology-Driven Gains in Stress Perfusion Imaging for Hemodynamically Significant CAD: A Regional-Level Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Current recommendations for the initiation of anticoagulation in atrial flutter (AFL) patients are identical to those originally established for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the evidence base supporting these guidelines remains limited by the absence of dedicated randomized trials in AFL patients. Whether AFL carries equivalent stroke risk to AF at the same CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score remains unestablished. We hypothesized that AFL carries a lower ischemic stroke risk than AF at equivalent CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scores. Methods: We conducted a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global federated research network. Adult patients with a new diagnosis of AF or AFL were identified and stratified by CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score (0-8) and sex. AF and AFL cohorts were matched on 29 covariates including demographics, comorbidities, and medications. A total of 139,476 patients were included across all CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc strata and sex subgroups following propensity score matching (69,738 AF and 69,738 AFL). To avoid incorrect attribution of pre-existing strokes as incident events during the follow-up period, patients with a prior history of ischemic stroke were excluded. Primary outcome was ischemic stroke at 1 year and 3 years. Secondary outcomes included TIA, systemic embolism, intracranial hemorrhage, gastrointestinal bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Results: AF carried significantly higher 1-year ischemic stroke risk than AFL across most CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scores. The excess risk was most pronounced at score 2 (RR 2.01, 95% CI 1.66-2.43, p<0.001), with AF patients facing more than double the stroke risk of matched AFL patients. Critically, 1-year AFL stroke rates remained below the 2% anticoagulation threshold through score 5 (1.47%), while AF crossed this threshold at score 4 (2.00%). This pattern was consistent across sexes: in males, 1-year AFL stroke risk remained below 2% through score 5 (1.26%) vs. AF crossing at score 4 (2.37%); in females, 1-year AFL stroke risk remained below 2% through score 5 (1.61%) vs. AF reaching 3.40% at score 6. AF also demonstrated significantly higher rates of TIA and intracranial hemorrhage at lower CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scores. Conclusions: In a large propensity-matched AF vs. AFL cohort to date, AFL demonstrated consistently and substantially lower ischemic stroke risk than AF across CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scores and in both sexes. These data challenge the one-size-fits-all approach to anticoagulation in AFL and suggest arrhythmia-specific thresholds may better align treatment intensity with true stroke risk. Prospective validation is warranted.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Cediranib, a potent pan-VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has shown antitumor activity in several malignancies and is clinically combined with the PARP inhibitor olaparib in selected oncological settings. However, cediranib-associated cardiovascular toxicity, including hypertension, left ventricular dysfunction and heart failure, remains an important limitation of VEGFR-targeted therapy. Although olaparib is primarily used as an antitumor agent, whether it modulates cediranib-induced cardiac injury has not been fully defined. We hypothesized that cediranib-induced cardiotoxicity is associated with oxidative stress, PARP1/PARylation activation and PI3K/AKT signaling dysregulation, and that olaparib may attenuate these alterations in preclinical models. Methods: Cediranib-induced cardiotoxicity was modeled in C57BL/6 mice (5-week oral cediranib ± olaparib) and in H9c2 cardiac-derived cells. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography; myocardial injury was evaluated by histology and circulating hs-cTnT/NT-proBNP. Oxidative stress, DNA damage, PARP1/PARylation, and PI3K/AKT signaling were profiled by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and Western blotting. Quantitative proteomic analysis was performed to identify cediranib-associated molecular pathways in myocardial tissue. Results: Cediranib reduced LVEF and fractional shortening, increased plasma hs-cTnT and NT-proBNP levels, disrupted myocardial architecture, increased OGG1 expression, reduced SOD1 expression, and enhanced PARP1 expression and global PARylation. Quantitative proteomic profiling identified 265 differentially expressed proteins in cediranib-treated hearts, with enrichment of pathways related to focal adhesion, oxidative stress response and PI3K/AKT signaling. Western blot analysis confirmed that cediranib reduced p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios in myocardial tissue. Co-administration of olaparib improved cardiac systolic function, attenuated myocardial injury biomarkers, reduced oxidative stress-associated alterations, suppressed PARP1/PARylation activation, and partially restored PI3K/AKT signaling in vivo and in H9c2 cardiac-derived cells. Conclusions: This study suggests that PARP1/PARylation activation is associated with cediranib-induced cardiac injury and that olaparib attenuates this toxicity in preclinical models, potentially through modulation of oxidative stress and PI3K/AKT signaling.
title: Abstract 4232: The Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerase 1 Inhibitor Olaparib Ameliorates Cediranib-Induced Cardiotoxicity

abstract: Background: TTS is historically described as a disease of postmenopausal women, yet males comprise a clinically distinct subgroup with consistently worse outcomes. The mechanistic basis of this sex difference, particularly whether it reflects differential trigger exposure rather than inherent biological vulnerability, has not been characterized in large contemporary cohorts. Methods: We compared outcomes between 3,241 male and 16,632 female TTS patients from 74 U.S. healthcare organizations, 2016-2025, through Trinetx database. Trigger patterns were defined by co-coded diagnoses. Primary outcomes were cardiogenic shock (R57.0) and all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and 12 comorbidities. Results: Male TTS patients had a CS rate of 7.9% versus 3.0% in females (p<0.001), and all-cause mortality of 25.9% versus 13.5% (p<0.001). Males were younger (median age 62, IQR 49-71 vs. 66, IQR 57-74, p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, male sex remained independently associated with CS (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34-1.89, p<0.001) and mortality (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.67-2.07, p<0.001). Crucially, trigger patterns differed markedly: male TTS was more commonly associated with sepsis (26.3% vs. 12.0%, p<0.001) and pneumonia (25.1% vs. 15.5%, p<0.001), while psychiatric triggers were significantly less prevalent among males (36.3% vs. 49.4%, p<0.001). Males also had significantly higher rates of atrial fibrillation (21.5% vs. 15.5%), diabetes (26.4% vs. 21.8%), CKD (17.6% vs. 14.2%), and stroke (14.2% vs. 10.7%), all p<0.001. Conclusions: In this large real-world cohort, male TTS is characterized by predominantly physical/infectious triggers, higher sepsis and end-organ comorbidity burden, and an independent 86% excess mortality risk versus females. The sex difference in TTS outcomes is driven at least in part by fundamentally different trigger mechanisms, suggesting that sex-specific surveillance protocols, particularly vigilance for TTS in male patients presenting with sepsis or acute illness, are warranted.
title: Abstract 4237: Male Takotsubo Syndrome: A Sepsis- and Illness-Driven Phenotype with Excess Cardiogenic Shock and Mortality

abstract: Background: Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (OAC) before left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), reserving LAAO for intolerance, failure, or contraindication. However, real-world patterns in OAC-naive patients—those undergoing LAAO without prior OAC—remain unclear. Whether this reflects off-label use or appropriate selection of high-risk patients is unknown. We evaluated the prevalence, characteristics, and outcomes of OAC-naive LAAO recipients. Methods: Using the TriNetX network (2016-2026), we identified 29,553 patients undergoing LAAO (CPT 33340). Patients were categorized as OAC failure (n=8,356), OAC tolerant (n=13,698), or OAC naive (n=7,499) based on pre-procedural RxNorm data. Trends in OAC-naive use were assessed (2017-2024). Multivariable logistic regression compared outcomes between OAC-naive and OAC-tolerant patients, adjusting for 25 covariates including CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc, HAS-BLED, and comorbidities. Results: OAC-naive patients comprised 25.4% of LAAO recipients. They had lower baseline risk (CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc 4.1 vs 4.7 vs 5.5; HAS-BLED 2.5 vs 3.0 vs 4.5; all p<0.001) compared with OAC-tolerant and OAC-failure groups. Notably, 26.4% had prior major bleeding despite no OAC exposure, suggesting preemptive avoidance of anticoagulation. OAC-naive prevalence declined from 31.3% (2017) to 24.6% (2024; p=0.021). Crude outcomes were similar between groups. After adjustment, OAC-naive status was not associated with increased mortality (aOR 1.10, 95% CI 0.97-1.24), stroke/TIA (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.93-1.20), or major bleeding (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.91-1.13). Readmission was slightly higher (aOR 1.10, p=0.043). Conclusions: One in four LAAO recipients is OAC-naive. Despite lower baseline risk, outcomes are comparable to guideline-concordant patients, suggesting LAAO effectiveness independent of prior OAC exposure. These findings challenge current appropriateness frameworks and support consideration of LAAO in selected OAC-naive patients with bleeding risk or contraindications.
title: Abstract 4238: The OAC-Naive Paradox: Characterization and Outcomes of LAAO Recipients Who Never Received Oral Anticoagulation — A Nationwide Real-World Analysis

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a recognized complication of TTS, but whether new-onset AF carries different prognostic implications than pre-existing AF — and the mechanism by which AF influences outcomes — has not been systematically evaluated in a large cohort. Methods: Among 19,897 TTS patients (74 U.S. healthcare organizations, 2016-2025), AF was classified as new-onset (first AF code at or after TTS diagnosis date) or chronic (AF coded prior to TTS). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and cardiogenic shock (R57.0). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, sepsis, and pneumonia. Results: New-onset AF occurred in 2,037 patients (10.2%), chronic AF was present in 1,246 (6.3%), and 16,614 (83.5%) had no AF. New-onset AF carried 24.9% all-cause mortality and a 7.3% CS rate, compared with 13.7% mortality and 3.2% CS in AF-free patients (both p<0.001). Strikingly, chronic pre-existing AF conferred identical mortality to new-onset AF (24.9% vs. 24.9%, p=1.00) and a similar CS rate (5.4%). On multivariable analysis, both new-onset AF (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.26-1.62, p<0.001) and chronic AF (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.21-1.66, p<0.001) were independently associated with mortality relative to no AF, with virtually identical adjusted risk estimates. New-onset AF patients were younger (median age 70, IQR 62-77) than chronic AF patients (median 73, IQR 66-79), had higher sepsis prevalence (23.7% vs. 20.5%), and were more often female (79.6% vs. 77.3%). Conclusions: AF, whether new-onset or pre-existing, independently predicts mortality in TTS with identical adjusted risk (OR 1.42 for both), and is associated with more than double the rate of cardiogenic shock compared with AF-free patients. The equivalence of new-onset and chronic AF in adjusted mortality risk suggests AF serves as a hemodynamic severity marker in TTS rather than an independent arrhythmic cause of death, with important implications for how AF should be interpreted and managed acutely in this population.
title: Abstract 4240: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Takotsubo Syndrome: Incidence, Hemodynamic Impact, and Equivalence with Pre-Existing AF

abstract: Background: People with HIV (PWH) have a higher burden of cardiovascular disease compared to people without HIV (HIV-), attributable to chronic inflammation, immune dysregulation, HIV viremia, structural barriers to care, and stigma. However, differences in utilization of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in PWH versus HIV- have not been evaluated. Methods: We analyzed data from adults with a diagnosis of cardiogenic shock in 27 states in the United States using the State Inpatient Database (2010, 2012, 2016-2019). HIV status and mechanical circulatory support utilization were extracted using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. The primary outcome measure was the utilization of MCS, defined as a composite of ventricular assist device (VAD), percutaneous ventricular assist device (pVAD), intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), and heart transplant utilization among PWH versus HIV- persons. Secondary outcomes include individual MCS utilization. Baseline demographic factors and socioeconomic characteristics were compared between PWH and HIV-. Multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, race/ethnicity, median household income, primary payer, admission type, urban/rural, comorbid conditions, discharge year, and hospital region evaluated the relationship between HIV status and MCS utilization. Results: Among 351,085 adults with cardiogenic shock, 2,460 (0.7%) had HIV. Among PWH, mean (SD) age was 53.9 (12.0) compared to HIV- was 67.2 (14.5); PWH were more likely to be Black (52.0% vs 14.8%) and more likely to have Medicaid (31.2% vs 10.7%) than HIV- (P<.001). Adjusted regression analyses suggest PWH were 32% less likely (aOR 0.68, 95% CI 0.61, 0.77, P<.001) to receive any MCS compared to HIV. On secondary analysis, PWH were less likelyto receive VAD (aOR 0.63, 95% CI 0.51, 0.78, P<.001), pVAD (aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.57, 0.94, P=.014), IABP (aOR 0.77, 95% CI 0.67, 0.88, P<.001), and VA-ECMO (aOR 0.51, 95% CI 0.36, 0.73, P<.001). Conclusion: PWH are more likely to be Black, have Medicaid, be younger, have lower income, and are less likely to receive MCS for cardiogenic shock compared to HIV- adults. More targeted efforts to address underlying disparities and improve access to care are needed among PWH.
title: Abstract 4242: Differences in Mechanical Circulatory Support Utilization for Cardiogenic Shock Among Patients With HIV and Without HIV

abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipid guidelines recommend prompt attainment of LDL-C targets in patients after acute coronary syndrome (ACS); however, timely goal achievement remains challenging. METHODS/RESULTS: We developed DECIDE-ACS, a lipid management algorithm for cardiologists evaluating post-ACS patients at a first post-discharge visit. The tool integrates multi-society guideline recommendations and incorporates a validated 10-year CV risk score with treatment prompts. Cardiologists were invited to use DECIDE-ACS for five consecutive post-ACS patients. Treatment decisions were recorded after presentation of guideline-endorsed LDL-C targets, after guideline-based intensification recommendations, and after risk score calculation. In total, 104 cardiologists enrolled 501 patients (74% male; mean age 66 years) at a median of 16 weeks post-discharge. Index events included NSTEMI (53%), STEMI (31%), and unstable angina (16%). Revascularization occurred in 90% of patients (PCI 73%, CABG 17%). CV risk factors included smoking (18%), hypertension (72%), and diabetes (35%). Prior ASCVD included MI (19%), revascularization (20%), stroke (6%), and peripheral artery disease (4%). Median LDL-C and non-HDL-C at the DECIDE-ACS visit were 61.9 and 85.1 mg/dL respectively; 36% and 62% of patients exceeded LDL-C thresholds of 70 and 55 mg/dL, respectively. ApoB levels were available in 39% of patients, median 0.7 g/L. Lipoprotein(a) was measured in 32% of patients, with 37% >100 nmol/L. Lipid therapy included statin monotherapy (70%), statin plus ezetimibe (28%), and PCSK9 modulation (2.8%); high-intensity statins were used in 88% of patients. Desired LDL-C targets reported by cardiologists were <70 mg/dL in 73% and <55 mg/dL in 27%. Following guideline LDL target prompts, treatment changes occurred in 42% of patients. Guideline-endorsed recommendation prompts led to revisions in 16%. Cardiologist-estimated risk was concordant with SMART-REACH in 35% of cases, overestimated in 9%, and underestimated in 56%. Risk score prompts resulted in treatment changes for an additional 16% of patients. Overall, treatment decisions were modified in 55.7% of patients entered into DECIDE-ACS. Follow-up lipid testing was ordered in 87% of patients, and 97% had a clinic visit scheduled within 6-12 weeks. CONCLUSIONS: At 16 weeks post-ACS, 36-62% of patients had not achieved LDL-C goals despite 88% use of high-intensity statin therapy. Cardiologists underestimated validated 10-year risk in 56% of patients. Use of DECIDE-ACS integrating multi-society guidelines and validated risk scoring substantially altered management, with treatment revisions in 55.7% of patients; this effect is likely underestimated given that 41% lacked risk scoring. Structured multi-society guideline prompts combined with risk calculation may improve timely post-ACS lipid management.
title: Abstract 4251: DECIDE-ACS: An Online Lipid Optimization Algorithm for Cardiologists Managing Post-ACS Patients

abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a feared complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Administrative database studies have characterized stroke epidemiology but lack clinical granularity, including stroke subtype, precise timing, hemodynamic parameters, and cerebral protection device (CPD) details. Registry-based analyses with granular data are needed to identify modifiable predictors and evaluate real-world CPD effectiveness. METHODS: We analyzed 1,039 consecutive TAVR patients (January 2021-June 2025) from the TVT/NCDR Registry at a single academic center. Stroke/TIA was identified through standardized structured follow-up and classified by subtype (ischemic, hemorrhagic, undetermined, TIA) and timing (≤30 vs >30 days). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified predictors. Model discrimination was assessed by C-statistic. Sentinel CPD effectiveness was evaluated after multivariable adjustment. Statistical significance: p<0.05. RESULTS: Over a median 354-day follow-up (746.7 person-years), 17 patients (1.6%) experienced stroke/TIA (incidence 2.28/100 person-years): 9 ischemic strokes (52.9%), 5 TIAs (29.4%), 2 undetermined (11.8%), and 1 hemorrhagic (5.9%). Sixty-five percent occurred within 30 days, with nearly all ischemic strokes within 18 days. On multivariable analysis (C-statistic 0.741), atrial fibrillation (AF) was the sole independent predictor (adjusted OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.03-7.93, p=0.043). Univariable signals included STS-PROM (OR 1.07 per 1%, p=0.012) and low stroke volume index <35 mL/m 2 (OR 2.26, p=0.043). Sentinel CPD (used in 17.9%) showed no stroke reduction (1.9% vs 1.9%, adjusted OR 1.12, p=0.865). Stroke/TIA patients had significantly higher readmission rates (64.7% vs 27.1%, p<0.001) and numerically higher mortality (17.6% vs 7.8%, p=0.148). CONCLUSIONS: In this granular single-center registry analysis, post-TAVR stroke/TIA was predominantly ischemic and periprocedural. Atrial fibrillation was the sole independent predictor, and Sentinel CPD conferred no real-world stroke reduction. These findings reinforce AF management as the primary modifiable target for post-TAVR stroke prevention.
title: Abstract 4254: Outcomes and Predictors of Stroke After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Cerebral Protection Device Era

abstract: BACKGROUND: TAVR is performed with the dual goal of prolonging survival and improving functional status in patients with severe aortic stenosis. New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class is a widely used clinical marker of symptom burden, and improvement in NYHA class after TAVR reflects successful symptom relief. However, not all patients improve, and the proportion achieving combined improvement in both NYHA class and health-related quality of life (as measured by KCCQ-12) remains poorly characterized. Identifying patients who fail to improve on either metric is essential for understanding procedural futility. METHODS: We analyzed patients with paired pre- and post-procedural NYHA class data at 30 days using the TVT/NCDR Registry at a single academic center (January 2021-June 2025). NYHA class was coded numerically (I=1, II=2, III=3, IV=4), with improvement defined as any decrease in class. Combined outcome analysis incorporated 30-day KCCQ-12 data where available. Patients with missing baseline or follow-up data were excluded. Baseline characteristics were compared between those with and without NYHA improvement using standard statistical methods. RESULTS: The analytic cohort comprised 788 patients (mean age 77.7 ± 8.4 years; 421 male [53.4%], 367 female [46.6%]). Overall, 65.6% of patients demonstrated improvement in NYHA class at 30 days. Among patients presenting with NYHA class III or IV symptoms, 83.4% improved by at least one functional class. In the combined analysis (NYHA + KCCQ-12), 88.3% of patients improved in at least one metric, while 11.7% demonstrated no improvement in either NYHA class or KCCQ-12 score at 30 days. CONCLUSIONS: The majority of TAVR patients achieve meaningful improvement in functional status at 30 days, particularly those with advanced baseline symptoms. Nevertheless, nearly 1 in 9 patients fails to improve on both NYHA class and KCCQ-12, representing a population at risk for procedural futility. These findings support the integrated use of functional and patient-reported outcomes in TAVR program quality assessment and patient-centered decision-making frameworks.
title: Abstract 4269: Functional Status Improvement After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: NYHA Class Trajectories and Combined Symptom Outcomes

abstract: BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 45 days followed by aspirin after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), reserving oral anticoagulation (OAC) for select high-risk patients. However, real-world post-LAAO antithrombotic strategies and the independent impact of OAC continuation remain poorly defined. METHODS: We analyzed antithrombotic regimens initiated within 90 days of LAAO (CPT 33340) among 29,553 patients in the TriNetX Network (2016-2026). Regimens were categorized into six groups using RxNorm codes. The primary comparison was OAC continuation vs. no OAC (n=27,563). Propensity scores were derived using 28 covariates, followed by 1:1 matching (caliper 0.2 SD). Doubly robust models assessed outcomes including mortality, stroke/TIA, major bleeding, and 30-day readmission. RESULTS: Marked heterogeneity in post-LAAO antithrombotic prescribing was observed: DAPT was the most common regimen (28.9%), followed by no antithrombotic documentation (24.9%), OAC + DAPT (22.6%), OAC + single antiplatelet (10.5%), single antiplatelet alone (7.5%), and OAC alone (5.6%). Of 29,553 patients, 11,446 (38.7%) received post-LAAO OAC. Among the analytic cohort of 27,563, propensity score matching yielded 10,479 well-balanced pairs (max standardized mean difference [SMD] 0.053 across 28 covariates, vs. pre-match max SMD 0.608), confirming excellent covariate balance. In the matched cohort, OAC continuation was associated with higher crude rates of all-cause mortality (18.9% vs. 13.2%), stroke/TIA (19.0% vs. 15.5%), major bleeding (30.5% vs. 27.6%), and 30-day readmission (24.3% vs. 18.3%; all p<0.001). After doubly-robust adjustment within the matched cohort, OAC continuation remained independently associated with higher all-cause mortality (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.49-1.75; p<0.001), stroke/TIA (aOR 1.35, 95% CI 1.25-1.47; p<0.001), major bleeding (aOR 1.20, 95% CI 1.13-1.29; p<0.001), and 30-day readmission (aOR 1.46, 95% CI 1.37-1.56; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Post-LAAO antithrombotic prescribing in real-world practice is highly heterogeneous, with nearly 1 in 4 patients having no antithrombotic documentation within 90 days of LAAO. Even after rigorous 1:1 propensity score matching on 28 covariates achieving excellent balance (max SMD <0.06), OAC continuation post-LAAO was associated with independently higher mortality, stroke, bleeding, and readmission compared with non-OAC strategies. While substantial residual confounding by indication — clinicians selectively maintaining OAC in the most complex patients — cannot be fully excluded, these findings support renewed emphasis on structured guideline-adherent antithrombotic protocols after LAAO, prompt OAC de-escalation in eligible patients, and prospective trials to definitively establish optimal post-LAAO antithrombotic de-escalation pathways.
title: Abstract 4270: Real-World Post-Procedural Antithrombotic Regimens After LAAO and Their Association with Outcomes

abstract: Background: Papillary fibroelastoma (PFE) is a rare benign cardiac tumor with significant embolic potential. Although neurologic manifestations such as ischemic stroke are well described, mass-like intracranial lesions mimicking high-grade glioma (HGG) are exceedingly uncommon. Such presentations may lead to diagnostic anchoring and delay identification of a cardiac source of embolism. Case Description: A 56-year-old man with insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a three-month history of headache, dizziness, and mood changes. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed a partially hemorrhagic, contrast-enhancing right frontal lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema, highly suspicious for glioblastoma. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction 15-20%). During hospitalization, the patient developed acute abdominal pain, and imaging revealed splenic and multifocal renal infarctions, raising concern for systemic embolization. Craniotomy was performed, and histopathology demonstrated multiple subacute cerebral infarcts rather than malignancy. Subsequent transesophageal echocardiography identified a mobile mass on the right coronary cusp of the aortic valve. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed a pedunculated valvular mass consistent with PFE. Hypercoagulability testing showed mildly reduced antithrombin III activity and low-titer anticardiolipin IgG positivity without fulfilling criteria for antiphospholipid syndrome. The patient was discharged on systemic anticoagulation with referral for cardiothoracic surgical evaluation. Conclusion: This case illustrates an unusual presentation of aortic valve PFE causing multifocal cerebral and visceral infarctions that radiographically mimicked HGG. Comprehensive cardiac evaluation should be considered in patients with atypical enhancing intracranial lesions and systemic embolic phenomena. Early recognition of a cardiac embolic source is critical to guide anticoagulation and definitive surgical management, thereby reducing the risk of recurrent thromboembolism.
title: Abstract 4279: Papillary Fibroelastoma Presenting as Multifocal Cerebral and Visceral Infarctions Mimicking Glioblastoma: A Diagnostic Challenge

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac myxomas are the most common primary cardiac tumors but rarely present with acute coronary embolization. Carney complex is a genetic syndrome predisposing to recurrent myxomas and other neoplasms. Patient Information: A 20 year old man with Carney complex, including pituitary adenoma, testicular masses and prior bilateral adrenalectomies for Cushing syndrome, was admitted for evaluation of a known left atrial myxoma. Clinical Findings & Timeline: During hospitalization, he developed acute chest pain with electrocardiographic findings consistent with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Emergent coronary angiography demonstrated subtotal occlusion of the mid-left circumflex artery and complete occlusion of an obtuse marginal branch without evidence of underlying atherosclerosis. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The absence of coronary artery disease and presence of a known atrial myxoma suggested tumor embolization as the cause of myocardial infarction. Aspiration thrombectomy yielded solid material consistent with myxoma fragments, confirming the diagnosis. Therapeutic Intervention: Percutaneous intervention with aspiration thrombectomy and balloon angioplasty restored coronary flow without stent placement.
