An intra-aortic balloon pump was placed for hemodynamic support. Antithrombotic therapy was initiated as a bridge to definitive surgical management. Follow-up & Outcomes: The patient stabilized and underwent successful surgical resection of the atrial myxoma with mitral valve repair. Postoperative course was notable for transient atrial arrhythmia. Left ventricular function improved on follow-up. Discussion & Conclusion: This case highlights cardiac myxoma embolization as a rare cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction in patients with Carney complex. Recognition of a nonatherosclerotic etiology is critical to guide management, favoring thrombectomy without stenting and early surgical resection. Multidisciplinary care is essential to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 4294: Cardiac Myxoma Embolization Presenting as ST Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction in Carney Complex

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) has undergone rapid nationwide growth since device approval, yet population-level trends in patient selection, comorbidity burden, and longitudinal outcomes over a full decade of real-world utilization remain uncharacterized. As LAAO volumes expand and indications evolve, understanding whether procedural growth has been accompanied by improving outcomes or offset by increasing complexity is critical for guideline development. Methods: We identified 29,553 patients undergoing LAAO (CPT 33340) from 2016 to 2026 across the TriNetX Research Network (48 U.S. HCOs; mean age 75.3 years, 39.9% female, mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc 4.8). Annual trends in procedural volume, patient characteristics, comorbidities, and indication subgroups were assessed using linear regression. Outcome trends were restricted to patients with index procedures through 2024 to ensure ≥1 year of follow-up (n=21,724). Results: LAAO volume expanded 9.1-fold from 643 procedures in 2017 to 5,873 in 2024, representing a mean annual growth of 37%. The procedural population became progressively older (mean age 73.4 to 75.7 years; +0.30 years/year, p<0.001), more CKD-burdened (29.5% to 36.9%; +0.68 percentage points/year, p=0.024), and carried increasing rates of heart failure (46.9% to 52.9%). The proportion undergoing LAAO for OAC failure declined from 30.0% to 27.5% (slope –0.73%/year, p=0.053), consistent with expansion into broader indications. Despite rising complexity, post-procedural stroke/TIA rates declined from 26.3% to 14.0% (–2.02 percentage points/year, r=–0.94, p<0.001) and major bleeding from 45.9% to 24.3% (–2.99 percentage points/year, r=–0.98, p<0.001), while 1-year all-cause mortality remained stable (5.9% vs. 5.8%; p=0.32). Conclusions: Real-world LAAO utilization grew nearly 10-fold over a decade, with procedures increasingly performed in older, more CKD-burdened patients with higher heart failure burden. Stroke and bleeding rates declined by nearly half despite rising patient complexity, suggesting genuine advances in technique, operator experience, and post-procedural management, while 1-year mortality remained stable. These data provide a critical decade-long benchmark for real-world LAAO performance and support continued expansion to higher-risk populations.
title: Abstract 4303: A Decade of Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Temporal Trends in Patient Complexity and Outcomes in Real-World Patients (2016-2026)

abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is increasingly used in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients with prior oral anticoagulation (OAC)-related bleeding (“OAC failure”), a population at simultaneously high thrombotic and hemorrhagic risk. Whether LAAO provides comparable stroke protection and how bleeding risk evolves in this subgroup remain incompletely defined. METHODS: Among 29,553 LAAO patients in the TriNetX network (2016-2026), those with pre-procedural OAC use (n=22,054) were stratified as OAC failure (prior major bleeding; n=8,356) or OAC tolerant (no prior bleeding; n=13,698). Given inherent collinearity of bleeding with group assignment, propensity matching was not performed. Multivariable logistic regression with doubly robust adjustment was applied across 24 covariates. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, stroke/TIA, major bleeding, and 30-day readmission. RESULTS: OAC failure patients had greater comorbidity burden, including higher rates of CKD (49.6% vs. 33.0%), heart failure (54.1% vs. 41.3%), and anemia (38.9% vs. 24.7%) (all p<0.001). Crude outcomes were worse in OAC failure versus tolerant patients: mortality (22.1% vs. 13.0%), stroke/TIA (22.6% vs. 14.9%), major bleeding (53.3% vs. 16.0%), and 30-day readmission (24.8% vs. 19.9%) (all p<0.001). After adjustment, OAC failure remained independently associated with higher major bleeding (aOR 4.93, 95% CI 4.59-5.28), mortality (aOR 1.35, 95% CI 1.24-1.47), stroke/TIA (aOR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15-1.37), and readmission (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01-1.17) (all p≤0.033). The near 5-fold excess bleeding risk persisted despite adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: OAC failure patients comprise a large proportion of LAAO recipients and have significantly worse post-procedural outcomes, particularly a marked and persistent bleeding risk. Although stroke risk remained modestly higher after adjustment, attenuation from crude estimates suggests LAAO confers meaningful thromboembolic protection in this high-risk group. Prior bleeding history appears to be a dominant driver of post-LAAO hemorrhagic risk, underscoring the need for tailored post-procedural management and antithrombotic strategies.
title: Abstract 4312: OAC Failure as an Indication for LAAO: Post-Procedural Outcomes of Patients with Prior Anticoagulation-Related Bleeding: Multivariable-Adjusted Analysis

abstract: Background: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for cardiogenic shock (CS) carries substantial in-hospital mortality, yet reliable bedside predictors of outcome during the early support phase remain limited. Serial lactate measurement is widely available, but its trajectory after ECMO initiation has not been systematically characterized in a large real-world cohort. We examined whether admission lactate and 24-hour lactate clearance independently predict 30-day mortality and survival to ECMO decannulation. Methods: Using the TriNetX Research Network (108 healthcare organizations, 6,904 CS-VA-ECMO patients), we identified 5,436 patients with admission lactate and 4,649 with 24-hour paired lactate measurements enabling clearance calculation. Lactate clearance was defined as (admission – 24h lactate)/admission х 100%. The primary outcomes were 30-day all-cause mortality and survival to ECMO decannulation. Discriminative performance was assessed by ROC analysis with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Outcome gradients were examined across clinically defined clearance categories and empirical tertiles with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis (log-rank test). Results: One-third of patients (33.8%, n=1,572) had worsening lactate (negative clearance) by 24 hours. Admission lactate modestly but significantly discriminated 30-day mortality (AUC=0.612, 95% CI 0.597-0.629). The 24-hour and 48-hour clearance metrics provided complementary discrimination (AUC=0.556 and 0.560 respectively). Outcome gradients were pronounced across lactate trajectory categories: patients with worsening lactate (<0% clearance) had 30-day mortality of 52.9% and decannulation rate of 43.4%, compared to 43.5% and 52.5% in those with high clearance (≥30%), representing a 9.4 percentage-point absolute mortality difference. Across tertiles of 24-hour clearance, 30-day mortality declined monotonically from 53.0% (lowest tertile) to 45.7% to 43.4% (highest tertile), while decannulation rates improved from 43.4% to 50.5% to 52.5%. Kaplan-Meier survival curves demonstrated early and sustained separation favoring higher lactate clearance (log-rank p<0.001, lowest vs. highest tertile). Conclusions: In the largest real-world analysis to date, one in three CS-VA-ECMO patients fails to clear lactate within the first 24 hours, and this failure is associated with nearly 10 percentage points higher 30-day mortality and substantially lower rates of successful ECMO weaning. Admission lactate and 24-hour clearance together provide actionable early prognostic information that may inform escalation decisions and patient selection for advanced therapies. Prospective validation of lactate trajectory thresholds as decision-support tools is warranted.
title: Abstract 4332: Lactate Trajectory During the First 24 Hours of VA-ECMO Support Predicts 30-Day Mortality and Decannulation Success in Cardiogenic Shock: A Nationwide Real-World Analysis

abstract: Background: Hot-phase arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inflammatory phenotype that mimics acute myocarditis but may reveal an inherited arrhythmogenic substrate, especially desmoplakin (DSP) cardiomyopathy. Objective: To synthesize evidence and propose an electrophysiology-oriented framework integrating presentation, CMR, genotype, arrhythmic risk, and management. Methods: We performed a structured evidence map of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science from January 2020 to May 2026 using terms for ACM, desmosomal genes, myocarditis-like episodes, CMR, ventricular arrhythmias, HF, immunosuppression, exercise, and inflammation. Eligible studies included systematic reviews, clinical cohorts, CMR studies, treatment reports, and translational investigations. We extracted genotype, sample size, event rates, and treatment outcomes. Because of heterogeneity in study design, genotype enrichment, and outcome definitions, findings were summarized descriptively rather than pooled quantitatively. Results: Evidence supports hot-phase ACM as a genotype-enriched inflammatory-arrhythmic phenotype. In a systematic review of myocarditis-like ACM, DSP was the most common gene, accounting for 69% of reported hot-phase cases. In a cohort of 800 DSP carriers, sustained ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 17.4%, HF hospitalizations in 9.0%, and myocardial injury episodes in 8.8%. Myocardial injury was associated with a higher risk of subsequent arrhythmias and HF hospitalizations. In a DSP-ERADOS treatment analysis of 1,014 DSP patients, 177 had at least one myocarditis-like episode. Immunosuppression during the first episode was associated with lower subsequent ventricular arrhythmia (HR 0.18) and HF hospitalization risk (HR 0.09) in observational data, whereas NSAIDs or colchicine were not associated with improved outcomes. CMR distinguishes active injury from established substrate: edema supports inflammation, whereas subepicardial or ring-like LV late gadolinium enhancement suggests scar. Exercise may promote myocardial injury in DSP carriers. Mechanistic studies implicate NF-kB activation, CCR2-positive macrophage recruitment, and autoimmune signaling. Conclusions: Hot-phase ACM should be recognized as a genotype-driven inflammatory-arrhythmic phenotype rather than isolated myocarditis. In patients with recurrent chest pain, troponin elevation, ECG changes, normal coronaries, ventricular arrhythmias, or nonischemic CMR abnormalities, inherited ACM, especially DSP cardiomyopathy, should be considered. A framework integrating CMR, genotype, rhythm phenotype, family screening, exercise counseling, and ICD risk assessment may improve risk stratification. Immunosuppression remains investigational pending prospective validation.
title: Abstract 4396: The Inflammatory “Hot Phase” of Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy: A Mechanistic and Imaging-Based Framework for Disease Progression and Clinical Risk Stratification

abstract: To describe a rare case of complete postoperative vision loss due to cortical blindness following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and to highlight the importance of early recognition and management of this uncommon complication. Introduction: Postoperative vision loss (POVL) is a rare but devastating complication of non-ocular surgery, encompassing ischemic optic neuropathy, central retinal artery occlusion, and cortical blindness. Risk factors include patient-related conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and vascular disease, as well as perioperative factors including prolonged surgery, significant blood loss, prone positioning, and intraoperative hypotension. The incidence of POVL is highest in cardiac and spinal procedures, and the underlying mechanism is thought to involve impaired vascular perfusion to components of the visual pathway secondary to elevated venous pressure, interstitial edema, or infarction. Patient Information: An 81-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis, prior transient ischemic attacks, left carotid endarterectomy, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia underwent elective TAVR. Clinical Findings and Timeline: Shortly after the procedure, she developed acute binocular vision loss, prompting activation of a stroke code. Neurological examination revealed cortical blindness and a mild left facial droop (NIHSS 4). Diagnostic Evaluation and Reasoning: CT and CTA head/neck were unremarkable for ischemia, hemorrhage, or large vessel occlusion. Ophthalmologic evaluation showed no intraocular pathology. MRI revealed embolic-appearing infarcts in bilateral occipital lobes and cerebellar hemispheres. Therapeutic Intervention: Given her disabling symptoms, tenecteplase was administered. Follow-up, outcomes and Adverse Events: Her vision returned to baseline during hospitalization, and she was discharged on aspirin monotherapy. Discussion and Synthesis: POVL following TAVR is exceedingly rare, likely resulting from embolic phenomena related to procedural manipulation of the aortic valve or calcified aortic structures. Early recognition of postoperative visual symptoms and timely thrombolysis contributed to this patient’s favorable recovery. This case highlights the importance of vigilance for postoperative visual symptoms following non-ocular surgical procedures and immediate activation of stroke protocols to allow for timely treatment and to maximize the possibility of visual recovery.
title: Abstract 4417: A Patient with Complete Post-Operative Vision Loss Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Successfully Treated with Tenecteplase

abstract: Background: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with right heart failure and increased mortality. Transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) offers a less invasive alternative to surgery, but its impact on clinical outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing TTVI (edge-to-edge repair or valve replacement) with optimal medical therapy in patients with significant TR. PubMed and EMBASE were searched. Outcomes included Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) score, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), all-cause mortality, cardiac death, and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year. Continuous and dichotomous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 . Results: Four RCTs (n = 1,614) were included. TTVI significantly improved KCCQ score (MD +11.71; 95% CI 11.33-12.09; P < 0.00001) and 6MWD (MD +27.54 m; 95% CI 7.06-48.02; P < 0.00001). There were no significant differences in all-cause mortality (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.80-1.37; P = 0.67), cardiac death (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.94-1.71; P = 0.12), or heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.71-1.18; P = 0.48). Findings were consistent across trials with low heterogeneity. Conclusions: TTVI provides meaningful improvements in symptoms and functional capacity but does not reduce mortality or heart failure hospitalization at 1 year. These findings highlight a persistent gap between symptomatic benefit and hard outcomes, underscoring the need for longer follow-up and earlier intervention strategies.
title: Abstract 4538: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Intervention Improves Symptoms but Not Survival A Meta Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a systemic inflammatory disorder linked to myocardial remodeling and atrial arrhythmogenesis, but national-level data evaluating its association with new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) remain limited.Research Hypothesis: We hypothesized that hospitalized patients with MASH would have higher odds of new-onset in-hospital AF compared to propensity-matched non-MASH controls, independent of demographic, cardiovascular, and liver disease severity covariates. Methods: Retrospective cohort study using the 2022 National Inpatient Sample. Adult MASH hospitalizations identified by ICD-10-CM codes. Excluded prior AF/flutter, AF on admission, ablation/rhythm devices, pregnancy, elective admissions, interhospital transfers, missing data. Primary outcome: new-onset in-hospital AF. Secondary outcomes: mortality, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, AKI, mechanical ventilation, LOS, charges, non-home discharge. Survey-weighted multivariable regression adjusted for demographics, hospital characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, liver disease severity, and Elixhauser. Sensitivity: propensity score matching (1:1 nearest-neighbor, caliper 0.05; SMDs <0.1 achieved), IPW, subgroup analyses, interaction testing, and E-value. Results: 2,362 MASH hospitalizations. New-onset AF: 8.9% (MASH) vs. 5.8% (matched non-MASH); absolute risk difference 3.1% (p=0.012); NNH=32. Multivariable: MASH independently associated with AF (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.71, p=0.002). E-value point estimate = 1.96 (lower CI 1.51). MASH also associated with mortality (aOR 1.36), acute heart failure (1.51), cardiogenic shock (1.33), AKI (1.29), mechanical ventilation (1.27), prolonged LOS (+1.3d), higher charges (+$14,870), non-home discharge (1.22); all p<0.05. Sensitivity analyses consistent. Conclusions: MASH was independently associated with a 42% relative and 3.1% absolute increase in new-onset AF plus multiple adverse outcomes. Residual confounding may persist, but E-value analysis supports robustness. These findings highlight the electrophysiologic implications of MASH and may support heightened rhythm surveillance in high-risk hospitalized patients.
title: Abstract 4565: Association of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis with New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation and Adverse In-Hospital Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Isolated IgG4-related myocarditis is an exceedingly rare cause of progressive nonischemic cardiomyopathy and may only be recognized on myocardial histology. Case: A 48-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension presented with 6 months of progressive exertional dyspnea and edema. Initial TTE showed LVEF 30% with global hypokinesia; coronary angiography and CT coronary angiography were normal. Labs revealed NT-proBNP 6,000 pg/mL, normal troponin, ESR 40 mm/h, and CRP 22 mg/L. Viral, autoimmune, and infiltrative work-up (including serum/urine electrophoresis, iron studies, ACE level) was unrevealing. Over 5 months, he developed recurrent decompensated heart failure despite maximally uptitrated guideline-directed therapy, with LVEF falling to 15% and RV dysfunction. Endomyocardial biopsy showed dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates with storiform fibrosis; immunostaining revealed >40% of plasma cells IgG4-positive and >50 IgG4+ cells/high-power field, consistent with IgG4-related myocarditis. Serum IgG4 was 380 mg/dL; PET-CT showed no extracardiac uptake. Management and outcome: Pulse IV methylprednisolone followed by high-dose oral prednisone and azathioprine was initiated. However, the patient deteriorated to INTERMACS 2 shock requiring inotropes and biventricular mechanical circulatory support. Given extensive fibrosis on surgical LV core biopsies and lack of extracardiac IgG4-RD amenable to targeted debulking, he was listed urgently and underwent orthotopic heart transplantation. Explant histology confirmed diffuse IgG4-related myocarditis with severe interstitial fibrosis. At 1-year follow-up, he remains NYHA I with normal graft function on standard immunosuppression. Conclusion: Isolated IgG4-related myocarditis should be considered in rapidly progressive nonischemic cardiomyopathy with biopsy showing IgG4-rich lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates. Early histologic diagnosis is key, as some patients may respond to immunosuppression, whereas others require timely mechanical support and transplantation due to irreversible fibrosis.
title: Abstract 4599: Isolated IgG4-Related Myocarditis Causing End-Stage Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy Requiring Heart Transplantation

abstract: Background: Paravalvular leak (PVL) following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common, and while moderate-to-severe PVL is consistently associated with adverse outcomes, the long-term clinical impact of mild PVL remains uncertain. Question: Is there an association between mild PVL and mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in TAVR patients? Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies comparing outcomes in patients with mild versus no PVL following TAVR. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane was conducted from inception through March 2026. Two independent reviewers screened studies and conducted full-text reviews using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Random-effects models were used to pool hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed according to follow-up duration (1-2 years, 2-5 years, ≥5 years) and heart failure rehospitalization. Results: 33 studies met inclusion criteria; due to variability in reporting and time-to-event data, 20 studies contributed to the primary all-cause mortality analysis. Overall, across all follow-up periods (median follow-up 2.25 years), mild PVL was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.18-1.41; p < 0.0001; I 2 = 55.7%). Although there was no significant difference in mortality at 1-2 years (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.94-1.25; p = 0.25; I 2 = 0%), the difference emerged at 2-5 years (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.26-1.64; p < 0.0001; I 2 = 48.2%) and persisted at ≥5 years (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.09-1.35; p = 0.0006; I 2 = 58.5%) (Figure 1). These associations persisted in both the VARC-2 and VARC-3 eras. Mild PVL was also associated with increased hospitalizations for heart failure (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.05-1.49; p = 0.011; I 2 = 0%), though this was mostly driven by a single 2-year follow-up study. Conclusions: Our analysis demonstrated that patients with mild PVL experienced a higher risk of all-cause mortality and may be at higher risk of heart failure hospitalization, though confounding from the burden of calcification, bicuspid anatomy, or post-dilatation cannot be excluded. Mild PVL should not be considered benign; efforts should be taken to minimize PVL at implantation, and close longitudinal follow-up is essential.
title: Abstract 4631: Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Mild Paravalvular Leak Following TAVI

abstract: Background: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) are currently the mainstay treatment for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). Dasatinib, a second generation TKI, is effective in both chronic and advanced phase patients that is widely used in practice today. Common medication side effects include pleural effusions and pulmonary hypertension, with cardiomyopathy being a rare complication. Although rare, early recognition of drug-induced cardiomyopathy is critical to prevent significant morbidity and mortality. Case Presentation: A 69-year-old man with chronic phase CML, who recently transitioned from Imatinib to Dasatinib three weeks prior, presented with rapidly progressive dyspnea, tachypnea, and severe orthopnea. Upon presentation, he was hemodynamically stable, with symptom improvement after a dose of intravenous furosemide. Electrocardiogram revealed normal sinus rhythm with occasional PVCs, T wave abnormalities in the anterolateral leads, and prolonged QT interval at 556 msec. Laboratory evaluation revealed an elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, consistent with demand ischemia. Chest radiography demonstrated diffuse interstitial and central vascular congestion consistent with pulmonary edema. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed new left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 35-40%, grade II diastolic dysfunction, and hypokinesis of the inferior and inferolateral wall, representing a significant decline from a previously normal ejection fraction three years earlier. Exercise myocardial perfusion imaging demonstrated no inducible ischemia with a Duke treadmill score of 9. At discharge, the patient was started on guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure.Discussion: In the absence of prior cardiac history, with normal previous ejection fraction, Dasatinib can be considered a primary cause of acute heart failure. The medication was held immediately following hematology-oncology consultation, and the patient was started on GDMT for heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction. Emerging research on Dasatinib-induced cardiomyopathy has shown the potential relation of off-target inhibition of cardiomyocyte survival signaling pathways. While the incidence of cardiotoxicity remains low, this case highlights the importance of early recognition and multidisciplinary management of acute heart failure symptoms following recent TKI initiation or transition. Conclusion: Cardiomyopathy with worsening EF is a very rare but clinically significant complication of Dasatinib. Clinical practitioners should be aware of TKI-induced cardiac dysfunction when seeing patients with acute heart failure symptoms following initiation of therapy. Prompt recognition and intervention can significantly reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.
title: Abstract 4646: When Leukemia Treatment Breaks the Heart: Dasatinib-Induced Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background/Purpose: Atrial fibrillation (AF) develops in 30-50% of patients with mechanical mitral valve replacement (MVR), but catheter ablation is underutilized owing to concerns about catheter entrapment and procedural safety. No systematic review has evaluated ablation in this population. We therefore assessed whether catheter ablation in mechanical MVR is safe and effective, and whether outcomes differ from non-MVR controls. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO: CRD420261324697), we searched PubMed, CENTRAL, and Embase from inception through February 8, 2026, for studies of catheter ablation for AF in adults with mechanical MVR. We assessed risk of bias with ROBINS-I (comparative studies) and the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist (single-arm studies), and certainty with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analysis used generalized linear mixed models for proportions and inverse-variance methods for comparative outcomes. Results: Fourteen studies (489 patients; all observational) met inclusion criteria. The primary safety concern — catheter entrapment — did not occur in any of 470 patients (0/470; upper 95% CI ≤0.6% by Rule of Three; GRADE: High). Other adverse events were infrequent: tamponade 0.2% (0.0-1.0%), stroke/TIA 0.6% (0.0-2.5%), and vascular complications 3.4% (2.1-5.6%). Freedom from arrhythmia was 59.0% (95% CI: 46.9-70.1%; k=6; I 2 =79.1%; GRADE: Low), with a 95% prediction interval of 31.6-81.8%. Compared with non-MVR controls, MVR patients had non-significantly lower freedom from arrhythmia (RR=0.88; 0.74-1.05; P=0.14; k=4); this gap narrowed to RR=0.96 after excluding a study with serious confounding. MVR patients underwent repeat ablation more frequently than controls, with an absolute risk increase of 12.1% (95% CI: 3.5-23.5%; RR=1.62; 1.18-2.21; P=0.003; I 2 =0%). In a within-study analysis, pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone carried a 3.67-fold higher recurrence hazard than extended lesion sets (adjusted HR=3.67; 95% CI 1.32-10.25; P=0.013). Conclusions: Catheter ablation for AF in mechanical MVR is feasible, with zero entrapment and 59.0% single-procedure freedom from arrhythmia; entrapment concerns should no longer deter referral. Patients should be counseled about higher repeat ablation requirements, and extended lesion sets beyond PVI alone may improve outcomes.
title: Abstract 4649: Outcomes of Percutaneous Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Mechanical Mitral Valve Prostheses: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) and SGLT-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) have redefined cardiovascular medicine. SGLT-2i are now foundational guideline-directed therapies for heart failure, while GLP-1 RA have emerged as critical agents for cardiovascular risk reduction in patients with atherosclerotic disease. While clinical trials established their efficacy, real-world adoption patterns, pharmaceutical expenditure, and payer burden remain poorly defined. Methods: We analyzed data from the 2016-2023 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, identifying adults with HF and MI. We estimated the prevalence of GLP-1 RA and SGLT-2i use, temporal utilization trends, and mean annual per-person expenditures stratified by payer. Estimates were generated using survey weights with Taylor series linearization, and trends were evaluated using design-based F statistics. Results: We analyzed weighted populations of 13.8 million adults with HF and 37.8 million with MI. While overall use of these agents remained low, it accelerated sharply during the study period. In the HF cohort, GLP-1 RA use was 3.6% and SGLT-2i use 5.8%; in the MI cohort, use was 4.5% and 5.2%, respectively. Utilization growth was concentrated in recent years (P=0.01 for GLP-1 RA in HF; P<0.001 for all other groups), with SGLT-2i use in HF exhibiting the steepest trajectory. Mean annual per-person expenditures were substantial: $285 (GLP-1 RA) and $290 (SGLT-2i) for HF patients; $342 and $329 for those with MI. Medicare was the dominant payer across all groups, covering 50-67% of costs, while out-of-pocket spending remained relatively stable ($12-25). Total expenditures rose markedly, with mean SGLT-2i spending in HF increasing from $35 in 2016 to nearly $980 by 2023. Conclusion: Adoption of these new therapies for HF and MI accelerated between 2016 and 2023, yet remains confined to a small fraction of the eligible population. Simultaneously, per-person costs have risen steeply, placing a disproportionate financial load on Medicare. These findings emphasize that improving real-world implementation requires addressing medication access and the long-term cost burden on public payers alongside clinical guideline adoption.
title: Abstract 4690: Trends and Expenditure of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and SGLT-2 Inhibitors in Adults with Heart Failure and Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Introduction: Next-generation immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies, and bispecific T-cell engagers (BiTEs), have revolutionized oncology but present distinct cardiovascular immune-related adverse events (irAEs) with mechanistic and clinical implications divergent from traditional anthracycline cardiotoxicity. This umbrella review synthesizes the cardiovascular toxicity profiles, mechanistic distinctions, and clinical management strategies across all three immunotherapy classes.Research Question:How do the incidence, underlying mechanisms, and clinical outcomes of cardiovascular immune-related adverse events (irAEs) differ across next-generation immunotherapies (ICIs, CAR-T cells, and BiTEs) Methods: We conducted a comprehensive systematic search across PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar for systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large observational studies reporting cardiovascular irAEs from ICIs (anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-CTLA-4, and combination regimens), CAR-T therapies, and BiTEs. Primary outcomes included incidence rates, CTCAE severity grading, mortality data, and mechanistic pathways for myocarditis, arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, QTc prolongation), heart failure, pericarditis, and vascular events. Results: Overall cardiovascular irAE incidence ranged from 1.14-5% for ICIs and 16.7% (95% CI 13.8-20.0%) for CAR-T therapies. ICI-associated myocarditis occurred in 0.5-1% of patients but carried a 30-50% mortality rate, with combination anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 regimens associated with the highest overall treatment-related mortality risk (1.23%). CAR-T cardiotoxicity manifested predominantly as arrhythmias (6.5%, 95% CI 2.9-11.5%), supraventricular arrhythmias (7.79%, 95% CI 4.87-11.27%), left ventricular dysfunction (8.68%, 95% CI 2.26-17.97%), and heart failure (3.87%, 95% CI 1.77-6.62%), with an 18.7% incidence in patients with CRS grade ≥2. ICI-associated atrial fibrillation occurred in 7.6% (95% CI 1.0-14.1%). Mechanistically, CAR-T and BiTE cardiotoxicity results from CRS-mediated cytokine storms (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-γ) causing endothelial dysfunction and direct myocardial injury, while ICI cardiotoxicity involves T-cell-mediated autoimmunity with CD3+/CD4+/CD8+ lymphocytic infiltrates and cross-reactive cardiac antigens. QT dispersion (QTd) increased significantly post-ICI therapy (32±16 ms vs. 47±19 ms, p<0.0001). Conclusions: Next-generation immunotherapies demonstrate class-specific cardiovascular toxicity hierarchies: ICIs present rare but highly fatal myocarditis, while CAR-T therapies show higher overall cardiovascular event rates dominated by CRS-associated arrhythmias and heart failure.
title: Abstract 4706: Cardiovascular Toxicities of Next-Generation Immunotherapies — An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses

abstract: Background: Pulmonary embolism (PE) causes significant morbidity and mortality with presentations ranging from an incidental finding to hemodynamic collapse. Most PEs arise from lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (DVT). The clinical significance of DVT and PE is further amplified by the presence of a patent foramen ovale (PFO), present in roughly 25% of adults. We present a case of DVT complicated by bilateral PE and cerebrovascular accident. Case Description: A 75-year-old male with hypertension and type II diabetes, presented with generalized weakness. He was tachycardic. Elevated troponin I prompted a computed tomography angiogram of the chest, which showed bilateral PEs, with right ventricle (RV) enlargement and possible thrombus. Heparin was started. Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed RV dysfunction, presence of PFO and a mobile thrombus appearing to be attached to the interatrial septum and extending to the right atrium (RA), with prolapse through the tricuspid valve. Transesophageal echocardiogram confirmed the presence of a tunneled PFO, but the thrombus was no longer seen and presumed embolized. Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) of the PE was initiated. Heparin was paused due to elevated activated partial thromboplastin time (>200 seconds). Three hours later, he developed left-sided deficits. Imaging revealed right internal carotid artery (ICA) occlusion. USAT was discontinued and he underwent aspiration thrombectomy of the right ICA. As systemic anticoagulation was contraindicated in the immediate post thrombectomy period and he was known to have residual DVT from lower extremity ultrasound, an IVC filter was placed to prevent further episodes. He was ultimately discharged to rehabilitation and is progressing well. Discussion: Paradoxical embolism is a rare but life-threatening complication of DVT in the presence of PFO, especially following PE. Acute PE results in an abrupt increase in pulmonary vascular resistance and right-sided pressures resulting in reversal of the typical left-to-right pressure gradient, facilitating thrombus passage from the RA to the systemic circulation, with cerebral circulation being the most frequent target. This causes further morbidity and mortality. A meta-analysis demonstrated that among patients with PE, the presence of a PFO confers a 5.36-fold increased odds of ischemic stroke. Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are primarily indicated for patients with absolute contraindications to anticoagulants or failure of anticoagulation. While no guidelines support routine prophylactic filter placement in VTE with PFO, isolated reports describe its use in select high-risk scenarios with situations similar to our case. Conclusion: VTE in the setting of PFO is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Temporary prophylactic IVC filter placement should be considered in high-risk patients.
title: Abstract 4712: A Clot in Transit: A Case of Venous Thromboembolism Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism and Cerebrovascular Accident Due to Patent Foramen Ovale

abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) and Impaired Cognitive (IC) disease share sociodemographic, genetic, and clinical factors but the association of IC with statin use in CAD remains unclear. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that IC is associated with statin use, and the effect could be modified based on sex, APO (ε) genotypes or lipid level changes in CAD. METHODS: We analyzed unique NIH AllofUS participants with CAD (age≥60 yrs) enrolled from 2017-2023 (Figure 1). We defined CAD as having a history of angina/myocardial infarction/chronic ischemic heart disease or having percutaneous coronary intervention/CABG, and IC as having mild cognitive impairment and all-cause dementia, defined using ICD/SNOMED codes. We assessed the association between IC and statin use using logistic regression analysis, while adjusting for clinical factors, sociodemographics, and APO (ε) genotypes before and after propensity score matching. We further performed stratified analysis by sex, and APO (ε) genotypes. We finally assessed the association between IC and statin users, based magnitude on the change in lipid levels before CAD and after IC (TC- Total cholesterol, LDL - low density lipoprotein, HDL- High Density Lipoprotein). We defined significance at p < 0.05. RESULTS: The cohort included 22,089 participants with CAD and 1343 with IC. Thirty-nine percent of participants were females, 77% were European, 13% were African American, and 9% were of Admixed American ancestry. The proportion of IC was higher ( 6.8% vs 3.5%, p<0.001 ) in statin users (n=17,191) vs non-statin users (n=4,898). IC was significantly associated with statin use ( OR:1.70;1.40-2.10, p = 4.9e-7 ) after adjustment for clinical factors, sociodemographics, and APO (ε) genotypes. After propensity-score matching between IC and CAD, we observed an association between IC and statin use ( OR:1.55;1.24-1.94, p =1e-4 ). In stratified analysis, the association between IC and statin use was strongest in the APO ε3/ε3 group ( OR:2.04;1.53-2.75, p = 1e-6 ), and in females ( OR:2.20;1.60-3.06, p = 2.e-6 ) compared to males ( OR:1.43;1.10-1.90, p = 0.01 ). While we did not observe any change in association between IC and statin use, based on the magnitude of decrease in TC and LDL levels, we observed an increased association between IC and statin users having higher HDL increase ( > 10 mg/dl: OR:1.95;1.44-2.66, p=1e-5 ) as compared to statin users with lesser HDL increase ( ≤ 10mg/dl: OR:1.61;1.22-2.15, p=8e-4 ). CONCLUSION: In the AllofUS cohort, IC was significantly associated with statin use in CAD participants. We observed the strongest association in the APO ε3ε3 group, among females, and with a greater increase in HDL levels in statin users.
title: Abstract 4718: Association of Cognitive Impairment with Statin Use in Coronary Artery Disease Across APO (ε) Genotypes in AllofUS

abstract: Background: Reduced-dose direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used after left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), but their comparative efficacy and safety versus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remain uncertain, with no consensus on the optimal post-procedural antithrombotic strategy. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesised that reduced-dose DOAC therapy would reduce device-related thrombosis and thromboembolic events without increasing major bleeding compared with DAPT following LAAC. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts comparing reduced-dose DOAC (apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10-15 mg once daily) with DAPT after successful LAAC in adults (≥18 years) with NVAF was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov through February 2026. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 and χ 2 statistics. Analyses were performed with RevMan 5.4. Results: Seven studies (3 RCTs, 4 cohorts) including 2,126 patients (reduced-dose DOAC = 1,088; DAPT = 1,038) were analysed. Reduced-dose DOAC significantly reduced composite thromboembolic events (RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.10-0.39; I 2 =0%), ischaemic stroke (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.13-0.80; I 2 =0%), and device-related thrombosis (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.18-0.60; I 2 =0%) compared with DAPT. The net clinical benefit composite (thromboembolism plus major bleeding) favoured reduced-dose DOAC (RR 0.36, 95% CI 0.19-0.70; I 2 =63%), with apixaban-predominant subgroups showing the strongest effects (RR 0.14, 95% CI 0.05-0.36). Major bleeding was lower (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.35-0.83; I 2 =0%), any bleeding reduced (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.88; I 2 =64%), and minor bleeding trended lower (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.42-1.02; I 2 =34%), while cardiovascular (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.23-1.92) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.42-1.30) did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion: Reduced-dose DOAC, particularly apixaban-based regimens, represents a favourable antithrombotic strategy after LAAC in NVAF, significantly reducing thromboembolic events, device-related thrombosis, and major bleeding without excess mortality. These findings support reduced-dose DOAC as an effective post-procedural option in appropriately selected patients, though the significant heterogeneity observed in composite and any-bleeding outcomes warrants cautious interpretation and further confirmatory trials.
title: Abstract 4734: Reduced-Dose Direct Oral Anticoagulant versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients with Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Infants with functionally univentricular heart disease (FUHD) and heart failure have markedly high mortality. Ventricular assist devices (VADs) have emerged as a lifesaving therapy; however, the timing of VAD placement is highly variable. We aimed to assess whether the timing of VAD placement is associated with survival. Hypothesis: VAD placement with or prior to stage 1 palliation (S1P) is associated with improved survival compared with VAD placement after S1P. Methods: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Congenital Heart Surgery Database and Pedimacs Database were merged and queried for infants < 6 months of age with FUHD who underwent VAD placement. The timing of VAD placement was defined as early if the VAD was placed with or prior to S1P or late if VAD placement occurred after S1P. Survival analyses employed Kaplan-Meier curves, with censoring for events such as transplantation or recovery. Univariable and multivariable models, adjusting for clinical covariates, were constructed. The primary outcome of interest was survival after VAD placement. Results: From September 19, 2012, to December 31, 2024, 93 infants with FUHD underwent VAD placement: 47 early and 46 late. The most common diagnoses were hypoplastic left heart syndrome (n=48, 52%) and pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum (n=24, 26%). At the time of VAD implantation, infants with late VAD implantation were more likely to be older (mean age 0.2 +/- 0.1 years vs 0.1 +/- 0.1 years, p=0.04), intubated (98% vs 80%, p=0.008), and in critical cardiogenic shock (41% vs 17%, p=0.02), compared to those with early VAD implantation (Table). Among infants with late VAD implantation, 33% were alive on device, 15% had undergone transplant, and 46% died on device at 3 months post-VAD implantation. Among infants with early VAD implantation, 55% were alive on device, 28% had undergone transplant, and 13% died on device at 3 months post-VAD implantation. In a multivariable hazard model for survival, late VAD implantation was associated with a greater risk of death on device compared to early implantation (Figure) (hazard ratio 4.2, 95% CI, 1.9 - 9.3, p<0.001). Outcomes were similar among paracorporeal pulsatile and paracorporeal continuous flow devices. Conclusion: Infants with VAD implantation after failed S1P were more likely to be in critical cardiogenic shock at implantation and were 4 times as likely to die on support compared to those with early VAD implantation. These data may help inform clinical decisions and timing of VAD placement in high-risk infants with FUHD.
title: Abstract 4736: Early vs. Late Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Infants with Functionally Univentricular Heart Disease: An Analysis of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery and Pedimacs Databases

abstract: Background: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), marked by age-related somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells (mostly TET2 and DNMT3A), is a novel cardiovascular risk factor. Affecting approximately 10% of adults aged ≥70, CHIP links aging and cardiovascular pathology by driving systemic "inflammaging" via innate immune activation (NLRP3 inflammasome, IL-1β). This sustained inflammatory signaling promotes macrophage-mediated atherosclerotic plaque instability and mesenchymal calcification in aortic valves. Research Question: How do specific CHIP mutations, predominantly TET2 and DNMT3A, influence the incidence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases? Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library till Feb 2026 to identify relevant studies. This umbrella review synthesizes meta-analytic and cohort evidence (e.g., UK Biobank, All of Us, WHI) evaluating CHIP-associated cardiovascular endpoints. We focus on mutation-specific hazard ratios (HR) for coronary artery disease, heart failure (HF) subtypes, aortic valve stenosis (AVS), and post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) mortality to map the clinical phenotypes of TET2 and DNMT3A. Results: CHIP carriers exhibit a 1.9-fold increased coronary heart disease risk and a 4-fold early-onset myocardial infarction risk. Phenotypes diverge by mutation: TET2 strongly drives incident HF with preserved ejection fraction (HR=2.50, 95%CI 1.54-4.06) and elevated AVS risk, whereas DNMT3A shows attenuated HF associations (HR=1.11, 95%CI 0.74-1.67). However, combined DNMT3A/TET2 carriers face 3-fold higher post-TAVR mortality (HR=3.1, 95%CI 1.2-8.1) and doubled HF mortality (HR=2.1, 95%CI 1.0-4.2). Mechanistically, TET2 deficiency directly increases IL-1β/IL-6 secretion, while DNMT3A amplifies bone marrow inflammatory signaling to propagate systemic inflammaging. Conclusion: TET2 and DNMT3A mutations drive overlapping cardiovascular morbidities via innate immune activation. CHIP is a targetable inflammatory axis, refining prognostication and highlighting therapeutic avenues (e.g., IL-1β antagonism) for atherosclerosis, HF, and AVS.
title: Abstract 4738: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential as a Cardiovascular Driver - An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses

abstract: Background: Functional tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is common in adults with atrial septal defect (ASD) due to chronic right heart volume overload. Whether TR resolves after transcatheter ASD closure and which factors predict residual TR remain incompletely characterized, particularly in Asian populations. Hypothesis: Transcatheter ASD closure promotes right heart reverse remodeling and reduces TR severity; older age, greater TR vena contracta (VC), and lower right ventricular (RV) function independently predict residual moderate-to-severe TR. Methods: A prospective, longitudinal, single-center study enrolled 305 consecutive adults undergoing transcatheter secundum ASD closure at University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City (September 2019 to March 2025). Transthoracic echocardiography was performed pre-procedure and at 24 hours, 1 week, 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months post-procedure. Right atrial and RV dimensions, RV function (TAPSE, S-prime, fractional area change [FAC]), pulmonary artery pressures, tricuspid annular diameter, and TR grade were serially assessed. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of residual moderate-to-severe TR at 6 months. Results: Right atrial and RV dimensions decreased significantly at all post-procedure timepoints versus baseline (p<0.001). RV systolic function indices declined transiently then recovered by 1 month. The proportion of patients with moderate-to-severe TR decreased from 63.6% at baseline to 23.1% at 6 months (p<0.001). Among patients with complete 6-month data, 88.9% of those with severe TR and 64.3% with moderate TR at baseline improved. Three independent predictors of residual moderate-to-severe TR were identified: age (OR 1.05; p=0.026), VC (OR 1.63; p=0.031), and TAPSE (OR 0.78; p=0.003). Optimal cutoffs were age ≥48.5 years (AUC 0.692; sensitivity 61.8%, specificity 74.7%), VC ≥3.45 mm (AUC 0.656; sensitivity 96.8%, specificity 34.9%), and TAPSE ≤25.2 mm (AUC 0.737; sensitivity 76.5%, specificity 67.0%). Conclusion: Transcatheter ASD closure in adults produces significant right heart reverse remodeling and substantially reduces TR severity, most markedly within 6 months. Residual moderate-to-severe TR persists in a meaningful proportion of patients and is independently predicted by older age, larger VC, and lower TAPSE before the procedure. These parameters should be routinely assessed for pre-procedural risk stratification.
title: Abstract 4754: Residual Tricuspid Regurgitation and Right Heart Remodelling After Transcatheter Atrial Septal Defect Closure in Adults

abstract: Background: Reduced skeletal muscle strength has been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but its relationship with subclinical myocardial injury and cardiac stress biomarkers in the general population remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between quadriceps muscle strength and circulating cardiac biomarkers among U.S. adults without overt cardiovascular disease. Methods: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of participants aged ≥50 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2002 with available quadriceps strength testing and cardiac biomarker data. Quadriceps strength was normalized within sex and standardized to generate sex-specific z-scores and quartiles. Primary outcomes included high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Survey-weighted multivariable linear regression models were constructed adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, cardiometabolic, renal, and inflammatory variables. Secondary analyses evaluated hs-cTnI assays across Abbott, Siemens, and Ortho platforms. Results: A total of 2,305 adults without self-reported Cardiovascular disease representing approximately 48.9 Million US adults were included. In fully adjusted analyses, each 1-standard deviation (SD) increase in quadriceps strength was associated with 6.3% lower hs-cTnT concentrations (β –0.065; 95% CI –0.090 to –0.040; p=0.001) and 17.0% lower NT-proBNP concentrations (β –0.186; 95% CI –0.246 to –0.126; p<0.001). Compared with participants in the strongest quadriceps strength quartile, individuals in the weakest quartile demonstrated 20.0% higher hs-cTnT concentrations (95% CI 9.9%-31.0%; p=0.010) and 71.7% higher NT-proBNP concentrations (95% CI 44.1%-104.6%; p=0.002). Significant dose-response relationships were observed for both biomarkers (p-for-trend=0.003 for hs-cTnT; p<0.001 for NT-proBNP). Associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses using body weight-normalized strength and after excluding participants with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 or CRP >10 mg/dL. No significant interaction by sex was observed. Secondary analyses showed heterogeneous associations across hs-cTnI assay platforms, with a significant inverse association observed only for the Ortho assay. Conclusions: Lower quadriceps muscle strength was independently associated with higher concentrations of hs-cTnT and NT-proBNP among older U.S. adults without overt cardiovascular disease. The persistence of these associations after adjustment for inflammatory markers and established cardiovascular risk factors suggests that sarcopenia may reflect early subclinical myocardial injury and cardiac stress beyond inflammation alone.
title: Abstract 4756: Lower Quadriceps Muscle Strength is Associated with Elevated Cardiac Biomarkers Among U.S. Adults Without Overt Cardiovascular Disease

abstract: Introduction: The left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LVOT-VTI) is a rapidly obtainable echocardiographic marker of forward stroke distance, but its performance in identifying low invasive cardiac index (CI) before right heart catheterization (RHC) is less well defined. In this study, we evaluated whether early TTE-derived LVOT-VTI identifies low CI on subsequent RHC, compares favorably to LVEF and VTI-derived flow metrics, and is associated with hemodynamic escalation. Research Question: We hypothesized that lower LVOT-VTI would be independently associated with low invasive Fick-derived CI and new inotrope initiation. Methods: This single-institution retrospective cohort study included patients admitted to an academic hospital from 2019 to 2026 for suspected cardiogenic shock (CS) or decompensated heart failure. Patients underwent TTE followed by RHC within 24 hours. Patients with inotrope initiation or discontinuation between TTE and RHC, mechanical circulatory support, or severe aortic regurgitation were excluded. The primary outcome was low invasive CI, defined as CI <2.2 L/min/m 2 . Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic escalation after RHC and VTI-derived measures of forward flow. Multivariable logistic regression for LVOT-VTI was performed using age, heart rate at VTI measurement, LVEF, TTE-RHC interval, and inotrope status as covariates. Discrimination for low invasive CI was assessed using complete-case ROC analysis. Results: Among 177 patients, 96 had low invasive CI ( Table 1 ). Median TTE-RHC interval was similar between groups (4.1 vs. 4.8 hours; P = .21) ( Table 2 ). Median LVOT-VTI was lower in the low CI cohort than the preserved CI cohort (9.6 cm vs. 14.9 cm, P < .001). LVOT-VTI / BSA, LVOT-VTI x HR, and LVOT-VTI x HR / BSA were significantly lower in patients with low invasive CI ( P < .001). In multivariable logistic regression, each 1-cm increase in LVOT-VTI was associated with 26% lower odds of low invasive CI (OR 0.74; 95% CI: 0.65 - 0.83; P < .001). When indexed to BSA, lower LVOT-VTI remained independently associated with low invasive CI (OR 0.62; 95% CI: 0.49 - 0.75, P < .001). LVOT-VTI demonstrated better discrimination for low invasive CI compared to LVEF (AUC 0.828 [95% CI: 0.76 - 0.89] vs. AUC 0.727 [95% CI: 0.65 - 0.80], P = .013) ( Figure 1 ). The optimal LVOT-VTI discriminatory threshold for identifying low invasive CI was 12.6 cm (85.6% sensitive, 72% specific). LVOT-VTI <12.6 cm was associated with greater rates of new inotrope (43% vs. 12%, P < .001) and nitroprusside initiation (9.6% vs. 0%, P = .006) compared to patients with LVOT-VTI ≥12.6 cm. Conclusions: In patients with suspected CS or decompensated heart failure, early LVOT-VTI identifies low invasive CI before RHC and outperforms LVEF, with a discriminatory threshold of 12.6 cm. LVOT-VTI may provide rapid, noninvasive identification of low-flow physiology to guide earlier risk stratification.
title: Abstract 4778: Early Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Velocity-Time Integral Measurement for Identifying Low Invasive Cardiac Index Prior to Right Heart Catheterization

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock carries 30-50% hospital mortality despite advances in mechanical circulatory support and the 2019 AHA cardiogenic shock initiative. Recent national trend analyses have focused on cardiogenic shock subpopulations, leaving all-cause CS mortality and its evolving demographic disparities through 2024 incompletely characterized. Methods: We extracted CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (2011-2024) for decedents with cardiogenic shock (ICD-10 R57.0) as underlying or contributing cause. Bridged-race files (2011-2017) and single-race files (2018-2024) were combined; race/ethnicity was harmonized into Hispanic, non-Hispanic (NH) White, NH Black, and NH American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100,000 were calculated using the 2000 US Standard Population. Stratifications included sex, race/ethnicity, age group, and US Census region; urban-rural analyses (NCHS classification) were restricted to 2011-2021 due to incomplete population denominators. Rate ratios (RR) and rate differences (RD) quantified disparities. Annual percent change (APC), average APC (AAPC), and joinpoints were estimated by log-linear segmented regression weighted by inverse-variance of the rate. Results: From 2011 through 2024, 399,984 cardiogenic shock-related deaths were identified. AAMR doubled from 4.8 to 9.4 per 100,000 (AAPC +5.66%/yr; 95% CI 4.90 to 6.42), with a single joinpoint at 2021: rates rose 7.24%/yr (6.70 to 7.79) through 2021 then plateaued (APC 0.54%/yr; 95% CI -2.05 to 3.19). Mortality was higher in men (2024 male:female AAMR ratio 1.74). Racial disparities widened substantially: AAPC was greater for NH Black (7.39%/yr; 6.42 to 8.37) than for NH White (5.13; 4.26 to 6.00), Hispanic (5.92; 4.80 to 7.04), or NH AI/AN (4.53; 2.92 to 6.18); the NH Black:NH White rate ratio rose from 1.26 in 2011 to 1.76 in 2024, with the absolute rate difference increasing fivefold (1.2 to 6.6 per 100,000). Age-specific mortality rose most steeply in middle adulthood (ages 45-54: +144%; 55-64: +128%) and remained highest in those aged 85 years or older (101/100,000 in 2024). The Southern Census region had the largest increase (AAPC 6.02; 4.69 to 7.36). Across NCHS urbanization categories (2011-2021), AAMR rose 6.8-8.8%/yr in all strata; the absolute non-metro to metro rate difference more than doubled (2.1 to 4.5 per 100,000) while the rate ratio remained stable (~1.41). Conclusions: Cardiogenic shock mortality in the United States doubled between 2011 and 2024, with deceleration after 2021 of uncertain etiology, potentially reflecting saturation, post-COVID normalization, or expanded mechanical circulatory support. Disparities by race, geography, and rurality persisted or widened, most notably between NH Black and NH White populations. These findings underscore the need for equitable access to advanced cardiogenic shock care.
title: Abstract 4779: Widening Racial and Geographic Disparities in U.S. Cardiogenic Shock Mortality: A National Analysis of 399,984 Deaths, 2011-2024

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries in-hospital mortality of 30-50%. Some existing risk scores depend on echocardiographic measurements or post-procedural variables that are often unavailable when initial triage decisions must be made. We sought to develop and externally validate a practical mortality risk score using only variables available within 24 hours of coronary care unit (CCU) admission. Research Question: Can a bedside risk score using only routinely-available clinical variables stratify in-hospital mortality risk in CS? Methods: Using MIMIC-IV (2008-2022), we identified 3,405 adults admitted to the CCU with CS, defined by documentation (ICD coding or discharge note) or clinical criteria (≥2 of: systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg, vasopressor or inotrope requirement, lactate ≥2.0 mmol/L). The cohort was split 70:30 for development (n=2,383) and internal validation (n=1,022). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and clinical face validity reduced 16 candidate variables to a parsimonious 8-variable model. Logistic regression coefficients were converted to integer points using the Sullivan method. Missing values were imputed; sensitivity analyses with multiple imputation confirmed robustness. External validation used the eICU Collaborative Research Database (n=1,869). Discrimination was compared against BOS,MA2 and CardShock by DeLong test; reclassification by net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results: In-hospital mortality was 26.9% (MIMIC-IV) and 30.2% (eICU). The final score comprises lactate, urine output, age, blood urea nitrogen, invasive mechanical ventilation, acute myocardial infarction, vasopressor count, and hemoglobin (range 0-28 points). Discrimination was good in internal validation (AUROC 0.761, 95% CI 0.728-0.795) and preserved on external validation (AUROC 0.712, 95% CI 0.687-0.740). The score showed superior discrimination versus BOS,MA2 (ΔAUROC +0.057, DeLong p<0.001; continuous NRI +0.553, 95% CI 0.409-0.677; IDI +0.171, 95% CI 0.137-0.204) and CardShock in the subset with available ejection fraction (ΔAUROC +0.055, p=0.005). Four risk strata showed distinct mortality internally: Low (0-5 points) 8.7%, Moderate (6-10) 20.9%, High (11-15) 42.2%, Very High (≥16) 86.5%, with monotonic gradient preserved externally (16.9-80.7%). Unlike CardShock, the score required no echocardiographic data, broadening applicability. Conclusion: An 8-variable bedside risk score stratified in-hospital mortality risk in cardiogenic shock with good discrimination and compared favorably with existing scores. As a triage and stratification tool, not a stand-alone decision instrument, it may prompt timely escalation of care, mechanical circulatory support evaluation, and goals-of-care discussions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective score development in MIMIC-IV (3,405 adults; development n=2,383, internal validation n=1,022) with external validation in eICU (n=1,869).
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective critical care databases with variable shock definitions and no assessment of whether use of the score changes decisions or outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Conference abstract: development and external validation of an eight-variable bedside mortality score in cardiogenic shock using ICU databases.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Discrimination was good in internal validation (AUROC 0.761, 95% CI 0.728-0.795) and preserved on external validation (AUROC 0.712, 95% CI 0.687-0.740).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to risk stratification in cardiogenic shock, though external discrimination is modest and clinical utility is unproven.

register_verdicts.note: A development and validation of a risk score in database cohorts does not answer the register question.

title: Abstract 4789: Stratifying In-Hospital Mortality Risk in Cardiogenic Shock Using an Eight-Variable Bedside Risk Score: Development and External Validation

abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been shown to improve health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with severe aortic stenosis. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12 (KCCQ-12) is a validated, disease-specific HRQoL measure used routinely in the TVT/NCDR Registry. Despite generally favorable outcomes, a clinically meaningful subset of patients fails to achieve improvement after TAVR. Identifying preprocedural predictors of non-improvement in KCCQ-12 could inform patient selection, counseling, and shared decision-making. METHODS: We analyzed consecutive patients undergoing TAVR at a single academic center from January 2021 through June 2025 using prospectively collected TVT/NCDR Registry data. Patients with paired baseline and 30-day KCCQ-12 scores were included. Non-improvement was defined as a change in overall summary score of less than 5 points (below the minimal clinically important difference). Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of non-improvement, adjusting for age, sex, STS risk score, baseline KCCQ-12, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, peripheral artery disease, and left ventricular ejection fraction. RESULTS: The analytic cohort comprised 966 patients (mean age 77.8 ± 8.3 years; 522 male [54.0%], 444 female [46.0%]). Mean KCCQ-12 score improved significantly from 50.4 ± 23.9 at baseline to 74.6 ± 21.9 at 30 days (mean Δ +24.2 ± 25.2 points; p<0.001). Overall, 75.5% of patients achieved a ≥5-point improvement, and 59.4% achieved a ≥15-point improvement (large clinical benefit). On multivariable analysis, higher baseline KCCQ-12 score (aOR 1.06 per point, 95% CI 1.04-1.07; p<0.001) and atrial fibrillation (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.04-2.22; p=0.031) were independently associated with non-improvement. The model demonstrated good discrimination (C-statistic 0.787). CONCLUSIONS: TAVR produces substantial and clinically meaningful improvements in HRQoL at 30 days in the majority of patients. However, those with higher baseline KCCQ-12 scores and atrial fibrillation are significantly less likely to experience further improvement. These findings highlight the importance of baseline HRQoL assessment in TAVR patient selection and underscore the need for optimizing comorbidity management to maximize patient-centered outcomes.
title: Abstract 4831: Quality of Life After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Predictors of Non-Improvement in KCCQ-12 Scores

abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe complication of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), but its predictors, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, and outcomes remain incompletely defined in large real-world cohorts. METHODS: We analyzed nearly 20,000 patients with incident TTS (ICD-10-CM I51.81) in the TriNetX research network, including 74 U.S. health care organizations from 2016-2025. CS was identified by ICD-10-CM code R57.0. MCS was defined by procedural codes for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), Impella, and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of CS and mortality. RESULTS: CS occurred in 752 patients (3.8%) and was present at TTS diagnosis in 79.8%. Mortality was higher in CS-TTS than non-CS TTS (53.3% vs 14.0%; p<0.001). CS patients were more often male (33.9% vs 15.6%), slightly younger (median 64 vs 65 years), and had lower systolic blood pressure and higher heart rate. Independent predictors of CS included sepsis (OR 4.48, 95% CI 3.75-5.34), atrial fibrillation (OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.52-2.20), pneumonia (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.45-2.09), male sex (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34-1.89), NSTEMI (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.22-1.69), and prior stroke (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.08-1.66). Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, and anxiety disorder were associated with lower odds of CS. MCS was used in 77 CS patients (10.2%). Mortality was 62.5% with IABP, 63.6% with VA-ECMO, 50.0% with Impella, and 52.9% without MCS. VA-ECMO recipients were younger than IABP and Impella recipients (median 40 vs 72 and 68 years). In CS patients, MCS use was not independently associated with mortality (OR 1.63, 95% CI 0.85-3.15; p=0.14), whereas age, sepsis, cancer, and atrial fibrillation predicted death. CS incidence increased in 2020 (5.1%) and 2023 (4.7%). Asian race was more common in CS-TTS than in the overall TTS cohort (7.3% vs 3.4%). CONCLUSIONS: In nearly 20,000 real-world TTS patients, CS occurred in 3.8% and was associated with 53% mortality. CS-TTS was linked to acute systemic illness, arrhythmia, male sex, and prior stroke rather than traditional cardiovascular risk factors, suggesting a phenotype driven by acute hemodynamic and inflammatory stress. MCS was infrequently used and was not associated with lower adjusted mortality, although confounding by indication limits causal interpretation. These findings support risk stratification and studies of MCS timing and selection in TTS-CS.
title: Abstract 4834: Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Takotsubo Syndrome: Incidence, Predictors, Mechanical Circulatory Support Utilization, and Outcomes

abstract: Background: Hypertensive emergency (HTNE) is associated with acute cardiovascular and renal end-organ injury, yet racial disparities in inpatient outcomes remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We stratified National Inpatient Sample hospitalizations from 2016 to 2022 for adults with HTNE by race/ethnicity. Multivariable regression was performed using White patients as the reference group, adjusting for age, cardiovascular comorbidities, household income quartile, primary payer, comorbidity burden, hospital location/teaching status, hospital region, and bed size. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, ventricular arrhythmia, acute kidney injury (AKI), and acute heart failure. Results: Among 1,582,050 HTNE hospitalizations with documented race/ethnicity, White patients represented 46.1%, Black patients 37.5%, Hispanic patients 12.5%, and Asian patients 3.5%. Compared with White patients, Black patients had lower adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.68, 95% CI 0.65-0.72), but higher odds of cardiac arrest (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.09-1.26), ventricular arrhythmia (aOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.12-1.25), AKI (aOR 1.38, 95% CI 1.35-1.41), and acute heart failure (aOR 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33). Asian patients had higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.11, 95% CI 1.01-1.22), cardiac arrest (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.06-1.44), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.40, 95% CI 1.15-1.69), AKI (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 1.01-1.11), and acute heart failure (aOR 1.19, 95% CI 1.13-1.26), as summarized in the See figure for details. Compared with White patients, adjusted total hospital charges were higher among Hispanic and Asian patients and lower among Black patients. Conclusions: Racial disparities in hypertensive emergencies were evident across acute cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Black patients had greater odds of cardiorenal complications despite lower mortality, while Asian patients had higher mortality, cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, AKI, and acute heart failure. These findings support earlier hypertension control and lower thresholds for cardiology and nephrology co-management in high-risk populations.
title: Abstract 4835: Racial Disparities in Cardiorenal Outcomes Among Adults Hospitalized with Hypertensive Emergency

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become the mainstay treatment for severe aortic stenosis across all surgical risk profiles. As indications expand to younger populations, the proportion of patients with Bicuspid Aortic Valve (BAV) undergoing TAVR is increasing. However, BAV anatomy—including elliptical annulus, calcified raphe, and extensive leaflet and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) calcification—poses unique procedural challenges and is associated with a higher incidence of paravalvular leak (PVL). Given its association with worse outcomes, identifying modifiable predictors of PVL in BAV is critical for optimizing TAVR performance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted using PubMed, EBSCOhost, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar to identify studies evaluating predictors of PVL following transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid aortic valve patients. Observational studies reporting odds ratios (ORs) for PVL were included. Extracted variables were grouped into device-related, anatomical (calcification), and procedural domains. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using log-transformed ORs. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 statistics. Analyses were performed using R. Results: Five studies including 2,500 patients were analyzed. Higher calcification burden (LVOT/annular) was consistently associated with PVL (pooled OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.75-4.33; I 2 =0.0%), while raphe calcification demonstrated a significant association with PVL (pooled OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.11; I 2 =0.0%), although data was limited. Self-expanding valves were associated with a significantly increased risk of PVL compared with balloon-expandable valves (pooled OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.13-7.46; I 2 =85.5%).Post-dilatation showed a non-significant trend toward increased PVL (pooled OR 1.57, 95% CI 0.92-2.69; I 2 =63.5%). Conclusions: In patients with BAV undergoing TAVR, self-expanding valves and increased calcification burden are the principal determinants of PVL. These findings highlight the importance of pre-procedural anatomical assessment and device selection to mitigate PVL risk. Further refinement of procedural strategies and patient selection may improve outcomes in this complex population.
title: Abstract 4846: Self Expanding Valves and Calcification Increase Paravalvular Leak After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Bicuspid Aortic Valve

abstract: Introduction: Epsilon waves are considered a hallmark of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), but they are not disease-specific and may occur in other right ventricular pathologies. We report a diagnostically challenging case of ventricular tachycardia (VT) with prominent epsilon waves, ultimately revealing an underlying systemic disease. Case Summary: A 50-year-old patient presented with palpitations and angina. An Apple Watch ECG showed sustained VT (~215 bpm), confirmed on 12-lead ECG (RVOT origin) and terminated by electrical cardioversion (Fig. 1A). Baseline ECG in sinus rhythm demonstrated first-degree AV block, right bundle branch block, T-wave inversion, and prominent epsilon waves in V1-V3 (Fig. 1B). Echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular function and moderately reduced right ventricular function with dilatation, raising suspicion of ARVC. Coronary artery disease was excluded by CT. Cardiac MRI revealed biventricular LGE with right ventricular predominance but atypical features. 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated cardiac sarcoidosis with nodal and extranodal involvement (liver, spleen, bone, lungs), confirmed by lymph node biopsy. A dual-chamber ICD was implanted and immunosuppressive therapy initiated. Two months later, recurrent VT/VF occurred despite appropriate ICD therapies. PET/CT showed no active inflammation, suggesting scar-related arrhythmia. Despite amiodarone therapy, recurrent VT persisted, leading to referral for catheter ablation in our center. Repeat MRI showed extensive LGE involving the right ventricle, septum, and inferolateral left ventricle (Fig. 2). VT ablation under Impella support was performed. High-density electroanatomical mapping revealed extensive low-voltage areas in the RVOT (right ventricular outflow tract), septum, and inferior right ventricle with late potentials. Two main VTs (TCL 350 ms and 400 ms) originating from the RVOT were mapped and successfully ablated (Fig. 3). Additional substrate modification was performed. No VT was inducible thereafter. No complications occurred. Discussion and Conclusion: Epsilon waves are not specific for ARVC and may also occur in systemic inflammatory diseases with predominant right ventricular involvement, such as cardiac sarcoidosis. This case highlights the risk of misdiagnosis and the importance of multimodality imaging for identifying underlying systemic disease. Management requires a combined approach including immunosuppressive therapy, antiarrhythmic drugs, device implantation, and catheter ablation in selected patients. In hemodynamically unstable VT, mechanical circulatory support may facilitate mapping and ablation in patients with cardiac sarcoidosis. Despite advanced therapy, prognosis may remain limited, and follow-up is essential.
title: Abstract 4863: The Epsilon Wave Trap: From Suspected ARVC to Systemic Disease with Impella-Supported VT Ablation

abstract: Background: There is compelling evidence that the cardio-protective effects of stem cells can be duplicated by their extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched secretome. Objective: This phase 1 trial (NCT 05774509) assessed the feasibility and safety of repeated infusions of a cardiac cell-derived secretome in heart failure (HF). Methods: Nine patients (aged 67.2 ± 8.6 yrs, m±SD) with a nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, severe symptoms (NYHA Class III) despite maximal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and low Ejection Fraction (EF: 24.3% ± 6.7%) were intravenously infused 3 times (over 30-45 minutes per infusion), 3 weeks apart, with the EV-enriched secretome of cardiovascular progenitor cells differentiated from human induced pluripotent stem cells, at an initial dose (number of particles/kg of bw) of 20x10 9 (n=3), then escalated to 40x10 9 (n=6). Feasibility was assessed by the ability to produce, under GMP conditions, a large-scale batch meeting the following regulation-compliant critical quality attributes (CQA): purity, cargo identity (flow cytometry, omics), potency (angiogenesis, anti-inflammatory and immunogenicity assays), reproducibility, sterility and stability. Safety was assessed on the occurrence of any Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT): death (cardiovascular or of any cause), hospitalization for worsening HF, acute coronary syndrome (including myocardial infarction), sustained atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, ischemic stroke, immune-allergic or infectious reactions to the intravenous infusions of the secretome, and any other potential adverse effects detected and corroborated by clinical presentation, laboratory investigations and image analysis, over the 28 days following the 3rd infusion and subsequently until 1 year. Results: A single large batch of secretome was successfully produced by tangential flow filtration using a low (30 kDa) molecular weight cut-off to retain proteins and soluble factors in addition to EV. This batch met all the pre-set CQA and covered the needs for all included patients and preclinical toxicity/oncogenicity studies. The cargo was fully characterized and potency assays show a 4-year stability under -80°C storage. Safety, a co-primary endpoint, was also successfully achieved: none of the patients presented a DLT and despite the absence of immunosuppression, none had an immune response, as demonstrated by the absence, on repeated assays, of HLA donor-specific antibodies against the secretome-producing cells. While the trial was not designed for efficacy, 1- and 6-month post-treatment assessments show a symptomatic improvement (by 1 NYHA class) in most patients with stable echo and NT-proBNP values. Conclusion: Repeated intravenous administrations of a cardiac cell-derived secretome are safe and may improve patient symptoms. This user-friendly strategy might thus become part of the armamentarium of HF therapies.
title: Abstract 4869: First-in-Man Intravenous Administration of a Cardiac Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Secretome in Dilated Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background: Myocardial infarction (MI) in children is exceptionally rare and most often occurs in patients with coronary artery aneurysms (CAA) following Kawasaki disease (KD). Giant CAAs confer a substantial risk of coronary thrombosis, recurrent ischemia, and premature mortality. Evidence to guide acute reperfusion strategies in pediatric MI remains scarce, particularly regarding fibrinolytic rescue therapy.
