Case Presentation: A 10-year-old boy with giant right coronary artery (RCA) and left anterior descending (LAD) aneurysms secondary to KD presented with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated complete thrombotic occlusion of the RCA aneurysm. Initial percutaneous intervention with aspiration thrombectomy and balloon angioplasty successfully restored TIMI 3 flow. However, acute re-occlusion from recurrent thrombosis developed within 10 hours. Given the high thrombus burden and failed mechanical reperfusion, rescue therapy with combined intracoronary and intravenous tenecteplase was undertaken. This resulted in rapid reperfusion, marked thrombus resolution, and restoration of coronary flow. The only complication was a self-limited groin hematoma without major bleeding. Follow-up angiography confirmed significant reduction in thrombus burden. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function with only a small non-viable infarct (9% of myocardium). At two-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with complete resolution of ST-segment elevation and no further thrombotic or bleeding events. Discussion: Management of MI in KD is uniquely challenging because aneurysmal, inflamed and calcified coronary arteries predispose to massive thrombosis and recurrent occlusion despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While PCI is the cornerstone of treatment, adjunctive fibrinolysis may be lifesaving when thrombosis is refractory. Combined intracoronary and systemic tenecteplase may enhance local clot dissolution while maintaining distal reperfusion. Conclusion: This case highlights combined intracoronary and intravenous tenecteplase as a potentially effective rescue strategy for refractory coronary thrombosis in pediatric MI complicating KD. Early multidisciplinary escalation integrating PCI with targeted fibrinolysis may salvage myocardium and improve outcomes in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 4870: Successful Combined Intravenous and Intracoronary Tenecteplase Therapy for Massive Coronary Thrombosis in a Child with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Following Kawasaki Disease

abstract: Background: Patients with chronic B-cell malignancies on Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKi) have an increased risk for atrial fibrillation (AF) and flutter (AFL). However, decisions to initiate oral anticoagulation (OAC) are complicated by a concomitant increased risk for bleeding and ischemic stroke. Methods: Single-center retrospective cohort study of all patients with chronic B-cell malignancies and AF/AFL prescribed a BTKi from 1/1/2012 to 1/1/2025 at Froedtert / Medical College of Wisconsin (Milwaukee, WI). ICD codes and manual chart review were used to abstract baseline comorbidities, anticoagulation exposure, and adjudicate outcomes. The index date was the BTKi start date or AF/AFL detection date (whichever was later). Major bleeding events were determined using the primary diagnosis associated with inpatient admissions. Results: Of 802 patients prescribed a BTKi, 148 had AF/AFL (mean age, 72 ± 9.5 years; 70% male; 70 [47%] with prior AF/AFL; Table 1 ). Within 3 months of the index date, 77 (52%) were prescribed OAC, including 84% prescribed a direct OAC. Long-standing persistent AF/AFL was present in 4 patients (2.7%) at baseline and 37 patients (25%) by the end of follow-up. Among patients with AF/AFL, there were 30 major bleeding events and 10 ischemic stroke/TIA events over a mean follow-up period of 2.5 ± 2.4 years ( Table 2 ). There were 17 major bleeding events in the OAC group and 13 in the no OAC group (p=0.57). Patients started on OAC were older with a lower CHA 2 DS 2 -VASC score (3.6 [1.5] vs 4.2 [2.0], p<0.05) but a less negative CHA 2 DS 2 -VASC minus ATRIA bleeding risk score (-0.5 [2.3] vs -1.5 [3.2], p<0.01). The risk scores had poor discriminative performance ( Figure 1 ): CHA 2 DS 2 -VASC for predicting ischemic stroke/TIA (AUROC: 0.58); ATRIA for predicting major bleed (AUROC: 0.60); CHA 2 DS 2 -VASC+ATRIA for predicting a composite of ischemic stroke/TIA or major bleed (AUROC: 0.57; 34 total events). 14 patients (9.5%) received either a surgical left atrial appendage (LAA) clip or LAA occlusion (LAAO) device during the follow-up period, 4 of whom had prior major bleeding events. Among the 7 patients in the anticoagulation subgroup who experienced ischemic stroke/TIA, only 2 were receiving anticoagulation at the time of the event (1 DOAC failure, 1 warfarin failure). One event occurred after LAAO, and 4 patients had discontinued anticoagulation before the stroke/TIA event because of prior bleeding. Conclusion: Major bleeding and ischemic stroke events were high in a cohort of BTKi-associated AF/AFL. The discriminative performance of commonly used risk scores for predicting ischemic stroke/TIA or major bleed was poor. A significant proportion of patients underwent procedures for LAA clip/LAAO device. Further study on long-term outcomes of LAA clips/LAAO devices in this population is warranted.
title: Abstract 4872: Ischemic Stroke versus Major Bleeding with Anticoagulation in Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Associated Atrial Fibrillation: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Introduction: Blunt chest trauma is a rare cause of tricuspid valve (TV) injury in children and may go unrecognized at the time of initial presentation. Patient Information: A 15-year-old male with chronic mild elevation in liver aminotransferases was referred to pediatric cardiology after his liver elastography showed a significantly elevated liver stiffness measurement and abdominal ultrasound demonstrated diffuse dilation of the inferior vena cava and hepatic veins with associated pulsatile hepatoportal flow and absent-to-reversed flow in the portal veins. He reported significant exercise intolerance and exertional chest pain with associated dizziness, diaphoresis, dyspnea, and palpitations. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Physical examination revealed a soft systolic ejection murmur along the left midsternal border with radiation across the precordium; there was no diastolic murmur. The liver edge was palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin. Further history revealed he sustained significant chest trauma in a motor vehicle accident two years prior. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Given concern for elevated right atrial pressure, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was obtained on the day of presentation, which revealed torrential tricuspid regurgitation (TR) with suspected avulsion of the anterior TV leaflet and severe right atrial (RA) and right ventricular (RV) dilation. Cardiac MRI was pursued to further delineate the TV anatomy for operative planning; the leaflet anatomy was not well seen; however, there was severe tricuspid annular dilation with a TR fraction of 77%. He was referred for urgent TV repair. Therapeutic Intervention(s): One month later, the patient underwent TV repair including annuloplasty (36 mm Genesse annuloplasty ring) and suture plication around the area of the anterior leaflet, inferior septal commissure, and anteroseptal commissure, with improved leaflet coaptation. RA reduction was also performed. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient was extubated in the operating room and discharged home on postoperative day three. Discharge TTE showed mild residual TR, moderate RV dilation, and moderate RV systolic dysfunction. At his one-month postoperative follow-up, TTE demonstrated trivial TR, mild RV dilation, and borderline normal RV systolic function. He was cleared to resume all activity except contact sports. At four months postoperative, he remained asymptomatic and his TTE was stable. Discussion & Synthesis: TV avulsion is a rare complication of pediatric chest trauma and may lead to secondary complications such as congestive hepatopathy if unrecognized. Early evaluation with TTE is essential in patients with suspected blunt cardiac injury to identify potential TV injury and prevent long-term sequelae. If present, TV repair can be achieved with an excellent operative result.
title: Abstract 4873: Driven Apart: Tricuspid Valve Avulsion in a Teenager Following Motor Vehicle Accident

abstract: Abstract & Keywords: Left atrial diverticula and left atrial appendages can be found in up to 29% of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) scans and are associated with increased risk of stroke. We present a patient with stroke, newly reduced ejection fraction (rEF), and left atrial diverticulum thrombus on CCTA. Keywords: Left Atrial Diverticulum, Thrombus, Anticoagulation, Heart Failure, Case Report Introduction: Left atrial diverticula and appendages, particularly with rEF can promote hemostasis. We describe a case where a Left atrial diverticulum thrombus, in the setting of rEF, was found to be the source of a cardioembolic stroke, highlighting the value of multimodal imaging. Patient Information (De-identified): A 63-year-old male with tobacco, methamphetamine, and alcohol use presents with aphasia and left arm weakness. Clinical Findings & Timeline: CTA head/neck was obtained on presentation, revealing partial occlusion of the right anterior and middle cerebral arteries, for which he underwent mechanical thrombolysis and thrombectomy. Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed a rEF of 25%. CCTA performed for ischemic evaluation did not reveal obstructive coronary artery disease but identified an 11-mm left atrial diverticulum with a 3-mm thrombus (Figure 1). Continuous cardiac monitoring for 30 days did not reveal any arrhythmias. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Increased hemostasis seen in rEF, often shown by spontaneous echo contrast, proposes a mechanism for thrombus development in our patient’s left atrial diverticulum. This is supported by direct thrombus visualization within the diverticulum on CCTA. Therapeutic Intervention(s): This patient was discharged on warfarin, consistent with literature supporting anticoagulation with left atrial thrombus and systolic dysfunction. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: Nearly one year from initial presentation, the patient’s EF recovered to 40% while on GDMT and anticoagulation was transitioned to apixaban due to noncompliance with INR checks. He has not had another stroke or episodes of bleeding during this time. The patient underwent monitoring with Zio patch twice without any findings of atrial fibrillation. Discussion & Synthesis: This case highlights how multimodal cardiac imaging can identify occult causes of thromboembolism and suggests how rEF can contribute to thromboembolism with structural variants. There are no guidelines on anticoagulation in patients with rEF and structural variants. Individualized risk assessment and further research are needed to guide anticoagulation in structural variants.
title: Abstract 4905: Stroke in Sinus Rhythm: Left Atrial Diverticulum Thrombus in Severe Systolic Dysfunction

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac Rhabdomyoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in infancy and is frequently associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Here, we report a case of cardiac rhabdomyoma without a TSC gene mutation and a striking ST-segment elevation pattern on ECG. Case Presentation: A 5-month-old asymptomatic infant presented with an electrocardiogram (ECG) showing marked ST-segment elevation in the anterolateral and inferior leads. Echocardiogram showed a cardiac rhabdomyoma in the left ventricle with preserved ventricular function and no evidence of hemodynamic compromise. Cardiac biomarkers were negative. There was no other evidence, clinically or radiologically, for tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Genetic testing for TSC was also negative. The infant remained clinically well with persistent but stable ECG changes at 10-month follow-up. Discussion: This case highlights a rare but striking ECG presentation of a benign cardiac tumor. It was diagnostically challenging, as the ECG findings were not consistent with those typically seen in cardiac tumors. Review of the literature reveals only a handful of case reports of a cardiac tumor appearing to be a STEMI, thus emphasizing the importance of clinical context when interpreting ischemic-appearing ECG changes in infants.
title: Abstract 4929: Benign Tumor, Malignant ECG: Isolated Cardiac Rhabdomyoma with Marked ST-Segment Elevation: Case Report

abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a prevalent and detrimental complication following cardiac surgery, with significant influence on patient morbidity and mortality. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) can promptly reverse life-threatening complications associated with AKI. Nevertheless, the optimal timing and indications for initiating RRT remain controversial. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impacts of RRT initiation strategies based on AKI severity and urgent indications on 30-day mortality and renal recovery at hospital discharge. Methods: This retrospective cohort study enrolled adult patients who underwent cardiac surgery and required postoperative RRT at China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases, from January 2015 to July 2025. Patients receiving preoperative RRT or with incomplete serum creatinine measurements were excluded. All patients were assessed for the severity of AKI based on the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria before RRT initiation. Urgent indications included severe hyperkalaemia, severe pulmonary oedema refractory to diuretics, severe acidosis, and marked elevations in serum urea levels. Results: A total of 710 patients were included in the primary analyses. Of these, 259 (36.4%) developed stage 3 AKI, and 236 (33.2%) presented with at least one urgent indications before RRT initiation. After adjusting for covariates, patients with stage 3 AKI and no urgent indications before RRT initiation had significantly lower 30-day mortality than those with milder AKI and urgent indications (15.7% vs. 36.6%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.32 [95% CI, 0.18-0.58]; P < 0.001). In addition, these patients were more likely to attain renal recovery at hospital discharge and had a shorter length of intensive care unit stay. In the subgroup of patients who did not receive mechanical circulatory support prior to RRT initiation, these associations remained significant. Conclusions: Patients receiving RRT with severe AKI and no urgent indications before RRT initiation achieved better in-hospital outcomes. These findings suggest that RRT initiation strategies after cardiac surgery warrant carefully considered, with particular attention to the severity of renal dysfunction.
title: Abstract 4965: Renal Replacement Therapy Initiation Strategies and 30-day Mortality in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A 15-year Experience in China

abstract: Background: The proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)/ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) and PCSK9/ATP-binding cassette transporter G1 (ABCG1) ratios reflect the functional balance between PCSK9-driven atherogenicity and macrophage cholesterol efflux capacity. Elevated PCSK9 impairs macrophage cholesterol efflux by suppressing ABCA1 and ABCG1. Whether integrated PCSK9/transporter ratios are associated with coronary lesion severity, nonlinear dose-response patterns, and inflammatory mediation in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains unknown. Research Questions: (1) Are PCSK9/ABCA1 and PCSK9/ABCG1 ratios independently associated with severe coronary lesions in ACS? (2) Do these associations exhibit nonlinear threshold effects? (3) Are the associations mediated by systemic inflammation? Methods: Among 616 statin-naïve ACS patients, coronary atherosclerotic burden was quantified by the Gensini score. PCSK9/ABCA1 and PCSK9/ABCG1 ratios were derived from admission plasma. Multivariable logistic regression, generalized additive models, and two-piecewise linear regression were applied. Mediation analysis quantified inflammatory contributions. Results: After full adjustment, each 0.2-unit increment in PCSK9/ABCA1 (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.18-1.65, P <0.001) and PCSK9/ABCG1 (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.06-1.66, P =0.014) was independently associated with severe lesions (Gensini upper tertile). Both ratios exhibited inverted L-shaped dose-response: steep associations below inflection points of 0.74 (PCSK9/ABCA1) and 0.48 (PCSK9/ABCG1), plateauing beyond thresholds (Figure 1). Subgroup analyses revealed significant effect modification by current smoking ( P for interaction = 0.019 and 0.030) and diabetes mellitus ( P for interaction = 0.039 and 0.008), with particularly pronounced associations for the PCSK9/ABCG1 ratio in diabetic patients (Figure 2). Mediation analysis indicated that white blood cell (WBC) count and interleukin-6 (IL-6) jointly mediated 14-25% of the observed associations, supporting an inflammation-dependent pathway linking PCSK9/efflux transporter imbalance to coronary lesion severity (Figure 3). Conclusion: Elevated PCSK9/ABCA1 and PCSK9/ABCG1 ratios are independently associated with severe coronary lesions in ACS, exhibiting nonlinear threshold effects. These associations are modified by smoking and diabetes and partially mediated by systemic inflammation, highlighting combined contributions of lipid metabolism disruption and inflammatory activation to coronary vulnerability.
title: Abstract 4975: Nonlinear Effects of PCSK9/ABCA1 and PCSK9/ABCG1 Ratios on Coronary Severity in Acute Coronary Syndrome

abstract: Introduction: While lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] levels are considered relatively stable over the life course, limited data suggest Lp(a) levels may vary within individuals after acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Research Question: Among participants with recent ACS in VICTORION-INCEPTION, how do Lp(a) levels change over time, with up to 330 days of follow-up? Methods: VICTORION-INCEPTION was a 330-day, phase 3b, open-label, multicenter trial of inclisiran + usual care compared with usual care in participants with recent ACS. Eligible participants were screened within 5 weeks of discharge from an ACS hospitalization and randomized 1:1 to inclisiran + usual care or usual care alone. Lp(a) levels (nmol/L) were measured by a central laboratory using an immunoturbidimetric assay (Randox) at Day 0 (i.e., the last measurement before or at study treatment start) and at Days 90, 270, and 330. In this post hoc, exploratory analysis, we evaluated Lp(a) levels by treatment arm among those with an Lp(a) level at Day 0 and ≥1 follow-up measure, and intra-individual variability in Lp(a) levels over time in those with ≥2 follow-up measurements. Participants in the usual care arm who initiated a proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)-targeting lipid-lowering therapy (anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies or inclisiran) were excluded (n=21). Results: Of 400 participants enrolled in VICTORION-INCEPTION, 343 were included in this analysis (inclisiran + usual care: n=185; usual care: n=158). The median time from ACS hospitalization discharge to study treatment start was 33 days (interquartile range [Q1 to Q3] 25 to 43). At Day 0, the overall median Lp(a) level was 71.6 nmol/L (Q1 to Q3: 20.0 to 187.4), 28.6% of those in the inclisiran + usual care arm and 30.4% in the usual care arm had Lp(a) ≥175 nmol/L. At Day 330, 21.3% in the inclisiran + usual care arm and 25.9% of those in the usual care arm had Lp(a) ≥175 nmol/L. Changes in the distribution of Lp(a) levels by category in each arm are shown in Figure 1 . Among 320 participants with ≥2 follow-up Lp(a) measurements, 52 (16.3%) exhibited ≥50 nmol/L intra-individual variability between maximum and minimum Lp(a) levels measured during the study period (inclisiran + usual care: 15.1%, n=26/172; usual care: 17.6%, n=26/148; Figure 2 ). In those participants, variability was observed across a range of Lp(a) levels at Day 0 and included individuals with both increases and decreases in Lp(a) levels over time. Conclusions: While Lp(a) levels were generally stable after ACS in participants in VICTORION-INCEPTION, a small number experienced variability up to ~1 year following the index ACS event
title: Abstract 4999: Temporal Variability of Lipoprotein(a) After Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights from VICTORION-INCEPTION

abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with significant thromboembolic stroke risk. While oral anticoagulation remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention, some patients are unable to tolerate long-term therapy due to bleeding complications. In these cases, percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) offers an alternative strategy. The Watchman™ device has demonstrated efficacy and safety in trials such as PROTECT-AF and PREVAIL; however, device embolization remains a rare but serious complication. We present a case of delayed Watchman embolization causing near-complete abdominal aortic occlusion with renal and lower extremity ischemia. A man in his 80s with heart failure and persistent AF/flutter underwent elective Watchman implantation due to recurrent hematuria limiting anticoagulation use. The procedure was uncomplicated, post-procedural echocardiography showed no pericardial effusion, and he was discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy. The following day, he presented with sudden bilateral lower extremity weakness and bowel incontinence. Examination revealed lower extremity mottling to the waist, absent femoral pulses, and diminished sensation and strength. Laboratory studies showed hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.61 mg/dL from baseline 1.4 mg/dL), and reduced eGFR. CT angiography demonstrated a foreign body lodged in the abdominal aorta distal to the superior mesenteric artery with markedly diminished pelvic and renal perfusion, consistent with embolization of the Watchman device causing near-complete aortic obstruction. The patient underwent emergent bilateral iliofemoral cutdown, aortoiliac embolectomy, balloon angioplasty, endovascular retrieval of the Watchman device, and femoral artery repair. His postoperative course was complicated by groin hematoma requiring evacuation, wound infection requiring washout and VAC exchange, bilateral thromboembolism, gastrointestinal bleeding, and severe acute kidney injury with peak creatinine of 7.9 mg/dL. Despite significant renal dysfunction, he remained non-oliguric and recovered without dialysis. After a 3-week hospitalization, he was discharged to a skilled nursing facility for rehabilitation. Device embolization after LAAO occurs in approximately 0.2%-0.6% of cases, most commonly within 48 hours. Risk factors include undersizing, inadequate anchoring, challenging appendage anatomy, and failure of PASS criteria. Delayed embolization may still occur despite appropriate deployment. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for abdominal pain, limb ischemia, or unexplained acute kidney injury following LAAO. Early recognition and prompt multidisciplinary intervention are critical to minimizing catastrophic vascular and renal complications.
title: Abstract 5014: The Wandering Watchman: Device Migration Beyond the Heart

abstract: Introduction: Bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) antibodies such as glofitamab-gxbm, a CD3xCD20 engager, have emerged as a promising treatment for refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). The most common adverse effect is cytokine release syndrome (CRS); however, cardiovascular side effects have not been reported. Evidence from other T-cell-engaging therapies suggests cardiotoxicity may represent an underrecognized side effect. We report a case of acute, reversible heart failure with reduced ejection fraction following glofitamab. Patient Information: A 71 year old male with a history of relapsed DLBCL was admitted for BiTE therapy with glofitamab. A transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) five months prior showed normal cardiac function with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 64%. Clinical Findings: On the first day following the glofitamab infusion, the patient developed a fever and tachycardia, meeting criteria for Grade 1 CRS. No dyspnea or chest pain was reported. IV Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg IV was administered for CRS prevention. On the third day, he developed orthopnea and dyspnea. Jugular venous distention and peripheral pitting edema was found on examination. Diagnostics: Labs revealed a troponin of 56 ng/L and proBNP of 18,062 pg/mL. Electrocardiography showed a stable right bundle branch block unchanged from prior. A repeat TTE showed global hypokinesis with severely reduced LVEF of 26% and mild biatrial dilation, a significant decline from the baseline LVEF of 64%. Intervention: Upon recognition of heart failure, IV furosemide was initiated for volume optimization. Carvedilol and valsartan were subsequently started as guideline directed medical therapy. Further glofitamab infusions were held. Outcomes: Symptoms improved over 48 hours, and the patient was subsequently discharged on oral furosemide, carvedilol, and valsartan. A repeat TTE two weeks post discharge demonstrated significant recovery with a LVEF of 53%, residual left atrial dilation, and a normal right atrium. The patient remained clinically stable on follow up. Discussion: This case represents one of the first descriptions of acute left ventricular systolic dysfunction temporally associated with glofitamab. The temporal association (Figure 1), absence of prior cardiac history, recovery timeline, and global hypokinesis pattern support a diagnosis of inflammatory cardiomyopathy rather than acute coronary syndrome or structural injury. This pattern is increasingly being recognized following BiTE therapy. As bispecific antibodies are being used in more patients, structured cardiovascular surveillance including baseline TTE, cardiac biomarkers, and a low threshold for repeat imaging in symptomatic patients is warranted. Prospective cardio-oncology studies are needed to define incidence and establish evidence based monitoring strategies for this emerging class-effect cardiotoxicity.

Abstract 5016: Reversible Heart Failure Following Bi-Specific T-Cell Engager Therapy:
                    A Case Report

abstract: Background: With the rapid expansion of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), increasing numbers of patients undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after repeated PCI procedures. Prior PCI has been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after CABG; however, the long-term impact of in-stent restenosis (ISR) requiring subsequent surgical revascularization remains poorly understood. Methods: Among 2349 consecutive patients who underwent isolated CABG between January 2007 and December 2023, patients undergoing redo CABG (n=12) or salvage operations (n=11) were excluded. Patients were categorized into three groups according to PCI and ISR history: PCI-naïve (n=1605 [69%]), prior PCI without ISR (PCI/non-ISR; n=428 [18%]), and prior ISR (ISR; n=293 [13%]). Early postoperative and long-term clinical outcomes were compared during follow-up of up to 15 years. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for clinically relevant baseline covariates was performed. Results: Thirty-day mortality did not differ among groups (0.9% vs. 1.4% vs. 1.2%, p=0.77). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant differences in long-term all-cause mortality (16.6% vs. 14.5% vs. 36.5%, overall p<0.0001). Post hoc pairwise comparisons showed no significant difference between the PCI-naïve and PCI/non-ISR groups (p=0.11), whereas the ISR group demonstrated significantly worse survival than both groups (both p<0.0001). Similarly, cardiac death differed significantly among groups (5.7% vs. 6.5% vs. 22.2%, overall p<0.0001), with no difference between the PCI-naïve and PCI/non-ISR groups (p=0.71). ISR patients were older and had a higher prevalence of renal dysfunction. Multivariable Cox regression analysis demonstrated that prior ISR remained associated with increased risks of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-2.22; p=0.003) and cardiac death (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.23-3.01; p=0.004). Conclusions: Patients with prior ISR undergoing CABG demonstrated substantially worse long-term outcomes than both PCI-naïve patients and patients with prior PCI without ISR. These findings highlight the importance of early Heart Team evaluation to distinguish patients suitable for continued PCI from those who may benefit from timely transition to surgical revascularization. Further investigation is warranted to clarify the relationship between ISR-related coronary anatomy, subsequent ischemic events, and long-term outcomes after CABG.
title: Abstract 5056: Impact of Prior In-Stent Restenosis on Long-Term Outcomes After CABG: A Three-Group Analysis Including PCI-Naïve Patients

abstract: Background: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) carries substantial long-term morbidity and mortality comparable to acute coronary syndromes, yet there is scarcity of data on pharmacotherapy. SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have established cardioprotective effects across the heart failure spectrum and offer mechanistic plausibility in TTS through anti-inflammatory, neurohumoral modulatory, and myocardial metabolic pathways. Their role in TTS remains unexplored. Methods: We conducted a multi-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (ICD-10 coded) across a single healthcare system (January 2010 - January 2024). Patients were stratified by SGLT2i prescription at hospital discharge and followed for 30 days and one year. Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included TTS recurrence, all-cause rehospitalization, and stroke/TIA. Between-group comparisons used risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs (Wald method); chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests were applied as appropriate. Results: Among 160 patients (mean age 67.7 years; ~91% female), 78 (48.8%) were prescribed SGLT2i at discharge. Cohorts were well-balanced at baseline across demographics, comorbidities, and background cardiac medications. At 30 days, rehospitalization was numerically lower in the SGLT2i group (7.7% vs. 18.3%, RR 0.42, p=0.047), with no significant differences in mortality, recurrence, or stroke/TIA. At one year, SGLT2i use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (9.0% vs. 22.0%, RR 0.41, p=0.024), rehospitalization (17.9% vs. 35.4%, RR 0.51, p=0.013), and TTS recurrence (5.1% vs. 18.3%, RR 0.28, p=0.013). Conclusions: In this first observational study examining long-term outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors in TTS, discharge prescription was associated with significant reductions in one-year mortality, rehospitalization, and recurrence. These hypothesis-generating findings support the need for dedicated prospective trials to establish the role of SGLT2 inhibitors in TTS secondary prevention.
title: Abstract 5100: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Long-Term Outcomes in Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy: A Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Patient Information: A 34-year-old male with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot, pulmonary atresia, and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries was admitted to an outside hospital with right-sided heart failure symptoms, chills, and neck pain. Clinical Findings and Timeline: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a severely dilated right ventricle (RV) with severely reduced function, a right ventricle to pulmonary artery (RV-PA) conduit peak gradient of 93 mmHg, and a new <1 cm tricuspid valve (TV) vegetation with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) (Figure 1). Diuretics and broad-spectrum antibiotics were started. Over 24 hours, his lactate precipitously rose to 15, AST 633, ALT 1204, and INR 2.0. He was hypotensive and required norepinephrine. A hospital transfer request was made. Due to worsening RV-predominant cardiogenic shock, severe pulmonic stenosis (PS), and suspected infective endocarditis (IE), the Shock Team was activated. Patient was transferred to our institution’s catheterization lab for evaluation and congenital intervention. Right heart catheterization demonstrated a mean RA pressure 24 mmHg, RV pressures 130/26 mmHg, PA pressures 19/4/9 mmHg, PCWP 15 mmHg, and LVEDP 2 mmHg giving a RV-PA gradient of 111 mmHg. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) confirmed the TTE findings. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The over-diuresis and near-systemic RV pressures from severe PS led to a dangerous hemodynamic state with insufficient preload, ventricular interdependence, RV-PA uncoupling, and ultimately RV shock. Therapeutic Intervention(s): A right-sided percutaneous micro-axial flow pump (Impella RP Flex®) was placed across the severely stenotic prosthetic RV-PA conduit to offload the failing RV. Initially, the device would not cross the pulmonary valve (PV) due to the severe PS, so he underwent PV valvuloplasty followed by successful placement (Figure 2). LVEDP immediately improved from 2 mmHg to 15 mmHg and norepinephrine was turned off. Follow-up, Outcomes, & Adverse Events: Patient was admitted to the cardiac ICU where his lactate and shock liver resolved. Blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecalis and a CT scan demonstrated early discitis/osteomyelitis at C5-6. Ultimately, he underwent his fourth re-do sternotomy with RA-PA conduit removal and replacement with a pulmonary homograft, RV outflow tract (RVOT) and PA reconstruction, and TV replacement. Surgical pathology confirmed infection of the TV and RV-PA conduit. Patient was safely discharged after an 18-day hospitalization. Discussion & Synthesis: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients with RVOT IE have an elevated risk of morbidity and mortality, representing a highly vulnerable patient population. This case highlights a novel and expanded use of a RV micro-axial flow pump as a temporizing bridge to definitive surgical repair in a patient with ACHD experiencing RVOT IE and RV shock (Figure 3).
title: Abstract 5102: No Easy Exit: A Case of Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Infective Endocarditis, Critical Obstruction, and Shock in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot

abstract: Introduction: Vitamin K antagonists remain the guideline-mandated standard of care for mechanical prosthetic heart valves. True warfarin resistance, failure to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation despite doses exceeding 15 mg/day after exclusion of modifiable causes, occurs in fewer than 0.1% of patients. This is particularly consequential in the mechanical mitral position, where an INR of 2.5-3.5 is essential to prevent valve thrombosis and systemic embolism. No AHA/ACC or ESC guideline addresses this scenario. Patient Information: A 42-year-old female (BMI 29 kg/m 2 ) in sinus rhythm with rheumatic heart disease underwent mechanical mitral valve replacement with concomitant aortic valve repair. Baseline INR was 0.9. Clinical Findings and Timeline: Warfarin was escalated stepwise to 30 mg/day with INR monitoring at 3-5 day intervals. INR remained below 1.5 throughout, including during supervised inpatient administration. Warfarin was overlapped with enoxaparin, then continued as enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily. No thromboembolic or bleeding events occurred. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Pseudo-resistance was systematically excluded: adherence confirmed via inpatient supervision; medication review, dietary assessment, liver function, thyroid function, serum vitamin K, oral vitamin K trial, and multiple warfarin formulations were unremarkable or ineffective. Factor X was 48% and Factor II was 71%, both above therapeutic suppression ranges of 10-30% and 20-40% respectively, confirming pharmacodynamic failure. Echocardiography confirmed preserved ejection fraction of 50-60% with no thrombus; fluoroscopy confirmed unobstructed bileaflet excursion. Probable true warfarin resistance was diagnosed, likely reflecting a VKORC1 gain-of-function or CYP4F2 polymorphism; pharmacogenetic testing was unavailable due to resource limitations. Therapeutic Interventions: Warfarin was escalated to 30 mg/day under inpatient supervision. Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily was initiated as long-term anticoagulation. Direct oral anticoagulants were contraindicated. Follow-up and Outcomes: No thromboembolic or bleeding events occurred. Valve function remained normal on echocardiography. Discussion: This case biochemically confirms probable true warfarin resistance via clotting factor assays, not previously reported in comparable cases. Warfarin remains the preferred lifelong anticoagulant for mechanical mitral valves, offering proven thromboprophylaxis orally; its failure leaves no ideal alternative. Indefinite enoxaparin, while necessary, is suboptimal by carrying injection burden, renal monitoring requirements, and absence of long-term outcome data. This exposes a critical guideline gap and underscores the urgent need for pharmacogenetic infrastructure and evidence-based protocols in resource-limited settings.
title: Abstract 5121: Warfarin Resistance After Mechanical Mitral Valve Replacement: Diagnostic Approach and the Unmet Need for Evidence-Based Protocols

abstract: Background: The C-Reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index(CTI), a reliable surrogate indicator of inflammatory and insulin resistance, is independently associated with coronary artery disease of various clinical manifestations. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of the CTI index in predicting repeat revascularization and in-stent restenosis (ISR) in chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: A total of 2147 participants were enrolled and divided into groups according to the tertiles of the CTI index. The primary endpoint was a composite of repeat revascularization and ISR during follow-up. Log-rank tests and Kaplan-Meier methods were performed to explore differences in event rates between CTI tertiles and plot time-to-event curves. The associations between the CTI index and the primary endpoint were assessed by multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis with restricted cubic splines (RCS). The predictive performance of the models was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, with the area under curve (AUC) metric quantifying the model’s discriminative ability. The value of the CTI was defined as the Ln (fasting triglycerides (mg/dL)хfasting plasma glucose (mg/dL)/2) + 0.412 х ln [CRP (mg/L)]. Results: Over a median follow-up of 60 months, 992 (46.20%) patients had experienced at least one primary endpoint event. The follow-up incidence of the primary endpoint increased with the CTI index tertiles. After adjusting for potential confounders, the CTI index was independently associated with the primary endpoint in CCS patients (HR, 1.11; 95% CI 1.01-1.22; P=0.03). Additionally, the highest tertile of the CTI group was correlated with a 1.30-fold risk of the primary endpoint compared with the lowest tertile of the CTI group (HR, 1.30; 95% CI 1.10-1.54; P=0.002). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant linear association between CTI and the primary endpoint(non-linear P=0.174, P overall=0.042). CTI index, age, gender, BMI, diabetes, hypertension, previous PCI, previous MI, Lp(a), HDL-C, presence of multivessel CAD, presence of lesion length≥20 mm, number of stents, and stent length can be used as independent variables to construct a clinical prediction model. The ROC analysis demonstrated that this multivariate prediction model had moderate predictive accuracy for the primary endpoint, with area-under-the-curve estimates of 0.63 (95%CI 0.60-0.65) at 3 years and 0.65 (95%CI 0.62-0.67) at 5 years. Conclusions: The CTI index is independently associated with an increased risk of repeat revascularization and in-stent restenosis during long-term follow-up in patients with chronic coronary syndrome after PCI. These findings suggest that the CTI index may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.
title: Abstract 5133: C-Reactive Protein-Triglyceride Glucose Index for Predicting Repeat Revascularization or In-Stent Restenosis in Patients with Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI

abstract: Background: The AHA Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT™) equation is the current standard for cardiovascular risk assessment but omits Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], a genetic, causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Whether elevated Lp(a) adds prognostic value within PREVENT™ risk categories in real-world populations has not been established in a real-world community-based setting with independently validated events. Methods: In a historical cohort of ASCVD-free adults residing in Olmsted County, MN (1999-2025), we used the Rochester Epidemiology Project records-linkage system to identify those who underwent Lp(a) measurement and to ascertain comorbidities and incident events (validated in duplicate). The primary composite cardiovascular (CVD) events were myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral vascular disease (PAD or carotid artery disease), or coronary revascularization (PCI or CABG). Lp(a) was classified as elevated (≥50 mg/dL or ≥125 nmol/L) and by population percentile (<75th, 75th-<90th, ≥90th). Fine-Gray competing-risks models, treating all-cause death as the competing event, estimated the association between Lp(a) and the composite endpoint, adjusted for age, sex, and PREVENT™ score. Subgroup analyses evaluated the Lp(a)-ASCVD association within PREVENT™ risk categories (<3%, 3-<5%, 5-<10%, ≥10%). Results: Among 10,023 individuals (mean age 53±12; 50.9% male; 93.6% White), 1,211 composite events occurred over a median of 8.5 years (921 CVD events; 290 died). Overall, 75.6% were considered low- or borderline-risk by PREVENT™. Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with CVD (sHR 1.34; 95% CI 1.16-1.55; p<0.001), with a graded dose-response by percentile (P for trend=0.006, Fig. 1A). Within PREVENT™ categories, elevated Lp(a) was significantly associated with incident CVD in individuals considered to be borderline-risk and low-risk (Fig. 1B). Findings were consistent across Lp(a) assay (P for interaction=0.77). Conclusions: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with incident CVD events in a community-based primary prevention cohort. These findings support current guideline recommendations for Lp(a) measurement to refine PREVENT-based risk stratification, particularly among patients classified as low or borderline risk.
title: Abstract 5135: Lipoprotein(a) and Cardiovascular Risk Stratification Within the PREVENT™ Equation: A Real-World Community-Based Cohort Study

abstract: Abstract: A 56-year-old high-surgical-risk woman on hemodialysis developed a large right atrial mass, complicated by segmental pulmonary embolism and septic emboli. Progressive mass enlargement on serial TEE prompted AngioVac vacuum-assisted thrombectomy, achieving debulking without procedural complications. Introduction: Large right atrial (RA) masses in high-surgical-risk patients pose significant management challenges. Open surgical extraction carries prohibitive morbidity and mortality. AngioVac vacuum-assisted thrombectomy offers a minimally invasive alternative; however, experience in cases with concomitant septic embolism and pulmonary embolism (PE) remains limited. Patient Information: 56-year-old woman with ESRD on hemodialysis, diabetes mellitus, coronary disease, and chronic hypotension. Clinical Findings: Presented with altered mental status and refractory hypotension requiring vasopressors. Workup revealed hyperglycemia, leukocytosis, and RSV infection. TTE identified a large RA echodense mass (3.4х2.1 cm) with a mobile component (1.8х1 cm) prolapsing across the tricuspid valve, tethered to the tunneled dialysis catheter. CTA confirmed segmental PE with cavitary right lower lobe opacity suspicious for septic embolism. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Serial TEE showed progressive mass enlargement from 3.3х2.2 cm to 4.2х3.2 cm, with the mobile component prolapsing into the tricuspid valve in diastole. Cardiothoracic surgery deemed open intervention to carry unacceptably high operative risk. Intervention: AngioVac vacuum-assisted debulking was performed with venovenous extracorporeal bypass, fluoroscopic, and intracardiac echocardiographic guidance. AngioVac cannula was advanced via the right femoral vein into the RA. The tunneled dialysis catheter was simultaneously removed. Approximately 60-75% debulking was achieved (residual: 1.5 cm on the RA free wall). Follow-up: Post-procedural TEE confirmed significant reduction in thrombus burden without new pericardial effusion or valvular injury. No immediate complications occurred. Discussion: This case demonstrates successful AngioVac thrombectomy in a critically ill patient with a large, progressive RA mass, PE, and septic emboli, a combination carrying elevated risk of fatal embolization. The multidisciplinary approach involving interventional radiology, cardiothoracic surgery, and cardiology was essential. AngioVac served as both a definitive debulking strategy and a bridge in a patient ineligible for open surgery. Teaching Points: AngioVac thrombectomy is viable for large RA masses in poor surgical candidates. Serial echocardiographic surveillance is critical to monitor mass progression and valvular obstruction. Multidisciplinary coordination and early surgical involvement are essential when intracardiac masses are identified in similar patients
title: Abstract 5142: When Surgery Isn't an Option: AngioVac Thrombectomy for a Progressive Right Atrial Mass with Septic and Pulmonary Emboli

abstract: Background: Myocardial infarction (MI) induces cardiomyocyte (CM) loss and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Epigenetic remodeling has been implicated in regulating the CM response after ischemic injury, although the specific stress-induced changes remain unclear. We investigated whether the repressive histone mark H3K9me3 regulates metabolic adaptation and CM survival following ischemic stress. Methods: H3K9me3 depletion was achieved using expression of the H3K9 demethylase KDM4D in cultured CMs and in an inducible CM-specific KDM4D mouse model. Results: Using both in vitro and in vivo models, we found that H3K9me3 levels increased in CMs following MI (1.69-fold), hypoxia (1.24-fold), and oxidative stress (1.18-fold), suggesting that stress-induced H3K9me3 may represent a generalized response. To test this physiologic impact, Ad-KDM4D transduction was performed in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). Ad-KDM4D reduced oxidative stress-induced apoptosis (Ad-GFP + H 2 O 2 : 86.7 ± 1.0% vs. Ad-KDM4D + H 2 O 2 : 56.5 ± 1.4% TUNEL + CMs, P < 0.0001) and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential following H 2 O 2 treatment (Ad-GFP + H 2 O 2 : 36.2 ± 3.1 vs. Ad-KDM4D + H 2 O 2 : 58.7 ± 1.5 fluorescence intensity, P < 0.0001). In adult hearts, CM-specific KDM4D expression reduced infarct size (control: 10.33 ± 0.90% vs. iKDM4D: 6.14 ± 0.18%, P < 0.05), decreased CM apoptosis (control: 0.20 ± 0.04 vs. iKDM4D: 0.06 ± 0.01 CM/mm 2 , P < 0.05), reduced scar size (control: 5.79 ± 0.88% vs. iKDM4D: 3.1 ± 0.65% LV area, P < 0.05), and improved systolic function after MI (control: 30.3 ± 1.7% vs. iKDM4D: 50.8 ± 6.0% ejection fraction, P < 0.05). These findings suggest that H3K9me3 depletion enhances CM resistance to ischemic and oxidative stress. To investigate the mechanisms underlying these protective effects, transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were performed, which demonstrated activation of glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-associated programs, including increased G6PD and TKT expression, accumulation of PPP intermediates, increased G6PD activity, reduced NADP+/NADPH ratio, and decreased reactive oxygen species. Pharmacologic inhibition of the PPP pathway attenuated the reduction in TUNEL + CMs induced by H3K9me3 depletion. Conclusions: H3K9me3 is a stress-induced epigenetic barrier that limits metabolic adaptation and CM survival after ischemic injury. Epigenetic activation of PPP metabolism enhances redox homeostasis and improves cardiac repair following MI.
title: Abstract 5144: Epigenetic Activation of Pentose Phosphate Metabolism Protects the Heart After Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Background: Cardiac amyloid occurs in 15 to 40% of patients with aortic stenosis (AS), depending on subtype of AS, with potentially significant impact on prognosis. Definitive diagnosis of cardiac amyloid requires dedicated imaging or biopsy. We sought to develop a screening tool for amyloid in AS patients referred for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) using readily available pre-procedure EKG and echo data. Methods: EKGs and echoes of 4 groups were analyzed: (1) controls, (2) pre-procedure patients undergoing TAVR with D1 or (3) with D3 type AS, and (4) patients with known cardiac amyloid without AS (CA). Left ventricular mass index (LVMI, g/m 2 ) was calculated using end-diastolic dimensions of the LV, interventricular septum and posterior wall. A ratio (V/LVMI) was derived using the sum of S V1 and R V5 for voltage (V) divided by the LVMI. The groups were compared for EKG and echo findings, and a receiver-operator curve (ROC) was created for the CA group to optimize detection of cardiac amyloid in AS patients. A cutoff for V/LVMI in each group was adjusted for extracellular volume fractions (ECV) previously established for normals, AS with cardiac amyloid, and CA. Results: A total of 822 patients were studied, including 100 controls, 495 D1, 103 D3, and 124 CA patients. Patients with bundle branch blocks or paced rhythms were excluded from V/LVMI analysis. AS patients had higher LVMI, more LVH, atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances than controls (all P<0.0001). Comparing D1 and D3 patients, the latter had lower LVMI and less LVH, but nearly 4-fold higher incidence of low voltage and 3-fold higher incidence of AF (all P < 0.0001). CA patients had the highest rates of low voltage and permanent pacemaker implants. The V/LVMI was highest in our controls, and progressively lower in D1 AS, D3 AS, and CA (all P<0.006, see Figure). A V/LVMI cutoff for amyloid of 17.8 mV/g/m 2 was derived for the CA group with the ROC curve below showing sensitivity of 85% and specificity of 82%. Using our V/LVMI cutoffs adjusted for known ECVs in these populations, 2% of controls, 18.6% of D1 AS, 46.4% of D3 AS, and 83.1% of CA patients met high probability criteria for amyloid infiltration (all comparisons P<0.0001). Conclusions: The voltage/LVMI ratio correlates strongly with known prevalence of amyloid infiltration in controls, D1 AS, D3 AS and CA populations. This ratio, applied to patients undergoing TAVR, may serve as a simple, readily-available screening tool for identifying subjects at high risk of concomitant amyloid. These patients should be investigated further.
title: Abstract 5145: An Electrocardiographic and Echo Based Algorithm to Screen for Amyloid in Aortic Stenosis Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement

abstract: Background: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is safe and effective therapy for severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is an exceptionally rare and underrecognized complication, with limited data describing potential mechanisms. Case: A 76-year-old woman with coronary artery disease and chronic systolic heart failure presented with progressive dyspnea. Echocardiography demonstrated severe MR and left ventricular ejection fraction of 40-45%. She experienced persistent symptoms despite guideline-directed medical therapy and underwent successful TEER with two mitral clips, reducing MR to mild-to-moderate (Figure 1). Two days after discharge, she presented with hemodynamically unstable wide-complex tachycardia. Electrocardiogram demonstrated monomorphic VT with right bundle branch block morphology and left axis deviation, consistent with left posterior fascicular VT (Figure 2). She required urgent synchronized cardioversion and antiarrhythmic therapy. No evidence of acute ischemia or metabolic derangement was identified. The temporal relationship to TEER, combined with post-procedural imaging demonstrating increased transmitral gradient and evolving volume status, supports a mechanistic trigger involving papillary muscle stretch and mechano-electrical feedback facilitating a fascicular reentry circuit. Her hospital course was complicated by acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis with ultrafiltration and recurrent VT, prompting implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement for secondary prevention. Following discharge, she experienced a single recurrence of VT in the setting of antiarrhythmic nonadherence, which was successfully terminated with antitachycardia pacing. Conclusion: This case identifies TEER as a potential trigger for sustained fascicular VT, in which intended leaflet approximation and mitral constraint may secondarily alter ventricular loading and papillary muscle mechanics, promoting ventricular arrhythmogenesis. These findings suggest that ventricular arrhythmias after TEER may be underrecognized rather than absent in clinical practice. Early post-procedural rhythm surveillance and careful volume optimization should be considered to mitigate arrhythmic risk and guide timely intervention. Figures:
title: Abstract 5147: Sustained Ventricular Tachycardia Following Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Mitral Valve Repair: A Potentially Mechanically Mediated Arrhythmogenic Substrate

abstract: Background: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established treatment for mitral regurgitation. Single-leaflet device attachment with clip embolization is very rare (0.3%) and may result in systemic arterial embolization. Transcatheter endovascular retrieval offers a minimally invasive alternative to surgery in selected cases. We present a rare novel technique of using the ONOCOR basket to aid retrieval of the clip from the renal artery. Case Summary: A 71-year-old male presented with symptomatic severe degenerative mitral regurgitation and was deemed appropriate for TEER by the heart team. He has history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with dual-chamber ICD, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, severe obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, and severe pulmonary hypertension. The TEER procedure was challenging due to sub-optimal imaging; despite all the challenges a decent result was obtained acutely. Two clips (One XTW and one NTW) were deployed. However, follow-up imaging revealed embolization of one MitraClip devices, later confirmed to be in the left renal artery. The patient remained asymptomatic. Transthoracic echocardiography showed preserved LV systolic function (LVEF 57%) and only mild residual mitral regurgitation; one clip remained stable, while the second clip was detached. Given the systemic embolization, the patient was admitted electively for transcatheter retrieval. Procedure: After large bore access (18Fr Gore Dryseal) was obtained, abdominal angiography confirmed an embolized MitraClip lodged in the left renal artery. A transcatheter retrieval system consisting of a 12F FlexCath (Medtronic), ONO retrieval device, and a 7F EN Snare Multi-Loop inside of a multipurpose (MP) guide catheter was advanced into the abdominal aorta. The MP catheter was used to engage the left renal artery and the 7F EN Snare Multi-Loop (18/30) was used to capture the NTW Clip. Following confirmation of secure engagement, gentle traction was applied, and the clip was withdrawn in a controlled manner into the ONO device positioned in the abdominal aorta. The ONO device was closed on the clip and was then withdrawn as a unit into the 18 Fr Dryseal with no issues. Results: The NTW clip was retrieved successfully without complications. Final renal angiography demonstrated a patent left renal artery with no complications. Hemostasis was achieved using an 18F Manta closure device. Final femoral angiography confirmed adequate hemostasis. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that transcatheter endovascular retrieval of an embolized MitraClip using the ONOCOR device is feasible and safe. The use of ONOCOR device allows a seamless re-aligning of the snared clip into the sheath without the chance of catching the sheaths edge.
title: Abstract 5148: Successful Transcatheter Retrieval of an Embolized MitraClip Using ONOCOR® Device

abstract: Introduction/Background: The Myval balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve (THV) has emerged as an alternative to established platforms; however, comparative evidence with the Evolut self-expanding THV remains limited, particularly regarding procedural performance and conduction outcomes. Research Questions/Hypothesis: We evaluated comparative clinical and procedural outcomes between Myval and Evolut THVs in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Methods/Approach: A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published through March 2026. Eligible studies were observational comparative cohorts directly comparing Myval and Evolut THVs. Quality was appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), and transvalvular aortic regurgitation. Secondary outcomes included technical success and vascular complications. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 statistics, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots. Results/Data: Six observational studies (n=1332) were included. Myval was associated with a significantly lower PPI risk (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.37-0.84; p=0.005; I 2 =0%) and comparable 30-day mortality (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.31-2.23; p=0.72; I 2 =0%). No significant difference was observed in transvalvular aortic regurgitation (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.03-1.97; p=0.19; I 2 =45%); however, sensitivity analysis excluding one heterogeneity-driving study demonstrated a significant reduction favoring Myval (RR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.56; p=0.008; I 2 =0%). Myval demonstrated higher technical success (RR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.10; p<0.001; I 2 =0%) and lower minor vascular complications (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.85; p=0.02; I 2 =8%). Stroke (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.29-2.15; p=0.65; I 2 =0%) and acute kidney injury (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.07-1.79; p=0.21; I 2 =55%) rates were similar. Conclusion: In patients undergoing TAVI, balloon-expandable THVs were associated with lower PPI risk and higher technical success compared with self-expanding systems. While no significant difference in transvalvular aortic regurgitation was observed, sensitivity analysis suggests improved valve sealing with Myval. These findings support their use as a viable alternative to established self-expanding systems.
title: Abstract 5159: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Myval versus Evolut Transcatheter Heart Valves in Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Underlying mechanisms of right ventricular (RV) functional changes following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation are not fully understood, and RV failure remains a common complication if a sub-group of patients. LVAD-induced left ventricular unloading alters RV loading conditions and may modify RV end-systolic elastance (Ees, “contractile efficiency”), pulmonary artery (PA) elastance (Ea, “flow obstruction”) and RV- PA coupling (“energy inefficiency”) Hypothesis: LVAD support reduces PA Ea while improving RV-PA coupling, promoting a more efficient energetic state. Methods: In this prospective observational study, 29 LVAD patients (age 55±10 years, 86% male, 24% ischemic cardiomyopathy, 48% destination therapy) underwent invasive hemodynamic assessment at baseline and serial follow-up (median follow up 115 [15-653] days post LVAD). A total of 76 hemodynamic recordings were analyzed. Mixed-effects linear regression with patient-level random intercepts evaluated the association of LVAD support and time after implantation with RV end-systolic pressure (PES), RV Ees, PA Ea, and RV-PA coupling (Ees/Ea). Models accounted for repeated measurements within patients. Results: LVAD support was associated with a significant reduction in PES (β = -16.5 mmHg, 95% CI -21.1 to -11.9; p<0.001), Ees (β = -0.52 mmHg/mL, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.27; p<0.001), and Ea (β = -0.83 mmHg/mL, 95% CI -1.10 to -0.56; p<0.001). In contrast, RV-PA coupling increased (β = +0.32, 95% CI +0.02 to +0.63; p=0.038), indicating improved ventricular-vascular interaction and energy efficiency. In this cohort, time after implantation was not significantly associated with any parameter. Random-effects analysis demonstrated significant inter-patient variability. Conclusions: LVAD support is associated with a reduction in RV contractility and PA elastance, resulting in overall an improved RV contractile energetic efficiency and RV-PA coupling. These findings suggest that LVAD-induced unloading enhances RV-PA efficiency. Further studies are needed to determine the relationship between these changes, long term vascular reverse remodeling, clinical outcomes, and to specifically investigate how these physiological responses differ in patients who develop RV failure after LVAD implantation.
title: Abstract 5164: Left Ventricular Assist Device Support Improves Right Ventricular Energetics: A Mixed Effects Analysis of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling

abstract: Background: Fulminant cardiopulmonary collapse is a rare manifestation of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). We present a case of TTP presenting as combined cardiogenic shock and respiratory failure requiring veno-arterial-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VAV-ECMO) and Impella CP support to enable therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE). Case: A 37-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting before suffering cardiac arrest in the setting of refractory hypoxemia requiring VV-ECMO. She was found to be in cardiogenic shock with LVEF 5-10%, necessitating addition of an arterial limb to achieve a VAV configuration. Laboratory results showed thrombocytopenia and hemolysis with a PLASMIC score of 5 triggering ADAMTS13 activity testing, which was <10%, consistent with TTP. Several hours after cannulation, the patient developed worsening LV distension, poor pulsatility and minimal aortic valve opening, prompting consideration of LV unloading. Decision-making: Transesophageal echocardiography excluded LV thrombus prior to Impella CP placement for LV unloading. Ischemic evaluation was deferred given low pretest probability, hemodynamic instability, and acute renal failure. Endomyocardial biopsy was not performed due to bleeding risk. High-dose glucocorticoids and TPE were initiated for treatment of TTP, also serving as empiric treatment for potential giant cell or eosinophilic myocarditis. Caplacizumab was considered for her TTP but deferred due to bleeding risk related to suspected diffuse alveolar hemorrhage upon initial presentation. Outcome: Following TPE, steroids, and Impella CP support, she demonstrated rapid improvement in biventricular function, pulsatility, and hemodynamics within 12 hours, allowing stepwise deescalation of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). ADAMTS13 inhibitor assay was positive, confirming immune-mediated TTP. She exhibited remarkable neurologic preservation, was extubated 8 days after initial presentation, and completed intensive rehabilitation after hospitalization. On most recent follow-up 4 months after discharge, she has maintained myocardial recovery and normalization of ADAMTS13 activity. Discussion: In this case, the precise etiology of cardiomyopathy remains uncertain or multifactorial, whether TTP-associated microvascular thrombi, critical illness cardiomyopathy, or fulminant myocarditis. Nonetheless, VAV-ECPELLA served as a bridge to TPE, enabling end-organ recovery. Early recognition of TTP in unexplained shock and multiorgan failure facilitates prompt TPE, which is lifesaving. Multidisciplinary shock teams remain critical in guiding tMCS in these complex cases, as multiple forms of MCS may be needed for a successful outcome.
title: Abstract 5178: VAV-ECPELLA as Bridge to Therapeutic Plasma Exchange in Fulminant TTP Presenting with Cardiopulmonary Collapse

abstract: Background: Intravascular imaging (IVI; IVUS and OCT) is increasingly used to optimise percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in complex lesions, but its impact on hard clinical endpoints versus angiography-guided PCI remains debated. Hypothesis: We hypothesised that IVI-guided PCI improves hard clinical endpoints compared with angiography-guided PCI in patients undergoing intervention for complex coronary lesions. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane (through April 2026) for RCTs comparing IVI- vs angiography-guided PCI. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE); secondary outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), target-vessel revascularisation (TVR), target-lesion revascularisation (TLR), and stent thrombosis. Random-effects pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 . Results: Fourteen RCTs comprising 14,524 patients (7,531 IVI-guided; 6,993 angiography-guided) were analysed. Compared with angiography, IVI guidance significantly reduced the risk of MACE (RR 0.65; 95% CI: 0.53-0.81; I 2 = 77%), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.71; 95% CI: 0.52-0.97; I 2 = 39%), and MI (RR 0.85; 95% CI: 0.72-0.99; I 2 = 1%). Furthermore, IVI-guided PCI was associated with lower rates of TVR (RR 0.62; 95% CI: 0.46-0.83; I 2 = 65%), TLR (RR 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52-0.81; I 2 = 47%), and stent thrombosis (RR 0.44; 95% CI: 0.25-0.77; I 2 = 0%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.88; 95% CI: 0.74-1.05; I 2 = 0%) or target-vessel MI (RR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.50-1.03; I 2 = 64%). In subgroup analyses, IVUS and OCT showed comparable benefit on MACE (RR 0.63, 95% CI: 0.47-0.84; and RR 0.68, 95% CI: 0.53-0.87; interaction p=0.70). In Asian trials, intravascular imaging guidance was associated with a significant reduction in MACE (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.50-0.69), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.37-0.79), any MI (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.88), and TLR (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40-0.68) compared with angiography guidance, wheares European trials showed no significant benefit for same outcomes, with MACE results showing a significant subgroup interaction. Conclusion: In patients undergoing complex PCI, IVI guidance significantly improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography, with marked reductions in MACE, cardiovascular mortality, target-vessel revascularisation, and stent thrombosis. These data support intravascular imaging as a primary strategy in optimising stent deployment and mitigating long-term ischaemic risk.
title: Abstract 5190: Intravascular Imaging-Guided versus Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Complex Coronary Lesions: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials

abstract: Introduction: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), including peripheral artery disease (PAD), is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. PAD often co-occurs with diabetes (DM), coronary artery disease (CAD), and chronic kidney disease (CKD), which may further amplify risk. Estimating the prevalence of diagnosed PAD and associated MACE, MALE, and mortality risk may inform strategies to identify the highest risk patients and optimize prevention. Research Question: To estimate the prevalence of diagnosed PAD among older US adults and the associated risk of MACE, MALE, and mortality, overall and in those with comorbid DM, CAD, and CKD. Methods: Fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries were identified from CMS Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse Research Identifiable Files. Patients were stratified as diagnosed with PAD (PAD+) or not (PAD-) as of Jan 1, 2023, after which they were followed over 1 year for outcomes: MACE-plus (ischemic stroke, acute limb ischemia/major amputation, myocardial infarction, urgent arterial revascularization, cardiovascular death), MALE (acute/chronic limb ischemia, lower extremity arterial revascularization or amputation), and all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations of PAD and its interactions with DM, CAD, and CKD on outcomes. Results: Among 8,833,456 patients, 7.5% (n=663,119) had diagnosed PAD. Adults with PAD were older (mean age: 78.1 vs. 75.2 years), more often male (49.0% vs. 42.3%), and had more ASCVD risk factors, including DM (61.0% vs. 14.1%), CAD (59.9% vs. 11.4%), and CKD (44.1% vs. 8.6%). Overall, 85.7% of the PAD+ cohort vs. 23.8% of the PAD- had DM, CAD, and/or CKD. PAD was associated with increased hazards of all outcomes, regardless of the presence and any combination of concurrent DM, CAD, or CKD (Table 1). This effect was stronger for MALE, where PAD more than doubled the risk among patients with all three risk amplifiers. However, in the absence of risk amplifiers, the relative risk increase associated with PAD was even higher (e.g., for MALE, HR: 7.19 [95%CI: 7.02, 7.36]). Among patients with PAD, the presence of DM, CAD, or CKD was associated with increased hazards of having an ASCVD event and mortality (Table 2). Conclusions: A substantial proportion of older adults in the US had diagnosed PAD, which was associated with increased risk of MACE-plus, MALE, and all-cause mortality compared to those without PAD. Comorbid DM, CAD, or CKD were common and shown to increase risks in any combination. These findings underscore the urgent need for strategies to identify patients with PAD, characterize additional risk, implement intensive preventive care, and manage patients as outlined in guidelines.
title: Abstract 5196: Evaluating the Risk of Adverse Cardiovascular Events Among Older Adults with Diagnosed Peripheral Artery Disease in the US

abstract: Introduction: No head-to-head trial has compared PCSK9 inhibitors against each other or against oral dual lipid-lowering therapy on hard cardiovascular outcomes. We conducted three parallel analyses using real-world electronic health records to address this gap. Hypothesis: Evolocumab-based regimens are associated with lower mortality, fewer cardiovascular events, and lower rates of new-onset diabetes compared with alirocumab and oral dual lipid-lowering strategies. Methods: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we performed three 1:1 propensity-score-matched analyses in adults aged 50 to 80 with atherosclerotic disease or high-risk diabetes, and LDL-C of at least 90 mg/dL or apolipoprotein B of at least 80 mg/dL on lipid-lowering therapy with no prior history of myocardial infarction or stroke: Analysis A, evolocumab versus alirocumab, Analysis B; evolocumab plus statin versus statin plus ezetimibe; Analysis C, evolocumab monotherapy versus statin plus ezetimibe. Outcomes assessed over three years included all-cause mortality, MACE-plus, myocardial infarction, stroke or TIA, heart failure, revascularization, acute kidney injury, rhabdomyolysis, new-onset type 2 diabetes, and LDL-C goal attainment at or below 55 mg/dL. Results: Analysis A (2,610 matched pairs) showed evolocumab versus alirocumab was associated with lower mortality (1.4% vs 2.7%; RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.36-0.78), lower MACE-plus (RR 0.66, 0.50-0.87), lower stroke/TIA (RR 0.56, 0.37-0.86), and higher LDL-C goal attainment (32.2% vs 24.7%; all p<0.01). Analysis B (10,465 matched pairs) showed evolocumab plus statin versus statin plus ezetimibe was associated with lower mortality (RR 0.76, 0.64-0.90), MACE-plus (RR 0.77, 0.68-0.88), stroke/TIA (RR 0.80, 0.66-0.98), heart failure (RR 0.83, 0.75-0.92), acute kidney injury (RR 0.77, 0.67-0.87), new-onset diabetes (RR 0.66, 0.58-0.74), and higher LDL-C goal attainment (28.8% vs 19.2%; all p<0.05). Analysis C (9,279 matched pairs) showed evolocumab monotherapy versus statin plus ezetimibe was associated with lower mortality (RR 0.78, 0.65-0.94), MACE-plus (RR 0.65, 0.56-0.75), myocardial infarction (RR 0.62, 0.49-0.79), stroke/TIA (RR 0.51, 0.40-0.66), heart failure (RR 0.61, 0.54-0.68), acute kidney injury (RR 0.56, 0.48-0.65), rhabdomyolysis (RR 0.50, 0.32-0.78), new-onset diabetes (RR 0.63, 0.55-0.72), and higher LDL-C goal attainment (22.2% vs 17.6%; all p<0.01). Conclusions: Across three analyses totaling over 44,000 patients, evolocumab was consistently associated with lower mortality, fewer cardiovascular events, lower heart failure and new-onset diabetes rates, and higher LDL-C goal attainment versus alirocumab and oral dual lipid-lowering strategies. These findings contribute real-world comparative data on PCSK9 inhibitor selection in high-risk primary prevention.
title: Abstract 5197: PCSK9 Inhibitors in Primary Cardiovascular Prevention: A Multi-Cohort Comparative Effectiveness Study of Evolocumab and Alirocumab versus Oral Dual Lipid-Lowering Therapy Using Real-World Electronic Health Records

abstract: Background: Blood-based epigenetic histone modifications are emerging as pivotal biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in cardiovascular diseases. Histone serotonylation—the covalent attachment of serotonin to glutamine 5 on histone H3 (H3K4me3Q5ser)—is a novel dual-modification. However, its relevance in leukocytes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. Aims: This study investigated the prognostic value of circulating leukocyte H3K4me3Q5ser levels in patients with HFpEF and to elucidate its mechanistic impact on monocyte-macrophages. Methods: Leukocyte H3K4me3Q5ser levels were quantified by immunoblotting in 191 hospitalized patients with HFpEF (mean age, 67.1 ± 14.4 years). Mechanistically, transglutaminase 2 (TGM2), an enzyme involved in histone serotonylation, was investigated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated TGM2-knockout (KO) RAW264.7 macrophages. Macrophage-specific TGM2 conditional KO mice were generated and subjected to a two-hit HFpEF model (L-NAME and high fat diet). Results: Clinical stratification revealed that lower leukocyte H3K4me3Q5ser levels were associated with a significantly higher risk of composite cardiac events, including worsening heart failure, cardiac death, and acute coronary syndrome, compared to higher levels during a median follow-up of 2238 days (Fig. 1) . In multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, the low H3K4me3Q5ser group had a higher risk of composite cardiac events compared with the high H3K4me3Q5ser group (hazard ratio, 2.60; P = 0.02). RNA sequencing analysis revealed that TGM2-KO macrophages displayed a transcriptomic profile distinct from that of wild-type macrophages after lipopolysaccharide stimulation, with 1,158 differentially expressed genes, including 545 upregulated and 613 downregulated genes (Fig. 2) . Enrichment analysis showed that downregulated genes were mainly associated with immune pathways, including cytokine regulation, TLR signaling, and NF-κB signaling, while upregulated genes were enriched in cell adhesion molecule binding, integrin binding, tissue morphogenesis, and actin filament-based movement. In vivo, macrophage-specific TGM2-deficient mice showed exacerbated cardiac diastolic dysfunction, including an elevated E/A ratio in the HFpEF model compared to wild-type littermates (P< 0.01). Conclusion: Lower leukocyte H3K4me3Q5ser levels were associated with worse cardiac outcomes in HFpEF patients. Macrophage TGM2 deficiency may impair appropriate inflammatory response while promoting an abnormal tissue-infiltrative and remodeling phenotype, thereby contributing to HFpEF-related diastolic dysfunction.
title: Abstract 5201: Clinical and Mechanistic Significance of Blood-Based Histone Serotonylation in Leukocytes in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

abstract: Introduction: Device migration is a complication of endovascular embolization procedures. Retrieval of intracardiac foreign bodies involving valvular structures carries risk of irreversible valve injury. We report delayed embolization coil migration from an extracranial arteriovenous malformation (AVM) into the tricuspid valve apparatus complicated by catastrophic valve injury during retrieval requiring surgical repair. Case Description: A 45-year-old woman with congenital right masticator space AVM underwent two prior staged coil embolization procedures. Months later, during evaluation for planned third-stage embolization, she reported pleuritic chest tightness. Chest radiography demonstrated metallic wire extending from the right neck through the superior vena cava (SVC) into the cardiac silhouette. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a 2.1 х 0.79 cm mobile foreign body attached to the anterior and septal tricuspid leaflets extending into the right ventricle with mild tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a knotted coil extending from the SVC with entrapment within the tricuspid subvalvular apparatus. CT angiography demonstrated coil migration from the facial AVM through the SVC into the right ventricle with septal leaflet and subvalvular involvement. A multidisciplinary team including interventional cardiology, vascular surgery, and neurosurgery pursued retrieval in a hybrid operating room. Percutaneous extraction via femoral venous access using a goose-neck snare removed the intracardiac coil segment. Residual coil fragments required surgical extraction. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated acute massive TR from flail anterior leaflet and papillary muscle avulsion following extraction. Post-procedural transthoracic echocardiography confirmed massive TR with right-sided chamber dilation and preserved biventricular systolic function. The patient developed hypotension requiring intensive care and underwent tricuspid valve repair with a 26-mm annuloplasty ring. Recovery was unremarkable with symptom resolution. Discussion: Delayed migration of embolization coils into cardiac structures following extracranial AVM treatment is rare. This case highlights the role of multimodality imaging before intervention. Although percutaneous retrieval of intravascular foreign bodies is generally successful, devices entrapped within valvular structures present unique procedural challenges. In this case, the coil’s knotted configuration and papillary muscle entrapment made atraumatic extraction impossible, resulting in catastrophic valve injury despite successful retrieval. This case underscores the importance of multidisciplinary planning and immediate cardiac surgical availability when managing intracardiac foreign bodies involving valvular structures.
title: Abstract 5234: Delayed Embolization Coil Migration to the Tricuspid Valve Apparatus with Catastrophic Iatrogenic Valve Injury During Percutaneous Retrieval: A Case Highlighting the Need for Multidisciplinary Preparedness

abstract: Introduction: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treats high-risk COVID-19. Ritonavir inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, decreasing hepatic clearance of propafenone and warfarin. Propafenone inhibits CYP1A2 and may further decrease warfarin clearance. Clinical consequences of these interactions have not been described.
