Patient Information: The patient is a 51-year-old female with bicuspid aortic valve and aortic stenosis s/p mechanical replacement, coarctation of the aorta s/p repair, atrial fibrillation, HFpEF, and OSA. Her medications include warfarin 5 mg daily (INR goal 2-3, time in therapeutic range 81.2%) and propafenone 225 mg BID. Clinical Findings and Timeline: The patient was prescribed nirmatrelvir/ritonavir for COVID-19 without warfarin or propafenone dose adjustment. Three days later, she presented with dyspnea and hematochezia. HR was 36 bpm and BP was 111/46 mmHg; EKG showed sinus bradycardia. Exam revealed bleeding external hemorrhoids and 1+ bilateral lower extremity edema. Labs were notable for NT-Pro BNP 2,178 pg/mL, increased from 469 pg/mL prior, INR of 4.2, and hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL. Chest X-ray showed pulmonary edema. Transthoracic echocardiogram was unremarkable. Given the risk of cardiogenic shock, the patient was transferred to the cardiac intensive care unit at a tertiary care center. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The patient’s bradyarrhythmia and heart failure exacerbation were consistent with propafenone toxicity. Her hemorrhoidal bleeding was likely caused by supratherapeutic INR. Both effects were likely precipitated by nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. Therapeutic Interventions: The patient was normotensive with no signs of hypoperfusion, so hemodynamic support was deferred. Hemorrhoidal bleeding resolved without intervention. Warfarin and propafenone were held, and nirmatrelvir/ritonavir was discontinued. A net 3 L diuresis was achieved with IV furosemide. By hospital day 2, the patient’s heart rate normalized, and her INR decreased to 3.0. Warfarin was resumed at a reduced dose of 2.5 mg daily and propafenone was held at discharge. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient fully recovered. In the ambulatory setting, warfarin was increased to 5 mg BID and propafenone was resumed. Discussion & Synthesis: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir can precipitate a compounding pharmacokinetic interaction with propafenone and warfarin. Ritonavir innibits hepatic metabolism of warfarin via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. Ritonavir also impairs CYP3A4-mediated metabolism of propafenone, increasing the risk of bradycardia and arrhythmia. Propafenone inhibits CYP1A2 and may further amplify warfarin exposure. Clinicians must anticipate INR elevation and consider reducing warfarin dose. Propafenone can be held in select patients. This case underscores the importance of consulting interaction-checking resources before initiating nirmatrelvir/ritonavir.
title: Abstract 5253: A Case of Propafenone and Warfarin Toxicity Precipitated by Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir for COVID-19

abstract: Background: A 51 year old man with HFrEF due to non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation and flutter s/p PVI/CTI, and aortic regurgitation presented for optimization prior to planned aortic valve replacement. Ten months prior to admission, he was found to have atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; echocardiography revealed a dilated LV with LVIDd of 7.0 cm, severely reduced LVEF of 21%, and moderate-severe aortic regurgitation. He underwent PVI with CTI ablation six months prior to admission. Cardiac MRI demonstrated mild curvilinear mid-wall enhancement of the basal LV septum without other delayed enhancement and an LVEF of 27%. Case Description: Given ongoing HF symptoms, he presented for inpatient HF optimization prior to AVR. He endorsed NYHA class III symptoms with severely decreased exercise tolerance. Initial vitals and laboratory studies were unremarkable. Given uncertainty regarding the severity of his valvular disease, transesophageal echocardiography was obtained and demonstrated only moderate aortic regurgitation (Figure 1). AVR was cancelled due to lack of indication. While hospitalized, he experienced several incessant runs of wide complex tachycardia (Figure 2), initially concerning for supraventricular tachycardia with aberrant conduction as well as non-sustained ventricular tachycardia in the setting of apparent AV dissociation and structural heart disease. He was initiated on amiodarone. Given NICM of unclear etiology and electrical activity, sarcoid protocol PET imaging was obtained and demonstrated equivocal myocardial FDG uptake in the inferolateral LV papillary muscle. Endomyocardial biopsy demonstrated no evidence of myocarditis or sarcoidosis. Genetic testing revealed variants of uncertain significance in multiple cardiomyopathy-associated genes (ANKRD1, CASQ2, TPM1). Electrophysiology evaluation ultimately determined the predominant arrhythmia to be dual AV nodal non-reentrant (“double fire”) tachycardia with LBBB aberrancy incited by phase 3 block and maintained by concealed conduction. He subsequently underwent electrophysiology study demonstrating infrahisian disease and two distinct AH intervals with decremental RV pacing (Figure 3). Radiofrequency ablation of the AV nodal slow pathway was performed during sinus rhythm. At three months post-ablation, his HF symptoms had resolved completely, consistent with a large contribution of conduction-mediated cardiomyopathy, pending objective reassessment of LV function. Discussion: This case illustrates the complexity at the intersection of valvular heart disease, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, and wide complex tachycardia. Careful characterization of both the patient’s arrhythmia and cardiomyopathy avoided unnecessary valve intervention and ultimately led to a successful ablative strategy with marked clinical improvement.
title: Abstract 5272: Mr. DoubleFire: Dual AV Nodal Physiology Masquerading as Wide Complex Tachycardia in a Patient with Cardiomyopathy and Aortic Regurgitation

abstract: Introduction: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a leading cause of pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction while pulmonary embolism (PE) is a well-recognized peripartum complication. Their concurrent presentation is rare and poses unique therapeutic dilemmas as management strategies for each entity may theoretically conflict. We present a case of simultaneous sub-massive PE and SCAD in a post-partum patient. Patient Information: A 39-year-old G11P11 female with obesity and hyperlipidemia presented one week after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Clinical Findings & Timeline: The patient reported acute left-sided chest pain and dyspnea. She was normotensive with a heart rate of 73 BPM and was saturating 96% on room air. Labs were notable for a peak troponin I of 86.2 ng/mL, pro-BNP of 135 pg/mL, and mild transaminitis. Electrocardiogram demonstrated anterolateral ST-segment elevations (Figure 1). Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The combination of dyspnea and risk factors in the peripartum period prompted CT pulmonary angiography, showing sub-massive PE in the right pulmonary artery. Concurrent anterior ST-segment elevations raised concern for a coronary event. Urgent cardiac catheterization revealed long tubular non-flow-limiting stenoses of the mid-LAD and D1 consistent with type 2 SCAD (Figure 2). Echocardiography demonstrated a newly reduced LVEF of 38% with severe hypokinesis of the apex and mid to apical septum. Right ventricular size and function were preserved, suggesting that hemodynamic burden predominated from SCAD. Lower extremity venous duplex was negative for deep venous thrombosis. Therapeutic Interventions: She was managed in the CCU with aspirin, a heparin drip, and guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF. PCI was deferred due to absence of refractory chest pain or arrhythmias. Anticoagulation was continued for the PE despite the theoretical risk of propagating the dissection, following multidisciplinary risk-benefit analysis involving our primary Cardiology team with the pulmonology, hematology, and OB/GYN consult teams. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: She was eventually discharged on apixaban with resolution of chest pain and no adverse bleeding events during her CCU stay. Discussion & Synthesis: Concurrent SCAD and PE in the peripartum period created a therapeutic paradox: anticoagulation was necessary for the PE but carried a risk of propagating the dissection. This case underscores the need for individualized decision-making, close hemodynamic monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration when managing competing life-threatening conditions with distinct treatment algorithms. Reporting such cases is important to inform future management protocols for this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 5284: Concurrent Postpartum Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection and Submassive Pulmonary Embolism- A Complex Anticoagulation Challenge

abstract: Cardiac PET is valuable in the evaluation of inflammatory heart disease, including cardiac sarcoidosis. PET abnormalities are highly sensitive but not fully specific. As the use of PET increases, there is potential for anchoring bias and premature closure when findings are interpreted without sufficient clinical context. A 32-year-old man presented with dyspnea, productive cough, fever, night sweats, and 20-pound weight loss. Symptoms were present for the last year but worsened over the preceding month. His only medical history was anemia. He was born in Haiti, had lived in Brazil, and was now living in Ohio. On presentation, he was tachycardic, febrile, and hypoxic, requiring supplemental oxygen. Labs showed chronic mild anemia, mildly elevated high-sensitivity troponin I, and NT-proBNP 3885. EKG showed sinus tachycardia. CXR revealed multifocal opacities and small right pleural effusion. CTPE was without PE but showed cardiomegaly with hepatic venous reflux of contrast, pulmonary edema, ground glass opacities, consolidation, bilateral pleural effusions, and an enlarged prevascular lymph node. TTE showed LVEF 55%, dilated LV, LA, severe MR, moderate TR, and moderately severe AR. LHC showed normal epicardial coronary arteries. CMR showed multifocal subendocardial LGE. Cardiac PET demonstrated active myocardial inflammation with additional pulmonary FDG uptake. QuantiFERON testing was positive, active TB was excluded with three respiratory cultures. Bronchoscopy with biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation without malignancy. Multidisciplinary evaluation favored cardiac and pulmonary sarcoidosis based on PET and biopsy findings. Glucocorticoids and methotrexate were planned. Given severe symptomatic multivalvular disease, immunosuppression was deferred to allow surgical aortic, mitral, and tricuspid valve replacement/repair, then initiated postoperatively. Subsequent skin findings prompted biopsy. Pathology and universal PCR from valve and skin specimens were positive for Mycobacterium chelonae . He was treated with azithromycin, tigecycline, and tobramycin. Isoniazid was prescribed for LTBI. At follow-up, symptoms improved, LVEF was 45%. This case underscores the importance of integrating imaging with the broader clinical picture when nonspecific findings support multiple competing diagnoses. Constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, LGE on CMR, active inflammation on PET, and granulomatous biopsy findings initially supported sarcoidosis in a patient with LTBI. However, the predominant cardiac manifestation, severe valvular disease, was atypical for sarcoidosis and should have prompted reconsideration of the working diagnosis. M. chelonae valvulitis is rare, particularly in native valves, and this case illustrates how advanced imaging may inadvertently reinforce anchoring bias when discordant clinical features are underweighted.
title: Abstract 5285: Beyond the Uptake: When Cardiac PET Fuels Anchoring Bias and Mycobacterium chelonae Goes Undetected

abstract: Background: Fulminant myocarditis (FM) accounts for up to 25% of cardiogenic shock cases and carries in-hospital mortality exceeding 45%. Parainfluenza virus is a rare but recognized trigger; outcomes remain poor despite advances in care. Dual mechanical circulatory support (MCS) combining venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) with a microaxial left ventricular unloading device (ECPella strategy) has emerged as a potential bridge to recovery, yet clinical data in virus-confirmed FM remain sparse. Case Summary: A 53-year-old man with prediabetes and former tobacco use presented to the emergency department after three days of myalgia, chest soreness, and an unwitnessed syncopal episode. Electrocardiogram demonstrated diffuse ST-segment changes across leads V1-V6. Initial high-sensitivity troponin was markedly elevated at 18,234 ng/L, peaking at 31,232 ng/L. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed an ejection fraction (EF) of 55% on arrival, with rapid deterioration to 37% within 24 hours and a small-to-moderate pericardial effusion without tamponade. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary disease; cardiac catheterization confirmed low cardiac index (1.78 L/min/m 2 ) and elevated systemic vascular resistance. Cardiac MRI demonstrated diffuse late gadolinium enhancement. Despite inotropic support with milrinone, pulse-dose corticosteroids, and pericardiocentesis (yielding 300 mL), the patient progressed to refractory arrhythmias, hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring vasopressor escalation, and multiorgan dysfunction. VA-ECMO with concomitant Impella for LV unloading (ECPella) was initiated. Endomyocardial biopsy confirmed lymphocytic myocarditis; respiratory viral panel identified parainfluenza virus. With hemodynamic stabilization, the patient improved progressively, enabling successful device weaning. At 8-week follow-up, EF recovered to 45% and functional status was NYHA class II. He was discharged on sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, dapagliflozin, and spironolactone. Discussion: This case illustrates that parainfluenza virus can precipitate rapidly fatal FM requiring maximal MCS. The ECPella strategy provided biventricular support and LV unloading, stabilizing hemodynamics while myocardial recovery occurred. Early escalation to dual MCS may shift outcomes away from transplantation or death toward recovery in carefully selected patients. Endomyocardial biopsy with viral panel remains essential for etiologic diagnosis and guiding therapy. Conclusion: In parainfluenza-associated FM, timely escalation to dual MCS with the ECPella strategy can serve as an effective bridge to myocardial recovery, avoiding transplantation in an otherwise potentially fatal presentation. Prospective registries are needed to establish consensus thresholds for dual MCS initiation in FM.
title: Abstract 5288: Dual Mechanical Circulatory Support in Parainfluenza-Associated Fulminant Myocarditis: A Case Report

abstract: Background: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in adults, affecting an estimated 3-6 million people in the United States, with projections rising to nearly 16 million cases by 2050. AF is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly due to an increased risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation therapy, especially with direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC), remains the standard strategy for stroke prevention. However, DOAC therapy may be unsuitable for some patients because of an elevated risk of major bleeding, contraindications, or poor treatment adherence. Consequently, left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as a nonpharmacologic alternative for stroke prevention in patients with AF who are at high bleeding risk or unable to tolerate long-term anticoagulation. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted through May 2026 to identify studies comparing LAAC versus DOAC in patients with AF. Meta-analysis inclusion criteria were established according to Cochrane Collaboration guidelines. Three independent reviewers performed data extraction and study quality assessment. Risk of bias was evaluated using the ROBINS-I and ROB-2 tools for observational studies and randomized controlled trials, respectively. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled using odds ratios (OR) with 95% CI through the inverse-variance method under a random-effects model. Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using hazard ratios (HR) with corresponding 95% CI using a random-effects model. Statistical analyses were performed using RevMan version 5.3. Results: A total of 23 studies (8 RCT and 15 observational studies) were included examining 324,321 patients with AF (305,949 DOAC vs 18,372 LAAC). Compared with DOAC, LAAC showed no significant difference in the primary composite endpoint (stroke, systemic embolism, major bleeding, and cardiovascular death) (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.72-1.03). Similarly, stroke risk was comparable between groups (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.84-1.09). However, LAAC was associated with a significantly lower risk of major bleeding (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.87). A trend toward reduced cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.56-1.00) and all-cause mortality (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.56-1.02) was also observed with LAAC, although these findings did not consistently reach statistical significance. Conclusion: In patients with AF, LAAC showed comparable efficacy to DOAC for stroke prevention, with a significantly lower risk of major bleeding and a potential reduction in mortality. Further large-scale randomized trials are needed to better define the long-term comparative effectiveness of these strategies.
title: Abstract 5293: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Technologies Compared with Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Atrial Fibrillation: Updated Evidence from a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 324,321 Patients

abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite carrying a substantially higher procedural risk profile than conventional percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), outcomes of chronic total occlusion (CTO) PCI in patients with active malignancy remain entirely uncharacterized. We examined cancer prevalence trends and in-hospital outcomes among cancer patients undergoing CTO PCI nationally. METHODS: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), identifying CTO PCI admissions using ICD-10-CM/PCS codes. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) compared outcomes in cancer vs no-cancer patients within the CTO PCI cohort. Myelosuppression was examined as a pre-specified high-risk subgroup. RESULTS: Among 214,365 weighted CTO PCI admissions, cancer prevalence rose significantly from 1.61% to 2.06% (OR/year 1.065, 95%CI 1.028-1.104, p=0.001). Despite higher unadjusted mortality (5.21% vs 3.69%), cancer was not independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 0.911, 95%CI 0.627-1.323, p=0.625) or IPTW analysis (adjusted odds ratio 1.135, p=0.538). Myelosuppression identified a high-risk subgroup and was associated with more than twofold higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 2.593, 95% CI 1.068-6.294, p=0.037); however, this finding is based on a small, unweighted sample (n=44) with a wide CI and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Hispanic cancer patients had significantly lower odds of CTO PCI receipt (adjusted odds ratio 0.742, p=0.036), suggesting disparities in procedural utilization. CONCLUSIONS: Cancer patients undergoing CTO PCI, when appropriately selected, demonstrate comparable adjusted outcomes to non-cancer patients, supporting the feasibility of this complex procedure in the oncologic population. In a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis limited by small sample size, myelosuppression was associated with higher in-hospital mortality warranting prospective validation.
title: Abstract 5307: Revascularization of Chronic Total Occlusion in Cancer Patients: Comparable Outcomes with Myelosuppression as a Potential Risk Modifier

abstract: Introduction: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with significant perioperative risk in patients undergoing solid organ transplantation. In patients with decompensated cirrhosis, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) carries high operative morbidity and mortality, frequently precluding transplant candidacy. While transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has emerged as a bridging strategy to isolated liver or kidney transplantation in high-risk patients, its use as a bridge specifically to simultaneous liver-kidney (SLK) transplantation remains rarely reported. Case Presentation: A 71-year-old man with decompensated NASH cirrhosis (MELD-Na 20) complicated by esophageal and rectal varices, hepatic encephalopathy, severe thrombocytopenia (platelets ~20х10 9 /L), chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease presented for transplant evaluation. Initial echocardiography suggested moderate-to-severe AS (mean gradient: 36 mmHg; aortic valve area index [AVAi]: 0.45 cm 2 /m 2 ); repeat echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic assessment during transplant evaluation confirmed severe AS (mean gradient: 40 mmHg; peak velocity: 3.89 m/s; AVAi: 0.53 cm 2 /m 2 ). Given advanced cirrhosis and multiple comorbidities, he was deemed unsuitable for SAVR by cardiothoracic surgery, making him ineligible for transplantation. After multidisciplinary evaluation, transfemoral TAVR was selected as bridging therapy. Intervention and Outcomes: Given severe thrombocytopenia, the patient received packed red blood cells, platelets, and fresh frozen plasma prior to the procedure. Transfemoral TAVR with a 29-mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 Resilia valve was performed without intraprocedural complications. Follow-up echocardiography showed marked improvement in valve hemodynamics (mean gradient: 6 mmHg; peak velocity: 1.72 m/s; AVAi: 1.24 cm 2 /m 2 ). Prior to transplantation, he was hospitalized for hepatorenal syndrome requiring initiation of hemodialysis. Three months post-TAVR, SLK transplantation was performed, complicated intraoperatively only by transient atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Longitudinal tracking confirmed durable valve function, with a transient, self-resolving gradient increase to 13 mmHg at one month post-transplant, normalizing to 8 mmHg at one year (AVAi: 1.39 cm 2 /m 2 ), alongside excellent dual-graft function with normalized bilirubin and creatinine (1.36 mg/dL) without rejection. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that TAVR can safely restore SLK transplantation eligibility in patients with severe AS and prohibitive surgical risk, with durable valve and dual-graft function confirmed at one year. Careful multidisciplinary coordination may permit successful SLK transplantation in select patients otherwise considered unsuitable surgical candidates.
title: Abstract 5320: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement as a Bridge to Simultaneous Liver and Kidney Transplantation in Severe Aortic Stenosis and Cirrhosis

abstract: Background: Percutaneous mechanical circulatory support (pMCS) is increasingly used in critically ill patients, yet its value in relation to cost and outcomes remains unclear. We evaluated national variation in utilization, outcomes, and cost, and introduced a value-of-care framework integrating risk-adjusted outcomes and expenditures. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample to identify non-elective hospitalizations of critically ill patients undergoing intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous left ventricular assist device (pLVAD) placement using ICD-10 codes. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized linear models were used to estimate expected outcomes and costs. Observed-to-expected (O/E) ratios were calculated, and a value index was derived to compare procedural strategies. Results: A total of 57,910 weighted hospitalizations were included (IABP 78%, pLVAD 22%). In-hospital mortality exceeded 30% across regions. Significant regional variation was observed, with the West demonstrating the highest costs and the Midwest the lowest (p<0.001). Mean hospital charges were higher for pLVAD compared with IABP ($403,731 vs $320,769). Both strategies achieved outcomes better than expected after risk adjustment (O/E ~0.90-0.92); however, costs were higher than expected for both, with greater relative cost inflation observed for IABP (O/E ~1.41) and higher absolute costs for pLVAD. In value-of-care analysis, IABP was associated with lower cost and comparable outcomes, while pLVAD demonstrated higher cost without proportional outcome improvement. Conclusion: Substantial variation exists in the cost, outcomes, and value of pMCS strategies. While both IABP and pLVAD achieve favorable risk-adjusted outcomes, pLVAD is associated with higher costs without commensurate clinical benefit at the population level. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing patient selection and incorporating value-based frameworks in the use of advanced mechanical circulatory support.
title: Abstract 5325: Cost-Outcome Variation in Percutaneous Mechanical Circulatory Support: A National Value-of-Care Analysis

abstract: Background: Hemodynamic response to intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) therapy is highly heterogeneous, and predictors of response remain poorly defined. To date, no studies have evaluated the role of right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling, a key determinant of RV energetic efficiency, in modulating response to IABP support. Hypothesis: Baseline (before IABP implant) RV-PA coupling is associated with cardiac index (CI), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and wedge pressure following IABP support. Methods: We performed a longitudinal analysis using mixed-effects modeling to evaluate the association between baseline RV-PA coupling (ratio of RV end-systolic elastance [Ees], reflecting contractility, to PA elastance [Ea], reflecting afterload) and CI (by Fick method), MAP, and wedge pressure during IABP support. Ees/Ea was estimated using a single-beat method derived from invasive pressure waveforms obtained during right heart catheterization prior to IABP insertion. The models included fixed effects for baseline Ees/Ea, IABP support, and time from IABP initiation, with random intercepts at the patient level. A maximum of 102 observations from 31 patients were analyzed (mean 3.3 observations per patient). Results: 31 cardiogenic shock patients (baseline demographics in the Table) were included. Baseline RV-PA coupling was independently associated with higher CI during IABP support (β=0.60, SE=0.25, p=0.016, 95% CI 0.11-1.08). IABP support was associated with a significant increase in CI (β=0.58, SE=0.17, p<0.001, 95% CI 0.26-0.91). In contrast, neither baseline RV-PA coupling (p=0.231) nor IABP support (p=0.952) were associated with changes in MAP. While IABP support was associated with a marked reduction in wedge pressure (β=–10.0 mmHg, SE=1.00, p<0.001, 95% CI –11.96 to –8.03), baseline RV-PA coupling was not significantly associated with wedge pressure during IABP support (p=0.241). There was significant between-patient variability, supporting heterogeneity in hemodynamic response. Conclusions: Baseline (before IABP) RV-PA coupling is directly associated with CI after initiation of IABP support. These findings suggest that baseline RV-PA coupling identifies patients more likely to derive hemodynamic benefit from IABP, supporting a physiology-driven approach to patient selection. Further studies are needed to determine whether RV-PA coupling can guide device allocation and improve outcomes in cardiogenic shock.
title: Abstract 5328: Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling is Associated with Cardiac Index During Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support

abstract: Background: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established minimally invasive therapy for mitral regurgitation (MR). However, post-procedural mitral stenosis (PPMS) remains a major complication. While the posterior mitral leaflet is classically described as comprising three distinct scallops (P1, P2, and P3), studies have shown that this “textbook” morphology is present in only approximately 41-72.5% of the population. Despite the relatively common presence of these anatomical variations, they are often underrecognized, and their impact on post-procedural hemodynamics, including the development of PPMS following TEER, has not been well studied.(Figure 1) Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study evaluating 192 patients who underwent TEER. Patients were categorized according to mitral valve morphology, including fused P1-P2, fused P2-P3, and other anatomical variants such as accessory P2, absent P2, and dichotomous scallops. Additional variables assessed included Carpentier classification of MR, mitral annular diameter, number of clips deployed, preprocedural mitral valve gradient, and other echocardiographic parameters. Associations between morphologic and clinical variables and PPMS status were assessed using categorical statistical analyses.PPMS was defined as mean mitral valve gradient greater than 6 mmHg, heart rate less than 90 bpm, and Doppler velocity index (DVI) greater than 2.5. Results: Non-classical posterior scallop morphology was identified in 22% of patients overall with fused posterior scallops present in 12% of patients most commonly involving fusion of P1-P2. PPMS occurred in 9% of patients who underwent TEER. Fused posterior leaflet scallops were associated with increased odds of PPMS following TEER (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.2-12.3, p=0.02). Additional predictors of PPMS included elevated pre-TEER mitral gradient, mitral annular calcification, smaller mitral annular dimensions, and deployment of multiple clips (Table 1). Figure 2 demonstrates an illustrative case of fused P1/P2 posterior scallops associated with development of PPMS despite clip repositioning. Conclusions: Mitral valve morphology, particularly posterior scallop fusion, is associated with an increased risk of PPMS following TEER. These findings highlight the importance of detailed pre-procedural anatomical assessment to improve risk stratification and procedural planning.
title: Abstract 5357: Impact of Mitral Valve Morphology on the Development of Mitral Stenosis Following Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Sex differences in aortic stenosis (AS) biology, presentation, referral patterns, and outcomes have increasingly been recognized. Women demonstrate distinct valvular phenotypes, present later with more advanced symptoms, and historically undergo aortic valve replacement less frequently than men. However, whether sex-based differences in AS mortality vary geographically across the United States remains poorly understood. We evaluated national and state-level sex-specific mortality patterns for nonrheumatic AS from 2018-2024. Methods: Death certificate data were obtained from the CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death database for nonrheumatic AS from 2018-2024. National and state-level crude mortality rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated by sex. National and state-level sex differences and temporal mortality trajectories were evaluated across the study period using regression-based modeling. Results: A total of 92,518 deaths attributable to nonrheumatic AS occurred from 2018-2024. Nationally, women demonstrated higher crude mortality rates compared with men (4.45 vs 3.52 per 100,000 person-years; P<0.001). Female mortality exceeded male mortality in every study year (all P<0.001). Although mortality declined in both sexes, women demonstrated a steeper annual decline in mortality compared with men (–0.13 vs –0.03 per 100,000/year), resulting in progressive narrowing of the sex gap over time. Marked geographic heterogeneity was observed across the United States. Women demonstrated higher mortality rates in 49 states, reaching statistical significance in 35 states. The largest female excess mortality differences were observed in Vermont (11.37 vs 6.87 per 100,000), Maine (12.10 vs 9.12 per 100,000), and Iowa (8.02 vs 5.38 per 100,000). New Mexico was the only state in which male mortality significantly exceeded female mortality (2.62 vs 2.04 per 100,000; P=0.022). Conclusion: Nonrheumatic AS mortality in the United States demonstrates a persistent but narrowing female excess mortality pattern. Despite major advances in structural heart disease therapies, women continued to exhibit significantly higher mortality nationally and across most states. However, the more rapid decline in female mortality suggests evolving epidemiology or differential benefits from contemporary AS management strategies - heart team, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Significant geographic heterogeneity further suggests that regional differences in diagnosis, referral patterns, and access to structural heart interventions may contribute to persistent sex-based disparities in AS mortality.
title: Abstract 5374: Geographic Patterns of Excess Mortality in Females with Aortic Stenosis

abstract: Background: Current guidelines recommend aortic valve replacement at peak aortic jet velocity (Vmax) ≥4.0 m/s, yet emerging evidence suggests irreversible myocardial fibrosis develops at lower velocities. We hypothesized that a critical "Fibrotic Tipping Point" exists where hazard acceleration becomes exponential, marking the transition from reversible hypertrophy to irreversible damage. Methods: We have systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to Feburary 2026 to identify relevant studies and performed restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling using pooled data from three international cohorts: Strange et al. 2022 NEDA registry (Australia n=217,599; US n=30,865; total N=248,464), Chen et al. 2022 (n=37,131), and AlcÓn et al. 2022 (n=118,684). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. We identified the velocity of maximum hazard acceleration (second derivative inflection point) and integrated histological fibrosis data from Puls et al. 2020 and clinical outcomes from CURRENT-AS registry (Taniguchi et al. 2017). Results: The RCS model revealed non-linear risk acceleration across the Vmax continuum. Strange et al. demonstrated ~1.55-fold mortality risk at Vmax 3.0-3.49 m/s and ~1.95-fold at ≥3.5 m/s versus reference (1.0-1.49 m/s). Chen et al. showed stepwise hazard ratios: 1.30 (2.5-2.99 m/s), 1.50 (3.0-3.49 m/s), 1.80 (3.4-3.99 m/s), and 2.50 (≥4.0 m/s). AlcÓn et al. reported a continuous per-1.0 m/s hazard ratio of 1.26 (95% CI 1.19-1.33). The RCS model identified the Fibrotic Tipping Point at Vmax=3.55 m/s (HR=1.72), representing maximum hazard acceleration. Beyond this threshold, risk curves plateaued at ~1.75-2.25-fold, consistent with established irreversible fibrosis. Puls et al. demonstrated that myocardial fibrosis conferred a 27.4-fold increased cardiovascular mortality risk post-intervention. CURRENT-AS registry confirmed severe AS hazard ratio of 3.33, validating guideline-threshold outcomes. Conclusions: The 4.0 m/s guideline threshold is dangerously late, occurring well beyond the Fibrotic Tipping Point where myocardial damage becomes irreversible. Our RCS analysis identifies 3.5 m/s as the critical intervention threshold to prevent irreversible fibrosis and preserve long-term ventricular function. Early intervention strategies should be reconsidered for asymptomatic patients reaching this velocity.
title: Abstract 5403: The Fibrotic Tipping Point: A Restricted Cubic Spline Analysis Mapping Continuous Aortic Jet Velocity and the Exponential Risk of Irreversible Myocardial Damage

abstract: INTRODUCTION / BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) carries lower mortality than obstructive AMI in general registries, supporting its characterisation as a lower-risk phenotype. Whether this holds in critically ill patients, where MINOCA presentations are enriched with haemodynamic compromise and demand ischaemia overlap, has not been characterised. We hypothesised ICU MINOCA would carry higher mortality than matched obstructive AMI and that mortality would not differ by sex. Research QUESTIONS / HYPOTHESIS: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) carries lower mortality than obstructive AMI in general registries, supporting its characterisation as a lower-risk phenotype. Whether this holds in critically ill patients, where MINOCA presentations are enriched with haemodynamic compromise and demand ischaemia overlap, has not been characterised. We hypothesised ICU MINOCA would carry higher mortality than matched obstructive AMI and that mortality would not differ by sex. MethodS / APPROACH: From MIMIC-IV v3.1, MINOCA was identified among 5,554 ICU AMI admissions by AMI ICD codes without obstructive CAD, refined by troponin T 0.030 ng/mL or greater (3x upper limit of normal; sole assay) and exclusion of sepsis-primary and AKI-primary admissions. Sensitivity analysis excluded Takotsubo and myocarditis. A 1:1 age- and sex-matched obstructive AMI cohort (pool n=24,989) served as controls. Sex-specific mortality was estimated by adjusted logistic regression. ResultS / DATA: After refinement, 737 MINOCA admissions were retained (30-day mortality 24.7%); Takotsubo and myocarditis exclusion did not alter this. In 729 matched pairs, MINOCA carried a 10.3 percentage-point mortality excess over obstructive AMI (25.0% vs 14.7%, p<0.001), despite PCI receipt in only 22.4% of controls. Women comprised 48.6% (median age 70 years versus 63 in men); cardiogenic shock was equivalent by sex (10.9% vs 10.8%), and adjusted mortality showed no sex difference (OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.26, p=0.64). Vasopressor use (OR 1.92), age (OR 1.68), and AKI (OR 1.43) were the strongest mortality predictors (AUC 0.773). Conclusion(S): Intensive care unit MINOCA carries substantially higher mortality than matched obstructive AMI, driven by vasopressor dependence, AKI, and cardiogenic shock. This excess is not explained by absent revascularisation in controls and is not modified by sex, consistent with general registry evidence of sex-equivalent MINOCA outcomes. The finding is opposite to registry data showing MINOCA as a lower-risk phenotype, reflecting critical care selection toward the severe end of the MINOCA spectrum.
title: Abstract 5406: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries in the Intensive Care Unit: Mortality, Sex Differences, and Comparison Against Obstructive Disease in a MIMIC-IV Cohort

abstract: INTRODUCTION / BACKGROUND: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy carries substantially lower mortality in general populations, yet neurological and physical triggers carry markedly higher complication rates than emotional triggers. Intensive care unit characterisation of trigger-stratified outcomes has not been reported at scale. Research QUESTIONS / HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesised that physical and neurological triggers would carry higher cardiogenic shock rates and 30-day mortality than psychological triggers, and that catecholamine exposure would differ by trigger type. MethodS / APPROACH: From MIMIC-IV v3.1, 340 ICU admissions with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (ICD-10 I51.81 or ICD-9 429.83) were identified, excluding confirmed obstructive coronary artery disease. Trigger phenotype was classified as psychological, physical, neurological, or unclassified using ICD codes; categories were non-mutually exclusive. Cardiogenic shock and catecholamine exposure were ascertained from diagnosis and prescription records. Logistic regression with sex-by-trigger interaction terms was performed as an exploratory analysis. ResultS / DATA: Women comprised 75.9%; overall 30-day mortality was 22.9%, substantially exceeding general registry rates; in-hospital cardiogenic shock occurred in 19.7%. Physical triggers (36.2%) carried 28.5% mortality and 27.6% shock; 85.4% received catecholamines. Neurological triggers (14.7%) carried 30.0% mortality; catecholamine exposure was 60.0% but catecholamine-exposed mortality was 36.7%, the highest of any trigger type. Psychological triggers (27.4%) had the lowest mortality (15.1%) and lowest catecholamine-exposed mortality (18.0%). Catecholamine exposure rates differed significantly by trigger type (46.0% to 85.4%; chi-squared(3) = 44.25, p<0.001). Unclassified triggers comprised 40.3% (mortality 18.2%); trigger codes were non-mutually exclusive. In the neurological subgroup (n=50; approximately 12 men), men had higher observed mortality than women (46.2% vs 24.3%); the reverse was observed for psychological triggers (16.0% vs 11.1%). These are hypothesis-generating only. Conclusion(S): In ICU Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, neurological and physical triggers carry approximately twice the 30-day mortality of psychological triggers. Physical triggers show the highest catecholamine need; neurological triggers show the highest catecholamine-exposed mortality, suggesting haemodynamic vulnerability beyond vasopressor burden. The sex-neurological trigger mortality difference is exploratory.
title: Abstract 5412: Trigger Phenotype, Sex, and Clinical Outcomes in Intensive Care Unit Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy: A MIMIC-IV Analysis

abstract: INTRODUCTION / BACKGROUND: ACC/AHA and ESC guidelines specify left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below 50% as the Class I aortic valve replacement (AVR) trigger in severe aortic stenosis. Women remodel concentrically, preserving LVEF while accruing haemodynamic burden, but the impact on guideline eligibility has not been quantified at echo-confirmed population scale. Research QUESTIONS / HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesised that women have paradoxically higher LVEF than men at equivalent aortic stenosis severity, rendering them less likely to meet the LVEF below 50% AVR trigger, and that preserved LVEF reflects concentric remodelling not better compensation. MethodS / APPROACH: From the EchoNext cohort (36,286 patients), 1,987 had echo-confirmed moderate-or-greater aortic stenosis (48.6% female); echo-normal patients established sex-specific reference LVEF. LVEF distributions, age at detection, pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), and LVEF below 50% eligibility were compared by sex. A sex by LVEF interaction tested whether LVEF modifies pulmonary hypertension risk differently by sex. ResultS / DATA: Women were detected 2.0 years later (80.7 vs 78.7 years, p<0.001) with higher LVEF (56.5% vs 50.0%, p<0.001). LVEF below 35% occurred in 12.1% of women vs 22.4% of men (p<0.001); hyperdynamic LVEF of 65% or greater in 29.0% vs 15.8% (p<0.001). Only 23.5% of women met the LVEF below 50% AVR trigger vs 38.4% of men (14.9pp gap, p<0.001). Among preserved-LVEF patients, women carried greater haemodynamic burden: PASP 45.1 vs 41.4 mmHg (p=0.0004); PASP 45 mmHg or greater in 28.3% vs 19.4% (p=0.0002). The sex by LVEF interaction (p=0.025) confirmed that LVEF preservation does not confer equivalent pulmonary hypertension protection in women. Conclusion(S): Women with aortic stenosis present later with paradoxically higher LVEF yet carry greater pulmonary hypertension burden, consistent with concentric remodelling rather than better compensation. Substantially fewer women meet the LVEF-based AVR trigger, and the sex by LVEF interaction confirms LVEF misleads severity assessment differently by sex. Current ejection fraction thresholds may not adequately capture disease severity in women.
title: Abstract 5413: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction as an Aortic Valve Replacement Trigger in Women with Aortic Stenosis: A Sex-Stratified Echocardiographic Cohort Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Social determinants of health (SDoH) are increasingly recognized as important contributors to disparities in cardiovascular outcomes. However, the long-term impact of documented SDoH on clinical outcomes among patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains incompletely understood. Research Questions: Among AMI patients undergoing PCI, do patients with documented SDoH have a higher risk of adverse outcomes compared with those without documented SDoH? Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network between January 2011 and January 2026. Adult patients with AMI who underwent PCI were identified using ICD-10 and procedural codes. Two cohorts were defined based on the presence or absence of documented SDoH-related ICD-10 codes (Z55-Z65) within one year before PCI. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline demographics, comorbidities, laboratory parameters, and cardiovascular medications between groups. Results: After propensity score matching, 6,552 patients were included in each cohort with no significant baseline differences. During follow-up, patients with documented SDoH had a significantly higher risk of heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.141, 95% CI 1.090-1.195; P < 0.001), recurrent myocardial infarction (HR 1.160, 95% CI 1.115-1.207; P < 0.001), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (HR 1.151, 95% CI 1.108-1.196; P < 0.001), and major bleeding (HR 1.238, 95% CI 1.148-1.336; P < 0.001) compared with patients without documented SDoH. There was no significant difference in all-cause mortality between groups (HR 0.971, 95% CI 0.891-1.059; P = 0.507). Conclusion: Among patients undergoing PCI for AMI, documented SDoH were associated with significantly increased risks of heart failure hospitalization, recurrent myocardial infarction, MACE, and major bleeding. However, no significant difference in all-cause mortality was observed. These findings highlight the potential impact of socioeconomic factors on long-term cardiovascular outcomes following PCI.
title: Abstract 5423: Impact of Social Determinants of Health to Clinical Outcome in AMI Underwent PCI Population: A Real-World Database Analysis

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established non-pharmacological alternative to oral anticoagulants (OACs) in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients at high thromboembolic risk. However, comparative effectiveness across clinical outcomes, particularly across study designs, remains incompletely characterized. Hypothesis: LAAO is non-inferior to OACs for ischemic stroke and systemic thromboembolism (STE) while conferring superior bleeding and mortality outcomes. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted per PRISMA guidelines. Studies comparing LAAO versus OACs in AF patients were included. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major bleeding. Secondary outcomes included cardiac mortality, ischemic stroke, and STE. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated via random-effects models. Heterogeneity was quantified using I 2 and tau 2 . Subgroup analyses by study design (randomized controlled trials [RCTs] versus observational) and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Meta-regression assessed the influence of age imbalance between arms. Publication bias was evaluated via contour-enhanced funnel plots. Results: Ten studies comprising 6,094 LAAO and 5,864 OAC patients were analyzed for all-cause mortality; twelve studies (15,684 vs. 15,454) for bleeding; seven for cardiac mortality (4,466 vs. 4,373); nine for ischemic stroke (14,784 vs. 14,560); and nine for STE (13,523 vs. 13,171). LAAO was associated with a non-significant reduction in all-cause mortality (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.52-1.03; I 2 =83.1%) and a significant reduction in major bleeding (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.51-0.97; I 2 =86.0%) and cardiac mortality (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-0.99; I 2 =73.2%). Ischemic stroke (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.70-1.14; I 2 =48.9%) and STE (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.53-1.60; I 2 =0%) were similar between groups. Subgroup analysis revealed observational studies influenced mortality and bleeding reductions, while RCTs showed neutral effects. Leave-one-out analyses confirmed robustness of all estimates. Meta-regression showed age imbalance did not significantly moderate any outcome (all p>0.05). Conclusions: LAAO significantly reduces major bleeding and cardiac mortality compared to OACs, with comparable ischemic stroke and STE rates. Substantial heterogeneity and design-dependent effect modification underscore the need for adequately powered RCTs to confirm mortality benefits.
title: Abstract 5430: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion versus Oral Anticoagulation for Anticoagulation Eligible Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular risk paradigms are largely sex-based, yet comparative major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) risk in transgender and gender diverse (TGD) populations remains imprecisely characterized. Methods: Adults with ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor (hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, obesity, tobacco smoking, or HIV) diagnosed between 2006-2018 were identified from the TriNetX database (n=12,843,847), including 27,730 (0.2%) classified as TGD using a composite phenotyping algorithm incorporating gender identity diagnostic codes, gender-affirming procedures, and sex-discordant hormone prescriptions. Cohorts were stratified by gender identity and separately 1:1 propensity-matched to cisgender men (transfeminine n=14,496; transmasculine n=13,234). Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses evaluated a primary composite outcome of non-fatal MACE (acute coronary syndrome, coronary revascularization, ischemic stroke) and all-cause mortality, with absolute risk differences (ARDs) calculated from cumulative event rates. Results: After propensity matching, cisgender women had lower cumulative event rates for the primary composite outcome than cisgender men (19.0% vs 23.4%; ARD –4.4%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.77, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.76-0.77; p<0.001). Transfeminine adults demonstrated the greatest excess cardiovascular event burden compared with cisgender men (20.5% vs 12.7%; ARD +7.8%; HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.19-1.34; p<0.001). Transmasculine adults demonstrated modestly higher cumulative event rates for the primary composite outcome (10.1% vs 9.1%; ARD +1.1%), despite experiencing lower all-cause mortality (3.9% vs 4.9%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.52-0.65; p<0.001). Outcome-specific risk patterns across non-fatal MACE and mortality did not consistently align with either sex assigned at birth or affirmed gender ( Figures 1 and 2 ). Sensitivity analyses censoring at death and using cisgender women as comparator demonstrated consistent directional findings. Conclusion: Risk patterns did not consistently align with either sex assigned at birth or affirmed gender. In this multicenter propensity-matched cohort of adults with cardiometabolic risk, cardiovascular outcomes were heterogeneous, outcome-specific, and not fully explained by traditional sex-based frameworks. These findings challenge the generalizability of traditional sex-based cardiovascular risk paradigms and underscore the need for gender identity-specific risk stratification and prevention strategies.
title: Abstract 5445: Cardiovascular Event Burden in Transgender and Gender Diverse Adults with Cardiometabolic Disease

abstract: Background: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), driven by somatic mutations in TET2, DNMT3A, and ASXL1, accelerates major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) through vascular inflammation. The conventional 2% variant allele frequency (VAF) diagnostic threshold represents a sequencing artifact rather than a biological boundary. Emerging evidence suggests cardiovascular risk acceleration begins at substantially lower VAF levels, yet the precise dose-response relationship remains unmapped. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to March 2026 to identify relevant studies and conducted a restricted cubic spline (RCS) meta-analysis of 10 primary cohorts (total n > 6,000), including UK Biobank analyses (n=425,573 for venous thromboembolism; n=362,058 for heart failure), ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) cohorts, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) cohorts, and the CANTOS trial CHIP subset. VAF was mapped continuously from 0.1% to 20% to identify non-linear inflection points in cardiovascular risk. Results: Pooled hazard ratio at VAF≥2% was 1.92 (95% CI: 1.62-2.28). Risk acceleration initiated at VAF 0.8%, with ΔHR ≈ +0.41 between 0.8%→2%, representing the steepest segment of the dose-response curve. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC)-derived optimal cutoffs identified gene-specific thresholds: TET2 at 0.73% (5-year mortality 32% vs. 19%), DNMT3A at 1.15% (5-year mortality 31% vs. 18%), and stable coronary artery disease at 1.07%. Mortality at VAF>0.5% was 17.8% versus 9.8% in non-carriers. Gene-specific hazard ratios included TET2/DNMT3A HR=2.10 (95% CI: 1.10-4.00) in chronic heart failure and CABG cardiovascular death HR=2.58 (95% CI: 1.47-4.55). In CANTOS, canakinumab reduced MACE in TET2-CHIP carriers by 62% (HR 0.38, 95% CI: 0.15-0.96). Conclusions: The 2% VAF threshold systematically misses the highest-acceleration zone of the CHIP dose-response curve. Redefining clinical CHIP detection to 0.8-1.0% VAF would capture patients in the steepest risk-acceleration phase and optimize identification of candidates for interleukin-1β blockade therapy.
title: Abstract 5474: A Primary Restricted Cubic Spline Meta-Analysis Mapping Continuous Variant Allele Frequency in CHIP Against Non-Linear MACE Acceleration

abstract: Introduction/Background: Popliteal artery aneurysms are associated with limb-threatening ischemia due to thrombosis or distal embolization. Current guidelines recommend elective repair at defined size thresholds but provide no evidence-based guidance for medical management to reduce thromboembolic risk. Evaluation of anticoagulation in large datasets is limited by incomplete medication capture. Research Question/Hypothesis: We evaluated whether anticoagulation indication burden is associated with major adverse limb events (MALE) in patients with popliteal artery aneurysm. Methods/Approach: A retrospective cohort of 105,248 patients with popliteal artery aneurysms was analyzed using a de-identified federated database. Anticoagulation indications (atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, mechanical valve) were used as a proxy for likelihood of anticoagulation and grouped by burden (0-3). Patients with prior popliteal bypass or stent were excluded. The primary outcome was MALE, defined as thrombolysis, thrombectomy, embolectomy, or major amputation. Mortality was evaluated to assess for potential healthy-user bias. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, peripheral artery disease, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, and hypertension. A Cochran-Armitage trend test assessed dose-response. Results/Data: Mean age was 70.1±13.7 years and 30.7% were female; MALE occurred in 1.91%. Indication burden was 57.6% (0), 31.9% (1), 9.5% (2), and 1.0% (3). MALE decreased with increasing burden: 2.07%, 1.73%, 1.64%, and 0.83% (Figure 1; p=0.000003).Any indication was associated with lower odds of MALE (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.74-0.89), remaining significant after adjustment (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80-0.97, p=0.011). Atrial fibrillation (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.61-0.77) and mechanical valve (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.41-0.69) were associated with lower MALE, whereas venous thromboembolism was associated with higher MALE (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.26-1.56). Indication-specific differences in MALE rates are shown in Figure 2, with lowest rates in mechanical valve-only (0.67%) and atrial fibrillation-only (1.14%) groups and highest in venous thromboembolism-only (3.22%). Mortality increased across indication burden (11.9% to 26.6%). Conclusion(s): Greater anticoagulation indication burden was associated with lower MALE despite higher mortality, a pattern that runs counter to a simple healthy-user effect. Associations differed by indication: atrial fibrillation and mechanical valve were associated with lower MALE, whereas venous thromboembolism was associated with higher MALE, possibly reflecting differences in anticoagulation duration and underlying thrombotic risk. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective evaluation of anticoagulation in this population.
title: Abstract 5479: Association of Anticoagulation Indication Burden with Major Adverse Limb Events in Popliteal Artery Aneurysm

abstract: Background: Employment status (ES) is a social determinant of health that is linked to cardiovascular risk and adverse outcomes. Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), a biomarker of chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, independent of C-reactive protein levels. We tested the hypothesis that adverse outcomes associated with lack of employment are mediated by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation. Aims: To examine whether suPAR and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels vary by ES, and to determine whether the impact of ES on long-term outcomes is mediated by elevated suPAR and hs-CRP levels. Methods: A total of 2,025 unretired patients (mean age of 56.6, 34% female, 22% Black) being investigated for coronary heart disease (CHD) and enrolled in the Emory Cardiovascular Biobank, were categorized into “employed” (full-time or part-time) and “non-employed” (unemployed/disabled) groups. Associations between ES and suPAR levels were examined using multivariable regression models after adjustment for age, sex, race, smoking history, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, BMI, history of MI, heart failure, eGFR, LVEF, and use of aspirin or statins. The relationship between ES and the composite outcome of cardiovascular death and non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI) was investigated using Fine and Gray’s subdistribution competing risk model. The potential mediating effects of suPAR and hs-CRP were assessed using mediation analysis. Results: Of the total, 1,360 (67%) were employed, and 665 (33%) were non-employed. Non-employed individuals had 17% higher suPAR and 32% higher hs-CRP levels after adjustment compared to employed individuals. Non-employed status was associated with a 68% [95% confidence interval (CI) 30 - 116] higher rate of cardiovascular death/MI compared to employed individuals after covariate adjustment. This was attenuated but remained significant after the addition of suPAR [sHR 1.43 (95% CI 1.10 - 1.87), p = 0.007] or hs-CRP [sHR 1.58 (95% CI 1.22 - 2.06), p = < 0.001]. SuPAR mediated ~31%, hsCRP mediated ~12%, and in combination, the two biomarkers jointly mediated 35% of the association between ES and cardiovascular death/MI. Conclusion: Circulating suPAR and hs-CRP levels are significantly higher among non-employed compared to employed individuals with CHD. Chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation mediate a third of the impact of unemployed status on adverse CHD events.
title: Abstract 5480: Systemic Inflammation and Immune Dysregulation Mediate the Effects of Employment Status on Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease

abstract: Background: Beta-blockers have negative inotropic properties, however, they promote myocardial recovery and are foundational therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Whether beta-blockers (BB) are safe to use in the severe, inotrope-dependent, HFrEF patients is unknown. Methods: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (66 healthcare organizations), we identified adults (aged >= 18 years) with systolic heart failure (ICD-10 I50.2x/I50.4x) and a first outpatient-dispensed inotrope (milrinone, dobutamine, or home inotrope infusion services) between January 2010 and January 2025. Patients were grouped by whether an outpatient BB (metoprolol, bisoprolol, or carvedilol) was dispensed within 7 days on or after the first inotrope. Cohorts were matched 1:1 on 58 baseline covariates (demographics, comorbidities, guideline-directed medical therapy, and serum biochemistry for hepatic and renal function). To prevent immortal time bias, follow-up for both groups began the day after group-defining criteria were met — the day after BB dispense in the treated group and the day after the 7-day ascertainment window closed in the comparator group. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality through day 365; secondary outcomes were hospitalization, durable ventricular assist device (VAD), or transplantation. Results: A total of 11,968 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom, 3,175 were matched to each group (mean age 63.5 years; 68% male; all standardized differences below 0.1). Beta-blocker therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality (17.2% versus 19.7%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.94; log-rank p=0.01; 1-year survival 82.3% versus 79.8%). Hazards were non-proportional (p<0.001): the survival difference emerged within 30 days (HR 0.59, p<0.001) and was no longer significant in a 30-365-day landmark analysis (HR 1.10, p=0.25). The direction was consistent across milrinone (HR 0.80), dobutamine (HR 0.84), male (HR 0.80), and female (HR 0.83) subgroups. Hospitalization did not differ (HR 1.00, p=0.66); mechanical circulatory support or transplantation was more frequent (8.4% versus 5.3%; HR 1.54, p<0.001). Conclusions: In a large propensity-matched cohort of inotrope-dependent HFrEF, the association between outpatient BB therapy and lower all-cause mortality was confined to the first 30 days and attenuated to null thereafter, while VAD or transplantation was more frequent. These results support individualized management of this high-risk population and warrant prospective validation to delineate true early protective effects of BB’s vs confounding by acuity.

register_verdicts.note: Beta-blocker use in outpatient inotrope-dependent heart failure does not address first-line inotrope or vasopressor choice in shock.

title: Abstract 5483: Throttling the Sympathetic Drive: Beta-Blockade in Inotrope-Dependent Heart Failure

abstract: Introduction: Optimal antithrombotic management following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with pre-existing indications for chronic oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains poorly defined. Current evidence, including the POPular TAVI trial, suggests OAC monotherapy may be sufficient, yet combination therapy with antiplatelet remains common in clinical practice. We evaluated clinical outcomes of OAC monotherapy versus OAC combined with antiplatelet therapy in this high-risk population using a large real-world dataset. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (2020-2024) including adults on chronic OAC who underwent TAVR. Patients with prior valve replacement, rheumatic aortic stenosis, allergy to aspirin/clopidogrel, or coronary intervention within 3 months prior to TAVR were excluded. Patients were stratified into three cohorts based on antiplatelet use in the 3 months post-TAVR: OAC monotherapy, OAC + aspirin, and OAC + clopidogrel. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics. Outcomes were assessed from TAVR through 1 year of follow-up. Hazard ratios (HR) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression. Statistical significance was defined as two-sided p<0.05. Results: A total of 12,900 patients on chronic OAC underwent TAVR, of whom 4,088 received OAC monotherapy, 7,137 received OAC + aspirin, and 1,675 received OAC + clopidogrel. Post-propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were well-balanced with mean ages of 81.4±8.1, 81.2±8.9, and 82.1±7.6 years, respectively, over a mean follow-up of 322±101 days. Compared with OAC monotherapy, OAC + aspirin was associated with significantly higher rates of major bleeding (intracranial hemorrhage and bleeding requiring transfusion) (HR 1.36; 95% CI 1.14-1.63; p<0.001), gastrointestinal bleeding (HR 1.49; 95% CI 1.20-1.86; p<0.001), non-GI bleeding (HR 1.37; 95% CI 1.16-1.63; p<0.001), major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 1.24; 95% CI 1.15-1.34; p<0.001), acute heart failure exacerbation (HR 1.21; 95% CI 1.11-1.32; p<0.001). OAC + clopidogrel was similarly associated with higher major bleeding (HR 1.34; 95% CI 1.02-1.77; p=0.04), GI bleeding (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.13-2.39; p=0.009), and acute HF exacerbation (HR 1.17; 95% CI 1.02-1.34; p=0.03). No significant difference was observed across groups for all-cause mortality (OAC + aspirin: HR 1.08; p=0.29; OAC + clopidogrel: HR 0.93; p=0.50), valvular reintervention (HR 0.72; p=0.25), or valvular thrombosis (HR 0.98; p=0.94). Conclusions: In patients on chronic OAC undergoing TAVR, addition of antiplatelet therapy was associated with significantly higher rates of bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, and acute HF exacerbation, without reduction in all-cause mortality, valvular thrombosis and reintervention.
title: Abstract 5502: Oral Anticoagulation Monotherapy versus Combination Antithrombotic Therapy with Antiplatelet Following TAVR in Patients on Chronic Oral Anticoagulation

abstract: The use of implantable cardiovascular and extracorporeal circulation technologies has exponentially surged to improve patient lives. However, these blood-contacting medical devices made of polymers and metal alloys are plagued by thrombosis and bacterial infections, complications that lead to device failure and result in extended hospitalization, increased medical costs, and even patient morbidity. Commercially available surface coatings on medical devices inhibit either protein or platelet adhesion (leading to thrombosis) or treat only bacterial infections. Despite decades of research, no single antithrombotic and antibacterial surface design has yet been commercialized. This work introduces an unprecedented antibiofouling surface design integrating bioactive and passive pathways to combat thrombosis and bacterial infections in blood-contacting cardiovascular technologies (Image 1). Functionalized polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as the low surface energy polymer, multi-functional epoxy cross-linker and a nitric-oxide generating (NOgen) catalyst is covalently cross-linked to develop NOgen solid slippery surface coatings (NOgen-SSC) on medical-grade polymers such as silicone rubber (SR). The presence of hydrophobic, flexible PDMS solid chains covalently bound to the device surface constitutes the passive pathway that limits bio foulant and liquid adhesion on the surface. NOgen-SSC-SR exhibits a water sliding angle (WSA) of <25° (WSA for uncoated SR >90°). NOgen-SSC-SR maintained WSA <25° under dynamic aqueous conditions up to 7 days, indicating coating stability. The inability of the surface passivation strategy to mitigate platelet activation and planktonic bacterial growth necessitated co-integration with the bioactive NO generating catalyst in the same coating. NOgen-SSC-SR generates NO flux ~15 x 10 -10 mol min -1 cm -2 compared to uncoated SR (~3 x 10 -10 mol min -1 cm -2 ), in the presence of the bio-mimicked NO donor ( S -nitrosoglutathione, GSNO) and the thiol reducing molecule (glutathione, GSH). Preliminary antibacterial testing for 4 h with regular GSNO/GSH supplementation, revealed that NOgen-SSC-SR inhibited >80% surface adhered S. aureus bacterial growth compared to uncoated SR. NOgen-SSC-SR will be further tested against clinical bacterial strains under high-shear conditions, subjected to hemocompatibility analysis, and investigated in an extracorporeal thrombogenicity rabbit model for thrombosis prevention, without systemic anticoagulation.
title: Abstract 5529: Nitric Oxide Generating Solid Slippery Surface Coatings to Combat Biofouling of Cardiovascular Devices

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) is a well-established marker of subclinical atherosclerosis. Individuals with CAC ≥300 have CVD event rates comparable to stable secondary prevention populations. CAC ≥1000 defines an especially high-risk subgroup. However, the very long-term prognosis and PREVENT-ASCVD risk profiles of asymptomatic individuals with CAC ≥1000 versus CAC 300-999 remain incompletely characterized. Across 30 years, we characterize the imaging features, PREVENT-ASCVD risk, and long-term all-cause and cause-specific mortality associated with CAC ≥1000 vs CAC 300-999. Methods: We analyzed 8,472 asymptomatic adults aged 30-79 years with CAC ≥300 from the CAC Consortium. There were 5,860 individuals with CAC 300-999 and 2,612 with CAC ≥1000. Median follow-up time was 20.4 years (IQR 14.7-23.0, max 31.9). Outcomes included all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models evaluated associations between CAC burden and mortality after adjustment for CVD risk factors. A Kaplan-Meier and Gompertz modeling approach estimated survival over 20-30 years. Results: Compared to CAC 300-999 (mean 555.1 ± 194.2 AU), CAC ≥1000 (mean 1,925.6 ± 1,122.2 AU) was associated with greater systemic atherosclerosis, including left main disease (45.5% vs 31.8%; p<0.001), 4-vessel involvement (52.3% vs 30.2%; p<0.001), thoracic aortic calcification (74.1% vs 61.6%; p<0.001), and aortic valve calcification (42.3% vs 34.3%; p=0.004). At baseline, 47% of CAC ≥ 1000 and 40.2% of CAC 300-999 received lipid-lowering therapy. After adjusting for CVD risk factors, CAC ≥1000 was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.26-1.49), CVD mortality (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.32-1.74), and CHD mortality (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.48-2.12), compared with CAC 300-999 (ref. group). Estimated 30-year survival was lower in individuals with CAC ≥1000 than CAC 300-999 in both age-adjusted (22.7% [95% CI 19.9-25.6] vs. 28.3% [26.1-30.4]) and unadjusted analyses (20.2% [95% CI, 17.7-22.4] vs. 31.9% [29.8-33.9]; Figure 1 ). At 30 years, cumulative incidence of CVD mortality was 33.7% (95% CI 31.4-36.3) in those with CAC ≥1000 vs 23.2% (95% CI 21.6-25.0) in those with CAC 300-999. Differences were significant at all 5-year intervals throughout the follow-up period ( Figure 2 ). Despite elevated mortality risk, over 1 in 3 adults with CAC ≥1000 were classified as low or borderline risk by 10-year PREVENT-ASCVD at baseline ( Figure 3 ). Conclusion: CAC ≥1000 identifies a unique systemic atherosclerosis phenotype associated with profound long-term cardiovascular mortality risk that is incompletely captured by contemporary ASCVD risk assessment tools, supporting the need for the most aggressive preventive risk factor modification and pharmacotherapy in this extreme-risk population.
title: Abstract 5559: 30-Year Mortality Risk, Imaging Characteristics, and PREVENT-ASCVD Risk in Asymptomatic Adults with Coronary Artery Calcium ≥1000: Insights from the CAC Consortium

abstract: Background: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) reduces tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improves quality of life, yet pooled randomized data have not demonstrated a mortality benefit. Functional TR is now recognized in two phenotypes: an atrial phenotype (AFTR), driven by atrial enlargement and annular dilation with preserved right ventricular function, and a ventricular phenotype (VFTR), driven by right ventricular dilation and leaflet tethering. Whether outcomes after T-TEER differ by phenotype has not been quantified in a pooled analysis. Methods: We performed a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through April 2026. Studies were eligible if patients received T-TEER, the AFTR and VFTR phenotypes were prespecified, and a multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) for death and/or HFH was reported. The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or HFH; the secondary outcome was acute procedural success, defined as residual TR grade 2+ or less at discharge. Hazard ratios and risk ratios were pooled on the log scale using inverse-variance random-effects (REML). Robustness was assessed by leave-one-out analysis. Heterogeneity was assessed by Cochran Q, I-squared, and tau-squared; risk of bias by ROBINS-I; certainty of evidence by GRADE. Results: Three cohorts (EuroTR, TriValve, TRIC-Ulm) enrolling 1,075 patients (288 AFTR, 787 VFTR) met inclusion. Each cohort defined AFTR differently (RA/RV ratio + TAPSE; LVEF + AF + sPAP; LVEF + RV FAC + sPAP). The pooled adjusted HR for death or HFH (AFTR vs VFTR) was 0.44 by inverse-variance random-effects REML (95% CI 0.22-0.87, p=0.019); Heterogeneity was moderate (tau-squared=0.19; Q=3.82, p=0.148; I-squared=49%), and effect direction was concordant across all three studies. Leave-one-out HRs ranged from 0.27 (0.12-0.62) to 0.59 (0.37-0.93). Acute procedural success did not differ (pooled RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10, I-squared=26%), indicating the survival benefit is not explained by differential technical success. Risk of bias was moderate (ROBINS-I); GRADE certainty was moderate, downgraded for imprecision. Conclusions: In patients undergoing T-TEER, the atrial phenotype is associated with approximately half the risk of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with the ventricular phenotype, despite similar acute procedural success. The estimate is consistent across cohorts but limited by observational design, heterogeneous phenotype definitions, and small study size. Phenotype classification should be prespecified and reported in ongoing randomized trials of T-TEER to refine patient selection.
title: Abstract 5571: Atrial versus Ventricular Functional Tricuspid Regurgitation Phenotype and Outcomes After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction/Background: Resistant and uncontrolled hypertension remain major drivers of cardiovascular morbidity despite multidrug pharmacotherapy, lifestyle intervention, and recognition of nonadherence and therapeutic inertia. Catheter-based renal denervation (RDN) has re-emerged after sham-controlled trials, but its blood pressure effect and safety profile require precise quantification. Research Questions/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that RDN reduces ambulatory and office blood pressure compared with sham control without increasing renal or procedural safety events. Methods/Approach: Randomized, sham-controlled adult trials of catheter-based RDN for hypertension were synthesized. Eligible trials evaluated first- or second-generation radiofrequency, ultrasound, or alcohol-mediated RDN in patients treated with or without antihypertensive medications. Outcomes included 24-hour and office systolic blood pressure (SBP), 24-hour and office diastolic blood pressure (DBP), medication-status interaction, vascular complications, renal artery stenosis >70%, hypertensive crisis, all-cause death, and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Summary data were pooled using study-level, pairwise, random-effects meta-analysis. Results/Data: A total of 10 trials comprising 2,478 participants were included. Compared with sham control, RDN reduced 24-hour SBP (mean difference [MD], -4.4 mm Hg; 95% CI, -6.1 to -2.7; P<0.00001) and office SBP (MD, -6.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, -9.7 to -3.6; P<0.0001). RDN also reduced 24-hour DBP (MD, -2.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, -3.6 to -1.5; P<0.00001) and office DBP (MD, -3.5 mm Hg; 95% CI, -5.4 to -1.6; P=0.0003). SBP effects did not differ significantly between trials performed with versus without concomitant antihypertensive medications for 24-hour SBP (P for interaction=0.62) or office SBP (P for interaction=0.73). RDN did not significantly increase vascular complications (OR, 1.69; 95% CI, 0.57 to 5.00; P=0.34), renal artery stenosis >70% (OR, 1.50; 95% CI, 0.06 to 36.97; P=0.80), hypertensive crisis (OR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.30 to 1.38; P=0.26), or all-cause death (OR, 1.76; 95% CI, 0.34 to 9.20; P=0.50). Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate was comparable between groups (P for interaction=0.84). Conclusion(s): In sham-controlled randomized evidence, RDN produces statistically significant but modest reductions in ambulatory and office blood pressure without a significant short-term safety penalty. RDN should be considered an adjunctive option for carefully selected patients after confirmation of true uncontrolled hypertension, medication optimization, adherence assessment, lifestyle intervention, and exclusion of secondary causes.
title: Abstract 5592: Renal Denervation for Resistant or Uncontrolled Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis of Sham-Controlled Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Current clinical guidelines dichotomize coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) using a binary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) cutoff of ≥25 units to define abnormal microvascular resistance. However, this threshold may obscure continuous, non-linear relationships between microvascular resistance and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), potentially misclassifying intermediate-risk patients. We performed a restricted cubic spline (RCS) meta-analysis to characterize the continuous dose-response relationship between angio-IMR and MACE risk across diverse cardiovascular populations. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to March 2026 to identify relevant studies and identified 13 studies (2021-2026) reporting angio-IMR and MACE outcomes in 2,712 patients (561 MACE events, follow-up 12-60 months). Populations included ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI, 4 studies) ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA, 2 studies), myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), anterior STEMI, diabetic chronic coronary syndrome, calcified coronary artery disease, and post-percutaneous coronary intervention cohorts. We pooled binary hazard ratios (HRs) for IMR ≥25 using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting and fitted five-knot RCS models (knots: 10, 16, 22, 32, 42 units) to continuous IMR values. Non-linearity was assessed via likelihood ratio testing. Publication bias was evaluated using Egger's regression test. Results: Pooled binary HR for IMR ≥25 was 4.30 (95% CI 3.47-5.33, I 2 =0%). RCS analysis revealed trending non-linearity (p=0.095) with a "microvascular cliff" identified at IMR ≈16 units—the inflection point of maximum curvature where HR acceleration begins exponentially (HR=1.45 at this threshold). At the guideline cutoff of IMR=25, HR reached 3.53, indicating substantial risk accumulation occurs before the conventional threshold. Critically, patients with IMR 16-24 units, currently classified as "normal," already demonstrate significantly elevated MACE risk compared to those with IMR <16. No significant publication bias was detected (Egger's intercept=2.42, p=0.104). Conclusions: The binary IMR ≥25 cutoff is biologically arbitrary and systematically misclassifies intermediate-risk patients with subclinical microvascular dysfunction. The microvascular cliff at IMR ≈16 supports adoption of continuous risk stratification paradigms for CMD rather than dichotomous classification. These findings challenge current diagnostic criteria and suggest that earlier intervention thresholds (IMR ≥16) may substantially improve risk prediction and guide therapeutic decision making in patients with microvascular disease across diverse clinical presentations.
title: Abstract 5597: The Microvascular Cliff: A Restricted Cubic Spline Meta-Analysis of Continuous Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance (angio-IMR) and Non-Linear MACE Risk

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) dynamically alters hemodynamic status in patients with severe aortic stenosis. However, perioperative changes in blood pressure and pulse pressure, as well as their prognostic significance, remain unclear.
