title: Abstract 7425: Impact of Sepsis on Electrical Cardioversion Success and Mortality in Cardiogenic Shock with Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac and mediastinal malignancies are rare but can cause life-threatening cardiovascular syndromes including tamponade, SVC obstruction, pulmonary embolism, and obstructive right heart failure. Because symptoms are nonspecific, diagnosis is often delayed, especially in young adults. We present two young adults with distinct mediastinal malignancies and extensive cardiac involvement, highlighting multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management. Case 1: A 20-year-old man with 2 years of chest pain presented with weight loss, fatigue, fever, and borderline hypotension. CT showed a large invasive anterior mediastinal mass encasing the trachea, great vessels, and SVC with right atrial extension, pericardial effusion and bilateral pulmonary emboli (Fig 1). Echo showed EF 45% with constrictive physiology; cardiac MRI confirmed pericardial invasion, RV dysfunction, and absent late gadolinium enhancement. Biopsy revealed inoperable WHO B2 thymoma. He received chemoradiation with doxorubicin plus dexrazoxane. A new right atrial mass on follow-up echo could not be characterized as thrombus versus tumor; cardiac MRI identified avascular thrombus, guiding continued anticoagulation rather than escalation of cancer therapy (Fig 2). Serial biomarkers and imaging confirmed preserved myocardium and LV recovery throughout cardiotoxic treatment. Case 2: A healthy 26-year-old woman presented with 2 months of progressive dyspnea, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and proBNP 5376 pg/mL. Echo showed an RV apical mass and pericardial effusion with tamponade. CT demonstrated widespread metastases; CTA characterized a 9.9x4x6.8 cm mass obliterating the RV/RVOT and compressing the LV (Fig 3). A second biopsy revealed intimal sarcoma after initial nondiagnostic sampling. Deemed a poor surgical candidate, she started liposomal doxorubicin with dexrazoxane. After one cycle, rising proBNP (13,044 pg/mL) with stable troponin indicated deterioration from tumor burden rather than anthracycline toxicity. She developed mixed obstructive-cardiogenic shock and died 3 months after presentation. Discussion: These cases underscore early consideration of cardiac or mediastinal malignancy in young adults with persistent cardiopulmonary symptoms, particularly with pericardial effusion, venous thrombosis, or right-sided intracardiac masses. Multimodality imaging was essential: CT/CTA defined anatomic and metastatic burden, echo captured hemodynamics, and cardiac MRI provided tissue characterization that directly altered management. Cardio-oncology collaboration enabled safe cardiotoxic therapy through thoughtful anthracycline selection and surveillance, yet remained bounded by tumor biology, permitting myocardial recovery in Case 1 while Case 2 was limited by aggressive disease.
title: Abstract 7428: A Tale of Two Tumors: Role of Multimodality Imaging and Cardio-Oncology Decision-Making in 2 Young Adults with Invasive Thymoma and Primary Cardiac Sarcoma

abstract: Background: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is an increasingly recognized indication for orthotopic heart transplantation, but comparative outcomes and the role of pretransplant mechanical circulatory support (MCS) remain incompletely defined. Research Question/Hypothesis: Among adult first heart transplant recipients, CA is associated with worse post-transplant survival than dilated nonischemic cardiomyopathy (DCM), while outcomes among MCS-bridged recipients may be comparable. Methods/Approach: We analyzed 23,181 adults in the UNOS registry who underwent first orthotopic heart transplantation from January 1, 2010, through September 25, 2025, including 717 with CA, 21,534 with DCM, and 930 with restrictive nonamyloid cardiomyopathy (RNA-CM). The primary outcome was all-cause post-transplant mortality. Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, and Cox proportional hazards models were used. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, body mass index, creatinine, pretransplant MCS, and transplant era, with missing covariates handled by multiple imputation. A prespecified subgroup analysis evaluated recipients bridged with pretransplant MCS. Results/Data: CA recipients were older and less likely to receive pretransplant MCS than DCM recipients. All-cause mortality occurred in 23.7% of CA, 21.8% of DCM, and 19.8% of RNA-CM recipients. Kaplan-Meier survival differed across phenotypes (log-rank p=0.0035), with 10-year survival of 50.7% in CA, 66.8% in DCM, and 70.5% in RNA-CM. After multivariable adjustment, CA remained associated with higher mortality versus DCM (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.03-1.41; p=0.019), whereas RNA-CM did not differ from DCM (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90-1.21; p=0.551). In overlap-weighted analyses, CA remained associated with higher mortality versus DCM (HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.07-1.56; p=0.008). Among MCS-bridged recipients, survival did not differ significantly by phenotype (log-rank p=0.146), and CA was not associated with significantly higher adjusted mortality versus DCM (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.93-1.62; p=0.145). Conclusion(s): CA was associated with worse overall post-transplant survival compared with DCM. However, among recipients bridged with pretransplant MCS, CA was not associated with significantly higher mortality, suggesting that carefully selected CA patients requiring MCS may still achieve acceptable post-transplant outcomes.
title: Abstract 7449: Cardiac Amyloidosis, Pretransplant Mechanical Circulatory Support, and Survival After Heart Transplantation

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is common in cardiogenic shock (CS), but data on synchronized direct current cardioversion (sDCCV) in CS are limited. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with CS undergoing sDCCV for AF in 2023. Paired invasive hemodynamic analyses used measurements obtained before and after index sDCCV. Predictors were modeled with Bayesian logistic regression and summarized as risk differences (RDs, percentage points [pp]) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Results: Among 68 patients, sDCCV restored sinus rhythm in 54 (79.4%) and during follow-up (median 4.6 months), 36 deaths occurred (52.9%). After successful sDCCV, cardiac index (CI) (7.6%; 95% CrI 0.5% to 15.2%; Pr[Δ > 0] = 0.982) and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi) increased (19.3%; 95% CrI 0.5% to 40.4%; Pr[Δ > 0] = 0.978), but vasoactive-inotropic score did not change. In contrast, among patients with unsuccessful DCCV, CI (–10.0%; 95% CrI –14.7% to –3.7%; Pr[Δ < 0] = 0.996) and PAPi tended to decrease (–13.6%; 95% CrI –36.0% to 16.6%; Pr[Δ < 0] = 0.855), while right atrial pressure (16.4%; 95% CrI –6.3% to 45.2%; Pr[Δ > 0] = 0.923) and mean pulmonary artery pressures tended to increase (8.1%; 95% CrI –4.1% to 22.5%; Pr[Δ > 0] = 0.907). Estimated success probability of sDCCV was higher with nonischemic cardiomyopathy-related CS (RD +16.1 pp; 95% CrI –0.6 to 34.4), higher baseline CI (RD +13.9 pp per +1 L/min/m 2 ; 95% CrI –2.8 to 28.3), and lower with higher tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (RD –10.8 pp per +5 mm; 95% CrI –24.9 to 0.4) and higher baseline PAPi (RD –8.2 pp per +1 unit; 95% CrI –20.5 to 2.4). No post-procedural bradycardia or stroke occurred. Conclusions: In CS with AF, sDCCV often restored sinus rhythm with modest hemodynamic improvement, while unsuccessful sDCCV was associated with deterioration.
title: Abstract 7455: Synchronized Direct Current Cardioversion for Atrial Fibrillation in Cardiogenic Shock: Procedural Success, Hemodynamic Response, and Outcomes

abstract: Introduction: Caseous calcification of the mitral annulus (CCMA) is a rare cause of cardioembolic stroke that may mimic infective endocarditis (IE) and nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE). Recognition is important because embolizing CCMA may require surgical rather than antimicrobial or antithrombotic therapy. Patient Information: A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and psoriatic arthropathy presented with acute gait instability and left-sided weakness. She had no known hypercoagulable disorder. Clinical Findings & Timeline: One week prior to presentation, she developed chills, malaise, and sore throat without fever. Symptoms progressed to gait instability, prompting presentation. Examination demonstrated mild left-hand weakness without pronator drift (NIHSS 1) and a 2/6 systolic murmur in the mitral area without peripheral stigmata of IE. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated C-reactive protein (96.8 mg/L), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (88 mm/h), β2-glycoprotein IgM (53.0), anticardiolipin IgM (25.3), and positive lupus anticoagulant testing. Neuroimaging, including non-contrast head CT, CT angiography, and brain MRI, demonstrated calcified cerebral emboli and >20 acute infarcts involving both cerebral hemispheres and the cerebellum across multiple vascular territories. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography identified extensive posterior mitral annular calcification with an associated mobile 16 х 9 mm echodense mass. Cardiac CT further characterized the lesion as bulky CCMA and demonstrated severe mid-left anterior descending artery stenosis. Infectious and malignancy evaluations were negative. Therapeutic Interventions: Anticoagulation with heparin and empiric antimicrobial therapy were initiated. Given the mobile lesion and extensive embolic burden, she underwent mitral valve replacement with annular debridement, autologous pericardial patch reconstruction, and coronary artery bypass grafting for concomitant coronary artery disease. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: Surgical pathology confirmed sterile CCMA without infection or thrombus, establishing the diagnosis and allowing discontinuation of antimicrobial therapy. Warfarin was continued for suspected antiphospholipid syndrome, bioprosthetic valve replacement, and postoperative atrial fibrillation, with repeat antiphospholipid antibody testing planned. Discussion & Synthesis: This case highlights how embolizing CCMA can mimic both IE and NBTE. Calcified cerebral emboli provided a critical clue to a structural calcific source, while transient antiphospholipid antibody positivity complicated the evaluation. Multimodality imaging was essential for diagnosis and guided definitive surgical management.
title: Abstract 7469: Shower of Emboli: Caseous Calcification of the Mitral Annulus Mimicking Endocarditis in a Patient with Suspected Antiphospholipid Syndrome

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic Shock (CS) is traditionally characterized by elevated filling pressures and managed with diuresis. However, in acute myocardial infarction (AMI)-CS, elevated filling pressures may be the result of sudden impairment of ventricular relaxation and emptying, rather than excess intravascular volume. Additionally, some patients may be intravascularly depleted, especially after unloading with a microaxial flow pump (mAFP). Hypothesis: We hypothesize that there is a subset of patients with AMI-CS requiring mAFP in whom volume resuscitation is safe and potentially beneficial. Methods: All adult patients with AMI-CS supported with a mAFP were analyzed. Hemodynamic data was recorded pre-mAFP implant and every 6 hours after. Interaction testing was performed to examine the effect of IVF administration on patients with low central venous pressure (CVP). Similarly, the effect of IVF on patients with a low cardiac output was explored. The primary outcome in these analyses was death or escalation of temporary mechanical support (tMCS). Results: Out of 80 patients analyzed, 41 (51%) received fluids, 35 (44%) received diuretics, and 14 (18%) received both during the first 12 hours post-mAFP implant. Most volume administered (77%) was isotonic or balanced crystalloid, whereas only 15% was blood products. Median left ventricular end diastolic pressure was 32mmHg, CVP was 17mmHg, and CO was 3.9L/min. IVF administration during the first 12 hours did not lead to a higher CVP (7mmHg vs 8mmHg, p = 0.79) or pulmonary arterial diastolic pressure (16 mmHg vs 17mmHg, p =0.06). There was no increased risk of mechanical ventilation (p =0.81), renal replacement therapy (p=0.98), or in- hospital mortality (p=0.81) in patients receiving fluids. Among patients with a low CVP at baseline, IVF administration was protective against in- hospital death and tMCS escalation, and the effect was attenuated with increasing CVP (p interaction = 0.04). Similarly, among patients with a low baseline CO, IVF was protective using the same outcomes with a diminishing effect at higher CO (p interaction = 0.03). Conclusion: In patients with AMI-CS patients supported with a mAFP, IVF administration did not lead to markedly increased filling pressures and was not associated with any measured adverse clinical events. In patients with lower baseline CO and CVP, IVF administration appeared to be protective against escalation of tMCS or death. *Drs. Le and Li contributed equally to this abstract
title: Abstract 7472: Fluid Resuscitation in Acute Myocardial Infarction Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Paravalvular leak (PVL) is an underrecognized complication following mitral valve replacement (MVR), occurring in up to 7-17% of patients. PVL can lead to clinically significant hemolysis and heart failure. Case: A 71-year-old male with a history of mitral valve repair (1996) followed by redo sternotomy and mechanical MVR with a 25 mm On-X valve (2019), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and chronic kidney disease, presented with progressive fatigue and dyspnea. Two years after MVR, he was evaluated for Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia and treated empirically with prednisone, rituximab, and iron supplementation, with only marginal improvement over six years. His clinical course was further complicated by refractory atrial fibrillation requiring multiple cardioversions, antiarrhythmic therapy, and ultimately AV nodal ablation with biventricular pacemaker implantation. By the time of valve clinic evaluation, he had developed severe functional limitation (NYHA class III), with progressive dyspnea limiting basic activities. Physical examination revealed a 4/6 systolic murmur at the apex and lower extremity edema. Laboratory findings were consistent with hemolysis, including elevated lactate dehydrogenase, low haptoglobin, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia. Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated severe mitral PVL with an anteromedial jet, defect area of 1.14 cm 2 , and dimensions of 1.74 х 0.74 cm. Given the high risk associated with a third sternotomy, the multidisciplinary heart team elected a transcatheter approach. Under general anesthesia with transseptal access and TEE guidance, two Amplatzer Vascular Plug II devices (12 mm and 8 mm) were successfully deployed across the defect. Post-procedural imaging demonstrated reduction of regurgitation from torrential to trivial. The patient was discharged the following day. At three-month follow-up, he demonstrated marked symptomatic improvement, resolution of hemolysis, and return to full functional activity, including recreational sports. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for PVL in patients with prosthetic valves presenting with unexplained hemolytic anemia and heart failure symptoms. Early recognition and timely transcatheter intervention can result in significant clinical improvement and avoidance of high-risk reoperation.
title: Abstract 7475: When the Heart Breaks Blood: Paravalvular Leak Presenting as Refractory Hemolytic Anemia

abstract: Background: Abbreviated dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) has been proposed to reduce bleeding in high bleeding risk (HBR) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but the optimal duration remains uncertain. Existing studies often compare heterogeneous DAPT durations, with limited focused evidence comparing 1-month (abbreviated) versus 3-6 months(standard) regimens in HBR cohorts. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of abbreviated versus standard DAPT in HBR-PCI patients, focusing on ischemic and bleeding outcomes. Methods: We systematically searched four databases (Pubmed, Google Scholar, Central Cochrane and Sciencedirect) from inception till May 2026 for studies comparing 1-month versus 3-6 month DAPT after PCI in HBR patients. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 for randomized trials and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Outcomes were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 . Primary outcomes included net adverse clinical events (NACE), major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and BARC 2-5 bleeding. Secondary outcomes included all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, stent thrombosis, any revascularization, and target lesion revascularization. Results: Four studies (3 RCTs, 1 propensity-matched study) comprising 11,213 HBR patients were included; 5,330 received abbreviated DAPT and 5,883 standard DAPT, with a mean follow-up of 357.5 days. Abbreviated DAPT significantly reduced BARC 2-5 bleeding (RR= 0.74, 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.83, p < 0.001), with comparable risk reduction of ischemic stroke (RR= 0.88, 95% CI, 0.29 to 2.73, p= 0.83), hemorrhagic stroke (RR= 0.57, 95% CI, 0.13 to 2.58, p= 0.47), overall stroke (RR= 0.76, 95% CI, 0.34 to 1.70, p= 0.50), MI (RR= 0.98, 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.24, p= 0.89), NACE (relative risk [RR]=1.01, 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.31, p=0.95), MACCE (RR=1.13, 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.61, p=0.50), all cause death (RR= 1.06, 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.27, p= 0.52), any revascularization (RR= 1.40, 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.09, p= 0.10), stent thrombosis (RR= 1.09, 95% CI, 0.59 to 2.02, p= 0.78), target lesion vascularization (RR= 1.54, 95% CI, 0.55 to 4.27, p= 0.41) and cardiovascular death (RR= 1.00, 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.35, p= 0.98). Conclusions: In HBR patients undergoing PCI, abbreviated (1-month) DAPT significantly reduces major bleeding without increasing ischemic events compared to standard (3-6 month) therapy. Comparable NACE and MACCE suggest a favorable net clinical benefit. These findings support abbreviated DAPT as a safer alternative in HBR populations, though larger adequately powered non-inferiority trials with standardized HBR definitions are needed for definitive guidance.
title: Abstract 7503: Efficacy of Abbreviated versus Standard Duration of Dual Anti-Platelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in High Bleeding Risk Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Hypo-attenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) has increasingly been recognized not only after transcatheter aortic valve replacement but also after conventional surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). Previous studies have suggested that deformation of the Perceval sutureless valve may contribute to HALT development; however, the relationship between prosthesis deformation and HALT remains unclear. This study evaluated the incidence, and clinical impact of HALT following SAVR with Perceval. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that HALT is associated with adverse early clinical outcomes and that prosthesis deformation contributes to HALT development after Perceval sutureless valve implantation. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 31 patients who underwent SAVR with Perceval and postoperative ECG-gated cardiac computed tomography (CT) one week after surgery. HALT was defined as hypo-attenuated thickening involving one or more prosthetic valve leaflets during the early left ventricular diastolic phase. Prosthesis deformation was assessed by CT-derived valve eccentricity [1 – (Dmin/Dmax)] and asymmetric leaflet angle (sum of deviations from the ideal 120° leaflet angles) ( Fig 1A-B). Postoperatively, heparin was initiated (target APTT 1.5-2.0 imes control), followed by warfarin administration (PT-INR 1.6-2.5). Patients were divided into HALT (n=13) and non-HALT (n-18) groups. Results: The overall incidence of HALT following SAVR with the Perceval valve was 42% (13/31). HALT involved three leaflets in 7 patients, two leaflets in 4 patients (RN: 2, LN: 2), and one leaflet in 2 patients (N: 2). Warfarin was administered in 9 patients (69%) in the HALT group and 16 patients (89%) in the non-HALT group, with no significant between-group difference. Apart from body surface area (1.39 vs. 1.55 m 2 , p=0.007), no significant differences were observed in baseline, preoperative, or intraoperative characteristics. Neither the eccentricity index nor the asymmetric leaflet angle differed significantly between the groups. Postoperative echocardiographic findings are shown in Figure 1C. Although AVA was significantly smaller in the HALT group, AVAI did not differ significantly between groups. One patient in the HALT group died of sepsis during follow-up. No stroke or thromboembolic events occurred in either group. Conclusions: HALT occurred frequently after implantation of the Perceval sutureless valve. However, CT-derived indices of prosthesis deformation were not associated with HALT development. Furthermore, HALT did not adversely affect early valve hemodynamics. These findings suggest that factors other than valve deformation may play a more important role in the pathogenesis of HALT following Perceval implantation.
title: Abstract 7506: High Incidence of Hypo-Attenuated Leaflet Thickening After Perceval Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement

abstract: Introduction: Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SOVA) of left coronary cusp (LCC) is exceptionally rare. Submitral aneurysm (SMA) is also uncommon that may cause severe mitral regurgitation, heart failure, arrhythmias, systemic embolism and coronary compression. The coexistence of a ruptured SOVA of LCC communicating with a giant SMA of left ventricle (LV) and left atrium (LA) resulting in coronary artery compromise is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Patient Information: A 28-year-old male presented with acute chest pain followed by progressive dyspnea for seven days leading to NYHA functional class III. Pulse rate was 118/min with blood pressure was 102/70mmHg. Jugular venous pulse was elevated with hyperdynamic apical impulse and a grade IV/VI holosystolic murmur at mitral area. Diagnostic Assessment: Electrocardiography demonstrated sinus tachycardia with ST-segment depression in anterolateral leads. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed rupture of SOVA of LCC into a large SMA arising from the basal anterolateral wall of LV associated with severe mitral regurgitation and lateral wall hypokinesia. LV ejection fraction was 45-50%. Cardiac computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a giant LV aneurysm measuring 72 х 67 х 55 mm with a wide neck (43 х 38 mm) and a smaller 13-mm aneurysm arising from LCC communicating with the aneurysm cavity. Coronary angiography (CAG) revealed complete occlusion of the Left Circumflex artery (LCx) with collaterals from the right coronary artery (RCA) and significant extrinsic compression of the left coronary circulation including distal Left Main Coronary Artery (LMCA) and proximal Left Anterior Descending artery (LAD). Therapeutic Intervention: Intraoperative findings revealed rupture of the SOVA originating from LCC and communicating with LA and SMA cavity, with a dilated and dehiscent mitral annulus dealt successfully with repair of the ruptured SOVA, repair of the SMA, mitral valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting using a reversed saphenous vein graft to the obtuse marginal branch. Discussion: SMA is traditionally considered a congenital lesion resulting from developmental deficiency in the fusion of myocardium and cardiac fibro skeleton leading to weakness at the junction of the LV myocardium and the mitral annulus. Other acquired causes are infective endocarditis, Takayasu arteritis, tuberculosis, prior cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, and inflammatory disorders. Similarly, SOVA may be congenital or secondary to infective, degenerative, traumatic, or inflammatory processes. Detailed evaluation failed to identify any acquired cause. This coexistence in a young adult supports an idiopathic congenital origin. Multimodality imaging using TTE, Cardiac CT and CAG was critical in defining the complex anatomy and guiding operative planning.
title: Abstract 7520: Concomitant Ruptured Left Coronary Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm with Giant Submitral Left Ventricular Aneurysm Causing Circumflex Coronary Occlusion in a Young Adult

abstract: Introduction: Malignancy is associated with procedural and in-hospital complications after permanent pacemaker implantation; however, it is unclear whether this differs based on malignancy phenotype or patient sex. Research Questions: We evaluated whether hematologic and solid malignancies are associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes after permanent pacemaker implantation and whether these associations differ by sex. Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample, we identified adult hospitalizations undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation. Admissions were categorized as no malignancy, hematologic malignancy only, or solid malignancy only. Patients with both malignancy types were excluded because of sparse events. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% CIs for in-hospital outcomes. Sex-stratified interaction models assessed effect modification by sex. Results: We included 863,090 weighted hospitalizations, where 829,755 were without malignancy, 10,735 were with hematologic malignancy, and 22,600 were with solid malignancy. Compared with no malignancy, hematologic and solid malignancies were associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.06, 95% CI 1.52-2.80 and aOR 2.29, 95% CI 1.86-2.83, respectively) and major bleeding or transfusion (aOR 1.89, 95% CI 1.58-2.25 and aOR 1.89, 95% CI 1.65-2.16, respectively). Solid malignancy showed a more adverse profile, with higher odds of postprocedural pneumothorax, cardiogenic shock, mechanical ventilation, acute ischemic stroke, and intracranial hemorrhage. In sex-specific analyses, major bleeding was consistently higher in both males and females across malignancy groups. Hematologic malignancy showed a numerically higher mortality association among females vs males (interaction P=0.06). In solid malignancy, postprocedural pneumothorax was increased only in males (interaction P<0.001), whereas hemopericardium (interaction P=0.05) and cardiac arrest (interaction P=0.03) were increased only in females. Conclusions: Hematologic and solid malignancies are associated with increased risks of both in-hospital mortality and major bleeding after permanent pacemaker implantation. Solid malignancy has higher odds of several procedure-related complications. Sex significantly modified several outcomes, underscoring the need for phenotype-specific and sex-conscious risk assessment in patients with malignancy undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation.
title: Abstract 7529: Sex Differences, Malignancy Type, and In-Hospital Outcomes After Permanent Pacemaker Implantation: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis

abstract: Background: Patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remain at risk of adverse cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have demonstrated consistent benefits in heart failure populations, but their role in patients undergoing TAVI remains unclear. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients undergoing TAVI. Methods: Methods: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant, GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261377322). Randomized and observational studies comparing SGLT2 inhibitors with non-SGLT2 inhibitor therapy or standard care were identified through March 2026. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), acute kidney injury (AKI), urinary tract infection, and echocardiographic parameters. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Results: Five studies, including 6,111 patients (SGLT2i: n=2,933; control: n=3,178) were included. SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.48-0.97; p=0.03; I 2 =74%) and heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.62; 95% CI 0.42-0.90; p=0.01; I 2 =15%). Although a reduction in MACE was observed (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.48-0.96; p=0.03; I 2 =86%), this finding was not robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were found in AKI (RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.13-1.87; p=0.30; I 2 =81%), urinary tract infection (RR 0.96; 95% CI 0.59-1.55; p=0.87; I 2 =86%), or echocardiographic parameters including LVEF, LVESD, and LVEDD. In patients with low LVEF, SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with a greater reduction in mortality (RR 0.56; 95% CI 0.35-0.89; p=0.01; I 2 =75%). Conclusion: SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with reduced mortality and heart failure hospitalization in patients undergoing TAVI, with enhanced benefit in those with reduced LVEF. Effects on other cardiovascular, renal, and echocardiographic outcomes were neutral. These findings may support a potential role for SGLT2 inhibitors as adjunctive therapy in this population; however, dedicated randomized trials are needed to confirm these benefits.
title: Abstract 7542: Clinical Impact of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction/Background: Uncontrolled hypertension remains a major modifiable cause of cardiovascular and renal disease. Catheter-based renal denervation may lower blood pressure by reducing renal sympathetic activity, but sham-controlled evidence is needed. Research Question/Hypothesis: This meta-analysis evaluated whether radiofrequency renal denervation reduces ambulatory and office blood pressure compared with sham control in adults with uncontrolled hypertension. Methods/Approach: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized sham-controlled trials according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, reference lists, and relevant reviews were searched. Eligible studies enrolled adults with uncontrolled hypertension and compared contemporary radiofrequency renal denervation with a sham procedure. The primary outcome was change in 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure. Secondary outcomes included office systolic blood pressure, ambulatory and office diastolic blood pressure, escape criteria, and short-term safety. Mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models. Results/Data: Three multicenter randomized sham-controlled trials including 491 participants were included. Townsend et al. and Böhm et al. evaluated patients not receiving antihypertensive medications, whereas Kandzari et al. enrolled patients receiving 1 to 3 antihypertensive drugs. All trials used the Symplicity Spyral system; follow-up ranged from 3 to 6 months. Renal denervation reduced 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure versus sham control (MD -4.50 mmHg, 95% CI -6.60 to -2.41; p<0.0001; I 2 =0%). Office systolic blood pressure was also lower with renal denervation (MD -6.74 mmHg, 95% CI -9.45 to -4.02; p<0.00001; I 2 =0%). Reductions favored renal denervation for 24-hour ambulatory diastolic blood pressure (MD -3.45 mmHg, 95% CI -4.67 to -2.24; p<0.00001; I 2 =0%) and office diastolic blood pressure (MD -4.33 mmHg, 95% CI -5.79 to -2.87; p<0.00001; I 2 =0%). Escape criteria were met by 20 of 242 renal denervation patients and 35 of 249 sham-control patients (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.97; p=0.04; I 2 =0%). Adverse events were rare or absent, with no major device-related or procedure-related safety signal. Conclusion(s): In randomized sham-controlled trials of adults with uncontrolled hypertension, radiofrequency renal denervation was associated with consistent reductions in ambulatory and office blood pressure and fewer escape-criteria events compared with sham control. Safety findings were reassuring, but limited trial numbers and follow-up preclude conclusions about rare events or long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
title: Abstract 7584: Radiofrequency Renal Denervation for Uncontrolled Hypertension A Meta-Analysis of Sham Controlled Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Preadmission beta-blocker therapy is considered cardioprotective in acute coronary syndromes (ACS), but its independent contribution to short-term outcomes among patients with preserved ventricular function proceeding to coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains unclear. Methods: We retrospectively identified 1,060 ACS patients (STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina) with preserved EF (≥40%) undergoing isolated CABG. Patients on pre-admission beta-blockers (BB+, n=560) were compared with beta-blocker-naïve patients (BB–, n=500). Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, length of stay (LOS), and intensive care unit (ICU) hours, analyzed by multivariable logistic and OLS regression. A 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching sensitivity analysis (11 covariates; caliper = 0.2 х SD of the logit score) was performed. Results: In the unmatched cohort, in-hospital mortality was similar between BB+ and BB– patients (0.6% vs 0.3%, p=1.000), as was 30-day mortality (1.3% vs 0.6%, p=0.349). After multivariable adjustment, pre-admission beta-blocker therapy was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.12-18.96; p=0.742) or 30-day mortality (OR 2.48, 95% CI 0.62-9.91; p=0.198). Baseline imbalances before matching (hypertension SMD +0.51, prior PCI +0.46, heart failure +0.25) were eliminated after propensity matching (311 pairs; maximum SMD=0.06). In the matched cohort, mortality remained similar, with in-hospital mortality of 1.6% in BB+ patients versus 0.6% in BB– patients (p=0.450) and 30-day mortality of 1.6% in BB+ patients versus 0.6% in BB– patients (p=0.286). Median hospital LOS was identical in the unmatched cohort (9 days in BB+ vs 9 days in BB–; p=0.793). Following matching, LOS remained similar at 9.0 days (IQR 7-13) in BB+ patients versus 9.0 days (IQR 6-12) in BB– patients (p=0.929). Median ICU duration did not differ between groups in the unmatched cohort (41 hours in BB+ vs 43 hours in BB–; p=0.649). After matching, ICU stay remained comparable at 40.7 hours (IQR 22.6-67.5) in BB+ patients versus 44.1 hours (IQR 22.1-69.3) in BB– patients (p=0.871). Conclusions: Pre-admission beta-blocker therapy conferred no independent perioperative survival benefit in ACS patients with preserved EF undergoing isolated CABG. The numerically higher BB+ mortality reflects confounding by indication, and these findings should not be interpreted as justification to withhold the therapy.
title: Abstract 7594: Preadmission Beta-Blocker Therapy and Short-Term Outcomes After CABG in Acute Coronary Syndrome Patients with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) is associated with adverse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but its independent impact on mortality and postoperative resource utilization among patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains uncertain. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 1,824 patients with AMI (STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina) undergoing isolated CABG at a single center. Patients were stratified by preoperative EF <40% (reduced EF, n=338) versus ≥40% (preserved EF, n=1,486). Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, hospital length of stay (LOS), and intensive care unit (ICU) duration. Multivariable regression adjusted for age, STS Predicted Risk of Mortality, diabetes, prior myocardial infarction, and extent of coronary artery disease. Propensity score matching yielded 567 well-balanced patients (284 reduced EF vs 283 preserved EF). Results: Patients with reduced EF had higher unadjusted in-hospital mortality (3.9% vs 0.8%, p=0.002) and 30-day mortality (3.6% vs 1.1%, p=0.002), as well as longer median LOS (12 vs 9 days, p<0.001) and ICU duration (76 vs 41 hours, p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, reduced EF was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.38, 95% CI 0.77-7.32, p=0.131) or 30-day mortality (aOR 1.91, 95% CI 0.76-4.75, p=0.167). However, reduced EF remained independently associated with longer LOS (+1.81 days, p<0.001) and ICU duration (+22.08 hours, p<0.001). In the propensity-matched cohort, mortality remained similar between groups (30-day mortality 2.1% vs 1.8%, p=0.765), whereas LOS (11 vs 10 days, p=0.004) and ICU duration (70.6 vs 46.8 hours, p<0.001) remained significantly greater among patients with reduced EF. Conclusions: Among patients presenting with AMI undergoing isolated CABG, reduced preoperative EF was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization and ICU utilization but not short-term mortality after risk adjustment and propensity matching. These findings suggest that excess mortality risk is largely explained by baseline comorbidity burden, whereas reduced EF remains an important determinant of postoperative resource utilization and may aid preoperative planning and ICU resource allocation.
title: Abstract 7597: Impact of Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction on Early Outcomes Following CABG for Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Multi-Variable and Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Right heart failure (RHF) is a hemodynamically distinct syndrome with almost no population-level outcome data, as ICD-10-CM subtype codes (I50.810-I50.813) were introduced only in late 2016. The national burden of cardiogenic shock in RHF and the frequency with which mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is deployed when shock occurs remain undefined. Hypothesis: Cardiogenic shock complicates a large percentage of RHF hospitalizations and is the principal driver of in-hospital death, yet MCS is deployed far below the burden of shock. Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2017-2020), we identified adult primary-diagnosis RHF hospitalizations (I50.810-I50.813). Cardiogenic shock (R57.0) and MCS (ECMO, RVAD/Impella, IABP) were captured from all diagnosis and procedure fields. Survey-weighted logistic and linear regression identified independent predictors of in-hospital mortality and length of stay (LOS), adjusting for subtype, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics, with unspecified RHF as the reference subtype. Results: Among 7,555 weighted RHF hospitalizations (mean age 62.2 years; 55.3% female; pulmonary hypertension 41.5%), acute-on-chronic RHF predominated (56.0%). Cardiogenic shock complicated 8.93% of admissions and was the overwhelming driver of death: mortality 37.8% vs 4.4% (crude OR 13.3), and after full adjustment, it remained by far the dominant independent predictor of mortality (aOR 14.25, 95% CI 8.43-24.10; p<0.001), alongside comorbidity burden (CCI per point aOR 1.28; p<0.001). Despite this, MCS was used in only 1.06% of admissions and in 11.1% of shocked patients—89% received no device. MCS was exclusively ECMO (81%) and RVAD/Impella (19%); no IABP was used. Acute-on-chronic RHF did not confer higher adjusted mortality but was the highest-resource subtype, independently predicting longer LOS (+2.2 days; p<0.001) and the highest charges; atrial fibrillation independently predicted longer LOS (+1.0 day; p=0.038) but not mortality. Conclusion: In this first national, subtype-resolved analysis of RHF, cardiogenic shock affected 1 in 10 hospitalizations and was the overwhelming independent predictor of in-hospital mortality, yet only 1 in 9 shocked patients received device support. This deployment gap—and the distinct resource burden of acute-on-chronic RHF and atrial fibrillation—defines high-priority targets for prospective study and guideline development.
title: Abstract 7614: Cardiogenic Shock in Right Heart Failure National Prevalence, Outcomes, and the Mechanical Circulatory Support Deployment Gap

abstract: Background: Clonal hematopoiesis is the age-related clonal expansion of blood stem cells with genomic changes linked to cancer and adverse outcomes. It encompasses single-nucleotide variants or short insertions/deletions, termed clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), and larger structural alterations, termed mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs). While certain CHIP subtypes have been linked to venous thromboembolism (VTE), associations between mCAs and VTE are not well described. Objective: To test the association of mCAs with incident VTE. Methods: We included UK Biobank and Mass General Brigham (MGB) Biobank participants without prevalent malignancy or VTE and with available genotype data. Co-primary exposures were autosomal mCAs, loss of Y chromosome (LOY), and loss of X chromosome (LOX), ascertained from genome-wide genotyping. The primary outcome was incident VTE ascertained by qualifying ICD codes in both biobanks. Associations of mCAs and large mCAs (clonal fraction ≥10%) with incident VTE were tested using Cox regression, adjusted for baseline demographics, cardiovascular and VTE risk factors, and medications. Results of the two biobanks were combined by fixed-effect meta-analysis. Results: We examined 416,287 UK Biobank participants (mean [SD] age 56.2 [8.1] years, 54.6% female) and 36,379 MGB Biobank participants (50.9 [17.3] years, 56.8% female). In both cohorts, mCA carriers were older and had greater cardiometabolic comorbidity. In the UK Biobank, mCAs were present in 59,032 participants (14.1%; 13,718 autosomes, 36,514 LOY, 11,331 LOX); VTE occurred in 7055 (1.7%) over a median of 13.7 (IQR 13.0-14.4) years. In the MGB Biobank, mCAs were present in 5,236 participants (14.4%; 1695 autosomes, 1732 LOY, 2159 LOX); VTE occurred in 1843 (5.1%) over a median of 3.5 (IQR 1.5-5.5) years. Large autosomal mCAs were associated with increased risk of VTE (HR, 95% CI 1.29 [1.06-1.57]). LOY and large LOY were associated with decreased risk of VTE (0.87 [0.81-0.94] and 0.76 [0.66-0.87], respectively). LOX and large LOX were not significantly associated with VTE. There was no significant between-cohort heterogeneity. Given the known association between LOY and atrial fibrillation, which may prompt anticoagulation, we performed a sensitivity analysis that included time-varying atrial fibrillation. This analysis yielded consistent results. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that large autosomal mCAs constitute a novel risk factor for VTE, whereas LOY is associated with lower risk of VTE. Future work should investigate pathways through which specific mCAs relate to thromboembolic risk.
title: Abstract 7624: Association of Mosaic Chromosomal Alterations with Incident Venous Thromboembolic Disease in 450,000 Individuals

abstract: Background: The efficacy of P2Y12 inhibitor pre-treatment in non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) before PCI remains uncertain, with guidelines recommending selective use. Prior meta-analyses included out-of-scope trials, potentially biasing conclusions. We performed frequentist and Bayesian meta-analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA). Research Question: Is P2Y12 inhibitor pre-treatment before PCI for NSTEMI safe and efficacious? Methods: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and propensity-adjusted observational studies. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel and random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by I 2 . TSA was performed for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major bleeding. A Bayesian hierarchical model using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with the No-U-Turn Sampler estimated RRs with 95% credible intervals (CrI). Posterior probability of benefit [Pr(RR<1)] was calculated for MACE and overt bleeding, with absolute risk differences, NNT/NNH, and likelihood to be helped or harmed (LHH). Results: Eight RCTs and two observational studies totaling 21,314 patients were included. Frequentist analysis showed no significant reduction in 30-day MACE with pre-treatment [RR 0.72 (95% CI 0.52-1.00)]. No significant differences were found for major bleeding, all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, stroke, stent thrombosis, revascularization, or long-term major bleeding, myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death. TSA showed the cumulative Z-curve did not cross monitoring boundaries and required information size was not reached (57,557), suggesting non-significance may not exclude benefit. Bayesian analysis showed a median RR for 30-day MACE of 0.78 (95% CrI 0.55-1.00; ARR 1.7% [0.0-3.5%], NNT 58), with 97.7% posterior probability of benefit and 87.4% predictive probability for future studies. For major bleeding, median RR was 1.13 (95% CrI 0.86-1.51; ARI 0.2% [-0.2-0.8%], NNH 509), with 18.8% probability of benefit. Median net absolute benefit was 1.53% (95% CrI -0.25% to 3.33%), with 95.7% probability benefit exceeds harm and LHH 4.98. Conclusion: P2Y12 pre-treatment before PCI in NSTEMI did not significantly affect any outcomes in the frequentist analysis, but TSA suggests underpowered evidence. Bayesian analysis indicates probable MACE reduction with a limited risk of major bleeding, supporting targeted use and further trials.
title: Abstract 7631: P2Y12 Inhibitor Pre-Treatment Before PCI in NSTEMI Provides Probable Reduction in Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Without Significant Excess Bleeding: Frequentist and Bayesian Meta-Analyses with Trial Sequential Analysis

abstract: Background: Veno-arterial ECMO is increasingly used to support adults in cardiogenic shock (CS), yet women remain a minority of recipients and sex-specific outcomes are poorly defined. Whether female sex independently affects in-hospital mortality and the vascular and bleeding complications intrinsic to ECMO cannulation is unknown at the national level. Hypothesis: Among adults with CS supported by ECMO, female sex is independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality and a greater burden of vascular and bleeding complications, independent of obesity. Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020), we identified adults with cardiogenic shock and a concurrent ECMO procedure code. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated the independent association of female sex with in-hospital mortality and a pre-specified panel of ECMO-related complications, adjusting for age, race, income, insurance, Elixhauser comorbidities, shock etiology (AMI vs non-AMI), obesity, hospital characteristics, and year. The sex х obesity interaction was formally tested. Results: Among 11,356 unweighted hospitalizations (~56,780 weighted; 36.9% female; overall mortality 43.1%), women comprised barely a third of CS-ECMO recipients yet had higher adjusted in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.14-1.35; p<0.001). Female sex was independently associated with a greater burden of composite vascular/access complications (aOR 1.41, 95% CI 1.20-1.64), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.41), pericardial complications (aOR 1.35), blood transfusion (aOR 1.29), and post-operative bleeding (aOR 1.21; all p<0.001). Conversely, women had lower odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 0.63) and atrial fibrillation (aOR 0.76; both p<0.001). The effect of obesity on outcomes did not differ by sex (sex х obesity interaction p=0.76 for mortality and p=0.82 for vascular complications). Conclusions: In this first national, sex-focused analysis of CS-ECMO, women—though only one-third of recipients—experienced independently higher in-hospital mortality and a disproportionate burden of vascular, bleeding, and pericardial complications, while obesity modified outcomes equally in both sexes. These disparities, plausibly rooted in smaller vessel caliber and access-related injury, identify sex as an under-recognized axis of risk in ECMO and a priority target for cannulation strategy and prospective study.
title: Abstract 7638: Sex Disparities in Cardiogenic Shock Requiring ECMO: Higher Mortality and Vascular Complications in Women—A National Analysis

abstract: Background: As TAVR expands into younger, lower-risk patients, an increasing number will outlive two successive bioprosthetic valves, making valve-in-valve-in-valve (ViViV) intervention an emerging clinical reality. The THIRD multicenter registry reported on 51 patients undergoing three aortic interventions, but only 14 underwent transcatheter procedures at both the second and third interventions. Patient-level data on procedural sequencing, valve combinations, and granular outcomes remain scarce, limiting the ability to counsel patients and plan ViViV procedures. Methods: We performed a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar for case reports and series with patient-level data describing a third aortic valve procedure. After deduplication of 353 records, screening of 197 abstracts, and full-text review of 50 reports, 31 articles met inclusion criteria, yielding 32 patient-level observations. All outcomes were classified per VARC-3 definitions. Results: Thirty-two patients (median age 77 years; 59.4% male) across 10 countries (2012 to 2026) were included. The dominant sequence was SAVR-TAVR-TAVR (87.5%); four patients underwent TAVR-TAVR-TAVR, a pattern expected to grow as index TAVR recipients age. Structural valve deterioration was the indication in 50%, non-structural dysfunction in 37.5%, and endocarditis in 6.3%. Median interval from first to second intervention was 8.0 years; second to third was 4.0 years. All third procedures were transcatheter (balloon-expandable in 18, self-expanding in 13). Median mean aortic gradient fell from 60 to 11 mmHg, a reduction of 43 mmHg. VARC-3 technical success was 100% (32/32); 30-day device success 100% (21/21 evaluable); 30-day mortality 0/19 evaluable. Coronary obstruction occurred in 1/32 (3.1%); tamponade, valve embolization, and open conversion each in 0/32. Conclusions: ViViV TAVR is technically feasible with high procedural success and substantial gradient reduction across diverse valve combinations and sequences. The accelerating interval between interventions, 8 years to first reintervention and 4 years to the third, underscores the need for prospective ViViV registries and standardized coronary protection protocols. These findings provide actionable patient-level granularity to inform pre-procedural planning at structural heart programs anticipating growing ViViV volume.
title: Abstract 7654: Valve-in-Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review of Patient-Level Analysis

abstract: Background: The 2024 FDA approval of lifileucel (Amtagvi) established tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy as the first cellular therapy for unresectable/metastatic melanoma, yet its cardiovascular profile remains poorly defined. TIL therapy includes infusion of the cellular product, lymphodepletion with cyclophosphamide/fludarabine, and post-infusion high-dose interleukin-2, usually in immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-exposed patients, creating potential arrhythmogenic, hemodynamic, and thromboembolic sequelae. Hypothesis: TIL therapy is associated with short-term cardiovascular events, and cardio-oncology evaluation may help characterize post-TIL cardiovascular toxicity. Methods: We retrospectively included 19 adults receiving FDA-approved lifileucel for unresectable/metastatic melanoma at UCLA Health from 2024-2026. Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) events were defined per International Cardio-Oncology Society domains: arrhythmia/conduction events, including new atrial fibrillation/flutter, supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), ventricular ectopy/nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, or corrected QT interval (QTc) ≥500 ms; myocardial injury, defined as troponin above the 99th-percentile upper reference limit; new left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, defined as LVEF ≤50%; new/worsened pericardial effusion; and thromboembolic events, defined as venous/arterial thromboembolism or ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack. Statistical analyses used Fisher exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Results: Median age was 61 years; 57.9% were female, 94.7% had stage IV melanoma, and 100% had prior ICI exposure. All patients had pre-TIL QTc <500 ms, while 5/19 (26.3%) developed post-TIL QTc ≥500 ms (range 509-607 ms). CTR-CVT events occurred in 10/19 (52.6%): arrhythmia/conduction events in 6/19 (31.6%), myocardial injury in 3/19 (15.8%), thromboembolic events in 3/19 (15.8%), pericardial effusion in 2/19 (10.5%), and LV dysfunction in 1/19 (5.3%). In univariable, unadjusted analyses, new atrial fibrillation/SVT was associated with longer hospitalization (20 vs. 10.5 days; p=0.008), SVT was more frequent among patients with 30- and 90-day readmission (both p=0.035), and thromboembolic events were associated with higher all-cause mortality (3/3 vs. 4/16; p=0.036), with no primarily cardiovascular deaths. Myocardial injury was numerically lower among patients with pre-TIL cardio-oncology evaluation (10.0% vs. 22.2%; p>0.05). Post-TIL cardio-oncology evaluation occurred only among patients with pre-TIL evaluation (6/10 vs. 0/9; p=0.011). Conclusions: In this real-world TIL cohort, CTR-CVT events occurred in a majority of patients and were associated with hospitalization, readmission, and mortality, supporting systematic cardiovascular surveillance as TIL therapy expands.
title: Abstract 7668: Defining the Cardiovascular Toxicity Landscape of Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte Therapy: A Real-World Cardio-Oncology Characterization

abstract: Background: Non-rheumatic valvular heart disease, encompassing degenerative aortic stenosis and mitral regurgitation, disproportionately affects aging populations in high-income countries. Although the past three decades have seen substantial expansion in echocardiographic surveillance, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and surgical valve repair, whether this era of broadened intervention has translated into population-level mortality reductions remains unknown. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that NRVHD-related mortality has continued to rise across high-income countries between 1990 and 2021, with persistent sex-based and geographic disparities. Methods: A retrospective secondary analysis was conducted using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 data for 36 World Bank-classified high-income countries. Age-standardized death rates (ASDRs) per 100,000 population were extracted and stratified by sex and country. The Average Annual Percentage Change (AAPC) was estimated by fitting weighted log-linear regression to the natural logarithm of annual ASDRs in R (version 4.4.2), with weights inversely proportional to the variance of log-transformed rates; 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived from the standard error of the regression slope. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.050. Results: NRVHD mortality rose steadily from 6.75 to 11.30 deaths per 100,000 over the study period (AAPC +1.88%; 95% CI, 1.60%-1.97%; p less than 0.001), increasing without pause throughout the modern valve-intervention era. Female mortality rose from 8.05 to 13.61 per 100,000 (AAPC +1.86%), consistently exceeding male mortality, which increased from 5.38 to 8.92 per 100,000 (AAPC +1.74%). Female AAPC exceeded male AAPC in 20 of 36 countries, confirming a widening sex-based mortality gap. In 2021, the highest ASDRs were observed in Germany (20.49 per 100,000), the Netherlands (19.09), and Finland (17.89). The steepest mortality trajectories were in Portugal (AAPC +4.91%), the Republic of Korea (+4.61%), Greece (+3.49%), Italy (+3.10%), and Finland (+3.03%). Singapore was the sole high-income country with a declining NRVHD mortality trajectory (AAPC –0.20%). Conclusions: Across 36 high-income countries over 32 years, NRVHD-related mortality increased significantly and continuously, even as valve-intervention capacity expanded, a paradox suggesting that current detection and treatment pathways are not producing population-level mortality benefit. Persistently higher and accelerating female mortality identifies women as a priority population for investigation of referral and access barriers. Singapore’s divergent decline suggests that health-system-level factors, including structured referral protocols and proactive adoption of minimally invasive procedures, may modify national NRVHD outcomes and warrant dedicated comparative investigation.
title: Abstract 7678: Non-Rheumatic Valvular Heart Disease Mortality Trends in High Income Countries from 1990 to 2021: A Global Burden of Disease Analysis

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (AF), but recent large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded conflicting results, leaving its comparative efficacy and safety incompletely defined. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that LAAC would demonstrate overall efficacy similar to OAC for stroke prevention while offering a nonprocedural bleeding advantage. Methods: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261374782). Electronic databases were searched from inception through April 2026. Primary outcomes were all strokes, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and disabling stroke. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, major nonprocedural bleeding, systemic embolism, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, composite cardiovascular endpoints, and periprocedural adverse events. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess the sufficiency of cumulative evidence. Results: Five RCTs comprising 5,428 patients were included. LAAC was associated with a significantly higher risk of ischemic stroke (4.1% vs. 2.6%; RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.09-1.99; P=0.012) and periprocedural adverse events (2.2% vs. 0.2%; RR 9.79, 95% CI 1.78-53.88; P=0.009), but a significantly lower risk of major nonprocedural bleeding (5.4% vs. 7.5%; RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.46-0.87; P=0.004). No significant differences were observed for all stroke (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.81-1.55), hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.24-1.05), overall major bleeding (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.82-1.15), all-cause mortality (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.77-1.10), or cardiovascular death (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.60-1.24). TSA indicated that current evidence remains insufficient to make a conclusive determination of several outcomes. GRADE certainty ranged from moderate to very low. Conclusions: In patients with nonvalvular AF, LAAC yielded broadly similar overall efficacy to OAC but with a trade-off between reduced major nonprocedural bleeding and increased ischemic stroke and periprocedural complication risks. Current evidence does not support the superiority of LAAC over OAC.
title: Abstract 7693: Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Oral Anticoagulation for Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Introduction: Left main coronary artery (LMCA) thrombus is a rare but life-threatening cause of acute coronary syndrome and cardiogenic shock. Floating thrombi involving the LMCA bifurcation are exceedingly uncommon. We report a case of postoperative cardiogenic shock caused by a floating LMCA thrombus with superimposed in-stent thrombosis. Case Presentation: A 73-year-old woman with coronary artery disease status post PCI to the LAD and LCx, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, constrictive pericarditis status post pericardiectomy, combined factor V and VII deficiency, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, breast cancer, and newly diagnosed bladder cancer underwent elective transurethral resection of a bladder tumor (TURBT). The procedure was uncomplicated; however, in the recovery unit she developed abrupt hypotension progressing to cardiogenic shock requiring vasopressor support. She subsequently developed complete heart block and pulseless electrical activity arrest. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after approximately five minutes of CPR. Electrocardiography demonstrated complete heart block with widening of a pre-existing left bundle branch block. Lactate was elevated to 8 mmol/L. Bedside echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction with an estimated ejection fraction of 10% and extensive anterior-apical akinesis. Emergent coronary angiography demonstrated a mobile thrombus within the LMCA extending across the LAD-LCx bifurcation, 70% mid-LM stenosis, and thrombus within prior LAD and LCx stents. The patient underwent successful aspiration thrombectomy and balloon angioplasty with restoration of flow. A temporary transvenous pacemaker and Impella device were placed, and bivalirudin was initiated. Within 48 hours, left ventricular function improved to 50-55% and Impella support was removed. Due to persistent conduction abnormalities, a dual-chamber permanent pacemaker was implanted. Her course was complicated by hematuria and transfusion-dependent anemia. Serial echocardiograms demonstrated complete recovery of ventricular function with ejection fraction improving to 60-65% by discharge. Discussion: This case illustrates a rare presentation of floating LMCA thrombus causing complete heart block, cardiac arrest, and profound cardiogenic shock in the immediate postoperative setting. Prompt recognition, emergent angiography, mechanical circulatory support, and revascularization resulted in complete recovery of ventricular function. Floating LMCA thrombus should be considered in postoperative patients with sudden cardiogenic shock and conduction abnormalities, as early invasive management can be lifesaving.
title: Abstract 7701: Floating Left Main Coronary Thrombus Causing Cardiogenic Shock Following Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour

abstract: Background: Acute right ventricular failure (RVF) is highly lethal. It is usually managed as a single entity. Pulmonary embolism (PE)-related acute cor pulmonale is seen as the classic cause. No national study has examined whether the specific cause—not just its presence—affects outcome. Hypothesis: Building on this observation, we hypothesize that mortality in acute RVF is governed by the precipitating insult: RVF from acute injuries (post-LVAD, post-cardiotomy, ARDS/COVID, sepsis) is far deadlier than RVF from PE or chronic pulmonary-vascular disease. Methods: To test this, we used the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020) to identify adult hospitalizations with acute RVF—acute cor pulmonale (I26.0x) or acute/acute-on-chronic right heart failure (I50.811/I50.813)—in any diagnosis position and assigned a hierarchical primary etiology. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality for each etiology versus PE and for a pooled acute-insult exposure, adjusting for demographics, payer, income, year, hospital characteristics, and Elixhauser comorbidity burden; mechanical support use was assessed by etiology. Results: Our analysis revealed that among 175,285 weighted acute RVF hospitalizations (35,057 unweighted), in-hospital mortality varied nearly 9-fold by cause. Counterintuitively, PE—the most common etiology (59.1%)—was among the most survivable (6.5%), and chronic pulmonary-vascular disease was lower still (PAH 6.2%, COPD 4.6%); compared with PE, both were protective after adjustment (PAH aOR 0.62; COPD 0.55). In contrast, RVF from acute insults was markedly lethal: post-LVAD 34.6% (aOR 5.03), ARDS/COVID 29.3% (aOR 5.60), sepsis 28.1% (aOR 4.17), and post-cardiotomy 20.4% (aOR 2.59). When pooled, acute-insult etiology conferred ~5-fold higher adjusted odds of death than PE/chronic causes (aOR 5.10, 95% CI 4.68-5.57; p<0.001). Mechanical support (ECMO/percutaneous RVAD) was used in only 1.7% overall and tracked surgical context rather than mortality risk: 53.3% of post-LVAD and 38.9% of post-cardiotomy cases received support, versus 5.4% of ARDS/COVID and 2.9% of sepsis, despite their ~28% mortality. Conclusions: In summary, in this first national, etiology-resolved analysis, the prototypical cause of acute RVF—PE was among the most survivable, whereas RVF precipitated by an acute insult was 3-5х deadlier. Importantly, mechanical support was concentrated in surgical etiologies and minimal in the equally lethal medical ones. These findings demonstrate that acute RVF is not a single disease; outcomes are defined by the precipitant, supporting the need for etiology-specific risk stratification and the prospective study of support strategies.
title: Abstract 7702: The Survivable and the Lethal: Etiology Determines Mortality—and Mechanical Support—in Acute Right Ventricular Failure (NIS 2016-2020)

abstract: Introduction: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) in adolescents is most often attributed to inherited channelopathies, cardiomyopathies, or anomalous coronary arteries. Rare non-atherosclerotic, non-inflammatory coronary arteriopathies may be clinically occult, evade conventional pre-transplant evaluation, and only be apparent on explant pathology. Patient Information: A 14-year-old male with developmental delay (de novo 2q14.3q21.2 deletion), growth hormone deficiency, and marfanoid habitus, with no personal or family cardiac history, presented after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Clinical Findings Timeline: The patient collapsed while sprinting at school, prompting bystander CPR and AED defibrillation for ventricular tachycardia (Figure 1). Initial evaluation showed severe LV systolic dysfunction (EF 30%),hsTrop 249 ng/L, and BNP 2,134 pg/mL. Diagnostic Assessment: Coronary CTA showed normal coronary origins, large LV thrombus, chamber dilation, and subendocardial hypoattenuation consistent with infarction (Figure 2). Respiratory panel detected rhinovirus, but endomyocardial biopsy showed no myocarditis and rheumatologic evaluation was unrevealing. Therapeutic Interventions: Despite inotropic support, he suffered an in-hospital VT/VF arrest requiring VA-ECMO, complicated by RV thrombus requiring biventricular thrombectomy which revealed a fibrotic LAD and extensive transmural scar. He underwent an orthotopic heart transplant and explant pathology (Figure 3) revealed diffuse non-atherosclerotic, non-vasculitic, coronary vasculopathy with severe intimal fibromuscular proliferation, organizing thrombi with recanalization, intimal dissection, and internal elastic lamina disruption with remote and acute transmural infarction. Follow-up Outcomes: Whole genome sequencing identified no pathogenic variants in known aortopathy or connective tissue genes. His chromosome deletion includes PROC, potentially contributing to thrombotic burden via impaired anticoagulant regulation. Two years after transplant, he remains well with normal graft function and no evidence of cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Discussion: This case illustrates an occult, diffuse, and severe non-atherosclerotic and non-inflammatory coronary arteriopathy presenting as exercise-induced SCA, ischemic cardiomyopathy, refractory VT, and extensive intracardiac thrombosis in an adolescent. Extensive pre-transplant evaluation was unrevealing; the diagnosis was established only on explant pathology. Histology resembled intimal-type fibromuscular dysplasia described in coronary sudden death, although the diffuse multivessel involvement and thrombotic burden were atypical. Recognition of this rare phenotype may inform future evaluation of pediatric SCA when ischemic injury and thrombosis are disproportionate to findings on standard coronary imaging.
title: Abstract 7739: Adolescent Sudden Cardiac Arrest from Diffuse Non-Inflammatory Coronary Arteriopathy Diagnosed at Explant

abstract: Background: Premature ventricular complex (PVC)-related cardiomyopathy is a potentially reversible cause of heart failure. We compared long-term outcomes of catheter ablation versus antiarrhythmic drugs in patients with PVC-related cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult patients with PVCs and underlying cardiomyopathy or systolic heart failure were identified. Patients undergoing PVC ablation were compared with those treated with antiarrhythmic drugs including amiodarone, sotalol, mexiletine, flecainide, or propafenone. Patients with ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, congenital heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, cardiac transplantation, sarcoid myocarditis, or transthyretin amyloidosis were excluded. Outcomes were assessed from 1 day after index event through 1- and 3-year follow-up. Primary outcomes included heart failure hospitalization, composite heart failure worsening (heart failure hospitalization or cardiogenic shock), and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included CRT or ICD implantation. Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 fashion using demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, heart failure severity, and baseline medication use. After matching, 2,258 patients remained in each cohort at 1 year and 2,329 patients remained in each cohort at 3 years. Results: At 1 year, catheter ablation was associated with lower rates of heart failure hospitalization compared with antiarrhythmic drugs (2.2% vs 11.1%; OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.12-0.25; HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.14-0.27; p<0.001). The composite outcome of heart failure hospitalization or cardiogenic shock was reduced (2.3% vs 11.2%; OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.13-0.26; HR 0.20, 95% CI 0.14-0.28; p<0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly lower following ablation (2.0% vs 7.8%; OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.18-0.34; HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.19-0.36; p<0.001), while CRT/ICD implantation rates were similar (3.1% vs 3.6%; p=0.320).At 3 years, ablation demonstrated lower rates of heart failure hospitalization (4.7% vs 16.6%; HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.22-0.36; p<0.001), composite heart failure worsening (4.7% vs 16.8%; HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23-0.36; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (3.9% vs 12.1%; HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.26-0.41; p<0.001). Device implantation was lower in the ablation cohort (4.2% vs 5.7%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.97; p=0.019). Recurrent heart failure events were reduced following ablation (2.6 vs 3.9 events; p=0.041). Conclusions: In patients with PVC-related cardiomyopathy and heart failure, catheter ablation was associated with lower rates of heart failure hospitalization, heart failure worsening, mortality, recurrent heart failure events, and device implantation compared with antiarrhythmic drug therapy. These findings support catheter ablation as a disease-modifying therapy.
title: Abstract 7740: Catheter Ablation versus Antiarrhythmic Drug Therapy in Patients with Premature Ventricular Complex-Induced Cardiomyopathy and Heart Failure: A Propensity-Matched Nationwide Analysis

abstract: Background: In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) receiving cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), rhythm control with AF ablation and rate control with atrioventricular node (AVN) ablation are both used to optimize outcomes. However, comparative long-term outcomes between these strategies remain uncertain. We evaluated 1-year and 3-year outcomes after AVN ablation versus AF ablation in patients with AF and CRT. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged >18 years with AF and prior CRT or implantable device therapy were included. Patients undergoing AVN ablation were compared with patients undergoing AF ablation. Outcomes were assessed from 1 day after the index procedure through 1 and 3 years. Outcomes included heart failure hospitalization, composite heart failure worsening (heart failure hospitalization or cardiogenic shock), all-cause mortality, and stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 using age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, prior myocardial infarction, heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors/ARBs/ARNI, antiarrhythmic drugs, anticoagulants, left ventricular ejection fraction, and natriuretic peptide levels. Before matching, 1,742 patients had AVN ablation and 3,674 had AF ablation. After matching we got 1,331 patients in each cohort. Results: At 1 year, heart failure hospitalization was similar between AVN ablation and AF ablation groups (8.0% vs 8.1%; OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.62-1.56; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.62-1.50; p=0.936). Composite heart failure worsening was also similar (8.8% vs 8.5%; OR 1.04, 95% CI 0.66-1.63; p=0.882). All-cause mortality was significantly higher after AVN ablation (13.1% vs 6.4%; HR 2.06, 95% CI 1.59-2.67; p<0.001). Stroke/TIA rates were comparable (2.6% vs 2.5%; HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.62-1.76; p=0.847).At 3 years, heart failure hospitalization remained similar (18.8% vs 16.8%; HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.75-1.37; p=0.412), as did composite heart failure worsening (20.1% vs 16.9%; HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.80-1.45; p=0.201). Mortality remained significantly higher following AVN ablation (24.5% vs 12.8%; OR 2.22, 95% CI 1.81-2.72; HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.54-2.23; p<0.001). Stroke/TIA rates were again similar (4.9% vs 4.3%; HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.75-1.65; p=0.441). Conclusions: Among patients with AF and CRT, AVN ablation and AF ablation were associated with similar rate of heart failure hospitalization, heart failure worsening, and thromboembolic events at 1 and 3 years. However, AVN ablation was associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that AF ablation may provide a survival advantage over AVN ablation however warrants prospective studies.
