Distinct electrophysiologic behavior across aortic root structures suggests the presence of specialized pacing niches that may inform future conduction-system and valve-integrated pacing technologies.
title: Abstract 8079: Human Electrophysiology of Aortic Root Pacing: Differential Capture Characteristics of the Coronary Cusps and Left-Sided His Region

abstract: Background: As the population ages, increasing numbers of nonagenarians are referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Although advanced age remains an important consideration during Heart Team evaluation, chronological age may inadequately reflect biological vulnerability. Frailty has emerged as a potential predictor of outcomes in elderly patients undergoing structural heart interventions. We sought to compare the prognostic value of chronological age and frailty for mortality after TAVI. Methods: We analyzed consecutive patients who underwent TAVI at Geneva University Hospitals between 2008 and 2023 and were prospectively enrolled in an institutional registry. Patients were stratified by age (<90 vs. ≥90 years) and frailty status. Frailty was assessed as part of the routine geriatric evaluation and defined by an Essential Frailty Toolset (EFT) score ≥3. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and outcomes were evaluated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC-3) definitions. Results: Among 710 patients undergoing TAVI, 107 (15.1%) were nonagenarians. Overall 1-year mortality was 10.5%, including 4.6% cardiovascular mortality. Mortality declined over time, from 21% among the first 100 treated patients to 7% among the last 100 patients. No significant differences in 1-year mortality or other clinical outcomes were observed between patients aged <90 and ≥90 years. In contrast, frailty was strongly associated with adverse outcomes. Frail patients exhibited higher early mortality within 7 days after TAVI (4.8% vs. 1.2%, p=0.003) and significantly lower long-term survival through 7 years of follow-up (64.9% vs. 74.5%, p=0.01). Frailty-based stratification provided superior prognostic discrimination compared with age-based stratification, with significant differences observed in Cox proportional hazards analyses from 30 days through 7 years of follow-up (all p≤0.01). Conclusions: Chronological age alone should not be used to deny TAVI, even among nonagenarians. In this 15-year single-center cohort, frailty was a stronger predictor of mortality than age and provided superior risk stratification after TAVI. Routine frailty assessment may improve patient selection and help identify elderly patients most likely to benefit from intervention.
title: Abstract 8081: Frailty Outperforms Chronological Age in Predicting Mortality After TAVI: Insights From a 15-Year Single-Center Cohort

abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) combined with anthracyclines have transformed triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment, yet cardiovascular safety in real-world practice remains poorly defined. Pivotal trials (KEYNOTE-355, IMpassion130) had limited follow-up, highly selected populations, and insufficient power for rare cardiac events. Hypothesis: The addition of ICIs to anthracycline-based chemotherapy is associated with differential cardiovascular risk compared to anthracyclines alone in a real-world TNBC population. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (113 US healthcare organizations). Adults with TNBC receiving anthracyclines from 2019- 2025 were identified. Cohort 1 (anthracyclines + ICIs) and Cohort 2 (anthracyclines alone) underwent 1:1 propensity score matching on demographics, 14 comorbidities, cardiovascular medications, and laboratory values, achieving excellent balance (all standardized differences < 0.01). Nine incident cardiovascular outcomes were assessed: atrial fibrillation (AF), myocarditis, acute heart failure (AHF), stroke/TIA, ventricular arrhythmias (VA), acute MI, PE/DVT, cardiogenic shock (CS), and MACE. Cox proportional hazards regression generated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% CIs over a 5-year follow-up. Proportional hazards assumptions were verified using Schoenfeld residuals (all p>0.65). Results: After matching, 26,797 patients per group were analyzed (mean age 53.6 years, 98.7% female; median follow-up 2.5 years). No statistically significant differences were observed for any outcome. HRs (ICI vs. no-ICI): AHF 1.01 (95% CI 0.95-1.07, p=0.768); MACE 1.05 (0.97-1.15, p=0.216); acute MI 1.05 (0.90-1.22, p=0.539); PE/DVT 1.07 (0.96-1.19, p=0.218); stroke/TIA 1.07 (0.90-1.28, p=0.425); AF 1.10 (0.94-1.29, p=0.242); CS 1.12 (0.73-1.72, p=0.607); myocarditis 1.24 (0.60-2.59, p=0.559); VA 1.03 (0.78-1.36, p=0.843). Cumulative incidences were: AHF 7.81% vs 7.86%, MACE 4.34% vs 4.19%, PE/DVT 2.59% vs 2.45%, acute MI 1.24% vs 1.20%, AF 1.17% vs 1.08%, stroke/TIA 0.98% vs 0.94%, VA 0.37% vs 0.37%, CS 0.164% vs 0.149%, myocarditis 0.060% vs 0.049%. Kaplan-Meier curves demonstrated parallel trajectories throughout follow-up with no late divergence. Conclusions: In the largest real-world matched cohort studying this combination, ICIs added to anthracycline-based chemotherapy were not associated with significantly increased cardiovascular toxicity across all nine outcomes over intermediate-term follow-up. These findings provide important real-world validation beyond pivotal trial data, supporting guideline-concordant use of ICI combinations in TNBC without evidence of additive cardiotoxicity.
title: Abstract 8086: Cardiovascular Safety of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Combined with Anthracyclines in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: A Large Real-World Propensity-Matched Analysis

abstract: Introduction: U.S. adults living in rural areas have worse cardiovascular outcomes than those in urban areas. One contributing factor may be rural-urban differences in arrhythmia care. Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter (AF/AFL) increase cardioembolic stroke risk and can be diagnosed with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIED). The 2023 AHA/ACC AF guideline gives a Class 2a recommendation for oral anticoagulation (OAC) in CIED-detected AF/AFL ≥ 24 hours. Research Question: Does OAC prescription differ by rural vs. urban residence? Methods: This retrospective electronic health-record based study identified veteran patients with new CIED-detected AF/AFL ≥ 24 hours based on clinician adjudication from 1/1/2019 to 5/27/2025 in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Exclusion criteria encompassed recent significant bleeding, OAC prescription within past 180 days, cardiac surgery, or CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc < 2. Cumulative probabilities of OAC prescription were plotted using Kaplan-Meier curves with censoring for cessation of CIED remote monitoring or death. A multivariable Cox proportional hazard model was adjusted for demographics, clinical covariates, substance use, and medications, with a frailty term for VA facility. Results: Among 4,020 patients with new CIED-detected AF/AFL ≥ 24 hours across 126 facilities, 1,506 (37.5%) were rural and 2,514 (62.5%) were urban. Mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc was 4.55 in rural vs. 4.57 in urban patients. Rural patients were slightly younger (mean age 78.4 vs. 79.1 years) and more likely to have had myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft surgery than urban patients. Other comorbidities had similar rates between rural and urban patients. Over 1 year, 59.9% of rural vs. 56.2% of urban patients were prescribed OAC ( Figure ) with shorter median time to anticoagulation in rural vs. urban patients (156 vs. 206 days). In the adjusted Cox model, rurality was associated with a higher OAC prescription rate (hazard ratio [HR] 1.10, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.20). In patients with CIED-detected AF/AFL > 7 days ( n = 850), rural patients had higher OAC prescription rates than urban patients (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.47). There was no significant difference in the proportion of rural vs. urban patients prescribed a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) compared with warfarin (96.6% vs. 96.9%, p=0.83). Conclusion: In the national VHA, there were overall low rates of OAC prescription for patients with new CIED-detected AF/AFL ≥ 24 hours, although higher in rural vs. urban patients. Patient, clinic, and health care system factors should be investigated to improve OAC prescription.
title: Abstract 8105: Rural-Urban Differences in Oral Anticoagulation for Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device-Detected Atrial Fibrillation/Flutter ≥ 24 Hours

abstract: Introduction: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiovascular (CV), renal, and heart failure (HF) outcomes and are increasingly being evaluated in valvular heart disease. In patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), randomized and observational data suggest fewer HF events and improved composite clinical outcomes with SGLT2i therapy. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network comprising 112 healthcare organizations and more than 135 million patients. Adults 18 years or older undergoing isolated SAVR with nonrheumatic aortic stenosis (AS) from 2016 onward were included. Exclusions included rheumatic/congenital heart disease, endocarditis, end-stage renal disease/dialysis, kidney transplant, pregnancy, and same-day coronary bypass/other valve surgery. The exposure was SGLT2i use within 1 year before or after SAVR; comparators had no SGLT2i exposure. Outcomes were assessed from 30 to 365 days after SAVR. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity-score matched on demographics, comorbidities, medications, laboratory values, and cardiac function; Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses tested preoperative first-recorded SGLT2i use and 1-to-3-year follow-up. Results: The analysis included 706 exposed patients and 8,866 comparators; after matching, 539 remained per group. SGLT2i use was not associated with acute HF (8.5% vs 10.9%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.57-1.23), hospitalization/emergency department visit (34.9% vs 38.4%; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.81-1.21), composite CV events, defined as death, acute HF, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (17.6% vs 19.5%; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.73-1.27), mortality (2.2% vs 3.9%; HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.32-1.33), or acute kidney injury (6.1% vs 9.6%; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.44-1.05; Figure 1). In the preoperative analysis, 283 patients were matched per group; no consistent benefit was observed, although inpatient encounters were higher with SGLT2i exposure (22.3% vs 15.5%; HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.14-2.47). In the 1-to-3-year analysis, 269 patients were matched per group, with no significant differences. Conclusions: Among matched adults undergoing isolated SAVR with nonrheumatic AS, SGLT2i exposure within 1 year of surgery was not associated with significantly lower composite CV events, acute kidney injury, healthcare utilization, or mortality. These findings suggest that benefits reported after TAVR may not translate directly to SAVR and support prospective studies defining the timing and role of SGLT2i therapy in surgical valve populations.
title: Abstract 8124: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Outcomes After Isolated Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement

abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a non-atherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome typically managed conservatively; however, revascularization may be required in high-risk presentations with ongoing ischemia or compromised coronary flow. The optimal approach to percutaneous intervention in SCAD remains technically challenging due to the risk of dissection propagation and difficulty confirming true lumen access. A 40-year-old woman with a past medical history of hyperlipidemia, unprovoked deep vein thrombosis, lyme arthritis with lumbar radiculopathy and iron deficiency anemia presented with acute chest pain and was found to have an inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. She was transferred for emergent coronary angiography, which demonstrated SCAD involving the ostial to mid right coronary artery with impaired flow.Given ongoing ischemia and high-risk coronary anatomy, the decision was made to proceed with revascularization. The patient underwent successful intravascular ultrasound guided percutaneous coronary intervention with placement of overlapping drug-eluting stents, resulting in restoration of coronary perfusion. Procedural management required careful hemodynamic support and intravascular imaging to confirm true lumen wiring and appropriate stent placement, minimizing the risk of dissection propagation.Post procedural echocardiography obtained demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function without significant regional wall abnormalities. Her hospital course was notable for transient ventricular ectopy, including non-sustained ventricular tachycardia and accelerated idioventricular rhythm, which improved with beta-blocker titration. She remained hemodynamically stable without recurrent ischemia and was discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy with plans for cardiac rehabilitation, close outpatient follow up.This case highlights the role of intravascular ultrasound-guided intervention in select high risk SCAD presentations requiring revascularization. Careful use of intravascular imaging can facilitate safe and effective percutaneous coronary intervention. Additionally emphasizes the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary decision making in complex coronary dissections.
title: Abstract 8128: IVUS Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD) Presenting as STEMI

abstract: Introduction: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a challenging valvulopathy and has been associated with worse quality of life. This has spurred ongoing innovation in transcatheter tricuspid interventions. CIEDs, which are common in this population, remain a procedural difficulty. We present a case of successful 3D TEE-guided navigation around an ICD lead with multiple TriClip devices to treat severe TR. Case: A 67 year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 35%), ICD placed 13 years prior, ventricular tachycardia with an appropriate shock 1 year ago, atrial fibrillation, and bi-leaflet mitral valve prolapse with P2 flail underwent a Duran band annuloplasty and bi-atrial MAZE two years prior to presentation. He subsequently developed severe TR due to annular dilation and prolapse with worsening exertional dyspnea. His ICD lead was between the posterior-septal leaflets, but not tucked in the commissure (Figure 1). Due to his reduced EF and history of appropriate shock, ICD removal was not recommended. However, given his progressive symptoms despite medical management, the decision was made to attempt tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. Utilizing fluoroscopy, 3D TEE, and ICE, two XT TriClip G5 devices were placed immediately adjacent to each other and anterior to the lead along the anterior and septal leaflets. There was residual 2+ TR originating between the septal and posterior leaflets, so a third XT TriClip G5 was placed posterior to the lead, thereby entrapping it between the clips (Figure 2). The TR improved to trivial-1+ with a transvalvular gradient of 2mmHg and improved hemodynamics: blood pressure 98/64 to 110/75mmHg, right atrial (RA) pressure 16 to 15mmHg, RA V wave 20 to 12mmHg (Figure 3). At six-month follow-up his dyspnea had significantly improved and his TR remained 1+ with a gradient of 1mmHg. Conclusion: CIED leads are a frequent procedural challenge in many patients with symptomatic severe TR who are failing medical management. In these situations, transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement is sometimes considered, however, this involves jailing the CIED lead or performing lead extraction prior to the procedure. This case demonstrates that transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is a viable alternative therapeutic option, and that maintaining a central course of the CIED lead as opposed to a commissural location can result in clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic improvement. Multi-planar reconstruction with TEE is particularly helpful in guiding complex TriClip placement such as this.
title: Abstract 8138: Clipping Around the Lead - Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Thyroid storm is a serious complication of amiodarone therapy that may precipitate arrhythmias and acute decompensated heart failure. Typically, medical management is sufficient for amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis (AIT). We present a case of AIT refractory to medical management requiring plasmapheresis and total thyroidectomy prior to heart transplant. Presentation & Clinical Course: A 50-year-old male with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, cardiac resynchronization therapy, left ventricular thrombus on anticoagulation, ventricular tachycardia, and persistent atrial fibrillation on chronic amiodarone presented with acute decompensated heart failure. Lab work on admission was notable for thyroid-stimulating hormone below 0.010 uIU/mL and free T4 (FT4) was elevated at 5.02 ng/dL. These findings were consistent with hyperthyroidism thought to be secondary to AIT. He was started on treatment with methimazole and prednisone. His hospital course was complicated by recurrent supraventricular tachycardia. Given persistently elevated FT4 levels and frequent arrhythmias, his treatment regimen was escalated to propylthiouracil, potassium iodide, and hydrocortisone. He subsequently developed cardiogenic shock requiring Impella 5.5 support and underwent emergent atrioventricular nodal ablation for unstable persistent atrial fibrillation refractory to medical management and cardioversion. Despite maximum medical management of his thyroid disease, there was only a modest reduction in FT4 levels to 3.96 ng/dL and his clinical course was further complicated by ventricular arrhythmias. Therapeutic plasma exchange was initiated as a bridge to definitive thyroidectomy. There was a significant reduction in FT4 levels to 2.70 ng/dL after a single session of therapeutic plasma exchange, but further sessions were held due to challenges with volume management. The patient subsequently underwent total thyroidectomy, after which his hyperthyroidism resolved. He was unfortunately unable to be weaned from mechanical support and was listed for transplant. Less than two weeks later, he successfully underwent orthotopic heart transplant. Discussion: AIT is rare in North America but can lead to severe cardiac decompensation and increased arrhythmia burden. This case offers multiple clinical insights: 1) While AIT typically permits a treatment course spanning weeks to months, this patient with concomitant advanced heart failure did not tolerate this timeline. 2) Therapeutic plasma exchange may be used as a bridge to reduce arrythmia burden and improve thyroid hormone levers faster than medical therapy until thyroidectomy may be performed. 3) Thyroidectomy should be considered early in patients who fail medical therapy. In this case, it allowed for stabilization to the point that transplantation could be pursued.
title: Abstract 8139: Refractory Amiodarone-Induced Thyrotoxicosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy Requiring Total Thyroidectomy and Heart Transplant

abstract: Background: Global myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is an established prognostic marker in positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI), but may fail to detect localized coronary artery disease (CAD) or regional microvascular dysfunction. We investigated whether regional quantitative MFR provides incremental prognostic value beyond conventional PET-MPI findings and global MFR in patients undergoing rubidium-82 (Rb-82) and nitrogen-13 ammonia (N-13) PET-MPI from the REFINE-PET registry. Methods: We analyzed data from the multicenter international REFINE-PET registry, including 35,393 patients from 13 sites who underwent PET-MPI. Abnormal MFR was defined as global or regional MFR <2.0. Regional MFR was assessed in the left anterior descending (LAD), left circumflex (LCX), and right coronary artery (RCA) territories. Patients were classified into three groups: Group 1 (normal global and regional MFR; n=19,744), Group 2 (normal global MFR but abnormal regional MFR; n=3,089), and Group 3 (abnormal global and regional MFR; n=12,558). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) included all-cause mortality, nonfatal myocardial infarction, late revascularization (>90 days), and hospitalization for unstable angina. Results: Over a median follow-up of 4.0 ± 2.9 years, 9,903 patients (28.0%) experienced MACE. The highest event rate was observed in Group 3, followed by Group 2, whereas Group 1 had the lowest event rate (11.7%/year vs. 7.9%/year vs. 4.0%/year, respectively; p<0.001). Abnormal regional MFR in any vascular territory was independently associated with increased MACE risk after adjustment for clinical risk factors, global MFR, and ischemic total perfusion deficit (hazard ratio [HR] 1.33, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.24-1.42). Individual vessel territory analyses demonstrated similar associations with MACE (LAD: HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.25-1.41; LCX: HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.13-1.28; RCA: HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.18-1.33; all p<0.05). Conclusions: Abnormal regional MFR is an independent predictor of MACE in patients undergoing Rb-82 and N-13 PET-MPI. Incorporating regional MFR into PET-MPI interpretation may improve risk stratification beyond conventional global MFR assessment.
title: Abstract 8154: Prognostic Value of Abnormal Regional Myocardial Flow Reserve: Results from REFINE PET

abstract: Background: Transradial access is the standard for primary PCI in STEMI, offering lower bleeding and vascular complications than femoral access. However, rare but limb-threatening complications can occur when device entrapment leads to arterial injury. Case: A 60-year-old male with inferior STEMI underwent primary PCI via right radial access. The right coronary artery was a calcified vessel, so prepared with a small balloon to an NC balloon, but the stent would not cross the segment, even proximal to the lesion. Here, the stent got dislodged, and we were able to bring the stent back up to the radial sheath. The stent in the radial artery got compressed like a longitudinal stent deformity, and we were unable to pull it into our sheath even after upgrading the sheath. Percutaneous retrieval attempts caused a longitudinal radial artery tear with an expanding forearm hematoma and impending compartment syndrome. Emergent surgical exploration revealed complete radial artery avulsion with the entrapped stent protruding through the torn vessel end. The stent was removed surgically. The whole segment of the radial artery was non-salvagable; the segment was ligated and not grafted, because ulnar collateralization was normal and intact palmar arch on Doppler. Hence, the surgery team ligated the radial artery after confirming ulnar artery preoxygenation and circulation. No fasciotomy was required. Discussion: Stent entrapment during TRA is infrequent, but forceful traction on an undeployed stent in a small, spastic radial artery can cause full-thickness avulsion. An expanding hematoma with compartment threat mandates immediate surgical consultation. Radial artery ligation is safe and definitive when the ulnar collateral circulation is intact, thereby avoiding the need for complex reconstruction. Delayed recognition can lead to nerve injury, muscle necrosis, or limb loss. Conclusion: Complete radial artery avulsion from stent entrapment during transradial PCI is an exceptionally rare but catastrophic complication. Prompt recognition of an expanding hematoma with compartment threat; immediate surgical consultation; and decisive management, including radial artery ligation, when collateral circulation is intact, can preserve limb viability and functional outcome without complex reconstruction. Patient's hand movements were normal without any deficit on follow-up visits.
title: Abstract 8168: Radial Access Nightmare: Stent Entrapment, Arterial Tear and Surgical Salvage During Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

abstract: Post-operative atrial fibrillation (PoAF) is a prevalent complication of cardiac surgery. Given the multifactorial nature of PoAF, there is growing interest in a multimodal pharmacologic approach that targets multiple underlying mechanisms, including sympathetic activation, inflammation, and atrial remodeling. This study aims to compare the effectiveness and tolerability of a 2-drug regimen versus a 5-drug regimen in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. This was an observational, single-center, institutional review board approved, retrospective cohort study at New York University Langone Health from August 1, 2023 to July 31, 2024. The study included adult patients who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), with or without aortic valve replacement or repair. Eligible patients received either a standard regimen of amiodarone and metoprolol, or a five-drug regimen of amiodarone, metoprolol, colchicine, spironolactone, and methylprednisolone during the post-operative period. The primary outcome of the incidence of PoAF from the time of surgery to day of discharge, occurred in 12 (16.7%) patients in the 5-drug regimen group compared to 21 (41.2%) patients in the 2-drug regimen group (P=0.003). The median time to PoAF did not differ significantly between the 2 groups (5-drug regimen: 2 days [IQR 1-2.75] vs 2-drug regimen: 2 days [IQR 1-2.5], P=0.421). On the univariate analysis, predictors of PoAF included age greater than 65 years old, history of chronic kidney disease, postoperative vasopressor utilization after surgery use, initiation of metoprolol more than 24 hours after surgery, and hospital lengths of stay longer greater than 5 days. These variables were included as covariates in the multivariate analysis. Age greater than 65 was the only factor that independently increased risk of PoAF (OR 2.6, CI 1.0-6.8; P=0.048) . This study provides the first direct comparison of a 2-drug versus a 5-drug pharmacological strategy for PoAF prevention in patients undergoing CABG with or without AVR, demonstrating a significant reduction in PoAF incidence with the multidrug approach. These findings are consistent with the emerging evidence base supporting mechanistically diverse, multifaceted prophylactic strategies and align with the multidisciplinary consensus favoring individualized, protocol-driven PoAF prevention.
title: Abstract 8170: The Power of Five: Multimodal Pharmacologic Prophylaxis for Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery

abstract: Background: Post-infarction ventricular septal rupture (PIVSR) is a rare mechanical complication of myocardial infarction with high early mortality. Although Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock staging is widely used for cardiogenic shock risk stratification, its prognostic validity has not been established in PIVSR, a distinct mechanical shock phenotype. Research Question: We evaluated the prognostic performance of SCAI shock staging and SCAI-defined pre-intervention shock progression for in-hospital mortality in patients with PIVSR. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective prognostic validation study of 80 patients with PIVSR who had available intervention-day SCAI stage and known in-hospital vital status. SCAI stage was assessed at admission, as maximum pre-intervention stage, and on the day of intervention. Because of sparse strata in stages B and E, intervention-day SCAI was analyzed both as individual stages and grouped as A/B, C, and D/E. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Mortality gradients were assessed across SCAI groups using Fisher’s exact test. SCAI stage was modeled as an ordinal variable to estimate the odds ratio for death per 1-stage increase. Discrimination was assessed using the receiver-operating characteristic analysis. Pre-intervention shock progression was defined as maximum pre-intervention SCAI stage greater than admission SCAI stage. Age-adjusted logistic regression was performed as a robustness analysis. Results: Overall in-hospital mortality was 52.5% (42/80). Intervention-day SCAI stage distribution was A in 30 patients (37.5%), B in 2 (2.5%), C in 19 (23.8%), D in 24 (30.0%), and E in 5 (6.3%). Mortality increased stepwise across grouped intervention-day SCAI stages: 12.5% in A/B, 57.9% in C, and 93.1% in D/E (p<0.001). Each 1-stage increase in intervention-day SCAI stage was associated with higher odds of in-hospital death (OR 4.01, 95% CI 2.50-7.27; p<0.001), with strong discrimination for mortality (AUC 0.882, 95% CI 0.803-0.947). This association persisted after age adjustment (adjusted OR 4.22, 95% CI 2.53-8.07; p<0.001). Discrimination was also strong for admission SCAI stage and maximum pre-intervention SCAI stage, with AUCs of 0.827 (95% CI 0.730-0.907) and 0.891 (95% CI 0.818-0.950), respectively. Pre-intervention shock progression occurred in 33 patients (41.3%) and was associated with increased in-hospital mortality compared with no progression (OR 5.39, 95% CI 1.86-17.12; p<0.001), including after age adjustment (adjusted OR 5.97, 95% CI 2.18-18.16; p<0.001). Conclusions: In patients with PIVSR, SCAI shock staging demonstrated strong prognostic validity for in-hospital mortality. Serial SCAI assessment may help identify patients with pre-intervention deterioration who are at particularly high risk of early death.
title: Abstract 8172: Prognostic Validation of SCAI Shock Staging in Post-Infarction Ventricular Septal Rupture

abstract: Background: Bolus and continuous thermodilution are two invasive techniques used to assess the coronary microcirculation and diagnose coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD). Bolus thermodilution derives coronary flow reserve (CFR) and the index of microvascular resistance (IMR) from resting and hyperemic transit times, with hyperemia induced by intravenous adenosine; continuous thermodilution uses steady saline infusion to measure absolute coronary flow and microvascular resistance, yielding CFR and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR). Because these methods rest on distinct physiologic assumptions, their diagnostic concordance and the physiological patterns underlying discordance remain incompletely defined. Research Question: What is the frequency of concordance and discordance of bolus and continuous thermodilution-derived measures in diagnosing CMD? What, if any, clinical and physiologic features distinguish concordant from discordant phenotypes? Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing clinically indicated invasive coronary physiology assessment for angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) between August 2023 and December 2025 were retrospectively included at a single center. All procedures were performed by a single experienced operator. Paired bolus and continuous thermodilution were performed in the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery during the same procedure. CMD was defined as CFR < 2.5. Patients were classified into four mutually exclusive phenotypes: concordant normal, concordant abnormal, Discordant A (abnormal bolus CFR with preserved continuous CFR) and Discordant B (preserved bolus CFR with abnormal continuous CFR). Continuous variables are reported as medians [IQR]. Results: Among the 148 patients included, there was a weak correlation (r=0.34) between bolus- and continuous-derived CFR. Concordance was noted in 103 (70%): 74 (50%) normal, 29 (20%) abnormal. Discordance was observed in 45 (30%): 17 (11%) Discordant A, 28 (19%) Discordant B. Traditional cardiovascular risk factors were not predictive of discordance, with the exception of older age (p=0.006); continuous thermodilution-derived CFR was lower in discordant patients (p=0.010), whereas bolus-derived CFR did not differ. Neither fractional flow reserve nor myocardial bridging accounted for discordant physiologic phenotypes, consistent with a microcirculatory rather than epicardial mechanism. Conclusions: Bolus and continuous coronary thermodilution were discordant in nearly one-third of patients with ANOCA. Discordance was not explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors, fractional flow reserve, or myocardial bridging, and was associated only with older age and lower continuous thermodilution-derived CFR. Further study of the mechanisms and clinical significance of thermodilution discordance is needed.
title: Abstract 8209: Discordance Between Bolus and Continuous Coronary Thermodilution in Patients with Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries

abstract: Introduction: Aortic regurgitation (AR) is associated with more severe aortic wall degeneration compared to aortic stenosis (AS). Long-term risk of adverse aortic events following an isolated aortic valve replacement (AVR) in patients with aortic regurgitation (AR) compared with aortic stenosis (AS) has not been previously explored. Hypothesis: Adverse aortic events (defined as a composite of aortic dissection or rupture, aortic-related death or need for thoracic aortic surgery) are more common in patients undergoing AVR due to AR compared to AS. Methods: All patients undergoing isolated surgical AVR in Sweden from 1997 to 2022 were included in a nationwide, population-based observational cohort study. Individual patient data were collected from the national SWEDEHEART registry, the National Patient Register and National Cause of Death Register. Patients were classified by aortic valve disease (AS, AS/AR or AR). Primary outcomes were first-ever adverse aortic events. Outcomes were analysed using time-to-event methods including Cox proportional hazard model adjusted for age and sex and absolute risk was estimated using cumulative incidence function, treating death as a competing event. Sensitivity analyses were performed in patients included between 2019–2022 due to available valve morphology. Results: A total of 24,905 patients with AS (median (IQR) age at surgery 73 (67-78), 61% males) were compared with 4916 patients with AS/AR (age 72 (63-77), 66% males) and with 3525 patients with AR (age 65 (54-73), 83% males). The primary outcome occurred in 237 (1.0%) with AS and in 79 (1.6%) patients with AS/AR and in 109 (3.1%) patients with AR. Compared with AS, AR was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.34, 95% CI 1.83–3.00; p<0.001). Accounting for competing mortality, cumulative incidence differed significantly between groups (Gray’s test p<0.001); at 5, 10, and 20 years, cumulative incidence was highest in AR patients (1.6%, 2.3%, and 5.4%), compared with AS (0.5%, 0.9%, and 1.3%). In the sensitivity analysis, AR remained associated with increased risk of the primary outcome after adjustment for bicuspid aortic valve, age and sex ([aHR] 4.54, 95% CI 1.16-17.84, p=0.030). Conclusions: Patients undergoing isolated AVR due to AR have a substantially higher risk of adverse aortic events after surgery compared to AS, even after accounting for competing mortality.
title: Abstract 8214: Incidence of Adverse Aortic Events After Isolated Aortic Valve Replacement - Long Term Results Comparing Aortic Regurgitation with Aortic Stenosis

abstract: Background: Residual lipoprotein-attributable cardiovascular (CV) risk persists despite statin therapy in individuals with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Apolipoprotein B (apoB) is a biomarker of the amount of LDL, triglyceride (TG)-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) in plasma. However, as these lipoproteins differ in atherogenic potential, it may not be the optimal biomarker of residual risk. For example, Lp(a) is a minor contributor to apoB concentration but a strong predictor of CV risk. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB) accounts for differing lipoprotein particle atherogenicity and may thereby improve risk stratification and prediction of benefit from lipid-lowering therapy. Research Question: We compared baseline RW-apoB with unweighted apoB and Lp(a) as predictors of residual risk and the magnitude of treatment benefit from PCSK9 inhibition. Methods: This was a post hoc analysis of the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trial that evaluated the benefit of PCSK9 inhibitor treatment in 18,924 patients with recent ACS on optimized statin therapy who were randomized to alirocumab or placebo and followed for a median of 2.8 years. The primary outcome was a composite of coronary heart disease death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal/nonfatal ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina. Based on prior published derivation and validation studies, RW-apoB (mg/dL) was calculated as 0.132 x TG (mg/dL) + 0.215 x Lp(a) (nmol/L) + 0.736хapoB (mg/dL) in 11,957 participants with available measurements. In the placebo arm univariable Cox models assessed the ability of baseline Lp(a), apoB and RW-apoB to predict CV risk. Multivariable models assessed if apoB or Lp(a) provided additional prediction beyond RW-apoB. Spline from unadjusted Cox models evaluated the relationship between baseline biomarkers (percentiles) and CV risk in the placebo arm and absolute risk reduction (ARR) on alirocumab. Results: RW-apoB at baseline correlated with apoB but was on average 20 mg/dL higher. ( Panel A ) In the placebo arm, RW-ApoB identified residual CV risk better than apoB or Lp(a) (higher C index). In multivariable Cox models, RW-apoB remained associated with CV event rate after adjusting for apoB (P≤0.0001). Lp(a) provided no additional prognostic information beyond RW-ApoB. ( Panel B ) Spline fits showed that RW-apoB gave the steepest risk gradient and most effectively identified subjects with the greatest ARR. This was driven largely by the ability of RW-apoB to incorporate the contribution of Lp(a)-associated risk which was mitigated by alirocumab. RW-apoB gave a consistent upward gradient across its full range compared with the other lipid markers ( Panel C ), with an ARR ranging from 0.5 to 4%. Conclusions: In statin-treated patients with recent ACS, RW-apoB outperformed apoB and Lp(a) in predicting residual risk in the placebo arm and in identifying the treatment benefit of alirocumab.
title: Abstract 8221: Risk-Weighted apoB Outperforms Unweighted apoB or Lipoprotein(a) as a Biomarker of Residual Cardiovascular Risk After Acute Coronary Syndrome and the Benefit of Alirocumab Therapy

abstract: Background: The international Small Annuli Randomized To Evolut or SAPIEN Trial (SMART, NCT04722250; Medtronic funded) compares performance of the Evolut self-expanding valve and the SAPIEN balloon-expandable valve in TAVR patients with severe aortic stenosis and small aortic annuli (SAA). These patients, predominantly women (87%), are at higher risk for adverse hemodynamics post TAVR. Through 12 months, women in SMART had similar clinical outcomes with both devices but significantly lower bioprosthetic valve dysfunction (BVD) with Evolut. Research Question: At 3 years, do clinical and hemodynamic outcomes differ in women with SAA who undergo TAVR with Evolut vs SAPIEN? Methods: Key eligibility criteria included aortic valve annulus area ≤430 mm 2 by CT and anatomy suitable for transfemoral TAVR with either Evolut PRO/PRO+/FX or SAPIEN 3/3 Ultra valves. Coprimary endpoints include a clinical outcome composite of death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization, and composite endpoint for BVD, both at 1 year. Patients are being followed for 5 years. Three-year outcomes in women are reported here. Results: A total of 621 women underwent attempted TAVR (312 Evolut, 309 SAPIEN) at 81 sites. Mean age was 80.2±6.2 years, mean STS score was 3.4±1.8%, and mean aortic annulus area was 378.7±34.2 mm 2 . At 3 years, the clinical composite outcome remained similar between Evolut and SAPIEN (25.5% vs 23.3%, log-rank P =0.61), while the BVD composite remained significantly lower for Evolut (16.4% vs 55.3%, P <0.001). Additional 3-year outcomes showed similar rates between Evolut and SAPIEN for reintervention (0.7% vs 1.1%, P =0.66) and ≥ mild total aortic regurgitation (16.2% vs 23.5%, P =0.07), but women with Evolut had lower rates of VARC-3 prosthetic valve thrombosis (1.5% vs 6.6%, P =0.002) and maintained lower mean gradient (8.5±5.1 vs 15.9±7.2 mmHg, P <0.001) and larger effective orifice area (1.90±0.48 vs 1.51±0.38 cm 2 , P <0.001). KCCQ Overall Summary Score remained similar between groups (Evolut 78.5±21.3 vs SAPIEN 79.3±19.6, p=0.66). An exploratory analysis of PPM in women will also be presented. Conclusions: In the SMART trial, 3-year clinical outcomes were similar in women treated with Evolut or SAPIEN. However, women with Evolut had significantly lower rates of BVD and thrombosis and better hemodynamic outcomes than those with SAPIEN. These findings underscore Evolut’s hemodynamic advantage and the importance of continued follow-up through 5 years.
title: Abstract 8223: Three-Year Outcomes for Women in the the Five-Year SMART Trial

abstract: Background: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) is a less invasive alternative to Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement (SAVR) for the treatment of aortic stenosis (AS). Following FDA approval for low-risk patients in 2019 and incorporation into the 2020 valvular heart disease guidelines, utilization of TAVR has expanded. Coronary artery evaluation is a standard component of pre-procedural assessment for both TAVR and SAVR, and concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD) often necessitates Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) or Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG), respectively. Methods: Using ICD-10 codes, we queried the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2016-2023 to identify hospitalizations for AS undergoing either TAVR+PCI or SAVR+CABG. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included complications and resource utilization measures. Outcomes were also compared between the pre- and post-2020 eras following expansion of TAVR to low-risk patients. Survey-weighted (SVY) analysis was performed for national estimates, and propensity score matching (PSM) analysis was used to reduce selection bias. Results: A total of 15,944 unweighted hospitalizations met inclusion criteria, including 12,184 (76.4%) undergoing SAVR + CABG and 3,760 (23.6%) undergoing TAVR + PCI. Utilization of TAVR+PCI increased from 15.9% in 2016 to 30.8% in 2023, particularly in the post-2020 era, while SAVR+CABG utilization declined from 84.1% in 2016 to 69.2% in 2023. In SVY analysis, TAVR+PCI was associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with SAVR+CABG (aOR 0.44, 95% CI 0.32-0.60, p<0.001). TAVR+PCI was additionally associated with lower odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 0.34), PRBC transfusion (aOR 0.21), mechanical ventilation (MV) (aOR 0.37), vasopressor use (aOR 0.28), and facility discharge (aOR 0.16), along with significantly shorter length of stay (LOS) (aGMR 0.46) and lower total hospitalization charges (TOTCHG) (aGMR 0.96) (all p<0.05). Stroke and cardiac arrest were similar between groups. However, TAVR+PCI was associated with greater odds of permanent pacemaker implantation (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.27-1.82, p<0.001). Findings remained consistent following PSM analysis, which included 15,261 hospitalizations. Era-based interaction analysis demonstrated consistent treatment effects over time, with significant interaction observed for MV, LOS, and TOTCHG. Conclusions: TAVR+PCI was associated with lower in-hospital mortality, fewer peri-procedural complications, shorter LOS, and more favorable discharge disposition compared with SAVR+CABG. Following expansion of TAVR to low-risk patients, utilization of transcatheter strategies increased substantially. These findings support the growing role of less invasive transcatheter approaches in appropriately selected patients with AS and concomitant CAD.
title: Abstract 8247: National Trends and In-Hospital Outcomes of TAVR+PCI Versus SAVR+CABG in Aortic Stenosis: Impact of the Low-Risk TAVR Era

abstract: Background: Global longitudinal strain (GLS) is an established marker of subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in aortic stenosis (AS), providing prognostic information independent of left ventricular ejection fraction. Speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) is the reference modality, but suboptimal acoustic windows limit its application in a substantial fraction of AS patients. Cardiac CT, already obtained routinely in pre-procedural AS workup, may serve as an alternative source of functional information — yet the agreement between CT-derived and STE-derived GLS remains uncertain. Hypothesis: CT-GLS correlates strongly with STE-GLS in AS and may serve as a complementary functional assessment. Methods: We performed a systematic review of PubMed and Embase (through January 2026) for studies reporting paired CT-GLS and STE-GLS in adults with AS. Pooled Pearson correlation (Fisher's z transformation) and mean differences (|CT-GLS|–|STE-GLS|; standard errors back-calculated from Bland-Altman limits of agreement) were estimated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses included leave-one-out and stratification by analytical software workflow. Results: Five studies met inclusion criteria (n=536; mean age 78-84 years; 44-61% female; pre- and post-TAVI severe AS cohorts). The pooled correlation between CT-GLS and STE-GLS was strong (r=0.75; 95% CI 0.67-0.82; I 2 =69%), unchanged by exclusion of any single study (range 0.73-0.79; all p<0.001), indicating that both modalities rank patients similarly. The pooled mean difference showed a non-significant trend toward CT underestimation of GLS magnitude (–1.00%; 95% CI –3.15 to +1.15; p=0.36), with the notable particularity that four studies using different software platforms for CT and STE underestimated GLS (sensitivity pooled MD excluding the outlier: –2.06%; 95% CI –2.75 to –1.37; p<0.001), while the single study using identical vendor-independent software for both modalities overestimated it (+3.3%). Inter-modality bias may therefore relate to software/vendor differences, although other unmeasured factors likely contribute. Conclusions: CT-derived GLS correlates strongly with STE-GLS in aortic stenosis, supporting its potential utility as a complementary functional marker. Because inter-modality bias appears clinically relevant and may relate to analytical software, CT-GLS values should be interpreted using software-specific reference ranges rather than treated as directly interchangeable with STE-GLS. These findings support an expanding role of cardiac CT in AS, complementing anatomic assessment with quantitative myocardial function.
title: Abstract 8257: Computed Tomography versus Speckle-Tracking Echocardiographic Global Longitudinal Strain in Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Primary cardiac tumors are rare and may present significant diagnostic challenges when benign and malignant etiologies share overlapping features. We present a case of metastatic synovial sarcoma initially suspected to be cardiac myxoma and Carney complex. Case Presentation: A 21-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with subacute diffuse subdermal nodules of limbs and torso. He developed disequilibrium and left arm weakness and was found to have an acute ischemic stroke on imaging. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a large 4.7х3.7cm mobile mass fixed to the anterior mitral valve leaflet with prolapse into left ventricle, concerning for tumor or thrombus. Femur imaging showed a large 9.2cm hemorrhagic mass of the lateral vastus musculature. While awaiting cardiac MRI, he developed hematemesis and melena with hemodynamic instability requiring superior mesenteric artery embolization. Upper endoscopy identified a jejunal mass, subsequently resected with initial pathology suggested myxoma. Carney complex was initially suspected given the combination of cardiac, bowel, and dermal myxomatous tumors. However, PRKAR1A testing was inconclusive, and ultimately immunochemistry SS18 SSX fusion diagnosed synovial sarcoma. Cardiac MRI revealed multiple intracardiac masses, the largest attached to the anterior mitral valve leaflet. Cardiothoracic surgical exploration identified additional epicardial lesions, prompting extensive intra- and extra-cardiac tumor resection and mechanical mitral valve replacement. Surveillance echocardiography two months later demonstrated new, recurrent intracardiac disease, prompting initiation of anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Discussion: To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of metastatic stage IV synovial sarcoma presenting with concurrent cardiac and gastrointestinal tumors resulting in stroke and gastrointestinal bleeding, respectively. Definitive diagnosis and management required multimodality imaging, surgical exploration, and specialized immunochemical testing demonstrating an SS18 SSX fusion after initial pathology and genetic evaluation proved inconclusive. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis for intracardiac masses and illustrates how stepwise integration of history, imaging, pathology, genetics, and multidisciplinary expertise can establish the correct diagnosis and guide timely complex, multidisciplinary management. Learning Points: Metastatic synovial sarcoma may mimic cardiac myxoma and syndromic myxomatous disorders. Diagnostic uncertainty should prompt consideration of specialized molecular testing and multidisciplinary evaluation. Multimodality imaging and coordinated surgical, oncologic, and cardio-oncologic management are essential for optimizing outcomes.
title: Abstract 8264: Metastatic Synovial Sarcoma Masquerading as Atrial Myxoma: A Multimodal Diagnostic Challenge Following Cardioembolic Ischemic Stroke and Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage

abstract: Background: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent cardiovascular risk factor with prothrombotic, pro-inflammatory, and pro-atherogenic properties. Its prognostic role following PCI and its utility in identifying patients who may benefit from prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remain incompletely characterized. Research Question/Hypothesis: Elevated Lp(a) (≥30 mg/dL) is independently associated with adverse post-PCI outcomes and may identify patients deriving preferential benefit from prolonged DAPT (>1 year). Methods: We conducted a systematic review of observational studies reporting cardiovascular outcomes in PCI patients stratified by Lp(a) level (elevated defined as ≥30 mg/dL). Eligible studies enrolled adults undergoing PCI with drug-eluting or bare-metal stents, measured Lp(a) at baseline, and reported at least one pre-specified outcome: MACE, MI, stroke/TIA, all-cause mortality, CV mortality, repeat revascularization, stent restenosis, or major bleeding. DAPT-stratified analyses (≤1 year vs. >1 year) were separately synthesized. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Results: Eleven studies encompassing 49,310 patients were included (7 prospective, 4 retrospective), with elevated Lp(a) prevalence ranging from 21.3% to 56.2% across cohorts. Among elevated Lp(a) patients, the pooled MACE event rate was 21.7% (range 2.0-71.4%) across 8 studies, with higher rates in STEMI and in-stent restenosis populations. The pooled MI rate was 5.0% (range 0.8-14.3%, 7 studies), all-cause mortality was 7.7% (range 1.1-16.7%, 7 studies), CV mortality was 4.6% (range 0.8-7.5%, 5 studies), repeat revascularization was 13.9% (range 2.4-22.3%, 5 studies), and stent restenosis was 5.0% (range 1.7-12.1%, 3 studies).In 3 DAPT-stratified analyses among elevated Lp(a) patients, prolonged DAPT (>1 year) was associated with lower MACE rates vs. standard duration (≤1 year): 1.2-1.6% vs. 2.0-3.8%, an absolute reduction of 1.1-2.2%. All-cause mortality was markedly lower with prolonged DAPT: 0.1-0.2% vs. 1.8-2.3%, an absolute reduction of 1.7-2.1%. CV mortality followed a similar pattern: 0.0-0.1% vs. 1.1-1.3%, an absolute reduction of 1.1-1.2%. Major bleeding was higher with prolonged DAPT: 1.2-1.4% vs. 0.7-1.9%, an absolute excess of 0.5-0.6%. All DAPT-stratified analyses were single-center. Risk of bias was low in 7 of 11 studies. Conclusions: Elevated Lp(a) (≥30 mg/dL) was associated with adverse post-PCI outcomes across 11 observational studies. In DAPT-stratified analyses, prolonged DAPT in elevated Lp(a) patients was associated with absolute mortality reductions markedly exceeding the absolute bleeding excess. Lp(a) measurement may inform post-PCI risk stratification and antiplatelet therapy duration decisions. Prospective randomized trials incorporating Lp(a)-guided DAPT strategies are warranted.
title: Abstract 8283: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) and Adverse Outcomes Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review with DAPT Duration Analysis

abstract: Introduction: The backward expansion wave (BEW), generated during myocardial relaxation, reflects decompression of the intramyocardial vasculature and the suction effect that accelerates coronary flow in early diastole. Wave intensity analysis quantifies this phenomenon from simultaneous coronary pressure and velocity measurements, limiting clinical applicability. We introduce velocity-derived BEWI Reserve, defined as the ratio of hyperemic to resting backward expansion wave intensity, as a pressure-free index of coronary wave dynamics and vasodilatory reserve. Hypothesis: Velocity-derived BEWI Reserve can be estimated from coronary velocity waveforms without pressure input and shows stronger association with fractional flow reserve (FFR) than coronary flow reserve (CFR). Methods: We analyzed 838 coronary pressure-velocity recordings from 332 subjects (age 67 ± 10 years, 75.3% male, DFLOW dataset). A Random Forest regression model was trained using a subject-level 60/40 train-test split to predict BEWI Reserve from velocity-derived Fourier spectral features, without pressure input. Association with FFR was quantified by Spearman rank correlation with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and FFR stratification across velocity-derived BEWI Reserve tertiles was evaluated by Kruskal-Wallis test. Results: In the held-out test population (133 subjects, 316 waveforms), velocity-derived BEWI Reserve showed a stronger Spearman correlation with FFR (ρ = 0.244, 95% CI [0.139, 0.348]) than CFR (ρ = 0.097, 95% CI [–0.031, 0.216]), shown in figure 1. Stratification by velocity-derived BEWI Reserve tertile revealed significant FFR gradients (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001) with significant pairwise differences between Low and Mid and Low and High tertiles (figure 2). Conclusions: Velocity-derived BEWI Reserve provides a pressure-free, wave-intensity-based index of coronary physiology that is more strongly associated with FFR than CFR and significantly stratifies FFR in a held-out test population. These findings support velocity-based WIA as a mechanistically grounded and clinically accessible framework for coronary functional assessment.
title: Abstract 8284: Velocity-Based Backward Expansion Wave Intensity Reserve Assesses Coronary Physiologic Function

abstract: Background: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is an established noninvasive modality for evaluating suspected coronary artery disease (CAD). However, the real-world downstream impact of integrating CT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) into CCTA-based triage pathways remains under active investigation. We evaluated whether FFR-CT use after CCTA was associated with improved risk stratification, downstream procedural yield, resource utilization, and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes compared with CCTA alone. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global federated research network. Adult patients from 111 healthcare organizations who underwent CCTA between September 1, 2020, and February 9, 2026, were identified. Patients were stratified into two cohorts: CCTA followed by FFR-CT within 7 days and CCTA alone. Propensity score matching in a 1:1 ratio was performed to balance baseline demographics, comorbidities, and cardiovascular risk profiles, yielding 15,406 patients in each cohort. Clinical endpoints, downstream testing, invasive procedures, and resource utilization were assessed from day 8 through day 365 after the index CCTA. Results: After propensity matching, patients who underwent FFR-CT demonstrated higher rates of downstream invasive coronary angiography compared with CCTA alone, 21.3% versus 12.7%, respectively; RR 1.675, 95% CI 1.591-1.763, p < 0.001. The FFR-CT cohort also had higher rates of percutaneous coronary intervention, 7.4% versus 4.0%; RR 1.858, 95% CI 1.689-2.044, p < 0.001, and coronary artery bypass grafting, 2.8% versus 1.9%; RR 1.439, 95% CI 1.243-1.666, p < 0.001. In contrast, repeat noninvasive stress testing was significantly lower in the FFR-CT cohort, 4.9% versus 9.2%; RR 0.533, 95% CI 0.489-0.580, p < 0.001. At 1 year, FFR-CT use was associated with lower rates of major adverse cardiac events, 7.0% versus 9.2%; RR 0.762, 95% CI 0.707-0.823, p < 0.001, acute myocardial infarction, 3.4% versus 4.4%; RR 0.771, 95% CI 0.689-0.863, p < 0.001, and all-cause mortality, 1.1% versus 2.2%; RR 0.503, 95% CI 0.418-0.605, p < 0.001. The FFR-CT cohort had modestly higher rates of short emergency department encounters and cardiovascular hospitalizations. Conclusion: In this large real-world propensity-matched cohort, FFR-CT integration after CCTA was associated with increased downstream invasive evaluation and revascularization, reduced repeat noninvasive stress testing, and significantly lower 1-year rates of MACE, acute myocardial infarction, and all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that FFR-CT may improve CCTA-based care triage by identifying patients with clinically actionable CAD while reducing redundant noninvasive testing. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm whether these observed associations translate into causal improvements in long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
title: Abstract 8285: Real-World Outcomes of FFR-CT Integration After Coronary CT Angiography for Suspected Coronary Artery Disease

abstract: Introduction: Massive pulmonary embolism (MPE) is a rare but deadly cause of cardiac arrest with an estimated mortality of 64-74%. 1,2,3,4 Survival improves with systemic thrombolytics, with 30-day mortality decreasing to 6% compared with 16% without. 5 Alteplase (tPA) is currently the only FDA-approved thrombolytic for MPE. Although not approved, Tenecteplase (TNK) offers favorable pharmacologic characteristics for MPE. We present a case of successful thrombolysis with TNK for MPE complicated by cardiac arrest. Case presentation: A previously healthy 39-year-old male presented to the emergency department with chest pain and dyspnea following several days of right lower extremity pain. On arrival, he was tachycardic, hypotensive, and hypoxic. Given concern for MPE, he was sent for urgent CTA. While in CT, he deteriorated into PEA cardiac arrest. ACLS was initiated with ROSC after one round; however, he remained in obstructive shock. CTA revealed MPE and right heart strain (Figure 1). 50 mg TNK was administered at 11 minutes, and again at 23 minutes due to continued hemodynamic instability. He was subsequently transferred to the ICU. Repeat CTA 48 hours after cardiac arrest demonstrated near full resolution of thrombus in the proximal main pulmonary artery (Figure 2). Over the next 24 hours, the patient’s shock improved. No bleeding or neurological complications were observed. On hospital day 4, he was discharged on Apixaban with minimal shortness of breath. His symptoms have since completely been resolved. Discussion: Thrombolytics play an essential role in the management of MPE. tPA is administered as a 100 mg infusion over 2 hours. Its short half-life of 4-5 minutes necessitates extended infusion to allow for intravascular accumulation. Thrombolytic effects of tPA progressively accumulate throughout the infusion period with an estimated initial response at 30 minutes and peak plasma concentration at 60 minutes. 6,7 In contrast, TNK has a half-life of 20-24 minutes allowing for administration as a single weight-based bolus for over 5-10 seconds, and peak plasma concentrations are achieved rapidly with an initial thrombolytic response in 11 minutes. 8 TNK is not well studied in MPE, but is FDA-approved for treatment of STEMI and ischemic stroke. It is therefore reasonable to consider TNK for MPE to facilitate faster thrombolysis and hemodynamic improvement. Conclusion: MPE remains a rare but lethal clinical entity, for which systemic thrombolysis is a key therapeutic strategy. While tPA is the only FDA-approved thrombolytic for MPE, TNK offers advantageous pharmacokinetics and administrative ease. However, TNK use in MPE is off-label, and further studies are needed to establish whether TNK offers clinical benefits over tPA for MPE.
title: Abstract 8311: Cardiac Arrest Due to Massive Pulmonary Embolism Successfully Treated with Tenecteplase

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) and oral anticoagulation (OAC) are established options for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, but comparative evidence across contemporary LAAC devices and OAC strategies remains limited. Hypothesis: We evaluated whether percutaneous LAAC devices, surgical LAAC, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), or no anticoagulation differ in efficacy or safety for stroke prevention in adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through March 30, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC devices, DOACs, VKAs, or no anticoagulation were eligible for network meta-analysis; single-arm studies were summarized descriptively for safety. Primary outcomes were stroke/systemic embolism and major bleeding. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed using netmeta in R. Results: Twenty studies, including 18 randomized controlled trials and 2 single-arm registries, enrolled 71,802 participants. For stroke/systemic embolism, 11 trials contributed to the network. No intervention differed significantly from DOACs or from each other. Compared with DOACs, point estimates were RR 0.83 (95% CI, 0.18-3.74) for Amplatzer Amulet and RR 1.01 (95% CI, 0.27-3.85) for Watchman FLX; however, precision was low, and heterogeneity was severe (I 2 =98.6%). For major bleeding, 8 trials contributed to the network. Watchman FLX was associated with lower major bleeding than DOACs (RR 0.65; 95% CI, 0.46-0.90), whereas VKAs were associated with higher major bleeding than DOACs (RR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.06-1.55). Conclusion: In randomized evidence synthesized by network meta-analysis, contemporary LAAC devices did not show a statistically significant difference in stroke/systemic embolism compared with DOACs, but estimates were imprecise and limited by extreme heterogeneity. Watchman FLX was associated with lower major bleeding than DOACs. LAAC may be a reasonable alternative for selected patients at increased bleeding risk, while individualized decision-making remains essential.
title: Abstract 8318: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Left Atrial Appendage Closure Devices and Oral Anticoagulation Strategies for Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Introduction: Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) affects more than half of patients undergoing elective coronary angiography for suspected ischemia. Invasive physiologic testing has been proposed to clarify underlying mechanisms and guide management, yet its real-world impact on downstream clinical outcomes remains uncertain. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that invasive physiologic testing at the time of coronary angiography would be associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with angiography alone. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18 years or older with angina pectoris or chest pain who underwent coronary angiography without revascularization. Patients with percutaneous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass grafting, or acute myocardial infarction were excluded. The exposure cohort underwent CPT-defined invasive physiologic testing (CPT 93571-93572); the comparator cohort underwent angiography without physiologic testing. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 8,340 patients were retained in each cohort. Primary outcomes were repeat coronary angiography, all-cause mortality, and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included recurrent chest pain, repeat noninvasive ischemia testing, anti-anginal initiation or intensification, and ventricular arrhythmias. Time-to-event analyses generated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: Cohorts were well balanced after matching (mean age 65.0 years; 35.1% female). Physiologic testing was associated with higher repeat coronary angiography (25.0% vs 23.2%; HR 1.096, 95% CI 1.030-1.166; p=0.004). All-cause mortality (11.5% vs 11.5%; HR 1.004; p=0.926) and heart failure hospitalization (31.4% vs 31.6%; HR 0.987; p=0.636) were similar between groups. Among secondary outcomes, recurrent chest pain (HR 1.060; p=0.007), repeat noninvasive ischemia testing (HR 1.072; p=0.021), and anti-anginal intensification (HR 1.041; p=0.019) were modestly higher in the physiologic testing cohort. Ventricular arrhythmias were similar (HR 0.996; p=0.932). Conclusion: In a large propensity-matched real-world cohort with suspected INOCA, invasive physiologic testing was associated with higher downstream diagnostic testing and anti-anginal escalation but did not reduce all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or ventricular arrhythmias. These findings suggest that physiologic testing without confirmed mechanism-guided therapy primarily influences diagnostic reassessment rather than hard clinical outcomes. Physiology-directed treatment pathways may be necessary to translate diagnostic information into improved patient outcomes.
title: Abstract 8324: Invasive Physiologic Testing and Downstream Outcomes in Patients with Suspected Ischemia and Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries

abstract: BACKGROUND: In cardiogenic shock, where mortality remains high, clinicians judge severity at admission. However, outcomes are shaped by how patients respond over the following hours. The SCAI shock classification, the standard framework for this assessment, captures a single time point and not the response to resuscitation. Lactate clearance is an inexpensive, repeatable marker of that response, although its prognostic value in cardiogenic shock is not well established. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that early lactate clearance independently predicts in-hospital mortality in cardiogenic shock and improves prediction beyond established severity measures. METHODS: We studied adults with cardiogenic shock in the MIMIC-IV critical care database, identified by ICD-10 coding and confirmed by vasoactive support, mechanical circulatory support, hypotension, or hyperlactatemia. Patients were included if they had paired lactate measurements at 0 to 6 and 18 to 30 hours after ICU admission. Clearance was defined as the percentage fall from the initial value. The outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for initial lactate severity, etiology, age, sex, organ-failure (SOFA) score, vasoactive agents, mechanical ventilation, creatinine, and mechanical circulatory support; troponin, pre-specified as a covariate, was excluded for high missingness. Adjusted models used complete cases. Discrimination with and without clearance was compared using the DeLong test. The protocol was pre-registered on the Open Science Framework before analysis. RESULTS: The cohort comprised 580 patients (median age 67 years, 62% male); adjusted models included 519 with complete covariates. In-hospital mortality was 36% and rose with initial lactate severity, from 29% in the low stratum to 51% and 64% in the moderate and severe strata. Higher clearance was independently associated with lower mortality (adjusted OR 0.94 per 10% increase, 95% CI 0.90 to 0.97, P=0.001). Patients achieving at least 10% clearance had 55% lower adjusted odds of death (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.70, P=0.0003). Adding clearance to the severity model improved discrimination (C-statistic 0.766 vs 0.740, P=0.007). The association held in both myocardial infarction and heart failure related shock. CONCLUSION: Early lactate clearance independently predicted in-hospital mortality in cardiogenic shock and improved prediction beyond severity already captured at admission. Unlike static, admission-based assessment, clearance reflects the response to initial resuscitation and carried prognostic information independent of baseline severity. These findings are limited by the single-center, retrospective design and reliance on administrative coding. Serial lactate assessment may help identify patients whose risk diverges from their admission severity, and warrants prospective validation.
title: Abstract 8329: Lactate Clearance and Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock: A Pre-Registered Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Thoracic radiation therapy is associated with valvular calcification, mediastinal fibrosis, and conduction abnormalities, potentially increasing procedural complexity and adverse outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Large-scale real-world data evaluating TAVR outcomes in patients with prior thoracic radiation remain limited. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults undergoing TAVR between 2015-2025 were identified using CPT procedural codes. Patients with prior thoracic radiation exposure were identified using ICD-10 code Z92.3 documented at least 1 year before TAVR. Patients without prior radiation served as controls. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed for demographics and baseline comorbidities, yielding 1,422 matched patients in each cohort. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year mortality, atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF), pacemaker implantation, atrioventricular block, stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), heart failure hospitalization, prosthetic valve dysfunction/paravalvular leak, and infective endocarditis. Results: Mean age at index was 77.3±8.9 years in the radiation cohort and 77.8±8.8 years in controls, with females comprising 44.8% of the radiation cohort. At 30 days, mortality occurred in 1.7% of radiation-exposed patients versus 1.4% of controls (RR 1.20; p=0.54). At 1 year, mortality was 10.3% versus 10.1%, respectively (RR 1.02; p=0.85). Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 14.1% versus 13.9% (RR 1.02; p=0.83), AV block in 44.8% versus 43.6% (RR 1.03; p=0.52), and stroke in 17.0% versus 17.5% (RR 0.97; p=0.73). Prosthetic valve leak (1.0% vs 0.8%; p=0.69), prosthetic valve infection (3.5% vs 3.8%; p=0.69), heart failure (67.3% vs 66.2%; p=0.50), and atrial fibrillation/flutter (69.7% vs 68.7%; p=0.57) were also comparable. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in long-term survival between cohorts (HR 1.02; p=0.74). Conclusions: In this large propensity-matched real-world analysis, prior thoracic radiation exposure was not associated with significantly increased mortality following TAVR. Major post-procedural complications were largely comparable between groups, suggesting TAVR remains a feasible therapeutic option in carefully selected patients with radiation-associated valvular heart disease.
title: Abstract 8333: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients with Prior Thoracic Radiation: A Propensity-Matched Real-World Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Hearts of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) are under chronic wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. Methods: We prospectively enrolled stable patients with HCM in the outpatient settings. Plasma cfDNA was isolated and whole genome bisulfite sequencing libraries were created and multiplexed for Illumina paired-end sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. Results: A total of 57 patients (mean age 46.4±16.6 years, 35% female) with HCM were enrolled. cfDNA isolation and quantification was feasible in all of the enrolled subjects. The median cfDNA concentration was 0.63ng/ul [IQR: 0.41, 1.05]. The cfDNA-CM fraction ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI) as a continuous variable (p=0.001) and a greater prevalence of BMI ≥30 kg/m 2 (p<0.001), as well as a higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (p=0.038). In an exploratory analysis, the prevalence of advanced heart failure symptoms (NYHA III/IV) increased across ascending cfDNA-CM tertiles (10.5%, 15.8%, and 42.1%; p-trend=0.057). Although not statistically significant, a trend toward a greater prevalence of left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction was observed across ascending tertiles (26.3% vs 47.4% vs 63.2%; p=0.088). There was no significant difference across tertiles of cfDNA-CM for demographic, genetic, and standard blood assays used in HCM. Notably, circulating biomarkers of wall stress (NT-proBNP) and myocardial injury (troponin) did not differ across tertiles. Conclusion: Isolation and quantification of cfDNA and cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM is feasible. Higher cfDNA-CM fraction was associated with increasing BMI and greater cardiometabolic comorbidity burden, with a trend toward a higher prevalence of advanced heart failure symptoms (NYHA class III/IV). The absence of association with traditional circulating biomarkers suggests that cfDNA-CM may reflect a distinct domain of myocardial health, injury and adverse remodeling.
title: Abstract 8336: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) remain at high risk for adverse outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) may identify residual risk in this setting. Objective: To evaluate whether baseline hsCRP is associated with all-cause mortality (ACM) and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) after ACS in patients with T2D, and whether the association with HFH persists after adjustment for cardiac biomarkers. Methods: We performed a post hoc analysis of 5,380 patients with T2D and recent ACS in the EXAMINE trial who had available baseline hsCRP. Patients were categorized into hsCRP tertiles: T1 ≤1.30, T2 1.30-3.70, and T3 >3.70 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated ACM, and Fine-Gray models evaluated HFH, treating death without prior HFH as a competing event. Models were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, prior HFH, T2D duration, history of myocardial infarction, hypertension, smoking and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Cumulative incidence curves were compared. In sequential biomarker-adjusted analyses, associations between log-hsCRP as continuous predictor and HFH were examined at 1 year and over full follow-up, with additional adjustment for troponin I (TnI) and clinical B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP). Sensitivity analyses using Olink BNP were performed. Results: Across increasing hsCRP tertiles, patients had higher BMI, HbA1c, smoking prevalence, prior HFH, TnI, BNP, and more frequent insulin and diuretic use. Compared with T1, after multivariable adjustment, T3 was associated with higher risk of ACM (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.35-2.33; P<0.001) and HFH (SHR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40; P=0.0034), whereas T2 was not. T3 had the highest cumulative incidence of ACM and HFH (log-rank p<0.001 and Gray's test p<0.001, respectively) (Fig 1) . Log-hsCRP remained associated with 1-year HFH after adjustment for TnI (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.10-1.44; P<0.001), clinical BNP (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.06-1.81; P=0.0160), and both biomarkers (HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.00-1.77; P=0.049). Findings were consistent in the Olink BNP sensitivity analyses after adjustment for Olink BNP alone (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.45; P<0.001) and Olink BNP plus TnI (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.07-1.41; P=0.0039). Over full follow-up, the association was preserved after adjustment for TnI alone (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.06-1.35; P=0.0034), Olink BNP alone (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.06-1.35; P=0.0032), and Olink BNP plus TnI (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.03-1.32; P=0.014), but was attenuated in the smaller subset of patients with available clinical BNP. (Fig 2) . Conclusion: In patients with T2D after recent ACS, elevated hsCRP identified a high-risk phenotype associated with ACM and HFH. Persistence of the association between hsCRP and HFH after adjustment for TnI and BNP suggests that inflammation captures residual HF risk not fully explained by myocardial injury or cardiac stress biomarkers.
title: Abstract 8341: High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein, All-Cause Mortality and Heart Failure Hospitalization After Acute Coronary Syndrome in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights from the Examination of Cardiovascular Outcomes with Alogliptin versus Standard of Care (EXAMINE) Trial

abstract: Keywords: Epstein-Barr virus, Myocarditis, Left ventricular thrombus, Cardioembolic stroke, Pulmonary embolism Introduction: Epstein-Barr virus infection affects approximately 95% of the adult population worldwide. Very few reports of EBV-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) exist in the medical literature. Myocarditis is also a rare but significant complication of EBV infection. This case, in which both complications occur simultaneously, results in a life-threatening cardioembolic stroke and emphasizes the need for a thorough workup in such cases. Patient information and clinical findings: A 42-year-old male with a history of hypertension who recently had cough and dyspnea that required an urgent care visit presented with acute aphasia, left-sided hemiparesis, and facial droop. Diagnostic assessment and reasoning: The patient initially received thrombolytic therapy. Brain MRI showed bilateral punctate infarcts in the cerebrum and cerebellum, consistent with embolism. CTA revealed bilateral pulmonary emboli and a 3.2 cm apical LV thrombus. Echocardiography indicated severe biventricular dysfunction (LVEF 15%) and suspected intracardiac thrombus. Lab results included elevated troponin (2.52 ng/mL), pro-BNP (4,775 pg/mL), leukocytosis, and positive EBV IgM and IgG. Viral, autoimmune, and hypercoagulability panels were unremarkable. PET/CT excluded malignancy; left heart catheterization showed no significant coronary disease. Cardiac MRI confirmed severe cardiomyopathy, LV thrombus, and bilateral pulmonary infarcts. Therapeutic intervention: Anticoagulation was deferred initially post-thrombolysis due to stroke risk.
