Given the interval increase of intracranial hemorrhage and the operative risk of cardiopulmonary bypass; surgery was initially deferred. Despite anticoagulation and intravenous antibiotics, transcranial Doppler revealed persistent microemboli, and serial MRI showed relatively stable brain abscess, and new brain and splenic infarcts. Transcatheter RA thrombectomy with temporary balloon occlusion of the defect was considered as a bridge strategy. However, repeat TEE on hospital day 13 showed a new left atrial mass despite ongoing therapy, strongly suggesting interval paradoxical embolization across the defect (figure 3). Given continued progression, a multidisciplinary team proceeded with surgical excision of the RA masses and repair of the SV ASD and PAPVR. Pathology demonstrated fibrin thrombi with inflammatory debris. Postoperative brain MRI showed a stable abscess with several small acute infarcts, while CT angiography demonstrated bilateral subsegmental pulmonary emboli. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 8 with 6 weeks of intravenous antibiotics and apixaban. Conclusion: This case highlights progressive right atrial thrombus to left atrium via SV ASD complicated by multi-organ embolization and brain abscess. The development of a new left atrial mass despite anticoagulation and antimicrobial therapy provided compelling evidence of ongoing right-to-left embolization and shifted the risk-benefit balance toward early surgery despite intracranial hemorrhage. Bridge strategies such as transcatheter thrombectomy with temporary defect occlusion may warrant further investigation in similar high-risk scenarios.
title: Abstract 9165: The Crossing: Progressive Paradoxical Embolization Through a Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect

abstract: Background: Transcatheter left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) prevents cardioembolic stroke in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation who cannot tolerate long-term anticoagulation. Whether the third generation Watchman FLX confers superior clinical outcomes over the second generation Watchman 2.5 remains incompletely characterised. Methods: We performed a PRISMA 2020 compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of studies comparing Watchman FLX with Watchman 2.5. Three electronic databases were searched through April 2026. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived using DerSimonian-Laird random effects models. Nine prespecified outcomes were analysed: procedural success, device related embolism, device related thrombosis (DRT), major bleeding, pericardial effusion, all-cause mortality, any stroke, ischaemic stroke, and length of hospital stay (LOHS). Results: Seven observational cohort studies enrolling 131,728 patients (Watchman FLX: n = 54,023; Watchman 2.5: n = 77,705) were included. All studies received Newcastle Ottawa Scale scores of 8-9 (high quality). The Watchman FLX demonstrated significantly higher procedural success (RR 1.02 [1.02-1.02]; p < 0.00001) and significant reductions in pericardial effusion (RR 0.33 [0.27-0.41]; p < 0.00001), device related embolism (RR 0.38 [0.23-0.60]; p < 0.0001), all-cause stroke (RR 0.75 [0.65-0.86]; p < 0.0001), ischaemic stroke (RR 0.81 [0.69-0.96]; p = 0.01), major bleeding (RR 0.65 [0.53-0.81]; p < 0.0001), and all-cause mortality (RR 0.54 [0.37-0.78]; p = 0.001). DRT showed a directional but non-significant trend toward reduction (RR 0.33 [0.09-1.20]; p = 0.09). LOHS was not reliably estimable (I 2 = 87%). Conclusions: The Watchman FLX is associated with significantly superior safety and efficacy outcomes relative to the Watchman 2.5 across the principal clinical domains of transcatheter LAAO, supporting its preferential use in all eligible patients. These findings should inform device selection, guideline recommendations, and the design of future prospective comparative studies.
title: Abstract 9182: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Comparing the Clinical Outcomes of the Watchman FLX versus Watchman 2.5 Device for Transcatheter Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Introduction: Tangier disease, caused by biallelic ABCA1 loss-of-function, is a rare cause of marked HDL deficiency with a prevalence of 1 in 640,000. Whether Tangier disease increases ASCVD risk remains controversial. Here we describe two genetically confirmed cases of Tangier Disease with ASCVD and demonstrate how advanced lipoprotein testing may provide insight into lipid-related risk for ASCVD. Patient Cases: Patient 1 is a 55-year-old White woman with a history of premature CAD requiring PCI in the setting of exertional angina at age 52 yrs (Table). She was active with a normal BMI, and had no history of diabetes, hypertension, smoking, or family history of premature CAD. A routine lipid profile was notable for very low HDL-C, minimally elevated LDL-C, and moderate triglyceride elevation. Advanced lipid testing demonstrated significantly elevated apoB, LDL-P, and sdLDL-C, discordant with her LDL-C value. HDL particle analysis revealed very low levels of apoA-I, HDL-P, and all HDL particle subtypes. Patient 2 is a 56-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish woman with a history of hypertension and prior smoking. Routine lipid panel revealed very low HDL-C with elevated LDL-C, elevated non-HDL-C, and normal triglycerides. LDL-P and apoB were also noted to be discordantly elevated in comparison to her LDL-C. ApoA-I and HDL-P were very low. She reported no prior cardiovascular events but was found to have a CAC score of 93 (94 th percentile for age/gender). Genetic testing was performed in both cases. In patient 1, genetic testing revealed biallelic ABCA1 mutations. In Patient 2, genetic testing was also notable for biallelic ABCA1 mutations as well as a heterozygous VUS in LDLR. Both patients were started on lipid lowering therapy including statins and ezetimibe with the goal of lowering LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and apoB. Four years after initial presentation, patient 2 had a repeat calcium score CT which demonstrated an increased CAC score of 219 (95 th percentile) for which daily low-dose aspirin was added. Discussion: The patients in both cases demonstrate discordant elevation of apoB and LDL-P relative to LDL-C, though the precise mechanism in each case is likely distinct. Patient 1 exhibits the classic Tangier pattern of triglyceride-enriched sdLDL predominance. Patient 2’s more significant LDL-C elevation and relatively larger LDL particle size is likely the result of her co-occurring LDLR VUS. In both cases, LDL-C alone may underrepresent atherogenic risk. The recent AHA/ACC Multisociety Dyslipidemia Management Guideline emphasizes the role of non-HDL-C and apoB to refine risk assessments and treatment targets which is directly applicable to the characterization of the residual risk seen in Tangier disease. In Tangier disease, for ASCVD risk reduction it is important to lower atherogenic lipoprotein levels which can be achieved with standard lipid-lowering therapies.
title: Abstract 9214: Advanced Lipoprotein Characterization of Occult Atherogenic Risk in Tangier Disease: A Two-Patient Case Series

abstract: Introduction: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are being developed as cell-free therapeutic candidates for cardiovascular disease, but the cellular routes that allow EV microRNA (miRNA) cargo to enter cardiomyocytes remain unclear. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that MSC EVs deliver miRNA cargo into cardiomyocytes through specific endocytic pathways, with macropinocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis contributing to cargo uptake. Methods: Mouse MSC EVs were loaded with the exogenous miRNA cel-miR-39-3p and applied to H9C2 cardiomyocytes at increasing EV doses for 2 hours. Intracellular cel-miR-39-3p was quantified by real-time polymerase chain reaction. Cytosolic cargo delivery was tested using a cholesterol-modified antagomir against cel-miR-39-3p. Uptake pathways were probed with inhibitors of macropinocytosis, including 5-(N-ethyl-N-isopropyl) amiloride, and clathrin-mediated endocytosis, including chlorpromazine and ES9-17. Transferrin uptake was used to confirm clathrin pathway inhibition. Results: MSC EV treatment increased cardiomyocyte cel-miR-39-3p levels in a dose-dependent manner, with significant increases at 1х, 2х, and 4х EV doses compared with phosphate-buffered saline control ( p ≤0.05 to p ≤0.0001). Antagomir treatment reduced EV-delivered cel-miR-39-3p by 89% compared with scrambled control ( p ≤0.0001), supporting cytosolic accessibility of transferred cargo. Inhibiting macropinocytosis decreased EV-mediated miRNA transfer by 71% ( p ≤0.001). Selective inhibition of clathrin-mediated endocytosis with ES9-17 decreased transfer by 36% at the highest EV dose, while chlorpromazine blocked transferrin uptake but paradoxically increased EV-miRNA transfer, suggesting compensatory or membrane curvature-dependent uptake. Combined macropinocytosis and clathrin pathway inhibition reduced cel-miR-39-3p levels to near control values. Conclusion(s): MSC EVs deliver miRNA cargo into cardiomyocytes through endocytic mechanisms involving macropinocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Defining these uptake routes provides a mechanistic basis for improving EV engineering, dosing, and targeted delivery strategies for myocardial injury and other cardiovascular diseases.
title: Abstract 9264: Endocytic Pathways for Mesenchymal Stem Cell Extracellular Vesicle Cargo Delivery to Cardiomyocytes

abstract: Introduction: Obstetric cardiac care for complex patients is challenging, requiring a multidisciplinary approach attentive to both maternal and fetal health. We present the safe delivery of a dialysis-dependent patient with a massive right atrial thrombus. Patient Information: A 33-year-old patient with a history of heart failure with improved ejection fraction and end stage renal disease on dialysis secondary to sepsis during a prior pregnancy was admitted for medical optimization before delivery at 36 weeks. She had recently undergone placement of a tunneled catheter for hemodialysis access. Clinical Findings: She was asymptomatic and her exam at the time was unremarkable. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: A routine transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) prior to delivery revealed a massive, mobile thrombus in the right atrium and right ventricle with possible extension across the interatrial septum into the left atrium. A heparin infusion was started. A bubble study confirmed an interatrial shunt. Because vaginal delivery would require repeated Valsalva maneuvers that could provoke right-to-left embolization, elective cesarean delivery was planned. The Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) team was consulted and recommended placement of arterial and venous sheaths for cannulation if needed. Invasive thrombus aspiration to reduce the risk of pulmonary or paradoxical embolism was considered early in her course, but the multidisciplinary team consensus was to prioritize delivery. Therapeutic Interventions: Cesarean delivery was uncomplicated. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiogram revealed that the thrombus was confined to the right heart, without left atrial extension that would have precluded percutaneous aspiration. Several days later, attempted aspiration of the thrombus was unsuccessful and complicated by hemodynamic compromise. She underwent emergent sternotomy with thrombus excision, right atrial reconstruction, and patent foramen ovale closure. Surgical pathology confirmed organizing fibrin thrombus. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: The patient recovered well. After hematology consultation, she was transitioned to warfarin given its safety in end stage renal disease and breastfeeding. Follow-up TTE showed a normal ejection fraction. She was safely discharged with her child. Discussion: Cesarean delivery can be a safe strategy in pregnant patients with intracardiac thrombus and interatrial shunt. Interatrial shunting should therefore be sought before delivery, as it may influence delivery mode. Warfarin remains the preferred anticoagulant while breastfeeding due to negligible infant exposure. Multidisciplinary care is integral to managing complex cardiac conditions in pregnancy, including large intracardiac thrombi. Such patients should be delivered at a quaternary center with access to cardiac surgery and ECMO.
title: Abstract 9315: The Clot Thickens: A Right Atrial Mass in Pregnancy

abstract: Background: HF readmissions carry substantial morbidity and mortality, yet the relative effects of metabolic burden (MB) and acute inflammatory stress on in-hospital outcomes are poorly defined. Hypothesis: High MB and inflammatory stress will both independently and synergistically increase 30-day readmission risk and in-hospital complications among HF patients. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult HF hospitalizations from 2010-2024 at Baptist Health South Florida. MB was classified as low (0-2 components) or high (≥ 3 components) based on presence of obesity, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, NAFLD/MASLD, and obstructive sleep apnea. Inflammatory stress was defined by presence of sepsis, pneumonia, UTI, bacteremia, or influenza/COVID-19 during hospitalization. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission; secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital complications. Group differences were assessed via Wilcoxon rank-sum and chi-square tests. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CIs were estimated using multivariable logistic regression for binary outcomes and linear regression for LOS. All models adjusted for demographics, insurance, discharge disposition, and comorbidities (α=0.05). Results: Among 25,124 patients with decompensated HF (57.3% HFpEF and 42.7% HFrEF), high MB was present in 15,522 patients (61.8%) and was associated with younger age, male sex, HFpEF, greater prevalence of acute inflammatory stress (78.9% vs. 65.7%, p<0.001), and higher rates of atrial fibrillation, CAD, PAD, stroke, valvular disease, anemia, CKD, COPD, and liver disease (all p<0.001)( Table 1 ). After adjustment, high MB independently predicted 30-day readmission (aOR 1.14, 95% CI: 1.06-1.21), AKI (aOR 1.27, 95% CI: 1.20-1.35), respiratory failure (aOR 1.31, 95% CI: 1.23-1.39), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.17, 95% CI: 1.04-1.31), and ICU admission (aOR 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.23). Inflammatory stress independently predicted 30-day readmission (aOR 1.67, 95% CI: 1.54-1.81), longer length of stay (β = 1.85 days, 95% CI: 1.45-2.25), AKI (aOR 2.82, 95% CI: 2.65-3.01), respiratory failure (aOR 2.92, 95% CI: 2.74-3.12), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.17, 95% CI: 1.04-1.31), mechanical ventilation (aOR 2.45, 95% CI: 2.21-2.72), and hemodialysis requirement (aOR 1.62, 95% CI: 1.44-1.83)( Table 2 , Figure ). Patients with both high MB and inflammatory stress did not experience greater odds of adverse outcomes. Conclusion: High MB and inflammatory stress independently predicted 30-day readmission and in-hospital complications in HF patients, with inflammatory stress as the dominant driver. However, no synergistic effect was observed in HF patients with both. These findings support MB and inflammatory stress as independent predictors of adverse outcomes that may enhance risk stratification of HF patients at the time of hospitalization and discharge.
title: Abstract 9348: Metabolic Burden and Acute Inflammatory Stress as Predictors of Adverse Outcomes in Hospitalized Heart Failure Patients: A Large Single-Center Analysis

abstract: Background: Infective endocarditis (IE) following mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) with MitraClip is a rare but increasingly recognized complication associated with significant morbidity and mortality. While overall in-hospital mortality for IE is estimated at 20-30%, mortality in MitraClip-associated infective endocarditis (MAIE) approached 50% in a prior review. Research Question: With increasing M-TEER use, we sought to characterize the timing, microbiology, management, and outcomes of MAIE. Methods: A systematic review using PubMed, Google Scholar, and references from a prior review identified cases of MAIE. Of 93 identified records, 36 studies comprising 39 patients were included. Results: Early-onset infection (<1 year) occurred in 24 cases, while 14 were late-onset (≥1 year). Staphylococcus aureus was the most common pathogen, accounting for 13/36 (36.1%) identified organisms. Among cases with identified pathogens, S. aureus accounted for 13/23 (56.5%) early-onset infections, whereas late-onset infections demonstrated a broader microbiologic spectrum, with S. aureus identified in only 1/13 (7.7%) cases. Among 38 cases with reported outcomes, overall survival was 65.8%. Surgically managed patients demonstrated higher survival than medically managed patients (72.7% vs 56.3%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (Fisher exact p = 0.323). Conclusions: This expanded review represents the largest characterization of MAIE to date, comprising 39 patients across 36 studies. Compared with a prior 2023 review, this cohort demonstrated lower overall mortality (34.2% vs 50%), including among both surgically managed (27.3% vs 38.4%) and medically managed patients (43.7% vs 58.3%), while also identifying more late-onset infections. Distinct microbiologic profiles between early- and late-onset infections may reflect differing mechanisms of acquisition. Early infections were predominantly caused by S. aureus , Staphylococcus epidermidis , and Enterococcus species, suggesting peri-procedural or healthcare-associated infection, whereas late-onset infections demonstrated a broader spectrum of oral flora, atypical organisms, and gram-negative pathogens. Surgically managed patients had higher observed survival; however, this may reflect selection bias, as medically managed patients were likely poor surgical candidates. There are no dedicated guidelines for MAIE, and management is largely extrapolated from prosthetic valve endocarditis recommendations supporting surgery for heart failure, periannular complications, uncontrolled or recurrent infections, and large vegetations. However, these recommendations do not account for the procedural complexity and comorbidity burden of M-TEER patients. These findings highlight the need for further research as M-TEER use continues to grow.
title: Abstract 9352: Characterizing MitraClip-Associated Infective Endocarditis: An Expanded Systematic Review

abstract: Background: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock staging supports serial reassessment, but large cohorts typically report only baseline or admission-wide maximum stage. Whether early electronic health record (EHR)-derived stage trajectories provide prognostic information beyond initial severity in acute myocardial infarction cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) and heart failure cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) is not well established. Research Question: Among patients with AMI-CS or HF-CS, does a change in EHR-derived Cardiogenic Shock Working Group-modified SCAI (CSWG-SCAI) stage from 6 to 24 hours after admission provide prognostic information for 30-day mortality beyond the initial stage? Methods: Using MIMIC-IV v3.1 (2008-2022), we studied 2,027 admissions with AMI-CS or HF-CS. At 9 checkpoints from 6 to 168 hours after admission, CSWG-SCAI stages (A to E; increasing severity) were operationalized from CSWG-modified SCAI criteria using the most recent blood pressure, lactate, pH, and alanine transaminase measurements within 24 hours and concurrent vasoactive or device support. The primary trajectory was classified as improved (lower stage), stable (same stage), or worsened (higher stage) from 6 to 24 hours. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality among admissions staged at both landmarks; in-hospital and 90-day mortality were secondary outcomes. Patient-clustered logistic regression adjusted for initial stage, etiology, age, and Charlson score. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for SOFA score and were restricted to each patient's first admission or cases reaching stage C or higher within 6 hours of admission. Results: Among 1,958/2,027 (96.6%) landmark-evaluable admissions (1,060 AMI-CS; 898 HF-CS; median age, 71 years [IQR, 61-80]), stage improved in 336 (17.2%), remained stable in 1,121 (57.3%), and worsened in 501 (25.6%). Thirty-day mortality increased across trajectory groups (30.1%, 36.0%, and 42.1%, respectively; P=0.002). Compared with improvement, adjusted odds of 30-day mortality were higher with stable (OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.59-3.20) and worsened trajectories (OR 3.42, 95% CI 2.30-5.08). Associations were consistent across AMI-CS and HF-CS, with no significant trajectory-by-etiology interaction. At 24 hours, stage E carried 30-day mortality of 75.5% in AMI-CS and 52.5% in HF-CS. Findings were consistent across sensitivities and for in-hospital and 90-day mortality. Conclusion: Early CSWG-SCAI stage trajectory provided prognostic information beyond the initial stage in both AMI-CS and HF-CS. Failure to improve by 24 hours identified patients at persistently elevated risk and may help guide reassessment of hemodynamics, treatment response, and escalation strategies. This retrospective single-center EHR study measured landmarks from hospital admission rather than shock onset; external validation is warranted.
title: Abstract 9358: Early Shock Stage Trajectories and Mortality in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Right ventricular assist devices (RVADs) are increasingly used for acute right heart failure, and percutaneous platforms (Impella RP) have expanded rapidly. National data describing RVAD utilization trends and comparing percutaneous versus surgical support remain limited. Hypothesis: RVAD utilization—particularly percutaneous support—has increased over time, and percutaneous RVAD is associated with comparable in-hospital mortality but lower resource use than surgical RVAD. Methods: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020), we identified adult RVAD hospitalizations (ICD-10-PCS 02HA0RZ surgical; 02HA3RZ/02HA4RZ percutaneous), excluding biventricular and cardiac-output codes. Survey-weighted logistic and linear regression compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total charges, and non-routine discharge by device type, adjusting for demographics, etiology, Elixhauser comorbidity burden, hospital characteristics, and year. Results: Among 56,015 weighted RVAD hospitalizations (mean age 64.5 years; 28.3% female; mean Elixhauser 5.8), the leading etiology was acute myocardial infarction (66.1%), followed by non-ischemic heart failure (24.5%). Annual volume rose from ~2,550 in 2016 to ~14,000 in 2020, and percutaneous support comprised 94.2% of cases, increasing from 85.5% to >93%. Overall in-hospital mortality was 38.7% and rose significantly over the period (trend p=0.007). After full adjustment, percutaneous (vs surgical) RVAD was associated with similar in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69-1.02; p=0.078) but markedly lower resource use: –17.7 days LOS (p<0.001), ~47% lower total charges (p<0.001), and lower odds of non-routine discharge (aOR 0.70; p=0.003). Results were consistent across etiology subgroups and sensitivity analyses (excluding 2020, percutaneous-only, and cardiogenic-shock-only). Conclusions: RVAD use—overwhelmingly percutaneous—rose nationally from 2016 to 2020, with persistently high and increasing in-hospital mortality (~39%) reflecting a sicker or broader treated population. Percutaneous RVAD achieved comparable adjusted mortality with substantially shorter, less costly hospitalizations, supporting its expanding real-world role and underscoring the need for prospective comparative data.
title: Abstract 9379: Percutaneous versus Surgical Right Ventricular Assist Device Support: National Utilization Trends and In-Hospital Outcomes (NIS 2016-2020)

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Intermediate coronary stenosis remains challenging because angiography alone poorly predicts functional ischemia. Pressure wire-based fractional flow reserve (FFR) is the gold standard for invasive physiological assessment but remains underused. Angiography-derived physiology (ADP) offers a wire-free, adenosine-free method to assess stenosis significance from routine angiographic images. Research Question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether ADP-guided strategies provide comparable clinical outcomes to pressure wire-based FFR in patients with CAD undergoing physiological lesion assessment. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. Randomized controlled trials directly comparing ADP modalities, including quantitative flow ratio, vessel fractional flow reserve, or FFRangio, with pressure wire-based FFR for revascularization guidance were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at 12 months. Random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian-Laird method pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using I2. Trial sequential analysis was performed for the primary endpoint. Results: Three randomized controlled trials enrolling 6,141 patients were included. The primary composite endpoint occurred in 211 versus 185 patients and did not differ significantly between ADP and FFR strategies (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.85-1.54; p=0.37; I2=57%). All-cause mortality (RR 1.08, 95% CI 0.75-1.56; p=0.68; I2=0%) and cardiac death (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.53-1.49; p=0.66; I2=0%) were similar. Myocardial infarction also did not differ significantly (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.66-1.98; p=0.64; I2=65%). Clinically indicated revascularization was higher with ADP (RR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.20; p=0.005; I2=0%). Safety outcomes, including acute kidney injury, BARC 3 or higher bleeding, stent thrombosis, and adverse procedural events, were comparable. Trial sequential analysis supported sufficient evidence for no significant difference in 12-month MACE between ADP- and FFR-guided strategies. Conclusion: ADP-guided revascularization demonstrated comparable 12-month clinical outcomes and safety profiles to pressure wire-based FFR in patients with CAD, although clinically indicated revascularization was higher with ADP. These findings support ADP as a practical wire-free alternative for physiological lesion assessment while emphasizing the need for continued outcome evaluation
title: Abstract 9388: Angiography-Derived Physiology versus Pressure Wire-Based Fractional Flow Reserve for Coronary Revascularization Guidance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Hospital procedure volumes have been shown to impact clinical outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). There is limited data regarding emergent TAVR. Research Questions/Hypothesis: Among adult patients undergoing emergent TAVR, do hospital procedural volumes (low vs. medium vs. high) influence in-hospital outcomes — specifically mortality, length of stay, and total hospital charges? Methods: We identified adult patients undergoing emergent TAVR utilizing the National Inpatient Sample from 2016-2022. Hospitals were categorized into tertiles of annual TAVR volume (low, medium, high). Survey-weighted analyses were performed to assess mortality, LOS, and total hospital charges (inflation-adjusted to 2022 USD) across tertiles. Results: A total of 71,728 patients undergoing emergent TAVR were included. Across the study period, the overall in-hospital mortality was 2.7% (95% CI: 2.5-3%). Mortality was highest in low-volume centers (3.1%), followed by medium centers (2.8%), and high centers (2.2%) (p<0.001 in all). Mean LOS decreased with increasing volume (low: 10 days, medium: 9.1 days, high: 7.1 days) (Figure 1A). Mean total hospital charge varied by tertile (low: $71,664, medium: $67,506, high: $60,675) (Figure 1B). Conclusion: Patients undergoing emergent TAVR at higher procedural volume centers, had lower in-hospital mortality with shorter LOS and lower costs. These findings highlight the critical role of procedural experience and support directing complex, time-sensitive TAVR cases to high-volume institutions to optimize patient outcomes and healthcare value.
title: Abstract 9408: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients Undergoing Emergency Procedure in High vs Low Volume Centers: Nation Wide Study of a Large Cohort

abstract: Introduction: ST-segment elevation requires emergent evaluation for acute coronary occlusion, but noncoronary processes can produce STEMI mimics. We describe a surgical gastric emergency presenting with an anteroseptal STEMI pattern from extrinsic cardiac compression. Patient Information: A 76-year-old man presented with two weeks of poor oral intake and two days of inability to tolerate solid food, with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and lower back pain. Clinical Findings and Timeline: Initial electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia with premature ventricular complexes, anteroseptal ST-segment elevation with strain pattern, and hyperacute T waves. High-sensitivity troponin I was mildly elevated and increased from 106 to 141 ng/L. Bedside cardiac ultrasound raised suspicion for extrinsic compression of the left atrium and left ventricle. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Computed tomography angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed a fluid-distended esophagus, hiatal hernia, massive gastric dilation with gastric pneumatosis and air-fluid level, abrupt pyloric tapering without definite mass, and extensive portal venous gas. The gastric fundus was intrathoracic and markedly dilated, compressing the left atrium and left ventricle. The duodenum was compressed and flattened. These findings favored gastric outlet obstruction with ischemic gastric injury and secondary cardiac compression as the cause of the pseudo-STEMI pattern. Therapeutic Intervention: General surgery was emergently consulted. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed pneumoperitoneum and peritonitis, requiring conversion to open laparotomy. Peritoneal lavage, partial gastrectomy, and gastrojejunostomy tube placement were performed. Follow-up and Outcomes: After gastric decompression and surgical management, repeat electrocardiogram showed resolution of the ST-segment elevations. Discussion: ST-segment elevation from extracardiac compression may result from myocardial compression or displacement, altered depolarization-repolarization vectors, impaired chamber filling with relative ischemia, or rarely coronary compression or vasospasm. In this patient, rapid integration of electrocardiography, bedside ultrasound, and cross-sectional imaging identified an extracardiac surgical emergency rather than primary coronary occlusion. Conclusion: The final diagnosis was pseudo-STEMI from massive intrathoracic gastric distension causing left-sided cardiac compression in the setting of gastric outlet obstruction and ischemic gastric injury. Clinicians should remain alert to discordant features suggesting a STEMI mimic while maintaining urgent evaluation for acute coronary occlusion.
title: Abstract 9449: Pseudo-STEMI from Massive Gastric Distension and Cardiac Compression

abstract: Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of mortality in acute myocardial infarction, with mortality exceeding 40% despite mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Comparative effectiveness of Impella versus veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) remains uncertain due to confounding and lack of adequately powered randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Generative models offer a novel approach to synthesize counterfactual control arms from real-world data. Methods: We developed a tabular denoising diffusion probabilistic model (TabDDPM) to generate synthetic digital twins for CS patients receiving Impella and simulate counterfactual VA-ECMO outcomes. The model was validated using a retrospective cohort of 1,827 CS patients from published meta-analyses. Fidelity was assessed using statistical similarity metrics, utility by downstream classification performance (AUC), and privacy via membership inference attacks. Results: TabDDPM achieved a fidelity score of 0.83 and utility AUC of 0.81, outperforming CTGAN, TVAE, and SMOTE. Generated counterfactual survival curves reproduced observational findings, with lower in-hospital mortality for Impella versus synthetic VA-ECMO twins (42.4% vs 50.1%), consistent with published meta-analyses. Synthetic propensity-matched cohorts yielded an adjusted odds ratio of 0.57 (95% CI 0.44-0.74) favoring Impella. Impella twins demonstrated lower bleeding (19.9% vs 28.8%), stroke (5.2% vs 8.7%), limb ischemia (7% vs 17%), and renal replacement therapy requirements. Performance remained robust across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: TabDDPM successfully generated clinically plausible counterfactual control arms for CS device comparisons, reproducing observed treatment effects and complication patterns. This framework may enable RCT-like comparisons when randomization is infeasible, although external validation and assessment of residual confounding remain essential.
title: Abstract 9459: Synthesizing the Missing Control Arm: A Tabular Diffusion Counterfactual Model for Cardiogenic Shock Regimens

abstract: Introduction: Timely diagnosis of genetic cardiomyopathies can guide acute management and facilitate family screening. We report a case of PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy presenting as sudden cardiac arrest and refractory cardiogenic shock requiring OHT. Patient Information: A 21-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with abdominal pain, vomiting, chest pain, and dyspnea after consuming three alcoholic beverages. Family history was notable for early-onset heart failure in her mother and maternal aunt. Clinical Findings and Timeline: ECG demonstrated inferior and lateral ST-segment elevations with reciprocal anterior depressions. She developed profound hypotension followed by pulseless electrical activity arrest en route to coronary angiography. ECRP was performed for one hour, including two defibrillations for ventricular fibrillation and VA-ECMO cannulation. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries. High-sensitivity troponin increased from 27,000 ng/L to 135,000 ng/L following cardiac arrest. TTE demonstrated severe biventricular dysfunction with LVEF <20%. Given her young age, family history, severity of presentation, and absence of coronary disease, endomyocardial biopsy and expedited duo whole-genome sequencing were pursued. Biopsy demonstrated myocardial necrosis without evidence of myocarditis. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic PPA2 variant (c.514G>A; p.E172K) and a second rare PPA2 variant (c.184C>T; p.P62S). Therapeutic Intervention and Outcomes: Impella 5.5 was placed for left ventricular unloading; however, no myocardial recovery occurred. She was listed as UNOS Status 1 and underwent successful OHT. Pathologic examination of the explanted heart demonstrated extensive acute and subacute myocardial necrosis with associated scarring. The presumed trans configuration of the two PPA2 variants, together with the pathological findings and phenotypic overlap with previously reported cases, supported PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy as the diagnosis. Genetic counseling was provided, and cascade testing was recommended for at-risk relatives. Discussion: PPA2-related cardiomyopathy is a rare mitochondrial disorder associated with dilated cardiomyopathy, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death often precipitated by viral illness or alcohol exposure. This case highlights the importance of considering inherited cardiomyopathies in young patients presenting with cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, and normal coronary arteries. Rapid genomic testing established the diagnosis, guided management, and facilitated cascade screening. Early identification of affected family members may enable preventive strategies, including alcohol avoidance counseling and consideration of prophylactic ICD placement.
title: Abstract 9468: ECPR-to-Heart Transplant in a Young Woman with PPA2-Associated Metabolic Cardiomyopathy Presenting as Inferolateral STEMI

abstract: Introduction: Carcinoid heart disease classically causes serotonin-mediated right-sided valvular fibrosis. Direct myocardial or pericardial neuroendocrine tumor (NET) metastases are uncommon and may be missed when pulmonary comorbidities appear explanatory. We report dyspnea initially treated as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation but ultimately attributed to carcinoid valvopathy with intramyocardial/pericardial NET metastases. Patient Information & Clinical Findings: A 54-year-old man with COPD, pulmonary sarcoidosis, hypertension, and metastatic well-differentiated NET presented with one week of worsening dyspnea and new orthopnea after viral exposure. Outpatient exertional desaturation, wheezing, and inconsistent inhaler use supported an initial pulmonary diagnosis. Oxygen saturation was 94% on room air. A baseline echocardiogram had shown preserved ejection fraction without structural valve disease. Chest radiograph was normal, troponin downtrended, and electrocardiogram showed no acute ischemic changes. Diagnostic Assessment: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography was limited by motion but showed cardiomegaly without definite large pulmonary embolism. Transthoracic echocardiography showed left ventricular ejection fraction 55-60%, small left ventricular cavity, right ventricular dilation, severe right atrial dilation, septal flattening from right ventricular volume overload, restricted fibrotic tricuspid leaflets with moderate tricuspid regurgitation and mild-moderate tricuspid stenosis, and borderline severe pulmonary regurgitation. Prior transesophageal echocardiography showed a 1.8 х 2.2 х 1.2 cm mass infiltrating the anterior left atrial wall and a 2.0 х 2.5 cm basal right ventricular wall mass. Prior DOTATATE positron emission tomography showed radiotracer-avid myocardial and pericardial lesions, supporting cardiac metastatic NET. These findings reframed the presentation as right-sided carcinoid cardiac disease rather than isolated pulmonary disease. Therapeutic Intervention and Follow-up: Cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery recommended coronary angiography followed by bioprosthetic tricuspid and pulmonic valve replacement. The patient deferred inpatient intervention, was discharged with outpatient multidisciplinary follow-up, and continued oncologic therapy. Discussion: This case illustrates a cardio-oncology diagnostic trap: dyspnea in metastatic NET may be anchored to COPD, sarcoidosis, infection, or pulmonary embolism. Coexisting hormone-mediated carcinoid valvopathy and direct cardiac metastases create a distinct syndrome best recognized by multimodality imaging. Progressive dyspnea in metastatic NET should prompt early echocardiography and somatostatin receptor PET imaging, even when pulmonary disease appears clinically plausible.
title: Abstract 9479: When Dyspnea is Not Just COPD: Carcinoid Valvopathy with Cardiac Neuroendocrine Metastases

abstract: Background: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ApHCM) is characterized by marked asymmetric thickening of left ventricular (LV) apical or mid-to-apical segments. Hallmark electrocardiographic (ECG) features of ApHCM include giant negative T waves and tall R waves in the left precordial leads. We present two cases of ApHCM with extensive apical scarring without an aneurysm or mid-cavitary obstruction and unique ECG features. Case Description: Two elderly women, a 79-year-old (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, exertional dyspnea, chest pain, and lightheadedness) and an 81-year-old (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and exertional chest pain), were found to have precordial ST segment elevation on presentation ECG (Fig 1A and 2A) that persisted unchanged on follow-up. Marked asymmetric apical hypertrophy (Fig 1B and 2B), severe localized reduction in apical longitudinal strain (reverse apical sparing) [Fig 1C and 2C], and hyperdynamic LV systolic function without mid-cavitary or outflow tract obstruction were found on echocardiography. Cardiac MRI confirmed the presence of ApHCM (Fig 1D and 2D) with extensive scarring of the apex (Fig 1E and 2E, arrows) in the absence of an aneurysm. Genetic testing showed a pathogenic variant in the MYBPC3 gene in case 2. Discussion: Classic ECG signature of ApHCM, giant negative T waves and tall R waves in precordial leads, is widely regarded as the hallmark of this condition. Both patients in this report exhibited ST-segment elevation in multiple precordial leads. ST-segment elevation in ApHCM has been described in rare cases of ApHCM and has been attributed to apical ischemia or aneurysm leading to T wave positivation (pseudo-STEMI). In our patients with persistent ST segment elevation, however, no active ischemia or apical aneurysm was present. Conclusion: Persistent ST elevation in precordial leads in the absence of active ischemia or apical aneurysm appears to be a feature of ApHCM with widespread apical scarring (WAS), a unique sub-phenotype of ApHCM.
title: Abstract 9504: Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy with Extensive Fibrosis: A Unique ECG Phenotype

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is associated with conduction system injury that may necessitate permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation, most commonly due to atrioventricular block and new bundle branch conduction disturbances. While the incidence of PPM implantation after TAVR is well described, the natural history of post-TAVR pacemaker dependency (PMD) remains less clear. Hypothesis: We sought to characterize the incidence of PMD following post-TAVR PPM implantation at our institution and determine whether specific post-TAVR conduction disturbance patterns are associated with pacing dependence. We hypothesized that patients with high-grade conduction abnormalities would have the highest early risk of PMD but that a proportion would demonstrate recovery of intrinsic conduction. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent TAVR between 2017-2025. First, all TAVR patients were classified according to post-TAVR conduction disturbance risk groups described by El-Sabawi et al (Table 1), and subsequent PPM implantation rates were studied. Non-group 3 patients served as the lower-risk comparator group. Second, among patients who received a post-TAVR PPM, PMD was assessed using device interrogation data at 1 week and >1 month. PMD was defined as >90% ventricular pacing on device interrogation. The primary comparison was incidence of PMD between group 3 and non-group 3. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize pacing outcomes, and Fisher’s exact testing was performed to compare PMD rates between groups. Results: 70 patients underwent post-TAVR PPM implantation. Group 3 accounted for 80% of all post-TAVR PPM implantations, highlighting CHB & LBBB-related conduction injury as the predominant indication for pacing. Overall, PMD was present in 28.2% of patients at 1 week and declined to 18.6% at >1 month. Among group 3 patients who had PMD at 1 week, 36% were no longer dependent at 1-3 months, suggesting recovery of intrinsic conduction in a subset of patients. Notably, no patient who was non-dependent at the 1-week interrogation subsequently developed PMD by 1-3 months. Comparisons between group 3 and non-group 3 patients were limited by small sample size; however, Group 3 patients demonstrated an increase in PMD risk (OR 4.74, p = 0.162). Conclusion: CHB and LBBB-related conduction injury phenotypes accounted for the majority of post-TAVR PPM implantations in this cohort and appeared associated with higher PMD risk. However, recovery of intrinsic conduction was common, with more than one-third of initially dependent Group 3 patients becoming non-dependent within 3 months. The absence of new PMD among patients non-dependent at 1 week suggests that early device interrogation may help identify patients at low risk for persistent PMD. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate predictors of PMD.
title: Abstract 9509: Incidence and Predictors of Pacemaker Dependency Following TAVR: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Introduction: Descending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is a rare, life-threatening infection with mortality rates of 18-36%. Mediastinal inflammation can involve the pericardium, producing EKG changes mimicking STEMI or pericarditis. Streptococcus constellatus is an uncommon cause of DNM. We present DNM in a young healthy male initially suspected of STEMI, highlighting non-coronary etiologies of ST elevation. Clinical Findings and Timeline: A 31 year old healthy male presented with acute chest pain preceded by cough, congestion, dyspnea and fever for one week. EKG showed ST elevations in the leads II, aVL, V2, V4, V5 and ST depression in V1, suspicious of STEMI; he was loaded with aspirin and emergently transferred to ED. Tmax 100 F, hemodynamically stable. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Labs revealed leukocytosis to 25,000. Troponins were elevated but flat (239 -> 234 ng/L) and ST changes were non-contiguous, shifting suspicion towards myopericarditis. CTA chest revealed phlegmonous mediastinal soft tissue with gas bubbles consistent with necrotizing mediastinitis. Echocardiography showed a small pericardial effusion with normal LV function. Cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus. Therapeutic Interventions: Emergent right VATS with mediastinal washout was performed. Empiric vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and fluconazole were narrowed to IV ceftriaxone, transitioned to oral levofloxacin per susceptibilities, completing a 4-week course. Follow Up and Outcome: The patient recovered fully with no complications at follow-up Discussion and Synthesis: This case illustrates DNM presenting as a STEMI mimic-a rarely reported phenomenon. Acute chest pain associated with ST elevation appropriately raised the suspicion of STEMI, however non-contiguous lead distribution, flat troponins and viral prodrome were critical clues against ACS. CTA chest proved pivotal, revealing the underlying process coronary angiography alone would have missed. Early surgical drainage with targeted antibiotics remains the cornerstone of DNM management, with the cervicothoracic approach reducing mortality from 47% to 19%. ST elevation has broad differentials beyond ACS and pericarditis; cross sectional imaging should be pursued when EKG findings are atypical. Clinicians should maintain high suspicion for mediastinal pathology when chest pain, fever and EKG changes that do not conform to a single coronary territory.
title: Abstract 9517: ST Elevation Beyond the Coronaries: A Case of Necrotizing Mediastinitis

abstract: Background: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) has become a promising noninvasive biomarker for rejection surveillance after heart transplantation (HT). Prior adult studies have suggested associations between elevated dd-cfDNA and rejection as well as demographic and peri-HT clinical factors. Multicenter longitudinal pediatric data remain limited. We sought to analyze clinical characteristics associated with persistent dd-cfDNA elevation during the first year post-HT using the Pediatric Heart Transplant Society (PHTS) Registry. Methods: We performed a retrospective multicenter analysis of pediatric primary HT recipients with dd-cfDNA testing using AlloSure (CareDx, Inc., Brisbane, CA, USA) recorded in the PHTS Registry between November 2023 and June 2025. Recipients with ≥1 surveillance dd-cfDNA measurement within the first year post-HT were compared using the threshold of 0.2% as elevated. Longitudinal analyses included recipients with ≥3 surveillance measurements in the first year post-HT. Comparisons were focused on recipients with persistently low dd-cfDNA (0% elevated measurements) or persistently elevated dd-cfDNA (>50% elevated measurements). Results: A total of 5,372 dd-cfDNA measurements were identified. Among recipients with ≥1 surveillance measurement within the first year post-HT (N=238), elevated dd-cfDNA (≥0.2%) was more commonly observed earlier after HT (74.3±83.0 vs 152.9±111.8 days, p<0.0001) and was associated with younger recipient age (6.9±6.1 vs 8.8±6.5 years, p=0.015), smaller recipient body surface area (BSA) (0.9±0.5 vs 1.1±0.6m 2 , p=0.008), and history of rejection prior to dd-cfDNA testing (20.4% vs 8.9%, p=0.005). Among recipients with ≥3 surveillance measurements within the first year post-HT (N=170), 55 had persistently low dd-cfDNA while 36 had persistently elevated dd-cfDNA. Compared to those with persistently low dd-cfDNA, persistently elevated dd-cfDNA was associated with younger recipient age at transplant (5.6±6.1 vs 10.1±6.3 years, p=0.001), smaller recipient BSA (0.8±0.6 vs 1.2±0.5m 2 , p=0.004), and younger donor age (8.4±9.8 vs 12.9±7.8 years, p=0.018). Most notably, persistently elevated dd-cfDNA was more frequently observed among recipients with a history of rejection during the first year post-HT (50.0% vs 5.6%, p<0.0001). Other demographic factors including pre-HT PRA value, recipient race, primary diagnosis, ischemic time, donor weight mismatch, and mechanical circulatory support had no significant differences. Conclusion: In this early multicenter pediatric experience, persistent dd-cfDNA elevation appeared to correlate with recipient and donor size and age characteristics as well as rejection history.
title: Abstract 9534: Experience and Trends in Donor-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients in the Early Post-Transplant Period: An Analysis Using the Pediatric Heart Transplant Society (PHTS) Registry

abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the standard of care for severe aortic stenosis in elderly and frail populations. Although rates of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and mortality increase with age, age dependent differences in comorbidity burden and risk factors following TAVR remain incompletely characterized. Methods: This single center retrospective chart review was conducted at a tertiary care center in New Jersey and included 502 patients who underwent TAVR between 2023 and 2026. Patients were stratified by decade of life (60s, 70s, 80s, and 90s). Baseline comorbidities including atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, obesity, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, conduction abnormalities, prior permanent pacemaker implantation, peripheral vascular disease, prior cerebrovascular accident, prior coronary artery bypass grafting, and prior myocardial infarction were evaluated. MACE was defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Outcomes were assessed from the date of TAVR through April 2026. Trends in outcomes across age cohorts were analyzed using the Cochran-Armitage trend test. Age-stratified multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify predictors of MACE and all cause mortality. Results: Among the study population, 10.5% of patients were in their 60s, 33.3% in their 70s, 41.4% in their 80s, and 13.7% in their 90s. Rates of MACE and all cause mortality increased significantly with advancing age, from 6% in patients in their 60s to 21% in patients in their 90s (p=0.049). The prevalence of obesity and diabetes mellitus decreased with increasing age (both p<0.001), whereas atrial fibrillation (p<0.001), prior permanent pacemaker implantation (p=0.013), and right bundle branch block (p=0.009) became increasingly prevalent across older age cohorts. Other studied comorbidities did not significantly differ per decade. In multivariable analysis, atrial fibrillation was independently associated with increased risk of MACE and all cause mortality among patients in their 80s and 90s (OR 4.58, 95% CI 2.121-10.599, p<0.001). No independent predictors of adverse outcomes were identified among patients in their 60s and 70s. Conclusions: Risk of adverse outcomes following TAVR increases with advancing age; however, comorbidity burden and predictors of adverse outcomes vary substantially across age cohorts. These findings suggest that age-specific risk profiles may better characterize post-TAVR risk than chronological age alone. Atrial fibrillation was strongly associated with adverse outcomes among patients ≥80 years old and may represent an important target for future risk stratification strategies specific in elderly TAVR populations.
title: Abstract 9549: Age-Dependent Predictors of Major Adverse Cardiac Events and Mortality Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Atrial Fibrillation as a Key Risk Factor in Older Adults

abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in adolescents and young adults without an identifiable cause presents a significant diagnostic challenge. Disorders of mitochondrial aminoacyl-transfer RNA synthetases (mt-aaRS) are uncommon causes of DCM and are typically associated with significant neurodevelopmental disease. Cardiac involvement has been infrequently reported in PARS2-associated mitochondrial disease. We present a case of advanced DCM in an adolescent with PARS2 deficiency and relatively preserved neurologic function requiring orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT), highlighting the limitations of lactate as a hemodynamic surrogate in mitochondrial disease. An 18-year-old woman with developmental delay, mild intellectual disability, and hypotonia presented with progressive dyspnea, lower extremity edema, abdominal distention, and malaise. One month prior, she had been empirically treated for community acquired pneumonia without improvement in her symptoms. Initial evaluation showed elevated lactate (3.8 mmol/L) and cardiac biomarkers, marked transaminitis, and severe biventricular dilation with left ventricular ejection fraction less than 15% on transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Viral myocarditis was initially considered; however, the infectious workup was unrevealing. Given her developmental delay, hypotonia, and unexplained severe cardiomyopathy at a young age, genetic testing was pursued and identified biallelic pathogenic variants in PARS2, consistent with an mt-aaRS disorder. Inotropic support and diuresis were initiated for cardiogenic shock. Her cardiac index (CI) further declined, prompting escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS). She was initially supported with an intra-aortic balloon pump, which was advanced to an Impella 5.5. Notably, lactate remained elevated (2.4-4.1 mmol/L) despite improvement in CI from 1.69 to 3.8 L/min/m 2 . Although hemodynamics improved with support, her clinical status continued to deteriorate and lactate increased to 8.8 mmol/L, prompting escalation of support to veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and subsequent OHT. At eight months after OHT, TTE showed normal biventricular function and surveillance biopsy was without allograft rejection. No progression of neurologic deficits has been observed. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of PARS2-associated mitochondrial disease, demonstrating that advanced DCM can predominate in adolescence despite only mild neurologic impairment. It also highlights that lactate measurements cannot reliably distinguish inadequate perfusion from intrinsic metabolic dysfunction in patients with mitochondrial disease. In this population, invasive hemodynamics, end-organ perfusion markers, and clinical trajectory should guide assessment of circulatory adequacy and escalation of support rather than lactate trends alone.
title: Abstract 9552: PARS2 Deficiency Presenting as Advanced Dilated Cardiomyopathy Requiring Heart Transplantation: A Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high short-term mortality despite increasing use of Impella support, with or without veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) has been reported to be associated with outcomes in critically ill populations, including septic shock; however, evidence regarding its prognostic utility during Impella support in CS remains limited. Purpose: To evaluate the prognostic utility of serial LAR after Impella initiation and to identify the optimal time point for predicting 30-day mortality in patients with CS. Methods: This was a single-center, retrospective observational study of patients with CS who received Impella support between April 2018 and March 2026. First, ROC analyses were performed in the overall cohort of 267 patients to compare the discriminative ability of LAR measured at baseline and at 24, 48, and 72 hours after Impella initiation for 30-day mortality. Because 48-hour LAR showed the best discrimination, subsequent analyses focused on 48-hour LAR. For these analyses, patients who died within 48 hours after Impella initiation were excluded, and 252 patients with available 48-hour LAR were included. Patients were stratified into quartiles according to 48-hour LAR, and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed for 30-day mortality. Independent associations were evaluated using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, including adjustment for age, sex, acute coronary syndrome, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, support strategy, 0-48-hour net fluid balance, and pre-MCS SCAI stage. Results: In the overall cohort of 267 patients, 48-hour LAR demonstrated the highest discriminative ability for 30-day mortality, with an AUC of 0.784, compared with 0.652 at baseline, 0.725 at 24 hours, and 0.779 at 72 hours. The optimal cutoff value of 48-hour LAR was 0.478, with a sensitivity of 71.3% and specificity of 71.7%. Among the 252 patients included in the 48-hour LAR analysis, 107 died within 30 days. Thirty-day mortality increased stepwise across quartiles of 48-hour LAR: 14.3%, 33.3%, 44.4%, and 77.8% from Q1 to Q4, respectively. Log-transformed 48-hour LAR remained independently associated with 30-day mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio 2.780, 95% confidence interval 2.083-3.711; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion: Among serial LAR measurements after Impella initiation, 48-hour LAR showed the strongest discrimination for 30-day mortality. In patients surviving beyond 48 hours, higher 48-hour LAR was independently associated with 30-day mortality and may serve as a simple early treatment-response marker for short-term risk stratification during Impella support.
title: Abstract 9554: The 48-hour Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio Predicts 30-day Mortality in Cardiogenic Shock Patients Treated with Impella

abstract: Background: Permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation remains a recognized complication following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) is a well-established predictor of post-TAVR PPM. Whether obesity influences this relationship is unclear. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing TAVR at a tertiary care center between 2023 and 2026. After excluding 69 patients with a pre-existing PPM, the primary cohort consisted of 433 patients. The primary outcome was new PPM implantation after TAVR. Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m 2 . Crude PPM rates were compared across obesity and baseline RBBB with Wilson 95% CI for each proportion of the cohort. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of PPM implantation adjusting for sex, baseline RBBB, baseline left bundle branch block, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, ejection fraction category, and STS risk category. Effect modification of obesity on the RBBB and PPM association was evaluated by adding an obesity and RBBB interaction into the multivariable model. Results: Among the 433 patients undergoing TAVR, 142 were obese and 291were non-obese. The overall incidence of new PPM implantation was 19.6%. Obesity was not associated with increased risk of PPM implantation compared to non-obese (21.1% vs. 18.9%; OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.70-1.89, p=0.607). Baseline RBBB was strongly associated with PPM implantation (46.9% vs. 14.9%; OR 5.04, 95% CI 2.85-8.89, p<0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, baseline conduction abnormalities, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, ejection fraction category, and STS risk category, baseline RBBB remained an independent predictor of PPM implantation (OR 4.79, 95% CI 2.58-8.96, p<0.001). PPM implantation rates were 12.6% among non-obese patients without RBBB, 53.3% among non-obese patients with RBBB, 19.5% among obese patients without RBBB, and 31.6% among obese patients with RBBB. In a multivariable model including an obesity-by-RBBB interaction term, significant effect modification was observed (interaction OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.05-0.80, p=0.025), indicating attenuation of the association between baseline RBBB and PPM implantation among obese patients. Conclusions: Obesity was not independently associated with post-TAVR PPM implantation. However, obesity significantly modified the association between baseline RBBB and PPM requirement, with the baseline RBBB effect concentrated among non obese patients. These findings suggest that obesity status should be incorporated when using baseline RBBB to risk stratify patients for post TAVR conduction disturbances and warrant validation in larger multicenter studies.
title: Abstract 9572: Obesity Modifies the Association Between Baseline Right Bundle Branch Block and Permanent Pacemaker Implantation Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Single Center Retrospective Cohort

abstract: Introduction/Background: The optimal role of reperfusion therapy in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism remains controversial. Although reperfusion improves right ventricular function and reduces clinical deterioration, its impact on mortality has been inconsistent. Research Question/Hypothesis: We hypothesized that prevention of right ventricular decompensation is the dominant clinical determinant of benefit from reperfusion strategies in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism. Methods/Approach: We performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of comparative studies evaluating systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed therapies, or mechanical thrombectomy versus anticoagulation alone in adults with intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism. The primary endpoint was hemodynamic decompensation or clinical deterioration. Secondary endpoints included composite adverse clinical outcomes, all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and minor bleeding. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were pooled. Results: Fourteen studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the quantitative synthesis. Reperfusion strategies significantly reduced hemodynamic decompensation compared with anticoagulation alone (RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.17-0.50; p<0.001; I 2 =18.5%). A similar reduction was observed for composite adverse clinical outcomes (RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.20-0.42; p<0.001; I 2 =0%), supporting right ventricular decompensation as a key driver of overall clinical benefit. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.49-1.09; p=0.12; I 2 =0%) or major bleeding (RR 1.33, 95% CI 0.70-2.54; p=0.38; I 2 =55.6%). However, minor bleeding was significantly more frequent with reperfusion strategies (RR 2.06, 95% CI 1.29-3.29; p=0.003; I 2 =0%). Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent reductions in hemodynamic decompensation across study designs and reperfusion modalities. Conclusions: In intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism, reperfusion strategies substantially reduce hemodynamic decompensation and adverse clinical outcomes without a demonstrated mortality benefit. The nearly identical treatment effects observed for hemodynamic decompensation and composite adverse outcomes suggest that prevention of right ventricular failure is the principal mechanism underlying the clinical benefit of reperfusion therapy.
title: Abstract 9574: Right Ventricular Decompensation and Clinical Benefit of Reperfusion in Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Anomalous origin of left main coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsava is a rare condition found in 0.03-0.15% of the general population. It is a malignant condition as it predisposes to ischemia, leading to death resulting from myocardial infarctions, particularly if the anomalous blood vessel travels posteriorly between the pulmonary artery and aorta. Despite having been noted in up to 21% of patients with aortic origin of coronary artery (AAOCA), STEMI resulting from anomalous LMCA is an uncommon phenomenon. The discovery of ITP further complicates the case. Case: Patient is a 64-year-old man with history of HTN, HLD, and type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented to the hospital with 2-day history of substernal chest discomfort with ration to his back. In the ER he was found to have inferior ST elevation, and he was urgently taken to the cath lab. Left heart catheterization reported anomalous left main which arises from the right sinus of Valsalva with a 75% mid LAD lesion. Coronary CTA revealed the course of the anomalous left main between the aorta and pulmonary artery, associated with luminal narrowing, representing a high-risk malignant coronary anomaly. A TTE reported normal LVEF of 55-60%. The patient was initially started on heparin, aspirin and statin however he was noted to have thrombocytopenia, so aspirin and heparin was held. Hematology/oncology attributed the thrombocytopenia to an immune mediated process secondary to recent viral infection. Given the complexity of the anatomy of his case, the patient was referred to a tertiary center for evaluation by adult congenital service. Discussion: Anomalous left main coronary artery arising from the right sinus of Valsalva represents a rare type of AAOCA associated with increased mortality, including an interarterial location, intramural segment, slit-like origin, and sharp take-off from its ostium. According to ACC/AHA guidelines for 2025, surgical treatment is mandatory for symptomatic patients suffering from ischemia due to the anomaly (Class I). Additionally, the treatment is recommended (Class IIa) in asymptomatic patients suffering from anomalous left main coronary artery. CABG is the method of choice for surgical treatment if there is coexisting atherosclerotic disease. In this case, the diagnosis of ITP added another difficulty. Thrombocytopenia makes it impossible to administer antiplatelet medication required for post-myocardial infarction treatment. Antiplatelets should be avoided if platelet counts drop below 30 х 10 9 /L. Intravenous immunoglobulin and corticosteroid administration helps increase the number of platelets before the procedure. This case emphasizes the necessity of the detection of coronary anomalies during urgent angiography and coordination among specialists dealing with malignant coronary anomaly and thrombocytopenia complicating the surgical procedure.
title: Abstract 9581: The Perfect Storm: Malignant Coronary Anomaly, Atherosclerosis, and Thrombocytopenia Converging in Acute STEMI

abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery aneurysms (CAAs) represent the most consequential sequela of Kawasaki disease (KD). These aneurysms are prone to mural thrombus formation, increasing risk of coronary occlusion, myocardial infarction, and sudden cardiac death. Although thrombotic risk peaks within the first 2 years, coronary occlusion can progress over decades. Consequently, acute coronary syndromes in adolescents are rare, and management pathway remains poorly defined. Case: A 16-year-old female with atypical KD diagnosed at age 11, complicated by giant CAAs of the left main (LM), left anterior descending (LAD) artery, and right coronary artery (RCA), presented with one day of substernal chest pain and emesis. Previous surveillance with stress cardiac magnetic resonance and coronary CT angiography (CCTA) demonstrated no perfusion defects or inducible ischemia. High-sensitivity troponin I peaked at 25,896 ng/L, and a 12-lead ECG revealed new T-wave inversions in V1-V3. She was admitted to the pediatric ICU for management of NSTEMI and started on therapeutic heparin and aspirin. Diagnostic Assessment: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated new inferior wall motion abnormality (WMA), mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF 52%), and reduced right ventricular systolic function (TAPSE 1.57 cm). Coronary angiography (CA) demonstrated heavy thrombus burden in a large proximal RCA aneurysm (10-12 mm) with total thrombotic occlusion of the proximal-to-mid RCA and TIMI 0 flow (Fig 2C), saccular aneurysms of the LM, LAD, and proximal circumflex without obstructive disease (Fig 2A, 2B), and well-developed left-to-right collaterals reconstituting the posterior descending and posterolateral branches (Fig 2D). Management and Outcome: Given hemodynamic stability, established collaterals, and resolution of chest pain at the time of CA, no intervention was performed as the procedural risk of intervening on a heavily thrombotic aneurysm outweighed the benefit. A repeat TTE showed resolution of the WMA with normalized biventricular function. She was transitioned to apixaban and clopidogrel and discharged with pediatric cardiology follow-up. Outpatient CCTA confirmed chronic RCA occlusion with distal reconstitution and stable aneurysmal burden (Fig 4A). Discussion: CAAs carry a lifelong thrombotic threat that persists beyond the acute phase of KD and can cause infarction despite reassuring functional surveillance. Bilateral involvement confers the highest risk, and absent inducible ischemia does not exclude impending thrombosis. In a patient with mature collaterals, intensive anticoagulation may be a viable alternative to high-risk revascularization. Consistent with the 2024 AHA statement on KD and CAAs, combined antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy, including a direct oral anticoagulant, offers a practical secondary-prevention strategy.
title: Abstract 9583: A Decade of Latency: Coronary Aneurysm Thrombosis in an Adolescent with Treated Kawasaki Disease

abstract: Background: Sex-based differences in TAVR hemodynamics and valvular outcomes are incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the effect of TAVR on bystander valve disease. We assessed sex-specific differences in pre- and post-procedural valvular function in a consecutive TAVR cohort. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of consecutive TAVR patients at a single urban center from January 2022 to September 2025. Factors such as valve type, pre- and post-procedural AVA, mean gradient, and mitral/tricuspid regurgitation (MR/TR) severity were compared by sex using chi-square or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U for continuous variables. Results: In total, there were 245 subjects of which 132 (53.9%) were women and 113 men. Women at baseline had a smaller AVA size (0.7 vs 0.8 cm 2 , p<0.01) and higher mean gradients (42.5 vs 35.5 mmHg, p<0.01). Baseline MR and TR severity did not differ between sexes (moderate-or-greater [mod+] MR: 33.8% vs 30.4%, p=0.66; mod+ TR: 26.9% vs 26.4%, p=1.00). Post-TAVR, women achieved significantly smaller valve areas (1.5 vs 1.9 cm 2 , p<0.01) and higher residual gradients (12.9 vs 10.5 mmHg, p<0.01). Among the valve types used balloon-expandable valves [BEV] (Sapien 3/Ultra/Resilia) were used in 80.8% and self-expanding valves [SEV] (Evolut/Navitor) in 18.8%, with no significant difference by sex (p=0.33). Despite similar baseline MR, moderate-or-greater post-procedural MR was significantly more prevalent in women (20.5% vs 5.1%; OR 4.8, p<0.01). It was also notable that baseline mitral stenosis was more common in women (20.5% vs 7.1%, p<0.01). Post-procedural TR was found to not differ by sex (p=0.39). Conclusions: Women undergoing TAVR showed increased post-procedural gradients and a fourfold higher rate of persistent moderate-or-greater MR despite equivalent baseline MR severity and similar BEV/SEV distribution. The clinical implications of these findings remain to be elucidated.
title: Abstract 9590: A Tale of Two Valves: Sex Differences in Hemodynamic Recovery and Residual Mitral Regurgitation After TAVR

abstract: Background: TAPSE/RVSP, the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to right ventricular systolic pressure, is an echocardiographic surrogate of RV-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling that integrates contractile reserve with afterload. Its comparative prognostic value versus TAPSE alone has not been established in large, contemporary percutaneous mitral valve cohorts. Hypothesis: Pre-procedural RV-PA uncoupling (TAPSE/RVSP ≤0.33 mm/mmHg) independently predicts long-term all-cause mortality and outperforms TAPSE alone in patients undergoing transcatheter mitral edge-to-edge repair (mTEER) or transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Methods: This retrospective analysis included 525 consecutive patients undergoing mTEER or TMVR at Mayo Clinic (January 2015-December 2025). Uncoupled was defined as TAPSE/RVSP ≤0.33 mm/mmHg (n=259) versus coupled >0.33 (n=266). Kaplan-Meier survival estimates were compared by likelihood ratio testing. Cox proportional hazards models with restricted cubic splines evaluated TAPSE/RVSP and TAPSE as mortality predictors, unadjusted and adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, LVEF, and MR severity. Discrimination was assessed by C-index and adequacy index. Interaction analyses by sex and procedure type were performed. Results: Among 525 patients, 186 deaths occurred over median follow-up 2.8 years (IQR: 0.8-5.2). Uncoupled patients had significantly worse survival at 1 year (74.7% vs. 89.2%), 3 years (56.7% vs. 72.6%), and 5 years (38.8% vs. 58.3%; p=0.002), with early and sustained curve divergence. ( Figure 1 ) Abnormal TAPSE (≤1.7 cm) also predicted worse outcomes, though with less distinct separation (p=0.021). ( Figure 2 ) In unadjusted analysis, TAPSE/RVSP outperformed TAPSE alone (C-index: 0.619 vs. 0.585; adequacy: 0.99 vs. 0.45). After multivariable adjustment, TAPSE/RVSP remained an independent predictor (HR: 1.74, 95% CI: 1.12-2.68; p=0.002), whereas TAPSE lost significance (p=0.122). Partial effects plots demonstrated a monotonic inverse association between TAPSE/RVSP and log-relative hazard in unadjusted (p<0.001) and adjusted (p=0.002) models; TAPSE splines attenuated to non-significance after adjustment. TAPSE/RVSP provided incremental prognostic value beyond TAPSE (partial χ 2 =10.0, p=0.018). ( Figure 3 ) Conclusion: Pre-procedural RV-PA uncoupling assessed by TAPSE/RVSP is a superior independent predictor of long-term mortality after percutaneous mitral valve interventions compared to TAPSE alone, with consistent effect across sex and procedure type. Routine pre-procedural reporting of TAPSE/RVSP may improve risk stratification for patients undergoing mTEER or TMVR.
title: Abstract 9614: Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling as a Superior Predictor of Long-Term Mortality After Percutaneous Mitral Valve Interventions: A Retrospective Single-Center Experience

abstract: Introduction: Unfractionated heparin (UFH), due to its rapid onset of action and widespread use during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI), has been proposed as a strategy to enhance pre-procedural coronary reperfusion in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), in whom PPCI remains the standard reperfusion therapy. Early restoration of infarct-related artery patency before primary PCI improves myocardial perfusion and outcomes. However, the efficacy of UFH pretreatment in STEMI patients undergoing PPCI remains unclear and needs further study. Hypothesis: We sought to determine if pre-treatment with UFH improves coronary reperfusion and clinical outcomes compared with standard care in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. Methods: A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus and the Cochrane Library from inception until May 2025. All randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared unfractionated heparin pre-treatment to standard care in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI (PROSPERO CRD420261405363) were included. Data were extracted for angiographic, clinical and safety outcomes. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals were estimated from random-effects models using the I 2 statistical heterogeneity. Results: A total of five RCTs comprising 12,288 participants were included in the analysis. Pre-PCI TIMI flow grade 2-3 or 3 was significantly higher in the UFH group (RR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.37-1.57; P < 0.01, I 2 = 0%). Post-PCI TIMI flow grade 3 showed a statistically significant but minimal improvement (RR = 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.01; P = 0.03; I 2 = 0%). All-cause mortality (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.75-1.08; P = 0.25; I 2 = 0%) and major bleeding were not significantly different between groups (RR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.60-1.61; P = 0.94), with no evidence of heterogeneity across studies. Conclusion: In STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, UFH pre-treatment is associated with improved early coronary reperfusion but does not increase major bleeding or the need for blood transfusion compared to standard care. These results are consistent with a procedural advantage of UFH pre-treatment to improve infarct-related artery patency within modern STEMI networks.
title: Abstract 9624: Upstream versus Routine Unfractionated Heparin in STEMI Patients Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: Functional recovery after aortic valve replacement (AVR) remains heterogeneous despite procedural success. The effectiveness of structured cardiac rehabilitation (CR) in improving recovery after both surgical and transcatheter AVR remains unclear. Research Question: We evaluated the comparative effectiveness of CR versus usual care following surgical or transcatheter AVR and examined whether outcomes varied according to procedure type, rehabilitation modality, timing of initiation, and program duration. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of randomized and comparative observational studies. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through January 2026. Eligible studies included adults who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR and compared structured exercise-based CR with usual care or no CR. Mean differences and risk ratios were pooled using random-effects models; correlated estimates from overlapping populations were handled using dependency-adjusted multilevel models with cluster-robust variance. Prespecified subgroup and leave-one-out analyses explored heterogeneity. Results: Fourteen reports met the inclusion criteria, and 12 contributed to quantitative synthesis.
