Compared with the non-hemolysis group, the hemolysis group had significantly lower drainage pressures at intensive care unit admission (–104 [–137 to –66] vs. –30 [–47 to –7] mmHg, p=0.017) and at 24 hours (–87 [–112 to –54] vs. –16 [–42 to –1] mmHg, p=0.005), as well as significantly higher pump head pressure at 24 hours (343 [298-397] vs. 188 [148-203] mmHg, p=0.003). Exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression analysis demonstrated that minimum drainage pressure (OR 0.58 per 10-mmHg increase, 95% CI 0.23-0.91, p<0.001) and maximum pump head pressure (OR 1.14 per 10-mmHg increase, 95% CI 1.01-1.37, p=0.017) were associated with hemolysis. Conclusions: More negative drainage pressure and higher pump head pressure during the early phase of V-A ECMO support were associated with hemolysis, as assessed by reduced serum haptoglobin levels. These ECMO circuit pressure parameters may serve as indicators associated with early hemolysis during V-A ECMO support.
title: Abstract P2072: Association of Drainage Pressure and Pump Head Pressure with Early Hemolysis During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Support: A Retrospective Study

abstract: Introduction: The effects of global ischemia-reperfusion injury on the brain have been widely studied in cardiac arrest animal models, and moderate therapeutic hypothermia (MTH) remains a promising treatment. However, its mechanisms are still unclear, and benefits seen in animals have not fully translated to humans, possibly because target temperature is reached too late after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Methods: Male Sprague Dawley rats (Charles River Laboratories) with a weight between 450-800g were subjected to 8 minutes of ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest (VFCA) and resuscitated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (eCPR) (n=33). Sham-operated animals (n= 6) served as controls. After ROSC, animals were randomized into three groups: Normothermia (NT, n=16), Immediate MTH with 33 ± 0.5 °C for 12 h (HT, n=9), and delayed MTH with cooling initiation 2h after ROSC following 33 ± 0.5 °C for 12 h (dHT, n=8). Over the course of 72 hours animals were evaluated using the Neurologic deficit score (NDS) and Overall performance category (OPC) daily. Then brains of five animals per group were fixed in formalin, embedded in paraffin and stained with hematoxylin and eosin. Neuronal necrosis was assessed semi-quantitatively in the hippocampal CA1 region. Results: Survival after 72h was 100% in both MTH groups (immediate: 9/9; delayed: 8/8) compared to 50% in the NT group (8/16), with all sham animals surviving to the study endpoint (6/6).At 72 hours, NDS scores differed significantly across groups (Kruskal-Wallis: p < 0.001). Both HT and dHT groups demonstrated significantly lower NDS scores compared to NT controls (p < 0.001 and p < 0.001, respectively). Importantly, HT showed superior neurological recovery compared to dHT(p = 0.020). OPC scores at 72 hours likewise differed significantly across groups (Kruskal-Wallis: p < 0.001). Both MTH groups demonstrated significantly improved OPC compared to NT controls (HT: p < 0.001; dHT: p = 0.002), with HT achieving superior outcomes compared to dHT (p = 0.022). Neither sham animals nor MTH groups showed neuronal necrosis in the hippocampus, while all NT animals exhibited marked neuronal necrosis. Conclusion: In this VFCA eCPR model, MTH showed clear beneficial effects, but delaying cooling by just two hours markedly reduced its neuroprotective and overall benefit. Interestingly, the histological findings only showed a significant difference between NT and HT+dHT, not between HT and dHT.
title: Abstract P2073: Effects of Delayed Treatment with Moderate Therapeutic Hypothermia in a 72-Hour Survival Rat Model of 8-Minute Ventricular Fibrillation Cardiac Arrest Resuscitated with eCPR

abstract: Introduction: Survival with favorable neurologic outcome from pediatric OHCA is poor and there are few data regarding who may benefit from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). We aimed to describe institutional use of post-arrest ECMO, characterize clinical features associated with ECMO initiation, and compare outcomes between ECMO-treated patients and post-OHCA patients not treated with ECMO. Hypothesis: Children treated with post-arrest ECMO support represent a highly selected subgroup with greater post-arrest hemodynamic instability but will have similar favorable neurologic survival compared with post-OHCA patients not treated with ECMO. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of pediatric OHCA patients achieving ROSC, admitted to the pediatric ICU or cardiac ICU not at their neurologic baseline, and requiring invasive mechanical ventilation between 2017-2025 using prospectively collected event data. Descriptive statistics compared patients treated with post-arrest ECMO to non-ECMO treated patients. Favorable neurologic survival was defined as PCPC 1-2 or no change from baseline. Results: Among 217 OHCA patients included, 12 (5.5%) received post-arrest ECMO support. Median times from ROSC and hospital admission to cannulation were 358 (229-545) and 143 (111-353) minutes; 75% received veno-arterial ECMO. Compared with the non-ECMO cohort, ECMO-treated patients demonstrated greater post-arrest cardiopulmonary instability within 6 hours of admission, including higher vasoactive infusion score (VIS) [27.0 (5.0-52.5) vs 1.9 (0.0-10.8); p=0.002], lactate [8.1 (5.5-12.1) vs 4.7 (2.8-7.7); p=0.02], PaCO 2 [51.0 (35.3-61.0) vs 37.5 (31.6-44.5); p=0.01], and FiO 2 [60.0 (30.0-100.0) vs 43.3 (29.6-71.7); p=0.19]. All ECMO-treated patients had an initial GCS of 3T or NT. No ECMO-treated patient had pre-cannulation acute brain injury or bleed on head CT. Favorable neurologic survival was 33.3% (4/12) among ECMO-treated patients and 32.7% (67/205) among non-ECMO treated patients. Conclusion: Post-arrest ECMO after pediatric OHCA was used infrequently. Despite greater post-arrest hemodynamic instability within 6 hours of admission, ECMO-treated patients demonstrated comparable favorable neurologic survival to the broader ICU OHCA cohort. These data provide an initial description of post-arrest ECMO utilization and outcomes after pediatric OHCA. Larger multicenter studies are needed to identify patients most likely to benefit from post-arrest ECMO support.
title: Abstract P2074: Institutional Selection Patterns and Outcomes of ECMO Initiated After ROSC Following Pediatric OHCA

abstract: Introduction: Mitochondrial dysfunction severely impacts neurological recovery after cardiac arrest (CA). While extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) improves cerebral blood flow post-CA compared to conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CCPR), its impact on brain mitochondrial function, critical for neuronal survival, is unknown. This study addresses this gap. Research Question: Does ECPR preserve cerebral mitochondrial function more effectively than CCPR after refractory asphyxial CA due to superior circulatory support? Aim: Our primary goal was to compare the effects of ECPR and CCPR on brain mitochondrial respiratory capacity in the cerebral cortex and hippocampal CA1 following refractory asphyxial CA in rats. Methods: Male Wistar rats underwent refractory asphyxial CA. CCPR consisted of chest compressions, ventilation, and epinephrine administration, whereas ECPR utilized veno-arterial extracorporeal circulation to restore systemic perfusion. Resuscitation with CCPR or ECPR began 20 minutes after asphyxia initiation. Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) was defined as a sustained MAP ≥ 60 mmHg. Cardiac function by echocardiography was monitored at 30 and 60 minutes post-ROSC. At 60 minutes post-ROSC, high-resolution respirometry was used to assess mitochondrial oxygen consumption in permeabilized brain cortical and hippocampal CA1. Results: ECPR achieved a higher ROSC rate than CCPR (83.3 % [5/6] vs. 42.3 % [11/26]). ECPR significantly improved cardiac function post-ROSC. At 60 minutes post-ROSC, fractional shortening (FS) was higher in ECPR (49.9 ± 4.8 %) vs. CCPR (22.8 ± 7.9 %; P < 0.01, Fig 1a). Stroke volume (SV) was also significantly preserved in ECPR at 30 and 60 minutes post-ROSC (at 60 min: ECPR 0.53 ± 0.13 ml vs. CCPR 0.19 ± 0.08 ml; P < 0.05, Fig 1b). Pyruvate/malate stimulated oxidative phosphorylation was significantly lower in both cortex and CA1 in the CCPR group when compared to the Naive group (Cortex: Naive 1.00 ± 0.16, vs. CCPR 0.83 ± 0.13, CA1: Naïve 1.00 ± 0.16, vs. CCPR 0.76 ± 0.21, both P < 0.05) (Fig 2a) and further uncoupling maintained reduced oxygen consumption in the CCPR group (CA1: Naive 1.00 ± 0.18, vs. CCPR 0.78 ± 0.14, P < 0.05) (Fig 2b). Conclusions: ECPR improved ROSC rate and cardiac function while preserving cerebral mitochondrial function compared with CCPR following refractory CA. These findings suggest that ECPR may mitigate early mitochondrial injury in vulnerable brain regions after CA.
title: Abstract P2075: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Preserves Cerebral Mitochondrial Function After Refractory Cardiac Arrest in Rats

abstract: Introduction: Nearly 15,00 children experience pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (pIHCA) in the US annually, yet limited research has investigated the reasons for death following acute survival from these events. Aims: To characterize modes and timing of death among children who achieved return of circulation (ROC) after pIHCA Methods: Single center retrospective study of children who achieved ROC after IHCA but died prior to discharge from 2013 to 2023. Modes of death were defined by either refractory organ failure leading to death without attempted resuscitation or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies (WLST) within the following categories: neurologic, circulatory, respiratory or other comorbidities. Recurrent arrest was defined as re-arrest with attempted but unsuccessful resuscitation. Intergroup characteristics were compared using Fisher’s exact, Chi-squared and Kruskal Wallis tests. Results: Of the 122 patients included in the study, circulatory failure (n=45; 37%) and recurrent arrest (n=27; 22%) accounted for the majority of deaths, followed by neurologic causes in 20 patients (16%) and respiratory and other comorbidities in 15 patients (12%) each (p<0.001). Pre-arrest characteristics varied by mode of death, including age, race and illness category (Table 1). The only event characteristic which varied by group was exposure to ECPR, with the highest rates in the neurologic and circulatory categories (Table 2). In the post-arrest phase, procurement of brain imaging and EEG varied by mode of death, with the highest rates for both in the neurologic category (Table 3).Finally, median time to death after initial arrest varied between groups, with the longest duration in circulatory group and the shortest in the re-arrest group; (p<0.001 Table 3). Conclusions: In this single center retrospective cohort study, we found that children who died following successful resuscitation from pIHCA were most likely to die due to non-neurologic causes, indicating that pIHCA occurs in the context of complex critical illness. Therefore, pIHCA may serve as a complication of severe illness rather than the direct cause of death in many patients. These findings are in contrast with prior work in children who die after resuscitation from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with deaths more likely related to neurologic causes from prolonged arrest. This distinction is key to interpreting long-term outcomes in pIHCA which are often influenced by factors unrelated to the arrest.
title: Abstract P2086: Modes of Death Following In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single Center Study

abstract: BACKGROUND: In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches–Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown. METHODS: Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality. RESULTS: Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87–1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84–1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834–2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885–2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of −99 days (−245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT01985360

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of the randomised ISCHEMIA-CKD trial; 777 participants (388 to INV and 389 to CON), median 8 years, 429 deaths.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size gives wide intervals, and cause-specific mortality classification in advanced CKD is imprecise.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of ISCHEMIA-CKD found no long-term mortality benefit from an initial invasive strategy in advanced CKD with moderate or severe ischaemia.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87-1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84-1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It extends the evidence for conservative-first management in a population largely excluded from other revascularisation trials.

authors: on behalf of the ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND Research Group
title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND

abstract: Management of prehospital hemorrhagic shock and traumatic cardiac arrest remains a critical capability gap in trauma resuscitation. Hybrid endovascular and extracorporeal technologies and techniques are evolving to meet the challenges of noncompressible hemorrhage, tissue perfusion, gas exchange, and metabolic derangement correction in the setting of complex traumatic injuries and aim to improve patient outcomes by augmenting the capabilities of interdisciplinary trauma/critical care resuscitation teams. The clinical value of these emerging technological advancements depends upon matching the intervention(s) to the dominant physiological failure modes while assisting in damage control surgery and definitive surgical repair. This narrative review discusses advancements in resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) and inferior vena cava (REBOVC), selective regional perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and the technical and logistical barriers facing their clinical implementation. An escalating care pathway and conceptual framework to manage noncompressible hemorrhage and hemorrhage-induced traumatic cardiac arrest utilizing an integrated endovascular and extracorporeal approach is proposed based on prior literature and recent developments in selective abdominopelvic perfusion. Market dynamics remain an important consideration for fielding new technologies; development of specialized medical devices would benefit from versatile, multi-use capabilities to serve broader patient populations to enable economically sustainable employment within healthcare systems.
title: Endovascular and Extracorporeal Management of Complex Traumatic Injuries: Emerging Technologies and Techniques

abstract: The current definitions, explanations, and clinical classification of angina pectoris, particularly the traditional definitions of "typical" and “atypical” angina or chest pain and the stable versus unstable dichotomy, contains conceptual inconsistencies that impair understanding concepts, diagnostic clarity and clinical decision-making. This article challenges several long-standing assumptions about angina, especially regarding the "typical angina" construct and unstable angina definition. We argue for a redefinition grounded in pathophysiology of ischemia and clinical logic rather than rigid historical formulas. These criticisms carry important implications for both education and practice.
title: Rethinking Angina Pectoris—Toward Conceptual and Diagnostic Clarity

abstract: Background: /aims: To identify predictors of long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and investigate the association between reduced kidney function (KF) and MACE in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) presenting with STEMI as their first clinically recognized manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods: We analyzed 512 patients with DM and STEMI without previous CVD. KF was assessed at admission and categorized as mildly, moderately, or severely reduced. The composite endpoint (MACE) included cardiovascular death, non-fatal recurrent myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, and non-fatal stroke. The follow-up lasted 8 years. Results: Reduced KF was present in 312 (60.9%) patients: 175 (56.1%) had mildly, 98 (31.4%) moderately, and 39 (12.5%) severely reduced KF. MACE was more frequent among patients with reduced KF across all severity stages. Moderately and severely reduced KF were independent predictors of 8-year MACE (HR 3.12, 95% CI 1.58–6.91 and HR 5.22, 95% CI 1.68–12.70, respectively). Other independent predictors included predischarge ejection fraction Conclusion: In patients with DM presenting with their first STEMI, moderately and severely reduced KF were associated with approximately three-fold and five-fold higher risks of 8-year MACE, respectively. Mildly reduced KF was not independently associated with MACE. Assessment of KF severity may help identify patients requiring more intensive cardiovascular and multidisciplinary follow-up after STEMI.
title: Reduced Kidney Function Severity and Long-Term Cardiovascular Outcomes After First ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus

abstract: Background: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most common valvular heart diseases and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality if left untreated. Despite guideline recommendations, many patients with significant MR do not undergo surgical or transcatheter mitral valve intervention. We aimed to identify the clinical and echocardiographic characteristics associated with mitral valve intervention. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1,637 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe or severe MR evaluated at Shaare Zedek Medical Center between December 2016 and December 2021. Patients were categorized into an intervention group (n = 191) and a conservatively managed group (n = 1,446). Clinical and echocardiographic characteristics were compared using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Results: Among 1,637 patients, only 191 (11.7%) underwent mitral valve intervention. Patients receiving intervention were younger (72.8 ± 12.9 vs. 76.5 ± 14.2 years; p = 0.001), more frequently male (57.6% vs. 48.0%; p = 0.013), and more commonly of Arab ethnicity (22.5% vs. 13.1%; p Conclusions: Only a small proportion of patients with significant MR underwent mitral valve intervention. Older patients and those with ischemic or renal comorbidities were more likely to be managed conservatively. Earlier referral to dedicated Heart Valve Teams may improve access to guideline-directed treatment.
title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Predictors of Underutilization of Mitral Valve Intervention in Patients with Significant Mitral Regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Objective: To investigate whether the hemoglobin-to-creatinine (Hb/Cr) ratio provides independent prognostic value in critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), and further, whether it offers incremental value beyond the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Design: Retrospective observational cohort study with external validation. Setting: ICUs from the MIMIC-IV database (2008–2019, discovery) and the eICU-CRD database (2014–2015, multi-center validation). Patients: A total of 6,182 ICU-AMI patients from MIMIC-IV and 3,761 from eICU-CRD (MICE-analyzable cohorts). Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. A three-tier hierarchical strategy was applied: Model 1 (age+sex) replicated prior literature; Model 2 further adjusted for lactate, mechanical ventilation, and cardiogenic shock; Model 3 added SOFA (and renal indicators in MIMIC-IV) to test incremental value. In MIMIC-IV, Hb/Cr was significantly independently associated with mortality in Model 1 (OR = 1.11, p = 0.002) and remained significant in Model 2 (OR = 1.06, p = 0.031), confirming its basic prognostic value. However, after SOFA inclusion in Model 3, the association was completely attenuated to null (OR = 1.003, p = 0.756). This exact pattern was replicated in eICU-CRD (Model 2 OR = 0.945, p 0.05), and SHAP confirmed SOFA consistently outranked Hb/Cr in feature importance. Conclusions: Hb/Cr does carry independent prognostic information in ICU-AMI patients under traditional/adjusted frameworks. However, this information is entirely encompassed by the SOFA score. In settings where 24-hour SOFA is already available, Hb/Cr offers no additional clinical utility
title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Hemoglobin-to-Creatinine Ratio for Prognosis in Critically Ill AMI Patients: A Two-Database Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Abstract Objective: To investigate the correlation between melanoma inhibitory activity 3 (MIA3) and coronary collateral circulation (CCC) formation in patients with coronary chronic total occlusion (CTO). Methods: A total of 489 patients with CTO admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from January 2021 to July 2022 were enrolled as study subjects. According to the Rentrop classification system, patients were divided into a poor CCC group and a good CCC group. Baseline clinical data were collected, and plasma levels of MIA3 and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) were quantitatively measured. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent factors correlated with good CCC formation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the clinical value of predicting good CCC formation. The net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were calculated to assess the incremental predictive performance of MIA3 when added to traditional risk models. Clinical subgroup and interaction analyses were also performed. Results: Compared with the poor CCC group, patients in the good CCC group showed significantly higher plasma MIA3 levels (1280.87 pg/ml vs.1041.30 pg/ml, P 1462.24pg/ml) was identified as an independent related factor for good CCC formation (OR= 3.152, P Conclusion: MIA3 is an independent protective factor for good CCC formation in patients with CTO. Higher MIA3 levels are correlated with better collateral development, and this association is particularly prominent in patients with dyslipidemia. Incorporating MIA3 into traditional clinical models significantly enhances the predictive performance for good CCC formation in CTO patients.
title: Association Between MIA3 and Coronary Collateral Circulation Formation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face complex physical, psychosocial, and self-management demands, yet their stage-specific symptoms and care needs across the PCI pathway remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map these stage-specific experiences and construct a patient journey map to inform tailored nursing care. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right (TIR) framework, we conducted a qualitative descriptive study using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Sixteen patients with CMM undergoing PCI were recruited from the Department of Cardiology at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China, from June to July 2026 and participated in 20 semi-structured interviews. Qualitative content analysis used four prespecified journey-map domains with inductive development of subthemes, which were synthesized into a patient journey map. Results The PCI pathway was represented by three phases: preprocedural preparation, postprocedural recovery, and transition. Forty-eight subthemes were identified across four domains: symptoms, care needs, emotions, and pain points. Preprocedural accounts emphasized symptom recognition, gaps in chronic disease self-management, and needs for procedural information and reassurance; postprocedural accounts centered on symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and rehabilitation support; before discharge, patients anticipated difficulties coordinating multimorbidity self-management and expressed needs for structured, multidisciplinary continuity of care. Conclusions The journey map identified distinct stage-specific patterns in symptoms, emotions, care needs, and pain points among patients with CMM undergoing PCI. These findings may help align nursing support with preprocedural information and reassurance needs, postprocedural symptom and rehabilitation needs, and pre-discharge preparation for coordinated multimorbidity self-management.
title: Symptom-Demand journey map for patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity undergoing the periprocedural pathway of percutaneous coronary intervention: A qualitative study

abstract: Abstract Background Slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with larger infarct size and worse outcomes, yet simple tools for pre-procedural risk estimation remain limited. We investigated whether the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) independently predicts slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI, and whether adding high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and culprit-vessel location improves prediction. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent PCI between January 2023 and December 2025. Slow flow/no-reflow was defined as a post-procedural Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow grade of 2 or less in the culprit vessel. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); the combined model was compared with NLR alone using paired bootstrap testing of the AUC difference and a nested likelihood-ratio test. Internal validation used bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Results Of 305 patients, 53 (17.4%) developed slow flow/no-reflow. Log-transformed NLR (odds ratio [OR] 1.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22–2.88, P = 0.004) and log-transformed hs-cTnI (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.01–1.53, P = 0.043) were independent risk factors, whereas a left anterior descending culprit vessel, including the left main, was inversely associated with slow flow/no-reflow (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.22–0.86, P = 0.016). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.735 (95% CI 0.659–0.805) versus 0.674 for NLR alone (ΔAUC 0.061, 95% CI 0.003–0.123, P = 0.039); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.719 and the 10-fold cross-validated AUC 0.722, and calibration was good (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.101). Adding thrombus burden, left ventricular ejection fraction, AMI type, age, or sex did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC ≤ 0.002). Conclusions NLR is an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI. Combining NLR with hs-cTnI and culprit-vessel location adds discriminative value that is retained after internal validation. NLR is easy to obtain at admission and may support pre-procedural risk stratification, but external validation is needed before clinical use.
title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a single-center retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary slow flow (CSF) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may coexist with microvascular abnormalities beyond the epicardial coronary circulation. We examined whether retinal and choroidal features measured by ultra-widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA) were associated with post-PCI CSF. Methods In this prospective cross-sectional study, 103 patients with AMI who underwent successful PCI were classified by corrected thrombolysis in myocardial infarction frame count (CTFC) into the CSF group (n = 58) and normal coronary flow (NCF) group (n = 45). SS-OCTA was performed 2–3 days after PCI. Between-group comparisons incorporated false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Exploratory correlations were assessed using Spearman rank correlation, and factors associated with CSF were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve; calibration was assessed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples; and clinical utility was explored using decision curve analysis. Results After FDR correction, patients with CSF had lower deep capillary plexus vessel density (VD-DCP), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), and choroidal vascular volume (CVV) than patients with NCF. In multivariable logistic regression, higher white blood cell count (WBC; odds ratio [OR] = 1.491, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.184–1.878, P
title: Retinal and choroidal microvascular features associated with coronary slow flow after percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction: a prospective cross-sectional study using ultra-widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography

abstract: Abstract Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an effective treatment for severely calcified coronary lesions during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, data regarding patient-reported pain and anxiety during IVL are limited. Objective: To compare pain and anxiety levels in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI with those undergoing conventional PCI. Methods In this prospective single-center observational study, 100 patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing PCI between 2024 and 2025 were enrolled. Fifty patients underwent IVL-assisted PCI and 50 underwent conventional PCI. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, while anxiety was assessed using the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS). Results Baseline demographic characteristics were similar between groups. The IVL group had more complex coronary artery disease, including a higher prevalence of three-vessel disease (70% vs. 38%, p = 0.001), more previous coronary angiographies ( p = 0.007), and higher radiation exposure ( p = 0.018). Despite greater lesion complexity, no significant differences were observed in pain or anxiety scores between groups. The number of IVL pulses was not associated with pain or anxiety. Conclusions IVL-assisted PCI was not associated with increased pain or anxiety compared with conventional PCI despite greater procedural complexity. These findings support IVL as a well-tolerated strategy for the treatment of severely calcified coronary lesions.
title: Pain and Anxiety During Intravascular Lithotripsy-Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared with Conventional PCI: A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study

abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with revascularization procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting and percutaneous coronary intervention being commonly performed interventions. Despite these procedures, patients frequently experience diminished functional capacity and quality of life. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a proven strategy for improving post-surgical outcomes, yet participation remains notably low in low-resource settings such as Pakistan. METHODS This comparative study enrolled 501 post-revascularization patients at a tertiary cardiac care center in Karachi, Pakistan between January 2020 and December 2022. Participants were categorized into attenders (n = 250) who completed ≥ 15 structured CR sessions within 8 weeks, and non-attenders (n = 251) who attended fewer sessions. Exercise capacity was measured using peak metabolic equivalents, while exercise duration was assessed as moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in minutes per week. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 8-week follow-up, and one-year follow-up. Non-parametric statistical tests including Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests were employed for analysis. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated improvements in peak metabolic equivalents and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity from baseline to follow-up. However, CR attenders showed significantly greater median improvements in peak metabolic equivalents (1.41 vs 0.76, p CONCLUSION Structured CR significantly enhances exercise capacity and physical activity duration in post-revascularization patients, with attenders demonstrating substantially greater improvements than non-attenders. These findings underscore the vital role of organized CR in optimizing recovery outcomes in low-resource settings and support the expansion of such programs in Pakistan.
title: Comparative Effectiveness of Cardiac Rehabilitation on Functional Capacity and Physical Activity Duration among Post-Revascularization Patients in a Tertiary Care Setting in Pakistan

abstract: Abstract Background. An intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is sometimes needed after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but it is unclear what the timing of that need says about the patient with preserved left ventricular function. Most published series mix different open-heart operations, and the chance of needing support depends partly on the operation. We studied IABP use and timing in one homogeneous group, comparing support already running when the patient left the operating room with rescue support started in the intensive care unit (ICU). Methods. We reviewed consecutive adults who had elective or urgent isolated on-pump CABG with cross-clamping between July 2024 and December 2025, all with a preoperative ejection fraction (EF) of at least 50%. The primary outcome was operative mortality: death during the index stay, or within 30 days. Patients given an IABP were grouped by when it went in and by where support was running: OR-IABP if the balloon was working as the patient came off bypass, ICU-IABP if it started later in the ICU. Results. Of 1224 patients, 57 (4.7%) received an IABP. Operative mortality was 49.1% with IABP and 2.3% without (p
title: Timing of intra-aortic balloon pump support and early mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting in patients with preserved ejection fraction: a single-centre retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Remimazolam, a novel short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to propofol for anesthesia. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness and safety of remimazolam compared to propofol for anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures. Methods We conducted a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled, non-inferiority trial in elderly patients undergoing TAVI under general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA). The eligibility criterion was age 65 to 80 years. Of 118 patients assessed for eligibility, 76 met the inclusion criteria and were randomized (39 remimazolam, 37 propofol). Patients were blinded to allocation; the treating anesthesiologist, who administered the agents and recorded the emergence times, was not blinded. The primary outcome was time to LMA removal, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 2 minutes. Results The remimazolam group demonstrated significantly faster recovery: LMA removal time was 9.7 ± 1.5 minutes versus 20.8 ± 2.0 minutes in the propofol group (mean difference − 11.1 minutes, 95% confidence interval (CI) − 11.9 to − 10.3; p
title: Remimazolam versus Propofol for General Anesthesia in Elderly Patients Undergoing TAVI: A Randomized Controlled Trial

abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the association of admission albumin–bilirubin (ALBI) score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and to assess whether ALBI provides prognostic information beyond the admission GRACE score. Methods We retrospectively included 681 patients hospitalized between January 1, 2023, and September 1, 2025, who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI. Patients were categorized into ALBI tertiles (T1, T2 and T3). Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analysis were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and long-term MACEs. Missing data were handled using predictive mean matching, generating 50 imputed datasets. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. The discriminatory performance of the admission GRACE-based model was compared before and after ALBI was added. Follow-up continued through September 6, 2026. Results Among 681 patients, the median follow-up duration was 585 days, during which 186 MACEs occurred, representing 27.3% of the cohort. The cumulative proportions of MACEs in T1, T2 and T3 were 18.1%, 29.1% and 34.8%, respectively, differing significantly among groups (all P
title: Association of the admission albumin–bilirubin score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a single-center cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) drives morbidity and resource use. Existing prediction models were derived mainly in elective, high-income-country cohorts, and it is unclear whether EuroSCORE II identifies these patients. We developed and internally validated two models to predict ICU stay ≥ 7 days, one for use before surgery and one 24 hours after ICU admission and compared them with EuroSCORE II. Methods Retrospective cohort of adults undergoing isolated or combined CABG at a university hospital in Bogotá, Colombia (2,600 m above sea level), between 2019 and 2026. Predictors were pre-specified. Model 1 included ten preoperative predictors; Model 2 added cardiopulmonary bypass duration, intraoperative transfusion, cardiogenic shock, PaO 2 /FiO 2 on ICU admission and first-day chest-tube drainage to the Model 1 linear predictor. Missing data were multiply imputed. Internal validation used bootstrapping, followed by uniform shrinkage. We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves and temporal transportability, and derived a point score. Results Of 915 patients, 131 (14.3%) stayed in the ICU for ≥ 7 days; 88.7% of operations were urgent in-hospital procedures. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.73 (95% CI 0.68–0.78) for Model 1 and 0.76 (95% CI 0.70–0.80) for Model 2 (optimism-corrected 0.70 and 0.73), compared with 0.68 (95% CI 0.63–0.73) for EuroSCORE II. Concomitant cardiac procedures (odds ratio 3.52), older age, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, renal dysfunction and extracardiac vascular disease were the main preoperative predictors; cardiogenic shock and chest-tube drainage added information at 24 hours. Both models had greater net benefit than recalibrated EuroSCORE II at thresholds of 10–30%. The 24-hour points score separated low- (7.1%), intermediate- (18.5%) and high-risk (47.3%) groups. Baseline risk varied across calendar periods (observed-to-expected ratio for Model 2, 0.58–1.60). Conclusions Preoperative and early postoperative data predicted prolonged ICU stay after CABG with moderate discrimination. The 24-hour model discriminated better than EuroSCORE II, whereas the advantage of the preoperative model was modest. The models may support ICU capacity planning and the early targeting of preventive care, but they require external validation and local recalibration before clinical use.
title: Prediction of prolonged intensive care unit stay after coronary artery bypass grafting: development and internal validation of preoperative and 24-hour models in a Colombian cohort

abstract: Abstract Myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of residual myocardial damage following coronary revascularisation. Unfortunately, effective mechanism-based pharmacological interventions that can be translated into clinical practice remain limited. Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis and inflammation mutually reinforce each other and constitute a critical pathological process responsible for the amplification of myocardial injury during the early phase of reperfusion. Upon myocardial reperfusion, ferroptotic cardiomyocytes release damage-associated molecular patterns and disrupt tissue barriers, thereby activating the innate immune system and initiating inflammatory responses. In turn, inflammation promotes oxidative stress, dysregulation of iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation through the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways and the release of pro-inflammatory mediators, ultimately exacerbating ferroptosis. This reciprocal interaction establishes a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that contributes to the progression of MIRI. Encouragingly, several Western medicines and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine have shown therapeutic potential in modulating MIRI. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the bidirectional interaction between ferroptosis and inflammation in MIRI and discusses emerging pharmacological strategies targeting this pathological network. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that future therapeutic approaches to MIRI should extend beyond reperfusion therapy, antioxidant treatment, or anti-inflammatory intervention alone and instead consider combined strategies that simultaneously suppress inflammation and ferroptosis. Such an integrated approach may provide a novel translational framework for early risk assessment, therapeutic response prediction and targeted intervention in patients with MIRI.
title: Targeting Ferroptosis-Inflammation Crosstalk: A Novel Strategy for the Prevention and Treatment of Myocardial Ischaemia Reperfusion Injury

abstract: Abstract Background Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) continue after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite advances in revascularisation. Systemic inflammation contributes to atherosclerosis and plaque instability. The Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) is an inexpensive, easily calculated biomarker derived from routine blood counts that integrates inflammatory and immune pathways. This study evaluated its prognostic value for MACE after PCI. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study included 400 consecutive adults undergoing PCI for stable angina or acute coronary syndromes over 1 year. Pre-procedural complete blood counts were used to calculate SII [(platelet × neutrophil)/lymphocyte]. The primary outcome was in-hospital MACE, comprising all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke. Patients were stratified by SII quartiles. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression assessed predictive performance and independent associations. Results MACE occurred in 6.8% (n = 27). SII was significantly higher in patients with MACE than without (1127.19 ± 335.99 vs. 599.92 ± 324.55 ×10⁹/L; p 27) occurred in 72% of the highest versus 1% of the lowest SII quartile (p
title: Prognostic Value of Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SIII) in Predicting Major Adverse Cardiac Events (MACE) in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI): An Observational Study

abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the multidisciplinary management of extensive first-trimester inferior vena cava (IVC) and iliofemoral thrombosis in a single patient, in whom an individualized, patient-requested elective delivery was performed at 34 weeks, with favorable short- and long-term outcomes. Results Extensive thrombosis involving the infrarenal IVC, left iliac veins, and left femoral veins was diagnosed. Thrombophilia workup demonstrated persistently elevated lupus anticoagulant (LA1 ratio 1.26–1.45), elevated coagulation factors (factor VIII 397%, factor II 158%, factor VII 155%, factor X 153%), and elevated PIC (1.2 µg/mL). Serial imaging demonstrated gradual IVC recanalization by 24 weeks, development of robust collateral circulation, and stable chronic thrombosis without extension. After repeated counseling and multidisciplinary review, and at the patient's request because of severe refractory anxiety and progressive post-thrombotic symptoms, elective induction was performed at 34 + 0 weeks. She delivered vaginally a healthy neonate weighing 2,450 g with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes. No postpartum hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, or thrombus extension occurred. At 8 months postpartum, follow-up imaging demonstrated recanalization of the left common femoral vein with slow flow and spontaneous echo contrast consistent with chronic post-thrombotic venous stasis. Conclusion In this single case, extensive first-trimester IVC and iliofemoral thrombosis was managed with therapeutic LMWH, serial venous imaging, and multidisciplinary planning, with a favorable maternal and neonatal outcome after an individualized, patient-requested delivery at 34 weeks. This report describes one management course and does not establish the safety or generalizability of late-preterm delivery, the clinical utility of serial PIC monitoring, or a benefit of hydroxychloroquine; these remain unproven and should not be adopted as general practice. Term delivery remains the recommended default for stable pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism.
title: Successful multidisciplinary management of first-trimester inferior vena cava and iliofemoral thrombosis with elective late-preterm delivery and favorable long-term outcome: a case report

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) induces profound metabolic disturbances that aggravate cardiomyocyte injury and impair cardiac function. Modulating these disturbances may provide novel strategies for myocardial protection. Cinnamomum migao , a traditional ethnic medicinal herb for cardiovascular disorders, is historically administered as a decoction. While previous studies have focused on its volatile oil fraction, the cardioprotective effects and mechanisms of its water extract (CMW), consistent with traditional use, remain insufficiently characterized. Purpose This study aimed to systematically evaluate the cardioprotective effects of CMW against AMI and elucidate the underlying mechanisms associated with its metabolic regulation. Methods A mouse AMI model was established by left anterior descending coronary artery ligation. Cardioprotective effects of CMW were assessed via electrocardiography, infarct size, serum biomarkers, and histopathology. LC-HRMS-based untargeted metabolomics combined with AFADESI mass spectrometry imaging was employed to characterize myocardial metabolic alterations and spatial distribution of key metabolites. Serum pharmacochemistry, target prediction, and molecular validation were further applied to explore potential mechanisms. Results CMW markedly attenuated AMI-induced myocardial injury, evidenced by reduced infarct size, decreased serum biomarkers, and improved histopathology. Metabolomics revealed that CMW reversed AMI-associated disturbances, with glycerophospholipid metabolism identified as a key pathway. AFADESI imaging confirmed partial normalization of phosphocholine, lysophosphatidylcholine (22:5), and glycerophosphocholine distribution. Serum pharmacochemistry identified absorbed constituents including chlorogenic acid, neochlorogenic acid, naringin, afzelin, quercitrin, and norboldine. Molecular validation demonstrated that CMW activated SRC/PI3K/AKT signaling and restored Bcl-2/Bax balance in AMI myocardium. Conclusion CMW exerts cardioprotective effects against AMI by ameliorating glycerophospholipid metabolic disturbances and activating SRC/PI3K/AKT-associated signaling. Integration of untargeted and spatial metabolomics provides complementary evidence for its metabolic regulatory actions, offering a modern pharmacological interpretation of the traditional decoction use of Cinnamomum migao .
title: Cardioprotective effects of Cinnamomum migao water extract against acute myocardial infarction: insights from integrated untargeted and spatial metabolomics into glycerophospholipid metabolism and SRC/PI3K/AKT signaling

abstract: Abstract Background Electronic medical record (EMR) data provide an opportunity to support early risk stratification in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but models with large predictor sets may be difficult to implement. We aimed to develop and externally validate a parsimonious, interpretable machine learning model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This two-center retrospective cohort study included 1,726 patients: 1,218 in the derivation cohort and 508 in an independent external validation cohort. The primary outcome was in-hospital MACE, defined as a composite of death, cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral infarction, cardiogenic shock, cardiac rupture, recurrent myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events. A total of 125 candidate EMR variables were evaluated. LASSO and Boruta-based feature selection, alternative preprocessing strategies including ADASYN, seven machine learning algorithms, and grid-search cross-validation were compared. Discrimination was assessed using AUROC and AUPRC, with calibration and decision-curve analyses used to assess agreement and potential clinical utility. Results: In-hospital MACE occurred in 138 of 1,218 patients (11.3%) in the derivation cohort and 15 of 508 patients (3.0%) in the external cohort. The final random forest model retained eight predictors: Killip class, inorganic phosphorus, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, left ventricular ejection fraction, absolute neutrophil count, total protein, alanine aminotransferase, and potassium. The model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73–0.90) in internal validation and 0.90 (95% CI 0.85–0.95) in external validation. At the reported operating point, sensitivity was 0.488 and specificity was 0.991. Conclusions: An eight-variable random forest model derived from routinely collected EMR data showed good discrimination and preserved ranking performance in an independent hospital cohort. The model is best considered an early in-hospital risk-stratification tool; prospective validation with a prespecified prediction time is required before clinical implementation.
title: Development and external validation of an interpretable machine learning model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after PCI in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background The clinical significance of incidental coronary calcification on non-gated chest computed tomography (CT) in asymptomatic individuals is unclear. We developed artery-specific prediction models for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using three-dimensional calcium volume, with invasive angiography as the reference standard. Methods Calcium volume was quantified for the left anterior descending artery, left circumflex artery, and right coronary artery using 3D Slicer. Artery-specific multivariable logistic regression models were evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis, with internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results Of 354 patients, 129 (36.4%) underwent PCI. Calcium volume independently predicted PCI in the left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries but not the right coronary artery; between-artery differences were borderline and primarily driven by the right coronary artery. Ejection fraction independently predicted PCI in all models (odds ratio 0.847–0.871, all P P = 0.008) but acceptable agreement on bootstrap-corrected calibration. Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across a wide range of thresholds. Conclusions These artery-specific models may support quantitative triage of incidental coronary calcification, potentially avoiding unnecessary downstream evaluation in low-risk patients while ensuring timely revascularization in high-risk patients. Between-artery differences require confirmation in larger cohorts.
title: Artery-specific prediction of percutaneous coronary intervention from coronary calcium volume on non- gated chest computed tomography

abstract: Abstract Objective This study explores the behaviors, emotions and pain points of patients undergoing PCI treatment for acute myocardial infarction throughout the entire process, in order to provide a basis for constructing an integrated nursing model that extends from acute treatment to full-cycle health management. Methods A descriptive qualitative design was used. Thirty-three patients with AMI treated with PCI were recruited from the cardiology department of a tertiary hospital in China by purposive sampling between October and December 2025. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, participatory observation, and medical record review at two time points (during hospitalization and 3 months after discharge), and were analyzed following Colaizzi's seven-step method. Journey maps were constructed for each phase of care. Results Along the timeline of the emergency warning phase, the catheterization laboratory phase, the in-hospital recovery phase, and the long-term rehabilitation phase, core themes were identified from three dimensions: behaviors, emotions, and pain points. These included neglect of early symptoms and rapid care-seeking, engagement in intraoperative communication, building a care support system, and self-managed rehabilitation, together with phase-specific emotional responses such as fear and illness uncertainty, loneliness during the procedure, postoperative role confusion, and post-traumatic stress responses. A visual patient journey map was developed on this basis. Conclusion The journey of patients undergoing PCI for AMI is a dynamic recovery process involving physiological restoration, psychological adjustment, and social reintegration. In the future, through full-cycle psychological interventions and digital intelligent platforms, we can achieve comprehensive, precise, and personalized care, reduce patients' anxiety levels, and improve their treatment experience and long-term rehabilitation outcomes.
title: Patient Journey Mapping in Patients Undergoing PCI for Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Qualitative Study

abstract: Abstract Background: The role of catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) in haemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism (PE) remains controversial with observational data supporting a mortality benefit for CDT. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the effect of CDT, compared with anticoagulation alone, on mortality, haemodynamic decompensation and major bleeding in haemodynamically stable PE. Methods: Randomised controlled trials comparing treatment with CDT versus anticoagulation in patients with acute haemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism were systematically searched in the PubMed/MEDLINE database. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 days. Secondary outcomes were haemodynamic decompensation (efficacy) and major bleeding, minor bleeding and intracranial haemorrhage (safety). Results: A total of 8 clinical trials comprising 1503 patients with acute haemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism were included. CDT was not associated with a significant difference in 30-day all-cause mortality compared with anticoagulation alone (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.24–2.92). CDT reduced the risk of haemodynamic decompensation at 7 days (OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.08–0.87). Regarding safety, there was no significant difference in major bleeding between groups (OR, 1.39; 95% CI, 0.63–3.07), whereas minor bleeding occurred more frequently with CDT (OR, 2.77; 95% CI, 1.41–5.42). There were four reported cases of intracranial haemorrhage in the CDT arm. Conclusions: In patients with haemodynamically stable acute PE, CDT reduced early haemodynamic decompensation without a detectable difference in mortality. There was no significant increase in major bleeding, but minor bleeding was significantly increased. These findings might inform decisions of pulmonary embolism response teams.
title: Clinical outcomes of catheter-directed thrombolysis compared with anticoagulation in acute haemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a common degenerative valvular disease in the elderly, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is now its mainstream treatment. Conventional risk scores based on demographic and comorbidity data do not capture local cardiac inflammation or systemic nutritional status, limiting prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after TAVR. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) reflect these dimensions, but their combined incremental value is unknown. We assessed their independent and incremental value for MACE after TAVR, using EuroSCORE II as reference. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 427 consecutive patients with severe CAVD undergoing TAVR (January 2020 to July 2025) were enrolled. EAT volume was quantified on computed tomography angiography and dichotomized at the cohort median; NPS was derived from routine laboratory indices and categorized as low (0–2) or high (3–4). The endpoint was MACE after TAVR, defined by Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. Multivariable Cox regression assessed independent prognostic value; nested models were compared by Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent ROC, net reclassification index (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and decision curve analysis. Proportional hazards were assessed. Results During a median follow-up of 24.51 months, 89 patients (20.8%) experienced MACE. After adjustment, both high EAT and high NPS were independent predictors, with average hazard ratios (HRs) of 3.01 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.80–5.03; P P = 0.003). Adding both markers raised the C-index from 0.716 to 0.751 (likelihood-ratio P P = 0.011) and net reclassification index was 0.075 (95% CI − 0.081–0.239; P = 0.345). Calibration and sensitivity analyses supported the model; time-varying analysis showed that the effect of high EAT increased over follow-up whereas that of high NPS was confined to the early period. Conclusions Preoperative EAT volume and NPS are independent, complementary predictors of MACE after TAVR. Their combination improves on conventional risk scores and requires only routine preoperative examinations.
title: Epicardial adipose tissue volume and the Naples Prognostic Score add incremental value to EuroSCORE II for predicting MACE after TAVR: a retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning models developed on standard 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) can detect acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but their performance on limb-lead ECGs from mobile devices is uncertain. We evaluated an artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to mobile limb-lead ECGs for AMI detection, using cardiologist interpretation of truncated limb-lead and 12-lead ECGs as comparators. Methods We performed an analysis of a prospective observational cohort of 153 patients referred for coronary angiography at a Korean tertiary center (September 2022–October 2023). Each patient underwent mobile limb-lead and standard 12-lead ECG acquisition before revascularization. The model was applied without retraining to the mobile ECGs at two thresholds prespecified during model development (high sensitivity, high specificity), and three cardiologists independently interpreted truncated limb-lead and 12-lead ECGs. AMI was diagnosed according to the Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, with coronary angiography in all patients. Results Twenty-five patients (16.3%) had AMI, including 3 ST-elevation and 22 non-ST-elevation myocardial infarctions. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.843 (95% confidence interval, 0.758–0.928). At the high-sensitivity threshold, the model showed higher sensitivity than cardiologists interpreting truncated limb-lead and standard 12-lead ECGs (88.0% vs. 20.0% and 40.0%; both p
title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of AI-Enhanced Mobile Limb-Lead ECG versus Cardiologist-Interpreted Standard 12-Lead ECG for Acute Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) for cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high risks of major bleeding and arterial thrombotic events (ATEs), potentially exceeding clinical trial rates in real-world practice. Characterizing the incidence and temporal patterns of these complications may provide opportunities for time-sensitive strategies to balance bleeding and ischemic risk. Objective Assessment of real-world incidence, timing, and risks for major bleeding and ATE with tMCS for CS. Methods Prospective data from patients with CS supported by microaxial flow pump (mAFP), with or without veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), at two quaternary shock centres, were analysed. Results Among 204 patients with CS (predominantly Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions stages D-E), major bleeding was frequent (59%), occurring early after tMCS implantation (median 3 days), whereas ATEs were less common (14%), predominantly occurring later (median 10 days) with prolonged mAFP support. At 30 days, cumulative incidences of major bleeding and ATEs were 59.1% and 13.4%, respectively, versus 14.8% and 37.1% for competing death. Conventional coagulation assays did not differentiate patients developing major bleeding or ATEs. Major bleeding was associated with ECMELLA support and dual antiplatelet therapy, while ATEs associated with prolonged mAFP support and elevated fibrinogen. Conclusion In patients with CS supported by tMCS, major bleeding was frequent and occurred earlier, whereas ATEs were less frequent, occurring later, among survivors receiving prolonged support. Neither complication was reflected by conventional coagulation assays. These distinct temporal patterns could inform more dynamic, individualised antithrombotic management to mitigate bleeding and thrombotic risks.
title: Distinct temporal patterns in bleeding and arterial thrombotic complications in cardiogenic shock supported by microaxial flow pump

abstract: Abstract Background Managing extreme multi-morbidity in very elderly patients presents a therapeutic dead-end in modern medicine, as single-target interventions often exacerbate other conditions. We report a case of an 80-year-old male with severe coronary artery disease, recurrent stroke, COVID-19 pneumonia (white lung), and severe ankle osteoarthritis, who achieved comprehensive functional recovery following Neo-Chinese Medicine treatment. Case Presentation: The patient had a history of acute myocardial infarction with two coronary stent implantations, recurrent cerebral infarctions (including thalamic infarction) with tremors, and severe bilateral ankle osteoarthritis with joint effusion. Prior to seeking our treatment, he was evaluated at several top-tier hospitals in Shenyang, where he was advised to return to a local hospital for conservative management due to his advanced age and complex comorbidities. In 2022–2023, he developed severe COVID-19 pneumonia (white lung) and respiratory insufficiency. Following Neo-Chinese Medicine treatment, his pulmonary symptoms completely resolved. His resting tremors ceased, and limb muscle strength and tone returned to normal, indicating the resolution of suspected Parkinsonism. Notably, his lower limb edema (secondary to venous valve insufficiency) disappeared within 8 days. Regarding ankle osteoarthritis, after 4 days of recent outpatient treatment, his daily walking capacity increased from 2,400 to 3,400 steps without symptoms, and he completely discarded his resting stool and specialized therapeutic socks. Conclusion Neo-Chinese Medicine demonstrated remarkable efficacy in managing extreme multi-system comorbidities in this elderly patient. By remodeling the local microcirculatory microenvironment, this integrative approach achieved simultaneous resolution of pulmonary, neurological, vascular, and musculoskeletal symptoms, challenging the conventional single-disease treatment paradigm.
title: Successful Management of Severe Multi-System Comorbidities (Coronary Heart Disease, Recurrent Stroke, COVID-19 Pneumonia, and Ankle Osteoarthritis) in an 80-Year-Old Patient Using Neo-Chinese Medicine: A Case Report
