abstract: Background: A dose-finding trial evaluated safety and adherence for pre-cardiac surgery administration of sodium valproate. Analyses of myocardium obtained from participants at surgery investigated mechanisms underlying treatment effects. Methods: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery were randomised 1:1:1:1 with concealed allocation to no treatment (Controls), sodium valproate 15mg/kg/day for 1-2 weeks, 15mg/kg/day for 4-6 weeks, or 25mg/kg/day for 4-6 weeks pre-surgery. The primary analysis evaluated adherence and toxicity. Myocardial injury was defined by high sensitivity serum troponin post-surgery. Myocardial biopsies were analysed with single-nucleus Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin with sequencing (snATACseq), single nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNAseq), and immunofluorescence staining. Candidate mechanisms were validated in vitro. Results: The analysis cohort included 42 participants enrolled between January 2020 and August 2024. Sodium valproate 15mg/kg/day for 1-2 weeks had the highest levels of complete treatment adherence (70%), without severe drug related adverse effects. Non-compliance (12/32, 38%) was increased with longer and higher dosing. An as-treated analyses demonstrated a trend towards lower troponin release in participants receiving Valproate[≤]14 days (n=11) where myocardial biopsies demonstrated activation of pAKT-GSK3{beta}, acetylation of p53 (K382) and GPX4 ferroptosis protection pathways versus controls (n=12). Silencing of p53 attenuated the ferroptosis protective effect of valproate in vitro. Treatment effects were not explained by changes in chromatin accessibility. Treatment >14 days (n=19) was associated with cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation, suppression of ferroptosis protection pathways, and increased myocardial injury. Conclusions: Valproate 15mg/kg/day for [≤]14 days pre-surgery is well tolerated in adults awaiting cardiac surgery and is associated with ferroptosis protection and lower troponin release.
title: Dose-finding, experimental medicine evaluation of sodium valproate for the prevention of post-cardiac surgery myocardial injury

abstract: Background Longitudinal blood transcriptomes describe immune changes after myocardial infarction, but later assays do not necessarily represent the population sampled at admission. We examined whether recovery summaries depend on observable selection and assumptions about unavailable assays. Methods We reanalyzed official processed data from GSE59867, linking 111 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction across admission, discharge, one month, and six months. Seven fixed Hallmark programs were scored on a common 17,590-gene vocabulary using a bounded within-sample rank statistic. The primary endpoint was the six-month inflammatory-response score. We separated paired-completer change from the observed follow-up mean minus the entire baseline mean; fitted cross-fitted availability and outcome models; and evaluated full-support completion bounds and prespecified missing-mean scenarios. Artificial deletion tested estimators in the 83 observed six-month participants. GSE123342 provided unlinked marginal comparisons and explicitly conditional completion scenarios. Results GSE59867 contained 101, 95, and 83 follow-up assays. At six months, inflammatory-response change was −0.00893 among paired completers and −0.00999 for the marginal contrast (95% participant-bootstrap interval −0.01217 to −0.00783). Augmented inverse-probability weighting gave −0.01004 (−0.01556 to −0.00727). The full-support completion interval was [−0.16460, 0.08765], but eliminating the negative change required an unavailable-assay mean 4.42 observed-follow-up standard deviations above the observed mean. The primary direction remained negative throughout the prespecified ± 2-SD scenarios; interferon and coagulation directions were less stable. Under artificial outcome-dependent deletion, all evaluated estimators retained bias. The unlinked external cohort had 65 admission, 64 day-30, and 37 year-one MI assays; the year-one inflammatory contrast was −0.00459, with a conditional tipping shift of 1.70 SD. Conclusions The observed inflammatory-response rank-score decline was stable to baseline-score adjustment and the prespecified ± 2-observed-SD missing-mean scenarios, while unrestricted completion did not identify its direction. Robustness varied across programs and data settings. These findings concern relative transcriptomic scores and assay availability, not clinical recovery, survival, or intervention efficacy.
title: Follow-up availability and the robustness of immune transcriptomic recovery after myocardial infarction

abstract: Background Myocardial infarction (MI) initiates ventricular remodeling that extends beyond the infarct into remote, viable myocardium, where diffuse extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and stiffening contribute to progressive dysfunction and heart failure. Latent transforming growth factor binding protein 2 (LTBP2) is an injury-induced, microfibril-associated ECM glycoprotein that, uniquely among the LTBP family, does not covalently bind latent TGF-β. We asked whether LTBP2 regulates remote remodeling after MI, and how a protein lacking latent TGF-β–binding capacity could influence TGF-β–dependent fibrosis. Methods Wild-type and Ltbp2 -null mice underwent permanent coronary ligation or sham surgery and were followed for 28 days by echocardiography and speckle-tracking strain analysis. Remote myocardium was assessed by histology, atomic force microscopy, and quantitative proteomics. Cellular mechanism was interrogated in primary cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) using a TGF-β reporter assay and quantitative imaging of LTBP1 and LTBP2 matrix incorporation. Sufficiency was tested with a minimal fibrillin-1–binding module of LTBP2 delivered as purified protein or by lentiviral expression. Results LTBP2 was induced in injury-activated CFs and localized to infarct and remote myocardium by 7 days post-MI. Ltbp2 deletion improved 28-day survival (P=0.0272) without altering infarct size or early post-infarct function. By 28 days, Ltbp2 -null hearts showed improved ejection fraction and faster diastolic strain rates, with protection concentrated in segments remote from the infarct. Remote myocardium contained less interstitial collagen and was significantly less stiff, while cardiomyocyte hypertrophy was unaffected. Proteomic profiling showed enrichment of ECM organization and TGF-β–responsive programs in wild-type hearts that was attenuated in knockouts. In fibroblasts, loss of LTBP2 increased LTBP1 matrix incorporation and shifted TGF-β from the soluble to the matrix-bound compartment; conversely, the minimal LTBP2 module bound fibrillin-1 directly and mobilized latent TGF-β from established matrix within 20 minutes. Conclusions LTBP2 drives maladaptive remodeling of remote myocardium after MI by limiting matrix sequestration of latent TGF-β and expanding the activatable pool, resolving how an LTBP that does not bind latent TGF-β amplifies TGF-β–dependent fibrosis. LTBP2 and its fibrillin-1 interaction surface may be tractable targets. Novelty and Significance What Is Known? Remodeling of the remote, non-infarcted myocardium after myocardial infarction drives progressive fibrosis, ventricular stiffening, and heart failure, largely independent of infarct size. Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) is a central profibrotic signal, and its availability is controlled by latent TGF-β binding proteins (LTBPs) that tether latent complexes to fibrillin-rich microfibrils. LTBP2 is induced in fibrotic tissue but, unlike other family members, does not bind latent TGF-β, and how it influences TGF-β–driven fibrosis has been unresolved. What New Information Does This Article Contribute? LTBP2 is induced in injury-activated cardiac fibroblasts, deposited into fibrillin-rich matrix of both infarct and remote myocardium, and elevated in failing human left ventricle across ischemic, non-ischemic, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Deletion of Ltbp2 improves survival, reduces remote fibrosis and tissue stiffness, and preserves regional systolic and diastolic mechanics without altering infarct size or the cardiomyocyte hypertrophic response. A minimal fibrillin-1–binding module of LTBP2 is sufficient to drive latent TGF-β out of the matrix and into the activatable pool, explaining how a protein that cannot bind latent TGF-β nonetheless amplifies TGF-β–driven fibrosis. Summary Most therapies after myocardial infarction target the infarct itself, yet much of the decline toward heart failure originates in the surviving muscle surrounding the scar, where diffuse fibrosis stiffens the ventricle and impairs filling. We identify LTBP2 as a driver of this process. LTBP2 is produced by activated fibroblasts and incorporated into the microfibrillar scaffold of the matrix, where it reduces the amount of latent TGF-β held in reserve and increases the pool available for activation. Mice lacking LTBP2 survive infarction better and develop less fibrosis and stiffening in remote myocardium, with preserved regional mechanics but an intact hypertrophic response, indicating that the effect is specific to the interstitium. Conversely, introducing a short fibrillin-1–binding fragment of LTBP2 is enough to release latent TGF-β from the matrix within minutes. Because LTBP2 alters where TGF-β resides rather than blocking the pathway outright, and appears dispensable in the uninjured heart, targeting this interaction may offer a way to limit pathologic fibrosis without the toxicity of global TGF-β inhibition. Graphical Abstract LTBP2 remodels microfibrillar composition to enhance TGF-β bioavailability and profibrotic signaling Under homeostatic conditions (left), latent TGF-β is sequestered within the extracellular matrix (ECM) as part of the large latent complex (LLC), in which TGF-β is covalently associated with LTBP1 or LTBP4 and tethered to fibrillin-1 microfibrils. This matrix sequestration maintains a balanced distribution between bound and soluble pools of latent TGF-β, thereby limiting ligand activation and downstream signaling. During fibroblast activation (right), LTBP2 expression is upregulated and incorporated into newly assembling fibrillin-1 microfibrillar networks. Although LTBP2 does not covalently bind latent TGF-β, it competes with TGF-β–binding LTBP isoforms for fibrillin-1 binding sites, reducing LLC deposition within the matrix. This competitive remodeling shifts the equilibrium from matrix sequestration toward an expanded soluble LLC pool. Soluble latent complexes are more readily activated through integrin-mediated mechanical stress or proteolytic processing, increasing local active TGF-β levels. This model provides a mechanistic framework whereby LTBP2 indirectly amplifies TGF-β signaling by altering microfibrillar composition and competitive binding dynamics within the ECM, promoting enhanced TGF-β bioavailability and sustained profibrotic remodeling in the remote myocardium.
title: Latent Transforming Growth Factor Binding Protein – 2 promotes microfibrillar TGF-β bioavailability to drive pathologic fibrosis in remote regions of infarcted hearts

abstract: Structured abstract Background Cardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy. Methods GT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV. Results Among healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean±SD age 59±10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R 2 >0.16 vs R 2 Conclusions In health, GT, unlike LVM/EDV, remains effectively unchanged across EDV values, indicating that GT is a physiological constant in health and can track pathological changes. After intervention, only GT and not LVM/EDV consistently changed. Instead of LVM/EDV, GT should be used to quantify remodelling after interventions in left ventricular hypertrophy.
title: Global thickness for accurate and precise evaluation of post-intervention remodelling in left ventricular hypertrophy

abstract: Background: Acute decompensated aortic stenosis (ADAS) carries high mortality, but the optimal timing of valve intervention is unknown. Objective: To assess the association between time to valve intervention (transcatheter aortic valve replacement [TAVR] or balloon aortic valvuloplasty [BAV]) and clinical outcomes in ADAS. Methods: Embase, Ovid MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched to May 15, 2026. Hazard ratios (HRs) for delayed versus earlier intervention were pooled using random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Unadjusted short-term mortality risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel method. Results: Eight observational cohort studies (n=6,044) met inclusion criteria: six TAVR (n= 5,986) and two BAV (n=58) studies. Patients were approximately 79 years old, and 63% were male. Early-intervention thresholds ranged from Conclusion: Point estimates favour earlier intervention, but current observational data do not establish a mortality benefit for an optimal door-to-valve interval, and existing study designs are biased against early treatment. Prospective and randomized-controlled trials on optimal valve intervention timing following ADAS are needed.

appraisal.design_and_n: Eight observational cohort studies (n=6,044) met inclusion criteria: six TAVR (n= 5,986) and two BAV (n=58) studies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; most studies were at serious risk of bias with substantial heterogeneity in severity, timing thresholds and treatment modality.
appraisal.one_line: Preprint meta-analysis of observational cohorts on the timing of valve intervention in acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Delayed intervention was not significantly associated with long-term all-cause mortality (HR 1.52, 95% CI 0.46-5.00; p=0.269; I2=58.2%). Crude short-term mortality was higher with delayed intervention (RR 4.96, 95% CI 1.17-20.92; p=0.029; I2=0.0%), although this association was not robust to sensitivity analyses.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It frames a timing question for a high-mortality presentation of aortic stenosis where only observational data exist and a randomised comparison is called for.

title: Door-to-Valve Time and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: ABSTRACT BACKGROUND Risk models from high-income transplant programmes may not generalise to resource-constrained settings with different recipient acuity, donor characteristics and access to mechanical circulatory support. We developed RIGHT-HTx, a parsimonious framework integrating clinical and physiological vulnerabilities, and evaluated its prognostic performance in a subsequent same-centre cohort. METHODS This retrospective single-centre study included 436 consecutive adult heart transplant recipients (2012– 2026). Of 357 development recipients, 341 (95.5%) were score-evaluable. RIGHT-HTx incorporated three vulnerability domains: clinical acuity (INTERMACS 1–2), graded renal dysfunction (eGFR 30– 59 or 12 mmHg combined with donor-to-recipient weight ratio RESULTS Among development recipients, 75/341 (22.0%) died within one year. Mortality increased across low-, intermediate- and high-risk categories (8.1%, 20.3% and 55.6%; log-rank P CONCLUSIONS RIGHT-HTx identifies cumulative multidomain vulnerability associated with early mortality after heart transplantation. Temporal discrimination was comparable, but absolute-risk calibration differed. The framework may support risk recognition and mitigation, not transplant eligibility or allocation; independent multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.
title: Cumulative Multidomain Vulnerability and Early Mortality After Heart Transplantation: Development and Temporal Evaluation of the RIGHT-HTx Framework

abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with excess mortality, and 2 randomized trials have tested early transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to estimate the effects of early TAVR vs clinical surveillance and to compare randomized with observational estimates. METHODS: Six databases and registries were searched through November 3, 2026. Adjusted observational studies were synthesized separately from trials. Certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: Two trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts were included. Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty), with one-fifth of the deaths needed to detect a 20% reduction. Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty), or 70 fewer patients per 1,000 at 2 years. New pacemakers were more frequent (PROGRESS: 17.3% vs 9.3%; moderate certainty). About half of surveillance patients underwent valve replacement within 2 years. Observational cohorts estimated a 48% mortality reduction (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.43-0.64; very low certainty), which differed from the randomized estimate (ratio of HRs: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.37-2.95). CONCLUSIONS: In older, predominantly symptomatic patients with moderate AS, early TAVR may make little or no difference to 2-year mortality and may reduce HF hospitalization, at the cost of more pacemakers. Because about half of patients under surveillance receive a valve within 2 years, the decision largely concerns timing. Observational survival estimates should not guide practice.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of two randomized trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts.
appraisal.main_limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; only two trials, with low certainty and a heterogeneous trial population.
appraisal.one_line: A preprint meta-analysis of two trials and seven cohorts suggests early TAVR in moderate aortic stenosis did not detectably change mortality but may reduce heart failure hospitalisation, with more pacemakers.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty). Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses a live guideline question on timing of intervention in moderate aortic stenosis and quantifies the gap between randomised and observational estimates.

title: Early Valve Replacement vs Surveillance in Moderate Aortic Stenosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Observational Evidence

abstract: Background Genetic abnormalities play a role in the phenotypic heterogeneity of congenital heart disease (CHD), but their associations with long-term cardiovascular outcomes in adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) remain inadequately defined. This study examined the correlations between pathogenic sequence variations and copy number variants (CNVs) with cardiovascular and significant clinical outcomes in persons suffering from CHD. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 1,000 adults with structurally confirmed CHD recruited from a tertiary care centre in Noida, India, between January 2022 and January 2026, with follow-up through August 2026. Those who have consented received exome sequencing and chromosomal microarray assessment and were categorized into four distinct, non-overlapping groups: reference, sequence-variant-only, CNV-only, and dual-positive. The primary outcome was the time to the first occurrence of any of the following events: cardiovascular death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, resuscitated cardiac arrest, qualifying sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia, heart transplantation or durable mechanical circulatory support. Appropriate statistical analysis was performed and results were obtained. Results The results showed that among the participants recruited, 800 were in the reference group, 120 had sequence variants alone, 60 had CNVs alone, and 20 had both sequence variants and CNVs. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 12.0%, 20.0%, 25.0%, and 30.0% of participants, respectively. In the fully adjusted model, the sequence-variant-only group had an HR of 1.65 (95% CI, 1.01–2.69; nominal p = 0.0455), while the CNV-only group had an HR of 1.92 (95% CI, 1.04–3.52; nominal p = 0.0360), compared with the reference group. After Holm adjustment, neither association reached statistical significance (adjusted p = 0.072 for both comparisons). The dual-positive group had an HR of 2.12 (95% CI, 0.83–5.42; p = 0.1182). Extracardiac congenital anomalies and neurological disorders were more prevalent in those with genetic variations. Nonetheless, the secondary outcomes revealed no statistically significant correlations. Conclusions Pathogenic sequence variations and CNVs exhibited a numerically elevated adjusted risk for the primary cardiovascular composite outcome in ACHD, however neither primary association reached statistical significance after multiplicity adjustment. The findings highlight the potential significance of genetic diversity concerning clinical variability in ACHD, however they do not confirm independent prognostic significance.
title: Associations of Pathogenic Sequence Variants and Copy Number Variants with Cardiovascular and Major Clinical Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease

abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether GLP-1 RA use added to statins is associated with lower all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and ischemic stroke versus statin monotherapy in ASCVD patients with body mass index (BMI) 30 kg/m2. Approach and Results:Using the TriNetX Research Network (108 U.S. healthcare organizations), we identified ASCVD patients with BMI 30 kg/m2 on statins initiating a GLP-1 RA (n=166,278) versus statin-only controls (n=920,176). Propensity score matching on 34 covariates yielded 119,911 matched pairs followed 3 years. Prespecified analyses included a BMI 35 subgroup (62,385 pairs), four washout sensitivity analyses (30-120 days), and a familial hypercholesterolemia exclusion analysis (161,312 matched pairs). Results. GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (4.0% vs. 7.5%; HR 0.479; 95% CI: 0.463-0.496; p Conclusion: ASCVD patients with obesity on statins, GLP-1 RA use was associated with substantially lower mortality, MI, and stroke, suggesting GLP-1 RAs may serve as cardioprotective adjuncts to statin therapy in this population.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Added to Statin Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes in ASCVD A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study

abstract: Background: Cardiac arrest (CA) is a leading cause of death and disability in the United States, and no pharmacologic therapies improve post-arrest outcomes. Acute myocardial dysfunction is a highly prevalent CA complication that contributes to post-arrest mortality, yet the molecular mechanisms that drive this dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Prior work in our laboratory has suggested that ribosome-associated pathways are altered after CA in the heart and that translational dysregulation may be a central feature of post-arrest myocardial injury. Objectives: To define the impact of CA on myocardial ribosome biology and protein synthesis across experimental models of CA and determine how transcriptome, ribosome-bound transcriptome, translational efficiency, and proteome changes evolve after CA in the heart. Methods: We studied complementary porcine and murine models of CA. In pigs, left ventricular myocardium was collected from naive controls, cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation (Arrest), and cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity (PEA) re-arrest in a myocardial infarction-induced CA model and analyzed tissue by RNA sequencing. In mice, left ventricular tissue was collected at various time points after potassium chloride-induced asystole and resuscitation for ribosome activity and multi-omic profiling including RNA sequencing, ribosome profiling, and proteomics. Results: In the porcine model, myocardial transcriptomes demonstrate enrichment of cytosolic ribosomal protein transcripts and translation-related pathways that increase with ischemic burden. In contrast, a functional assay of ribosome activity in mice demonstrates suppression of protein synthesis after CA with gradual recovery over days. Multi-omic profiling in the mouse model demonstrates that ribosome- and translation-related pathways are among the most consistently altered programs across time points and modalities. While 6 h studies note prevalent inflammatory signals, 24 h studies find disruptions to ion homeostasis and conduction-related pathways that are likely related to translational suppression. Conclusions: CA induces marked remodeling of myocardial ribosome biology, characterized by increasing ribosomal transcripts with ischemic burden in the pig model. However, functional studies in the mouse model demonstrate that ribosome activity is suppressed following CA and remains suppressed for at least 24 h after resuscitation, contributing to reduced nascent protein synthesis and may limit critical functions of the heart. These findings identify translational control as a central feature of post-arrest myocardial injury and suggest that ribosome-dependent recovery pathways may represent a novel therapeutic target in post-arrest cardiac dysfunction.
title: Ribosomal Remodeling and Translational Suppression in the Post-Arrest Heart
